sentences.english: And the frogs will be gone from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people and will be only in the Nile.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Firawuna to a to na fe nu bara dangi, a man naxa a xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, a mu tin Munsa nun Haruna xui ra, alɔ Alatala a masen ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh; and Moses made prayer to the Lord about the frogs which he had sent on Pharaoh.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «A fala Haruna bɛ a xa a xa yisuxuwuri itala, a xa din bɔxi xube ra alako a xa mafindi saasie ra Misira bɔxi birin kui.»

sentences.english: And the Lord did as Moses said; and there was an end of all the frogs in the houses and in the open spaces and in the fields.
sentences.susu: E naxa a raba na ki. Haruna to a xa yisuxuwuri itala, a fa bɔxi xube garin, na birin naxa findi saasie ra, mixie nun xurusee fɔxɔ ra. Xube birin naxa findi saasie ra Misira bɔxi birin kui.

sentences.english: And they put them together in masses, and a bad smell went up from the land.
sentences.susu: Mandurulae to kata na kaabanako mɔɔli rabade, e mu nɔ. Saasie nu dinxi mixi nun xuruse birin na.

sentences.english: But when Pharaoh saw that there was peace for a time, he made his heart hard and did not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
sentences.susu: Mandurulae naxa a fala Firawuna bɛ, «Ala fɔxi yati nan na ki,» kɔnɔ Firawuna xaxili man naxa xɔrɔxɔ, a mu tin Munsa nun Haruna xui ra, alɔ Alatala a masenxi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron, Let your rod be stretched out over the dust of the earth so that it may become insects through all the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Tina gɛɛsɛgɛ i xa kurun, i xa naralan Firawuna ra ye yire. I xa a fala a bɛ Alatala xa masenyi nan ya, ‹N ma ɲama bɛɲin, alako e xa siga n batude.

sentences.english: And they did so; and Aaron, stretching out the rod in his hand, gave a touch to the dust of the earth, and insects came on man and on beast; all the dust of the earth was changed into insects through all the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Xa i mu sa tin n ma ɲama bɛɲinde, n fama xɛɛrie nan nadinde i tan, i xa kuntigie, nun i xa ɲama ma wo xɔnyi. Xɛɛrie fama lude Misirakae xa banxie nun e xa bɔxie birin ma.

sentences.english: And the wonder-workers with their secret arts, attempting to make insects, were unable to do so: and there were insects on man and on beast.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ na lɔxɔɛ, Gosen bɔxi ratangama nɛ, n ma ɲama na dɛnnaxɛ. Xɛɛrie mu luma naa, alako i xa a kolon a n tan Alatala na yi bɔxi yire birin ma.

sentences.english: Then the wonder-workers said to Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: but Pharaoh's heart was hard, and he did not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
sentences.susu: N tagi rasa luma nɛ n ma ɲama nun i gbe ma. Wo na kaabanako toma nɛ tina.›»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Get up early in the morning and take your place before Pharaoh when he comes out to the water; and say to him, This is what the Lord says: Let my people go to give me worship.
sentences.susu: Alatala a raba na ki nɛ. Xɛɛrie naxa din Firawuna, nun a xa kuntigie ra. Misira bɔxi birin xun naxa rakana xɛɛrie ra.

sentences.english: For if you do not let my people go, see, I will send clouds of flies on you and on your servants and on your people and into their houses; and the houses of the Egyptians and the land where they are will be full of flies.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa Munsa nun Haruna xili, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo xa siga sɛrɛxɛ bade wo Marigi Ala bɛ Misira.»

sentences.english: And at that time I will make a division between your land and the land of Goshen where my people are, and no flies will be there; so that you may see that I am the Lord over all the earth.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a yaabi, «Na mu lanma, barima muxu xa sɛrɛxɛe mu rafan Misirakae ma. Xa muxu na sɛrɛxɛ mɔɔli ba Misirakae ya xɔri e naxee xɔnxi, e mu muxu magɔnɔma xɛ?

sentences.english: And I will put a division between my people and your people; tomorrow this sign will be seen.
sentences.susu: A lanma muxu xa xi saxan biyaasi raba gbengberenyi ma, muxu fa sɛrɛxɛe ba muxu Marigi Alatala bɛ, alɔ a muxu yamarixi ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And the Lord did so; and great clouds of flies came into the house of Pharaoh and into his servants' houses, and all the land of Egypt was made waste because of the flies.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa a fala Munsa bɛ, «N fama wo bɛɲinde, alako wo xa siga gbengberenyi ma sɛrɛxɛe bade wo Marigi Alatala bɛ. Kɔnɔ wo naxa wo makuya a gbe ra. Yakɔsi, wo Ala maxandi n bɛ.»

sentences.english: And Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, Go and make your offering to your God here in the land.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a yaabi, «N bara tin. N na mini i xɔnyi, n Alatala maxandima nɛ. Tina, xɛɛrie makuyama nɛ Firawuna, a xa kuntigie, nun a xa ɲama ra. Kɔnɔ i tan Firawuna, i naxa muxu madaxu. I naxa tondi Isirayila ɲama bɛɲinde alako e xa sɛrɛxɛe ba Alatala bɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses said, It is not right to do so; for we make our offerings of that to which the Egyptians give worship; and if we do so before their eyes, certainly we will be stoned.
sentences.susu: Munsa to mini Firawuna xɔnyi, a naxa Alatala maxandi.

sentences.english: But we will go three days' journey into the waste land and make an offering to the Lord our God as he may give us orders.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa Munsa xa duba suxu. Xɛɛrie naxa makuya Firawuna, a xa kuntigie, nun a xa ɲama ra. Hali keren mu lu naa.

sentences.english: Then Pharaoh said, I will let you go to make an offering to the Lord your God in the waste land; but do not go very far away, and make prayer for me.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Firawuna man naxa a xaxili xɔrɔxɔ, a mu tin Isirayila ɲama bɛɲinde.

sentences.english: Then the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go so that they may give me worship.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «I xa siga Firawuna yire, i xa a fala a bɛ, ‹Isirayilaka Marigi Alatala xa masenyi nan ya, «I xa n ma ɲama bɛɲin, alako e xa siga n batude.»

sentences.english: For if you will not let them go, but still keep them in your power,
sentences.susu: Xa i tondi e bɛɲinde, i kankan e ma,

sentences.english: Then the hand of the Lord will put on your cattle in the field, on the horses and the asses and the camels, on the herds and the flocks, a very evil disease.
sentences.susu: Alatala fama wuganyi ɲaaxi radinde i xa xurusee ma, alɔ soe, sofalee, ɲɔxɔmɛe, ningee, yɛxɛɛe, nun si.

sentences.english: And the Lord will make a division between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt; there will be no loss of any of the cattle of Israel.
sentences.susu: Alatala fama Isirayilakae xa gɔɔrɛ nun Misirakae xa gɔɔrɛ tagi rasade. Isirayilakae xa xurusee mu wuganyi sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: And the time was fixed by the Lord, and he said, Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land.
sentences.susu: Alatala bara natɛ tongo na rabama tɛmui naxɛ, a falafe ra, «Tina, n fama na nan nabade.»›»

sentences.english: And on the day after, the Lord did as he had said, causing the death of all the cattle of Egypt, but there was no loss of any of the cattle of Israel.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, Alatala a raba na ki nɛ. Misira gɔɔrɛ birin naxa faxa, kɔnɔ hali xuruse keren mu faxa Isirayilakae xa gɔɔrɛ ya ma.

sentences.english: And Pharaoh sent and got word that there was no loss of any of the cattle of Israel. But the heart of Pharaoh was hard and he did not let the people go.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa mixie xɛɛ na fe kolonde. E naxa a fala Firawuna bɛ xuruse keren mu faxaxi Isirayilakae xa gɔɔrɛ kui, kɔnɔ a xaxili naxa xɔrɔxɔ, a man mu tin Isirayila ɲama bɛɲinde.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron, Take in your hand a little dust from the fire and let Moses send it in a shower up to heaven before the eyes of Pharaoh.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa a masen Munsa nun Haruna bɛ, «Wo xa tɛ xube rate Firawuna ya xɔri.

sentences.english: And it will become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and will be a skin-disease bursting out in wounds on man and beast through all the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: A findima xube ra naxan dinma Misira bɔxi birin na, a suuri ramini Misirakae nun e xa xurusee birin ma.»

sentences.english: So they took some dust from the fire, and placing themselves before Pharaoh, Moses sent it out in a shower up to heaven; and it became a skin-disease bursting out on man and on beast.
sentences.susu: E naxa tɛ xube xanin Firawuna yire. Munsa naxa a woli koore ma, a fa suuri ɲaaxie ramini mixie nun xurusee ma.

sentences.english: And the wonder-workers were not able to take their places before Moses, because of the disease; for the disease was on the wonder-workers and on all the Egyptians.
sentences.susu: Mandurulae yati mu nɔ tide Munsa ya i suurie xa fe ra, naxee nu na Misirakae birin ma.

sentences.english: And the Lord made Pharaoh's heart hard, and he would not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Alatala naxa Firawuna xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, alako a naxa tin Munsa nun Haruna xui suxude, alɔ Alatala nu bara a masen Munsa bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Get up early in the morning and take your place before Pharaoh, and say to him, This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go so that they may give me worship.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Tina i xa kurun sigafe ra Firawuna yire, a fala a bɛ, ‹Isirayila Marigi Alatala xa masenyi nan ya, «N ma ɲama bɛɲin, e xa siga n batude,

sentences.english: For this time I will send all my punishments on yourself and on your servants and on your people; so that you may see that there is no other like me in all the earth.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra n gbaloe mɔɔli birin naminima i tan, i xa kuntigie, nun i xa ɲama ma n sɛnbɛ ra. Na kui i fama a kolonde n maniyɛ mu na duniɲa bɛndɛ fuɲi fari.

sentences.english: For if I had put the full weight of my hand on you and your people, you would have been cut off from the earth:
sentences.susu: N nu nɔma gbaloe ɲaaxi raminide wo ma n sɛnbɛ ra, naxan nu nɔma wo sɔntɔde, wo lɔɛ duniɲa ma,

sentences.english: But, for this very reason, I have kept you from destruction, to make clear to you my power, and so that my name may be honoured through all the earth.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ n bara wo lu duniɲa alako n xa n sɛnbɛ masen wo bɛ, duniɲa xa n xili kolon.

sentences.english: Are you still uplifted in pride against my people so that you will not let them go?
sentences.susu: Han ya i kira bolonma n ma ɲama ya ra, i tondi e xa siga.

sentences.english: Truly, tomorrow about this time I will send down an ice-storm, such as never was in Egypt from its earliest days till now.
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra, tina n fama nɛ balabalanyi magaaxuxi ragorode Misira ma, wo mu naxan mɔɔli to kabi duniɲa fɔlɛ.

sentences.english: Then send quickly and get in your cattle and all you have from the fields; for if any man or beast in the field has not been put under cover, the ice-storm will come down on them with destruction.
sentences.susu: I xa i xa gɔɔrɛ nun i xa se birin naso yire makantaxi kui, barima yi balabalanyi na bira, a mixi nun xuruse birin sɔntɔma nɛ.»›»

sentences.english: Then everyone among the servants of Pharaoh who had the fear of the Lord, made his servants and his cattle come quickly into the house:
sentences.susu: Firawuna xa kuntigi ndee naxa gaaxu Alatala xa masenyi ya ra, e xulun e xa konyie nun e xa xurusee rasode yire makantaxi kui.

sentences.english: And he who gave no attention to the word of the Lord, kept his servants and his cattle in the field.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naxee mu nu e ɲɔxɔ saxi Alatala xa masenyi xɔn ma, e naxa e xa konyie nun e xa xurusee lu tande.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Now let your hand be stretched out to heaven so that there may be an ice-storm on all the land of Egypt, on man and on beast and on every plant of the field through all the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «I bɛlɛxɛ itala koore mabiri, balabalanyi xa bira mixi, xurusee, nun xɛe fari Misira bɔxi birin ma.»

sentences.english: And Moses put out his rod to heaven: and the Lord sent thunder, and an ice-storm, and fire running down on the earth; the Lord sent an ice-storm on the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Munsa to a xa yisuxuwuri itala koore ma, Alatala naxa seyamakɔnyi, galanyi, nun balabalanyi ragoro Misira bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: So there was an ice-storm with fire running through it, coming down with great force, such as never was in all the land of Egypt from the time when it became a nation.
sentences.susu: Balabalanyi masunbuxi tɛ ra a naxa goro e ma. Misira bɔxi mu nu na gbaloe mɔɔli to kabi a fɔlɛ.

sentences.english: And through all the land of Egypt the ice-storm came down on everything which was in the fields, on man and on beast; and every green plant was crushed and every tree of the field broken.
sentences.susu: Na balabalanyi naxa mixie nun xurusee magɔnɔ Misira bɔxi birin ma. A naxa xɛe nun wuri bilie fan kana.

sentences.english: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, there was no ice-storm.
sentences.susu: Gosen bɔxi gbansan naxa ratanga na gbaloe ma, Isirayilakae nu na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron, and said to them, I have done evil this time: the Lord is upright, and I and my people are sinners.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa Munsa nun Haruna xili, a a fala e bɛ, «Yi biyaasi, n bara yunubi raba. Nɔndi na Alatala nan bɛ. N tan nun n ma ɲama bara tantan.

sentences.english: Make prayer to the Lord; for there has been enough of these thunderings of God and this ice-storm; and I will let you go and will keep you no longer.
sentences.susu: Wo xa Alatala madiɲɛ, alako seyamakɔnyi nun balabalanyi xa ɲɔn. N bara tin wo bɛɲinde, n mu kankanma wo ma sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: And Moses said, When I am gone outside the town, my hands will be stretched out to the Lord; the thunders and the ice-storm will come to an end, so that you may see that the earth is the Lord's.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala a bɛ, «N na mini taa kui, n Alatala maxandima wo bɛ. Galanyi nun balabalanyi danma nɛ, alako i xa a kolon a Alatala nan gbe duniɲa ra.

sentences.english: But as for you and your servants, I am certain that even now the fear of the Lord God will not be in your hearts.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n bara a kolon, i tan nun i xa kuntigie, wo mu gaaxuxi Marigi Alatala ya ra sinden.»

sentences.english: And the flax and the barley were damaged, for the barley was almost ready to be cut and the flax was in flower.
sentences.susu: Na balabalanyi nu bara sansi funden maniyɛ nun gɛsɛ futi kana, naxee mu nu mɔ sinden.

sentences.english: But the rest of the grain-plants were undamaged, for they had not come up.
sentences.susu: Mɛngi nun a maniyɛ tan mu kana, barima e tan tɛmui mu nu a lixi.

sentences.english: So Moses went out of the town, and stretching out his hands made prayer to God: and the thunders and the ice-storm came to an end; and the fall of rain was stopped.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa mini Firawuna xɔnyi, a siga taa fari ma. A to a bɛlɛxɛ itala Alatala maxandide, galanyi, balabalanyi, nun tunɛ naxa dan.

sentences.english: But when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the ice-storm and the thunders were ended, he went on sinning, and made his heart hard, he and his servants.
sentences.susu: Firawuna to na to, a man naxa yunubi sɔtɔ, barima a tan nun a xa kuntigie naxa e xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ.

sentences.english: And the heart of Pharaoh was hard, and he did not let the people go, as the Lord had said by the mouth of Moses.
sentences.susu: Na kui Firawuna mu tin Isirayilakae bɛɲinde, alɔ Alatala a masenxi ki naxɛ Munsa saabui ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh: for I have made his heart and the hearts of his servants hard, so that I may let my signs be seen among them:
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Siga Firawuna yire, barima n tan nan a xaxili nun a xa kuntigie xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, alako n xa n ma tɔnxuma makaabaxie masen e bɛ.

sentences.english: And so that you may be able to give to your son and to your son's son the story of my wonders in Egypt, and the signs which I have done among them; so that you may see that I am the Lord.
sentences.susu: N gbaloe naxan dɔxɔma Misirakae ma, wo xa na fala wo xa die nun wo xa mamadie bɛ, alako wo xa a kolon, n tan nan Alatala ra.»

sentences.english: Then Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and said to him, This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: How long will you be lifted up in your pride before me? let my people go so that they may give me worship.
sentences.susu: Munsa nun Haruna naxa siga Firawuna xɔnyi, e a fala a bɛ, «Isirayila Marigi Alatala xa masenyi nan ya, ‹I tondima i yɛtɛ magorode n bɛ han mun tɛmui? I xa n ma ɲama bɛɲin, e xa siga n batude.

sentences.english: For if you will not let my people go, tomorrow I will send locusts into your land:
sentences.susu: Xa i mu e bɛɲin, tina n katoe radinma nɛ i xa bɔxi birin ma.

sentences.english: And the face of the earth will be covered with them, so that you will not be able to see the earth: and they will be the destruction of everything which up to now has not been damaged, everything which was not crushed by the ice-storm, and every tree still living in your fields.
sentences.susu: E bɔxi gbaata makotoma nɛ, e sansi nun wuri bili birin donma nɛ balabalanyi mu naxee lixi.

sentences.english: And your houses will be full of them, and the houses of your servants and of all the Egyptians; it will be worse than anything your fathers have seen or their fathers, from the day when they were living on the earth till this day. And so he went out from Pharaoh.
sentences.susu: E fama sode i tan, i xa kuntigie, nun Misirakae birin xa banxie kui, alɔ wo benbae mu nu a toxi ki naxɛ kabi Misira fɔlɛ.›» Munsa to gɛ na falade, a naxa a kobe so, a mini Firawuna xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And Pharaoh's servants said to him, How long is this man to be the cause of evil to us? let the men go so that they may give worship to the Lord their God: are you not awake to Egypt's danger?
sentences.susu: Firawuna xa kuntigie naxa a fala a bɛ, «Yi xɛmɛ won tɔɔrɔma han mun tɛmui? I xa a xa ɲama bɛɲin alako e xa siga e Marigi Alatala batude. Han ya i mu a kolon Misira na sɔntɔfe nɛ?»

sentences.english: Then Moses and Aaron came in again before Pharaoh: and he said to them, Go and give worship to the Lord your God: but which of you are going?
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa Munsa nun Haruna xili, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo siga, wo sa wo Marigi Alatala batu.» A man naxa e maxɔrin, «Ndee na sigafe wo ya ma?»

sentences.english: And Moses said, We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds; for we are to keep a feast to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a yaabi, «Muxu birin sigama nɛ: fonikee, forie, xɛmɛe, ginɛe, muxu xa xurusee. Alatala xa sali xungbe na a ra.»

sentences.english: And he said to them, May the Lord be with you, if I will let you and your little ones go! take care, for your purpose clearly is evil.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa e yaabi, «Wo wama nɛ n xa a fala wo bɛ, ‹Alatala xa wo kanta.› Xa n sa a lu wo xa siga, wo nun wo xa die, n a kolon wo fe kobi rabama nɛ.

sentences.english: Not so; but let your males go and give worship to the Lord, as your desire is. This he said, driving them out from before him.
sentences.susu: N mu tinma na ra. Xɛmɛe gbansan nɔma sigade Alatala batude, barima wo na nan maxɔrinxi.» A to gɛ na falade, Firawuna naxa e keri.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Let your hand be stretched out over the land of Egypt so that the locusts may come up on the land for the destruction of every green plant in the land, even everything untouched by the ice-storm.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «I bɛlɛxɛ itala Misira bɔxi xun ma, katoee xa fa. E xa burɛxɛ xinde birin don balabalanyi mu naxee lixi.»

sentences.english: And Moses' rod was stretched out over the land of Egypt, and the Lord sent an east wind over the land all that day and all the night; and in the morning the locusts came up with the east wind.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a xa yisuxuwuri itala Misira bɔxi xun ma, Alatala fa foye ramini yanyi nun kɔɛ keren kui kelife sogetede. Na kuye iba, na foye nu bara fa katoee ra,

sentences.english: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, resting on every part of the land, in very great numbers; such an army of locusts had never been seen before, and never will be again.
sentences.susu: naxee din Misira bɔxi birin na. Katoee gbegbe naxa lu Misira yire birin. Han ya na fe maniyɛ mu toxi, a man mu toma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: For all the face of the earth was covered with them, so that the land was black; and every green plant and all the fruit of the trees which was untouched by the ice-storm they took for food: not one green thing, no plant or tree, was to be seen in all the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: E naxa bɔxi birin makoto han a ifɔɔrɔ. E naxa burɛxɛ xinde nun wuri bogi birin don balabalanyi mu naxan lixi. Burɛxɛ xinde yo mu lu wurie nun sansie kɔn na Misira bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: Then Pharaoh quickly sent for Moses and Aaron, and said, I have done evil against the Lord your God and against you.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa Munsa nun Haruna xili mafuren. A naxa a fala e bɛ, «N bara yunubi sɔtɔ wo Marigi Alatala ra, n bara haakɛ sɔtɔ wo fan na.

sentences.english: Let me now have forgiveness for my sin this time only, and make prayer to the Lord your God that he will take away from me this death only.
sentences.susu: Wo xa diɲɛ n ma, wo xa wo Marigi Alatala maxandi alako a xa yi tɔɔrɛ ba n ma.»

sentences.english: So he went out from Pharaoh and made prayer to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa keli Firawuna yire, a naxa Alatala maxandi.

sentences.english: And the Lord sent a very strong west wind, which took up the locusts, driving them into the Red Sea; not one locust was to be seen in any part of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa turunnaadɛ foye ramini, a katoe birin tutun sogegorode, a sa e rasin Xulunyumi Baa ma. Hali katoe keren mu lu Misira.

sentences.english: But the Lord made Pharaoh's heart hard, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi Alatala naxa Firawuna xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, alako a naxa Isirayilakae bɛɲin.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Let your hand be stretched out to heaven, and all the land of Egypt will be dark, so that men will be feeling their way about in the dark.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa a fala Munsa bɛ, «I bɛlɛxɛ itala koore ma, dimi binye xa sin Misira bɔxi ma.»

sentences.english: And when Moses' hand was stretched out, dark night came over all the land of Egypt for three days;
sentences.susu: Munsa to na raba, dimi binye naxa sin Misira bɔxi birin ma. Xi saxan bun ma

sentences.english: They were not able to see one another, and no one got up from his place for three days: but where the children of Israel were living it was light.
sentences.susu: mixi mu nɔ a boore tode, mixi mu nɔ kelide a xɔnyi. Kɔnɔ Isirayilakae nu sabatixi dɛnnaxɛ, mɛnni tan iyalanxi.

sentences.english: Then Pharaoh sent for Moses, and said, Go and give worship to the Lord; only let your flocks and your herds be kept here: your little ones may go with you.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa Munsa xili, a a fala a bɛ, «Wo xa siga Alatala batude. Wo nɔma wo xa die nun wo xa ginɛe xaninde, kɔnɔ wo xa wo xa xurusee tan lu be.»

sentences.english: But Moses said, You will have to let us take burned offerings to put before the Lord our God.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a yaabi, «I xa tin muxu xa xurusee xanin muxu naxee bama sɛrɛxɛ ra muxu Marigi Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: So our cattle will have to go with us, not one may be kept back; for they are needed for the worship of the Lord our God; we have no knowledge what offering we have to give till we come to the place.
sentences.susu: Muxu xa gɔɔrɛ birin xa siga. Hali keren mu luma be. Ndee bama sɛrɛxɛ nan na muxu Marigi Alatala bɛ, kɔnɔ muxu mu a kolon sinden xurusee mundun rawalima na kui, fo muxu xa so naa.»

sentences.english: But the Lord made Pharaoh's heart hard, and he would not let them go.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi Alatala naxa Firawuna xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, a mu tin e bɛɲinde.

sentences.english: And Pharaoh said to him, Go away from me, take care that you come not again before me; for the day when you see my face again will be your last.
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa a fala Munsa bɛ, «Keli n xun ma! I yɛtɛ ratanga tife ra n ya i sɔnɔn. Xa n i to be, n i faxama nɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses said, You say truly; I will not see your face again.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a yaabi, «A xa raba alɔ i a fala ki naxɛ. I mu n toma sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, I will send one more punishment on Pharaoh and on Egypt; after that he will let you go; and when he does let you go, he will not keep one of you back, but will send you out by force.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «N fama kaabanako dɔnxɔɛ ragorode Firawuna nun Misirakae ma. Na dangi xanbi, Firawuna wo bɛɲinma nɛ, wo siga kerenyi ra.

sentences.english: So go now and give orders to the people that every man and every woman is to get from his or her neighbour ornaments of silver and of gold.
sentences.susu: A fala ɲama bɛ e xa e dɔxɔboore makula gbeti nun xɛɛma ra.»

sentences.english: And the Lord gave the people grace in the eyes of the Egyptians. For the man Moses was highly honoured in the land of Egypt, by Pharaoh's servants and the people.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a ragiri Misirakae xa tin Isirayilakae kide. Misira ɲama nun Firawuna xa kuntigie naxa gaaxu Munsa ya ra.

sentences.english: And Moses said, This is what the Lord says: About the middle of the night I will go out through Egypt:
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala, «Alatala xa masenyi nan ya, ‹Kɔɛ tagi n Misira bɔxi igirima nɛ,

sentences.english: And death will come to every mother's first male child in all the land of Egypt, from the child of Pharaoh on his seat of power, to the child of the servant-girl crushing the grain; and the first births of all the cattle.
sentences.susu: di singe birin fa faxa kelife Firawuna xa di singe ma, a sa dɔxɔ konyi ginɛe xa di singe ra. Firawuna tan mangɛya fima a xa di ma, konyi ginɛ tan taami rafalama, kɔnɔ e xa di singe birin fama nɛ faxade. Hali Misirakae xa xurusee xa di singee faxama nɛ.

sentences.english: And there will be a great cry through all the land of Egypt, such as never has been or will be again.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Misira wa xui nde mɛma nɛ, e mu naxan mɔɔli mɛxi tɛmui dangixie, e mu naxan mɔɔli mɛma tɛmui naxee sa fama.

sentences.english: But against the children of Israel, man or beast, not so much as the tongue of a dog will be moved: so that you may see how the Lord makes a division between Israel and the Egyptians.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isirayilakae xɔnyi, hali bare keren mu wonwonma. Na kui wo xa a kolon n tagi rasa luxi Misirakae nun Isirayilakae tagi.

sentences.english: And all these your servants will come to me, going down on their faces before me and saying, Go out, and all your people with you: and after that I will go out. And he went away from Pharaoh burning with wrath.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui i xa kuntigie birin fama nɛ e xinbi sinde n bun ma, e a fala n bɛ, a n tan nun n ma ɲama birin xa mini e xa bɔxi kui. N na gɛ na rabade, n sigama nɛ.›» Munsa to gɛ na falade, a naxa keli Firawuna xun ma, a xɔnɔxi ki fanyi ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Pharaoh will not give ear to you, so that my wonders may be increased in the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Alatala nu bara a masen Munsa bɛ, «Firawuna mu a tuli matima wo ra. Na kui n nan n ma kaabanakoe xun masama nɛ Misira bɔxi kui.»

sentences.english: All these wonders Moses and Aaron did before Pharaoh: but the Lord made Pharaoh's heart hard, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
sentences.susu: Munsa nun Haruna nu bara na kaabanakoe birin naba Firawuna ya xɔri, kɔnɔ Alatala bara Firawuna xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, a mu tin Isirayilakae xa mini a xa bɔxi kui.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa nun Haruna bɛ Misira bɔxi ma,

sentences.english: Let this month be to you the first of months, the first month of the year.
sentences.susu: «Yi kike naxan ya, yi nan findima wo bɛ ɲɛ kike singe ra.

sentences.english: Say to all the children of Israel when they are come together, In the tenth day of this month every man is to take a lamb, by the number of their fathers' families, a lamb for every family:
sentences.susu: Wo xa a fala Isirayila ɲama birin bɛ, yi kike xi fu, denbaya yo denbaya xa yɛxɛɛ keren sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And if the lamb is more than enough for the family, let that family and its nearest neighbour have a lamb between them, taking into account the number of persons and how much food is needed for every man.
sentences.susu: Xa denbaya nde xurun, e mu nɔma na ra, e xa kafu e dɔxɔ boore ndee ma alako yɛxɛɛ keren xa e birin nali.

sentences.english: Let your lamb be without a mark, a male in its first year: you may take it from among the sheep or the goats:
sentences.susu: Na yɛxɛɛ xa findi xɛmɛ ra, naxan bara ɲɛ keren sɔtɔ, lanyuru yo mu naxan ma. Xa na mu a ra, wo nɔma si fan nawalide.

sentences.english: Keep it till the fourteenth day of the same month, when everyone who is of the children of Israel is to put it to death between sundown and dark.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a ragata han na kike xi fu nun naani. Na lɔxɔɛ Isirayila denbaya birin xa e gbe kɔn naxaba soge dula tɛmui.

sentences.english: Then take some of the blood and put it on the two sides of the door and over the door of the house where the meal is to be taken.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a wuli maso naadɛ gbanyi nun a sɛɛtie ma, a donma banxi naxan kui.

sentences.english: And let your food that night be the flesh of the lamb, cooked with fire in the oven, together with unleavened bread and bitter-tasting plants.
sentences.susu: Na sube xa gan tɛ ra, wo xa a don na kɔɛ ra taami lɛbinitare nun burɛxɛ xɔnɛ ra.

sentences.english: Do not take it uncooked or cooked with boiling water, but let it be cooked in the oven; its head with its legs and its inside parts.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa a don a gantare ra, wo naxa a ɲin ye ra. Wo xa a birin gan a fanyi ra beenu wo xa a ixaba. A xunyi, a sanyie, nun a furingɛe xa gan tɛmui keren.

sentences.english: Do not keep any of it till the morning; anything which is not used is to be burned with fire.
sentences.susu: Na sese naxa xi han gɛɛsɛgɛ. Xa nde luxi, wo xa na woli tɛ xɔɔra.

sentences.english: And take your meal dressed as if for a journey, with your shoes on your feet and your sticks in your hands: take it quickly: it is the Lord's Passover.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a don wo tagi ixirixi, wo xa sankirie soxi wo sanyie, a nun wo xa yisuxuwuri suxuxi wo bɛlɛxɛ ra. Wo xa a don mafuren mafuren. Alatala xa Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali sɛrɛxɛ na a ra.»

sentences.english: For on that night I will go through the land of Egypt, sending death on every first male child, of man and of beast, and judging all the gods of Egypt: I am the Lord.
sentences.susu: «Na kɔɛ ra, n Misira bɔxi isama nɛ, n di singe birin faxa mixie nun xurusee ya ma. N Misira xa alae ɲaxankatama nɛ. N tan nan Alatala ra.

sentences.english: And the blood will be a sign on the houses where you are: when I see the blood I will go over you, and no evil will come on you for your destruction, when my hand is on the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: N na na wuli tɔnxuma to wo xa naadɛe ma, n dangima nɛ mɛnni xun ma. Kasarɛ yo mu wo lima, n Misira bɔxi ratɔnma tɛmui naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And this day is to be kept in your memories: you are to keep it as a feast to the Lord through all your generations, as an order for ever.
sentences.susu: «Na lɔxɔɛ xa findi sali xungbe nan na wo bɛ Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma. Wo xa na sali raba ɲɛ yo ɲɛ Alatala xa yaamari ki ma.

sentences.english: For seven days let your food be unleavened bread; from the first day no leaven is to be seen in your houses: whoever takes bread with leaven in it, from the first till the seventh day, will be cut off from Israel.
sentences.susu: Na sali waxati wo xa taami lɛbinitare don xi solofere bun ma. Sali fɔlɛ lɔxɔɛ, wo xa lɛbini birin namini wo xa banxie kui. Mixi yo naxan taami lɛbini daaxi donma na xi solofere bun ma, na kanyi xa ramini Isirayila ɲama ya ma.

sentences.english: And on the first day there is to be a holy meeting and on the seventh day a holy meeting; no sort of work may be done on those days but only to make ready what is necessary for everyone's food.
sentences.susu: Na sali lɔxɔɛ singe nun na sali lɔxɔɛ solofere nde, wo xa wo malan Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma. Na lɔxɔɛ firinyie, wo naxa wali yo raba bafe donse rafalafe ra.»

sentences.english: So keep the feast of unleavened bread; for on this very day I have taken your armies out of the land of Egypt: this day, then, is to be kept through all your generations by an order for ever.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa yi Taami Lɛbinitare Sali raba, barima n wo xa ɲama ramini Misira bɔxi ra na lɔxɔɛ nɛ. N bara wo yamari wo xa yi sali raba ɲɛ yo ɲɛ abadan.

sentences.english: In the first month, from the evening of the fourteenth day, let your food be unleavened bread till the evening of the twenty-first day of the month.
sentences.susu: Kike singe, xi fu nun naani, nunmare fɔlɔ tɛmui, wo naxa taami yo don bafe taami lɛbinitare ra han a xi mɔxɔɲɛn nun keren, a nunmare tɛmui.

sentences.english: For seven days no leaven is to be seen in your houses: for whoever takes bread which is leavened will be cut off from the people of Israel, if he is from another country or if he is an Israelite by birth.
sentences.susu: Na xi solofere bun ma, lɛbini yo naxa to wo xɔnyi, barima xɔɲɛ nun Isirayilaka birin naxan lɛbini donma na waxati bun ma, a raminima nɛ Isirayila ɲama ya ma.

sentences.english: Take nothing which has leaven in it; wherever you are living let your food be unleavened cakes.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa taami lɛbini daaxi don dɛdɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Moses sent for the chiefs of Israel, and said to them, See that lambs are marked out for yourselves and your families, and let the Passover lamb be put to death.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa Isirayila fori birin xili, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo xa siga xuruse nde sɔtɔde wo xa denbayae bɛ. Wo xa e kɔn naxaba Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And take some hyssop and put it in the blood in the basin, touching the two sides and the top of the doorway with the blood from the basin; and let not one of you go out of his house till the morning.
sentences.susu: Wo na gɛ xuruse kɔn naxabade, wo xa a wuli maso naadɛ gbanyi nun naadɛ sɛɛtie ma hisopi burɛxɛ ra. Mixi yo naxa mini a xa banxi kui han gɛɛsɛgɛ.

sentences.english: For the Lord will go through the land, sending death on the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the two sides and the top of the door, the Lord will go over your door and will not let death come in for your destruction.
sentences.susu: Alatala na Misira bɔxi isa di singe faxafe ra, a dangima nɛ banxie xun ma, wuli na naxee naadɛ gbanyi nun a sɛɛtie ma. A mu tinma kanari yo xa so wo xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And you are to keep this as an order to you and to your sons for ever.
sentences.susu: Wo nun wo xa die xa yi yaamari ratinmɛ ɲɛ yo ɲɛ abadan.

sentences.english: And when you come into the land which the Lord will make yours, as he gave his word, you are to keep this act of worship.
sentences.susu: Wo na so bɔxi kui Alatala naxan laayidixi wo bɛ, wo xa yi sali raba a ki ma.

sentences.english: And when your children say to you, What is the reason of this act of worship?
sentences.susu: Wo xa die na wo maxɔrin, ‹Yi sali munse masenma won bɛ,›

sentences.english: Then you will say, This is the offering of the Lord's Passover; for he went over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he sent death on the Egyptians, and kept our families safe. And the people gave worship with bent heads.
sentences.susu: wo xa e yaabi, ‹Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali sɛrɛxɛ nan a ra. Won na rabama Alatala bɛ naxan dangi Isirayilakae xa banxie xun ma Misira, alako e xa ratanga, Misirakae tan xa faxa.›» Isirayila ɲama naxa a suyidi Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: And the children of Israel went and did so; as the Lord had given orders to Moses and Aaron, so they did.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae naxa na yaamari ratinmɛ alɔ Alatala a masenxi Munsa nun Haruna bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And in the middle of the night the Lord sent death on every first male child in the land of Egypt, from the child of Pharaoh on his seat of power to the child of the prisoner in the prison; and the first births of all the cattle.
sentences.susu: Kɔɛ tagi Alatala naxa di singe birin faxa Misira bɔxi kui, kelife Firawuna kibanyi kanyi xa di singe ma, a sa dɔxɔ geelimani xa di singe ra. A naxa xuruse xa di singe fan birin faxa.

sentences.english: Then Pharaoh got up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians; and a great cry went up from Egypt; for there was not a house where someone was not dead.
sentences.susu: Na kui Firawuna naxa keli kɔɛ ra, a tan, a xa kuntigie, nun Misirakae birin, e fa e wa xui rate, barima banxi keren mu lu faxɛ mu ti dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And he sent for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Get up and go out from among my people, you and the children of Israel; go and give worship to the Lord as you have said.
sentences.susu: Na kɔɛ ra Firawuna naxa Munsa nun Haruna xili, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo nun Isirayilakae, wo mini n ma ɲama ya ma. Wo siga, wo sa Alatala batu, alɔ wo nu wama a xɔn ma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And take your flocks and your herds as you have said, and be gone; and give me your blessing.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo xa xurusee xanin, alɔ wo a falaxi ki naxɛ. Wo siga! Wo xa duba n fan bɛ.»

sentences.english: And the Egyptians were forcing the people on, to get them out of the land quickly; for they said, We are all dead men.
sentences.susu: Misirakae nu gbataxi Isirayilakae xa siga. E nu a fala, «Xa e mu sigama, won birin fama nɛ sɔntɔde!»

sentences.english: And the people took their bread-paste before it was leavened, putting their basins in their clothing on their backs.
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra Isirayilakae naxa taami ramulanxi mafilin e xa dugie kui, beenu taami xa te. E naxa taami nun taami ramulanse dɔxɔ e xun ma, e fa siga.

sentences.english: And the children of Israel had done as Moses had said; and they got from the Egyptians ornaments of silver and of gold, and clothing:
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae naxa gbeti, xɛɛma, nun dugie makula Misirakae ma alɔ Munsa a fala e bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord had given the people grace in the eyes of the Egyptians so that they gave them whatever was requested. So they took away all their goods from the Egyptians.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a ragiri Misirakae xa tin Isirayilakae waxɔnfe ra. Na kui Isirayilakae naxa se gbegbe sɔtɔ Misirakae yi ra.

sentences.english: And the children of Israel made the journey from Rameses to Succoth; there were about six hundred thousand men on foot, as well as children.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae naxa keli Ramesesi, sigafe Sukɔti. Xɛmɛ wulu kɛmɛ senni nu na, bafe ginɛe nun dimɛdie ra.

sentences.english: And a mixed band of people went with them; and flocks and herds in great numbers.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbɛtɛe fan naxa bira e fɔxɔ ra, a nun gɔɔrɛ gbegbe mɔɔli birin.

sentences.english: And they made unleavened cakes from the paste which they had taken out of Egypt; it was not leavened, for they had been sent out of Egypt so quickly, that they had no time to make any food ready.
sentences.susu: E naxa taami gan, na taami lɛbinitare ramulanxi ra, e faxi naxan na e xun ma kelife Misira. Na taami mu nu texi, barima Misirakae to e keri, e mu nɔ fandɛ rafalade.

sentences.english: Now the children of Israel had been living in Egypt for four hundred and thirty years.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae nu bara ɲɛ kɛmɛ naani ɲɛ tongo saxan naba Misira.

sentences.english: And at the end of four hundred and thirty years, to the very day, all the armies of the Lord went out of the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Na ɲɛ kɛmɛ naani ɲɛ tongo saxan ɲɔn lɔxɔɛ yati, Alatala xa ɲama birin mini Misira bɔxi ra na nɛ.

sentences.english: It is a watch-night before the Lord who took them out of the land of Egypt: this same night is a watch-night to the Lord for all the children of Israel, through all their generations.
sentences.susu: Alatala to na kɔɛ radangi Isirayila ɲama raminife ra Misira, a lanma Isirayilakae birin xa na kɔɛ xungbilenyi radangi Alatala matɔxɔfe ra ɲɛ yo ɲɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, This is the law of the Passover: no man who is not an Israelite is to take of it:
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa yi sɛriyɛ so Munsa nun Haruna yi ra Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali xa fe ra, «Mixi yo naxa na sɛrɛxɛ don naxan mu findixi Isirayilaka ra.

sentences.english: But every man's servant, whom he has got for money, may take of it, when he has had circumcision.
sentences.susu: Wo xa konyi sunnaxie nɔma a donde,

sentences.english: A man from a strange country living among you, and a servant working for payment, may not take part in it.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ wo xa walikɛ naxee kelixi yire gbɛtɛ, e naxa a don.

sentences.english: It is to be taken in one house; not a bit of the flesh is to be taken out of the house, and no bone of it may be broken.
sentences.susu: Na sɛrɛxɛ xa don banxi nan kui, wo naxa a sube xanin tande, wo naxa a xɔri yo gira.

sentences.english: All Israel is to keep the feast.
sentences.susu: Isirayila ɲama birin xa Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali raba.

sentences.english: And if a man from another country is living with you, and has a desire to keep the Passover to the Lord, let all the males of his family undergo circumcision, and then let him come near and keep it; for he will then be as one of your people; but no one without circumcision may keep it.
sentences.susu: Xa wo xa xɔɲɛ nde wama Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali rabafe Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma, fo a xa xɛmɛ birin sunna a xa denbaya kui. Xa a bara na raba, a nɔma na sali rabade alɔ Isirayilakae. Kɔnɔ sunnataree mu nɔma a donde.

sentences.english: The law is the same for him who is an Israelite by birth and for the man from a strange country who is living with you.
sentences.susu: Lasiri nun xɔɲɛ birin na na sɛriyɛ bun ma.»

sentences.english: So the children of Israel did as the Lord gave orders to Moses and Aaron.
sentences.susu: Isirayilaka birin naxa a raba, alɔ Alatala Munsa nun Haruna yamarixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And on that very day the Lord took the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ yati, Alatala naxa Isirayilakae ramini Misira bɔxi ra, e lanxundɛ ki ma.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Let the first male child of every mother among the children of Israel be kept holy for me, even the first male birth among man or beast; for it is mine.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa di singe birin fi n ma, a findi mixi ra, a findi xuruse ra. N tan nan gbe na Isirayilakae birin xa di singee ra.»

sentences.english: And Moses said to the people, Let this day, on which you came out of Egypt, out of your prison-house, be kept for ever in memory; for by the strength of his hand the Lord has taken you out from this place; let no leavened bread be used.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala ɲama bɛ, «Wo xa ratu to lɔxɔɛ ma sali ra, barima Alatala sɛnbɛ nan wo raminixi Misira bɔxi ma konyiya kui. Wo naxa lɛbini yo don na lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: On this day, in the month Abib, you are going out.
sentences.susu: Wo minixi to Abibi kike nan na.

sentences.english: And it will be that, when the Lord takes you into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, the land which he made an oath to your fathers that he would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you will do this act of worship in this month.
sentences.susu: Alatala na wo raso bɔxi kui, a naxan laayidixi wo benbae bɛ, Kanaankae, Xitikae, Amorikae, Hiwikae nun Yebusukae sabatixi dɛnnaxɛ, xiɲɛ nun kumi xɛlɛma bɔxi naxan ma, wo xa Taami Lɛbinitare Sali raba na kike ra.

sentences.english: For seven days let your food be unleavened cakes; and on the seventh day there is to be a feast to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Na sali waxati wo xa taami lɛbinitare gbansan don xi solofere bun ma. Na xi solofere nde, wo xa sali raba Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma.

sentences.english: Unleavened cakes are to be your food through all the seven days; let no leavened bread be seen among you, or any leaven, in any part of your land.
sentences.susu: Na xi solofere bun ma taami lɛbinitare nan donma. Lɛbini yo naxa lu Isirayilaka nde xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And you will say to your son in that day, It is because of what the Lord did for me when I came out of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ wo xa yi sali xa fe fatanfasi wo xa die bɛ, wo fa a fala, ‹N yi sali rabama nɛ, barima Alatala bara n namini Misira bɔxi ra.›

sentences.english: And this will be for a sign to you on your hand and for a mark on your brow, so that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth: for with a strong hand the Lord took you out of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Yi sali luma nɛ wo bɛ alɔ tɔnxuma naxan saxi wo bɛlɛxɛ ma, xa na mu tɔnxuma naxan saxi wo tigi ma, alako wo naxa nɛɛmu Alatala xa sɛriyɛ ma.

sentences.english: So let this order be kept, at the right time, from year to year.
sentences.susu: Wo xa yi sali raba a waxati ɲɛ birin na.»

sentences.english: And when the Lord takes you into the land of Canaan, as he made his oath to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
sentences.susu: «Alatala na wo raso Kanaankae xa bɔxi ma, a a fi wo ma alɔ a laayidixi wo tan nun wo benbae bɛ ki naxɛ,

sentences.english: You are to put on one side for the Lord every mother's first male child, the first-fruit of her body, and the first young one of every beast; every male is holy to the Lord.
sentences.susu: wo xa wo xa di xɛmɛ singe birin fi Alatala ma, a nun wo xa xurusee xa di xɛmɛ singe. Wo xa di xɛmɛma singe birin findixi Alatala nan gbe ra.

sentences.english: And for the young of an ass you may give a lamb in payment, or if you will not make payment for it, its neck is to be broken; but for all the first sons among your children, let payment be made.
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma yɛxɛɛ xa na mu a ra si fide wo xa sofale xa di singe ɲɔxɔɛ ra, xa na mu a ra wo xa a kobe gira, a xa faxa. Wo xa wo xa di singe fan xun sara yɛxɛɛ ra.

sentences.english: And when your son says to you in time to come, What is the reason for this? say to him, By the strength of his hand the Lord took us out of Egypt, out of the prison-house:
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li wo xa di nde wo maxɔrinma a wo yi fe rabama fe naxan ma, wo xa a yaabi, ‹Alatala sɛnbɛ nan won naminixi konyiya kui Misirakae yi ra.

sentences.english: And when Pharaoh made his heart hard and would not let us go, the Lord sent death on all the first sons in Egypt, of man and of beast: and so every first male who comes to birth is offered to the Lord; but for all the first of my sons I give a price.
sentences.susu: Firawuna to tondi muxu bɛɲinde muxu xa siga, Alatala naxa Misira di singe birin faxa mixie nun xurusee ya ma. Na nan a ra won xurusee xa di singe birin fima Alatala ma sɛrɛxɛ ra, a nun won ma di xɛmɛ singe birin xun sarama nɛ yɛxɛɛ ra.›

sentences.english: And this will be for a sign on your hand and for a mark on your brow: for by the strength of his hand the Lord took us out of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Na luma nɛ wo bɛ alɔ tɔnxuma naxan saxi wo bɛlɛxɛ ma, xa na mu tɔnxuma naxan saxi wo tigi ma, barima Alatala sɛnbɛ nan wo raminixi Misira bɔxi ma konyiya kui.»

sentences.english: Now after Pharaoh had let the people go, God did not take them through the land of the Philistines, though that was near: for God said, If the people see war, they may have a change of heart and go back to Egypt.
sentences.susu: Firawuna to Isirayila ɲama bɛɲin, Alatala mu e xun ti Filisita bɔxi kira ra, hali na kira nan to sɔɔnɛya, barima a a fala nɛ, «Xa ɲama gere lima kira xɔn ma, e natɛ masarama nɛ, e fa gbilen Misira.»

sentences.english: But God took the people round by the waste land near the Red Sea: and the children of Israel went up in fighting order out of the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Na kui Alatala naxa ɲama ya rafindi gbengberenyi kira ma Xulunyumi Baa mabiri. Isirayilakae naxa mini Misira e xa geresosee ra e yi ra.

sentences.english: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had made the children of Israel take an oath, saying, God will certainly keep you in mind; and you are to take my bones away with you.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa Yusufu xɔrie fan xanin, barima Yusufu nu bara Isirayila xa die rakali na fe ma, a falafe ra, «N a kolon, Alatala fama nɛ wo malide. Na tɛmui wo xa n xɔrie xanin wo xun ma yire gbɛtɛ.»

sentences.english: Then they went on their journey from Succoth, and put up their tents in Etham at the edge of the waste land.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae naxa keli Sukɔti, e sa yonkin Etama gbengberenyi fɔlɔxi dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, guiding them on their way; and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light: so that they were able to go on day and night:
sentences.susu: Alatala nan nu tixi e ya ra. Yanyi ra a naxa e raɲɛrɛ nuxui ra, kɔɛ ra a naxa e raɲɛrɛ tɛ dɛxɛ ra koore ma, naxan nu kuye iyalanma e bɛ. Na ki e nu nɔma ɲɛrɛde kɔɛ nun yanyi ra.

sentences.english: The pillar of cloud went ever before them by day, and the pillar of fire by night.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ yo lɔxɔ na nuxui nu tixi e ya ra yanyi ra, na tɛ fan nu tixi e ya ra kɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Give orders to the children of Israel to go back and put up their tents before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-zephon, opposite to which you are to put up your tents by the sea.
sentences.susu: «A fala Isirayilakae bɛ e xa gbilen, e xa fa yonkin Pi Haxirɔti mabiri ra, Migidoli nun baa tagi. E xa lu baa dɛ ra Baali Sefon ya ra.

sentences.english: And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are wandering without direction, they are shut in by the waste land.
sentences.susu: Firawuna a maɲɔxunma nɛ, a Isirayilakae bara lɔɛ gbengberenyi mabiri.

sentences.english: And I will make Pharaoh's heart hard, and he will come after them and I will be honoured over Pharaoh and all his army, so that the Egyptians may see that I am the Lord. And they did so.
sentences.susu: N Firawuna xaxili raxɔrɔxɔma nɛ, alako a xa bira wo fɔxɔ ra. Na kui n fama matɔxɔɛ sɔtɔde Firawuna nun a xa sɔɔrie saabui ra. Misirakae fama nɛ a kolonde a n tan nan na Alatala ra.» Isirayilakae a raba na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: And word came to Pharaoh of the flight of the people: and the feeling of Pharaoh and of his servants about the people was changed, and they said, Why have we let Israel go, so that they will do no more work for us?
sentences.susu: Misira mangɛ nun a xa kuntigie to a kolon, a Isirayilakae bara siga, e naxa natɛ masara, a falafe ra, «Won munse rabaxi yi ki? Won to Isirayilakae bɛɲinxi, e mu walima won bɛ sɔnɔn!»

sentences.english: So he had his war-carriage made ready and took his people with him:
sentences.susu: Firawuna naxa yaamari fi soe xa xiri sɔɔri ragisee ra, sɔɔrie xa malan yire keren.

sentences.english: And he took six hundred carriages, all the carriages of Egypt, and captains over all of them.
sentences.susu: A naxa sɔɔri ragise fanyi kɛmɛ senni sugandi, sɔɔri ragise naxan birin na Misira e fa bira e fɔxɔ ra. Sɔɔri kuntigi nu bakixi e birin kui.

sentences.english: And the Lord made the heart of Pharaoh hard, and he went after the children of Israel: for the children of Israel had gone out without fear.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa Misira mangɛ Firawuna xaxili raxɔrɔxɔ, a fa bira Isirayilakae fɔxɔ ra, naxee nu sigafe xun nakeli kui.

sentences.english: But the Egyptians went after them, all the horses and carriages of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them in their tents by the sea, by Pihahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
sentences.susu: Firawuna nun a xa sɔɔri birin naxa bira Isirayilakae fɔxɔ ra e xa soe nun e xa sɔɔri ragisee ra. Misirakae naxa e li baa dɛ ra, e nu yonkinxi dɛnnaxɛ, Pi Haxirɔti mabiri ra, Baali Sefon ya ra.

sentences.english: And when Pharaoh came near, the children of Israel, lifting up their eyes, saw the Egyptians coming after them, and were full of fear; and their cry went up to God.
sentences.susu: Firawuna to makɔrɛ e ra, Isirayilakae naxa e ya rakeli, e naxa Misirakae to fa ra. E naxa gaaxu ki fanyi ra, e fa e mawa Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: And they said to Moses, Was there no resting-place for the dead in Egypt, that you have taken us away to come to our death in the waste land? why have you taken us out of Egypt?
sentences.susu: E naxa a fala Munsa bɛ, «I won naminixi Misira bɔxi ra munfe ra? Yakɔsi won faxama nɛ gbengberen yire. A mu nu fisa won xa faxa Misira?

sentences.english: Did we not say to you in Egypt, Let us be as we are, working for the Egyptians? for it is better to be the servants of the Egyptians than to come to our death in the waste land.
sentences.susu: Won nu na Misira bɔxi ma tɛmui naxɛ, muxu a fala nɛ i bɛ, ‹Muxu walife Misirakae bɛ, na fisa muxu bɛ dinɛ faxafe ra gbengberenyi ma.›»

sentences.english: But Moses said, Keep where you are and have no fear; now you will see the salvation of the Lord which he will give you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today you will never see again.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa ɲama yaabi, «Wo naxa gaaxu, wo xa limaniya. To wo fama Alatala xa kisi tode. Misirakae naxee yi ki, wo mu e toma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: The Lord will make war for you, you have only to keep quiet.
sentences.susu: Alatala nan gere soma wo bɛ. Wo sabari.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Why are you crying out to me? give the children of Israel the order to go forward.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «I mawafe n bɛ munfe ra? A fala Isirayilakae bɛ, e xa ti kira xɔn ma.

sentences.english: And let your rod be lifted up and your hand stretched out over the sea, and it will be parted in two; and the children of Israel will go through on dry land.
sentences.susu: I xa yisuxuwuri rate, a itala baa xun ma, alako baa xa rabi, Isirayilakae xa igiri bɔxi xaraxi ra.

sentences.english: And I will make the heart of the Egyptians hard, and they will go in after them: and I will be honoured over Pharaoh and over his army, his war-carriages, and his horsemen.
sentences.susu: N Misirakae xaxili raxɔrɔxɔma nɛ, alako e xa bira wo fɔxɔ ra. Na kui n matɔxɔɛ sɔtɔma Firawuna, a xa sɔɔrie, a xa sɔɔri ragisee, nun a xa soe ragimae saabui ra.

sentences.english: And the Egyptians will see that I am the Lord, when I get honour over Pharaoh and his war-carriages and his horsemen.
sentences.susu: N na gɛ matɔxɔɛ sɔtɔde Firawuna, a xa sɔɔri ragisee, nun a xa soe ragimae saabui ra, Misirakae a kolonma nɛ a n tan nan na Alatala ra.»

sentences.english: Then the angel of God, who had been before the tents of Israel, took his place at their back; and the pillar of cloud, moving from before them, came to rest at their back:
sentences.susu: Ala xa malekɛ naxan nu na sigafe Isirayila ɲama ya ra, a naxa gbilen e xanbi ra. Nuxui fan naxa keli e ya ra, a fa ti e xanbi ra

sentences.english: And it came between the army of Egypt and the army of Israel; and there was a dark cloud between them, and they went on through the night; but the one army came no nearer to the other all the night.
sentences.susu: Misirakae nun Isirayilakae tagi. Na nuxui naxa a niya Misirakae xa lu dimi kui, Isirayilakae tan xa lu naiyalanyi kui. E mu nɔ e makɔrɛde e boore ra na kɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: And when Moses' hand was stretched out over the sea, the Lord with a strong east wind made the sea go back all night, and the waters were parted in two and the sea became dry land.
sentences.susu: Munsa to a bɛlɛxɛ itala baa xun ma, Alatala naxa baa tutun kɔɛ birin na foye xungbe ra kelife sogetede. A naxa kira xaraxi ramini baa tagi.

sentences.english: And the children of Israel went through the sea on dry land: and the waters were a wall on their right side and on their left.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae dangima dɛnnaxɛ, baa yee naxa malan e yirefanyi ma nun e kɔɔla ma.

sentences.english: Then the Egyptians went after them into the middle of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses and his war-carriages and his horsemen.
sentences.susu: Misirakae naxa e sagata. Firawuna xa soe, a xa sɔɔri ragisee, nun a xa soe ragimae birin naxa bira e fɔxɔ ra baa tagi.

sentences.english: And in the morning watch, the Lord, looking out on the armies of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud, sent trouble on the army of the Egyptians;
sentences.susu: Subaxɛ ma, Alatala naxa a ya rasiga Misira xa sɔɔrie ma kelife koore ma, tɛ nun nuxui na dɛnnaxɛ, a fa e ifu.

sentences.english: And made the wheels of their war-carriages stiff, so that they had hard work driving them: so the Egyptians said, Let us go in flight from before the face of Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against the Egyptians.
sentences.susu: A naxa a ragiri sɔɔrie ragisee sanyie xa ba na, e xa ɲɛrɛ xa xɔrɔxɔ. Na kui, Misirakae naxa a fala, «Won xa won gi Isirayilakae ma, barima Alatala nan na e xa gere sofe.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Let your hand be stretched out over the sea, and the waters will come back again on the Egyptians, and on their war-carriages and on their horsemen.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «I bɛlɛxɛ itala baa xun ma, ye xa radin Misirakae, e xa sɔɔri ragisee, nun e xa soe ragimae xun na.»

sentences.english: And when Moses' hand was stretched out over the sea, at dawn the sea came flowing back, meeting the Egyptians in their flight, and the Lord sent destruction on the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.
sentences.susu: Munsa to na raba subaxɛ ma, baa naxa gbilen a yire. Misirakae nu na e gife tɛmui naxɛ, Alatala naxa ye dusu e birin xun na.

sentences.english: And the waters came back, covering the war-carriages and the horsemen and all the army of Pharaoh which went after them into the middle of the sea; not one of them was to be seen.
sentences.susu: Ye naxa Firawuna xa sɔɔrie, a xa ragisee, soe ragimae, nun a xa sɔɔri birin makoto. Naxee nu biraxi Isirayilakae fɔxɔ ra baa kui, nee birin naxa lɔɛ.

sentences.english: But the children of Israel went through the sea walking on dry land, and the waters were a wall on their right side and on their left.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isirayilakae naxa baa igiri kira xaraxi xɔn ma. Ye nu malanxi e yirefanyi ma nun e kɔɔla ma.

sentences.english: So that day the Lord gave Israel salvation from the hands of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the sea's edge.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ Alatala naxa Isirayilakae ratanga Misirakae ma. Isirayilakae naxa Misirakae furee to baa dɛ ra.

sentences.english: And Israel saw the great work which the Lord had done against the Egyptians, and the fear of the Lord came on the people and they had faith in the Lord and in his servant Moses.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae to Alatala sɛnbɛ to a naxan nawalixi Misirakae xili ma, e naxa gaaxu Alatala ya ra, e fa e taxu Alatala nun a xa xɛɛra Munsa ra.

sentences.english: Then Moses and the children of Israel made this song to the Lord, and said, I will make a song to the Lord, for he is lifted up in glory: the horse and the horseman he has sent down into the sea.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi Munsa nun Isirayilakae naxa yi bɛɛti ba Alatala bɛ. «N xa yi bɛɛti ba Alatala bɛ, naxan xili gbo. A bara soe nun a ragima madula baa ma.

sentences.english: The Lord is my strength and my strong helper, he has become my salvation: he is my God and I will give him praise; my father's God and I will give him glory.
sentences.susu: N sɛnbɛ na Alatala nan na. N a matɔxɔma bɛɛti ra. A bara findi n Nakisima nun n Marigi ra. N tantui rasigama n benbae Marigi ma.

sentences.english: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.
sentences.susu: Sɛnbɛma nan Ala ra. A xili nɛ Alatala.

sentences.english: Pharaoh's war-carriages and his army he has sent down into the sea: the best of his captains have gone down into the Red Sea.
sentences.susu: A naxa Firawuna xa sɔɔrie nun e ragisee rasin baa ma. Firawuna xa kuntigie naxa madula Xulunyumi Baa ma.

sentences.english: They were covered by the deep waters: like a stone they went down under the waves.
sentences.susu: Mɔrɔnyie naxa e makoto, e naxa goro a bɔtini ma alɔ gɛmɛ.

sentences.english: Full of glory, O Lord, is the power of your right hand; by your right hand those who came against you are broken.
sentences.susu: Alatala, i sɛnbɛ magaaxu. I bara nɔ i yaxuie ra, i bara nɔ i matandimae ra.

sentences.english: When you are lifted up in power, all those who come against you are crushed: when you send out your wrath, they are burned up like dry grass.
sentences.susu: I xa mangɛya sɛnbɛ magaaxu. I bɔɲɛ na te, e ganma nɛ alɔ sɛxɛ tɛ soxi naxan na.

sentences.english: By your breath the waves were massed together, the flowing waters were lifted up like a pillar; the deep waters became solid in the heart of the sea.
sentences.susu: I xa foye naxa Xulunyumi baa rabi, kira xaraxi naxa lu a tagi. Mɔrɔnyie naxa te alɔ banxi xalɛ. Ye naxa ti, a xɔrɔxɔ.

sentences.english: Egypt said, I will go after them, I will overtake, I will make division of their goods: my desire will have its way with them; my sword will be uncovered, my hand will send destruction on them.
sentences.susu: Isirayila yaxui a fala nɛ, ‹N birama nɛ e fɔxɔ ra, han n e li, n e harige tongoma nɛ, han n wasa. N e sɔntɔma nɛ n ma santidɛgɛma ra.›

sentences.english: You sent your wind and the sea came over them: they went down like lead into the great waters.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i tan naxa foye ramini, baa naxa e radula. E naxa goro ye xɔɔra alɔ yɔxui.

sentences.english: Who is like you, O Lord, among the gods? who is like you, in holy glory, to be praised with fear, doing wonders?
sentences.susu: Alatala, i maniyɛ mu na adama xa alae ya ma. I xa sɛniyɛnyi fiixɛ, i xa nɔrɛ gbo, i xa kaabanakoe wuya. I maniyɛ na minden?

sentences.english: When your right hand was stretched out, the mouth of the earth was open for them.
sentences.susu: I to i sɛnbɛ ramini, bɔxi naxa e gerun.

sentences.english: In your mercy you went before the people whom you have made yours; guiding them in your strength to your holy place.
sentences.susu: I xa ɲama naxan xun saraxi, i fama e xun tide i xa xanunteya ra, naxan mu ɲɔnma abadan. I fama e xun tide i xa lingira sɛniyɛnxi yire i sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: Hearing of you the peoples were shaking in fear: the people of Philistia were gripped with pain.
sentences.susu: Ɲamanɛ gbɛtɛe na na mɛ, e gaaxuma nɛ. Filisitakae bɔɲɛ minima nɛ.

sentences.english: The chiefs of Edom were troubled in heart; the strong men of Moab were in the grip of fear: all the people of Canaan became like water.
sentences.susu: Edon yareratie ifuma nɛ, Mowaba mangɛe sɛrɛnma nɛ. Limaniya birin bama nɛ Kanaan ɲamanɛ yi ra.

sentences.english: Fear and grief came on them; by the strength of your arm they were turned to stone; till your people went over, O Lord, till the people went over whom you have made yours.
sentences.susu: Alatala, gaaxui nun kɔntɔfili e suxuma nɛ, e dɛ balanma nɛ i sɛnbɛ ra, han i xa ɲama dangi, i naxan xun saraxi.

sentences.english: You will take them in, planting them in the mountain of your heritage, the place, O Lord, where you have made your house, the holy place, O Lord, the building of your hands.
sentences.susu: I fama nɛ i xa ɲama rasabatide i xa geya fari, i dɛnnaxɛ sugandixi i xa lingira sɛniyɛnxi ra.

sentences.english: The Lord is King for ever and ever.
sentences.susu: Alatala xa mangɛya buma abadan.»

sentences.english: For the horses of Pharaoh, with his war-carriages and his horsemen, went into the sea, and the Lord sent the waters of the sea back over them; but the children of Israel went through the sea on dry land.
sentences.susu: Firawuna xa soe, a xa sɔɔri ragisee, nun a xa soe ragimae to goro baa ma, Alatala naxa baa radin e xun ma, kɔnɔ Isirayilakae naxa dangi kira xaraxi ra baa tagi.

sentences.english: And Miriam, the woman prophet, the sister of Aaron, took an instrument of music in her hand; and all the women went after her with music and dances.
sentences.susu: Haruna maaginɛ Mariyama, naxan findixi namiɲɔnmɛ ginɛ ra, a naxa boote maxa. Ginɛ gbɛtɛe naxa fare boron.

sentences.english: And Miriam, answering, said, Make a song to the Lord, for he is lifted up in glory; the horse and the horseman he has sent into the sea.
sentences.susu: Mariyama naxa yi bɛɛti ba, «Wo bɛɛti ba Alatala bɛ, barima a xili gbo. A bara soe nun e ragimae radula baa ma.»

sentences.english: Then Moses took Israel forward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the waste land of Shur; and for three days they were in the waste land where there was no water.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa Isirayilakae xun ti Suru gbengberenyi rakelife Xulunyumi Baa dɛ ra. E naxa e ɲɛrɛ xi saxan gbengberenyi ma, e mu ye sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And when they came to Marah, the water was no good for drinking, for the waters of Marah were bitter, which is why it was named Marah.
sentences.susu: E naxa Mara li, kɔnɔ e mu nɔ Mara ye minde barima na ye nu xɔnɔ. «Mara» wama «xɔnɛ» nan falafe.

sentences.english: And the people, crying out against Moses, said, What are we to have for drink?
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa sɔnxɔ Munsa ma, «Won ye sɔtɔma minden?»

sentences.english: And in answer to his prayer, the Lord made him see a tree, and when he put it into the water, the water was made sweet. There he gave them a law and an order, testing them;
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a dɛ rawa Alatala xɔn ma. Alatala naxa wuri mɔɔli nde masen Munsa bɛ, a fa na woli ye xɔɔra, ye xɔnɛ naxa ba. Alatala to gɛ e xaxili matode mɛnni, a naxa yi saatɛ tongo e bɛ,

sentences.english: And he said, If with all your heart you will give attention to the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is right in his eyes, giving ear to his orders and keeping his laws, I will not put on you any of the diseases which I put on the Egyptians: for I am the Lord your life-giver.
sentences.susu: «Xa wo wo tuli mati n xui ra a fanyi ra, xa wo bira n ma tinxinyi fɔxɔ ra, xa wo n ma yaamari birin suxu, wo n ma sɛriyɛ birin binya, n tan, wo Marigi Alatala, n mu fure ɲaaxi yo ragoroma wo ma, alɔ n naxan nagoro Misirakae ma. N tan nan Alatala ra, naxan wo rayalanma.»

sentences.english: And they came to Elim where there were twelve water-springs and seventy palm-trees: and they put up their tents there by the waters.
sentences.susu: E to dulonyi fu nun firin nun tugi bili tongo solofere li Elimi, e naxa yonkin mɛnni.

sentences.english: And they went on their way from Elim, and all the children of Israel came into the waste land of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they went out of the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Isirayila ɲama birin naxa keli Elimi, sigafe ra Sini gbengberenyi ma, naxan na Elimi nun Turusinina tagi. E biyaasi naxan naba keli Misira han Sini gbengberenyi ma, na naxa bu kike firin a nun xi fu nun suuli.

sentences.english: And all the children of Israel were crying out against Moses and Aaron in the waste land:
sentences.susu: Mɛnni Isirayila ɲama naxa sɔnxɔ Munsa nun Haruna ma,

sentences.english: And the children of Israel said to them, It would have been better for the Lord to have put us to death in the land of Egypt, where we were seated by the flesh-pots and had bread enough for our needs; for you have taken us out to this waste of sand, to put all this people to death through need of food.
sentences.susu: a falafe ra, «Munfe ra Alatala mu a ragirixi won xa faxa Misira bɔxi ma? Mɛnni sube nun taami nu na won yi ra naxan won lugama, kɔnɔ be yi gbengberen yire, won fama faxade kaamɛ nan na.»

sentences.english: Then the Lord said to Moses, See, I will send down bread from heaven for you; and the people will go out every day and get enough for the day's needs; so that I may put them to the test to see if they will keep my laws or not.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «N fama taami ragorode wo bɛ kelife koore ma. Ɲama xa mini, e xa a matongo gɛɛsɛgɛ e naxan donma lɔxɔɛ keren kui. N fama e xaxili matode, xa e ɲɛrɛma n ma yaamari nan ma.

sentences.english: And on the sixth day they are to make ready what they get in, and it will be twice as much as they get on the other days.
sentences.susu: A xi senni nde, e xa xi firin daaxi matongo.»

sentences.english: And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, This evening it will be clear to you that it is the Lord who has taken you out of the land of Egypt:
sentences.susu: Munsa nun Haruna naxa a fala Isirayila ɲama bɛ, «To nunmare wo a kolonma nɛ, a Alatala nan wo raminixi Misira bɔxi ra.

sentences.english: And in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord; for your angry words against the Lord have come to his ears: and what are we that you are crying out against us?
sentences.susu: Tina gɛɛsɛgɛ, wo fama Alatala xa kaabanako tode. A bara wo xa sɔnxɔɛ mɛ. Munfe ra wo wama sɔnxɔfe muxu tan ma?

sentences.english: And Moses said, The Lord will give you meat for your food at evening, and in the morning bread in full measure; for your outcry against the Lord has come to his ears: for what are we? your outcry is not against us but against the Lord.
sentences.susu: To nunmare Alatala wo kima sube ra, gɛɛsɛgɛ a wo kima taami ra, han wo luga. Wo mu sɔnxɔxi muxu tan xa ma de. Wo sɔnxɔxi Alatala nan ma, naxan bara wo xui birin mɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses said to Aaron, Say to all the people of Israel, Come near before the Lord for he has given ear to your outcry.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala Haruna bɛ, «A fala Isirayila ɲama bɛ, e xa e yɛtɛ masen Alatala bɛ, barima a bara e xa sɔnxɔɛ mɛ.»

sentences.english: And while Aaron was talking to the children of Israel, their eyes were turned in the direction of the waste land, and they saw the glory of the Lord shining in the cloud.
sentences.susu: Haruna nu wɔyɛnfe Isirayila ɲama bɛ tɛmui naxɛ, e naxa e ya rafindi gbengberenyi ma, e fa Alatala xa nɔrɛ to mini ra nuxui kui.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: The outcry of the children of Israel has come to my ears: say to them now, At nightfall you will have meat for your food, and in the morning bread in full measure; and you will see that I am the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: «N bara Isirayilakae xa sɔnxɔɛ mɛ. A fala e bɛ, ‹Nunmare wo sube donma, gɛɛsɛgɛ wo lugama taami ra. Na kui wo a kolonma nɛ, a n tan nan na wo Marigi Alatala ra.›»

sentences.english: And it came about that in the evening little birds came up and the place was covered with them: and in the morning there was dew all round about the tents.
sentences.susu: Nunmare yati xɔnie naxee xili kɔnkɔlɛe naxa radin e yonkinde birin ma. Na kuye iba xini naxa lu e yonkinde rabilinyi ma.

sentences.english: And when the dew was gone, on the face of the earth was a small round thing, like small drops of ice on the earth.
sentences.susu: Na xini to ba na, se nde naxa lu bɔxi fari alɔ balabalanyi.

sentences.english: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, What is it? for they had no idea what it was. And Moses said to them, It is the bread which the Lord has given you for your food.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae to na to, e naxa e boore maxɔrin, «Munse ya?» E mu a kolon se yo na ki. Munsa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Taami nan a ra, Alatala naxan fixi wo ma baloe ra.»

sentences.english: This is what the Lord has said, Let every man take up as much as he has need of; at the rate of one omer for every person, let every man take as much as is needed for his family.
sentences.susu: Alatala xa yaamari nan ya, «Wo xa sigaati ya solofere tongo mixi birin bɛ naxan na wo xɔnyi.»

sentences.english: And the children of Israel did so, and some took more and some less.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae a raba na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: And when it was measured, he who had taken up much had nothing over, and he who had little had enough; every man had taken what he was able to make use of.
sentences.susu: E to a maniya, naxee gbe nu gboxi, a mu dangi yɛ, naxee fan gbe nu xurunxi, a e ralixi nɛ. Kankan naxa baloe xasabi sɔtɔ naxan a ralima.

sentences.english: And Moses said to them, Let nothing be kept till the morning.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Yi baloe naxa raxi han gɛɛsɛgɛ.»

sentences.english: But they gave no attention to Moses, and some of them kept it till the morning and there were worms in it and it had an evil smell: and Moses was angry with them.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ ndee mu Munsa xui suxu, e naxa a ragata han gɛɛsɛgɛ. Kulie naxa bira a i, a xiri ɲaaxi naxa mini. Munsa naxa xɔnɔ na kanyie ma.

sentences.english: And they took it up morning by morning, every man as he had need: and when the sun was high it was gone.
sentences.susu: Gɛɛsɛgɛ yo gɛɛsɛgɛ, kankan nu fa a gbe donse matongo, kɔnɔ soge na te, a dɔnxɔɛ naxan luxi, na xunu a i.

sentences.english: And on the sixth day they took up twice as much of the bread, two omers for every person: and all the rulers of the people gave Moses word of it.
sentences.susu: A xi senni nde, e naxa xi firin daaxi matongo, sigaati ya fu nun naani mixi keren bɛ. Yareratie naxa na dɛntɛgɛ sa Munsa bɛ.

sentences.english: And he said, This is what the Lord has said, Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the Lord: what has to be cooked may be cooked; and what is over, put on one side to be kept till the morning.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Alatala naxɛ a tina malabui lɔxɔɛ nan a ra, lɔxɔɛ sɛniyɛnxi Alatala bɛ. Wo xa nde gan, wo xa nde satun. A dɔnxɔɛ naxan na lu, wo xa na ragata han tina gɛɛsɛgɛ.»

sentences.english: And they kept it till the morning as Moses had said: and no smell came from it, and it had no worms.
sentences.susu: E to nde ragata han gɛɛsɛgɛ, alɔ Munsa a yamari e bɛ ki naxɛ, e naxa a to kuli mu biraxi a i, a man mu bɔrɔ.

sentences.english: And Moses said, Make your meal today of what you have, for this day is a Sabbath to the Lord: today you will not get any in the fields.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo xa a don to, barima to nan malabui lɔxɔɛ ra Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma. Na donse mu goroma bɔxi ma to.

sentences.english: For six days you will get it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will not be any.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a matongo xi senni bun ma, kɔnɔ a xi solofere nde, wo mu sese toma, barima malabui lɔxɔɛ na a ra.»

sentences.english: But still on the seventh day some of the people went out to get it, and there was not any.
sentences.susu: A xi solofere nde, mixi ndee mini nɛ na donse matongode, kɔnɔ e mu sese to.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, How long will you go against my orders and my laws?
sentences.susu: Na kui Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Wo n ma yaamari nun n ma sɛriyɛ matandima han mun tɛmui?

sentences.english: See, because the Lord has given you the Sabbath, he gives you on the sixth day bread enough for two days; let every man keep where he is; let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a kolon, n tan Alatala nan malabui lɔxɔɛ sɛriyɛ masenxi wo bɛ. Na nan a ra, xi senni nde wo donse xi firin daaxi sɔtɔma. A solofere nde wo naxa siga dɛdɛ, wo birin xa lu wo xɔnyie, malabui lɔxɔɛ nan a ra.»

sentences.english: So the people took their rest on the seventh day.
sentences.susu: Na kui ɲama naxa e malabu na lɔxɔɛ solofere nde ma.

sentences.english: And this bread was named manna by Israel: it was white, like a grain seed, and its taste was like cakes made with honey.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae naxa na donse xili fala «mana,» naxan nu wama a falafe, «Munse a ra?» A maniya funden xɔri ra, a fiixɛ, a ɲɔxun alɔ digiyanyi.

sentences.english: And Moses said, This is the order which the Lord has given: Let one omer of it be kept for future generations, so that they may see the bread which I gave you for your food in the waste land, when I took you out from the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala, «Alatala xa yaamari nan yi ki, ‹Wo xa yi mana sigaati ya solofere ragata, alako wo bɔnsɔɛ naxee fama baride e xa donse to n naxan nagoroxi wo ma gbengberenyi ma, n to wo ramini Misira bɔxi ra.›»

sentences.english: And Moses said to Aaron, Take a pot and put one omer of manna in it, and put it away before the Lord, to be kept for future generations.
sentences.susu: Na kui Munsa naxa a fala Haruna bɛ, «I xa mana sigaati ya solofere sa sesase kui, i xa a dɔxɔ hɔrɔmɔlingira yire, alako a xa findi tɔnxuma ra wo bɔnsɔɛe bɛ naxee fama baride.»

sentences.english: So Aaron put it away in front of the holy chest to be kept, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
sentences.susu: Haruna naxa na sesase dɔxɔ Alatala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira yire saatɛ kankira ya ra, alako a xa ragata alɔ Alatala a masenxi Munsa bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And the children of Israel had manna for their food for forty years, till they came to a land with people in it, till they came to the edge of the land of Canaan.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae mana don nɛ ɲɛ tongo naani bun ma, han e sa so Kanaan bɔxi ma, si gbɛtɛe sabatixi dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
sentences.susu: Na sigaati ya solofere naxan nu rawalima na mana maniyafe ra, a dɔxɔ fu findixi busali keren nan na.

sentences.english: And the children of Israel went on from the waste land of Sin, by stages as the Lord gave them orders, and put up their tents in Rephidim: and there was no drinking-water for the people.
sentences.susu: Isirayila ɲama birin naxa keli Sini gbengberenyi ma, e fa biyaasi raba alɔ Alatala nu luma e yamari ra ki naxɛ. E to Refidimi li, e naxa yonkin naa, kɔnɔ e mu ye min daaxi sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: So the people were angry with Moses, and said, Give us water for drinking. And Moses said, Why are you angry with me? and why do you put God to the test?
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa ti Munsa kanke, e a fala a bɛ, «Ye so muxu yi ra.» Munsa naxa wɔyɛn e bɛ, «Wo tima n kanke munfe ra? Wo na Alatala matofe munfe ra?»

sentences.english: And the people were in great need of water; and they made an outcry against Moses, and said, Why have you taken us out of Egypt to send death on us and our children and our cattle through need of water?
sentences.susu: Ye xɔli nu bara gbaa ɲama ra, e nu fa a fala Munsa bɛ, «Munfe ra i muxu raminixi Misira bɔxi ra? I wama nɛ muxu xa denbaya nun muxu xa xurusee xa faxa ye xɔli ra gbengberenyi ma?»

sentences.english: And Moses, crying out to the Lord, said, What am I to do to this people? they are almost ready to put me to death by stoning.
