sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a dɛ rawa Alatala xɔn ma, a falafe ra, «N nɔma munse rabade yi ɲama ra? A gbe mu luxi e xa n faxa.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Go on before the people, and take some of the chiefs of Israel with you, and take in your hand the rod which was stretched out over the Nile, and go.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa Munsa yaabi, «I xa dangi ɲama ya ra, a nun Isirayila fori ndee. I xa i xa yisuxuwuri tongo, i Nili xure garin naxan na, i ti e ya ra.

sentences.english: See, I will take my place before you on the rock in Horeb; and when you give the rock a blow, water will come out of it, and the people will have drink. And Moses did so before the eyes of the chiefs of Israel.
sentences.susu: N tima i ya ra, fanye sɛɛti ma, naxan na Xorebe geya yire. I xa na fanye garin. Na kui ye minima nɛ ɲama naxan minma.» Munsa naxa a raba na ki Isirayila forie ya xɔri.

sentences.english: And he gave that place the name Massah and Meribah, because the children of Israel were angry, and because they put the Lord to the test, saying, Is the Lord with us or not?
sentences.susu: A naxa na yire xili sa Masa nun Meriba, na nan na ki «matoe nun sɔnxɔɛ,» barima Isirayilakae sɔnxɔ nɛ Munsa ma mɛnni, e man naxa Alatala mato na a falafe ra, «Alatala na won tagi ba, ka a mu won tagi?»

sentences.english: Then Amalek came and made war on Israel in Rephidim.
sentences.susu: Amalɛkikae naxa fa Isirayila gerede Refidimi.

sentences.english: And Moses said to Joshua, Get together a band of men for us and go out, make war on Amalek: tomorrow I will take my place on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala Yosuwe bɛ, «Xɛmɛ ndee mayegeti, wo fa mini Amalɛkikae gerede. Tina, n tima nɛ geya fari Ala xa yisuxuwuri ra n yi.»

sentences.english: So Joshua did as Moses said to him, and went to war with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
sentences.susu: Yosuwe naxa Amalɛkikae gere alɔ Munsa a yamarixi ki naxɛ. Munsa, Haruna, nun Xuru naxa te geya fari.

sentences.english: Now while Moses' hand was lifted up, Israel was the stronger: but when he let his hand go down, Amalek became the stronger.
sentences.susu: Munsa to a bɛlɛxɛ itema, Isirayila sɛnbɛ nu gboma, kɔnɔ a to a bɛlɛxɛ igoroma, Amalɛkikae sɛnbɛ tan nu gboma.

sentences.english: But Moses' hands became tired; so they put a stone under him and he took his seat on it, Aaron and Hur supporting his hands, one on one side and one on the other; so his hands were kept up without falling till the sun went down.
sentences.susu: Munsa bɛlɛxɛe to binya a ra, e naxa gɛmɛ nde tongo a dɔxɔma naxan fari. Haruna nun Xuru naxa lu Munsa sɛɛti ma, a kɔɔla nun a yirefanyi ma, a bɛlɛxɛ ratefe ra han soge dula tɛmui.

sentences.english: And Joshua overcame Amalek and his people with the sword.
sentences.susu: Na kui Yosuwe naxa nɔ Amalɛki nun a xa sɔɔrie ra santidɛgɛma xɛɲɛnxie ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Make a record of this in a book, so that it may be kept in memory, and say it again in the ears of Joshua: that all memory of Amalek is to be completely uprooted from the earth.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Yi taruxui sɛbɛ alako ɲama xa ratu a ma. I man xa a fala Yosuwe bɛ, ‹N fama nɛ Amalɛkikae xa fe ɲɔnde yi duniɲa ma.›»

sentences.english: Then Moses put up an altar and gave it the name of Yahweh-nissi:
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa yire nde rafala sɛrɛxɛbade ra, a naxa na yire xili sa, «Alatala nan xun nakeli fima n ma,»

sentences.english: For he said, The Lord has taken his oath that there will be war with Amalek from generation to generation.
sentences.susu: barima a nu bara a xaxili ti Alatala xa mangɛya ra. Munsa naxa a a fala, «Alatala Amalɛkikae gerema nɛ abadan.»

sentences.english: Now news came to Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, of all God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, and how the Lord had taken Israel out of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Munsa bitanyi Yetiro, naxan findixi Madiyan sɛrɛxɛdubɛ ra, a naxa a mɛ Alatala naxan nabaxi Munsa nun a xa ɲama Isirayila bɛ, e raminife ra Misira bɔxi kui.

sentences.english: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after he had sent her away,
sentences.susu: Munsa nu bara a xa ginɛ Sipora nun a xa di firinyi xɛɛ Yetiro xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And her two sons, one of whom was named Gershom, for he said, I have been living in a strange land:
sentences.susu: Munsa xa di singe nu xili Gerisomi, barima na xili nu wama a falafe e gbe xui, «Xɔɲɛ nan n na yi bɔxi ma.»

sentences.english: And the name of the other was Eliezer, for he said, The God of my father was my help, and kept me safe from the sword of Pharaoh:
sentences.susu: Boore nu xili Eliyeseri, barima na xili nu wama a falafe e gbe xui, «N baba Marigi bara n mali, a bara n natanga Firawuna xa santidɛgɛma ma.»

sentences.english: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to where Moses had put up his tent in the waste land, by the mountain of God.
sentences.susu: Munsa bitanyi Yetiro naxa Munsa xa ginɛ nun na xa die xanin Munsa yire gbengberenyi ma, a nu yonkinxi dɛnnaxɛ, Ala xa geya mabiri.

sentences.english: And he said to Moses, I, your father-in-law, have come to you, with your wife and your two sons.
sentences.susu: Yetiro nu bara xɛɛra xɛɛ Munsa xɔn a falafe ra, «N tan, i bitanyi Yetiro, n na fafe i xa ginɛ nun a xa di firinyie ra.»

sentences.english: And Moses went out to his father-in-law, and went down on his face before him and gave him a kiss; and they said to one another, Are you well? and they came into the tent.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa mini a bitanyi ralande. A naxa a xinbi sin a ya ra, a man fa a sunbu. E to e boore xɛɛbu, e naxa so Munsa xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And Moses gave his father-in-law an account of all the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians because of Israel, and of all the troubles which had come on them by the way, and how the Lord had given them salvation.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa fee ya ba a bitanyi bɛ, Alatala naxan birin naba Firawuna nun Misirakae ra Isirayila xa fe ra. A naxa Isirayila xa ɲaxankatɛ birin fala a bɛ, a nun Alatala e rakisixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And Jethro was glad because the Lord had been good to Israel, freeing them from the power of the Egyptians.
sentences.susu: Yetiro naxa sɛɛwa Alatala xa hinnɛ ra a naxan masenxi Isirayila bɛ, a e bafe ra Misirakae yi ra.

sentences.english: And Jethro said, Praise be to the Lord, who has taken you out of the hand of Pharaoh and out of the hand of the Egyptians; freeing the people from the yoke of the Egyptians.
sentences.susu: Yetiro naxa a fala, «Tantui na Alatala bɛ, naxan wo ba Misirakae nun Firawuna yi ra, naxan Isirayila ɲama raminixi e xa nɔɛ bun ma!

sentences.english: Now I am certain that the Lord is greater than all gods, for he has overcome them in their pride.
sentences.susu: N bara a kolon Alatala sɛnbɛ gbo dangi adamadie xa alae mɔɔli birin na, barima a bara ɲama igoro naxan nu bara a yɛtɛ rafisa Isirayilakae bɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, made a burned offering to God: and Aaron came, with the chiefs of Israel, and had a meal with Moses' father-in-law, before God.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Munsa bitanyi Yetiro naxa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi nun sɛrɛxɛ gbɛtɛe ba Alatala bɛ. Haruna nun Isirayila fori birin naxa na sɛrɛxɛ don Munsa bitanyi yire Alatala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira kui.

sentences.english: Now on the day after, Moses took his seat to give decisions for the people: and the people were waiting before Moses from morning till evening.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, Munsa naxa a magoro, a xa kiiti sa Isirayilakae tagi. Ɲama naxa lu a yire kelife gɛɛsɛgɛ han nunmare.

sentences.english: And when Moses' father-in-law saw all he was doing, he said, What is this you are doing for the people? why are you seated here by yourself, with all the people waiting before you from morning till evening?
sentences.susu: A bitanyi to a to Munsa naxan birin nabama ɲama bɛ, a naxa a fala a bɛ, «I na munse rabafe yi ɲama bɛ? Munfe ra kiiti wali birin dɔxɔxi i keren nan xun ma kelife gɛɛsɛgɛ han nunmare?»

sentences.english: And Moses said to his father-in-law, Because the people come to me to get directions from God:
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a bitanyi yaabi, «Ɲama faxi n yire Alatala xa kiiti nan fende.

sentences.english: And if they have any question between themselves, they come to me, and I am judge between a man and his neighbour, and I give them the orders and laws of God.
sentences.susu: Galanbui na lu mixie tagi e fama n yire n xa kiiti sa Alatala xa yaamarie nun a xa sɛriyɛ ra.»

sentences.english: And Moses' father-in-law said to him, What you are doing is not good.
sentences.susu: Munsa bitanyi naxa a fala a bɛ, «A mu lanma i xa a raba na ki.»

sentences.english: Your strength and that of the people will be completely used up: this work is more than you are able to do by yourself.
sentences.susu: I nun i xa mixie, wo taganma nɛ. I keren mu nɔma yi kote xaninde.

sentences.english: Give ear now to my suggestion, and may God be with you: you are to be the people's representative before God, taking their causes to him:
sentences.susu: I xa i tuli mati n ma marasi ra. Ala xa i mali. I tan xa findi ɲama xui madangima ra Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: Teaching them his rules and his laws, guiding them in the way they have to go, and making clear to them the work they have to do.
sentences.susu: I lan nɛ i xa e xaran Alatala xa sɛriyɛ nun a xa yaamarie ra. I xa Ala xa kira masen e bɛ, e birama naxan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But for the rest, take from among the people able men, such as have the fear of God, true men hating profits wrongly made; and put such men over them, to be captains of thousands, captains of hundreds and of fifties and of tens;
sentences.susu: Mixi kɛndɛe sugandi ɲama ya ma, nɔndi falɛ naxee gaaxuma Alatala ya ra, naxee riba xɔnxi. I xa nee findi yareratie ra ɲama xun ma xunlande ki ma. Nde xa lu mixi wulu keren xun ma, boore mixi kɛmɛ xun ma, boore mixi tongo suuli xun ma, boore mixi fu xun ma.

sentences.english: And let them be judges in the causes of the people at all times: and let them put before you all important questions, but in small things let them give decisions themselves: in this way, it will be less hard for you, and they will take the weight off you.
sentences.susu: Nee xa kiiti birin sa mixie tagi, fo kiiti nde naxee xɔrɔxɔ. E xa na kiiti xɔrɔxɔɛ masen i tan bɛ. Na ki, kote mu dɔxɔma i keren xun.

sentences.english: If you do this, and God gives approval, then you will be able to go on without weariness, and all this people will go to their tents in peace.
sentences.susu: Xa i Ala xui suxuma, na rabafe nɔma findide sɔɔnɛya ra wo birin bɛ, bɔɲɛsa fa lu ɲama bɛ e xɔnyi.

sentences.english: So Moses took note of the words of his father-in-law, and did as he had said.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a bitanyi xui suxu, a birin naxa raba alɔ a falaxi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And he made selection of able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, captains of thousands, captains of hundreds and of fifties and of tens.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa mixi kɛndɛe sugandi Isirayilakae ya ma, a fa e dɔxɔ ɲama xun na xunlande ki ma, mixi wulu keren xun ma, mixi kɛmɛ xun ma, mixi tongo suuli xun ma, nun mixi fu xun ma.

sentences.english: And they were judges in the causes of the people at all times: the hard questions they put before Moses; but on every small point they gave decisions themselves.
sentences.susu: E nu kiitisa wali raba tɛmui birin, fo kiiti xɔrɔxɔɛ e nee nan masenma Munsa bɛ.

sentences.english: And Moses let his father-in-law go away, and he went back to his land.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Munsa naxa a bitanyi bɛɲin. Yetiro naxa gbilen a xa bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: In the third month after the children of Israel went out from Egypt, on the same day, they came into the waste land of Sinai.
sentences.susu: Kike saxan yati to dangi, kelife e mini Misira bɔxi ra tɛmui naxɛ, Isirayilakae naxa so Turusinina gbengberenyi ma.

sentences.english: And when they had gone away from Rephidim and had come into the waste land of Sinai, they put up their tents in the waste land before the mountain: there Israel put up its tents.
sentences.susu: E to keli Refidimi, e naxa so Turusinina gbengberenyi ma, e yonkin geya ya tagi.

sentences.english: And Moses went up to God, and the voice of the Lord came to him from the mountain, saying, Say to the family of Jacob, and give word to the children of Israel:
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa te geya fari sigafe Alatala yire. Alatala naxa a xili geya fari, a a masen a bɛ, «I xa a fala Isirayilakae Yaxuba bɔnsɔɛ bɛ,

sentences.english: You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I took you, as on eagles' wings, guiding you to myself.
sentences.susu: ‹Wo bara a to, n fe naxan nabaxi Misirakae ra. Wo bara a kolon n faxi wo ra n yire ki naxɛ. A luxi alɔ wo bakixi xɔni nan fari.

sentences.english: If now you will truly give ear to my voice and keep my agreement, you will be my special property out of all the peoples: for all the earth is mine:
sentences.susu: Xa wo n xui suxu n ma saatɛ rakamalife ra, wo fama nɛ findide n ma ɲama sugandixi ra si birin ya ma. N gbe nan duniɲa birin na,

sentences.english: And you will be a kingdom of priests to me, and a holy nation. These are the words which you are to say to the children of Israel.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ wo tan findima n ma si sɛniyɛnxi nan na, naxan sɛrɛxɛdubɛ wali rabama.› I xa na masenyi ti Isirayilakae bɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses came and sent for the chiefs of the people and put before them all these words which the Lord had given him orders to say.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa goro, a fori birin xili, a fa Alatala xa masenyi birin dɛntɛgɛ e bɛ.

sentences.english: And all the people, answering together, said, Whatever the Lord has said we will do. And Moses took back to the Lord the words of the people.
sentences.susu: Ɲama birin naxa a fala, «Muxu Alatala xui birin suxuma nɛ.» Munsa naxa ɲama xa yaabi dɛntɛgɛ Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, See, I will come to you in a thick cloud, so that what I say to you may come to the ears of the people and they may have belief in you for ever. And Moses gave the Lord word of what the people had said.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «N fama wɔyɛnde i bɛ nuxui kui ɲama ya xɔri, alako e xa lanlanteya sa i ma tɛmui birin.» Munsa naxa ɲama xa masenyi dɛntɛgɛ Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Go to the people and make them holy today and tomorrow, and let their clothing be washed.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «A fala ɲama bɛ, e xa e yɛtɛ rasɛniyɛn to nun tina. E xa e xa dugie fan xa.

sentences.english: And by the third day let them be ready: for on the third day the Lord will come down on Mount Sinai, before the eyes of all the people.
sentences.susu: E xa rɛdi tina bora ya ra, barima n fama nɛ gorode ɲama birin ya tode ra na lɔxɔɛ Turusinina geya fari.

sentences.english: And let limits be marked out for the people round the mountain, and say to them, Take care not to go up the mountain or near the sides of it: whoever puts his foot on the mountain will certainly come to his death:
sentences.susu: I xa naaninyi sa geya rabilinyi birin ma, i fa a fala ɲama bɛ, ‹Mixi yo naxa te geya fari, mixi yo naxa a makɔrɛ a ra, barima naxan yo din a ra, na kanyi faxama nɛ.›

sentences.english: He is not to be touched by a hand, but is to be stoned or have an arrow put through him; man or beast, he is to be put to death: at the long sounding of a horn they may come up to the mountain.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo bɛlɛxɛ din na kanyi ra, wo a magɔnɔ gɛmɛ ra han a faxa. Xa na mu, wo xa a masɔxɔ xalie ra. A findi daalise ra, a findi mixi ra, a lanma a xa faxa. Mixi mu lanma a xa te geya fari, fo sara xui na mini mixi sugandixi ndee fa te.»

sentences.english: Then Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and made the people holy; and their clothing was washed.
sentences.susu: Munsa to goro geya ma ɲama yire, a naxa marasɛniyɛnyi fe fala e bɛ, e xa e yɛtɛ nun e xa dugie rasɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And he said to the people, Be ready by the third day: do not come near a woman.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala ɲama bɛ, «Wo xa wo yɛtɛ yailan tina bora ya ra. Sade fe naxa lu wo tan nun wo xa ginɛe tagi.»

sentences.english: And when morning came on the third day, there were thunders and flames and a thick cloud on the mountain, and a horn sounding very loud; and all the people in the tents were shaking with fear.
sentences.susu: A xi saxan lɔxɔɛ, galanyi nun seyamakɔnyi naxa bira bɔxi ma gɛɛsɛgɛ, nuxui ifɔɔrɔxi naxa to geya ma. Sara xui naxa mini sɛnbɛ ra. Ɲama birin naxa gaaxu.

sentences.english: And Moses made the people come out of their tents and take their places before God; and they came to the foot of the mountain,
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa ɲama mati geya lanbanyi Ala xui ramɛde.

sentences.english: And all the mountain of Sinai was smoking, for the Lord had come down on it in fire: and the smoke of it went up like the smoke of a great burning; and all the mountain was shaking.
sentences.susu: Tuuri nu na Turusinina geya ma, barima Alatala nu bara goro tɛ tagi. Na tuuri nu tema nɛ, alɔ fiili na gan. Geya nu sɛrɛnma sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: And when the sound of the horn became louder and louder, Moses' words were answered by the voice of God.
sentences.susu: Sara xui nu sigama gbo ra. Na tɛmui Munsa naxa wɔyɛn, Ala naxa a yaabi.

sentences.english: Then the Lord came down on to Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and the Lord sent for Moses to come up to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa goro Turusinina geya fari, a fa Munsa xili. Munsa to te naa,

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Go down and give the people orders to keep back, for fear that a great number of them, forcing their way through to see the Lord, may come to destruction.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen a bɛ, «I xa goro, i xa a fala ɲama bɛ, e naxa wuruntun n tofe ra de, xa na mu a ra, a gbegbe faxama nɛ.

sentences.english: And let the priests who come near to the Lord make themselves holy, for fear that the Lord may come on them suddenly.
sentences.susu: Hali sɛrɛxɛdubɛ naxee e makɔrɛma n na, e xa e yɛtɛ rasɛniyɛn, alako n naxa fa e faxa.»

sentences.english: And Moses said to the Lord, The people will not be able to come up the mountain, for you gave us orders to put limits round the mountain, marking it out and making it holy.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala Alatala bɛ, «Ɲama mu nɔma tide Turusinina geya fari, barima i ɲan bara muxu yamari naaninyie xa sa geya rabilinyi ma, ɲama xa lu e xati ma.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to him, Go down, and you and Aaron may come up; but let not the priests and the people make their way through to the Lord, or he will come on them suddenly.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen a bɛ, «I xa goro sinden Haruna fɔxɔ ra. Na tɛmui wo firin xa te. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛe nun ɲama naxa te de, xa na mu a ra, e faxama nɛ.»

sentences.english: So Moses went down to the people and said this to them.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa goro ɲama yire, a fa na masenyi ti e bɛ.

sentences.english: And God said all these words:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Alatala naxa yi masenyi ti:

sentences.english: I am the Lord your God who took you out of the land of Egypt, out of the prison-house.
sentences.susu: «N tan Alatala nan wo Marigi Ala ra, naxan wo ramini Misira konyiya kui.»

sentences.english: You are to have no other gods but me.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa ala gbɛtɛe batu bafe n tan na.»

sentences.english: You are not to make an image or picture of anything in heaven or on the earth or in the waters under the earth:
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa kuye yo yailan naxan misaalixi se nde ra, naxan toma koore nun bɔxi ma, xa na mu naxan luma ye nun bɔxi bun ma.

sentences.english: You may not go down on your faces before them or give them worship: for I, the Lord your God, am a God who will not give his honour to another; and I will send punishment on the children for the wrongdoing of their fathers, to the third and fourth generation of my haters;
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo mafelen na se mɔɔlie bɛ, wo naxa e batu, barima n tan wo Marigi Alatala, n mu wama n firin nde xɔn. Naxee n xɔnma, n nee bɔnsɔɛ ratɔnma nɛ han e tolontolonyie, xa na mu a ra e tolobitɛe xa die.

sentences.english: And I will have mercy through a thousand generations on those who have love for me and keep my laws.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxee n xanuma, e bira n ma sɛriyɛ fɔxɔ ra, n hinnɛma e ra xanunteya kui abadan.»

sentences.english: You are not to make use of the name of the Lord your God for an evil purpose; whoever takes the Lord's name on his lips for an evil purpose will be judged a sinner by the Lord
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa n xili yelefu, barima n tan Alatala mu diɲɛma mixie ma, naxee na fe mɔɔli rabama.»

sentences.english: Keep in memory the Sabbath and let it be a holy day.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa ratu malabui lɔxɔɛ ma, wo xa a binya.

sentences.english: On six days do all your work:
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma wali birin nabade xi senni bun ma,

sentences.english: But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God; on that day you are to do no work, you or your son or your daughter, your man-servant or your woman-servant, your cattle or the man from a strange country who is living among you:
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ na xi solofere nde findima malabui lɔxɔɛ ra wo Marigi Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma. Wo naxa wali yo raba na lɔxɔɛ, wo tan, wo xa die, wo xa konyie, wo xa xurusee, nun wo xa xɔɲɛe.

sentences.english: For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and the sea, and everything in them, and he took his rest on the seventh day: for this reason the Lord has given his blessing to the seventh day and made it holy.
sentences.susu: Alatala duniɲa nun se birin daa xi senni nan bun ma. A to gɛ na ra a naxa a malabu a xi solofere nde. Na nan a xɛɛxi, Alatala naxa barakɛ sa na malabui lɔxɔɛ ma, a findi lɔxɔɛ sɛniyɛnxi ra.»

sentences.english: Give honour to your father and to your mother, so that your life may be long in the land which the Lord your God is giving you.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa wo baba nun wo nga binya. Na kui wo xa simaya xɔn kuyama nɛ bɔxi ma, wo Marigi Alatala naxan fima wo ma.»

sentences.english: Do not put anyone to death without cause.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa mixi faxa.»

sentences.english: Do not be false to the married relation.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa yɛnɛ raba.»

sentences.english: Do not take the property of another.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa muɲɛ ti.»

sentences.english: Do not give false witness against your neighbour.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa wo boore tɔɔɲɛgɛ.»

sentences.english: Let not your desire be turned to your neighbour's house, or his wife or his man-servant or his woman-servant or his ox or his ass or anything which is his.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa mila wo boore xa harige ma, alɔ a xa banxi, a xa ginɛ, a xa konyie, a xa ninge, xa na mu a xa sofale.»

sentences.english: And all the people were watching the thunderings and the flames and the sound of the horn and the mountain smoking; and when they saw it, they kept far off, shaking with fear.
sentences.susu: Ɲama to na galanyi, seyamakɔnyi, nun tuuri to geya fari, e fa sara xui mɛ, e naxa sɛrɛn gaaxui ra. E naxa makuya mɛnni ra,

sentences.english: And they said to Moses, To your words we will give ear, but let not the voice of God come to our ears, for fear death may come on us.
sentences.susu: e fa a fala Munsa bɛ, «I tan xa wɔyɛn muxu ra, Alatala xui won faxama nɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses said to the people, Have no fear: for God has come to put you to the test, so that fearing him you may be kept from sin.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala ɲama bɛ, «Hali wo mu gaaxu. Ala na wo matofe, alako wo xa gaaxu a ya ra, wo xa yunubi lu na.»

sentences.english: And the people kept their places far off, but Moses went near to the dark cloud where God was.
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa lu yire makuye, kɔnɔ Munsa tan naxa siga na nuxui fɔɔrɔxi yire Alatala nu na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Say to the children of Israel, You yourselves have seen that my voice has come to you from heaven
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «I xa yi masenyi ti Isirayilakae bɛ, ‹Wo bara a to, n bara wɔyɛn wo ra kelife koore ma.

sentences.english: Gods of silver and gods of gold you are not to make for yourselves.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa kuye yo yailan gbeti nun xɛɛma ra naxan luma n sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: Make for me an altar of earth, offering on it your burned offerings and your peace-offerings, your sheep and your oxen: in every place where I have put the memory of my name, I will come to you and give you my blessing.
sentences.susu: Wo xa sɛrɛxɛbade yailan n bɛ bɛndɛ ra. Wo xa xurusee ba sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi nun xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ ra. Wo na n xili binya, n barakɛ sama nɛ wo ma.

sentences.english: And if you make me an altar of stone do not make it of cut stones: for the touch of an instrument will make it unclean.
sentences.susu: Xa wo sa sɛrɛxɛbade tima n bɛ gɛmɛ ra, wo naxa a ti gɛmɛ masolixie ra, barima na a niyama nɛ a xa findi se sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: And do not go up by steps to my altar, for fear that your bodies may be seen uncovered.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa n ma sɛrɛxɛbade ite, xa na mu a ra sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa donma kuye bunyi mabama nɛ.›»

sentences.english: Now these are the laws which you are to put before them.
sentences.susu: I xa yi yaamarie masen Isirayilakae bɛ.

sentences.english: If you get a Hebrew servant for money, he is to be your servant for six years, and in the seventh year you are to let him go free without payment.
sentences.susu: Xa wo konyi sara naxan findi Isirayilaka ra, a xa wali wo bɛ ɲɛ senni, kɔnɔ a solofere nde wo xa a bɛɲin barima a xunsare bara ɲɔn.

sentences.english: If he comes to you by himself, let him go away by himself: if he is married, let his wife go away with him.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li wo nu bara na konyi nun a xa ginɛ sara, wo xa e firin birin bɛɲin ɲɛ solofere nde.

sentences.english: If his master gives him a wife, and he gets sons or daughters by her, the wife and her children will be the property of the master, and the servant is to go away by himself.
sentences.susu: Xa konyi kanyi nan ginɛ so a xa konyi yi ra, a fa di bari, na ginɛ nun a xa die luma konyi kanyi yi ra. Xɛmɛ gbansan nan bɛɲinma.

sentences.english: But if the servant says clearly, My master and my wife and children are dear to me; I have no desire to be free:
sentences.susu: Xa na konyi fa a fala, «N marigi, n ma ginɛ, nun n ma die rafan n ma, n mu wama xɔrɛyafe,»

sentences.english: Then his master is to take him to the gods of the house, and at the door, or at its framework, he is to make a hole in his ear with a sharp-pointed instrument; and he will be his servant for ever.
sentences.susu: a marigi xa a dɛntɛgɛ Ala bɛ. Na tɛmui a xa a tuli tunba sɔxɔmɛ ra naadɛ wuri ma. Na nan a masenma na konyi bara lu a marigi xa yaamari bun ma a xa duniɲɛigiri birin kui.

sentences.english: And if a man gives his daughter for a price to be a servant, she is not to go away free as the men-servants do.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ na a xa di ginɛ mati konyi ra, ginɛ xɔrɛya ki mu luma alɔ xɛmɛ xɔrɛya ki.

sentences.english: If she is not pleasing to her master who has taken her for himself, let a payment be made for her so that she may go free; her master has no power to get a price for her and send her to a strange land, because he has been false to her.
sentences.susu: Xa na ginɛ mu rafan a marigi ma, naxan nu wama a findife a xa ginɛ ra, a lanma a xa lu a xun xa sara. A mu daxa a xa a mati mixi gbɛtɛ ma, barima a bara mɛɛ a ra.

sentences.english: And if he gives her to his son, he is to do everything for her as if she was his daughter.
sentences.susu: Xa a wama a fife a xa di ma ginɛ ra, a lanma a xa a suxu alɔ a xa di ginɛ yati.

sentences.english: And if he takes another woman, her food and clothing and her married rights are not to be less.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa ginɛ gbɛtɛ tongo, a naxa sese ba a xa ginɛ singe xa donse, a xa sosee, nun a xa sɔlɛ ra.

sentences.english: And if he does not do these three things for her, she has the right to go free without payment.
sentences.susu: Xa a mu na fe saxanyie rakamali a bɛ, ginɛ nɔma kelide a xɔn ma, a mu sese fi.

sentences.english: He who gives a man a death-blow is himself to be put to death.
sentences.susu: Naxan na mixi bɔnbɔ han a naxa faxa, na kanyi lan a fan xa faxa.

sentences.english: But if he had no evil purpose against him, and God gave him into his hand, I will give you a place to which he may go in flight.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a mu a faxafe ɲanigexi, Ala nan tun a ragirixi, a xa a xun taxu yire nde n dɛnnaxɛ masenma wo bɛ.

sentences.english: But if a man makes an attack on his neighbour on purpose, to put him to death by deceit, you are to take him from my altar and put him to death.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a nu a faxafe ɲanigexi nɛ kɔɔta nde ra, na kanyi mu nɔma a xun taxude n ma sɛrɛxɛbade ra. Wo xa a faxa.

sentences.english: Any man who gives a blow to his father or his mother is certainly to be put to death.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a nga, xa na mu a baba bɔnbɔ, na lan nɛ a xa faxa.

sentences.english: Any man who gets another into his power in order to get a price for him is to be put to death, if you take him in the act.
sentences.susu: Naxan na adamadi suxu, a xa a mati, na kanyi xa faxa hali a mu gɛxi na adamadi matide.

sentences.english: Any man cursing his father or his mother is to be put to death.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a nga, xa na mu a baba danka, na kanyi lan nɛ a xa faxa.

sentences.english: If, in a fight, one man gives another a blow with a stone, or with the shut hand, not causing his death, but making him keep in bed;
sentences.susu: Naxan na mixi maxɔnɔ gere kui, na kanyi mu suxuma xa mixi maxɔnɔxi mu faxaxi,

sentences.english: If he is able to get up again and go about with a stick, the other will be let off; only he will have to give him payment for the loss of his time, and see that he is cared for till he is well.
sentences.susu: xa a nɔma kelide a xa sade ma, a ɲɛrɛ a xa yisuxuwuri ra. Kɔnɔ maxɔnɛ ti tan lanma a xa kɔbiri ba na mixi maxɔnɔxi bɛ han a gɛma yalande tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: If a man gives his man-servant or his woman-servant blows with a rod, causing death, he is certainly to undergo punishment.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a xa konyi faxa bɔnbɔ wuri ra, a lanma nɛ na kanyi xa ɲaxankata.

sentences.english: But, at the same time, if the servant goes on living for a day or two, the master is not to get punishment, for the servant is his property.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa na konyi sa yalan beenu xi firin, a mu lanma konyi kanyi xa ɲaxankata, barima na konyi findixi a gbe nan na.

sentences.english: If men, while fighting, do damage to a woman with child, causing the loss of the child, but no other evil comes to her, the man will have to make payment up to the amount fixed by her husband, in agreement with the decision of the judges.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxee bɔnbɔma furi ginɛ nde ra, e xa gere kui, na fa a niya ginɛ xa di bari a waxati mu a lixi, kɔnɔ a mu fe kana a ma, na geresoee xa kɔbiri nde ba ginɛ bɛ. Ginɛ xa mɔri nun kiitisa xa natɛ tongo kɔbiri xasabi naxan bama.

sentences.english: But if damage comes to her, let life be given in payment for life,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa findi gbaloe ra, nii ɲɔxɔɛ na nii nan na,

sentences.english: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
sentences.susu: ya ɲɔxɔɛ na ya nan na, ɲinyi ɲɔxɔɛ na ɲinyi nan na, bɛlɛxɛ ɲɔxɔɛ na bɛlɛxɛ nan na, sanyi ɲɔxɔɛ na sanyi nan na,

sentences.english: Burning for burning, wound for wound, blow for blow.
sentences.susu: ganyi ɲɔxɔɛ na ganyi nan na, xabɛ ɲɔxɔɛ na xabɛ nan na, maxɔnɛ ɲɔxɔɛ na maxɔnɛ nan na.

sentences.english: If a man gives his man-servant or his woman-servant a blow in the eye, causing its destruction, he is to let him go free on account of the damage to his eye.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a xa konyi bɔnbɔ han a ya naxa kana, a lanma a xa a xa konyi xɔrɛya a xa ya kanɛ ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: Or if the loss of a tooth is caused by his blow, he will let him go free on account of his tooth.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a xa konyi ɲinyi gira, na kanyi lanma a xa a xa konyi xɔrɛya a xa ɲinyi girɛ ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: If an ox comes to be the cause of death to a man or a woman, the ox is to be stoned, and its flesh may not be used for food; but the owner will not be judged responsible.
sentences.susu: Tuura naxan na mixi faxa, a lanma na tuura xa magɔnɔ han a faxa. A sube naxa don. Tuura kanyi mu ɲaxankatɛ yo sɔtɔma na kui.

sentences.english: But if the ox has frequently done such damage in the past, and the owner has had word of it and has not kept it under control, so that it has been the cause of the death of a man or woman, not only is the ox to be stoned, but its owner is to be put to death.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa na tuura darixi na mɔɔli raba ra, a kanyi a kolon kɔnɔ a mu a xirima a fanyi ra, na kanyi yo, a xa tuura yo, e birin xa magɔnɔ han e xa faxa.

sentences.english: If a price is put on his life, let him make payment of whatever price is fixed.
sentences.susu: Kiitisa nɔma natɛ tongode na tuura kanyi xun sarama naxan na.

sentences.english: If the death of a son or of a daughter has been caused, the punishment is to be in agreement with this rule.
sentences.susu: Na sɛriyɛ keren nan nawalima hali tuura sa dimɛdi nan faxa.

sentences.english: If the death of a man-servant or of a woman-servant is caused by the ox, the owner is to give their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox is to be stoned.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li tuura fa mixi gbɛtɛ xa konyi nde faxa, gbeti kole tongo saxan nan fima na konyi marigi ma. Na tuura xa magɔnɔ han a faxa.

sentences.english: If a man makes a hole in the earth without covering it up, and an ox or an ass dropping into it comes to its death;
sentences.susu: Naxan na yili ge, a lu i mu a dɛ rakotoma, xa a sa li ninge xa na mu a ra sofale nde sa sin na yili kui,

sentences.english: The owner of the hole is responsible; he will have to make payment to their owner, but the dead beast will be his.
sentences.susu: a lanma na kanyi xa na xuruse sare fi, xuruse faxaxi xa lu a bɛ.

sentences.english: And if one man's ox does damage to another man's ox, causing its death, then the living ox is to be exchanged for money, and division made of the price of it, and of the price of the dead one.
sentences.susu: Naxan ma tuura na sa a boore gbe faxa, na tuura baloxi xa mati, na sare nun na tuura faxaxi xa itaxun e boore tagi.

sentences.english: But if it is common knowledge that the ox has frequently done such damage in the past, and its owner has not kept it under control, he will have to give ox for ox; and the dead beast will be his.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa a li, na tuura darixi na mɔɔli raba ra, a kanyi a kolon kɔnɔ a mu a xirima a fanyi ra, a lanma tuura baloxi kanyi xa a gbe fi tuura faxaxi kanyi ma, tuura faxaxi xa lu a tan bɛ.

sentences.english: If a man takes without right another man's ox or his sheep, and puts it to death or gets a price for it, he is to give five oxen for an ox, or four sheep for a sheep, in payment: the thief will have to make payment for what he has taken; if he has no money, he himself will have to be exchanged for money, so that payment may be made.
sentences.susu: Xa wo mixi suxu a muɲɛ tife kɔɛ ra, a fa faxa wo yi bɔnbɔɛ ra, faxɛ kote mu dɔxɔma wo xun ma.

sentences.english: If a thief is taken in the act of forcing his way into a house, and his death is caused by a blow, the owner of the house is not responsible for his blood.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa wo na mɔɔli raba yanyi ra, faxɛ kote dɔxɔma nɛ wo xun ma. Muɲɛti lanma a xa se muɲaxie sare ragbilen, kɔnɔ xa a mu nɔma na ra, a gundi xa mati konyi ra alako muɲɛ se sare xa fi.

sentences.english: But if it is after dawn, he will be responsible.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li, na se muɲaxi na a yi alɔ ninge, sofale, yɛxɛɛ, xa na mu a ra, a ɲiɲɛ ra, a e ɲɔndɔn firin nan fima a ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: If he still has what he had taken, whatever it is, ox or ass or sheep, he is to give twice its value.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a xa xurusee bɛɲin, a sa a boore xa xɛ kana, na kanyi lanma a xa a sare fi a xa xɛ bogi fanyi nan na.

sentences.english: If a man makes a fire in a field or a vine-garden, and lets the fire do damage to another man's field, he is to give of the best produce of his field or his vine-garden to make up for it.
sentences.susu: Naxan na tɛ sa ɲooge ganfe ra, kɔnɔ tɛ fa mixi nde xa sansi malanxi gan, xa na mu a xa xɛ, na kanyi lanma a xa na se birin sare fi.

sentences.english: If there is a fire and the flames get to the thorns at the edge of the field, causing destruction of the cut grain or of the living grain, or of the field, he who made the fire will have to make up for the damage.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi harige nde taxu a dɔxɔboore ra, kɔnɔ mixi fa na muɲa, na muɲɛti xa na se sare firin nagbilen a ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: If a man puts money or goods in the care of his neighbour to keep for him, and it is taken from the man's house, if they get the thief, he will have to make payment of twice the value.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa na muɲɛti mu to, se taxuxi naxan na, na xa a kali Ala xili ra kiitisamae yire, alako e xa a kolon a tan xa mu na harige tongoxi.

sentences.english: If they do not get the thief, let the master of the house come before the judges and take an oath that he has not put his hand on his neighbour's goods.
sentences.susu: Xa se nde sa lu mixi yi ra alɔ ninge, sofale, yɛxɛɛ, dugi, xa na mu a ra se gbɛtɛ, kɔnɔ mixi gbɛtɛ fa a fala a tan nan gbe na a ra, e lanma e xa siga kiitisae yire. Kiiti kanama naxan na, a xa na se sare dɔxɔ firin nagbilen a boore ma.

sentences.english: In any question about an ox or an ass or a sheep or clothing, or about the loss of any property which anyone says is his, let the two sides put their cause before God; and he who is judged to be in the wrong is to make payment to his neighbour of twice the value.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde xuruse taxu a boore ra, alɔ sofale, ninge, xa na mu yɛxɛɛ, na xuruse fa faxa, xa na mu a salonse nde fa gira, xa na mu mixi fa a muɲa,

sentences.english: If a man puts an ass or an ox or a sheep or any beast into the keeping of his neighbour, and it comes to death or is damaged or is taken away, without any person seeing it:
sentences.susu: a boore xa a kali Alatala ra a mu a yi. Se kanyi xa la na ra, a xa diɲɛ na se lɔɛxi ma.

sentences.english: If he takes his oath before the Lord that he has not put his hand to his neighbour's goods, the owner is to take his word for it and he will not have to make payment for it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa na xuruse muɲaxi na a xɔnyi nɛ, a ɲɔxɔɛ fima nɛ.

sentences.english: But if it is taken from him by a thief, he is to make up for the loss of it to its owner.
sentences.susu: Xa wulai sube nde nan fa a faxa, a taxu naxan na, na xa a binbi masen xuruse kanyi bɛ seedeɲɔxɔya ra. Na tɛmui, a mu na ɲɔxɔɛ fima.

sentences.english: But if it has been damaged by a beast, and he is able to make this clear, he will not have to make payment for what was damaged.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi xuruse yefu a boore ma, xuruse fa a yɛtɛ maxɔnɔ, xa na mu a ra a faxa xuruse kanyi xanbi, a yefuma xa a ɲɔxɔɛ fi.

sentences.english: If a man gets from his neighbour the use of one of his beasts, and it is damaged or put to death when the owner is not with it, he will certainly have to make payment for the loss.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa fe nde na xuruse sɔtɔ a kanyi ya xɔri, a yefuma mu a ɲɔxɔɛ fima. Xa a sa li, a hɛrixi nan a ra, hɛri masundi nan findima a ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: If the owner is with it, he will not have to make payment: if he gave money for the use of it, the loss is covered by the payment.
sentences.susu: Naxan na ginɛ dimɛdi futi kana naxan xa kote mu dɔxɔxi sinden, a lanma a xa a xa kote dɔxɔ alako a xa findi a xa ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: If a man takes a virgin, who has not given her word to another man, and has connection with her, he will have to give a bride-price for her to be his wife.
sentences.susu: Xa na ginɛ baba mu tin a fide a ma, na futikanɛ kɔbiri nan fima naxan lanma ginɛ dimɛdi xa kote ma.

sentences.english: If her father will not give her to him on any account, he will have to give the regular payment for virgins.
sentences.susu: Mandurula ginɛ lanma nɛ a xa faxa.

sentences.english: Any woman using unnatural powers or secret arts is to be put to death.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo yɛnɛ raba xuruse ra, a lanma a xa faxa.

sentences.english: Any man who has sex connection with a beast is to be put to death.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo na sɛrɛxɛ ba ala gbɛtɛ bɛ, bafe Alatala ra, na kanyi lan nɛ a xa faxa.

sentences.english: Complete destruction will come on any man who makes offerings to any other god but the Lord.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa xɔɲɛ tɔɔrɔ naxan fatan si gbɛtɛ ra a sabati wo xɔnyi, barima wo fan nu na xɔɲɛya nɛ Misira bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: Do no wrong to a man from a strange country, and do not be hard on him; for you yourselves were living in a strange country, in the land of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa fu kaaɲɛ ginɛ nun kiridi ma.

sentences.english: Do no wrong to a widow, or to a child whose father is dead.
sentences.susu: Wo na fu nee ma, n e wa xui mɛma nɛ.

sentences.english: If you are cruel to them in any way, and their cry comes up to me, I will certainly give ear;
sentences.susu: N ma xɔnɛ tema nɛ wo xili ma, n wo faxa santidɛgɛma ra. Wo xa ginɛe findima nɛ kaaɲɛ ginɛe ra, wo xa die fan findima nɛ kiridie ra.

sentences.english: And in the heat of my wrath I will put you to death with the sword, so that your wives will be widows and your children without fathers.
sentences.susu: Xa wo sa kɔbiri doni tɔɔrɔmixi nde bɛ n ma ɲama ya ma, wo naxa geeni yo fen a xun na alɔ doniti ɲaaxi ndee.

sentences.english: If you let any of the poor among my people have the use of your money, do not be a hard creditor to him, and do not take interest.
sentences.susu: Wo na wo boore xa dugi dɔxɔ sɛɛkɛ ra, wo xa a ragbilen a ma beenun soge xa dula,

sentences.english: If ever you take your neighbour's clothing in exchange for the use of your money, let him have it back before the sun goes down:
sentences.susu: barima na keren peti nan a yi ra, a na nan felenma a ma. A na n xili, n a xui suxuma nɛ, barima kinikininte nan n na.

sentences.english: For it is the only thing he has for covering his skin; what is he to go to sleep in? and when his cry comes up to me, I will give ear, for my mercy is great.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa n tan Ala bɛxu. Wo naxa wo xa ɲama mangɛ danka.

sentences.english: You may not say evil of the judges, or put a curse on the ruler of your people.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa dugundi n kide wo xa xɛ bogie ra. Wo xa wo xa di singe birin fi n ma.

sentences.english: Do not keep back your offerings from the wealth of your grain and your vines. The first of your sons you are to give to me.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo xa xurusee xa di singee fi n ma. Wo xa e lu e nga fɔxɔ ra xi solofere. A xi solomasaxan nde, wo fa e fi n ma.

sentences.english: In the same way with your oxen and your sheep: for seven days let the young one be with its mother; on the eighth day give it to me.
sentences.susu: Wo xa findi n ma ɲama sɛniyɛnxi ra. Wo naxa wulai sube don, sube gbɛtɛ naxan faxaxi. Wo xa na mɔɔli fi baree ma.

sentences.english: Do not let a false statement go further; do not make an agreement with evil-doers to be a false witness.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa mixi tɔɔɲɛgɛ, wo naxa wule seede ba mixi ɲaaxi bɛ.

sentences.english: Do not be moved to do wrong by the general opinion, or give the support of your words to a wrong decision:
sentences.susu: Wo naxa bira ɲama waxɔnfe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra, wo naxa wule seede ba ɲama xa fe ra. Na mɔɔli tinxinyi kanama nɛ.

sentences.english: But, on the other hand, do not be turned from what is right in order to give support to a poor man's cause.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa mixi rafisa a boore bɛ kiiti kui, hali a findi misikiinɛ ra.

sentences.english: If you come across the ox or the ass of one who is no friend to you wandering from its way, you are to take it back to him.
sentences.susu: Wo na wo yaxui xa ninge lɔɛxi to, xa na mu a xa sofale, wo xa a xanin a xɔn ma.

sentences.english: If you see the ass of one who has no love for you bent down to the earth under the weight which is put on it, you are to come to its help, even against your desire.
sentences.susu: Wo na wo yaxui xa sofale to, a biraxi kote xungbe bun ma, wo naxa a lu naa. Wo xa a mali.

sentences.english: Let no wrong decisions be given in the poor man's cause.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa sɛriyɛ matandi tɔɔrɔmixi makiitima tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: Keep yourselves far from any false business; never let the upright or him who has done no wrong be put to death: for I will make the evil-doer responsible for his sin.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa mixi tɔɔɲɛgɛ. Wo naxa a niya mixi tɔɔɲɛgɛxi xa faxa, barima n mu diɲɛma na mixi mɔɔli ma.

sentences.english: Take no rewards in a cause: for rewards make blind those who have eyes to see, and make the decisions of the upright false.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa tinxinyi kana kɔbiri ra, barima na a niyama nɛ seede xa dundu, tinxintɔɛ xa wɔyɛnyi xa mafindi.

sentences.english: Do not be hard on the man from a strange country who is living among you; for you have had experience of the feelings of one who is far from the land of his birth, because you yourselves were living in Egypt, in a strange land.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa xɔɲɛ tɔɔrɔ naxan fatan si gbɛtɛ ra. Wo tan yati bara na tɔɔrɛ mɔɔli kolon wo nu na Misira bɔxi ma tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: For six years put seed into your fields and get in the increase;
sentences.susu: Wo xa sansi si, wo xa a xaba ɲɛ senni bun ma,

sentences.english: But in the seventh year let the land have a rest and be unplanted; so that the poor may have food from it: and let the beasts of the field take the rest. Do the same with your vine-gardens and your olive-trees.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ a ɲɛ solofere nde, wo xa bɔxi lu na, a xa a malabu. Na tɛmui sansi naxan fama bulade a yɛtɛ ma, na nɔma findide Isirayila tɔɔrɔmixie xa baloe ra. Burunyi subee fan xa balo na dɔnxɔɛ ra. Wo xa na raba wo xa wɛni nun wo xa oliwi bilie fan na.

sentences.english: For six days do your work, and on the seventh day keep the Sabbath; so that your ox and your ass may have rest, together with the son of your servant and the man from a strange land living among you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wali birin naba xi senni bun ma, kɔnɔ a xi solofere nde wo naxa wali yo raba alako wo xa ninge, wo xa sofale, wo xa konyi, nun si gbɛtɛ mixi naxee na wo xɔnyi, e birin xa e malabu.

sentences.english: Take note of all these things which I have said to you, and let not the names of other gods come into your minds or from your lips.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo ɲɔxɔ sa n ma yaamari birin xɔn ma. Wo naxa ala gbɛtɛe batu, e xili ɲan naxa mini wo dɛ i.

sentences.english: Three times in the year you are to keep a feast to me.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛ yo ɲɛ wo xa sali saxan naba n ma binyɛ bun ma.

sentences.english: You are to keep the feast of unleavened bread; for seven days let your bread be without leaven, as I gave you orders, at the regular time in the month Abib (for in it you came out of Egypt); and let no one come before me without an offering:
sentences.susu: Wo xa Taami Lɛbinitare Sali raba yi ki. Xi solofere naxee sugandixi Abibi kike kui, wo xa taami lɛbinitare gbansan don, alɔ n wo yamarixi ki naxɛ. Wo xa a raba na tɛmui nɛ barima wo mini Misira bɔxi kui na kike nan na. Wo naxa n kuma na salie kui.

sentences.english: And the feast of the grain-cutting, the first-fruits of your planted fields: and the feast at the start of the year, when you have got in all the fruit from your fields.
sentences.susu: Xɛ Xabɛ Sali, wo xa a raba wo xa sansi bogi singee ra. Sansi Bogi Ba Sali, wo xa a raba ɲɛ raɲɔnyi, wo na sansi bogi se raso tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: Three times in the year let all your males come before the Lord God.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ birin xa na sali saxan naba e Marigi Alatala xa binyɛ bun ma ɲɛ birin kui.

sentences.english: Do not give the blood of my offering with leavened bread; and do not let the fat of my feast be kept all night till the morning.
sentences.susu: Wo na xuruse ba sɛrɛxɛ ra n bɛ tɛmui naxɛ, wo naxa taami lɛbini daaxi ba sɛrɛxɛ ra a sɛɛti ma de. Wo naxa n ma sali sɛrɛxɛ sube ture ragata han gɛɛsɛgɛ.

sentences.english: The best of the first-fruits of your land are to be taken into the house of the Lord your God. The young goat is not to be cooked in its mother's milk.
sentences.susu: Wo xa sansi bogi fisamante ba wo xa sansi bogi singee ya ma n tan wo Marigi Alatala bɛ, wo e xanin n ma hɔrɔmɔlingira kui. Wo naxa si ɲin a nga xiɲɛ ye ra.

sentences.english: See, I am sending an angel before you, to keep you on your way and to be your guide into the place which I have made ready for you.
sentences.susu: N malekɛ tima nɛ wo ya ra, naxan wo makantama kira ra sigafe ra bɔxi ma n dɛnnaxɛ yailanxi wo bɛ.

sentences.english: Give attention to him and give ear to his voice; do not go against him; for your wrongdoing will not be overlooked by him, because my name is in him.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo tuli mati a ra, wo xa a xui suxu. Wo naxa a matandi. A mu diɲɛma wo xa matandi ma, barima n xili na a xun ma.

sentences.english: But if you truly give ear to his voice, and do whatever I say, then I will be against those who are against you, fighting those who are fighting you.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa wo wo tuli mati a ra, xa wo a xui birin suxu, n findima nɛ wo yaxuie yaxui ra, wo gerefae gerema ra.

sentences.english: And my angel will go before you, guiding you into the land of the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Canaanite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, and they will be cut off by my hand.
sentences.susu: N ma malekɛ wo matima Amorikae, Xitikae, Perisikae, Kanaankae, Hiwikae, nun Yebusukae xɔnyi. N fama nɛ e birin sɔntɔde.

sentences.english: Do not go down on your faces and give worship to their gods, or do as they do; but overcome them completely, and let their pillars be broken down.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa suyidi e xa alae bɛ, wo naxa e batu, wo naxa bira e fɔxɔ ra. Wo xa e xa kuyee kana, wo xa e xa gɛmɛ masolixie magira.

sentences.english: And give worship to the Lord your God, who will send his blessing on your bread and on your water; and I will take all disease away from among you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo Marigi Alatala batu. A barakɛ sama nɛ wo xa taami nun wo xa ye ma. A wo xa fure yalanma nɛ.

sentences.english: All your animals will give birth without loss, not one will be without young in all your land; I will give you a full measure of life.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ furi mu kanama wo xa bɔxi ma, ginɛ di baritare fan mu toma wo ya ma. N simaya kamalixi fima nɛ wo ma.

sentences.english: I will send my fear before you, putting to flight all the people to whom you come; all those who are against you will go in flight, turning their backs before you.
sentences.susu: N sie ragaaxuma nɛ wo ya ra n sɛnbɛ ra. N e ifuma nɛ alako e xa e gi wo ya ra.

sentences.english: I will send hornets before you, driving out the Hivite and the Canaanite and the Hittite before your face.
sentences.susu: N ɲurie rasanbama nɛ wo ya ra naxan Hiwikae, Kanaankae, nun Xitikae kerima.

sentences.english: I will not send them all out in one year, for fear that their land may become waste, and the beasts of the field be increased overmuch against you.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n mu na rabama ɲɛ keren kui, alako bɔxi naxa fa kana, wulai subee naxa fa wuya wo xili ma.

sentences.english: Little by little I will send them away before you, till your numbers are increased and you take up your heritage in the land.
sentences.susu: N nee kerima a xuri xuri nan na wo ya ra, han wo wuya, wo fa nɔɛ sɔtɔ bɔxi birin ma.

sentences.english: I will let the limits of your land be from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the waste land to the river Euphrates: for I will give the people of those lands into your power; and you will send them out before you.
sentences.susu: N wo xa naaninyi igboma nɛ keli Xulunyumi Baa ma han Baa Xungbe, kelife Turusinina gbengberenyi ma han a sa dɔxɔ Efirati xure xungbe ra. N mɛnnikae sama nɛ wo sago, alako wo xa e keri.

sentences.english: Make no agreement with them or with their gods.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa saatɛ yo tongo mɛnnikae nun e xa alae bɛ.

sentences.english: Let them not go on living in your land, or they will make you do evil against me: for if you give worship to their gods, it will certainly be a cause of sin to you.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa lu e xa sabati wo xa bɔxi ma, xa na mu a ra e a niyama nɛ wo xa gbilen n fɔxɔ ra. E xa alae findima gantanyi nan na wo bɛ.

sentences.english: And he said to Moses, Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, and Nadab and Abihu and seventy of the chiefs of Israel; and give me worship from a distance.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Te n yire be geya fari, i tan, Haruna, Nadabo, Abihu, nun Isirayila forie mixi tongo solofere. Wo xa suyidi yire naxan makuya n na.

sentences.english: And Moses only may come near to the Lord; but the others are not to come near, and the people may not come up with them.
sentences.susu: Munsa, i gbansan xa makɔrɛ n na, booree xa lu yire makuye. Ɲama fan naxa te i tan Munsa fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: Then Moses came and put before the people all the words of the Lord and his laws: and all the people, answering with one voice, said, Whatever the Lord has said we will do.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa Alatala xa masenyi nun a xa yaamari birin nadangi ɲama ma. Ɲama birin naxa a yaabi xui keren na, «Muxu Alatala xui birin suxuma nɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Moses put down in writing all the words of the Lord, and he got up early in the morning and made an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa Alatala xa masenyi birin sɛbɛ. Na kuye iba, Munsa naxa sɛrɛxɛbade ti geya bunyi, a naxa gɛmɛ tundenyi fu nun firin ti mɛnni, naxee Isirayila bɔnsɔɛ fu nun firinyi misaalixi.

sentences.english: And he sent some of the young men of the children of Israel to make burned offerings and peace-offerings of oxen to the Lord.
sentences.susu: A naxa Isirayila fonike ndee xɛɛ e xa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxie ba. E man xa tuurae ba Ala bɛ xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And Moses took half the blood and put it in basins; draining out half of the blood over the altar.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa na wuli tagi sa fɛɲɛ die kui, a naxa na dɔnxɔɛ kasan sɛrɛxɛbade ma.

sentences.english: And he took the book of the agreement, reading it in the hearing of the people: and they said, Everything which the Lord has said we will do, and we will keep his laws.
sentences.susu: A naxa saatɛ kitaabui tongo, a a xaran ɲama birin bɛ. E naxa a yaabi, «Muxu Alatala xui birin suxuma nɛ. Muxu a ratinmɛma nɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Moses took the blood and let it come on the people, and said, This blood is the sign of the agreement which the Lord has made with you in these words.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa na wuli tongo, a a kasan ɲama ma. A naxa a masen, «Saatɛ wuli nan ya. Alatala yi saatɛ nan tongoxi wo bɛ a xa masenyi fari.»

sentences.english: Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the chiefs of Israel went up:
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa te, a tan nun Haruna, Nadabo, Abihu, nun Isirayila forie, mixi tongo solofere.

sentences.english: And they saw the God of Israel; and under his feet there was, as it seemed, a jewelled floor, clear as the heavens.
sentences.susu: E naxa Isirayila Marigi Ala to. A nu tixi gɛmɛ nɔrɔxi fari.

sentences.english: And he put not his hand on the chiefs of the children of Israel: they saw God, and took food and drink.
sentences.susu: Na Isirayila kuntigie naxa Ala to, kɔnɔ a mu e ɲaxankata na ma. E birin naxa e dɛge, e naxa e min.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses, Come up to me on the mountain, and take your place there: and I will give you the stones on which I have put in writing the law and the orders, so that you may give the people knowledge of them.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ, «Te geya fari n yire, i xa fa lu be sinden. N xa gɛmɛ walaxɛe so i yi ra, n nan n ma sɛriyɛ nun n ma yaamarie sɛbɛxi naxee ma. I xa Isirayilakae xaran nee ra.»

sentences.english: Then Moses and Joshua his servant got up; and Moses went up into the mountain of God.
sentences.susu: Munsa nun a malima Yosuwe naxa te Ala xa geya ma.

sentences.english: And he said to the chiefs, Keep your places here till we come back to you: Aaron and Hur are with you; if anyone has any cause let him go to them.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala forie bɛ, «Wo xa muxu mɛmɛ be. Muxu fafe. Haruna nun Xuru xa lu wo fɛ ma be. Xa fe nde bira a i wo tagi, wo xa a masen e bɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses went up into the mountain, and it was covered by the cloud.
sentences.susu: Munsa to te geya fari, nuxui naxa dusu a xun na.

sentences.english: And the glory of the Lord was resting on Mount Sinai, and the cloud was over it for six days; and on the seventh day he said Moses' name out of the cloud.
sentences.susu: Alatala xa nɔrɛ naxa lu Turusinina geya xun na. Nuxui naxa geya makoto xi senni. A xi solofere nde, Alatala naxa Munsa xili na nuxui kui.

sentences.english: And the glory of the Lord was like a flame on the top of the mountain before the eyes of the children of Israel.
sentences.susu: Alatala xa nɔrɛ nu luxi nɛ Isirayilakae bɛ, alɔ tɛ xungbe geya fari.

sentences.english: And Moses went up the mountain, into the cloud, and was there for forty days and forty nights.
sentences.susu: Munsa to nu tema, a naxa so na nuxui kui, a naxa lu geya fari xi tongo naani kɔɛ nun yanyi.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Say to the children of Israel that they are to make me an offering; from every man who has the impulse in his heart take an offering for me.
sentences.susu: «A fala Isirayilakae bɛ, foniserelae xa yi see mɔɔli ba hadiya ra:

sentences.english: And this is the offering you are to take from them: gold and silver and brass;
sentences.susu: xɛɛma, gbeti, wure gbeeli,

sentences.english: And blue and purple and red, and the best linen, and goats' hair;
sentences.susu: gɛsɛ gɛrɛ daaxi, gɛsɛ bulu daaxi, gɛsɛ gbeeli, suwa dugi, dugi naxan sɔxɔxi si xabe ra,

sentences.english: And sheepskins coloured red, and leather, and hard wood;
sentences.susu: yɛxɛɛ kontonyi kiri naxee soxi a gbeeli ra, peremui kirie, kasiya wuri,

sentences.english: Oil for the light, spices for the sweet-smelling oil, sweet perfumes for burning;
sentences.susu: ture naxan sama lanpui kui, labundɛ naxan sama ture sɛniyɛnxi nun surayi xun ma,

sentences.english: Beryls and stones of value to be put on the ephod and on the priest's bag.
sentences.susu: a nun gɛmɛ tofanyi naxee findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa donma kuye nun donma kanke raxunma se ra.

sentences.english: And let them make me a holy place, so that I may be ever present among them.
sentences.susu: Isirayilakae xa hɔrɔmɔlingira ti n bɛ, alako n xa sabati e ya ma.

sentences.english: Make the House and everything in it from the designs which I will give you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa na lingira nun a xa yirabase birin yailan alɔ n na masenma i bɛ ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And they are to make an ark of hard wood; two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide and high.
sentences.susu: «E xa saatɛ kankira yailan kasiya wuri ra. Na kankira xa kuya nɔngɔn firin nun a tagi, a xa igbo nɔngɔn keren nun a tagi, a xa ite nɔngɔn keren nun a tagi.

sentences.english: It is to be plated inside and out with the best gold, with an edge of gold all round it
sentences.susu: I xa a kui nun a fari maso xɛɛma ra. A dɛ kiri fan xa yailan xɛɛma ra.

sentences.english: And make four rings of gold for it, to be fixed on its four feet, two rings on one side of it and two on the other.
sentences.susu: I xa a suxude digilinxi naani rafala xɛɛma ra a tunxun naanie ma, firin na sɛɛti, firin na boore sɛɛti ma.»

sentences.english: And make rods of the same wood, plating them with gold.
sentences.susu: «I xa kasiya wuri kuye firin masoli, e maso xɛɛma ra.

sentences.english: And put the rods through the rings at the sides of the ark, for lifting it.
sentences.susu: I xa e raso kankira suxude digilinxie kui, na kankira xaninma e tan nan ma.

sentences.english: The rods are to be kept in the rings, and never taken out.
sentences.susu: E naxa ramini na abadan.»

sentences.english: Inside the ark you are to put the record which I will give you.
sentences.susu: «N na saatɛ tɔnxuma so i yi ra, i xa a sa na kankira kui.

sentences.english: And you are to make a cover of the best gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
sentences.susu: I xa a dɛrakote yailan xɛɛma fanyi ra, naxan findima xunsare yire ra. A xa kuya nɔngɔn firin nun a tagi, a xa igbo nɔngɔn keren nun a tagi.

sentences.english: And at the two ends of the cover you are to make two winged ones of hammered gold,
sentences.susu: Malekɛ sawurɛ firin xa yailan xɛɛma xabuxi ra kankira dɛrakote fari.

sentences.english: One at one end and one at the other; the winged ones are to be part of the cover.
sentences.susu: Malekɛe sawurɛ nun kankira dɛrakote xa findi keren na.

sentences.english: And their wings are to be outstretched over the cover, and the winged ones are to be opposite one another, facing the cover.
sentences.susu: Na malekɛ sawurɛ firinyie xa ti e boore ya i, e gabutenyie italaxi, e xun sinxi xunsare yire.»

sentences.english: And put the cover over the ark, and in the ark the record which I will give you.
sentences.susu: «I xa na kankira dɛrakote sa a ma, naxan findixi xunsare yire ra. N na saatɛ tɔnxuma so i yi ra, i xa a sa na kankira kui.

sentences.english: And there, between the two winged ones on the cover of the ark, I will come to you, face to face, and make clear to you all the orders I have to give you for the children of Israel.
sentences.susu: N nan n yɛtɛ masenma i bɛ mɛnni nɛ, na saatɛ kankira dɛrakote fari, malekɛ sawurɛ firinyie tagi. N yaamari birin soma i yi ra mɛnni nɛ katarabi Isirayilakae ma.»

sentences.english: And you are to make a table of the same wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high,
sentences.susu: «I xa teebili nde yailan kasiya wuri ra, naxan kuya nɔngɔn firin, a igbo nɔngɔn keren, a ite nɔngɔn keren nun a tagi.

sentences.english: Plated with the best gold, with a gold edge all round it;
sentences.susu: I xa xɛɛma fanyi maso a ma, a nun a dɛ kiri ma.

sentences.english: And make a frame all round it, as wide as a man's hand, with a gold edge to the frame.
sentences.susu: Xebenyi nde xa sa na dɛ kiri bun ma naxan igbo suxui keren a nun a tagi. Xɛɛma xa sa na fan dɛ kiri ma.

sentences.english: And make four gold rings and put them at the four angles, on the four feet of the table;
sentences.susu: I xa a suxude digilinxi naani rafala xɛɛma ra a tunxun naanie ma, naxee ilanma a sanyie ra

sentences.english: The rings are to be fixed under the frame to take the rods with which the table is to be lifted.
sentences.susu: na xebenyi bun ma. Wuri kuyɛe xa so nee kui teebili xaninfe ra.

sentences.english: Make rods of the same wood, plated with gold, for lifting the table.
sentences.susu: Na wuri kuyee xa masoli kasiya wuri ra, xɛɛma xa maso e ma. Nee nan findima teebili tongose ra.

sentences.english: And make the table-vessels, the spoons and the cups and the basins for liquids, all of the best gold.
sentences.susu: Piletie, tɔnbilie, pɔɔtie, nun paani naxee sama na teebili ma, naxee rawalima sɛrɛxɛ yeerama daaxi xa fe ra, nee birin xa yailan xɛɛma fanyi nan na.

sentences.english: And on the table at all times you are to keep my holy bread.
sentences.susu: Taami fan xa sa na teebili ma tɛmui birin, naxan findixi sɛrɛxɛ ra n bɛ.»

sentences.english: And you are to make a support for lights, of the best gold; its base and its pillar are to be of hammered gold; its cups, its buds, and its flowers are to be made of the same metal.
sentences.susu: «I xa lanpui dɔxɔse nde yailan xɛɛma fanyi xabuxi ra. A sanyi, a bili, a salonyie, nun lanpui dɔxɔde naxee maniya sansi fugee ra, na birin xa findi keren na.

sentences.english: It is to have six branches coming out from its sides; three branches from one side and three from the other.
sentences.susu: Salon senni xa mini lanpui dɔxɔse bili ma, saxan sɛɛti keren, saxan boore sɛɛti.

sentences.english: Every branch having three cups made like almond flowers, every cup with a bud and a flower, on all the branches.
sentences.susu: Tɔnbili saxan xa lu na salon senni birin xun ma. E xa maniya sansi bogi ra naxan dɔxɔxi a burɛxɛe nun a fugee tagi.

sentences.english: And on the pillar, four cups like almond flowers, every one with its bud and its flower:
sentences.susu: Tɔnbili naani gbɛtɛ xa lu lanpui bili ma. E fan xa maniya sansi bogi ra naxan dɔxɔxi a burɛxɛe nun a fugee tagi.

sentences.english: And under every two branches a bud, made with the branch, for all the six branches of it.
sentences.susu: Na salon firin firin dɔxɔ saxanyie bun ma naxee kelixi a bili ma, a sama nɛ mɛnni fan ma.

sentences.english: The buds and the branches are to be made of the same metal; all together one complete work of hammered gold.
sentences.susu: Na tɔnbilie nun lanpui salonyie xa findi keren na, e xa yailan xɛɛma fanyi xabuxi ra.»

sentences.english: Then you are to make its seven vessels for the lights, putting them in their place so that they give light in front of it.
sentences.susu: «I xa lanpui solofere yailan, i xa e dɔxɔ e dɔxɔdee ma alako e dɛxɛ xa yare iyalan.

sentences.english: And the instruments and trays for use with it are all to be of the best gold.
sentences.susu: I xa wuki xabase nun xube sase yailan xɛɛma fanyi ra.

sentences.english: A talent of gold will be needed for it, with all these vessels.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛma naxan nawalima lanpui dɔxɔse nun lanpui yirabase yailanfe ra, na xa findi xɛɛma kilo tongo saxan nun naani nan na.

sentences.english: And see that you make them from the design which you saw on the mountain.
sentences.susu: I xa na birin naba alɔ n a masenxi i bɛ ki naxɛ geya fari.»

sentences.english: And you are to make a House for me, with ten curtains of the best linen, blue and purple and red, worked with designs of winged ones by a good workman.
sentences.susu: «I xa Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira yailan suwa dugi fu ra, naxee raxunmaxi gɛsɛ mɔɔli saxan na, gɛsɛ gɛrɛ daaxi, gɛsɛ bulu daaxi, nun gɛsɛ gbeeli. Na gɛsɛ xa malekɛe sawurɛ ramini dugie ma. A xa tofan ki fanyi.

sentences.english: Every curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, all of the same measure.
sentences.susu: Dugi birin xa kuya nɔngɔn mɔxɔɲɛn nun solomasaxan, a xa igbo nɔngɔn naani. E kuyɛ nun e igboya xa lan.

sentences.english: Five curtains are to be joined together, and the other five are to be joined together.
sentences.susu: Dugi suuli xa dɛgɛ e boore ra, dugi suuli gbɛtɛ fan xa dɛgɛ e boore ra. Na kui na dugi fu bara findi dugi firin na.

sentences.english: And you are to put twists of blue cord on the edge of the outside curtain of the first group of five, and on the edge of the outside curtain of the second group of five;
sentences.susu: I xa gɛsɛ gɛrɛ daaxi dɛgɛ na dugi singe dɛ kiri ma, a nun na dugi firin nde dɛ kiri ma.

sentences.english: Fifty twists on one curtain and fifty on the other, the twists to be opposite one another.
sentences.susu: I xa gɛsɛ tongo suuli dɛgɛ na firinyi dɛ kiri ma alako e birin xa lan e boore ma.

sentences.english: Then make fifty gold hooks, joining the curtains together by the hooks, and in this way the House will be made.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi i xa suxuse tongo suuli yailan xɛɛma ra, i fa na dugi firinyie ralan e boore ra na suxusee ra. Na nan a niyama hɔrɔmɔlingira xa findi dugi keren na.»

sentences.english: And you are to make curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the House, eleven curtains.
sentences.susu: «I xa dugi fu nun keren sɔxɔ si xabe ra, naxee Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira makotoma.

sentences.english: Every curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide, all of the same measure.
sentences.susu: Dugi keren xa kuya nɔngɔn tongo saxan, a xa igbo nɔngɔn naani. Na dugi fu nun kerenyi birin xa lan.

sentences.english: Five of these curtains are to be joined together, and the other six are to be joined together, the sixth being folded over to make a hanging in front of the tent.
sentences.susu: I xa dugi suuli dɛgɛ e boore ra, e xa findi dugi keren na. Na dugi senni naxee luxi, i xa e fan dɛgɛ e boore ra. Na dugi senni nde singanma banxi yatagi nan xun ma.

sentences.english: And you are to put fifty twists of cord on the edge of the outside curtain of one group, and fifty twists on the edge of the outside curtain of the other group.
sentences.susu: I xa gɛsɛ tongo suuli dɛgɛ na dugi singe ra, a nun na dugi firin nde ra.

sentences.english: Then make fifty brass hooks and put the hooks into the twists, joining the tent together to make it one.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi i xa suxuse tongo suuli yailan wure gbeeli ra, i fa na dugi firinyie ralan e boore ra na suxusee ra. Na nan a niyama na birin xa findi dugi keren na naxan Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira makotoma.

sentences.english: And the folded part which is over of the curtains of the tent, the half-curtain which is folded back, will be hanging down over the back of the House.
sentences.susu: Na dugi xa mayigboe kɛɲa ma dɔnxɔɛ tagi singanma hɔrɔmɔlingira nan xanbi ra.

sentences.english: And the cubit which is over of the ten curtains at the sides will be hanging over the two sides of the House as a cover.
sentences.susu: Na dugi xa kuyɛ kɛɲa na ki naxɛ, nɔngɔn keren nan luma na sɛɛti firinyie ma, alako hɔrɔmɔlingira xa makoto.»

sentences.english: And then you are to make a cover for the tent, of sheepskins coloured red, and a cover of leather over that.
sentences.susu: «Na dangi xanbi i xa makotose gbɛtɛ yailan yɛxɛɛ kontonyi kiri ra, naxan soxi a gbeeli ra. I man xa makotose gbɛtɛ yailan peremui kiri ra.»

sentences.english: And you are to make upright boards of hard wood for the House.
sentences.susu: «I xa kasiya wuri xaba xebenyie ra hɔrɔmɔlingira tima naxee ma.

sentences.english: Every board is to be ten cubits high and a cubit and a half wide.
sentences.susu: Kankan xa kuya nɔngɔn fu, a xa igbo nɔngɔn keren nun a tagi.

sentences.english: Every board is to be joined to the one nearest to it by two tongues, and so for every board in the House.
sentences.susu: Suxuse firin xa lu hɔrɔmɔlingira xebenyi birin ma e kafuma e boore ma naxee ra.

sentences.english: These are the boards needed for the house; twenty boards for the south side,
sentences.susu: Xebenyi mɔxɔɲɛn nan tima hɔrɔmɔlingira yirefanyi ma.

sentences.english: With forty silver bases under the twenty boards, two bases under every board to take its tongues.
sentences.susu: Sanbunyi gbeti daaxi tongo naani nan sama na xebenyi mɔxɔɲɛn bun ma, xebenyi keren, sanbunyi firin. E xa lu xebenyi suxusee fɛ ma.

sentences.english: And twenty boards for the second side of the house on the north,
sentences.susu: Xebenyi mɔxɔɲɛn nan tima hɔrɔmɔlingira kɔɔla fan ma,

sentences.english: With their forty silver bases, two under every board.
sentences.susu: a nun e sanbunyi gbeti daaxi tongo naani, xebenyi keren, sanbunyi firin.

sentences.english: And six boards for the back of the House on the west,
sentences.susu: Xebenyi senni nan tima hɔrɔmɔlingira xanbi ra sogegorode mabiri.

sentences.english: With two boards for the angles of the House at the back.
sentences.susu: I xa xebenyi firin yailan tuxuie bɛ hɔrɔmɔlingira xanbi ra,

sentences.english: The two are to be joined together at the base and at the top to one ring, forming the two angles.
sentences.susu: naxee fuge nun lanbanyi lanma e boore ma, e xiri fuge ra se digilinxi ra. Na tuxui firinyi xa yailan na ki.

sentences.english: So there are to be eight boards, with their sixteen silver bases, two bases under every board.
sentences.susu: Na birin lanma xebenyi solomasaxan nan ma, a nun e sanbunyi gbeti daaxi fu nun senni, xebenyi keren, sanbunyi firin.»

sentences.english: And make rods of the same wood, five for the boards on the one side,
sentences.susu: «I xa wuri suuli yailan kasiya wuri ra, hɔrɔmɔlingira xebenyie tima naxee ma. Suuli rawali sɛɛti keren ma,

sentences.english: And five for the boards on the other side of the House, and five for the west side of the House at the back.
sentences.susu: suuli rawali boore sɛɛti ma, suuli rawalima hɔrɔmɔlingira xanbi ra sogegorode mabiri.

sentences.english: And the middle rod is to go through the rings of all the boards from end to end.
sentences.susu: Wuri naxan luma a tagi, na dangima xebenyie nan xun ma, a keli sɛɛti singe a sa dɔxɔ boore ra.

sentences.english: And the boards are to be plated with gold, having gold rings for the rods to go through: and the rods are to be plated with gold.
sentences.susu: Na xebenyie, nun na wurie, nun se digilinxie wuri soma naxee kui, i xa xɛɛma maso na birin ma.

sentences.english: And you are to make the House from the design which you saw on the mountain.
sentences.susu: I xa na hɔrɔmɔlingira ti alɔ n i yamarixi ki naxɛ geya fari.»

sentences.english: And you are to make a veil of the best linen, blue and purple and red, worked with designs of winged ones by a good workman:
sentences.susu: «I xa suwa dugi yailan gɛsɛ gbeeli nun gɛsɛ bulu daaxi ra. Malekɛ sawurɛe xa dɛgɛ na ma, a xa tofan ki fanyi.

sentences.english: Hanging it by gold hooks from four pillars of wood, plated with gold and fixed in silver bases.
sentences.susu: I xa a gbaku kasiya wuri naani ra xɛɛma masoxi naxee ma, e tixi gbeti sanbunyie ma. Suxuse naxee dugi xirima wurie ma, xɛɛma xa maso nee fan ma.

sentences.english: And you are to put up the veil under the hooks, and put inside it the ark of the law: the veil is to be a division between the holy place and the most holy.
sentences.susu: I na gɛ dugi gbakude na suxusee ra, i xa saatɛ kankira dɔxɔ a xanbi ra. Na ki, na dugi luma na yire firin tagi ra, naxan xili yire sɛniyɛnxi a nun naxan xili yire sɛniyɛnxi fisamante.

sentences.english: You are to put the cover on the ark of the law, inside the most holy place.
sentences.susu: I xa saatɛ kankira dɛ rakoto a dɛrakote ra yire sɛniyɛnxi fisamante kui. Na dɛrakote se findixi xunsare yire nan na.

sentences.english: And outside the veil you are to put the table, and the support for the lights opposite the table on the south side of the House; and the table is to be on the north side.
sentences.susu: I xa teebili tan dɔxɔ hɔrɔmɔlingira kɔɔla ma, lanpui dɔxɔse xa lu a ya ra yirefanyi ma.»

sentences.english: And you are to make a curtain for the doorway of the Tent, of the best linen with needlework of blue and purple and red.
sentences.susu: «I xa suwa dugi gbɛtɛ yailan gɛsɛ gɛrɛ daaxi, gɛsɛ bulu daaxi, nun gɛsɛ gbeeli ra hɔrɔmɔlingira sode. I xa a masɔxɔ a fanyi ra, a xa tofan.

sentences.english: And make five pillars for the curtain, of hard wood plated with gold; their hooks are to be of gold and their bases of brass.
sentences.susu: I xa a gbaku wuri suuli ma naxee yailanxi kasiya wuri ra, xɛɛma masoxi naxee ma, e tixi gbeti sanbunyie ma. Suxuse naxee dugi xirima wurie ma, nee yailanxi wure gbeeli ra.»

sentences.english: And make an altar of hard wood, a square altar, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high.
sentences.susu: «I xa sɛrɛxɛbade yailan kasiya wuri ra, naxan kuya nɔngɔn suuli, a igbo nɔngɔn suuli, a ite nɔngɔn saxan.

sentences.english: Put horns at the four angles of it, made of the same, plating it all with brass.
sentences.susu: I xa feri naani yailan a tuxui birin ma, naxee findixi se keren na sɛrɛxɛbade ra. I xa wure gbeeli maso na birin ma.

sentences.english: And make all its vessels, the baskets for taking away the dust of the fire, the spades and basins and meat-hooks and fire-trays, of brass.
sentences.susu: I xa a yirabase birin yailan wure gbeeli ra, alɔ xube sasee, pelie, pɔɔtie, sube sɔxɔsee, nun tundee tɛ sama naxee kui.

sentences.english: And make a network of brass, with four brass rings at its four angles.
sentences.susu: I xa se nde yailan wure gbeeli ra naxan sama tɛ xun ma, sube sama naxan fari. I xa suxuse digilinxie wure gbeeli daaxi sa a tuxui ma,

sentences.english: And put the network under the shelf round the altar so that the net comes half-way up the altar.
sentences.susu: alako a xa gbaku sɛrɛxɛbade kui a tagi.

sentences.english: And make rods for the altar, of hard wood, plated with brass.
sentences.susu: I xa wuri kuyee yailan kasiya wuri ra wure gbeeli masoxi e ma.

sentences.english: And put the rods through the rings at the two opposite sides of the altar, for lifting it.
sentences.susu: E rasoma suxuse digilinxi naanie nan kui sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛti firinyie ma a xaninfe ra.

sentences.english: The altar is to be hollow, boarded in with wood; make it from the design which you saw on the mountain.
sentences.susu: I xa na sɛrɛxɛbade yailan xebenyie nan na. Sese naxa lu a kui. I xa a yailan alɔ n i yamarixi ki naxɛ geya fari.»

sentences.english: And let there be an open space round the House, with hangings for its south side of the best linen, a hundred cubits long.
sentences.susu: «I xa hɔrɔmɔlingira tɛtɛ yailan yi ki nɛ: Tɛtɛ xa kuya nɔngɔn kɛmɛ yirefanyi mabiri ra. I xa gɛrɛ suwa dugi gbaku na

sentences.english: Their twenty pillars and their twenty bases are to be of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their bands are to be of silver.
sentences.susu: wuri mɔxɔɲɛn ma, naxee tixi sanbunyi wure gbeeli daaxie ma. Na dugi suxusee xa yailan gbeti ra.

sentences.english: And on the north side in the same way, hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty pillars of brass on bases of brass; their hooks and their bands are to be of silver.
sentences.susu: Tɛtɛ xa kuya nɔngɔn kɛmɛ kɔɔla fan mabiri ra. I xa gɛrɛ dugi gbaku na wuri mɔxɔɲɛn ma, naxee tixi sanbunyi wure gbeeli daaxie ma. Na dugi suxusee xa yailan gbeti ra.

sentences.english: And for the open space on the west side, the hangings are to be fifty cubits wide, with ten pillars and ten bases;
sentences.susu: Tɛtɛ xa igbo nɔngɔn tongo suuli sogegorode mabiri ra. I xa gɛrɛ dugi gbaku na wuri fu ma, naxee tixi sanbunyi wure gbeeli daaxie ma.

sentences.english: And on the east side the space is to be fifty cubits wide.
sentences.susu: Tɛtɛ xa igbo nɔngɔn tongo suuli sogetede fan mabiri ra.

sentences.english: On the one side of the doorway will be hangings fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases;
sentences.susu: Gɛrɛ dugi xa gbaku sɛɛti ma wuri saxan ma, naxee tixi sanbunyi ma. Na xa kuya nɔngɔn fu nun suuli.

sentences.english: And on the other side, hangings fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
sentences.susu: Gɛrɛ dugi gbɛtɛ xa gbaku boore sɛɛti ma wuri saxan ma, naxee tixi sanbunyi ma. Na fan xa kuya nɔngɔn fu nun suuli.

sentences.english: And across the doorway, a veil of twenty cubits of the best linen, made of needlework of blue and purple and red, with four pillars and four bases.
