sentences.susu: A na gɛ na wali ra, a xa a xa dugi fanyi ba a ma, a xa dugi gbɛtɛ ragoro a ma, alako a xa na tɛ xube xanin ɲama yonkinde fari ma, yire sɛniyɛnxi.

sentences.english: Or anything about which he took a false oath; he will have to give it all back, with the addition of a fifth of its value, to him whose property it is, when he has been judged to be in the wrong.
sentences.susu: Tɛ naxan dɛxɛxi sɛrɛxɛbade bun ma, na naxa xuben. Gɛɛsɛgɛ birin sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa yege radɔxɔ, a xa tɛ xuru, a sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi sa na fari. A xanunteya sɛrɛxɛe ture fan ganma naa nɛ.

sentences.english: Then let him take to the Lord the offering for his wrongdoing; giving to the priest for his offering, a male sheep from the flock, without any mark, of the value fixed by you:
sentences.susu: Na tɛ dɛxɛma tɛmui birin sɛrɛxɛbade bun ma, a mu xubenma.»

sentences.english: And the priest will take away his sin from before the Lord, and he will have forgiveness for whatever crime he has done
sentences.susu: «Sɛriyɛ nan ya sansi xɔri dinxi sɛrɛxɛ xa fe ra. Haruna xa die xa fa na sɛrɛxɛ ra sɛrɛxɛbade n tan Alatala ya i.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa suxu keren kɔ sansi xɔri dinxi ra, a nun ture, a nun surayi naxan birin sama a fari, a xa na birin gan sɛrɛxɛ tɔnxuma ra sɛrɛxɛbade fari. Na xiri rafan n tan Alatala ma.

sentences.english: Give orders to Aaron and to his sons, saying, This is the law for the burned offering: the offering is to be on the fire-wood on the altar all night till the morning; and the fire of the altar is to be kept burning.
sentences.susu: Naxan luxi, Haruna nun a xa die xa na don a lɛbinitare ra, hɔrɔmɔlingira tɛtɛ sɛniyɛnxi kui.

sentences.english: And the priest is to put on his linen robes and his linen trousers, and take up what is over of the offering after it has been burned on the altar, and put it by the side of the altar.
sentences.susu: A mu lanma a xa ɲin lɛbini ra, barima a fatanxi n ma sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxie nan na naxee sɛniyɛnxi han alɔ yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ nun yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ.

sentences.english: Then having taken off his linen robes and put on other clothing, he is to take it away into a clean place, outside the tent-circle.
sentences.susu: Haruna xa di xɛmɛe nɔma na donde. Yaamari na a ra wo bɔnsɔɛ bɛ naxan mu kanama abadan. Mixi naxan birin a makɔrɛma na sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxie ra naxee bama n tan Alatala bɛ, na kanyie sɛniyɛnma nɛ.»

sentences.english: The fire on the altar is to be kept burning; it is never to go out; every morning the priest is to put wood on it, placing the burned offering in order on it, and there the fat of the peace-offering is to be burned.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Let the fire be kept burning on the altar at all times; it is never to go out.
sentences.susu: «Haruna tima sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi ra lɔxɔɛ naxɛ, a lanma a tan Haruna nun a xa die xa sansi xɔri fanyi dinxi konbo ya keren ba sɛrɛxɛ ra. Na sɛrɛxɛ tagi bama gɛɛsɛgɛ, boore tagi bama nunmare. Na mɔɔli xa raba mixi tima sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi ra tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: And this is the law for the meal offering: it is to be offered to the Lord before the altar by the sons of Aaron.
sentences.susu: Yi sansi xɔri dinxi xa gilin tunde kui, ture xa sa a ma. A na ɲɔn, a xuntunyie xa gan tɛ xɔɔra, a xa findi xiri ɲɔxunmɛ ra Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: The priest is to take in his hand some of the meal of the meal offering and of the oil of it, and all the perfume on it, burning it on the altar as a sign, for a sweet smell to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ naxan findima Haruna ɲɔxɔɛ ra xa na sɛrɛxɛ mɔɔli ba. A xa raba na ki nɛ tɛmui birin n tan Alatala ya i. Na sɛrɛxɛ birin xa gan.

sentences.english: And whatever is over Aaron and his sons may have for their food, taking it without leaven in a holy place; in the open space of the Tent of meeting they may take a meal of it.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa sɛrɛxɛ birin xa gan, e naxa na sese don.»

sentences.english: It is not to be cooked with leaven. I have given it to them as their part of the offerings made by fire to me; it is most holy, as are the sin-offerings and the offerings for error.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Every male among the children of Aaron may have it for food; it is their right for ever through all your generations, from the offerings made by fire to the Lord: anyone touching them will be holy.
sentences.susu: «Yi yaamari so Haruna nun a xa die yi ra: ‹Sɛriyɛ nan ya yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ xa fe ra. Yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ kɔn naxabama sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi kɔn naxabade nɛ, barima se sɛniyɛnxi na a ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ naxan yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ bama, a na donma n tan Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira tɛtɛ sɛniyɛnxi nan kui.

sentences.english: This is the offering which Aaron and his sons are to make to the Lord on the day when he is made a priest: the tenth part of an ephah of the best meal for a meal offering for ever; half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo dinma na sɛrɛxɛ ra, na kanyi sɛniyɛnma nɛ. Xa na wuli sa kasan dugi nde ma, na dugi xa xa yire sɛniyɛnxi.

sentences.english: Let it be made with oil on a flat plate; when it is well mixed and cooked, let it be broken and taken in as a meal offering, for a sweet smell to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Xa na sube ɲinma tunde mɔɔli nde kui naxan maniya fɛɲɛ ra, a na gɛ a ɲinde, na tunde xa kana. Xa a ɲinma tunde kui naxan yailanxi yɔxui ra, na tunde xa maxa a fanyi ra ye ra.

sentences.english: And the same offering is to be given by that one of his sons who takes his place as priest; by an order for ever, all of it is to be burned before the Lord.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ birin xa na don, barima sɛrɛxɛ sɛniyɛnxi na a ra.

sentences.english: Every meal offering offered for the priest is to be completely burned: nothing of it is to be taken for food.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi yo naxa yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ don, naxan wuli xaninma hɔrɔmɔlingira kui xunsare ra. Na sɛrɛxɛ mɔɔli xa gan tɛ ra.›»

sentences.english: And this is the law of the offering for wrongdoing: it is most holy.
sentences.susu: «Yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ sɛriyɛ nan ya: Sɛrɛxɛ sɛniyɛnxi na a ra.

sentences.english: They are to put to death the offering for wrongdoing in the same place as the burned offering; and the priest is to put the blood on and round the altar.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ kɔn naxabama sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi kɔn naxabade nɛ. A wuli xa kasan sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And all the fat of it, the fat tail and the fat covering the inside parts, is to be given as an offering.
sentences.susu: A ture birin, a xuli, a ture naxan na a furingɛ sɛɛti ma,

sentences.english: And the two kidneys, and the fat on them, which is by the top of the legs, and the fat joining the liver and the kidneys, he is to take away:
sentences.susu: a gungui firinyi, e ture, nun laare naxan na a bɔɲɛ ma, na birin xa ba sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: They are to be burned by the priest on the altar for an offering made by fire to the Lord: it is an offering for wrongdoing.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na birin gan sɛrɛxɛbade fari sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra Alatala bɛ. Yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ na a ra.

sentences.english: Every male among the priests may have it as food in a holy place: it is most holy.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ sɛrɛxɛdubɛe nan na donma yire sɛniyɛnxi kui, barima sɛrɛxɛ sɛniyɛnxi na a ra.

sentences.english: As is the sin-offering, so is the offering for wrongdoing; there is one law for them: the priest who makes the offering to take away sin, he is to have it.
sentences.susu: Yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ nun yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ, e sɛriyɛ birin keren. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ naxan na xunsare sɛrɛxɛ baxi, a tan nan na sube donma.

sentences.english: And the priest offering any man's burned offering for him, may have the skin of the burned offering which is offered by him.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi kiri fan luma sɛrɛxɛdubɛ yi ra naxan na baxi sɛrɛxɛ ra.»

sentences.english: And every meal offering which is cooked in the oven and everything made in a cooking pot or on a flat plate, is for the priest by whom it is offered.
sentences.susu: «Sansi xɔri dinxi sɛrɛxɛ naxan ganxi nun naxan gilinxi, e fan findima sɛrɛxɛdubɛ nan gbe ra, naxan e baxi sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And every meal offering, mixed with oil or dry, is for all the sons of Aaron in equal measure.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri dinxi sɛrɛxɛ naxan mu ganxi, ture gbansan nan saxi a ma, xa na mu a ra ture mu saxi a ma, nee findima Haruna xa di birin nan gbe ra.»

sentences.english: And this is the law for the peace-offerings offered to the Lord.
sentences.susu: «Xanunteya sɛrɛxɛe sɛriyɛ nan ya, naxan bama n tan Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: If any man gives his offering as a praise-offering, then let him give with the offering, unleavened cakes mixed with oil and thin unleavened cakes covered with oil and cakes of the best meal well mixed with oil.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde wama tantui sɛrɛxɛ bafe, a man xa taami lɛbinitaree yailan ture ra, a nun taami xunxurie ture saxi naxee ma, nun taami xunxuri naxee ramulanxi ture ra.

sentences.english: With his peace-offering let him give cakes of leavened bread, as a praise-offering.
sentences.susu: A na xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ bama tɛmui naxɛ, naxan findixi tantui sɛrɛxɛ ra, a xa taami fan ɲin lɛbini na naxan xun.

sentences.english: And let him give one out of every offering to be lifted up before the Lord; that it may be for the priest who puts the blood of the peace-offering on the altar.
sentences.susu: Nde xa ba na taami mɔɔli birin na, a findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ gbe ra, naxan xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ wuli kasanma sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And the flesh of the praise-offering is to be taken as food on the day when it is offered; no part of it may be kept till the morning.
sentences.susu: Na xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ sube donma a ba lɔxɔɛ nɛ, sese naxa lu han gɛɛsɛgɛ.»

sentences.english: But if his offering is made because of an oath or given freely, it may be taken as food on the day when it is offered; and the rest may be used up on the day after:
sentences.susu: «Xa laayidi sɛrɛxɛ bama, xa na mu a ra sɛrɛxɛ ɲanigexi, na sube xa don a ba lɔxɔɛ nɛ, kɔnɔ xa nde sa lu a nɔma donde gɛɛsɛgɛ fan.

sentences.english: But if any of the flesh of the offering is still unused on the third day, it is to be burned with fire.
sentences.susu: Xa a dɔnxɔɛ sa lu han na fan kuye iba, na sube xa gan gbiki na xi saxan nde lɔxɔɛ ma.

sentences.english: And if any of the flesh of the peace-offering is taken as food on the third day, it will not be pleasing to God and will not be put to the account of him who gives it; it will be unclean and a cause of sin to him who takes it as food.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde sa a yɛtɛ xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ sube don na xi saxan nde lɔxɔɛ ma, Ala mu a xa sɛrɛxɛ tongoma. A luma alɔ a mu sɛrɛxɛ yo baxi, barima na sube findixi se sɛniyɛntare nan na. Mixi naxan na rabama, a yunubi sɔtɔma na kui.»

sentences.english: And flesh touched by any unclean thing may not be taken for food: it is to be burned with fire; and as for the flesh of the peace-offerings, everyone who is clean may take it as food:
sentences.susu: «Sɛrɛxɛ sube naxan dinma se sɛniyɛntare ra, a mu lanma na sube xa don. Fo a xa gan nɛ gbiki. Mixi sɛniyɛnxi nan nɔma na xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ sube donde,

sentences.english: But he who is unclean when he takes as food the flesh of the peace-offerings, which are the Lord's, will be cut off from his people.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ sɛniyɛntare mu nɔma n tan Alatala xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ donde, a raminima nɛ Isirayila ɲama ya ma.

sentences.english: And anyone who, after touching any unclean thing of man or an unclean beast or any unclean and disgusting thing, takes as food the flesh of the peace-offerings, which are the Lord's, will be cut off from his people.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a bɛlɛxɛ dinma se sɛniyɛntare ra naxan kelixi adamadi ma, xa na mu a ra a bɛlɛxɛ din sube sɛniyɛntare ra, xa na mu a ra se gbɛtɛ naxan mu sɛniyɛnxi, xa na kanyi fa n tan Alatala xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ don, a raminima nɛ Isirayila ɲama ya ma.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Say to the children of Israel: You are not to take any fat, of ox or sheep or goat, for food.
sentences.susu: «A fala Isirayilakae bɛ, ‹Wo naxa ninge, yɛxɛɛ, nun si ture don.

sentences.english: And the fat of that which comes to a natural death, and the fat of that which is attacked by beasts, may be used for other purposes, but not in any way for food.
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma xuruse ture rawalide alɔ wo wama a xɔn ma ki naxɛ xa a faxa a yɛtɛ ma, xa na mu a ra sube xaaɲɛ nde naxa a faxa, kɔnɔ wo mu nɔma a donde.

sentences.english: For anyone who takes as food the fat of any beast of which men make an offering by fire to the Lord, will be cut off from his people.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo ture donma, naxan nɔma rawalide sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra n tan Alatala bɛ, na kanyi raminima nɛ Isirayila ɲama ya ma.

sentences.english: And you are not to take for food any blood, of bird or of beast, in any of your houses.
sentences.susu: Wo man mu lanma wo xa xɔni wuli, xa na mu a ra xuruse wuli yo min yire birin wo na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: Whoever takes any blood for food will be cut off from his people.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo wuli minma, na kanyi raminima nɛ Isirayila ɲama ya ma.›»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Say to the children of Israel: He who makes a peace-offering to the Lord, is to give an offering to the Lord out of his peace-offering:
sentences.susu: «A fala Isirayilakae bɛ, ‹Naxan xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ bama n tan Alatala bɛ, a xa n tan Alatala gbe fi n ma.

sentences.english: He himself is to take to the Lord the offering made by fire, even the fat with the breast, so that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.
sentences.susu: A xa na xuruse ture nun a sisi xanin n tan Alatala yire alako a xa gan tɛ ra n tan Alatala bɛ. A lanma a xa na xuruse sisi lintan n tan Alatala ya i a masenfe ra n bɛ, na findixi n tan nan gbe ra.

sentences.english: And the fat is to be burned by the priest on the altar, but the breast is for Aaron and his sons.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na ture gan sɛrɛxɛbade fari. Na xuruse kanke luma Haruna nun a xa die nan bɛ.

sentences.english: And the right leg you are to give to the priest for an offering to be lifted up out of what is given for your peace-offerings.
sentences.susu: Wo xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛe kui, wo man xa xuruse yirefanyi tabe fi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ ma.

sentences.english: That man, among the sons of Aaron, by whom the blood of the peace-offering and the fat are offered, is to have the right leg for his part.
sentences.susu: Xuruse yirefanyi tabe xa findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ nan gbe ra naxan bara wuli nun ture ba xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: For the breast which is waved and the right leg which is lifted up on high I have taken from the children of Israel, from their peace-offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as their right for ever from the children of Israel.
sentences.susu: N bara natɛ tongo naxan mu kanama abadan, Isirayilakae xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛe kui, e xuruse kanke naxan lintanxi n tan Ala ya i, a nun xuruse yirefanyi tabe e naxan baxi, na birin xa findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ Haruna nun a xa die gbe ra.

sentences.english: This is the holy part given to Aaron and to his sons, out of the offerings made to the Lord by fire, on the day when they were made priests before the Lord;
sentences.susu: Kabi Haruna nun a xa die findi n tan Ala xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛe ra, e na nan sɔtɔma n tan Alatala xa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxie ya ma.

sentences.english: Which the Lord said the children of Israel were to give them, on the day when he made them his priests. It is their right for ever from generation to generation.
sentences.susu: E to findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛe ra, n tan Alatala naxa na yaamari fi Isirayilakae ma. Yaamari na a ra naxan mu kanama abadan.›»

sentences.english: These are the laws for the burned offering, the meal offering, and the offering for wrongdoing; and for the making of priests, and for the giving of peace-offerings;
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ nan na ki sɛrɛxɛe xa fe ra, sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi, sansi xɔri dinxi sɛrɛxɛ, yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ, yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ ti sɛrɛxɛ, nun xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ.

sentences.english: As they were given by the Lord to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day when the Lord gave orders to the children of Israel to make their offerings to the Lord, in the waste land of Sinai.
sentences.susu: Alatala nu bara na birin masen Annabi Munsa bɛ Turusinina geya fari a to Isirayilakae yamari e xa fa sɛrɛxɛe ra Turusinina gbengberenyi ma.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Take Aaron, and his sons with him, and the robes and the holy oil and the ox of the sin-offering and the two male sheep and the basket of unleavened bread;
sentences.susu: «Haruna nun a xa die xili hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra. I xa fa e xa dugi sɛniyɛnxie ra, a nun ture sɛniyɛnxi, tuura naxan bama yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra, yɛxɛɛ kontonyi firin, nun debe, taami lɛbinitaree na naxan kui.

sentences.english: And let all the people come together at the door of the Tent of meeting.
sentences.susu: I xa Isirayila ɲama birin malan hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra.»

sentences.english: And Moses did as the Lord said, and all the people came together at the door of the Tent of meeting.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa Alatala xa yaamari rakamali, ɲama fan naxa e malan hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra.

sentences.english: And Moses said to the people, This is what the Lord has given orders to be done.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a fala ɲama bɛ, «Alatala bara n yamari n xa yi raba.»

sentences.english: Then Moses took Aaron and his sons; and after washing them with water,
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa Haruna nun a xa die maso, a naxa e maxa ye ra.

sentences.english: He put the coat on him, making it tight with its band, and then the robe, and over it the ephod, with its band of needlework to keep it in place.
sentences.susu: A naxa dugi sɛniyɛnxie ragoro Haruna ma, a naxa a tagi xiri bɛlɛti ra, a guba ragoro a ma, a sɛrɛxɛdubɛ donma ragoro na fari, a a tagi xiri bɛlɛti ra.

sentences.english: And he put the priest's bag on him, and in the bag he put the Urim and Thummim.
sentences.susu: A naxa kanke makotose ragoro a kɔn ma, a gɛmɛ firin sa na kui naxee findixi Ala waxɔnfe masense ra.

sentences.english: And on his head he put the head-dress, and in front of the head-dress the plate of gold, the holy crown, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
sentences.susu: A naxa xunmase dɔxɔ Haruna xunyi ma, a tɔnxuma sɛniyɛnxi xɛɛma daaxi sa na ma, alɔ Alatala Munsa yamari ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And Moses took the holy oil and put it on the House and on all the things in it, to make them holy.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa ture sɛniyɛnxi tongo, a nde maso Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira ma, nun se naxan birin na a kui. A nee rasɛniyɛn na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: Seven times he put oil on the altar and on all its vessels, and on the washing-basin and its base, to make them holy.
sentences.susu: A naxa ture kasan sɛrɛxɛbade ma sanya solofere, a nun sɛrɛxɛbade yirabasee, ye ragatade xungbe, nun na saxi se naxan fari, alako e xa sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And some of the oil he put on Aaron's head, to make him holy.
sentences.susu: A man naxa ture nde sa Haruna xunyi ma, alako Haruna fan xa sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: Then he took Aaron's sons, clothing them with the coats, and putting the bands round them, and the head-dresses on their heads, as the Lord had given him orders.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa Haruna xa die maso, a dugi sɛniyɛnxie ragoro e fan ma. A naxa e tagi nun e xunyi xiri dugi ra, alɔ Alatala a yamarixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And he took the ox of the sin-offering: and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the ox,
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa to fa tuura yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra, Haruna nun a xa die naxa e bɛlɛxɛe sa na tuura xun tagi.

sentences.english: And he put it to death; and Moses took the blood and put it on the horns of the altar and round it with his finger, and made the altar clean, draining out the blood at the base of the altar; so he made it holy, taking away what was unclean.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a kɔn naxaba, a naxa a wuli nde tongo, a a maso sɛrɛxɛbade ferie ma naxee nu na sɛrɛxɛbade tunxunyi naani ra. A naxa na raba a bɛlɛxɛsole ra, alako a xa sɛrɛxɛbade rasɛniyɛn. A naxa wuli dɔnxɔɛ ifili sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma. A sɛrɛxɛbade rasɛniyɛn na ki nɛ barima a findi xunsarade nan na.

sentences.english: And he took all the fat on the inside parts, and the fat on the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, to be burned on the altar;
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa man naxa ture tongo naxan nu na ninge furingɛ rabilinyi, a nun laare naxan nu na a bɔɲɛ fari, nun a gungui xɔri firinyie nun e ture. A naxa nee birin sa tɛ i sɛrɛxɛbade fari.

sentences.english: But the ox, with its skin and its flesh and its waste, was burned with fire outside the tent-circle, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a naxa tuura gundi, a kiri, a sube, nun a ɲaɲɛ gan tɛ ra ɲama yonkinde fari ma, alɔ Alatala a yamarixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And he put the male sheep of the burned offering before the Lord, and Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head,
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa fa yɛxɛɛ kontonyi ra naxan findi sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra. Haruna nun a xa die naxa e bɛlɛxɛe sa na yɛxɛɛ xun tagi.

sentences.english: And he put it to death; and Moses put some of the blood on and round the altar.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a kɔn naxaba, a a wuli nde kasan sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And when the sheep had been cut into parts, the head and the parts and the fat were burned by Moses.
sentences.susu: A naxa yɛxɛɛ ixaba a xuntunyie ra. A naxa a xunyi, a xuntunyie, nun a ture gan tɛ i.

sentences.english: And the inside parts and the legs were washed with water and all the sheep was burned by Moses on the altar; it was a burned offering for a sweet smell: it was an offering made by fire to the Lord, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
sentences.susu: A naxa yɛxɛɛ furingɛ nun a sanyie raxa, a yɛxɛɛ kontonyi gundi birin gan tɛ ra sɛrɛxɛbade fari sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra, naxan xiri rafan Alatala ma. A na birin naba nɛ alɔ Alatala a yamarixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And he put the other sheep before the Lord, the sheep with which they were made priests; and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the sheep,
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa yɛxɛɛ kontonyi firin nde tongo naxan findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ dɔxɔ sɛrɛxɛ ra. Haruna nun a xa die naxa e bɛlɛxɛe sa na yɛxɛɛ xun tagi.

sentences.english: And he put it to death; and Moses took some of the blood and put it on the point of Aaron's right ear and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a kɔn naxaba, a a wuli nde tongo, a a sa Haruna yirefanyi tuli ma, a yirefanyi bɛlɛxɛkura ma, nun a sankura ma.

sentences.english: Then he took Aaron's sons, and Moses put some of the blood on the point of their right ears and on the thumbs of their right hands and on the great toes of their right feet: and Moses put the blood on and round the altar.
sentences.susu: A naxa Haruna xa die fan maso, a naxa wuli nde sa e yirefanyi tulie ma, e yirefanyi bɛlɛxɛkura ma, nun e yirefanyi sankura ma. A naxa a wuli nde kasan sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And he took the fat, and the fat tail, and the fat on the inside parts, and the fat on the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right leg;
sentences.susu: A naxa na yɛxɛɛ ture tongo, a nun a xuli, a furingɛ ture, laare naxan na a bɔɲɛ fari, a gungui xɔri firinyie nun e ture, nun a yirefanyi tabe.

sentences.english: And out of the basket of unleavened bread which was before the Lord he took one unleavened cake, and one cake of bread with oil on it, and one thin cake, and put them on the fat and on the right leg:
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa debe tongo taami lɛbinitaree na naxan kui, naxan nu dɔxɔxi Alatala ya i. A naxa taami lɛbinitare keren ba na, a nun taami keren naxan yailanxi ture ra, a nun taami lanmadi keren. A naxa e sa na yɛxɛɛ ture nun a yirefanyi tabe fari.

sentences.english: And he put them all on the hands of Aaron and on the hands of his sons, waving them for a wave offering before the Lord.
sentences.susu: A naxa na birin so Haruna nun a xa die yi ra, e fa na lintan Alatala ya i alako a xa a kolon a gbe na a ra.

sentences.english: And Moses took them from their hands, and they were burned on the altar on the burned offering, as a priest's offering for a sweet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, Annabi Munsa naxa e rasuxu e yi ra, a naxa e sa tɛ sɛrɛxɛbade fari, sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi nu na dɛnnaxɛ. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ dɔxɔ sɛrɛxɛ na a ra, naxan gan xiri rafan Alatala ma.

sentences.english: And Moses took the breast, waving it for a wave offering before the Lord; it was Moses' part of the sheep of the priest's offering, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa yɛxɛɛ kontonyi kanke tongo na sɛrɛxɛdubɛ dɔxɔ sɛrɛxɛ ra, a fa na lintan Alatala ya i a masenfe ra a bɛ. Na naxa findi Annabi Munsa gbe ra alɔ Alatala a yamarixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And Moses took some of the holy oil and of the blood which was on the altar and put it on Aaron and on his robes, and on his sons and on his sons' robes; and made Aaron holy, and his robes and his sons and his sons' robes with him.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa ture sɛniyɛnxi nde tongo, a nun wuli nde naxan nu na sɛrɛxɛbade fari, a naxa a kasan Haruna nun a xa dugie ma, a a kasan Haruna xa die nun e xa dugie fan ma, alako e tan nun e xa dugie birin xa sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And Moses said to Aaron and to his sons, The flesh is to be cooked in water at the door of the Tent of meeting, and there you are to take it as food, together with the bread in the basket, as I have given orders, saying, It is the food of Aaron and his sons.
sentences.susu: Munsa naxa a fala Haruna nun a xa die bɛ, «Wo sube ɲin hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra, wo xa a don mɛnni, a nun taami naxan na debe kui naxan findi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ dɔxɔ sɛrɛxɛ ra. N bara yaamari fi, Haruna nun a xa die xa na don.

sentences.english: And that which is over of the flesh and of the bread is to be burned with fire.
sentences.susu: Taami nun sube naxan luxi, wo xa na dɔnxɔɛ gan.

sentences.english: And you are not to go out from the door of the Tent of meeting for seven days, till the days for making you priest are ended; for this will be the work of seven days.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa keli hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra xi solofere bun ma, han wo xa dɔxɔɛ waxati kamalima tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: What has been done this day, has been ordered by the Lord to take away your sin.
sentences.susu: Naxan nabaxi to, Alatala a yamarixi wo yunubi xunsare xa fe nan na.

sentences.english: And you are to keep watch for the Lord at the door of the Tent of meeting day and night for seven days, so that death may not come to you: for so he has given me orders.
sentences.susu: Na na a toxi, wo luma hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra xi solofere bun ma, kɔɛ nun yanyi, alɔ Alatala n yamarixi a ra ki naxɛ, alako wo naxa faxa.»

sentences.english: And Aaron and his sons did all the things about which the Lord had given orders through Moses.
sentences.susu: Haruna nun a xa die naxa Alatala xa yaamari birin naba na ki a naxan masenxi e bɛ Annabi Munsa saabui ra.

sentences.english: And on the eighth day Moses sent for Aaron and his sons and the responsible men of Israel;
sentences.susu: Xi solomasaxan lɔxɔɛ, Annabi Munsa naxa Haruna nun a xa die, nun Isirayila forie xili.

sentences.english: And he said to Aaron, Take a young ox for a sin-offering and a male sheep for a burned offering, without a mark, and make an offering of them before the Lord.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen Haruna bɛ, «I xa sɛrɛxɛ firin masen Alatala bɛ, tuura di naxan findima yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra, a nun yɛxɛɛ kontonyi naxan findima sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra, lanyuru mu na naxan ma.

sentences.english: And say to the children of Israel: Take a he-goat for a sin-offering, and a young ox and a lamb, in their first year, without any mark on them, for a burned offering;
sentences.susu: I xa a fala Isirayilakae bɛ, ‹Wo xa sikɔtɛ keren ba yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra. Wo xa tuura di nun yɛxɛɛ di naxee bara ɲɛ keren sɔtɔ, lanyuru mu na naxee ma, wo xa e ba sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra.

sentences.english: And an ox and a male sheep for peace-offerings, to be put to death before the Lord; and a meal offering mixed with oil: for this day you are to see the Lord.
sentences.susu: Wo xa tuura nun yɛxɛɛ kontonyi ba xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ ra Alatala bɛ. Wo xa taami fan ba sɛrɛxɛ ra, ture sunbuxi naxan na. Wo xa na birin ba barima Alatala minima nɛ wo ma to.›»

sentences.english: And they took the things ordered by Moses, before the Tent of meeting, and all the people came near, waiting before the Lord.
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa sɛrɛxɛe xanin hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra alɔ Annabi Munsa e yamarixi ki naxɛ. E birin naxa e makɔrɛ hɔrɔmɔlingira ra, e ti Alatala ya i.

sentences.english: And Moses said, This is what the Lord has said you are to do; and you will see the glory of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo xa Alatala xa yaamari rabatu alako a xa a nɔrɛ masen wo bɛ.»

sentences.english: And Moses said to Aaron, Come near to the altar and make your sin-offering and your burned offering to take away your sin and the sin of the people, and make the people's offering to take away their sin; as the Lord has given orders.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a masen Haruna bɛ, «I maso sɛrɛxɛbade ra. I xa yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ nun sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ba xunsare ra i yɛtɛ bɛ, a nun ɲama bɛ. I xa ɲama xa sɛrɛxɛ fan ba e bɛ xunsare ra alɔ Alatala a yamarixi ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: So Aaron came near to the altar and put to death the ox for the sin-offering for himself;
sentences.susu: Haruna to a maso sɛrɛxɛbade ra, a naxa tuura di kɔn naxaba a yɛtɛ yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the sons of Aaron gave him the blood and he put his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, draining out the blood at the base of the altar;
sentences.susu: A xa die naxa tuura wuli so a yi ra. A naxa a bɛlɛxɛsole rasin wuli xɔɔra, a nde sa ferie ma naxee nu na sɛrɛxɛbade tunxunyi naani ra. A naxa wuli dɔnxɔɛ ifili sɛrɛxɛbade lanbanyi ma.

sentences.english: But the fat and the kidneys and the fat on the liver of the sin-offering were burned by him on the altar as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
sentences.susu: Xuruse ture, a gunguie, nun laare naxan na a bɔɲɛ ma, a naxa na birin gan sɛrɛxɛbade fari yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra alɔ Alatala Annabi Munsa yamarixi a ra ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And the flesh and the skin were burned with fire outside the tent-circle;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a naxa a sube nun a kiri gan ɲama yonkinde fari ma.

sentences.english: And he put to death the burned offering; and Aaron's sons gave him the blood and he put some of it on and round the altar;
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, Haruna naxa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi kɔn naxaba. A xa die naxa na wuli so a yi ra, a fa a kasan sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And they gave him the parts of the burned offering, in their order, and the head, to be burned on the altar.
sentences.susu: E naxa sɛrɛxɛ xuntunyie nun a xunyi so a yi ra, a na birin gan sɛrɛxɛbade fari.

sentences.english: And the inside parts and the legs, when they had been washed with water, were burned on the burned offering on the altar.
sentences.susu: A to gɛ a furingɛ nun a sanyie raxade, a naxa e gan e nun sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra sɛrɛxɛbade fari.

sentences.english: And he made an offering for the people and took the goat of the sin-offering for the people and put it to death, offering it for sin, in the same way as the first.
sentences.susu: Haruna gɛ xanbi na ra, a naxa ɲama xa sikɔtɛ kɔn naxaba, a xa findi yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra ɲama bɛ. A na raba nɛ alɔ a a singe raba ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And he took the burned offering, offering it in the ordered way;
sentences.susu: A naxa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ba a sɛriyɛ ki ma.

sentences.english: And he put the meal offering before the Lord, and taking some of it in his hand he had it burned on the altar, separately from the burned offering of the morning.
sentences.susu: A naxa sansi xɔri dinxi suxu keren gan sɛrɛxɛbade fari sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ba tɛmui gɛɛsɛgɛ.

sentences.english: And he put to death the ox and the sheep, which were the peace-offerings for the people; and Aaron's sons gave him the blood and he put some of it on and round the altar;
sentences.susu: A naxa tuura nun yɛxɛɛ kontonyi kɔn naxaba xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ ra ɲama bɛ. A xa die naxa na wuli so a yi, a a kasan sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And as for the fat of the ox and the fat tail of the sheep and the fat covering the inside parts and the kidneys and the fat on the liver;
sentences.susu: E naxa tuura nun yɛxɛɛ kontonyi ture tongo, naxan na e xuli nun e furingɛ mabiri, a nun e gunguie, a nun laare naxan na e bɔɲɛ ma,

sentences.english: They put the fat on the breasts, and the fat was burned on the altar.
sentences.susu: e naxa na birin sa sube kanke ma sɛrɛxɛbade fari, e a birin gan.

sentences.english: And Aaron took the breasts and the right leg, waving them for a wave offering before the Lord, as Moses gave orders.
sentences.susu: Haruna naxa sɛrɛxɛ subee kanke nun e yirefanyi tabe ite, a e lintan Alatala ya i a masenfe ra a bɛ, alɔ Annabi Munsa a yamarixi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And Aaron, lifting up his hands to the people, gave them a blessing; and he came down from offering the sin-offering, and the burned offering, and the peace-offerings.
sentences.susu: Haruna naxa a bɛlɛxɛe itala, a duba ɲama bɛ. A to yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ, sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi, nun xanunteya sɛrɛxɛ ba, a naxa goro kelife sɛrɛxɛbade sɛɛtie ma.

sentences.english: And Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of meeting, and came out and gave the people a blessing, and the glory of the Lord was seen by all the people.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa nun Haruna naxa so hɔrɔmɔlingira kui. E to mini, e naxa duba ɲama bɛ. Na tɛmui Alatala xa nɔrɛ naxa mini ɲama ma.

sentences.english: And fire came out from before the Lord, burning up the offering on the altar and the fat: and when all the people saw it, they gave a loud cry, falling down on their faces.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa tɛ ragoro sɛrɛxɛbade fari, a sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi nun ture gan. Ɲama to na to, e naxa e xui ite sɛɛwɛ ra, e e felen bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took their vessels and put fire in them and perfume, burning strange fire before the Lord, which he had not given them orders to do.
sentences.susu: Haruna xa di firinyie, Nadabo nun Abihu naxa surayi gansee tongo, e tɛ sa e kui, e surayi gan Alatala ya i. Kɔnɔ e mu na tɛ tongo Ala xa sɛriyɛ ki ma.

sentences.english: And fire came out from before the Lord, burning them up and causing their destruction before the Lord.
sentences.susu: Na na a to, Alatala naxa tɛ ragoro e ma, e faxa a xa hɔrɔmɔlingira yire sɛniyɛnxi kui.

sentences.english: Then Moses said to Aaron, This is what the Lord said, I will be holy in the eyes of all those who come near to me, and I will be honoured before all the people. And Aaron said nothing.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a fala Haruna bɛ, «Alatala wo rakolonxi nɛ yi ra, a to a fala, ‹Naxee makɔrɛ n na, e xa a kolon n sɛniyɛn, ɲama xa n binya.›» Haruna naxa dundu yen.

sentences.english: And Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the brother of Aaron's father, and said to them, Come near and take your brothers away from before the holy place, outside the tent-circle.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa Mikayeli nun Elisafan xili, Haruna baba xunya Yusiyɛli xa die. A naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo xa wo ngaxakerenyie furee xanin ɲama yonkinde fari ma, dɛnnaxɛ makuya yire sɛniyɛnxi ra.»

sentences.english: So they came and took them, in their coats, outside the tent-circle, as Moses had said.
sentences.susu: E naxa e furee xanin ɲama yonkinde fari ma, alɔ Annabi Munsa e yamarixi ki naxɛ. E nu bara sɛrɛxɛdubɛ dugie lu e furee ma.

sentences.english: And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons, Do not let your hair be loose, and give no signs of grief; so that death may not overtake you, and his wrath come on all the people; but let there be weeping among your brothers and all the house of Israel for this burning of the Lord's fire.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a fala Haruna nun a xa die bɛ, Eleyasari nun Itamari, «Wo naxa wo xunsɛxɛ rabɛɲin, wo naxa wo xa dugie fan ibɔɔ. Wo naxa sese raba naxan nɔma sunnunyi masende yi mixie xa faxɛ xa fe ra, alako Alatala naxa xɔnɔ ɲama ma, a wo fan faxa. Wo ngaxakerenyi Isirayilakae tan nɔma sunnunde yi mixie xa fe ra Alatala naxee faxaxi tɛ ra.

sentences.english: And do not go out from the door of the Tent of meeting, or death will come to you; for the holy oil of the Lord is on you. And they did as Moses said.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa keli Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra yi saxanyi, alako wo naxa faxa. Alatala xa mixi sugandixie nan wo tan na.» E naxa Annabi Munsa xa yaamari rabatu.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Aaron:
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Haruna bɛ,

sentences.english: Take no wine, or strong drink, you or your sons with you, when you go into the Tent of meeting, that it may not be the cause of death to you; this is an order for ever through all your generations.
sentences.susu: «Wo na so hɔrɔmɔlingira kui, wo naxa wɛni min. Wo naxa minse yo min naxan mixi siisima, xa na mu a ra wo faxama nɛ. Na sɛriyɛ mu kanama wo bɔnsɔɛ bɛ abadan.

sentences.english: And make a division between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean;
sentences.susu: Na nan a niyama wo nɔma Ala gbe nun adamadi gbe tagi rabade, sɛniyɛnyi nun sɛniyɛntareɲa.

sentences.english: Teaching the children of Israel all the laws which the Lord has given them by the hand of Moses.
sentences.susu: Na fan a niyama nɛ wo xa nɔ Isirayilakae xarande Alatala xa yaamarie ra, a naxee fixi e ma Annabi Munsa saabui ra.»

sentences.english: And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons who were still living, Take the rest of the meal offering from the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and take it for your food, without leaven, at the side of the altar, for it is most holy.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa a fala Haruna nun a xa di dɔnxɔɛe bɛ, Eleyasari nun Itamari, «Sansi xɔri dinxi naxan baxi sɛrɛxɛ ra Alatala bɛ, kɔnɔ naxan birin mu ganxi tɛ ra, wo xa na don sɛrɛxɛbade fɛ ma. Wo naxa lɛbini sa a xun ma de, barima a sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: It is to be for your food in a holy place, because it is your right and your sons' right, from the offerings of the Lord made by fire: for so am I ordered.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a don yire sɛniyɛnxi, barima a ganxi Alatala bɛ sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxie nan fɛ ma. Na findixi i gbe nun i xa die gbe nan na. Alatala sɛrɛxɛdubɛe yamarixi na nan na.

sentences.english: And the breast which is waved and the leg which is lifted up on high, you are to take as your food in a clean place; you and your sons and your daughters with you: for they are given to you as your right and your sons' right, from the peace-offerings of the children of Israel.
sentences.susu: Wo man xa sɛrɛxɛ sube kanke nun tabe don yire sɛniyɛnxi nɛ, naxee bara lintan Ala ya i, a masenfe ra a bɛ. Nee findixi wo gbe nan na, i tan, i xa di xɛmɛe, nun i xa di ginɛe. Ala bara na yaamari fi Isirayilakae ma e xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛe xa fe ra.

sentences.english: Let them take the breast which is waved and the leg which is lifted up on high, with the fat of the burned offering, to be waved for a wave offering before the Lord; and this will be for you and for your sons with you, for a right for ever, as the Lord has given orders.
sentences.susu: Ture naxan ganma yo, tabe naxan bama yo, nun kanke naxan lintanma yo, e xa na birin masen Alatala bɛ, na fa findi i gbe nun i xa die gbe ra, alɔ Alatala a yamarixi ki naxɛ. Sɛriyɛ na a ra naxan mu kanama abadan.»

sentences.english: And Moses was looking for the goat of the sin-offering, but it was burned; and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, who were still living, saying,
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa to sikɔtɛ xa fe maxɔrin, naxan ba yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra, a naxa a mɛ a e nu bara a birin gan tɛ ra, a naxa xɔnɔ Eleyasari nun Itamari ma, Haruna xa die naxee mu faxa. A naxa a fala e bɛ,

sentences.english: Why did you not make a meal of the sin-offering in the holy place? For it is most holy and he has given it to you, so that the sin of the people may be put on it, to take away their sin before the Lord.
sentences.susu: «Munfe ra wo mu yi yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ sube donxi yire sɛniyɛnxi? Sɛrɛxɛ sɛniyɛnxi na a ra Alatala naxan fixi wo ma, alako Isirayila ɲama xa yunubi xa xafari, a findi xunsare ra e bɛ Alatala ya i.

sentences.english: See, its blood was not taken into the holy place: certainly it was right for you to have taken it as food in the holy place, as I gave orders.
sentences.susu: Yi sɛrɛxɛ wuli to mu soxi yire sɛniyɛnxi ma hɔrɔmɔlingira kui, a nu lan nɛ wo xa a sube don yire sɛniyɛnxi nɛ, alɔ Ala n yamarixi a ra ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And Aaron said to Moses, You have seen that today they have made their sin-offering and their burned offering before the Lord, and such things as these have come on me. If I had taken the sin-offering as food today, would it have been pleasing to the Lord?
sentences.susu: Haruna naxa Annabi Munsa yaabi, «To e bara e xa yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ nun e xa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ba Alatala ya i, kɔnɔ n to bara yi fe xɔrɔxɔɛ mɔɔli sɔtɔ, Alatala nɔma tinde n xa yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ sube don to?»

sentences.english: And after hearing this, Moses was no longer angry.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa to na yaabi mɛ, a naxa tin a ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa nun Haruna bɛ,

sentences.english: Say to the children of Israel: These are the living things which you may have for food among all the beasts on the earth.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa a fala Isirayilakae bɛ, sube naxee radaxaxi wo bɛ, nee nan ya:

sentences.english: You may have as food any beast which has a division in the horn of its foot, and whose food comes back into its mouth to be crushed again.
sentences.susu: Sube tore kanyie naxee tore itaxunxi firinyi ra, e man e xa donse ratema e dɛ i e nu a idon. Wo nɔma na sube mɔɔli donde.»

sentences.english: But, at the same time, of those beasts, you may not take for food the camel, because its food comes back but the horn of its foot is not parted in two; it is unclean to you.
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ ndee na naxee donse ratema e dɛ i e nu a idon, e tore tan mu itaxunxi firinyi ra. Nee raharamuxi wo ma. Ɲɔxɔmɛ raharamuxi wo ma, barima a donse ratema a dɛ i a nu a idon, kɔnɔ a tore mu itaxunxi firinyi ra.

sentences.english: And the rock-badger, for the same reason, is unclean to you.
sentences.susu: Yere maniyɛ nde fan donse ratema a dɛ i a nu a idon, kɔnɔ a tore mu itaxunxi firinyi ra. A raharamuxi wo ma.

sentences.english: And the hare, because the horn of its foot is not parted in two, is unclean to you.
sentences.susu: Yere fan donse ratema a dɛ i a nu a idon, kɔnɔ a tore mu itaxunxi firinyi ra. A raharamuxi wo ma.

sentences.english: And the pig is unclean to you, because though the horn of its foot is parted, its food does not come back.
sentences.susu: Xɔsɛ tan, a tore itaxunxi firinyi ra, kɔnɔ a mu donse ratema a dɛ i a nu a idon. A raharamuxi wo ma.

sentences.english: Their flesh may not be used for food, and their dead bodies may not even be touched; they are unclean to you.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa na subee don, wo naxa din e binbie ra. E raharamuxi wo ma.»

sentences.english: These you may have for food of all things living in the water: anything living in the water, in the seas or rivers, which has special parts for swimming and skin formed of thin plates, may be used for food.
sentences.susu: «Yɛxɛ naxee na ye xɔɔra, wo nɔma naxee donde, nee nan ya: xale kanyi nun bɛlɛ kanyi naxee na baa ma, xa na mu a ra xure kui.

sentences.english: All other things living and moving in the water, in the sea or in the rivers, are a disgusting thing to you;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yɛxɛ naxee na baa ma, xa na mu a ra xure kui, bɛlɛ mu na naxee ma, xa na mu a ra xale mu na naxee ma, e raharamuxi wo ma.

sentences.english: They may not be used for food, and their dead bodies are disgusting to you.
sentences.susu: E raharamuxi wo ma, wo naxa e sube don. E binbie fan raharamuxi wo ma.

sentences.english: Anything in the water which has no special parts for swimming and no thin plates on its skin is disgusting to you.
sentences.susu: Yɛxɛ birin bɛlɛ nun xale mu na naxee ma, e raharamuxi wo ma.»

sentences.english: And among birds these are to be disgusting to you, and not to be used for food: the eagle and the gier-eagle and the ospray;
sentences.susu: «Xɔni raharamuxie nan ya wo mu lan wo xa naxee don: yubɛ, sɛgɛ, xaruma gbɔntɔɛ,

sentences.english: And the kite and the falcon, and birds of that sort;
sentences.susu: a nun nee maniyɛ birin.

sentences.english: Every raven, and birds of that sort;
sentences.susu: Xaaxa fan, wo naxa na don a nun a maniyɛ birin.

sentences.english: And the ostrich and the night-hawk and the sea-hawk, and birds of that sort;
sentences.susu: Xundi, koofole, a nun tagarantongoe,

sentences.english: And the little owl and the cormorant and the great owl;
sentences.susu: wo naxa e don a nun nee maniyɛ birin.

sentences.english: And the water-hen and the pelican and the vulture;
sentences.susu: Gbongboe, yedɔnmɛ,

sentences.english: The stork and the heron, and birds of that sort, and the hoopoe and the bat.
sentences.susu: laaba, tukɛ, a nun nee maniyɛ birin, wo naxa e don.»

sentences.english: Every winged four-footed thing which goes on the earth is disgusting to you;
sentences.susu: «Nimase gabutenyi nun sanyi na naxee ma, e raharamuxi wo ma.

sentences.english: But of the winged four-footed things, those which have long legs for jumping on the earth you may have for food;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ na nimase mɔɔlie ya ma, naxee tuganma, wo nɔma nee tan donde,

sentences.english: Such as all the different sorts of locust.
sentences.susu: alɔ katoe, tugumie, nun nee maniyɛ birin.

sentences.english: But all other winged four-footed things which go on the earth are disgusting to you.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ, nimase gabutenyi nun sanyi na naxee ma, e raharamuxi wo ma.»

sentences.english: By these you will be made unclean; anyone touching their dead bodies will be unclean till evening:
sentences.susu: «Xa wo dinma sube sɛniyɛntare ra, wo findima mixi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra.

sentences.english: Whoever takes away the dead body of one of them is to have his clothing washed, and will be unclean till evening.
sentences.susu: Naxan e binbie maxaninma, na kanyi lan nɛ a xa a xa dugie xa, a man fa findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra. Fo a xa a xa dugie xa.

sentences.english: Every beast, in the horn of whose foot there is not a complete division, and whose food does not come back, is unclean to you: anyone touching one of these will be unclean.
sentences.susu: Sube naxee birin tore mu itaxunxi firinyi ra, a nun naxee donse donma, kɔnɔ a mu gbilenma a rate ra e dɛ i e nu a idon, nee raharamuxi wo ma. Naxan dinma na mɔɔli ra a findima mixi sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: Any four-footed beast which goes on the ball of its foot, is unclean to you: anyone touching the dead body of one of these will be unclean till evening.
sentences.susu: Sube birin tore mu na naxee bɛ, e e ɲɛrɛ e sanyi naanie xun na, e raharamuxi wo ma. Naxan dinma e binbie ra na findima mixi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra.

sentences.english: Anyone who takes away the dead body of one of these is to have his clothing washed and be unclean till evening.
sentences.susu: E raharamuxi wo ma. Naxan e binbie maxaninma, na kanyi lan nɛ a xa a xa dugie xa, a man fa findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra.»

sentences.english: And these are unclean to you among things which go low down on the earth; the weasel and the mouse and the great lizard, and animals of that sort;
sentences.susu: «Nimase naxan birin luma yilie kui, e haramuxi wo bɛ. E xilie nan ya: bale, ɲɛnɛ, kasa,

sentences.english: And the ferret and the land crocodile and the lizard and the sand-lizard and the chameleon.
sentences.susu: bonbolika, koolo, nun nee maniyɛe.

sentences.english: All these are unclean to you: anyone touching them when they are dead will be unclean till evening.
sentences.susu: Na nimase xunxuri mɔɔlie raharamuxi wo ma. Naxan dinma e binbie ra a findima mixi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra.

sentences.english: The dead body of any of these, falling on anything, will make that thing unclean; if it is any vessel of wood, or clothing, or skin, or bag, whatever it is, if it is used for any purpose, it will have to be put into water, and will be unclean till evening; after that it will be clean.
sentences.susu: Xa e binbie sa bira se nde fari, na fan findima se sɛniyɛntare ra, alɔ se sa se wuri daaxi, dugi, xuruse kiri xaraxi, bɛki, xa na mu a ra yirabase nde. A lanma na se mɔɔli xa sa ye xɔɔra han nunmare ra alako a xa sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And if one of them gets into any vessel of earth, whatever is in the vessel will be unclean and the vessel will have to be broken.
sentences.susu: Xa na nimase mɔɔli bira fɛɲɛ nde kui, fɛɲɛ nun a kui se birin findima se sɛniyɛntare ra. Na fɛɲɛ xa kana.

sentences.english: Any food in it, and anything on which water from it comes, will be unclean: any drink taken from such a vessel will be unclean.
sentences.susu: Ye naxan nu na na fɛɲɛ kui, a na sa donse nde ma, na donse fan findima se sɛniyɛntare ra. Minse yo naxan nu na na fɛɲɛ kui, a fan findima se sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: Any part of the dead body of one of these, falling on anything, will make it unclean; if it is an oven or a cooking-pot it will have to be broken: they are unclean and will be unclean to you.
sentences.susu: Xa na nimase mɔɔli binbi bira se yo ma, na findima se sɛniyɛntare ra, alɔ taami ganse, xa na mu a ra tunde. E to findi se sɛniyɛntaree ra, a lanma wo xa e kana.

sentences.english: But at the same time a fountain or a place where water is stored for use will be clean; but anyone touching their dead bodies will be unclean.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa e binbi sa bira dulonyi nan kui, xa na mu a ra ye ragatade nde, nee tan mu findima se sɛniyɛntaree ra. Kɔnɔ mixi naxan a bɛlɛxɛ dinma e binbie ra, na findima mixi sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: If any part of the dead body of one of these gets on to any seed for planting, it is clean;
sentences.susu: Xa a binbi bira sansi xɔri ma naxan sima, na mu findima se sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: But if water is put on the seed, and any part of the dead body gets on to it, it will be unclean to you.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a binbi bira sansi xɔri tan ma naxan na ye xɔɔra, na sansi xɔri findima se sɛniyɛntare ra wo bɛ.»

sentences.english: And if any beast which may be used for food comes to a natural death, anyone touching its dead body will be unclean till evening.
sentences.susu: «Xa xuruse radaxaxi nde faxa, mixi fa din a binbi ra, na kanyi findima sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra.

sentences.english: And he who makes use of any part of its body for food is to have his clothing washed and be unclean till evening; and anyone taking away its body is to have his clothing washed and be unclean till evening.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a sube don, na kanyi lan nɛ a xa a xa dugie xa, a man fa findi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra. Naxan na sube binbi maxanin, na kanyi lan nɛ a xa a xa dugie xa, a man fa findi sɛniyɛntare ra han nunmare ra.»

sentences.english: Everything which goes flat on its body on the earth is disgusting, and is not to be used for food.
sentences.susu: «Nimase naxan birin a bubuma bɔxi ma, nee birin raharamuxi wo ma. A mu lanma wo xa nee don.

sentences.english: Whatever goes on its stomach or on four feet or has a great number of feet, even all those going flat on the earth, may not be used for food, for they are disgusting.
sentences.susu: Bubusee nun nimase xunxuri naxee ɲɛrɛma e sanyi naani xun na, xa na mu a ra e sanyi wuyaxi xun na, e sese mu radaxaxi. Wo naxa e don.

sentences.english: You are not to make yourselves disgusting with anything which goes about flat on the earth; you may not make yourselves unclean with them, in such a way that you are not holy to me.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo yɛtɛ findi sɛniyɛntare ra na nimase mɔɔli saabui ra. Wo naxa e don.

sentences.english: For I am the Lord your God: for this reason, make and keep yourselves holy, for I am holy; you are not to make yourselves unclean with any sort of thing which goes about flat on the earth.
sentences.susu: Alatala nan n na, wo Marigi Ala. Wo xa wo yɛtɛ fi n tan nan ma. Wo xa sɛniyɛn, barima n tan sɛniyɛn. Wo naxa wo yɛtɛ findi sɛniyɛntare ra na nimase xunxuri saabui ra naxee luma ɲɛrɛ ra bɔxi ma.»

sentences.english: For I am the Lord, who took you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God; so be you holy, for I am holy.
sentences.susu: «N tan nan Alatala ra naxan wo raminixi Misira bɔxi ma, alako n xa findi wo Marigi Ala ra. Wo xa sɛniyɛn, barima n tan sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: This is the law about beasts and birds and every living thing moving in the waters, and every living thing which goes flat on the earth:
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ nan na ki subee, xɔnie, yɛxɛɛe, nun bubusee xa fe ra.

sentences.english: Marking out the unclean from the clean, and the living thing which may be used for food from that which may not.
sentences.susu: Na kui wo nɔma sube sɛniyɛnxi nun sube sɛniyɛntare tagi raba kolonde, sube radaxaxi nun sube raharamuxi.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: Say to the children of Israel, If a woman is with child and gives birth to a male child, she will be unclean for seven days, as when she is unwell.
sentences.susu: «A fala Isirayilakae bɛ, xa ginɛ nde sa tɛɛgɛ, a di xɛmɛ bari, a findima sɛniyɛntare ra xi solofere bun ma, alɔ a kike walima tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: And on the eighth day let him be given circumcision.
sentences.susu: Xi solomasaxan lɔxɔɛ, di xa sunna.

sentences.english: And she will be unclean for thirty-three days till the flow of her blood is stopped; no holy thing may be touched by her, and she may not come into the holy place, till the days for making her clean are ended.
sentences.susu: Na xi solofere xanbi, dingɛ luma sɛniyɛntareɲa kui xi tongo saxan nun saxan bun ma a wuli xa fe ra naxan minixi a ma a di bari tɛmui. A mu lanma a xa din se sɛniyɛnxi ra, a mu lanma a xa so yire sɛniyɛnxi kui han marasɛniyɛnyi waxati xa kamali.»

sentences.english: But if she gives birth to a female child, then she will be unclean for two weeks, as when she is unwell; and she will not be completely clean for sixty-six days.
sentences.susu: «Xa dingɛ di ginɛ bari, a luma sɛniyɛntareɲa kui lɔxɔxun firin, alɔ a kike walima tɛmui naxɛ. Na xanbi a xa marasɛniyɛnyi waxati buma xi tongo senni nun senni, a wuli xa fe ra naxan minixi a di bari tɛmui.

sentences.english: And when the days are ended for making her clean for a son or a daughter, let her take to the priest at the door of the Tent of meeting, a lamb of the first year for a burned offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin-offering:
sentences.susu: A xa marasɛniyɛnyi waxati na kamali, di xɛmɛ, xa na mu a ra di ginɛ xa fe ra, a xa yɛxɛɛ ɲɛ keren daaxi xanin sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xɔn ma hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra. A xa na ba sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra. A man xa kolokonde yɔrɛ, xa na mu a ra ganbɛ ba yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the priest is to make an offering of it before the Lord and take away her sin, and she will be made clean from the flow of her blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth to a male or a female.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na sɛrɛxɛe ba Alatala bɛ, a findi na ginɛ xa xunsare ra. Na tɛmui a sɛniyɛnma nɛ na wuli xa fe ra. Sɛriyɛ nan na ki ginɛ bɛ naxan di xɛmɛ barima, xa na mu a ra di ginɛ.

sentences.english: And if she has not money enough for a lamb, then let her take two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burned offering and the other for a sin-offering, and the priest will take away her sin and she will be clean,
sentences.susu: Xa fɛɛrɛ mu na a yi a xa yɛxɛɛ sɔtɔ, a nɔma ganbɛ firin xaninde, xa na mu a ra kolokonde firin. Keren xa ba sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ra, boore xa ba yunubi xafari sɛrɛxɛ ra. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na ba, a findi xunsare ra ginɛ bɛ, a fa sɛniyɛn.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa nun Haruna bɛ,

sentences.english: If a man has on his skin a growth or a mark or a white place, and it becomes the disease of a leper, let him be taken to Aaron the priest, or to one of the priests, his sons;
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi fate kiri yire nde funtu, xa na mu a ra a fiixɛ, xa na mu a ra a findi fi ra, wo xa na kanyi xanin sɛrɛxɛdubɛ Haruna yire, xa na mu a ra a xa di nde yire.

sentences.english: And if, when the priest sees the mark on his skin, the hair on the place is turned white and the mark seems to go deeper than the skin, it is the mark of a leper: and the priest, after looking at him, will say that he is unclean.
sentences.susu: Fure naxan na a fate, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na mato. Xa fate xabe bara fiixɛ na fi yire, fi fan bara tilin, a sube li, fure ɲaaxi na a ra. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: But if the mark on his skin is white, and does not seem to go deeper than the skin, and the hair on it is not turned white, then the priest will keep him shut up for seven days;
sentences.susu: Xa fure ya mu itilin a na kiri nan gbansan fari, fate xabe mu fiixɛxi na longori, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa furema yamari a xa lu a kerenyi ma lɔxɔxun keren.

sentences.english: And the priest is to see him on the seventh day; and if, in his opinion, the place on his skin has not become worse and is not increased in size, then the priest will keep him shut up for seven days more:
sentences.susu: A xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa a mato. Xa a sa li fure mu na lantanfe, a man xa furema yamari a xa lu a kerenyi ma lɔxɔxun keren.

sentences.english: And the priest is to see him again on the seventh day; and if the mark is less bright and is not increased on his skin, then let the priest say that he is clean: it is only a skin-mark, and after his clothing has been washed he will be clean.
sentences.susu: A xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa a mato a sanmaya firin nde. Xa fure ɲingi bara masara, a man mu lantanfe, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara sɛniyɛn. Fure na a ra naxan mu ɲaaxu. A xa a xa dugie xa, a findi mixi sɛniyɛnxi ra.

sentences.english: But if the size of the mark on his skin is increased after he has been seen by the priest, let him go to the priest again:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ bara a mato, fure bara lantan yɛ na masenyi dangi xanbi, furema man xa gbilen sɛrɛxɛdubɛ yire tɛmui gbɛtɛ.

sentences.english: And if, after looking at him, he sees that the mark is increased in his skin, let the priest say that he is unclean; he is a leper.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa a mato. Xa fure bara lantan yɛ, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi sɛniyɛntare ra, fure ɲaaxi na a ra.»

sentences.english: When the disease of a leper is seen on a man, let him be taken to the priest;
sentences.susu: «Xa fure ɲaaxi bara lu mixi nde kiri ma, e xa a xanin sɛrɛxɛdubɛ yire.

sentences.english: And if the priest sees that there is a white growth on the skin, and the hair is turned white, and there is diseased flesh in the growth,
sentences.susu: A xa a mato. Xa na mixi kiri bara fiixɛ yire nde, a fa funtu, fate xabe fan fa fiixɛ na longori, a bula, sube mini kɛnɛ ma,

sentences.english: It is an old disease in the skin of his flesh, and the priest will say that he is unclean; he will not have to be shut up, for he is clearly unclean.
sentences.susu: fure ɲaaxi na a ra naxan mu dandanma. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra. Hali a mu lu a kerenyi ma waxati di bun ma sɔnɔn, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa a mato. Na tan bara gɛ findide mixi sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: And if the disease comes out all over his skin, from his head to his feet, as far as the priest is able to see,
sentences.susu: Xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ bara a to a na fi ɲaaxi birin bara bari fɔlɔ, naxan nu na furema fate ma, kelife a sanyie ma han a xunyi,

sentences.english: And if the priest sees that all his flesh is covered with the leper's disease, the priest will say that he is clean: it is all turned white, he is clean.
sentences.susu: a xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara sɛniyɛn, barima fi birin bara bari fɔlɔ. A bara sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: But whenever diseased flesh is seen on him, he will be unclean.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa, fure sa bula, sube mini kɛnɛ ma, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: And when the priest sees the diseased flesh he will say that he is unclean; the diseased flesh is unclean, he is a leper.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ na fure bulaxi to, a xa masenyi ti, fi bulaxi mu sɛniyɛn, fure ɲaaxi na a ra.

sentences.english: Or if the diseased flesh is turned again and changed to white then he is to come to the priest,
sentences.susu: Xa sube bulaxi fa bari, furema xa siga sɛrɛxɛdubɛ yire.

sentences.english: And the priest will see him: and if the place is turned white, then the priest will say that he is free from the disease.
sentences.susu: A xa a mato. Xa fure bara bari, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, furema bara sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And if a bad place has come out on the skin and is well again,
sentences.susu: Xa suuri mini mixi ma, a fa yalan,

sentences.english: And on the same place there is a white growth of a bright mark, red and white, then let the priest see it;
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ na kiri fa fiixɛ, xa na mu a ra a gbeeli, na kanyi xa siga sɛrɛxɛdubɛ yire.

sentences.english: And after looking at it, if it seems to go deeper than the skin, and the hair on it is turned white, then the priest will say that the man is unclean: it is the leper's disease, it has come out in the bad place.
sentences.susu: A xa a mato. Xa fure ya bara itilin, a sube li, fate xabe bara fiixɛ na longori, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra. Fure ɲaaxi na a ra, naxan minixi suuri fɔxi.

sentences.english: But if, after looking at it, he sees that there are no white hairs on it, and it is not deeper than the skin, and it is not very bright, then let the priest keep him shut up for seven days:
sentences.susu: Xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ mu fate xabe fiixɛ to, fi fan mu tilin, a mu sube lixi, a mu fiixɛ a gbe ra, furema xa lu a kerenyi ma lɔxɔxun keren.

sentences.english: And if it is increasing on the skin, the priest will say that he is unclean: it is a disease.
sentences.susu: Xa fure bara lantan yɛ a fate ma, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra, fure ɲaaxi na a ra.

sentences.english: But if the bright mark keeps in the same place and gets no greater, it is the mark of the old wound, and the priest will say that he is clean.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa fure mu masaraxi a mu lantanxi a i, suuri barixi na a ra. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi mixi sɛniyɛnxi na a ra.»

sentences.english: Or if there is a burn on the skin of the flesh, and if the diseased flesh in the burn becomes a bright place, red and white or white,
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi fate bara gan tɛ ra tɛmui dangixi, a kiri fa bari, kɔnɔ fure gbeeli, xa na mu a ra fure fiixɛ fa mini na fɔxi,

sentences.english: The priest is to see it: and if the hair on the bright place is turned white and it seems to go deeper than the skin, he is a leper: it has come out in the burn, and the priest will say that he is unclean: it is the leper's disease.
sentences.susu: sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na mato. Xa furema fate xabe bara fiixɛ na fɔxi, fure bara tilin, a sube li, fure ɲaaxi na a ra, naxan bara mini fate ma kiri dɛnnaxɛ nu ganxi. Na sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra, barima fure ɲaaxi na a ra.

sentences.english: But if, after looking at it, the priest sees that there is no white hair on the bright place, and it is not deeper than the skin, and is not very bright, then let the priest keep him shut up for seven days:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ mu fate xabe fiixɛ to fure ma, fi fan ya mu itilin, a mu sube lixi, a mu fiixɛ a gbe ra, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na kanyi yamari a xa lu a kerenyi ma lɔxɔxun keren.

sentences.english: And the priest is to see him again on the seventh day; if it is increased in the skin, then the priest will say that he is unclean: it is the leper's disease.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa a mato xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ. Xa fure bara lantan yɛ a fate ma, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra, fure ɲaaxi na a ra.

sentences.english: And if the bright place keeps the same size and gets no greater on the skin, but is less bright, it is the effect of the burn, and the priest will say that he is clean: it is the mark of the burn.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa fure mu masaraxi, a mu lantanxi a i, a mu fiixɛ alɔ a singe, a fatanxi na kiri ganxi nan na. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi mixi sɛniyɛnxi na a ra. Nari na a ra kiri dɛnnaxɛ gan.»

sentences.english: And when a man or a woman has a disease on the head, or in the hair of the chin,
sentences.susu: «Xa fure lu xɛmɛ, xa na mu a ra ginɛ xunyi ma, xa na mu a ra a kenkenyi ma,

sentences.english: Then the priest is to see the diseased place: and if it seems to go deeper than the skin, and if there is thin yellow hair in it, then the priest will say that he is unclean: he has the mark of the leper's disease on his head or in the hair of his chin.
sentences.susu: sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na fure mato. Xa fi ya bara itilin, a sube li, fate xabe fiixɛ, a xurun, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra. Fure ɲaaxi na a ra naxan bara lu a xunyi ma, xa na mu a ra a kenkenyi ma.

sentences.english: And after looking at the diseased place, if it does not seem to go deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the priest will have him shut up for seven days:
sentences.susu: Xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ sa a to fure ya mu itilinfe, a mu sube life, fate xabe fɔɔrɛ mu na, a xa furema yamari a xa lu a kerenyi ma xi solofere bun ma.

sentences.english: And on the seventh day the priest will see the place: and if it is not increased, and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not seem to go deeper than the skin,
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na fure mato xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ. Xa fure mu lantanfe a i, fate xabe mu fiixɛ na longori, fi ya mu itilinxi, a mu sube lixi,

sentences.english: Then his hair is to be cut off, but not on the diseased place, and he is to be shut up for seven days more:
sentences.susu: na kanyi xa a xunsɛxɛ nun a dɛxabe bi a xa a ba fi ra. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa furema yamari a xa lu a kerenyi ma lɔxɔxun keren.

sentences.english: And on the seventh day the priest will see the place: and if it is not increased, and does not seem to go deeper than the skin, the priest will say that he is clean: and after his clothing has been washed he will be clean.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na fure man mato xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ. Xa a mu lantanxi a i, a ya mu itilinxi, a mu sube lixi, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi mixi sɛniyɛnxi na a ra. A xa a xa dugie xa, a sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: But if the disease in his skin becomes worse after he has been made clean,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi dangi xanbi, xa fure bara lantan yɛ furema fate ma,

sentences.english: Then the priest is to see him: and if the mark is increased, the priest, without looking for the yellow hair, will say that he is unclean.
sentences.susu: sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa a mato. Xa fure bara lantan yɛ, hali sɛrɛxɛdubɛ mu fate xabe fiixɛ fen. Na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: But if, in his opinion, the growth is stopped, and black hair has come up on it, the disease has gone; he is clean and the priest will say that he is clean.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa na fure mu lantanxi a i, fate xabe fɔɔrɛ nde tan bara mini, fure bara yalan. Na kanyi mixi sɛniyɛnxi na a ra. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi mixi sɛniyɛnxi na a ra.»

sentences.english: And if a man or a woman has bright marks on the skin of their flesh, that is, bright white marks,
sentences.susu: «Xa xɛmɛ, xa na mu a ra ginɛ fate kiri bara fiixɛ yire ndee,

sentences.english: Then the priest is to see them: and if the white marks on their skin are not very bright, it is a skin disease which has come out on the skin; he is clean.
sentences.susu: sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na mato. Xa na mu fiixɛ a gbe ra, kasi mɔɔli nde gbansan na a ra. A sɛniyɛn.»

sentences.english: And if a man's hair has come out and he has no hair, still he is clean.
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi nde xunsɛxɛ bara makɔn, tɛrɛrɛ kanyi na a ra, a mu ɲaaxu. Na kanyi sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And if the hair has gone from the front part of his head, so that he has no hair there, still he is clean.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde xunsɛxɛ makɔnxi a tigi dɛ biri gbansan nɛ, tɛrɛrɛ na a ra a mu ɲaaxu. Na kanyi sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: But if, on his head or on his brow, where he has no hair, there is a red and white place, it is the disease of the leper coming out on his head or on his brow.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa fure fiixɛ, xa na mu a ra fure gbeeli mini a xunyi ma, xa na mu a ra a tigi ma, fure ɲaaxi na a ra.

sentences.english: Then if the priest sees that the growth of the disease has become red and white on his head or on his brow where there is no hair, like the mark in the skin of a leper;
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa na mato. Xa na fure funtu naxan minixi a xunyi ma, a fiixɛ, xa na mu a ra a gbeeli alɔ fure ɲaaxi na ki naxɛ,

sentences.english: He is a leper and unclean; the priest is to say that he is most certainly unclean: the disease is in his head.
sentences.susu: furema na a ra, a mu sɛniyɛnxi. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na kanyi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛntare ra. Fure na a xunyi ma.»

sentences.english: And the leper who has the disease on him is to go about with signs of grief, with his hair loose and his mouth covered, crying, Unclean, unclean.
sentences.susu: «Na fure ɲaaxi kanyi xa dugi ibɔɔxi ragoro a ma, a xa a xunyi bi, a xa a dɛ xabe makoto a bɛlɛxɛ ra, a nu a fala a xui itexi ra ‹Sɛniyɛntare, Sɛniyɛntare.›

sentences.english: While the disease is on him, he will be unclean. He is unclean: let him keep by himself, living outside the tent-circle.
sentences.susu: Danmi na fure ɲaaxi na a ma, a mu sɛniyɛn. Fo a xa lu a kerenyi ma ɲama yonkinde fari ma.»

sentences.english: And any clothing of wool or of linen in which is the mark of the disease;
sentences.susu: «Na fure ɲaaxi nɔma lude dugi ma naxan yailanxi xuruse xabe ra, xa na mu a ra gɛsɛ fute ra.

sentences.english: If it is in the threads of the linen or of the wool, or in leather, or in anything made of skin;
sentences.susu: A man nɔma lude se nde dɛnbɛxi ma naxan yailanxi xuruse xabe ra, xa na mu a ra gɛsɛ fute ra. A man nɔma lude se nde ma naxan yailanxi xuruse kiri ra.

sentences.english: If there are red or green marks on the clothing, or on the leather, or in the threads of the cloth, or in anything made of skin, it is the leper's disease: let the priest see it.
sentences.susu: Xa na fure bara ifɔɔrɔ, xa na mu a ra a bara gbeeli dugi ma, kiri ma, xa na mu a ra se dɛnbɛxi ma, fure ɲaaxi na a ra. A xa masen sɛrɛxɛdubɛ bɛ, a xa na mato.

sentences.english: And after it has been seen by the priest, the thing which is so marked is to be shut up for seven days:
sentences.susu: Na fure na se naxan ma, na se xa ragata yire nde a kerenyi ma xi solofere bun ma.

sentences.english: And he is to see the mark on the seventh day; if the mark is increased in the clothing, or in the threads of the material, or in the leather, whatever the leather is used for, it is the disease biting into it: it is unclean.
sentences.susu: Xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa a mato. Xa na fure bara lantan yɛ i na dugi ma, xa na mu a ra na se dɛnbɛxi ma, xa na mu a ra na kiri ma, fure ɲaaxi na a ra. Na bara findi se sɛniyɛntare ra.

sentences.english: And the clothing, or the wool or linen material, or anything of leather in which is the disease, is to be burned: for the disease is biting into it; let it be burned in the fire.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa se birin gan na fure na se naxan ma, dugi naxan yailanxi xuruse xabe ra, dugi naxan yailanxi gɛsɛ fute ra, dugi dɛnbɛxi, xa na mu a ra kiri.

sentences.english: And if the priest sees that the mark is not increased in the clothing or in any part of the material or in the leather,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ bara a mato, na fure mu lantanxi na see ma,

sentences.english: Then the priest will give orders for the thing on which the mark is, to be washed, and to be shut up for seven days more:
sentences.susu: a xa yaamari fi na see xa maxa ye ra, e xa sa e kerenyi ma xi solofere bun ma sanmaya firin nde.

sentences.english: And if, after the mark has been washed, the priest sees that the colour of it is not changed and it is not increased, it is to be burned in the fire: the disease is working in it, though the damage may be inside or outside.
sentences.susu: A na gɛ maxade, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ man xa na mato. Xa fure mu masaraxi, hali a man mu lantanxi a i, na findixi se sɛniyɛntare nan na. A birin xa gan tɛ ra, hali fure na a lahalɛ kerenyi gbansan nan ma.

sentences.english: And if the priest sees that the mark is less bright after the washing, then let him have it cut out of the clothing or the leather or from the threads of the material:
sentences.susu: Xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ bara a to fure mu fiixɛ alɔ singe, a xa na yire gbansan ba na.

sentences.english: And if the mark is still seen in the clothing or in the threads of the material or in the leather, it is the disease coming out: the thing in which the disease is will have to be burned with fire.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa fure na lantanfe a i dugi ma, xa na mu a ra dugi dɛnbɛxi ma, xa na mu a ra kiri ma, fure ɲaaxi na a ra, fo na xa gan tɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the material of the clothing, or anything of skin, which has been washed, if the mark has gone out of it, let it be washed a second time and it will be clean.
sentences.susu: Xa fure bara ba dugi ma, xa na mu a ra dugi dɛnbɛxi ma, xa na mu a ra kiri ma ye ra a firin nde, a bara sɛniyɛn.»

sentences.english: This is the law about the leper's disease in the thread of wool or linen material, in clothing or in anything of skin, saying how it is to be judged clean or unclean.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ nan na ki fure ɲaaxi xa fe ra naxan nɔma lude dugi nde ma naxan yailanxi xuruse xabe ra, xa na mu a ra gɛsɛ fute ra, a nun dugi nde ma naxan dɛnbɛxi, a nun kiri nde ma. Na sɛriyɛ nɔma a masende xa se nde sɛniyɛn, xa na mu a mu sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to Moses,
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a masen Annabi Munsa bɛ,

sentences.english: This is the law of the leper on the day when he is made clean: he is to be taken to the priest;
sentences.susu: «Marasɛniyɛnyi lɔxɔɛ, fure ɲaaxi kanyi xa siga sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xɔn.

sentences.english: And the priest is to go outside the tent-circle; and if, after looking, the priest sees that the mark of the disease has gone from him,
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa siga ɲama yonkinde fari ma na furema matode. Xa a bara yalan,

sentences.english: Then the priest is to give orders to take, for him who is to be made clean, two living clean birds and some cedar wood and red thread and hyssop.
sentences.susu: sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa yaamari fi, a xa fa xɔni ɲiɲɛ radaxaxi firin na, e nun sɛdiri wuri, gɛrɛ mɔɔli nde, nun hisopi wuri furema bɛ.

sentences.english: And the priest will give orders for one of the birds to be put to death in a vessel made of earth, over flowing water.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa yaamari fi, e xa xɔni keren kɔn naxaba fɛɲɛ nde xun ma, dulon ye na naxan kui.

sentences.english: And he will take the living bird and the wood and the red thread and the hyssop and put them in the blood of the bird which was put to death over flowing water.
sentences.susu: A xa xɔni ɲiɲɛ tongo, a nun sɛdiri wuri, gɛrɛ mɔɔli nde, nun hisopi wuri, a xa e birin dukulu xɔni wuli xɔɔra e naxan kɔn naxabaxi dulon ye xun ma.

sentences.english: And shaking it seven times over the man who is to be made clean, he will say that he is clean and will let the living bird go free into the open country.
sentences.susu: A xa na kasan sanmaya solofere na furema ma, naxan lanma a xa sɛniyɛn. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa masenyi ti, na mixi bara findi mixi sɛniyɛnxi ra. Na tɛmui a xa xɔni ɲiɲɛ bɛɲin wula i.»

sentences.english: And he who is to be made clean will have his clothing washed and his hair cut and have a bath, and he will be clean. And after that he will come back to the tent-circle; but he is to keep outside his tent for seven days.
sentences.susu: «Naxan wama sɛniyɛnfe, a xa a xa dugie xa, a xa a fate maxabe bi, a xa a maxa ye ra. Na kui, a sɛniyɛnma nɛ. Na dangi xanbi a nɔma sode ɲama yonkinde kui, kɔnɔ a mu nɔma sode a xa kiri banxi tan kui xi solofere.

sentences.english: And on the seventh day he is to have all the hair cut off his head and his chin and over his eyes — all his hair is to be cut off — and he will have his clothing washed and his body bathed in water and he will be clean.
sentences.susu: Xi solofere nde lɔxɔɛ, a man xa a xunsɛxɛ bi, a dɛ xabe, a ya xinbi xabe, a nun a fate maxabe birin. A man xa a xa dugie xa, a xa a fate maxa. Na kui, a sɛniyɛnma nɛ.

sentences.english: And on the eighth day let him take two male lambs, without any marks on them, and one female lamb of the first year, without a mark, and three tenth parts of an ephah of the best meal, mixed with oil, and one log of oil.
sentences.susu: Xi solomasaxan nde lɔxɔɛ, a xa yɛxɛɛyɔrɛ xɛmɛma firin tongo, a nun yɛxɛɛ ginɛma, ɲɛ keren daaxi, lanyuru mu na naxee ma. A man xa sansi xɔri dinxi konbo ya keren nun a tagi sɔtɔ, ture masunbuxi naxan na, a nun ture sigaati ya keren naxan findima sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the priest who is making him clean will put the man who is being made clean, together with these things, before the door of the Tent of meeting.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ xa furema nun a xa sɛrɛxɛ ti n tan Alatala ya i hɔrɔmɔlingira sode dɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the priest is to take one of the male lambs and give it as an offering for wrongdoing, and the log of oil, waving them for a wave offering before the Lord;
sentences.susu: A xa yɛxɛɛyɔrɛ keren tongo, a xa a ba yɛtɛ ragbilen sɛrɛxɛ ra, a nun ture sigaati ya keren. A xa nee lintan n tan Alatala ya i.
