sentences.english: If in war a town is shut in by your armies for a long time, do not let its trees be cut down and made waste; for their fruit will be your food; are the trees of the countryside men for you to take up arms against them?
sentences.susu: Wo na taa nde bilin a gerefe ma, a mu lan wo xa beera tongo sansie sɛgɛ xili ma. E findima wo balose nan na. Na daaxa sansie xa mu findixi wo gerefae ra.

sentences.english: Only those trees which you are certain are not used for food may be cut down and put to destruction: and you are to make walls of attack against the town till it is taken.
sentences.susu: Sansi naxee bogi mu nɔma donde, wo nɔma nee tan sɛgɛde e xa findi geresose ra wo bɛ taa mixie xili ma, wo nun naxee na gerefe han e sa rayarabima wo bɛ tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: If, in the land which the Lord your God is giving you, you come across the dead body of a man in the open country, and you have no idea who has put him to death:
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li wo naxa mixi nde fure to bɔxi ma burunyi, wo Marigi Alatala dɛnnaxɛ fixi wo ma, kɔnɔ wo mu a faxama kolon sinden,

sentences.english: Then your responsible men and your judges are to come out, and give orders for the distance from the dead body to the towns round about it to be measured;
sentences.susu: wo xa forie nun wo xa kiitisae xa a mato taa mundun makɔrɛxi na fure ra.

sentences.english: And whichever town is nearest to the body, the responsible men of that town are to take from the herd a young cow which has never been used for work or put under the yoke;
sentences.susu: E na taa kolon naxan makɔrɛxi na ra, na taa forie xa ninge ginɛ tongo, naxan singe mu nu wali, wuri mu nu xiri naxan kɔn ma,

sentences.english: And they are to take the cow into a valley where there is flowing water, and which is not ploughed or planted, and there the neck of the cow is to be broken:
sentences.susu: e xa a xanin xure nde ma, naxan mu xɔrima, sansi mu rawalima dɛnnaxɛ, e xa a kobe gira ye xɔɔra.

sentences.english: Then the priests, the sons of Levi, are to come near; for they have been marked out by the Lord your God to be his servants and to give blessings in the name of the Lord; and by their decision every argument and every blow is to be judged:
sentences.susu: Na birin xa raba Lewi xa di sɛrɛxɛdubɛe ya xɔri, barima wo Marigi Alatala nee nan sugandixi a xa wali rabafe ma, e xa duba mixi bɛ Alatala xili ra, e xa kiiti sa gere xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And all the responsible men of that town which is nearest to the dead man, washing their hands over the cow whose neck was broken in the valley,
sentences.susu: Fori naxee birin na taa kui naxan makɔrɛxi fure yire ra, e xa e bɛlɛxɛe raxa ninge ginɛ fari, e naxan faxaxi xure kui.

sentences.english: Will say, This death is not the work of our hands and our eyes have not seen it.
sentences.susu: E xa a fala, «Muxu tan xa mu faxɛ tixi, muxu mu a rabama fan kolon.

sentences.english: Have mercy, O Lord, on your people Israel whom you have made free, and take away from your people the crime of a death without cause. Then they will no longer be responsible for the man's death.
sentences.susu: Alatala, i xa Isirayila ɲama xun sara, i naxan xɔrɛyaxi. Yandi, i naxa faxɛ kote dɔxɔ Isirayila xun ma, e fɔxi mu na naxan na.» Na tɛmui Alatala fama nɛ e xun sarade.

sentences.english: So you will take away the crime of a death without cause from among you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma ratangade yi faxɛ tife mɔɔli ma, xa wo Alatala waxɔnfe rabama.

sentences.english: When you go out to war against other nations, and the Lord your God gives them up into your hands and you take them as prisoners;
sentences.susu: Wo na siga wo yaxuie gerede, xa wo Marigi Alatala e rayarabi wo bɛ, wo e findi wo xa geelimanie ra,

sentences.english: If among the prisoners you see a beautiful woman and it is your desire to make her your wife;
sentences.susu: tɛmunde mixi nde ya fama nɛ sinde geelimani ginɛ tofanyi nde ma. Xa na kanyi wama a dɔxɔfe nɛ,

sentences.english: Then take her back to your house; and let her hair and her nails be cut;
sentences.susu: a nɔma a xaninde a xɔnyi. Na ginɛ xa a yɛtɛ xunyi bi, a a bɛlɛxɛ xale maxaba,

sentences.english: And let her take off the dress in which she was made prisoner and go on living in your house and weeping for her father and mother for a full month: and after that you may go in to her and be her husband and she will be your wife.
sentences.susu: a dugi fanyi ragoro a ma. A xa sabati a xa mɔri xɔnyi, a fa a baba nun a nga xa ɲɔnfe raba kike keren bun ma. Na dangi xanbi xɛmɛ nɔma a findide a xa ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: But if you have no delight in her, you are to let her go wherever she will; you may not take a price for her as if she was your property, for you have made use of her for your pleasure.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li a xa fe naxa raɲaaxu a ma, a nɔma a bɛɲinde a xa siga a waxɔnde, kɔnɔ a mu lanma a xa a mati kɔbiri ra, a mu lanma a xa findi a xa konyi ra, barima a nu bara findi a xa ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: If a man has two wives, one greatly loved and the other hated, and the two of them have had children by him; and if the first son is the child of the hated wife:
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li ginɛ firin na xɛmɛ nde yi ra, keren fa rafan a ma dangi boore ra, kɔnɔ e firinyie bara di bari a bɛ, a mu lanma a xa baatɛ ginɛ xa di rafisa a boore xa di bɛ,

sentences.english: Then when he gives his property to his sons for their heritage, he is not to put the son of his loved one in the place of the first son, the son of the hated wife:
sentences.susu: a fa foriɲa tide fi baatɛ ginɛ xa di ma, a fa a li na ginɛ boore nan singe di barixi a bɛ.

sentences.english: But he is to give his first son his birthright, and twice as great a part of his property: for he is the first-fruits of his strength and the right of the first son is his.
sentences.susu: A lanma a xa a kolon ginɛ naxan naɲaaxuxi a ma na ki, na nan ma di findixi di singe ra. A harige dɔxɔ firin nan soma di fori yi ra, barima na nan findixi a xa fonike di ra. A tan nan lanma a xa di foriɲa tide sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: If a man has a son who is hard-hearted and uncontrolled, who gives no attention to the voice of his father and mother, and will not be ruled by them, though they give him punishment:
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li xɛmɛ nde naxa di xɛmɛ kalabante xurutare bari, naxan mu a tuli matixi a baba nun a nga xui ra, naxan tondima birade e xa sɛriyɛ fɔxɔ ra,

sentences.english: Then let his father and mother take him to the responsible men of the town, to the public place;
sentences.susu: a lanma na di baba nun a nga xa a suxu, e xa a xanin forie xɔn ma taa sode dɛ ra.

sentences.english: And say to them, This son of ours is hard-hearted and uncontrolled, he will not give attention to us; he gives himself up to pleasure and strong drink.
sentences.susu: E xa a fala e bɛ, «Muxu xa di naxan yi ki, a xurutare, a kalabante. Muxu fe naxan birin falama a bɛ, a mu a tuli matima a ra, fo wayuɲa rabafe nun siisi fe.»

sentences.english: Then he is to be stoned to death by all the men of the town: so you are to put away the evil from among you; and all Israel, hearing of it, will be full of fear.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a xa taa xɛmɛ birin xa a magɔnɔ gɛmɛ ra, han a faxa. Wo fe ɲaaxi ɲɔnma wo tagi na ki nɛ. Isirayilakae na na fe mɛ, gaaxui luma nɛ e birin ma.

sentences.english: If a man does a crime for which the punishment is death, and he is put to death by hanging him on a tree;
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li wo bara mixi gbaku wuri kɔn na, naxan bara yunubi fe raba a lan a xa faxa naxan ma,

sentences.english: Do not let his body be on the tree all night, but put it to rest in the earth the same day; for the man who undergoes hanging is cursed by God; so do not make unclean the land which the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage.
sentences.susu: a fure mu lan a xa lu wuri kɔn na han gɛɛsɛgɛ. A lan nɛ a xa ragata na lɔxɔɛ kerenyi, barima Ala bara fure gbakuxi danka. Wo wo mɛɛni ki fanyi ra, xa na mu a ra na fure gbakuxi nan bɔxi dankama, wo Marigi Alatala dɛnnaxɛ fixi wo ma kɛ ra.

sentences.english: If you see your brother's ox or his sheep wandering, do not go by without helping, but take them back to your brother.
sentences.susu: Wo na wo ngaxakerenyi xa ninge, xa na mu a ra a xa yɛxɛɛ to, a murutaxi, wo naxa wo kobe ti a ra. Wo lan nɛ wo xa a xanin a kanyi xɔn ma.

sentences.english: If their owner is not near, or if you are not certain who he is, then take the beast to your house and keep it till its owner comes in search of it, and then you are to give it back to him.
sentences.susu: Xa wo ngaxakerenyi yire makuya, xa na mu wo mu a kanyi kolon, wo xa xuruse xanin wo xɔnyi. Wo a ragata han beenun wo a kanyi toma tɛmui naxɛ, wo fa a so a yi ra.

sentences.english: Do the same with his ass or his robe or anything which has gone from your brother's keeping and which you have come across: do not keep it to yourself.
sentences.susu: Wo na mɔɔli nan nabama wo ngaxakerenyi xa sofale fan na, a xa donma, a nun a gbe se naxan birin lɔɛxi a ma. Wo mu lan wo xa wo kobe ti a ra.

sentences.english: If you see your brother's ox or his ass falling down on the road, do not go by without giving him help in lifting it up again.
sentences.susu: Xa wo bara wo ngaxakerenyi xa sofale, xa na mu a ra a xa ninge to, a bara bira kira xɔn ma, wo mu lan wo xa wo kobe ti a ra. Wo lan nɛ wo xa kafu a ma a rakelide.

sentences.english: It is not right for a woman to be dressed in man's clothing, or for a man to put on a woman's robe: whoever does such things is disgusting to the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ mu lan a xa xɛmɛ dugi so. Xɛmɛ fan mu lan a xa ginɛ dugi so. Mixi naxee na fe mɔɔli rabama, na kanyie mu rafan Marigi Alatala ma.

sentences.english: If by chance you see a place which a bird has made for itself in a tree or on the earth, with young ones or eggs, and the mother bird seated on the young ones or on the eggs, do not take the mother bird with the young:
sentences.susu: Wo na a to kira xɔn ma, xɔni bara a tɛɛ sa wuri kɔn na, xa na mu a ra bɔxi ma, a nga felenxi a xɛlɛ ma, xa na mu a ra a xa die ma, wo mu lan wo xa a nga nun a xa die birin tongo.

sentences.english: See that you let the mother bird go, but the young ones you may take; so it will be well for you and your life will be long.
sentences.susu: Wo lan nɛ wo xa a nga tan nabɛɲin, a xa siga, wo fa die tan tongo. Na kui wo fama nɛ simaya xɔnkuye nun hɛɛri sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: If you are building a house, make a railing for the roof, so that the blood of any man falling from it will not come on your house.
sentences.susu: Xa wo banxi nɛɛnɛ ti, wo lan nɛ wo xa bilixi nde rabilin banxi fuge ra, alako mixi naxee tema naa, e naxa bira, e fa faxa wo saabui ra.

sentences.english: Do not have your vine-garden planted with two sorts of seed: or all of it may become a loss, the seed you have put in as well as the increase.
sentences.susu: Wo mu lan wo xa sansi gbɛtɛ si wo xa wɛni bilie ya ma, xa na mu a ra a bogi fama findide se raharamuxi nan na.

sentences.english: Do not do your ploughing with an ox and an ass yoked together.
sentences.susu: Wo nɛ yire buxama, wo mu lan wo xa ninge nun sofale xiri e boore ra sari ra.

sentences.english: Do not have clothing made of two sorts of thread, wool and linen together.
sentences.susu: Wo mu lan wo xa sose ragoro wo ma naxan masunbuxi dugi yɛxɛɛ xabe daaxi nun gɛsɛ fute daaxi ra.

sentences.english: On the four edges of your robe, with which your body is covered, put ornaments of twisted threads.
sentences.susu: Wo gɛsɛ nan nafalama ponpon na wo a singan wo xa dugi tuxui naanie ra, wo naxan felenma wo ma.

sentences.english: If any man takes a wife, and having had connection with her, has no delight in her,
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li xɛmɛ nde naxa ginɛ dɔxɔ, e kafu, kɔnɔ a xa fe to raɲaaxu xɛmɛ ma,

sentences.english: And says evil things about her and gives her a bad name, saying, I took this woman, and when I had connection with her it was clear to me that she was not a virgin:
sentences.susu: a a xili kana wɔyɛn kobi ra, a nu fa a fala, «N bara yi ginɛ dɔxɔ, kɔnɔ muxu to kafu n naxa a li a bara futi kana,»

sentences.english: Then let the girl's father and mother put before the responsible men of the town, in the public place, signs that the girl was a virgin:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui ginɛ baba nun a nga xa ginɛdimɛdi dugi xanin taa forie xɔn ma taa sode dɛ ra, naxan a masenxi a e xa di futi rasoxi.

sentences.english: And let the girl's father say to the responsible men, I gave my daughter to this man for his wife, but he has no love for her;
sentences.susu: A baba xa a tagi raba, «N bara n ma di ginɛ fi yi xɛmɛ ma, kɔnɔ a mu rafan a ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: And now he has put shame on her, saying that she is not a virgin; but here is the sign that she is a virgin. Then they are to put her clothing before the responsible men of the town.
sentences.susu: A fa wule nan safe a xun ma a a mu futi rasoxi.» Na tɛmui tɛmɛdi xa mixie xa na ginɛdimɛdi dugi itala taa forie ya i.

sentences.english: Then the responsible men of the town are to give the man his punishment;
sentences.susu: Taa forie na na to, e xa na xɛmɛ suxu, e xa a ɲaxankata.

sentences.english: They will take from him a hundred shekels of silver, which are to be given to the father of the girl, because he has given an evil name to a virgin of Israel: she will go on being his wife, he may never put her away all his life.
sentences.susu: E na a makiiti, e xa alamani bolon a ma naxan findima kɔbiri kole kɛmɛ sofe ra tɛmɛdi baba yi ra, Isirayila ginɛ xili kanafe ma. Na xanbi a lan nɛ ginɛ xa gbilen xɛmɛ xɔnyi, na xɛmɛ naxa mɛɛ a ra abadan.

sentences.english: But if what he has said is true, and she is seen to be not a virgin,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa futi kanafe fa sa findi nɔndi ra, ginɛdimɛdi dugi yo mu na naxan a masenma a bara futi raso,

sentences.english: Then they are to make the girl come to the door of her father's house and she will be stoned to death by the men of the town, because she has done evil and put shame on Israel, by acting as a loose woman in her father's house: so you are to put away evil from among you.
sentences.susu: na ginɛ xa xanin a baba xa banxi sode dɛ ra, taa mixie fa a magɔnɔ gɛmɛ ra han a faxa, barima a bara fe kobi raba ginɛ mu lan a xa naxan naba Isirayila bɔxi ma, xɛmɛ fe kolonfe ra a na a baba xa nɔɛ bun ma tɛmui naxɛ. Wo fe ɲaaxi ɲɔnma wo tagi na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: If a man is taken in the act of going in to a married woman, the two of them, the man as well as the woman, are to be put to death: so you are to put away the evil from Israel.
sentences.susu: Xa wo xɛmɛ suxu, e nun ginɛ xɛmɛ taa idɔxɔɛ saxi, na fe kobi raba firinyie lan nɛ e xa faxa, ginɛ nun xɛmɛ. Wo fe ɲaaxi ɲɔnma na ki nɛ wo tagi Isirayila bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: If a young virgin has given her word to be married to a man, and another man meeting her in the town, has connection with her;
sentences.susu: Xa xɛmɛ naralan ginɛ dimɛdi nde ra taa kui, kote bara dɔxɔ naxan ma fe ra, a fa a futi kana,

sentences.english: Then you are to take the two of them to the doorway of the town, and have them stoned to death; the young virgin, because she gave no cry for help, though it was in the town, and the man, because he has put shame on his neighbour's wife: so you are to put away evil from among you.
sentences.susu: wo xa na mixi firinyie xanin taa sode dɛ ra, wo e magɔnɔ gɛmɛ ra han e xa faxa. Yi ginɛ dimɛdi faxaxi nɛ, barima a mu sɔnxɔɛ ratexi taa kui. Xɛmɛ fan faxaxi nɛ, barima a bara ginɛ futi kana kote bara dɔxɔ naxan ma fe ra. Wo fe ɲaaxi ɲɔnma wo tagi na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: But if the man, meeting such a virgin in the open country, takes her by force, then only the man is to be put to death;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa xɛmɛ naralan ginɛ dimɛdi ra wula i, kote bara dɔxɔ naxan ma fe ra, a naxa dutun a ma, a a futi kana, na xɛmɛ nan keren lan a xa faxa.

sentences.english: Nothing is to be done to the virgin, because there is no cause of death in her: it is the same as if a man made an attack on his neighbour and put him to death:
sentences.susu: Wo naxa fefe raba ginɛ dimɛdi tan na, barima a mu fe ɲaaxi yo rabaxi a lan a xa faxa naxan ma. Yi fe maniyaxi nɛ alɔ xɛmɛ naxan waxi a boore faxafe.

sentences.english: For he came across her in the open country, and there was no one to come to the help of the virgin in answer to her cry.
sentences.susu: Na naralanyi rabaxi wula nɛ. Hali yi ginɛ dimɛdi xɛmɛ kanyi sɔnxɔɛ rate nu, mixi yo mu sɔtɔma naxan nɔma a ratangade.

sentences.english: If a man sees a young virgin, who has not given her word to be married to anyone, and he takes her by force and has connection with her, and discovery is made of it;
sentences.susu: Xa xɛmɛ naralan ginɛ dimɛdi ra kote mu nu dɔxɔ naxan ma fe ra, a naxa bagan a ma, a a futi kana, mixi nde fa e suxu na fe xun,

sentences.english: Then the man will have to give the virgin's father fifty shekels of silver and make her his wife, because he has put shame on her; he may never put her away all his life.
sentences.susu: na xɛmɛ kɔbiri kole tongo suuli nan soma ginɛ baba yi ra, a fa yi ginɛ dɔxɔ, barima a bara a futi kana. A xa simaya kui, a mu lan a xa mɛɛ na ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: No man whose private parts have been wounded or cut off may come into the meeting of the Lord's people.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu lan a nun a baba xa ginɛ xa kafu. A tana fe nan na ra a baba mabiri.

sentences.english: One whose father and mother are not married may not come into the meeting of the Lord's people, or any of his family to the tenth generation.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan xɛmɛya kanaxi, xa na mu a ra a bolonxi, na kanyi mu lan a xa siga Alatala xa malanyi.

sentences.english: No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their people to the tenth generation may come into the meeting of the Lord's people:
sentences.susu: Yangamadi fan mu sigama Alatala xa malanyi hali a bɔnsɔɛ fu nde.

sentences.english: Because they gave you no bread or water on your way, when you came out of Egypt: and they got Balaam, the son of Peor, from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to put curses on you.
sentences.susu: Amonikae nun Mowabakae mu sigama Alatala xa malanyi hali e bɔnsɔɛ fu nde.

sentences.english: But the Lord your God would not give ear to Balaam, but let the curse be changed into a blessing to you, because of his love for you.
sentences.susu: A luma e bɛ na ki nɛ kudɛi barima yi ɲamae mu fa wo ralande taami nun ye ra, wo nu na kira xɔn ma tɛmui naxɛ wo kelixi Misira. E Beyori xa di xɛmɛ Balami nan sare fi wo dankafe ma Petori, Mesopotamiya bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: Do nothing for their peace or well-being for ever.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo Marigi Alatala mu tin a tuli matide Balami ra. A naxa na dankɛ masara barakɛ ra barima wo rafan wo Marigi Alatala ma.

sentences.english: But have no hate for an Edomite, because he is your brother, or for an Egyptian, for you were living in his land.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo ɲɛngi sa e xa bɔɲɛsa nun e xa baloe fe xɔn ma wo xa simaya kui.

sentences.english: Their children in the third generation may come into the meeting of the Lord's people.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa fe ɲaaxi yo raba Edonkae ra, barima wo ngaxakerenyi nan na e ra. Wo naxa fe ɲaaxi yo niya Misirakae ra, barima wo saxanyi raba nɛ e xa bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: When you go out to war and put your tents in position, keep from every evil thing.
sentences.susu: E fama bɔnsɔɛ naxee sɔtɔde, fo e tolobitɛe, nee nan fama sigade Alatala xa malanyi.

sentences.english: If any man among you becomes unclean through anything which has taken place in the night, he is to go out from the tent-circle and keep outside it:
sentences.susu: Wo na mini fafe ra tide wo yaxuie ya ra, wo lan nɛ wo xa wo yɛtɛ ratanga fe kobi birin ma.

sentences.english: But when evening comes near, let him take a bath: and after sundown he may come back to the tents.
sentences.susu: Xa xɛmɛ nde na wo ya ma naxan mu sɛniyɛnxi, a bara makana wantanyi kui, a lan nɛ a xa mini sɔɔri tɛtɛ fari ma.

sentences.english: Let there be a place outside the tent-circle to which you may go;
sentences.susu: Nunmare ra, a na a maxa ye ra, soge goro tɛmui a fa so sɔɔri tɛtɛ kui.

sentences.english: And have among your arms a spade; and when you have been to that place, let that which comes from you be covered up with earth:
sentences.susu: Wo fama yire nde nan sugandide dɛnnaxɛ makuya sɔɔri tɛtɛ ra, naa xa findi suturade ra.

sentences.english: For the Lord your God is walking among your tents, to keep you safe and to give up into your hands those who are fighting against you; then let your tents be holy, so that he may see no unclean thing among you, and be turned away from you.
sentences.susu: Yili ge se nde lan nɛ a xa lu wo xa kote i. Wo na siga suturade, wo yili ge. Wo na gɛ wo hayi rabade, wo a makoto, wo fa keli naa.

sentences.english: Do not give back to his master a servant who has gone in flight from his master and come to you:
sentences.susu: Wo xa sɔɔri tɛtɛ lan nɛ a xa sɛniyɛn, barima wo Marigi Alatala a maɲɛrɛma a kui wo kantafe ra, a man fa wo yaxuie rayarabi wo bɛ. Xa a fe ɲaaxi li sɔɔri tɛtɛ kui, a a makuyama nɛ wo ra.

sentences.english: Let him go on living among you in whatever place is most pleasing to him: do not be hard on him.
sentences.susu: Xa konyi nde a gi a kanyi ma, a naxa siga lude wo xɔnyi, wo naxa gbilen a ra a kanyi xɔn ma de.

sentences.english: No daughter of Israel is to let herself be used as a loose woman for a strange god, and no son of Israel is to give himself to a man.
sentences.susu: A lan nɛ a xa sabati wo xa taa nde kui dɛnnaxɛ na rafan a ma. Wo man naxa a tɔɔrɔ de.

sentences.english: Do not take into the house of the Lord your God, as an offering for an oath, the price of a loose woman or the money given to one used for sex purposes in the worship of the gods: for these two things are disgusting to the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Isirayila xɛmɛ, xa na mu a ginɛ mu lan a xa langoeɲa raba.

sentences.english: Do not take interest from an Israelite on anything, money or food or any other goods, which you let him have:
sentences.susu: Langoe sare mu lan a xa so wo Marigi Alatala xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui laayidi rakamalise ra, barima wo Marigi Alatala na fe mɔɔli xɔnxi.

sentences.english: From men of other nations you may take interest, but not from an Israelite: so that the blessing of the Lord your God may be on everything to which you put your hand, in the land which you are about to take as your heritage.
sentences.susu: Wo na se nde doni wo ngaxakerenyi bɛ, kɔbiri, donse, xa na mu a ra se gbɛtɛ, wo naxa geeni yo fen a fari.

sentences.english: When you take an oath to the Lord, do not be slow to give effect to it: for without doubt the Lord your God will make you responsible, and will put it to your account as sin.
sentences.susu: Ala kolontare nan lanma a xa wo xa geeni sa, kɔnɔ wo ngaxakerenyi tan mu a ra de. Wo na na sɛriyɛ rabatu bɔxi ma wo fama dɛnnaxɛ sɔtɔde, wo Marigi Alatala barakɛ sama nɛ wo isofe birin ma.

sentences.english: But if you take no oath, there will be no sin.
sentences.susu: Wo na daakan tongo wo Marigi Alatala bɛ, wo naxa taxiri a rabafe ma, xa na mu wo Marigi Alatala a maxɔrinma nɛ wo ma, wo fa findide yunubitɔɛe ra.

sentences.english: Whatever your lips have said, see that you do it; for you gave your word freely to the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Xa wo mu daakan tongoxi, yunubi fe mu na.

sentences.english: When you go into your neighbour's vine-garden, you may take of his grapes at your pleasure, but you may not take them away in your vessel.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa wo daakan tongo wo Marigi Alatala bɛ, wo lan nɛ wo xa a raba keren na a fanyi ra. Wo fa a raba alɔ wo a ɲanigexi wo dɛ ra ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: When you go into your neighbour's field, you may take the heads of grain with your hand; but you may not put your blade to his grain.
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma wuri bogi ndee bade wo gbe mu naxee ra, wo a don han wo luga, kɔnɔ a mu lan wo xa nde sa wo xa kote i.

sentences.english: If a man takes a wife, and after they are married she is unpleasing to him because of some bad quality in her, let him give her a statement in writing and send her away from his house.
sentences.susu: A nɔma a lide xɛmɛ nde xa ginɛ mu rafanxi a ma sɔnɔn, a fatan kɛɛdi sɛbɛ, a a so a yi ra, a fa a rasiga a baba xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And when she has gone away from him, she may become another man's wife.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui xa na ginɛ dɔxɔ xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ xɔn ma,

sentences.english: And if the second husband has no love for her and, giving her a statement in writing, sends her away; or if death comes to the second husband to whom she was married;
sentences.susu: a xa fe raɲaaxu na xɛmɛ fan ma, na fan fa fatan kɛɛdi sɛbɛ, a a so a yi ra, a fa a rasiga a baba xɔnyi, xa na xɛmɛ fa sa faxa nɛ,

sentences.english: Her first husband, who had sent her away, may not take her back after she has been wife to another; for that is disgusting to the Lord: and you are not to be a cause of sin in the land which the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage.
sentences.susu: xɛmɛ naxan singe mɛɛ na ginɛ ra, na mu lan a xa a findi a xa ginɛ ra kɔrɛ, barima a bara raharamuɲa a ma. Alatala na fe mɔɔli xɔnxi. Wo mu lan wo xa na yunubi mɔɔli raba bɔxi ma wo Marigi Alatala dɛnnaxɛ fixi wo ma kɛ ra.

sentences.english: A newly married man will not have to go out with the army or undertake any business, but may be free for one year, living in his house for the comfort of his wife.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ naxan baxi ginɛ dɔxɔde, a mu lan a xa sɔɔriɲa raba waxati nde bun ma. Kɔntɔfili gbɛtɛ yo mu lan a xa dɔxɔ a ra ɲɛ keren bun ma, alako a xa mɛɛni a xa ginɛ dɔxɔxi ma.

sentences.english: No one is to take, on account of a debt, the stones with which grain is crushed: for in doing so he takes a man's living.
sentences.susu: Wo mu lan wo xa mulunyi nun kile rasuxu mixi yi sɛɛkɛ ra, xa na mu a ra kile gbansan, barima wo a balose nan bama a yi ra na ki.

sentences.english: If a man takes by force one of his countrymen, the children of Israel, using him as his property or getting a price for him, that thief is to be put to death: so you are to put away evil from among you.
sentences.susu: Xa Isirayilaka a ngaxakerenyi nde suxu nɔɛ ra, a a findi konyi ra, xa na mu a a mati, a lan nɛ na kanyi xa faxa. Wo fe ɲaaxi ɲɔnma wo tagi na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: In connection with the leper's disease, take care to keep and do every detail of the teaching of the priests, the Levites: as I gave them orders, so you are to do.
sentences.susu: Wo lan nɛ wo xa fɛntɛn kunɛ fure xa fe ra. N xaranyi naxan soxi Lewi xa di sɛrɛxɛdubɛe yi, wo lan nɛ wo xa na raba a raba ki ma.

sentences.english: Keep in mind what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the way, when you came out of Egypt.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu a ma a wo Marigi Alatala naxan naba Mariyama ra wo kelixi Misira tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: If you let your brother have the use of anything which is yours, do not go into his house and take anything of his as a sign of his debt;
sentences.susu: Wo na doni ti wo ngaxakerenyi bɛ, a mu lanma wo tan xa so a xɔnyi a xa sɛɛkɛ se tongode.

sentences.english: But keep outside till he comes out and gives it to you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa lu tande, wo xa donifa xa fa sɛɛkɛ se ra wo xɔn ma, a a so wo yi ra.

sentences.english: If he is a poor man, do not keep his property all night;
sentences.susu: Xa setare na a ra, a fa a xa xinbeli donma so wo yi sɛɛkɛ se ra, wo mu lan wo xa na ragata wo xɔnyi kɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: But be certain to give it back to him when the sun goes down, so that he may have his clothing for sleeping in, and will give you his blessing: and this will be put to your account as righteousness before the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a ragbilen a ma soge goro waxati nɛ, alako a xa a felen a ma kɔɛ ra. Na kui a Ala maxandima nɛ wo bɛ. Setare malife na ki a findima tinxinyi nan na wo nun wo Marigi Alatala tagi.

sentences.english: Do not be hard on a servant who is poor and in need, if he is one of your countrymen or a man from another nation living with you in your land.
sentences.susu: Wo mu lan wo xa wo xa walikɛ setaree tɔɔrɔ, e findi wo ngaxakerenyie ra, xa na mu e findi xɔɲɛe ra.

sentences.english: Give him his payment day by day, not keeping it back over night; for he is poor and his living is dependent on it; and if his cry against you comes to the ears of the Lord, it will be judged as sin in you.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔɛ birin wo lan nɛ wo xa e xa wali sare fi e ma beenun soge xa goro, barima setare nan e ra, e hayi na na ma. Xa wo mu na rabama, a mawama nɛ Alatala bɛ wo xa fe ra, wo fa yunubi sɔtɔ na kui.

sentences.english: Fathers are not to be put to death for their children or children for their fathers: every man is to be put to death for the sin which he himself has done.
sentences.susu: Di babae mu lan e xa faxa e xa die xa yunubie rabafe ma. Die fan mu lan e xa faxa e babae xa yunubie rabafe ma. Ibunadama lanma a xa faxa a yɛtɛ xa yunubi rabaxi nan ma.

sentences.english: Be upright in judging the cause of the man from a strange country and of him who has no father; do not take a widow's clothing on account of a debt:
sentences.susu: Wo naxa tinxintareya raba mixie ra naxee faxi sabatide wo xa bɔxi ma. Wo naxa kiridie tɔɔrɔ. Wo naxa kaaɲɛ ginɛ xa donma tongo sɛɛkɛ ra.

sentences.english: But keep in mind that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God made you free: for this is why I give you orders to do this.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu a ma a wo Marigi Alatala wo xɔrɛyaxi ki naxɛ wo xa konyiya kui Misira bɔxi ma. Na fe na a toxi n yi yaamari fixi wo ma.

sentences.english: When you get in the grain from your field, if some of the grain has been dropped by chance in the field, do not go back and get it, but let it be for the man from a strange land, the child without a father, and the widow: so that the blessing of the Lord your God may be on all the work of your hands.
sentences.susu: Wo na gɛ xɛ xabade, wo naxa gbilen tɔnsɔɛ dɔnxɔɛe tongo ra. Wo xa e lu xɔɲɛe, kiridie, nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe bɛ, alako wo Marigi Alatala xa barakɛ sa wo xa fe.

sentences.english: When you are shaking the fruit from your olive-trees, do not go over the branches a second time: let some be for the man from a strange land, the child without a father, and the widow.
sentences.susu: Wo na gɛ oliwi bili ifuyanfuyande, wo naxa gbilen bogi dɔnxɔɛe bade sansie kɔn na. Wo xa e lu xɔɲɛe, kiridie, nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe bɛ.

sentences.english: When you are pulling the grapes from your vines, do not take up those which have been dropped; let them be for the man from a strange land, the child without a father, and the widow.
sentences.susu: Wo na gɛ wɛni bogi bade, wo naxa gbilen bogi dɔnxɔɛe ba ra. Wo xa e lu xɔɲɛe, kiridie, nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe bɛ.

sentences.english: Keep in mind that you were a servant in the land of Egypt: for this is why I give you orders to do this.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu wo xa konyiya ma Misira bɔxi ma. Na fe na a toxi n yi yaamari fixi wo ma.

sentences.english: If there is an argument between men and they go to law with one another, let the judges give their decision for the upright, and against the wrongdoer.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li mixi firin naxa gere, kiitisa xa e mato tinxinyi kui sɛriyɛ ki ma.

sentences.english: And if the wrongdoer is to undergo punishment by whipping, the judge will give orders for him to go down on his face and be whipped before him, the number of the blows being in relation to his crime.
sentences.susu: Nɔndi mu na naxan bɛ, xa a lanma a xa bɔnbɔ, na xa raba kiitisa ya xɔri fe rabaxi bɛrɛ ma.

sentences.english: He may be given forty blows, not more; for if more are given, your brother may be shamed before you.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo mu lan wo xa dangi luxusinyi ya tongo naani ra. Xa wo nde sa na fari, wo bara wo ngaxakerenyi rayarabi.

sentences.english: Do not keep the ox from taking the grain when he is crushing it.
sentences.susu: Wo na ninge rawali mɛngi turuxunde tɛmui naxɛ, wo mu lan wo xa a dɛ xiri.

sentences.english: If brothers are living together and one of them, at his death, has no son, the wife of the dead man is not to be married outside the family to another man: let her husband's brother go in to her and make her his wife, doing as it is right for a brother-in-law to do.
sentences.susu: Xa ngaxakerenma firin sabati yire keren, keren fa faxa a ditare ra, a xa kaaɲɛ ginɛ mu lan a xa dɔxɔ xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ xɔn ma xabilɛ gbɛtɛ kui. A lan a xa dɔxɔ a nimɔxɔ nan xɔn ma, a findi a xa ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: Then the first male child she has will take the rights of the brother who is dead, so that his name may not come to an end in Israel.
sentences.susu: Na ginɛ di singe naxan barima a nimɔxɔ bɛ, a xa findi a xa mɔri singe xa di nan na kɛ ki ma, alako a xa mɔri xili naxa lɔɛ Isirayila bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: But if the man says he will not take his brother's wife, then let the wife go to the responsible men of the town, and say, My husband's brother will not keep his brother's name living in Israel; he will not do what it is right for a husband's brother to do.
sentences.susu: Xa na xɛmɛ tondi a nimɔxɔ dɔxɔde, kaaɲɛ ginɛ xa siga taa forie nan xɔn ma kiitisae yire, a a tagi raba e bɛ yi ki, «N nimɔxɔ bara tondi bɔnsɔɛ fide a ngaxakerenyi ma, a mu tinma a xa sɛriyɛ rakamalide n tan mabiri.»

sentences.english: Then the responsible men of the town will send for the man, and have talk with him: and if he still says, I will not take her;
sentences.susu: Taa forie xa na xɛmɛ xili, e xa na fe mato. Xa na xɛmɛ tondi a ngaxakerenyi xa kaaɲɛ ginɛ dɔxɔde,

sentences.english: Then his brother's wife is to come to him, before the responsible men of the town, and take his shoe off his foot, and put shame on him, and say, So let it be done to the man who will not take care of his brother's name.
sentences.susu: kaaɲɛ ginɛ xa a makɔrɛ a ra taa forie ya xɔri, a xa a nimɔxɔ xa sankiri ba, a dɛye bɔxun a yatagi, a falafe ra, «Yi mɔɔli nan lan a xa raba xɛmɛ ra naxan tondima bɔnsɔɛ fide a ngaxakerenyi ma.»

sentences.english: And his family will be named in Israel, The house of him whose shoe has been taken off.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Isirayila, na xɛmɛ xa denbaya xili falama nɛ, «Sankiri ba xa denbaya.»

sentences.english: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one of them, coming to the help of her husband, takes the other by the private parts;
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li xɛmɛ firin na gerefe, keren xa ginɛ fa siga a xa mɔri bade boore yi ra a xɛmɛya suxufe ra,

sentences.english: Her hand is to be cut off; have no pity on her.
sentences.susu: wo xa na ginɛ bɛlɛxɛ bolon, wo naxa kinikini a ma.

sentences.english: Do not have in your bag different weights, a great and a small;
sentences.susu: Wo naxa kiloe kamalitare sa wo xa gbɔnfɔɛ kui, ndee binya, booree yelebu.

sentences.english: Or in your house different measures, a great and a small.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa se maniyase kamalitare fan lu wo xɔnyi, ndee xungbo, booree xurun.

sentences.english: But have a true weight and a true measure: so that your life may be long in the land which the Lord your God is giving you.
sentences.susu: Kiloe kamalixi nun se maniyase kamalixi nan lan a xa lu wo yi ra. Na tɛmui wo fama nɛ simaya xɔnkuye sɔtɔde bɔxi ma wo Marigi Alatala fama dɛnnaxɛ sode wo yi ra.

sentences.english: For all who do such things, and all whose ways are not upright, are disgusting to the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo na mɔɔli rabama, a mu rafanma wo Marigi Alatala ma.

sentences.english: Keep in mind what Amalek did to you on your way from Egypt;
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu a ma Amalɛkikae naxan naba wo ra wo to keli Misira.

sentences.english: How, meeting you on the way, he made an attack on you when you were tired and without strength, cutting off all the feeble ones at the end of your line; and the fear of God was not in him.
sentences.susu: E mu gaaxu Ala ya ra. E mini nɛ wo ma kira xɔn, e xanbirati taganxie bɔnbɔ.

sentences.english: So when the Lord your God has given you rest from all who are against you on every side, in the land which the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage, see to it that the memory of Amalek is cut off from the earth; keep this in mind.
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi, wo Marigi Alatala fama nɛ wo ratangade wo yaxuie ma, naxee na wo rabilinyi bɔxi ma a fama dɛnnaxɛ sode wo yi ra. Wo fama Amalɛkikae rahalakide, alako e xili xa lɔɛ duniɲa ma. Wo naxa nɛɛmu e xa fe rabaxi ma.

sentences.english: Now when you have come into the land which the Lord is giving you for your heritage, and you have made it yours and are living in it;
sentences.susu: Wo na so bɔxi ma wo Marigi Alatala naxan fima wo ma kɛ ra, a xa findi wo gbe ra, wo xa sabati naa,

sentences.english: You are to take a part of the first-fruits of the earth, which you get from the land which the Lord your God is giving you, and put it in a basket, and go to the place marked out by the Lord your God, as the resting-place of his name.
sentences.susu: wo keren keren ma fama na daxamui singe sɛɛti bade wo Marigi Alatala bɛ. Wo a sa debe kui, wo xa a xanin yire, wo Marigi Alatala dɛnnaxɛ sugandixi a xili matɔxɔfe ra.

sentences.english: And you are to come to him who is priest at that time, and say to him, I give witness today before the Lord your God, that I have come into the land which the Lord made an oath to our fathers to give us.
sentences.susu: Wo xa siga sɛrɛxɛdubɛe xɔn, naxee na naa na waxati, wo xa a fala e bɛ, «To lɔxɔɛ won bara so bɔxi, won Marigi Alatala dɛnnaxɛ laayidi won benbae bɛ a sofe ra won yi ra.»

sentences.english: Then the priest will take the basket from your hand and put it down in front of the altar of the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ na debe rasuxuma nɛ wo yi ra, a a dɔxɔ wo Marigi Alatala xa sɛrɛxɛbade ya i.

sentences.english: And these are the words which you will say before the Lord your God: My father was a wandering Aramaean, and he went down with a small number of people into Egypt; there he became a great and strong nation:
sentences.susu: Wo xa yi wɔyɛnyi fala wo Marigi Alatala bɛ, «N baba, Aramika nan nu a ra naxan nu a ɲɛrɛma. A naxa goro Misira mixi ndee ra, a saxanyi raba naa. E naxa wuya, han e findi si belebele sɛnbɛma ra,

sentences.english: And the Egyptians were cruel to us, crushing us under a hard yoke:
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ Misirakae tan naxa muxu ɲaxankata, e muxu tɔɔrɔ, e konyiya xɔrɔxɔɛ dɔxɔ muxu ma.

sentences.english: And our cry went up to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and the Lord's ear was open to the voice of our cry, and his eyes took note of our grief and the crushing weight of our work:
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa muxu benbae Marigi Alatala makula, a xa muxu mali. A naxa muxu xa maxandi suxu, a man naxa muxu xa mantɔɔrɔli to, e nu fe ɲaaxi nun fe xɔrɔxɔɛe naxee dɔxɔma muxu ma.»

sentences.english: And the Lord took us out of Egypt with a strong hand and a stretched-out arm, with works of power and signs and wonders:
sentences.susu: «Alatala naxa muxu ramini Misira bɔxi ma sɛnbɛ magaaxuxi, kaabanakoe, nun tɔnxumae ra.

sentences.english: And he has been our guide to this place, and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
sentences.susu: A naxa fa muxu ra han be, a fa yi bɔxi so muxu yi ra, xiɲɛ nun kumi xɛlɛma dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: So now, I have come here with the first of the fruits of the earth which you, O Lord, have given me. Then you will put it down before the Lord your God and give him worship:
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi, yakɔsi n faxi yi bɔxi daxamui singe ra i tan Alatala xɔn ma, i naxan fixi n ma.» Wo xa na dɔxɔ wo Marigi Alatala ya i, wo a batu.

sentences.english: And you will have joy in every good thing which the Lord your God has given to you and to your family; and the Levite, and the man from a strange land who is with you, will take part in your joy.
sentences.susu: Wo xa sɛɛwa wo boore ra, wo tan nun Lewikae, a nun xɔɲɛ naxee na wo ya ma, barakɛ ra, wo Marigi Alatala naxan fixi wo nun wo xa denbaya ma.

sentences.english: When you have taken out a tenth from the tenth of all your produce in the third year, which is the year when this has to be done, give it to the Levite, and the man from a strange land, and the child without a father, and the widow, so that they may have food in your towns and be full;
sentences.susu: Ɲɛ saxan yo ɲɛ saxan na a li, wo xa na ɲɛ farilɛ fi Lewikae, xɔɲɛe, kiridie, nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe ma, naxee na wo xa taae kui. Nee fan baloe findima na nan na.

sentences.english: And say before the Lord your God, I have taken all the holy things out of my house and have given them to the Levite, and the man from a strange land, and him who has no father, and the widow, as you have given me orders: I have kept in mind all your orders, in nothing have I gone against them:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, wo xa a masen wo Marigi Alatala bɛ, «Naxan findixi i gbe ra, n bara a birin namini n xɔnyi. N bara a so Lewikae, xɔɲɛe, kiridie, nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe yi alɔ i a yamarixi ki naxɛ muxu bɛ. N mu i xa yaamari matandixi, n mu nɛɛmuxi keren ma.

sentences.english: No part of these things has been used for food in a time of weeping, or put away when I was unclean, or given for the dead: I have given ear to the voice of the Lord my God, and have done all you have given me orders to do.
sentences.susu: N mu farilɛ siya donxi ɲɔnyi to so n ma, xa na mu a ra, n to lu sɛniyɛntareɲa kui. N mu a fixi sɛrɛxɛ ra mixi faxaxi bɛ. N bara bira i tan, n Marigi Alatala, xui nan fɔxɔ ra. I naxan yamarixi n bɛ, n bara na birin naba.

sentences.english: So, looking down from your holy place in heaven, send your blessing on your people Israel and on the land which you have given us, as you said in your oath to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
sentences.susu: I xa muxu mato, kelife i xa koore sɛniyɛnxi ma. I xa barakɛ sa i xa ɲama Isirayila ma, i xa barakɛ sa bɔxi ma, i naxan fixi muxu ma, i naxan laayidixi muxu benbae bɛ, xiɲɛ nun kumi gbegbe na dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: Today the Lord your God gives you orders to keep all these laws and decisions: so then keep and do them with all your heart and all your soul.
sentences.susu: To lɔxɔɛ wo Marigi Alatala bara wo yamari wo xa a xa masenyi nun a xa sɛriyɛ rabatu a rabatu ki ma. Wo xa wo ɲɛngi sa na sɛriyɛ xɔn ma wo bɔɲɛ fiixɛ ra.

sentences.english: Today you have given witness that the Lord is your God, and that you will go in his ways and keep his laws and his orders and his decisions and give ear to his voice:
sentences.susu: To lɔxɔɛ wo bara laayidi tongo Alatala bɛ, a a tan nan na wo Marigi Alatala ra, a wo xa ɲɛrɛ a xa kira xɔn ma, a wo xa a xa masenyi, a xa sɛriyɛ, nun a xa yaamari rabatu.

sentences.english: And the Lord has made it clear this day that you are a special people to him, as he gave you his word; and that you are to keep all his orders;
sentences.susu: Wo saatɛ tongoxi nɛ a bɛ, a wo tan nan na a xa ɲama ra, alɔ a a falaxi wo bɛ ki naxɛ. Wo xa bira a xa sɛriyɛ fɔxɔ ra,

sentences.english: And that he will make you high over all the nations he has made, in praise, in name, and in honour, and that you are to be a holy people to the Lord your God as he has said.
sentences.susu: alako a xa fisamanteya fi wo ma si birin xun ma a naxee daaxi. Wo xa nɔrɛ, wo xili, nun wo sɛnbɛ xa dangi e birin na. Wo xa findi ɲama ra naxan a xa wali rabama, alɔ a masenxi wo bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Then Moses and the responsible men of Israel gave the people these orders: Keep all the orders which I have given you this day;
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa nun ɲama forie yi masenyi nan ti Isirayilakae bɛ, «Wo xa mɛɛni yi yaamarie ma, n naxee fixi wo ma to lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: And on the day when you go over Jordan into the land which the Lord your God is giving you, put up great stones, coating them with building-paste,
sentences.susu: Wo na Yurudɛn xure igiri tɛmui naxɛ, sigafe ra bɔxi ma wo Marigi Alatala naxan fima wo ma, wo xa gɛmɛ xungbe ndee ti, wo e mafiixɛ.

sentences.english: And writing on them all the words of this law, after you have gone over; so that you may take the heritage which the Lord your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has said.
sentences.susu: Wo na Yurudɛn igiri sigafe ra bɔxi ma, wo Marigi Alatala naxan fima wo ma, xiɲɛ nun kumi gbegbe na dɛnnaxɛ, alɔ wo babae Marigi Alatala a falaxi wo bɛ ki naxɛ,

sentences.english: And when you have gone over Jordan, you are to put up these stones, as I have said to you today, in Mount Ebal, and have them coated with building-paste.
sentences.susu: wo xa yi gɛmɛe nan ti Ebali geya fari, n baxi naxee xa fe falade wo bɛ ya, wo fa e mafiixɛ.»

sentences.english: There you are to make an altar to the Lord your God, of stones on which no iron instrument has been used.
sentences.susu: «Mɛnni wo xa sɛrɛxɛbade yailan gɛmɛe ra wo Marigi Alatala bɛ, wure mu dinxi naxee ra,

sentences.english: You are to make the altar of the Lord your God of uncut stones; offering on it burned offerings to the Lord your God:
sentences.susu: naxee mu masolixi fefe ma. Wo xa sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi ndee ba wo Marigi Alatala bɛ na sɛrɛxɛbade fari.

sentences.english: And you are to make your peace-offerings, feasting there with joy before the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Wo xa xanunteya sɛrɛxɛe fan ba, wo naxee donma sɛɛwɛ kui wo Marigi Alatala ya i.

sentences.english: And put on the stones all the words of this law, writing them very clearly.
sentences.susu: Wo xa Ala xa sɛriyɛ sɛbɛ na gɛmɛ tixie ma, alako ɲama xa nɔ xarande a fanyi ra.»

sentences.english: Then Moses and the priests, the Levites, said to all Israel, Be quiet and give ear, O Israel; today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa nun Lewika sɛrɛxɛdubɛe naxa yi masenyi ti ɲama bɛ, «Isirayila ɲama, wo wo sabari. Wo xa wo tuli mati. To lɔxɔɛ, wo bara findi wo Marigi Alatala xa ɲama ra.

sentences.english: For this cause you are to give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and do his orders and his laws which I give you this day.
sentences.susu: Wo xa bira wo Marigi Alatala xui fɔxɔ ra. Wo xa a xa masenyi nun a xa sɛriyɛ rabatu a rabatu ki ma, n naxan xaranfe wo bɛ to lɔxɔɛ.»

sentences.english: That same day Moses said to the people,
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ kerenyi, Annabi Munsa man naxa yi yaamari so ɲama yi ra,

sentences.english: These are to take their places on Mount Gerizim for blessing the people when you have gone over Jordan: Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Joseph and Benjamin;
sentences.susu: «Wo na Yurudɛn igiri, Simeyɔn bɔnsɔɛ, Lewi bɔnsɔɛ, Yuda bɔnsɔɛ, Isakari bɔnsɔɛ, Yusufu bɔnsɔɛ, nun Bunyamin bɔnsɔɛ xa ti Garisimi geya fari, e xa dubɛe ti.

sentences.english: And these are to be on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
sentences.susu: Ruben bɔnsɔɛ, Gadi bɔnsɔɛ, Aseri bɔnsɔɛ, Sabulon bɔnsɔɛ, Dana bɔnsɔɛ, nun Nafatali bɔnsɔɛ xa ti Ebali geya fari, e xa dankɛe ti.

sentences.english: Then the Levites are to say in a loud voice to all the men of Israel,
sentences.susu: Lewi bɔnsɔɛ xa na masenyi madangi Isirayila ɲama bɛ e xui itexi ra.»

sentences.english: Cursed is the man who makes any image of wood or stone or metal, disgusting to the Lord, the work of man's hands, and puts it up in secret. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan kuye masolima, xa na mu a ra a kuye yailanma yɔxui raxunuxi ra, a tuubi a bɛ dunxui ra. Alatala na se mɔɔli xɔnxi.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who does not give honour to his father or mother. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan a baba nun a nga rayaagima.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who takes his neighbour's landmark from its place. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan naaninyi tɔnxuma masigama.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he by whom the blind are turned out of the way. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan dɔnxui ratantanma kira ma.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who gives a wrong decision in the cause of a man from a strange land, or of one without a father, or of a widow. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan sɛriyɛ rakanama xɔɲɛ, kiridi, xa na mu a ra kaaɲɛ ginɛ ra.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who has sex relations with his father's wife, for he has put shame on his father. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan sama a baba xa ginɛ fɛ ma, a a baba rayaagi.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who has sex relations with any sort of beast. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan yɛnɛ rabama xuruse ra, na findi xuruse yo ra.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who has sex relations with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan nun a maaginɛ kafuma, a baba xa di ginɛ, xa na mu a nga xa di ginɛ.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who has sex relations with his mother-in-law. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan nun a bitanyi ginɛma kafuma.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who takes his neighbour's life secretly. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan a boore faxama nɔxunyi kui.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who for a reward puts to death one who has done no wrong. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan kɔbiri rasuxuma mixi tɔɔɲɛgɛxi faxafe ra.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Cursed is he who does not take this law to heart to do it. And let all the people say, So be it.
sentences.susu: «Dankɛ na mixi bɛ naxan tondima Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatude.» Ɲama birin fa a ratin, «Amina.»

sentences.english: Now if you give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep with care all these orders which I have given you today, then the Lord your God will put you high over all the nations of the earth:
sentences.susu: «Xa wo bira wo Marigi Alatala xui fɔxɔ ra bɔɲɛ fiixɛ ra, xa wo yi yaamarie rabatu n naxee soxi wo yi ra to lɔxɔɛ, Alatala wo findima nɛ si fisamante ra si birin tagi duniɲa kui.

sentences.english: And all these blessings will come on you and overtake you, if your ears are open to the voice of the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Wo yi barakɛ nan sɔtɔma xa wo bira wo Marigi Alatala xui fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: A blessing will be on you in the town, and a blessing in the field.
sentences.susu: A barakɛ sama nɛ taakae nun daaxakae ma,

sentences.english: A blessing will be on the fruit of your body, and on the fruit of your land, on the fruit of your cattle, the increase of your herd, and the young of your flock.
sentences.susu: e xa die, daxamui, yɛxɛɛe, sie, nun ningee xun masama nɛ.

sentences.english: A blessing will be on your basket and on your bread-basin.
sentences.susu: A wo xa sagae rafe bogi se ra, a barakɛ sa wo xa farin namaxadee.

sentences.english: A blessing will be on your coming in and on your going out.
sentences.susu: Wo xa simaya kui, a barakɛ sama nɛ wo xa fe birin.

sentences.english: By the power of the Lord, those who take arms against you will be overcome before you: they will come out against you one way, and will go in flight from you seven ways.
sentences.susu: Wo yaxuie na fa wo gerede, Alatala e rayarabima nɛ wo bɛ. Xa e so kira keren nan na, e gbilenma e gi ra nɛ wo ya ra kira solofere xɔn.

sentences.english: The Lord will send his blessing on your store-houses and on everything to which you put your hand: his blessing will be on you in the land which the Lord your God is giving you.
sentences.susu: Wo Marigi Alatala barakɛ sama nɛ wo xa sansi rawalide nun wo na so fe naxan birin ya ma. A barakɛ sa wo xa fe bɔxi ma, a dɛnnaxɛ fima wo ma.

sentences.english: The Lord will keep you as a people holy to himself, as he has said to you in his oath, if you keep the orders of the Lord your God and go on walking in his ways.
sentences.susu: Xa wo wo Marigi Alatala xa masenyi raba a raba ki ma, wo man naxa bira a waxɔnfe fɔxɔ ra, a wo findima a yɛtɛ xa ɲama nan na alɔ a a rakalixi wo bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the Lord is on you, and they will go in fear of you.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi ɲamae birin a kolonma nɛ na tɛmui, a wo tan nan sugandixi Alatala xa wali rabafe ma, e gaaxuma nɛ wo ya ra.

sentences.english: And the Lord will make you fertile in every good thing, in the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your cattle, and the fruit of your fields, in the land which the Lord, by his oath to your fathers, said he would give you.
sentences.susu: Alatala wo harige xun masama nɛ bɔxi ma a dɛnnaxɛ saatɛ tongo wo benbae bɛ sofe ra wo yi. A wo xa die rawuyama nɛ, a wo xa xurusee rawuya.

sentences.english: Opening his store-house in heaven, the Lord will send rain on your land at the right time, blessing all the work of your hands: other nations will make use of your wealth, and you will have no need of theirs.
sentences.susu: Alatala ye ragatade rabima nɛ wo bɛ koore ma, tunɛ xa fa wo xa bɔxie ma a waxati ma, alako wo xa walie xa fan. Wo hayi mu birama kɔbiri doni fe ma, fo wo tan kɔbiri doni xɔɲɛe bɛ de.

sentences.english: The Lord will make you the head and not the tail; and you will ever have the highest place, if you give ear to the orders of the Lord your God which I give you today, to keep and to do them;
sentences.susu: Alatala wo tan nan findima si birin ma yarerati ra. Wo mu luma xanbi, wo fisamanteya nan sɔtɔma tɛmui birin. Wo mu nimisama fefe ma, kɔnɔ fo wo xa yi yaamari rabatu nɛ a rabatu ki ma, n naxan xaranxi wo ra to lɔxɔɛ wo Marigi Alatala xa fe ra.

sentences.english: Not turning away from any of the orders which I give you today, to the right hand or to the left, or going after any other gods to give them worship.
sentences.susu: Fefe yo naxa a niya wo xa ba yi kira xɔn ma n naxan falaxi wo bɛ. Wo naxa bira ala gbɛtɛe batufe fɔxɔ ra fefe ma.

sentences.english: But if you do not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and take care to do all his orders and his laws which I give you today, then all these curses will come on you and overtake you:
sentences.susu: Xa wo fa tondi wo Marigi Alatala batude, xa wo tondi a xa yaamarie nun a xa sɛriyɛ rabade, n naxee xaranxi wo ra to lɔxɔɛ a xa fe ra, na tɛmui a fama yi dankɛ nan birade wo fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: You will be cursed in the town and cursed in the field.
sentences.susu: A taakae nun daaxakae dankama nɛ.

sentences.english: A curse will be on your basket and on your bread-basin.
sentences.susu: A mu bogi se sama wo xa sagae kui, a man mu barakɛ sama wo xa farin namaxadee.

sentences.english: A curse will be on the fruit of your body, and on the fruit of your land, on the increase of your cattle, and the young of your flock.
sentences.susu: A tondima nɛ di fide wo ma, wo man mu baloe sɔtɔma. Wo xa ningee, yɛxɛɛe, nun sie xun mu masama.

sentences.english: You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.
sentences.susu: Wo dankɛ nan sɔtɔma yire birin wo xa simaya kui.

sentences.english: The Lord will send on you cursing and trouble and punishment in everything to which you put your hand, till sudden destruction overtakes you; because of your evil ways in which you have been false to me.
sentences.susu: Wo na so fefe yo naxan ya ma, a dankɛ ragoroma nɛ wo ma. A wo kui ifuma nɛ alako wo xa fe naxa sɔɔnɛya fefe ma, wo xun xa ra kana, barima wo bara fe ɲaaxi raba, wo man bara gbilen Alatala fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: The Lord will send disease after disease on you, till you have been cut off by death from the land to which you are going.
sentences.susu: Alatala fure ɲaaxi radinma nɛ wo ma, han wo ɲɔn bɔxi ma a dɛnnaxɛ soma wo yi ra.

sentences.english: The Lord will send wasting disease, and burning pain, and flaming heat against you, keeping back the rain till your land is waste and dead; so will it be till your destruction is complete.
sentences.susu: Alatala a niyama nɛ wo xa xɔsi, wo fate xa gan, wo xa fura a ɲaaxi ra. A man bɔxi xara, sansie gan soge bun ma, e fan fure ɲaaxi sɔtɔ. A na birin nabama nɛ wo ra, han wo lɔɛ.

sentences.english: And the heaven over your heads will be brass, and the earth under you hard as iron.
sentences.susu: Koore nun bɔxi xarama nɛ a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: The Lord will make the rain of your land powder and dust, sending it down on you from heaven till your destruction is complete.
sentences.susu: Alatala tunɛ mafindima nɛ xube ra, naxan goroma wo xa bɔxi ma, a wo sɔntɔ.

sentences.english: The Lord will let you be overcome by your haters: you will go out against them one way, and you will go in flight before them seven ways: you will be the cause of fear among all the kingdoms of the earth.
sentences.susu: Alatala sɛnbɛ fima nɛ wo yaxuie ma e wo rayarabi. Xa wo e gere kira keren nan na, wo wo gima nɛ e ya ra kira solofere xɔn. Naxan nabama wo ra, a duniɲa birin magaaxuma nɛ.

sentences.english: Your bodies will be meat for all the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth; there will be no one to send them away.
sentences.susu: Wo binbie findima xɔnie nun wulai subee xa donse nan na. Mixi yo mu fama e keride.

sentences.english: The Lord will send on you the disease of Egypt, and other sorts of skin diseases which nothing will make well.
sentences.susu: Alatala suuri ikonkonma nɛ wo ma alɔ a naxan naba Misirakae ra. A wo tɔɔrɔma nɛ mangɛ faxɛ ra, kasi, nun xɛɲɛnyi naxan mu yalanma.

sentences.english: He will make your minds diseased, and your eyes blind, and your hearts wasted with fear:
sentences.susu: Alatala wo findima nɛ dɔnxuie ra, a daxui fure fan fi wo ma.

sentences.english: You will go feeling your way when the sun is high, like a blind man for whom all is dark, and nothing will go well for you: you will be crushed and made poor for ever, and you will have no saviour.
sentences.susu: Yanyi ra wo nɛ wo ɲɛrɛma, wo luma kira mɛlɛn na nɛ alɔ dɔnxuie. Wo xa wali yo mu findima a ra, wo luma tɔɔrɔ ra nɛ. Mixie fama nɛ wo harige bade wo yi ra, e wo tɔɔrɔ a ɲaaxi ra. Marakisima yo mu luma wo bɛ.

sentences.english: You will take a wife, but another man will have the use of her: the house which your hands have made will never be your resting-place: you will make a vine-garden, and never take the fruit of it.
sentences.susu: Wo na kote dɔxɔ ginɛ xa fe ra, xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ a futi kanama nɛ. Wo na banxi ti, wo mu nɔma sode a kui. Wo na wɛni bilie si, wo mu nɔma e bogi bade.

sentences.english: Your ox will be put to death before your eyes, but its flesh will not be your food: your ass will be violently taken away before your face, and will not be given back to you: your sheep will be given to your haters, and there will be no saviour for you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ningee kɔn naxabama nɛ wo ya xɔri, wo mu nɔ e sube donde. E wo xa sofale muɲama nɛ wo ma, wo mu a masɔtɔma. Yaxuie wo xa xuruse yɔrɛe tongoma nɛ, mixi yo mu fama wo malide.

sentences.english: Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, and your eyes will be wasted away with looking and weeping for them all the day: and you will have no power to do anything.
sentences.susu: Si gbɛtɛ mixie wo xa die suxuma nɛ wo ya xɔri, e e findi konyie ra. Wo taganma nɛ wo xa die mamɛde, wo mu nɔma na yaxuie ra fefe ma.

sentences.english: The fruit of your land and all the work of your hands will be food for a nation which is strange to you and to your fathers; you will only be crushed down and kept under for ever:
sentences.susu: Si nde wo mu naxan kolon e baloma wo xa sansie nan xun na, wo xa bɔxi daxamui findima e tan nan gbe ra. E wo rawalima nɛ, e man fe ɲaaxi raba wo ra.

sentences.english: So that the things which your eyes have to see will send you out of your minds.
sentences.susu: Na fe tofe wo findima nɛ daxuie ra.

sentences.english: The Lord will send a skin disease, attacking your knees and your legs, bursting out from your feet to the top of your head, so that nothing will make you well.
sentences.susu: Alatala fi ɲaaxi dɔxɔma nɛ wo ma, naxan mu yalanma. A goroma xinbie nun bɛlɛnyie nan ma, a fa yensen fate yire birin na, keli wo xunyi ma, a dɔxɔ wo sanyie ra.

sentences.english: And you, and the king whom you have put over you, will the Lord take away to a nation strange to you and to your fathers; there you will be servants to other gods of wood and stone.
sentences.susu: Alatala fama nɛ wo tan nun wo xa mangɛe rasigade bɔxi nde ma, wo tan nun wo benbae mu naxan kolon. Mɛnni wo fama nɛ ala gbɛtɛe batude, naxee masolixi wuri nun gɛmɛ ra.

sentences.english: And you will become a wonder and a name of shame among all the nations where the Lord will take you.
sentences.susu: Mɛnnikae wo mayelema nɛ, e yoma wo ma.

sentences.english: You will take much seed out into the field, and get little in; for the locust will get it.
sentences.susu: Wo sansi xɔri gbegbe rawalima nɛ wo xa xɛe ma, kɔnɔ wo dondoronti nan xabama, barima katoe dinma nɛ a birin na.

sentences.english: You will put in vines and take care of them, but you will get no wine or grapes from them; for they will be food for worms.
sentences.susu: Wo wɛni sansi sima nɛ, wo mɛɛni a ma a fanyi ra, kɔnɔ wo mu a ye minma, barima kuli soma e i nɛ.

sentences.english: Your land will be full of olive-trees, but there will be no oil for the comfort of your body; for your olive-tree will give no fruit.
sentences.susu: Oliwi bilie luma nɛ bɔxi yire birin ma, kɔnɔ wo mu e ture masoma wo ma, barima oliwi bogie birama nɛ, e mu gbeeli.

sentences.english: You will have sons and daughters, but they will not be yours; for they will go away prisoners into a strange land.
sentences.susu: Wo die barima nɛ, kɔnɔ e mu luma wo yi, barima wo yaxuie e xaninma nɛ.

sentences.english: All your trees and the fruit of your land will be the locust's.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wurie nun bɔxi daxamui findima katoe nan gbe ra.

sentences.english: The man from a strange land who is living among you will be lifted up higher and higher over you, while you go down lower and lower.
sentences.susu: Xɔɲɛ naxee na wo ya ma, nee sɛnbɛ xun masama nɛ tɛmui birin, kɔnɔ wo tan xa fe magoroma nɛ.

sentences.english: He will let you have his wealth at interest, and will have no need of yours: he will be the head and you the tail.
sentences.susu: Fɛɛrɛ luma nɛ e yi ra, kɔnɔ wo tan luma setareɲa nan kui. E findima nɛ wo xa yareratie ra, kɔnɔ wo tan luma e xanbi ra nɛ.

sentences.english: And all these curses will come after you and overtake you, till your destruction is complete; because you did not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, or keep his laws and his orders which he gave you:
sentences.susu: Yi dankɛ birin dɔxɔma nɛ wo fari, han wo birin gɛ halakide, barima wo bara tondi wo Marigi Alatala xui ratinmɛde. Wo mu a xa yaamari nun a xa sɛriyɛ rabatuxi a rabatu ki ma.

sentences.english: These things will come on you and on your seed, to be a sign and a wonder for ever;
sentences.susu: Na findima tɔnxuma nun dɛixarɛ nan na wo tan nun wo bɔnsɔɛ bɛ abadan.

sentences.english: Because you did not give honour to the Lord your God, worshipping him gladly, with joy in your hearts on account of all your wealth of good things;
sentences.susu: Wo to mu tin wo Marigi Alatala batude sɛɛwɛ nun bɔɲɛsa kui, fe fanyi birin xa lu wo yi ra,

sentences.english: For this cause you will become servants to those whom the Lord your God will send against you, without food and drink and clothing, and in need of all things: and he will put a yoke of iron on your neck till he has put an end to you.
sentences.susu: wo fama nɛ tɔɔrɔde wo yaxuie yi ra. Kaamɛ nun ye xɔli wo suxuma nɛ. Wo tima nɛ wo mageli ra, wo luma setareɲa nan kui. Na kui Alatala fama yɔlɔnxɔnyi sade wo kɔnyi ma, han wo gɛ halakide.

sentences.english: The Lord will send a nation against you from the farthest ends of the earth, coming with the flight of an eagle; a nation whose language is strange to you;
sentences.susu: A fama nɛ si ra wo mu naxan xa xui mɛma kelife yire makuye, a xa goro wo ma alɔ sɛgɛ goroma tɔxɔɛ yɔrɛ ma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: A hard-faced nation, who will have no respect for the old or mercy for the young:
sentences.susu: Mixi kaarinxie nan e ra, naxee mu forie binyama, naxee mu kinikinima dimɛe ma.

sentences.english: He will take the fruit of your cattle and of your land till death puts an end to you: he will let you have nothing of your grain or wine or oil or any of the increase of your cattle or the young of your flock, till he has made your destruction complete.
sentences.susu: E wo xa xuruse nun wo xa baloe tongo e yɛtɛ bɛ, wo xa faxa kaamɛ ra. E wo xa mɛngi, wɛni, ture, ninge yɔrɛe, yɛxɛɛe, nun sie birin xaninma nɛ. Wo fama nɛ halakide.

sentences.english: Your towns will be shut in by his armies, till your high walls, in which you put your faith, have come down: his armies will be round your towns, through all your land which the Lord your God has given you.
sentences.susu: E fama nɛ wo xa taae birin nabilinde, wo Marigi Alatala naxee so wo yi ra. E wo gerema nɛ han wo xa tɛtɛ itexi sɛnbɛmae yolon, wo laxi naxee ra.

sentences.english: And your food will be the fruit of your body, the flesh of the sons and daughters which the Lord your God has given you; because of your bitter need and the cruel grip of your haters.
sentences.susu: Na geree kui wo yaxuie wo rakaamɛma nɛ, han wo wo xa die sube yati don, die wo Marigi Alatala naxee fixi wo ma.

sentences.english: That man among you who is soft and used to comfort will be hard and cruel to his brother, and to his dear wife, and to of those his children who are still living;
sentences.susu: Hali xɛmɛ fanyi naxan luma wo ya ma, a mu kinikinima a ngaxakerenma, a xa ginɛ, nun a xa die ma.

sentences.english: And will not give to any of them the flesh of his children which will be his food because he has no other; in the cruel grip of your haters on all your towns.
sentences.susu: A tondima nɛ a xa di sube itaxunde e ra, barima na findixi a baloe dɔnxɔɛ nan na. Wo yaxuie na marayarabi sama nɛ wo fari wo xa taae birin kui.

sentences.english: The most soft and delicate of your women, who would not so much as put her foot on the earth, so delicate is she, will be hard-hearted to her husband and to her son and to her daughter;
sentences.susu: Hali ginɛ fanyi naxan luma wo ya ma, naxan mu tinma a sanyi yati xa manɔxɔ, na tan fan mu kinikinima a xa mɔri fanyi nun a xa die ma.

sentences.english: And to her baby newly come to birth, and to the children of her body; for having no other food, she will make a meal of them secretly, because of her bitter need and the cruel grip of your haters on all your towns.
sentences.susu: A tondima nɛ a xa diyɔrɛ sube itaxunde e nun na xanbiratoe ma a naxan barixi, barima a tan wama na donfe, a xa lu a tan gbansan bɛ. Wo yaxuie fama na tɔɔrɛ mɔɔli nan dɔxɔde wo ma.

sentences.english: If you will not take care to do all the words of this law, recorded in this book, honouring that name of glory and of fear, THE LORD YOUR GOD;
sentences.susu: Xa wo mu mɛɛni yi masenyie ma naxee sɛbɛxi yi kitaabui kui, xa wo mu gaaxu wo Marigi Alatala xili xungbe magaaxuxi ya ra,

sentences.english: Then the Lord your God will make your punishment, and the punishment of your seed, a thing to be wondered at; great punishments and cruel diseases stretching on through long years.
sentences.susu: Alatala fama nɛ fure ɲaaxi magaaxuxie dɔxɔde wo tan nun wo bɔnsɔɛ ma, naxan mu yalanma.

sentences.english: He will send on you again all the diseases of Egypt, which were a cause of fear to you, and they will take you in their grip.
sentences.susu: A fure ɲaaxi ikonkoma nɛ wo xun na, wo nu gaaxuxi naxan ya ra Misira bɔxi ma. Na fure mɔɔli wo suxuma nɛ, a nɔ wo ra.

sentences.english: And all the diseases and the pains not recorded in the book of this law will the Lord send on you till your destruction is complete.
sentences.susu: Alatala fure mɔɔli gbegbe dɔxɔma nɛ wo ma, naxee xili mu sɛbɛxi yi kitaabui kui, han wo birin gɛ sɔntɔde.

sentences.english: And you will become a very small band, though your numbers were like the stars of heaven; because you did not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Wo tan naxee nu wuya dangi tunbuie ra koore ma, wo kɔnti xurunma nɛ, barima wo bara wo Marigi Alatala xui matandi.

sentences.english: And as the Lord took delight in doing you good and increasing you, so the Lord will take pleasure in cutting you off and causing your destruction, and you will be uprooted from the land which you are about to take as your heritage.
sentences.susu: Alatala fe fanyi rabaxi wo bɛ ki naxɛ, a nun a wo rawuyaxi ki naxɛ, a fama wo halakide na ki nɛ man, wo fa ɲɔn bɔxi ma a naxan fi wo ma.

sentences.english: And the Lord will send you wandering among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other: there you will be servants to other gods, of wood and stone, gods of which you and your fathers had no knowledge.
sentences.susu: A wo rayensen si birin ya ma, keli duniɲa tuxui ma, sa dɔxɔ boore tuxui ra. Wo fama nɛ ala gbɛtɛe batude, wuri nun gɛmɛ daaxie, wo tan nun wo benbae mu naxee kolon.

sentences.english: And even among these nations there will be no peace for you, and no rest for your feet: but the Lord will give you there a shaking heart and wasting eyes and weariness of soul:
sentences.susu: Na sie tagi, wo mu malabui yo sɔtɔma, wo mu yire yo sɔtɔma wo sabatima dɛnnaxɛ. Alatala wo bɔɲɛe ratema nɛ, a wo yaye ramini, a wo nii tɔɔrɔ.

sentences.english: Your very life will be hanging in doubt before you, and day and night will be dark with fears, and nothing in life will be certain:
sentences.susu: Wo xa simaya findima kɔntɔfili nan na, gaaxui fama nɛ wo rasɛrɛnde kɔɛ nun yanyi ra.

sentences.english: In the morning you will say, If only it was evening! And at evening you will say, If only morning would come! Because of the fear in your hearts and the things which your eyes will see.
sentences.susu: Wo na na fe mɔɔli to tɛmui naxɛ, gaaxui fama wo bɔɲɛ rafede. Gɛɛsɛgɛ, wo nu fa a fala, «Xa nunmare nan nu a ra nu!» Nunmare, wo nu fa a fala, «Xa gɛɛsɛgɛ nan nu a ra nu!»

sentences.english: And the Lord will take you back to Egypt again in ships, by the way of which I said to you, You will never see it again: there you will be offering yourselves as men-servants and women-servants to your haters for a price, and no man will take you.
sentences.susu: Alatala wo xaninma nɛ kunkuie kui Misira, n a fala wo bɛ dɛnnaxɛ ma wo mu naa toma sɔnɔn. Mɛnni, wo katama nɛ wo yɛtɛ matide wo yaxuie ma konyie ra, xɛmɛe nun ginɛe, kɔnɔ mixi yo mu wo sarama.

sentences.english: These are the words of the agreement which Moses was ordered by the Lord to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the agreement which he made with them in Horeb.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa naxa Isirayila ɲama birin maxili, a a masen e bɛ, «Wo nu na Misira tɛmui naxɛ, wo fe to nɛ Alatala naxan naba Firawuna ra, a xa sɔɔrie nun a xa bɔxi birin na.

sentences.english: And Moses said in the hearing of all Israel, You have seen all the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and to all his servants and all his land;
sentences.susu: Wo bara fe xɔrɔxɔɛe to, tɔnxumae nun kaabanakoe a naxee raba e ra,

sentences.english: The great tests which your eyes saw, and the signs and wonders:
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ han to Alatala mu xaxili fi wo ma naxan nɔma yi fee kolonde. Wo yae mu a toma, wo tuli man mu a mɛma.

sentences.english: But even to this day the Lord has not given you a mind open to knowledge, or seeing eyes or hearing ears.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛ tongo naani bun ma a wo ratangama gbengberenyi kui. Wo xa sose nun wo xa sankirie mu kana,

sentences.english: For forty years I have been your guide through the waste land: your clothing has not become old on your backs, or your shoes on your feet.
sentences.susu: wo mu taami don, wo mu wɛni nun beere min. Alatala bara a ɲɔxɔ rasiga wo xa fe xɔn alako wo xa nɔ a kolonde a tan nan na wo Marigi Ala ra.

sentences.english: You have had no bread, or wine, or strong drink: so that you might see that I am the Lord your God.
sentences.susu: Wo to so be, Xɛsibɔn mangɛ Sixɔn, nun Basan mangɛ Ogo, fa nɛ wo gerede, kɔnɔ wo naxa nɔ e ra.

sentences.english: When you came to this place, Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, came out to make war against us and we overcame them:
sentences.susu: Wo naxa e xa bɔxie tongo, wo a itaxun Ruben bɔnsɔɛ ma, Gadi bɔnsɔɛ ma, nun Manasi bɔnsɔɛ sɛɛti keren ma.

sentences.english: And we took their land and gave it to the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for their heritage.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi, wo lanma wo xa bira yi saatɛ sɛriyɛ fɔxɔ ra, alako wo na so fe naxan yo ya ma, a xa sɔɔnɛya wo bɛ.»

sentences.english: So keep the words of this agreement and do them, so that it may be well for you in everything you do.
sentences.susu: «Isirayilakae, wo tan nan malanxi yi ki to lɔxɔɛ wo Marigi Alatala ya i. Birin na be, wo xa mangɛe, wo xa yareratie, wo xa forie, wo xa sɔɔri mangɛe,

sentences.english: You have come here today, all of you, before the Lord your God; the heads of your tribes, the overseers, and those who are in authority over you, with all the men of Israel,
sentences.susu: wo xa ginɛe, wo xa die, nun xɔɲɛe naxee wuri sɛgɛma nun ye bama wo bɛ.

sentences.english: And your little ones, your wives, and the men of other lands who are with you in your tents, down to the wood-cutter and the servant who gets water for you:
sentences.susu: Wo Marigi Alatala bara saatɛ mabanban kali ra. Wo na be to alako wo xa na xiri, wo tan nun wo Marigi Alatala tagi.

sentences.english: With the purpose of taking part in the agreement of the Lord your God, and his oath which he makes with you today:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui wo tan nan na a xa ɲama ra, nun a tan nan na wo Marigi Ala ra, alɔ a kali wo benbae Iburahima, Isiyaga, nun Yaxuba bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And so that he may make you his people today, and be your God, as he has said to you, and as he made an oath to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
sentences.susu: N mu yi saatɛ mabanbanxi kali ra wo tan gbansan xa bɛ,

sentences.english: And not with you only do I make this agreement and this oath;
sentences.susu: wo tan naxee na be won Marigi Alatala ya i. N a mabanbanxi wo bɔnsɔɛ nan fan bɛ naxee mu nu bari sinden.»

sentences.english: But with everyone who is here with us today before the Lord our God, as well as with those who are not here:
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon won buxi Misira bɔxi ma ki naxɛ, nun won dangi si naxee xa bɔxie ra.

sentences.english: (For you have in mind how we were living in the land of Egypt; and how we came through all the nations which were on your way;
sentences.susu: Wo bara yi kuye xɔnxie to yi sie nu naxee batuma, kuye naxee yailanxi wuri, gɛmɛ, gbeti, nun xɛɛma ra.

sentences.english: And you have seen their disgusting doings, and the images of wood and stone and silver and gold which were among them:)
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ yo, ginɛ yo, bɔnsɔɛ yo, xabilɛ yo naxa gbilen wo Marigi Alatala fɔxɔ ra, birafe ra na sie xa alae batufe fɔxɔ ra. Wo ya ma, mixi yo naxa lu alɔ wuri sanke naxan pɔsɔnɛ xɔnɛ raminima.

sentences.english: So that there may not be among you any man or woman or family or tribe whose heart is turned away from the Lord our God today, to go after other gods and give them worship; or any root among you whose fruit is poison and bitter sorrow;
sentences.susu: Na mixi mɔɔli naxan bara gɛ yi kali mɛde, kɔnɔ a fa sɛɛwa a bɔɲɛ ma a falafe ra, ‹Sɔɔnɛya na n bɛ, n xa n yɛtɛ waxɔnfe raba tɛmui birin, ɲɛmɛ nun sogofure,›

sentences.english: If such a man, hearing the words of this oath, takes comfort in the thought that he will have peace even if he goes on in the pride of his heart, taking whatever chance may give him:
sentences.susu: Alatala mu diɲɛma na kanyi ma. A fama nɛ a xa xɔnɛ masende a bɛ a ɲaaxi ra, barima a mu wama a firin nde xɔn. A dankɛ ragoroma nɛ a ma, naxee sɛbɛxi yi kitaabui kui. A a xili ralɔɛma nɛ duniɲa ma.

sentences.english: The Lord will have no mercy on him, but the wrath of the Lord will be burning against that man, and all the curses recorded in this book will be waiting for him, and the Lord will take away his name completely from the earth.
sentences.susu: Alatala na mixi mɔɔli raminima Isirayila ɲama ya ma a dankɛ ki ma, alɔ a saatɛ sɛbɛxi ki naxɛ yi sɛriyɛ kitaabui kui.»

sentences.english: He will be marked out by the Lord, from all the tribes of Israel, for an evil fate, in keeping with all the curses of the agreement recorded in this book of the law.
sentences.susu: «Wo bɔnsɔɛe naxee fama wo xanbi ra, a nun xɔɲɛe naxee kelima bɔxi makuye ma, e fama furee nun fe xɔrɔxɔɛe tode, Alatala naxee dɔxɔma wo xa bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: And future generations, your children coming after you, and travellers from far countries, will say, when they see the punishments of that land and the diseases which the Lord has sent on it;
sentences.susu: Soda nun fɔxɔɛ fama lude bɔxi fari. Bɔxi mu nɔma rawalide, sese mu nɔma fande, hali burɛxɛ keren a mu nɔma findide a ra. Bɔxi luma nɛ alɔ Sodoma, Gomora, Adamaha, nun Seboyimi, Ala taa naxee kana a xa bɔɲɛ xɔnɛ kui.

sentences.english: And that all the land is a salt and smoking waste, not planted or giving fruit or clothed with grass, but wasted like Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, on which the Lord sent destruction in the heat of his wrath:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui si gbɛtɛe fama nɛ maxɔrinyi tide, ‹Alatala yi bɔxi niyaxi yi ki munfe ra? A bɔɲɛ xɔnɔxi yi mɔɔli ra munfe ra?›

sentences.english: Truly all the nations will say, Why has the Lord done so to this land? what is the reason for this great and burning wrath?
sentences.susu: E e yaabima nɛ, ‹Yi fe rabaxi nɛ barima yi ɲama bara saatɛ kana, e benbae Marigi Alatala naxan tongo e bɛ, a to e ramini Misira bɔxi ra.

sentences.english: Then men will say, Because they gave up the agreement of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he took them out of the land of Egypt:
sentences.susu: E bara kuyee batu e mu naxee kolonxi, Alatala mu tinxi naxee ra.

sentences.english: And they went after other gods and gave them worship, gods who were strange to them, and whom he had not given them:
sentences.susu: Na fe na a toxi Alatala yi ɲaxankatɛ birin dɔxɔxi yi bɔxi ma a xa xɔnɛ kui alɔ a xa kitaabui a masenma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And so the wrath of the Lord was moved against this land, to send on it all the curse recorded in this book:
sentences.susu: A bara a xa xɔnɛ belebele dɔxɔ a xa ɲama ma, a e tongo e xa bɔxi ma, a e keri bɔxi gbɛtɛ fan ma, e na dɛnnaxɛ yi waxati.›»

sentences.english: Rooting them out of their land, in the heat of his wrath and passion, and driving them out into another land, as at this day.
