sentences.susu: Hataki to na fala Morodekayi bɛ,

sentences.english: Then Mordecai sent this answer back to Esther: Do not have the idea that you in the king's house will be safe from the fate of all the Jews.
sentences.susu: Morodekayi naxa Esita yaabi, a naxɛ, «Esita, hali i to na mangɛ nan xɔnyi, i naxa a maɲɔxun de a i keren nɔma kiside Yuwifie ya ma.

sentences.english: If at this time you say nothing, then help and salvation will come to the Jews from some other place, but you and your father's family will come to destruction: and who is to say that you have not come to the kingdom even for such a time as this?
sentences.susu: Xa i dundu yi fe ma, saabui gbɛtɛ minima nɛ Yuwifie bɛ, kɔnɔ i tan nun i xabilɛ halakima nɛ. Nde a kolon xa i findixi mangɛ ginɛ ra yi lɔxɔɛ yati yati nan ma fe ra?»

sentences.english: Then Esther sent them back to Mordecai with this answer:
sentences.susu: Na kui Esita naxa Morodekayi yaabi yi wɔyɛnyi ra,

sentences.english: Go, get together all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and go without food for me, taking no food or drink night or day for three days: and I and my women will do the same; and so I will go in to the king, which is against the law: and if death is to be my fate, then let it come.
sentences.susu: «Siga, i sa Suse Yuwifie birin malan, wo xa sunyi suxu n bɛ. Wo naxa ye min, wo naxa wo dɛge yanyi saxan nun kɔɛ saxan bun ma. N tan nun n ma konyie fan sunyi suxuma na ki nɛ. Na dangi xanbi, n sigama nɛ mangɛ yire, hali tɔnyi to dɔxɔxi na ma. Xa e n faxa, awa yire.»

sentences.english: So Mordecai went away and did everything as Esther had said.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Morodekayi naxa Esita waxɔnfe raba, alɔ a fala a bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Now on the third day, Esther put on her queen's robes, and took her place in the inner room of the king's house, facing the king's house: and the king was seated on his high seat in the king's house, facing the doorway of the house.
sentences.susu: Sunyi xi saxan nde, Esita naxa a maxiri mangɛ ginɛ dugie ra, a sa siga mangɛ yire. Mangɛ nu dɔxɔxi a xa kibanyi kui, a ya tixi naadɛ ra.

sentences.english: And when the king saw Esther the queen waiting in the inner room, looking kindly on her he put out the rod of gold in his hand to her. So Esther came near and put her fingers on the top of the rod.
sentences.susu: A to mangɛ ginɛ Esita to, a tixi naa, a xa fe naxa rafan a ma. Mangɛ naxa a xa sawuri xɛɛma daaxi itala a bɛ, Esita naxa a bɛlɛxɛ din na sawuri xunyi ra.

sentences.english: Then the king said, What is your desire, Queen Esther, and what is your request? I will give it to you, even to the half of my kingdom.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a maxɔrin, «Mangɛ ginɛ Esita, munse niyaxi? I wama munse xɔn ma? N mu tondima, hali i wama n ma mangɛya tagi nan xɔn ma.»

sentences.english: And Esther in answer said, If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast which I have made ready for him.
sentences.susu: Esita naxa a yaabi, «Mangɛ, xa a sa i kɛnɛn, n wama a xɔn ma wo nun Haman xa fa n xɔnyi to, won birin xa won dɛge a fanyi ra i xa binyɛ bun ma.»

sentences.english: Then the king said, Let Haman come quickly, so that what Esther has said may be done. So the king and Haman came to the feast which Esther had made ready.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa xɛɛra rasiga Haman ma keren na, alako e xa sa Esita waxɔnfe raba.

sentences.english: And while they were drinking wine the king said to Esther, What is your prayer? for it will be given to you and what is your request? for it will be done, even to the half of my kingdom.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ nun Haman naxa siga Esita xɔnyi, e e dɛge yire keren. E nu na wɛni minfe tɛmui naxɛ, mangɛ naxa Esita maxɔrin, «Esita, i wama naxan xɔn ma, a fala n bɛ. N mu tondima. I waxɔnfe na munse ra? Hali i wama n ma mangɛya tagi nan xɔn ma, n a soma nɛ i yi ra.»

sentences.english: Then Esther said in answer, My prayer and my request is this:
sentences.susu: Esita naxa mangɛ yaabi, a naxɛ, «N wama naxan xɔn ma,

sentences.english: If I have the king's approval, and if it is the king's pleasure to give me my prayer and do my request, let the king and Haman come to the feast which I will make ready for them, and tomorrow I will do as the king has said.
sentences.susu: xa i bara tin a ra, a xɔli n ma wo nun Haman man xa fa n xɔnyi tina. Na tɛmui, won na gɛ won dɛgede, n na n waxɔnfe falama i bɛ.»

sentences.english: Then on that day Haman went out full of joy and glad in heart; but when he saw Mordecai in the king's doorway, and he did not get to his feet or give any sign of fear before him, Haman was full of wrath against Mordecai.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ Haman nu sɛɛwaxi ki fanyi, kɔnɔ a to Morodekayi to mangɛ xa banxi sode dɛ ra, a bɔɲɛ naxa te a ɲaaxi ra, barima Morodekayi tondixi a binyade, a mu gaaxuxi a ya ra fefe ma.

sentences.english: But controlling himself, he went to his house; and he sent for his friends and Zeresh, his wife.
sentences.susu: Na kui Haman naxa a sabari, a gbilen a xɔnyi. Mɛnni a naxa a booree nun a xa ginɛ Sɛrɛsi xili.

sentences.english: And he gave them an account of the glories of his wealth, and the number of children he had, and the ways in which he had been honoured by the king, and how he had put him over the captains and servants of the king.
sentences.susu: A naxa a yɛtɛ igbo fɔlɔ a xa naafuli xa fe ra, a xa di wuyaxi xa fe ra, nun a tide xa fe ra, mangɛ naxan fixi a ma kuntigie nun mangɛdie tagi.

sentences.english: And Haman said further, Truly, Esther the queen let no man but myself come in to the feast which she had made ready for the king; and tomorrow again I am to be her guest with the king.
sentences.susu: Haman naxa a fala e bɛ, «Safe na birin xun ma, mangɛ ginɛ Esita n tan keren nan xili, a muxu nun mangɛ xa sa muxu dɛge a xɔnyi to. Tina fan, muxu man sigama nɛ naa.

sentences.english: But all this is nothing to me while I see Mordecai the Jew seated by the king's doorway.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ na birin mu findima sɛɛwɛ ra n bɛ, danmi n na Yuwifi Morodekayi toma mangɛ xa banxi sode dɛ ra.»

sentences.english: Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, Let a pillar, fifty cubits high, be made ready for hanging him, and in the morning get the king to give orders for the hanging of Mordecai: then you will be able to go to the feast with the king with a glad heart. And Haman was pleased with the suggestion, and he had the pillar made.
sentences.susu: A xa ginɛ Sɛrɛsi nun a booree naxa a fala a bɛ, «I naxan nabama, tina gɛɛsɛgɛ, i xa wuri kuye nɔngɔn ya tongo suuli ti, i fa mangɛ mayandi Morodekayi xa gbaku na kɔn na. Na kui wo nun mangɛ sigama nɛ Esita xɔnyi sɛɛwɛ kui.» Na fe naxa rafan Haman ma ki fanyi ra, a fa na wuri ti naa.

sentences.english: That night the king was unable to get any sleep; and he sent for the books of the records; and while some one was reading them to the king,
sentences.susu: Na kɔɛ ra mangɛ mu nɔ xide. A naxa xɛɛra rasiga bukie tongode naxee nu findixi mangɛya xa taruxui ra. Na naxa xaran mangɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: It came out that it was recorded in the book how Mordecai had given word of the designs of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's servants, keepers of the door, by whom an attack on the king had been designed.
sentences.susu: E naxa fe nde xaran Morodekayi xa fe ra. A nu bara a kolon mangɛ banxi kantamae Bigitana nun Tɛrɛsi nu wama mangɛ Asuyerusu faxafe nɛ.

sentences.english: And the king said, What honour and reward have been given to Mordecai for this? Then the servants who were waiting on the king said, Nothing has been done for him.
sentences.susu: Na kui mangɛ naxa a xa batulae maxɔrin, «Won Morodekayi binya di na fe ma?» Mangɛ xa batulae naxa a yaabi, «Fefe mu nu raba a bɛ sinden.»

sentences.english: Then the king said, Who is in the outer room? Now Haman had come into the outer room to get the king's authority for the hanging of Mordecai on the pillar which he had made ready for him.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ man naxa e maxɔrin, «Nde baxi sode n ma banxi kui yakɔsi?» Haman nu bara so mangɛ xɔnyi, alako a xa a mayandi Morodekayi xa gbaku wuri ma, naxan nu bara gɛ tide naa.

sentences.english: And the king's servants said to him, See, Haman is waiting in the outer room. And the king said, Let him come in.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra mangɛ xa batulae naxa mangɛ yaabi, «Haman nan be.» Mangɛ naxa a fala e bɛ, «A xa fa n yire.»

sentences.english: So Haman came in. And the king said to him, What is to be done to the man whom the king has delight in honouring? Then the thought came into Haman's mind, Whom, more than myself, would the king have pleasure in honouring?
sentences.susu: Haman to so, mangɛ naxa a maxɔrin, «Mixi nde na n wama naxan binyafe ki fanyi. N lan n xa munse raba na kanyi bɛ?» Haman naxa a maɲɔxun a bɔɲɛ ma, «Mixi gbɛtɛ mu na mangɛ wama naxan binyafe bafe n tan na.»

sentences.english: And Haman, answering the king, said, For the man whom the king has delight in honouring,
sentences.susu: Na kui Haman naxa mangɛ yaabi, «Mangɛ, i wama mixi naxan binyafe,

sentences.english: Let them take the robes which the king generally puts on, and the horse on which the king goes, and the crown which is on his head:
sentences.susu: a lanma mangɛ dugi, mangɛ bara naxan nagoro a ma, a xa na ragoro na mixi ma. E man xa fa soe nde ra i bara dɔxɔ naxan fari, mangɛ tɔnxuma saxi naxan ma.

sentences.english: And let the robes and the horse be given to one of the king's most noble captains, so that they may put them on the man whom the king has delight in honouring, and let him go on horseback through the streets of the town, with men crying out before him, So let it be done to the man whom the king has delight in honouring.
sentences.susu: I xa mixi xungbe nde xa na dugi ragoro na mixi ma, i wama naxan binyafe. A na te soe fari, boore xa a raɲɛrɛ taa kui, a xa siga masenyi ti ra, ‹Wo a mato mangɛ naxan nabama mixi bɛ, a wama naxan binyafe.›»

sentences.english: Then the king said to Haman, Go quickly, and take the robes and the horse, as you have said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, who is seated at the king's doorway: see that you do everything as you have said.
sentences.susu: Awa, mangɛ naxa a fala Haman bɛ, «I xulun, i sa dugi nun soe tongo, i fa i xa wɔyɛnyi birin nakamali Morodekayi bɛ, na Yuwifi naxan dɔxɔma mangɛ xa banxi sode dɛ ra. I naxa nɛɛmu i fala xui sese ma.»

sentences.english: Then Haman took the robes and the horse, and dressing Mordecai in the robes, he made him go on horseback through the streets of the town, crying out before him, So let it be done to the man whom the king has delight in honouring.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Haman naxa sa dugi nun soe tongo. A naxa mangɛ dugi ragoro Morodekayi ma. Morodekayi to te soe fari, Haman naxa soe raɲɛrɛ taa kui a masenfe ra ɲama bɛ, «‹Wo a mato mangɛ naxan nabama mixi bɛ, a wama naxan binyafe.›»

sentences.english: And Mordecai came back to the king's doorway. But Haman went quickly back to his house, sad and with his head covered.
sentences.susu: E to gɛ na rabade, Morodekayi naxa gbilen mangɛ xa banxi sode dɛ ra, Haman tan naxa a xulun sigafe ra a xɔnyi, a yatagi ixɔnɔxi.

sentences.english: And Haman gave his wife Zeresh and all his friends an account of what had taken place. Then his wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, If Mordecai, who is starting to get the better of you, is of the seed of the Jews, you will not be able to do anything against him, but you will certainly go down before him.
sentences.susu: Haman to na birin fala a xa ginɛ Sɛrɛsi nun a dɛfanbooree bɛ, e naxa a yaabi, «Xa yi Morodekayi, Yuwifi bɔnsɔɛ na a ra, i mu nɔma tide a kanke. I fama nɛ i yɛtɛ xun nakanade tun!»

sentences.english: While they were still talking, the king's servants came to take Haman to the feast which Esther had made ready.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui yati mangɛ xa mixi ndee naxa fa a xilide, a xa siga mangɛ ginɛ Esita xɔnyi a dɛgede.

sentences.english: So the king and Haman came to take wine with Esther the queen.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ nun Haman naxa siga mangɛ ginɛ Esita xɔnyi e dɛgede.

sentences.english: And the king said to Esther again on the second day, while they were drinking, What is your prayer, Queen Esther? for it will be given to you; and what is your request? for it will be done, even to the half of my kingdom.
sentences.susu: Na sigɛ firin nde kui, mangɛ nu wɛni minma tɛmui naxɛ, a man naxa gbilen Esita maxɔrin na, «Esita, i wama naxan xɔn ma, a fala n bɛ alako n xa na raba. Munse xɔli i ma? Hali i wama n ma mangɛya tagi nan xɔn ma, n a fima nɛ i ma.»

sentences.english: Then Esther the queen, answering, said, If I have your approval, O king, and if it is the king's pleasure, let my life be given to me in answer to my prayer, and my people at my request:
sentences.susu: Mangɛ ginɛ Esita naxa a yaabi, «Mangɛ, xa i sa tin, n wama fe naxan xɔn ma, i xa n tan nun n bɔnsɔɛ rakisi.

sentences.english: For we are given up, I and my people, to destruction and death and to be cut off. If we had been taken as men-servants and women-servants for a price, I would have said nothing, for our trouble is little in comparison with the king's loss.
sentences.susu: N tan nun n ma mixie bara mati, alako muxu xa halaki, muxu xa faxa, muxu xa ɲɔn feo. Xa e muxu mati konyie gbansan nan na nu, n mu fefe falama i bɛ nu, n dunduma nɛ tun, barima na fe mu xɔrɔxɔ nu han n xa mangɛ tɔɔrɔ.»

sentences.english: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen, Who is he and where is he who has had this evil thought in his heart?
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Asuyerusu naxa mangɛ ginɛ Esita maxɔrin keren na, «Nde suusaxi yi fe mɔɔli maɲɔxunde? Na kanyi na minden?»

sentences.english: And Esther said, Our hater and attacker is this evil Haman. Then Haman was full of fear before the king and the queen.
sentences.susu: Esita naxa a yaabi, «Muxu yaxui xungbe, naxan wama muxu tɔɔrɔfe, na findixi yi Haman mixi kobi nan na.» Haman to na wɔyɛnyi mɛ, gaaxui naxa a suxu a ɲaaxi ra.

sentences.english: And the king in his wrath got up from the feast and went into the garden: and Haman got to his feet to make a prayer for his life to Esther the queen: for he saw that the king's purpose was evil against him.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ bɔɲɛ naxa te, a mini tande ma. Haman to a kolon mangɛ ɲan bara natɛ tongo a xa fe ra, a naxa lu mangɛ ginɛ Esita fɛ ma, a xa a mayandi a xa a rakisi.

sentences.english: Then the king came back from the garden into the room where they had been drinking; and Haman was stretched out on the seat where Esther was. Then the king said, Is he taking the queen by force before my eyes in my house? And while the words were on the king's lips, they put a cloth over Haman's face.
sentences.susu: Haman to a felen mangɛ ginɛ Esita bun ma, mangɛ so tɛmui nan na ki kelife tande ma. Mangɛ naxa sɔnxɔɛ rate, «Yi xɛmɛ na munse rabafe yi ki? A man wama dutunfe mangɛ ginɛ Esita nan ma n ya xɔri n ma banxi kui?» Mangɛ fɛfɛ na wɔyɛnyi fala, mixie naxa Haman yatagi makoto, e a xanin.

sentences.english: Then Harbonah, one of the unsexed servants waiting before the king, said, See, the pillar fifty cubits high, which Haman made for Mordecai, who said a good word for the king, is still in its place in Haman's house. Then the king said, Put him to death by hanging him on it.
sentences.susu: Xarabona, mangɛ xa mixi nde, naxa a fala mangɛ bɛ, «Haman ɲan bara wuri ti a xɔnyi, a nu wama Morodekayi gbakufe dɛnnaxɛ, Morodekayi naxan nu bara mangɛ rakisi. Na wuri ite nɔngɔn ya tongo suuli.» Awa, mangɛ naxa a yamari, «Haman xa gbaku mɛnni nɛ.»

sentences.english: So Haman was put to death by hanging him on the pillar he had made for Mordecai. Then the king's wrath became less.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra Haman naxa gbaku na wuri ma, naxan nu tixi Morodekayi xili ma a faxafe ra. Na dangi xanbi, mangɛ bɔɲɛ naxa goro.

sentences.english: That day the king gave all the family of Haman, the hater of the Jews, to Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had made clear what he was to her.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ mangɛ Asuyerusu naxa Yuwifie yaxui Haman xa se birin fi mangɛ ginɛ Esita ma. Morodekayi naxa a yɛtɛ masen mangɛ bɛ, barima Esita nu bara a fala mangɛ bɛ a Morodekayi findixi a taara nan na.

sentences.english: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther put Mordecai over the family of Haman.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a xa tɔnxuma ba a yɛtɛ bɛlɛxɛ ra, a naxan nasuxu Haman yi, a a so Morodekayi yi ra. Esita naxa Haman harige birin taxu Morodekayi ra.

sentences.english: Then Esther again came before the king, falling down at his feet, and made request to him with weeping, that he would put a stop to the evil purposes of Haman the Agagite and the designs which he had made against the Jews.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Esita naxa a mafelen mangɛ bun ma, a a mayandi a naxa Haman Agagaka waxɔnfe kobi raba Yuwifie ra.

sentences.english: Then the king put out the rod of gold to Esther, and she got up before the king.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a xa mangɛya sawuri xɛɛma daaxi itala Esita mabiri. Na nan a niya Esita naxa keli a ti a ya i.

sentences.english: And she said, If it is the king's pleasure and if I have his approval and this thing seems right to the king and I am pleasing to him, then let letters be sent giving orders against those which Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, sent out for the destruction of the Jews in all divisions of the kingdom:
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen a bɛ, «Mangɛ, xa i tin, xa n ma fe rafan i ma, xa i bara natɛ tongo, xa i n xanuxi yandi i xa kɛɛdi sɛbɛ naxan Hamɛdata xa di Agagaka Haman xa yaamari kanama, yaamari naxan fi Yuwifie faxafe ra i xa mangɛya birin kui.

sentences.english: For how is it possible for me to see the evil which is to overtake my nation? how may I see the destruction of my people?
sentences.susu: N tan mu nɔma n ya tide n ma mixie ra tɔɔrɛ nun gbaloe xa e sɔtɔ.»

sentences.english: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, See now, I have given Esther the family of Haman, and he has come to his death by hanging, because he made an attack on the Jews.
sentences.susu: Awa, mangɛ Asuyerusu naxa a masen mangɛ ginɛ Esita nun Yuwifi Morodekayi bɛ, «N bara Haman faxa, barima a nu wama Yuwifie halakife nɛ. N man bara Haman harige fi Esita ma.

sentences.english: So now send a letter about the Jews, writing whatever seems good to you, in the king's name, and stamping it with the king's ring: for a writing signed in the king's name and stamped with the king's ring may not be changed.
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi wo naxan nabama, wo xa kɛɛdi sɛbɛ n xili ra, naxan nɔma Yuwifie xa fe fande. Wo xa n ma mangɛ tɔnxuma sa a ma, barima xa n ma tɔnxuma na a ma, na yaamari mu nɔma masarade.»

sentences.english: Then at that time, on the twenty-third day of the third month, which is the month Sivan, the king's scribes were sent for; and everything ordered by Mordecai was put in writing and sent to the Jews and the captains and the rulers and the chiefs of all the divisions of the kingdom from India to Ethiopia, a hundred and twenty-seven divisions, to every division in the writing commonly used there, and to every people in their language, and to the Jews in their writing and their language.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ yati, e naxa sɛbɛlitie maxili. Morodekayi naxa yaamari fi e ma naxan nabama Yuwifie xa fe ra. E naxa na bataaxɛ sɛbɛ mangɛ rasimae, gominae, nun mangɛdie birin ma naxee nu na bɔxi kɛmɛ mɔxɔɲɛn nun solofere xun ma, kelife Inidya ma, han Etiyopi. Kankan gbe nu sɛbɛxi a xa sɛbɛli ki ma nun a bari xui ra. Yuwifie fan naxa e gbe sɔtɔ e xa sɛbɛli ki ma nun e bari xui ra. Na raba kike saxan nde nɛ, kike naxan xili «Sifan,» na xi mɔxɔɲɛn nun saxan nde lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: The letters were sent in the name of King Ahasuerus and stamped with his ring, and they were taken by men on horseback, going on the quick-running horses used for the king's business, the offspring of his best horses:
sentences.susu: Na bataaxɛe naxa sɛbɛ mangɛ xili ra, a xa tɔnxuma naxa sa e ma. Xɛɛra naxee nu lan e xa bataaxɛe rasanba, nee naxa siga e gi ra mangɛ xa soe fanyie fari.

sentences.english: In these letters the king gave authority to the Jews in every town to come together and make a fight for their lives, and to send death and destruction on the power of any people in any part of the kingdom attacking them or their children or their women, and to take their goods from them by force,
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xa kɛɛdi a masen nɛ, Yuwifie nɔma e malande e xa e yɛtɛ xun magere. Xa mixi yo wama e gerefe, mangɛ bara tin Yuwifie xa e faxa, e nun e xa ginɛe nun e xa die. E man nɔma e harige birin tongode.

sentences.english: On one day in every division of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, that is, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month Adar.
sentences.susu: Yi yaamari nu lanxi a xa raba mangɛ Asuyerusu xa mangɛya birin kui, Ada kike, ɲɛ kike fu nun firin nde, a xi fu nun saxan nde ma.

sentences.english: A copy of the writing, to be made public as an order in every division of the kingdom, was given out to all the peoples, so that the Jews might be ready when that day came to give punishment to their haters.
sentences.susu: Na yaamari nu sɛbɛxi kɛɛdie ma, bɔxi yo bɔxi xa e gbe sɔtɔ alako birin xa a kolon, Yuwifie fan xa rɛdi e gbeɲɔxɔde e yaxuie ma.

sentences.english: So the men went out on the quick-running horses used on the king's business, wasting no time and forced on by the king's order; and the order was given out in Shushan, the king's town.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ to yaamari fi, xɛɛrae naxa siga e gi ra mangɛ xa soe fanyie fari. Yi yaamari naxa xaran Suse mangataa kui.

sentences.english: And Mordecai went out from before the king, dressed in king-like robes of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold and clothing of purple and the best linen: and all the town of Shushan gave loud cries of joy.
sentences.susu: Morodekayi naxa mini mangɛ xa banxi kui, mangɛ dugi fɔɔrɛ nun a fiixɛ ragoroxi a ma, mangɛ tɔnxuma xɛɛma daaxi dɔxɔxi a xun ma, nun donma xungbe gbeeli ragoroxi a ma. Susekae birin naxa sɛɛwa, e e xui rate ɲɛlɛxinyi kui.

sentences.english: And the Jews had light and joy and honour.
sentences.susu: Yuwifie naxa sɛɛwa ki fanyi ra e xa xunnakeli xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And in every part of the kingdom and in every town, wherever the king's letter and his order came, the Jews were glad with great joy, and had a feast and a good day. And a great number of the people of the land became Jews: for the fear of the Jews had come on them.
sentences.susu: Yire birin nun taa birin mangɛ xa yaamari xaranxi dɛnnaxɛ, Yuwifie naxa xulunyi ti sɛɛwɛ kui. Mixi wuyaxi naxee kelixi si gbɛtɛe ya ma, e naxa e yɛtɛ findi Yuwifie ra, barima e nu bara gaaxu e ya ra.

sentences.english: Now on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, when the time came for the king's order to be put into effect, on the very day when the haters of the Jews had been hoping to have rule over them; though the opposite had come about, and the Jews had rule over their haters;
sentences.susu: Ada kike fu nun firin nde, xi fu nun saxan nde to a li, mangɛ xa yaamari nu lanma a xa raba. Na lɔxɔɛ ma Yuwifie yaxuie nu wama e masɔtɔfe, kɔnɔ fee naxa masara, Yuwifie naxa nɔ e ra.

sentences.english: On that day, the Jews came together in their towns through all the divisions of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, for the purpose of attacking all those who were attempting evil against them: and everyone had to give way before them, for the fear of them had come on all the peoples.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Asuyerusu xa mangɛya yire birin, Yuwifie naxa e malan e yaxuie gerede. Mixi yo mu nɔ tide e ya ra, sie birin naxa gaaxu.

sentences.english: And all the chiefs and the captains and the rulers and those who did the king's business gave support to the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai had come on them.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi birin mangɛdie, mangɛ rasimae, gominae, nun mangɛ xa mixie naxa Yuwifie mali, barima e nu gaaxuxi Morodekayi ya ra.

sentences.english: For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and word of him went out through every part of the kingdom: for the man Mordecai became greater and greater.
sentences.susu: Morodekayi nu bara findi mixi xungbe ra mangɛ banxi kui. A xili fanyi naxa yire birin li, a tide xun nu masama tun.

sentences.english: So the Jews overcame all their attackers with the sword and with death and destruction, and did to their haters whatever they had a desire to do.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra Yuwifie naxa e yaxuie bɔnbɔ santidɛgɛma ra, e e faxa. E naxa e waxɔnfe birin naba e yaxuie ra.

sentences.english: And in Shushan the Jews put to death five hundred men.
sentences.susu: Yuwifie naxa mixi kɛmɛ suuli faxa Suse mangataa.

sentences.english: They put to death Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
sentences.susu: E man naxa Parasandata, Dalifɔn, Asipata,

sentences.english: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
sentences.susu: Porata, Adaliya, Aridata,

sentences.english: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,
sentences.susu: Paramasata, Arisayi, Aridayi, e nun Fayesata birin faxa.

sentences.english: The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the hater of the Jews; but they put not a hand on any of their goods.
sentences.susu: Na mixi fu findi Hamɛdata xa di Haman xa die nan na, Yuwifie yaxui. E naxa na mixie faxa, kɔnɔ e mu mixi yo harige tongo.

sentences.english: On that day the number of those who had been put to death in the town of Shushan was given to the king.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ yati, mangɛ naxa a kolon mixi naxan xasabi faxaxi Suse mangataa.

sentences.english: And the king said to Esther the queen, The Jews have put five hundred men to death in Shushan, as well as the ten sons of Haman: what then have they done in the rest of the kingdom! Now what is your prayer? for it will be given to you; what other request have you? and it will be done.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a fala mangɛ ginɛ Esita bɛ, «Yuwifie bara mixi kɛmɛ suuli faxa Suse mangataa, a nun Haman xa di fu. Xa e bara na mɔɔli raba yi taa kui, e munse rabaxi yire gbɛtɛe n ma mangɛya kui? Kɔnɔ i wama naxan xɔn, n na rabama nɛ i bɛ. I waxɔnfe na munse ra di? Na birin nabama nɛ i bɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Esther said, If it is the king's pleasure, let authority be given to the Jews in Shushan to do tomorrow as has been done today, and let orders be given for the hanging of Haman's ten sons.
sentences.susu: Esita naxa a yaabi, «Xa i bara tin, Yuwifi naxee na Suse, e man xa nɔ e gbeɲɔxɔde tina. Haman xa di fu xa gbaku wuri ma.»

sentences.english: And the king said that this was to be done, and the order was given out in Shushan, and the hanging of Haman's ten sons was effected.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa yaamari fi a xa raba alɔ Esita a falaxi ki naxɛ. Na yaamari naxa xaran Susekae bɛ. Haman xa di fu fan naxa gbaku wuri ma.

sentences.english: For the Jews who were in Shushan came together again on the fourteenth day of the month Adar and put to death three hundred men in Shushan; but they put not a hand on their goods.
sentences.susu: Ada kike xi fu nun naani nde ra, Yuwifie man naxa e malan, e xɛmɛ kɛmɛ saxan faxa taa kui, kɔnɔ e mu e harige yo tongo.

sentences.english: And the other Jews in every division of the kingdom came together, fighting for their lives, and got salvation from their haters and put seventy-five thousand of them to death; but they did not put a hand on their goods.
sentences.susu: Yuwifi naxee nu na bɔxi gbɛtɛe ma, nee fan naxa e malan, e yɛtɛ xun magerede e yaxuie ma. E naxa e yaxui mixi wulu tongo solofere a nun suuli faxa, kɔnɔ e fan mu nee harige yo tongo.

sentences.english: This they did on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same month they took their rest, and made it a day of feasting and joy.
sentences.susu: Na birin naba Ada kike xi fu nun saxan nde nɛ. A xi fu nun naani nde ra, Yuwifie naxa e malabu sɛɛwɛ kui, e xulunyi ti.

sentences.english: But the Jews in Shushan came together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth day of the month; and on the fifteenth day they took their rest, and made it a day of feasting and joy.
sentences.susu: Yuwifi naxee nu na Suse, nee naxa e yaxuie gere na xi fu nun saxan nde nun fu nun naani nde ma. E naxa e malabu sɛɛwɛ kui a xi fu nun suuli nde lɔxɔɛ, e xulunyi fan ti.

sentences.english: So the Jews of the country places living in unwalled towns make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of feasting and joy and a good day, a day for sending offerings one to another.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi Yuwifi naxee na daaxae, nee xulunyi tima Ada kike xi fu nun naani nde ma sɛɛwɛ kui, kankan a dɔxɔboore buɲama na tɛmui.

sentences.english: And Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in every division of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, near and far,
sentences.susu: Morodekayi naxa na fe birin sɛbɛ bataaxɛe kui Yuwifie ma, naxee nu yire makuyee nun yire makɔrɔxie Asuyerusu xa mangɛya kui.

sentences.english: Ordering them to keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar and the fifteenth day of the same month, every year,
sentences.susu: A naxa a sɛbɛ, Yuwifie xa Ada kike xi fu nun naani nde nun a xi fu nun suuli nde findi sali lɔxɔɛe ra ɲɛ yo ɲɛ,

sentences.english: As days on which the Jews had rest from their haters, and the month which for them was turned from sorrow to joy, and from weeping to a good day: and that they were to keep them as days of feasting and joy, of sending offerings to one another and good things to the poor.
sentences.susu: barima e e yɛtɛ sɔtɔ e yaxuie yi ra na tɛmui nɛ, e xa tɔɔrɛ findi ɲɛlɛxinyi nan na, e xa sunnunyi findi sɛɛwɛ nan na. Na lɔxɔɛe a lan nɛ e xa e dɔxɔbooree buɲa, e man xa setaree ki.

sentences.english: And the Jews gave their word to go on as they had been doing and as Mordecai had given them orders in writing;
sentences.susu: Yuwifie naxa Morodekayi xa yaamari suxu, na naxa findi naamunyi ra e bɛ ɲɛ yo ɲɛ.

sentences.english: Because Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the hater of all the Jews, had made designs for their destruction, attempting to get a decision by Pur (that is, chance) with a view to putting an end to them and cutting them off;
sentences.susu: E na birin naba nɛ barima Hamɛdata Agagaka xa di Haman, Yuwifie yaxui, nu bara wa Yuwifie birin halakife. A nu bara ɲɛli bɔnbɔ, naxan xili Puri, alako a xa e halaki, a xa e sɔntɔ.

sentences.english: But when the business was put before the king, he gave orders by letters that the evil design which he had made against the Jews was to be turned against himself; and that he and his sons were to be put to death by hanging.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Esita nu bara siga mangɛ yire. Mangɛ naxa kɛɛdi sɛbɛ yi ki, «Haman nu wama fe ɲaaxi naxan nabafe Yuwifie ra, na xa gbilen a ma. A xa die fan xa gbaku wuri ma.»

sentences.english: So these days were named Purim, after the name of Pur. And so, because of the words of this letter, and of what they had seen in connection with this business, and what had come to them,
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi yi lɔxɔɛe xili falama «Purie,» barima e bari xui ra e ɲɛli xili falama, «Puri.» Bataaxɛ sɛbɛli to kamali na ki,

sentences.english: The Jews made a rule and gave an undertaking, causing their seed and all those who were joined to them to do the same, so that it might be in force for ever, that they would keep those two days, as ordered in the letter, at the fixed time every year;
sentences.susu: Yuwifie naxa na lɔxɔɛ firinyie findi sali lɔxɔɛe ra. Na naxa findi naamunyi ra e tan nun e bɔnsɔɛ bɛ, nun mixie bɛ naxee soma e xa diinɛ kui. E xa yi lɔxɔɛ firinyie binya ɲɛ yo ɲɛ, e xa fe birin naba alɔ Morodekayi a yamari ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And that those days were to be kept in memory through every generation and every family, in every division of the kingdom and every town, that there might never be a time when these days of Purim would not be kept among the Jews, or when the memory of them would go from the minds of their seed.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛ naxee sa fama, Yuwifie xa denbayae naxee na yire birin, e xa yi Puri lɔxɔɛe binya, alako e tan nun e bɔnsɔɛ naxa nɛɛmu yi fe dangixi ma.

sentences.english: Then Esther the queen, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, sent a second letter giving the force of their authority to the order about the Purim.
sentences.susu: Awa, Abixayili xa di Esita, naxan findixi mangɛ ginɛ ra, a nun Morodekayi, e naxa yi bataaxɛ mangɛ daaxi firin nde sɛbɛ Puri Sali xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And he sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred and twenty-seven divisions of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with true words of peace,
sentences.susu: E naxa bataaxɛe rasiga Yuwifie birin ma, naxee nu na mangɛ Asuyerusu xa bɔxi kɛmɛ mɔxɔɲɛn nun solofere birin kui, alako mixie xa ɲɛrɛ bɔɲɛsa nun tinxinyi kui.

sentences.english: Giving the force of law to these days of Purim at their fixed times, as they had been ordered by Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen, and in keeping with the rules they had made for themselves and their seed, in connection with their time of going without food and their cry for help.
sentences.susu: E man naxa a masen Yuwifie bɛ, e xa Puri Sali lɔxɔɛe raba a waxati yati ma, alɔ Morodekayi nun mangɛ ginɛ Esita e yamarixi ki naxɛ. E tan nun e bɔnsɔɛ birin xa sunyi suxu, e xa Ala maxandi.

sentences.english: The order given by Esther gave the force of law to the rules about the Purim; and it was recorded in the book.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ ginɛ Esita xa yaamarie Puri salie xa fe ra, na naxa findi sɛriyɛ ra, e fa sɛbɛ yi kitaabui kui.

sentences.english: And King Ahasuerus put a tax on the land and on the islands of the sea.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Asuyerusu naxa duuti maxili mixi birin ma, kelife xare ma han surie ma.

sentences.english: And all his acts of power and his great strength and the full story of the high place which the king gave Mordecai, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Media and Persia?
sentences.susu: Mangɛ sɛnbɛ nun a xa limaniya birin sɛbɛxi Perise nun Mediya mangɛe xa taruxui kui. Morodekayi tide gbo ki, na fan sɛbɛxi na kui.

sentences.english: For Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews and respected by the body of his countrymen; working for the good of his people, and saying words of peace to all his seed.
sentences.susu: Morodekayi Yuwifi naxa findi mangɛ Asuyerusu xa mixi xungbe ra, a man naxa findi mixi kɛndɛ ra Yuwifie bɛ. E naxa a xanu ki fanyi, barima a nu wali fanyi rabama e bɛ alako Yuwifie xa fe xa siga yare ma.

sentences.english: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. He was without sin and upright, fearing God and keeping himself far from evil.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ nde nu na Usu bɔxi ma naxan nu xili Ayuba. Mixi hagigɛ nan nu lanxi a ma, a matinxin. A nu gaaxuma Ala ya ra, a mu nu birama fe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And he had seven sons and three daughters.
sentences.susu: Di xɛmɛ solofere nun di ginɛ saxan nu na a yi ra.

sentences.english: And of cattle he had seven thousand sheep and goats, and three thousand camels, and a thousand oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a very great number of servants. And the man was greater than any of the sons of the east.
sentences.susu: A xa gɔɔrɛ nu lanxi yɛxɛɛ wulu solofere, ɲɔxɔmɛ wulu saxan, ninge wulu keren, a nun sofale kɛmɛ suuli nan ma. Walikɛ gbegbe saxi na nan fari. Binyɛ nu saxi yi xɛmɛ ma dangi mixi birin na na sogetede biri ra.

sentences.english: His sons regularly went to one another's houses, and every one on his day gave a feast: and at these times they sent for their three sisters to take part in their feasts with them.
sentences.susu: A xa die nu xulunyi tima nɛ e boore xɔnyie, e nu e maaginɛe xili alako e birin xa nu e dɛge yire keren.

sentences.english: And at the end of their days of feasting, Job sent and made them clean, getting up early in the morning and offering burned offerings for them all. For, Job said, It may be that my sons have done wrong and said evil of God in their hearts. And Job did this whenever the feasts came round.
sentences.susu: Xulunyie na ba a ra, Ayuba nu sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxie bama nɛ a xa di birin bɛ e rasɛniyɛnfe ra. A nu a maɲɔxunma nɛ a tɛmunde e bara yunubi nde sɔtɔ, xa na mu a ra e bara Ala danka e bɔɲɛ kui. Na kui Ayuba nu luma sɛrɛxɛ ba ra e bɛ tɛmui birin.

sentences.english: And there was a day when the sons of the gods came together before the Lord, and the Satan came with them.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔɛ nde Ala xa malekɛe naxa fa Alatala yire. Sentanɛ fan nu na e ya ma.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to the Satan, Where do you come from? And the Satan said in answer, From wandering this way and that on the earth, and walking about on it.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa Sentanɛ maxɔrin, «I kelixi minden?» Sentanɛ naxa a yaabi, «N kelixi duniɲa iɲɛrɛde.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to the Satan, Have you taken note of my servant Job, for there is no one like him on the earth, a man without sin and upright, fearing God and keeping himself far from evil?
sentences.susu: Alatala man naxa a maxɔrin, «I bara n ma konyi Ayuba rakɔrɔsi? A maniyɛ yo mu na duniɲa ma. A fan, a tinxin. Ala yaragaaxui nan a ra, fe ɲaaxi mu rafan a ma.»

sentences.english: And the Satan said in answer to the Lord, Is it for nothing that Job is a god-fearing man?
sentences.susu: Sentanɛ naxa a yaabi, «Ayuba xa gaaxui i ya ra tun mu a ra?

sentences.english: Have you yourself not put a wall round him and his house and all he has on every side, blessing the work of his hands, and increasing his cattle in the land?
sentences.susu: I mu a kantaxi xɛ, a tan, a xa denbaya, nun a harige birin? I bara barakɛ sa a suxufe birin ma, alako a xa gɔɔrɛ xa gbo tun.

sentences.english: But now, put out your hand against all he has, and he will be cursing you to your face.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa li i naxa din a harige ra, n xa a fala i bɛ, a fama nɛ i dankade keren na.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to the Satan, See, I give all he has into your hands, only do not put a finger on the man himself. And the Satan went out from before the Lord.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a fala Sentanɛ bɛ, «Awa yire, n bara a harige birin sa i sagoe, kɔnɔ i naxa a gundi tɔɔrɔ de.» Na tɛmui Sentanɛ naxa keli Alatala yire.

sentences.english: And there was a day when his sons and daughters were feasting in the house of their oldest brother,
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔɛ nde Ayuba xa die nu na xulunyi tife e taara xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And a man came to Job, and said, The oxen were ploughing, and the asses were taking their food by their side:
sentences.susu: Xɛɛra nde naxa fa Ayuba yire, a a fala a bɛ, «I xa walikɛe nu na ningee rawalife xɛ ma, sofalee fan nu na e dɛ madonfe na longori.

sentences.english: And the men of Sheba came against them and took them away, putting the young men to the sword, and I was the only one who got away safe to give you the news.
sentences.susu: Sebaka ndee naxa din i xa walikɛe ra, e e faxa santidɛgɛma ra. E man ningee fan xanin. N keren peti nan nɔ n yɛtɛ bade e yi. N faxi na fe nan dɛntɛgɛde i bɛ.»

sentences.english: And this one was still talking when another came, and said, The fire of God came down from heaven, burning up the sheep and the goats and the young men completely, and I was the only one who got away safe to give you the news.
sentences.susu: Na mu gɛ na masenyi ra, xɛɛra gbɛtɛ naxa fa, a a fala Ayuba bɛ, «Ala bara a ragiri galanyi xa goro i xa yɛxɛɛe nun e makantamae ma. A bara e birin faxa. N keren peti nan nɔ n yɛtɛ bade e yi. N faxi na fe nan dɛntɛgɛde i bɛ.»

sentences.english: And this one was still talking when another came, and said, The Chaldaeans made themselves into three bands, and came down on the camels and took them away, putting the young men to the sword, and I was the only one who got away safe to give you the news.
sentences.susu: Na fan mu gɛ a xa masenyi ra, xɛɛra gbɛtɛ naxa fa, a a fala Ayuba bɛ, «Kalidika, gaali dɔxɔ saxan bara bagan i xa ɲɔxɔmɛe ma, e e makantamae faxa santidɛgɛma ra, e ɲɔxɔmɛe xanin. N keren peti nan nɔ n bade e yi. N faxi na fe nan dɛntɛgɛde i bɛ.»

sentences.english: And this one was still talking when another came, and said, Your sons and your daughters were feasting together in their oldest brother's house,
sentences.susu: Na fan mu gɛ a xa masenyi ra, xɛɛra gbɛtɛ naxa fa, a a fala Ayuba bɛ, «I xa die to nu na xulunyi tife e taara xɔnyi.

sentences.english: When a great wind came rushing from the waste land against the four sides of the house, and it came down on the young men, and they are dead; and I was the only one who got away safe to give you the news.
sentences.susu: Foye belebele faxi na tɛmui nɛ keli gbengberenyi ma, a banxi rabira i xa die ma. E birin bara faxa. N keren peti nan kisixi. N faxi na nan dɛntɛgɛde i bɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Job got up, and after parting his clothing and cutting off his hair, he went down on his face to the earth, and gave worship, and said,
sentences.susu: Na kui Ayuba naxa keli, a a xa donma ibɔɔ a ma, a a xunyi bi sunnunyi ma, a fa a rafelen bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: With nothing I came out of my mother's body, and with nothing I will go back there; the Lord gave and the Lord has taken away; let the Lord's name be praised.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala, «N faxi duniɲa n mageli nan na n bari tɛmui, n man gbilenma n mageli nan na n siga tɛmui. Alatala bara n ki harige ra, Alatala man bara na harige ba n yi. Tantui na Ala bɛ.»

sentences.english: In all this Job did no sin, and did not say that God's acts were foolish.
sentences.susu: Na birin kui, Ayuba mu yunubi yo raba, a mu fe kobi yo fala Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: And there was a day when the sons of the gods came together before the Lord, and the Satan came with them.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔɛ nde Alatala xa malekɛe man naxa fa a yire, Sentanɛ man nu na e tagi.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to the Satan, Where do you come from? And the Satan said in answer, From wandering this way and that on the earth, and walking about on it.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa Sentanɛ maxɔrin, «I kelixi minden?» Sentanɛ naxa a yaabi, «N kelixi duniɲa iɲɛrɛde.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to the Satan, Have you taken note of my servant Job, for there is no one like him on the earth, a man without sin and upright, fearing God and keeping himself far from evil? and he still keeps his righteousness, though you have been moving me to send destruction on him without cause.
sentences.susu: Alatala man naxa a maxɔrin, «I bara n ma konyi Ayuba rakɔrɔsi? A maniyɛ yo mu na duniɲa ma. A fan, a tinxin. Ala yaragaaxui nan a ra, fe ɲaaxi mu rafan a ma. Han ya a xa tinxinyi mu masara, hali i to waxi n xa a halaki tun.»

sentences.english: And the Satan said in answer to the Lord, Skin for skin, all a man has he will give for his life.
sentences.susu: Sentanɛ naxa a yaabi, «Adama fe birin nabama a fate xa tɔɔrɛ matangafe nan na. A nɔma a harige birin masarade yalanyi ra.

sentences.english: But now, if you only put your hand on his bone and his flesh, he will certainly be cursing you to your face.
sentences.susu: Xa i a fate yati tɔɔrɔma, a i dankama nɛ keren na.»

sentences.english: And the Lord said to the Satan, See, he is in your hands, only do not take his life.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxa a fala Sentanɛ bɛ, «Awa yire, n bara a fate sa i sagoe, kɔnɔ i naxa a faxa de.»

sentences.english: And the Satan went out from before the Lord, and sent on Job an evil disease covering his skin from his feet to the top of his head.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Sentanɛ naxa keli Alatala yire. A naxa suurie ikonkon Ayuba fate birin ma, keli a sanyi kui ma han a xuntagi.

sentences.english: And he took a broken bit of a pot, and, seated in the dust, was rubbing himself with the sharp edge of it.
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa dɔxɔ tɛ xube xɔɔra sunnunyi kui, a nu a fate xɔɔlin fɛɲɛ kebele ra.

sentences.english: And his wife said to him, Are you still keeping your righteousness? Say a curse against God, and put an end to yourself.
sentences.susu: A xa ginɛ naxa a fala a bɛ, «Han ya i na i xa tinxinyi kui? Ala rasɔtɔ sɔnɔn, i xa faxa.»

sentences.english: And he said to her, You are talking like one of the foolish women. If we take the good God sends us, are we not to take the evil when it comes? In all this Job kept his lips from sin.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Ayuba naxa a yaabi, «I wɔyɛnfe nɛ na ki alɔ xaxilitare. Xa won tinma Ala xa hɛri ra, a mu lanma won xa tin a xa xɔrɔxɔɛ fan na?» Na kui Ayuba mu yunubi yo sɔtɔ a xa wɔyɛnyie kui.

sentences.english: And Job's three friends had word of all this evil which had come on him. And they came every one from his place, Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. So they came together to a meeting-place, in order that they might go and make clear to Job their grief for him, and give him comfort.
sentences.susu: Ayuba boore saxanyie to a xa tɔɔrɛ xa fe mɛ, e naxa keli e xɔnyi sigafe ra Ayuba yire. E xili: Elifasi Temanka, Bilidada Suuxaka, nun Sofara Naamaka. E naxa lu yire keren, e lan fe keren ma, e xa sa Ayuba kunfa ba, e xa a madundu.

sentences.english: And lifting up their eyes when they were still far off, it did not seem that the man they saw was Job because of the change in him. And they gave way to bitter weeping, with signs of grief, and put dust on their heads.
sentences.susu: E to sa a to keli yire makuye, e naxa san a ma, e bɔnbɔ gbelegbelefe ra. E naxa e xa donmae ibɔɔ e ma, e xube maso e ma sunnunyi kui.

sentences.english: And they took their seats on the earth by his side for seven days and seven nights: but no one said a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.
sentences.susu: E naxa dɔxɔ Ayuba sɛɛti ma bɔxi, han xi solofere. Mixi yo mu wɔyɛn keren fala a bɛ, barima e a to nɛ, a xa tɔɔrɛ nu gbo ki fanyi ra.

sentences.english: Then, opening his mouth, and cursing the day of his birth,
sentences.susu: Na birin to dangi, Ayuba naxa a bari lɔxɔɛ danka

sentences.english: Job made answer and said,
sentences.susu: yi masenyi ra:

sentences.english: Let destruction take the day of my birth, and the night on which it was said, A man child has come into the world.
sentences.susu: «N bari lɔxɔɛ xa nɛɛmu duniɲa ra. Na kɔɛ ra e naxɛ, ‹Di xɛmɛ na a ra.›

sentences.english: That day — let it be dark; let not God take note of it from on high, and let not the light be shining on it;
sentences.susu: Ala xa na lɔxɔɛ findi dimi ra, na lɔxɔɛ xa nɛɛmu a ra, a xa tɔnyi dɔxɔ soge yanbafe ra na lɔxɔɛ kui.

sentences.english: Let the dark and the black night take it for themselves; let it be covered with a cloud; let the dark shades of day send fear on it.
sentences.susu: Ala xa na lɔxɔɛ findi dimi ra, a xa nuxui ifɔɔrɛ dusu a xun na, a xa lu dimi magaaxuxi kui.

sentences.english: That night — let the thick dark take it; let it not have joy among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of the months.
sentences.susu: Ala xa na kɔɛ ifɔɔrɔ, a xa na ba kɔnti ra ɲɛ kui, a xa na ba kɔnti ra kike kui.

sentences.english: As for that night, let it have no fruit; let no voice of joy be sounded in it;
sentences.susu: Ala xa na kɔɛ kuma di ra, sɛɛwɛ xui yo naxa ite.

sentences.english: Let it be cursed by those who put a curse on the day; who are ready to make Leviathan awake.
sentences.susu: A xa findi dankɛ ti se ra mandurulae bɛ, naxee ninginangɛ xilima.

sentences.english: Let its morning stars be dark; let it be looking for light, but may it not have any; let it not see the eyes of the dawn.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ subaxɛ tunbuie naxa yanba, kuye naxa iba, naiyalanyi yo naxa mini,

sentences.english: Because it did not keep the doors of my mother's body shut, so that trouble might be veiled from my eyes.
sentences.susu: barima a mu sese raba naxan nu nɔma n barife dande, naxan nu nɔma n nɔxunde n ma tɔɔrɛ ma.

sentences.english: Why did death not take me when I came out of my mother's body, why did I not, when I came out, give up my last breath?
sentences.susu: Munfe ra n nga furi mu bira nu? Munfe ra n mu faxa nu beenu n xa bari?

sentences.english: Why did the knees take me, or why the breasts that they might give me milk?
sentences.susu: Munfe ra n nga n nasɛnɛxi a san ma, a xiɲɛ fi n ma?

sentences.english: For then I might have gone to my rest in quiet, and in sleep have been in peace,
sentences.susu: Xa na mu a ra, yi tɛmui n bɛlɛxi bɔɲɛsa kui nu

sentences.english: With kings and the wise ones of the earth, who put up great houses for themselves;
sentences.susu: mangɛe nun rasimae fɛ ma, naxee xa banxie bara gɛ kanade,

sentences.english: Or with rulers who had gold, and whose houses were full of silver;
sentences.susu: naxee nu bara xɛɛma nun gbeti gbegbe sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Or as a child dead at birth I might never have come into existence; like young children who have not seen the light.
sentences.susu: Munfe ra e mu n nagata, alɔ diyɔrɛ naxan mu waxi, naxan mu mini kɛnɛ ma?

sentences.english: There the passions of the evil are over, and those whose strength has come to an end have rest.
sentences.susu: Gaburi tan kui, mixi ɲaaxie mu nɔma sese ra, mixi taganxie e malabuma nɛ.

sentences.english: There the prisoners are at peace together; the voice of the overseer comes not again to their ears.
sentences.susu: Konyie bɔɲɛsa sɔtɔma nɛ, e mu e kanyi xui mɛma gaburi kui.

sentences.english: The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
sentences.susu: Dimɛdie nun forie na mɛnni, konyie e yɛtɛ sɔtɔma naa.

sentences.english: Why does he give light to him who is in trouble, and life to the bitter in soul;
sentences.susu: Munfe ra Ala a niyama adamadie xa mini kɛnɛ ma, naxee findi tɔɔrɔmixie ra, naxee nimisaxi e xa duniɲɛigiri kui,

sentences.english: To those whose desire is for death, but it comes not; who are searching for it more than for secret wealth;
sentences.susu: naxee faxɛ xɔli mawama, kɔnɔ e mu faxa, naxee faxɛ fenma dangi naafuli ra,

sentences.english: Who are glad with great joy, and full of delight when they come to their last resting-place;
sentences.susu: naxee ɲɛlɛxinma gaburi life ra?

sentences.english: To a man whose way is veiled, and who is shut in by God?
sentences.susu: Munfe ra mixi barima, Ala kira balanxi naxan ya ra, Ala naxan naxɛtɛnma yire birin?

sentences.english: In place of my food I have grief, and cries of sorrow come from me like water.
sentences.susu: N ma donse findixi n ma tɔɔrɛ nan na, n ma minse findixi n yaye nan na.

sentences.english: For I have a fear and it comes on me, and my heart is greatly troubled.
sentences.susu: N na gaaxu fe naxan na, na nan n lima. Fe naxan na n nasɛrɛn, n na nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: I have no peace, no quiet, and no rest; nothing but pain comes on me.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛsa mu na n bɛ, n mu nɔma n sabaride. Malabui mu na n bɛ, fo tɔɔrɛ.»

sentences.english: And Eliphaz the Temanite made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Elifasi Temanka naxa a fala,

sentences.english: If one says a word, will it be a weariness to you? but who is able to keep from saying what is in his mind?
sentences.susu: «Ayuba, i haakɛ to n bɛ n xa wɔyɛn. N mu nɔma dundude.

sentences.english: Truly, you have been a helper to others, and you have made feeble hands strong;
sentences.susu: I bara mixi gbegbe xaran, i bara e ralimaniya.

sentences.english: He who was near to falling has been lifted up by your words, and you have given strength to bent knees.
sentences.susu: I xa masenyie bara mixie mali, i xa wɔyɛnyie bara e sɛnbɛ so.

sentences.english: But now it has come on you and it is a weariness to you; you are touched by it and your mind is troubled.
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi i tan nan to fa na tɔɔrɔfe, limaniya bara ba i tan yi.

sentences.english: Is not your fear of God your support, and your upright way of life your hope?
sentences.susu: I mu i xaxili ti i xa danxaniya ra Ala ma? I mu lama i xa tinxinyi ra?

sentences.english: Have you ever seen destruction come to an upright man? or when were the god-fearing ever cut off?
sentences.susu: I bara mixi fanyi to halakixi tɔɔrɛ ma? Tinxintɔɛ nɔma bɔnɔde?

sentences.english: What I have seen is that those by whom trouble has been ploughed, and evil planted, get the same for themselves.
sentences.susu: N naxan nakɔrɔsixi, fe ɲaaxi rabae nan tɔɔrɔma.

sentences.english: By the breath of God destruction takes them, and by the wind of his wrath they are cut off.
sentences.susu: Ala e xun nakanama a xa xɔnɛ kui.

sentences.english: Though the noise of the lion and the sounding of his voice, may be loud, the teeth of the young lions are broken.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ xa yirindinyi nun baratɛ xa ɲarandanyi magaaxu, kɔnɔ e ɲinyie fama nɛ magirade.

sentences.english: The old lion comes to his end for need of food, and the young of the she-lion go wandering in all directions.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ yati faxama kaamɛ ra, a xa die yensen yɛ.»

sentences.english: A word was given to me secretly, and the low sound of it came to my ears.
sentences.susu: «Masenyi nde bara fala n bɛ a gundo ki ma, n tuli bara a makɔlikɔli xui mɛ.

sentences.english: In troubled thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep comes on men,

sentences.english: Something was present before me, but I was not able to see it clearly; there was a form before my eyes: a quiet voice came to my ears, saying:

sentences.english: May a man be upright before God? or a man be clean before his Maker?

sentences.english: Truly, he puts no faith in his servants, and he sees error in his angels;

sentences.english: How much more those living in houses of earth, whose bases are in the dust! They are crushed more quickly than an insect;
sentences.susu: ibunadama go, naxan yailanxi bɛndɛ ra, naxan nɔma iwurude alɔ kaari?

sentences.english: Between morning and evening they are completely broken; they come to an end for ever, and no one takes note.
sentences.susu: Adamadie faxama lɔxɔ yo lɔxɔ, sese mu na kanama.

sentences.english: If their tent-cord is pulled up, do they not come to an end, and without wisdom?
sentences.susu: E xa simaya luuti bolonma nɛ, e faxa fahaamutareɲa kui.›»

sentences.english: Give now a cry for help; is there anyone who will give you an answer? and to which of the holy ones will you make your prayer?
sentences.susu: «Yakɔsi, i xa xili ti i xui itexi ra. Nde i yaabima? I sɛniyɛntɔɛ mundun xilima?

sentences.english: For wrath is the cause of death to the foolish, and he who has no wisdom comes to his end through passion.
sentences.susu: Gbɛsɛnxɔnnɛya xaxilitare faxama nɛ, tɔɔnɛ lɔnnitare halakima nɛ.

sentences.english: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly the curse came on his house.

sentences.english: Now his children have no safe place, and they are crushed before the judges, for no one takes up their cause.

sentences.english: Their produce is taken by him who has no food, and their grain goes to the poor, and he who is in need of water gets it from their spring.
sentences.susu: Kaamɛtɔɛe xa a xa xɛ don, e xa baloe birin ba a yi ra hali naxan na tunbe xɔɔra. Mixie xa mila a xa naafuli ma, e xa a ba a yi.›

sentences.english: For evil does not come out of the dust, or trouble out of the earth;

sentences.english: But trouble is man's fate from birth, as the flames go up from the fire.
sentences.susu: Adamadi tɔɔrɔma nɛ a xa duniɲɛigiri kui. Na mu kanama, alɔ tɛ na radɛxɛ, a fulefule tefe fan to mu kanama.

sentences.english: But as for me, I would make my prayer to God, and I would put my cause before him:

sentences.english: Who does great things outside our knowledge, wonders without number:
sentences.susu: A kaabanakoe rabama, a xa fe xungbee mu kɔntima.

sentences.english: Who gives rain on the earth, and sends water on the fields:
sentences.susu: A tunɛ ragoro bɔxi ma, a ye rasiga xɛ ma.

sentences.english: Lifting up those who are low, and putting the sad in a safe place;
sentences.susu: A tɔɔrɔmixi xa fe itema, a mixi sunnunxi rakisima.

sentences.english: Who makes the designs of the wise go wrong, so that they are unable to give effect to their purposes.
sentences.susu: A mixi kɔɔtaxi xa fe xun nakanama, alako e waxɔnfe naxa sɔɔnɛya.

sentences.english: He takes the wise in their secret designs, and the purposes of the twisted are cut off suddenly.
sentences.susu: A mixi madaxui suxuma gantanyi ra, a yanfante waxɔnfe kanama.

sentences.english: In the daytime it becomes dark for them, and in the sunlight they go feeling about as if it was night.
sentences.susu: E xa yanyi findima e bɛ dimi ra, e luma alɔ dɔnxui naxee mu se toma.

sentences.english: But he keeps safe from their sword those who have no father, and the poor from the power of the strong.

sentences.english: So the poor man has hope, and the mouth of the evil-doer is stopped.
sentences.susu: Xaxili tide luma nɛ tɔɔrɔmixi bɛ. Tinxintare dɛ balanma nɛ.

sentences.english: Truly, that man is happy who has training from the hand of God: so do not let your heart be shut to the teaching of the Ruler of all.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛlɛxinyi na adama bɛ Ala naxan xuruma. Wo naxa tondi Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi xa xurui ra,

sentences.english: For after his punishment he gives comfort, and after wounding, his hands make you well.
sentences.susu: barima a fi naxan sama mixi ma, a na fan dandanma, a fe xɔnɛ naxan naminima, a na rayalanma.

sentences.english: He will keep you safe from six troubles, and in seven no evil will come near you.
sentences.susu: A mu tondima i ratangade tɔɔrɛ ma, a i rakisima tɔɔrɛ birin kui.

sentences.english: When there is need of food he will keep you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
sentences.susu: Kaamɛ na sin bɔxi ma, a i ratangama nɛ faxɛ ma, gere na mini, a i ratangama santidɛgɛma ma.

sentences.english: He will keep you safe from the evil tongue; and you will have no fear of wasting when it comes.
sentences.susu: A i ratangama nɛ wɔyɛn ɲaaxi ma, a i ba gbaloe kui.

sentences.english: You will make sport of destruction and need, and will have no fear of the beasts of the earth.
sentences.susu: I mu gaaxuma kaamɛ ya ra, i mu sɛrɛnma sube xaaɲɛ ya ra,

sentences.english: For you will be in agreement with the stones of the earth, and the beasts of the field will be at peace with you.
sentences.susu: barima saatɛ luma nɛ i nun duniɲa kui isee tagi, gɛmɛe nun subee mu i tɔɔrɔma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: And you will be certain that your tent is at peace, and after looking over your property you will see that nothing is gone.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛsa luma nɛ i xɔnyi, muɲɛ yo mu tima i xa gɔɔrɛ.

sentences.english: You will be certain that your seed will be great, and your offspring like the plants of the earth.
sentences.susu: I xa die wuyama nɛ, i bɔnsɔɛ gboma nɛ alɔ burunyi sɛxɛ.

sentences.english: You will come to your last resting-place in full strength, as the grain is taken up to the crushing-floor in its time.
sentences.susu: I mu gaburi lima, i xa simaya mu kamalixi, alɔ maale fan to mu xabama a xaba tɛmui mu a lixi.

sentences.english: See, we have made search with care, and it is so; it has come to our ears; see that you take note of it for yourself.
sentences.susu: Muxu bara yi nɔndi kolon, i fan xa a ramɛ, i xa a fahaamu.»

sentences.english: And Job made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa a yaabi,

sentences.susu: «Xa n ma tɔɔrɛ sa maniyama nu, xa a sa sama sikeeli ma nu,

sentences.susu: a binyɛ dangima nɛ baa mɛyɛnyi ra. Na nan a toxi yusi yo mu na n ma wɔyɛnyie ma.

sentences.english: For the arrows of the Ruler of all are present with me, and their poison goes deep into my spirit: his army of fears is put in order against me.

sentences.english: Does the ass of the fields give out his voice when he has grass? or does the ox make sounds over his food?
sentences.susu: Ɲooge fanxi dɛnnaxɛ, sofale wama mɛnni? Ninge wa xui mɛɛma a xa donse ya i?

sentences.english: Will a man take food which has no taste without salt? or is there any taste in the soft substance of purslain?
sentences.susu: Bande donma fɔxɛ xanbi? Tɔxɛlɛ ɲintare ɲɔxun?

sentences.english: My soul has no desire for such things, they are as disease in my food.
sentences.susu: N mu nu wama naxan xɔn, na bara findi n baloe ra hali na fa kanaxi.

sentences.english: If only I might have an answer to my prayer, and God would give me my desire!

sentences.susu: Ala xa n xun nakana, a xa n faxa.

sentences.susu: Na kui, n madundui sɔtɔma nɛ, hali n to yi tɔɔrɛ birin kolonxi, n sɛɛwa n to mu gbilen Ala Sɛniyɛntɔɛ xa yaamari fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Have I strength to go on waiting, or have I any end to be looking forward to?

sentences.susu: N sɛnbɛ gbo alɔ fanye? N fate xɔrɔxɔ alɔ wure?

sentences.susu: Ɲɛmɛ tɛmui, ye banbaran yɛ, a radunda,

sentences.susu: kɔnɔ sogofure ra, ye birin xɔri.

sentences.english: The camel-trains go out of their way; they go up into the waste and come to destruction.
sentences.susu: Biyaasilae kira bama a ma ye fenfe ra, e fa lɔɛ gbengberen yire.

sentences.susu: Tema Biyaasilae e xun tima ye yire ra. Seebakae fan e xaxili tima na xure ra,

sentences.english: They were put to shame because of their hope; they came and their hope was gone.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ e na mɛnni li, e xure xɔrixi nan toma. Na kui limaniya bama nɛ e yi ra.

sentences.english: So have you now become to me; you see my sad condition and are in fear.
sentences.susu: Wo luxi na ki nɛ n bɛ. Wo bara gaaxu n ma tɔɔrɛ ya ra.

sentences.english: Did I say, Give me something? or, Make a payment for me out of your wealth?

sentences.english: Or, Get me out of the power of my hater? or, Give money so that I may be free from the power of the cruel ones?
sentences.susu: N wo makula nɛ, wo xa n xun sara n yaxui gbeeli nde ma?

sentences.english: Give me teaching and I will be quiet; and make me see my error.
sentences.susu: Wo n xaran. Wo n ma tantanyi masen n bɛ, alako n xa n sabari.

sentences.english: How pleasing are upright words! but what force is there in your arguments?
sentences.susu: Nɔndi tan mu mixi yo tɔɔrɔma. Kɔnɔ wo xa masenyie tan fala xun?

sentences.english: My words may seem wrong to you, but the words of him who has no hope are for the wind.
sentences.susu: Wo bara kiiti sa, wo mu wo tuli matixi tɔɔrɔmixi tan xa wɔyɛnyi ra.

sentences.english: Truly, you are such as would give up the child of a dead man to his creditors, and would make a profit out of your friend.
sentences.susu: Wo fata kiiti ɲaaxi sade kiridie ma. Wo mu yanfanteya ba wo boore yɛtɛ yati ra.

sentences.english: Now then, let your eyes be turned to me, for truly I will not say what is false to your face.
sentences.susu: Kɔsi fa yandi, wo wo ya ti n na. N mu wule falama wo bɛ.

sentences.english: Let your minds be changed, and do not have an evil opinion of me; yes, be changed, for my righteousness is still in me.
sentences.susu: Wo xa kiiti tinxinxi sa, alako n xili fanyi naxa kana.

sentences.english: Is there evil in my tongue? is not the cause of my trouble clear to me?
sentences.susu: Wo fe falɛ ɲaaxi mɛma n na? N mu fata fe fanyi nun fe ɲaaxi tagi rasade?»

sentences.english: Has not man his ordered time of trouble on the earth? and are not his days like the days of a servant working for payment?
sentences.susu: «Mixi xa fe mu luxi xɛ duniɲa ma alɔ sɔɔri? A xa duniɲɛigiri mu luxi xɛ alɔ walikɛ?

sentences.english: As a servant desiring the shades of evening, and a workman looking for his payment:
sentences.susu: Konyi gbatama kɔɛ xa so, walikɛ gbatama a sare ra.

sentences.english: So I have for my heritage months of pain to no purpose, and nights of weariness are given to me.
sentences.susu: N tan fan, n kɛ bara findi tɔɔrɛ ra, n ma wali sare bara findi xɔnɛ ra.

sentences.english: When I go to my bed, I say, When will it be time to get up? but the night is long, and I am turning from side to side till morning light.
sentences.susu: N nɛ n sama, n lu ra a manɛ, ‹N kelima tɛmui mundun?› Xixɔli mu n tan bɛ, tɔɔrɛ nan tun a ra kɔɛ birin kui.

sentences.english: My flesh is covered with worms and dust; my skin gets hard and then is cracked again.
sentences.susu: Kuli dinfe n fate ra, n kiri na bɔrɔfe, yalee tife a ma.

sentences.english: My days go quicker than the cloth-worker's thread, and come to an end without hope.
sentences.susu: N ma simaya xulun mabɔɛ xa mabɔɛ wuri bɛ.

sentences.english: O, keep in mind that my life is wind: my eye will never again see good.
sentences.susu: Ala, i xa ratu a ma n ma simaya ɲɛngi nan tun a ra, n yae mu fe fanyi toma kɔrɛ.

sentences.english: The eye of him who sees me will see me no longer: your eyes will be looking for me, but I will be gone.
sentences.susu: Ya naxan tixi n na, na mu n toma sɔnɔn, a gbe mu luxi n xa lɔɛ i ma.

sentences.english: A cloud comes to an end and is gone; so he who goes down into the underworld comes not up again.
sentences.susu: Kunda na te, a man lɔɛ. Adamadi fan na siga aligiyama, a mu gbilenma fa ra.

sentences.english: He will not come back to his house, and his place will have no more knowledge of him.
sentences.susu: A mu gbilenma a xɔnyi sɔnɔn, a xa fɔxɔɛ mu ratuma a xa fe ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: So I will not keep my mouth shut; I will let the words come from it in the pain of my spirit, my soul will make a bitter outcry.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi n mu n dɛ suxuma, n nan n ma tɔɔrɛ ifalama nɛ, n nan n mawa n ma xɔrɔrɔɛ kui.

sentences.english: Am I a sea, or a sea-beast, that you put a watch over me?
sentences.susu: N findixi i bɛ baa nan na, xa na mu a ra, daalise xun solofere kanyi, i to fa biraxi n ma fe fɔxɔ ra yi mɔɔli ra?

sentences.english: When I say, In my bed I will have comfort, there I will get rest from my disease;
sentences.susu: N na a fala, ‹N xa n sa, n xa xi, alako n xa n ma tɔɔrɛ mayanfa,›

sentences.english: Then you send dreams to me, and visions of fear;
sentences.susu: i n magaaxu xiye nun laamatunyi ɲaaxie ra.

sentences.english: So that a hard death seems better to my soul than my pains.

sentences.english: I have no desire for life, I would not be living for ever! Keep away from me, for my days are as a breath.

sentences.english: What is man, that you have made him great, and that your attention is fixed on him,

sentences.english: And that your hand is on him every morning, and that you are testing him every minute?
sentences.susu: i nu a mato tɛmui birin?

sentences.susu: I i yae bama n na tɛmui mundun? I n luma n yɛtɛ ra mun lɔxɔɛ?

sentences.english: If I have done wrong, what have I done to you, O keeper of men? why have you made me a mark for your blows, so that I am a weariness to myself?
sentences.susu: Xa n bara yunubi raba i ra, na fala n bɛ, i tan naxan adamadi matoma. N tan yegetixi i yi ra munfe ra matoe ra?

sentences.english: And why do you not take away my sin, and let my wrongdoing be ended? for now I go down to the dust, and you will be searching for me with care, but I will be gone.
sentences.susu: Munfe ra i mu diɲɛ n ma fe kobi ma? Munfe ra i mu n ma yunubi xafari? A gbe mu luxi n xa findi bɛndɛ ra. Na tɛmui i mu n toma sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: Then Bildad the Shuhite made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Bilidada Suuxaka naxa a masen,

sentences.english: How long will you say these things, and how long will the words of your mouth be like a strong wind?
sentences.susu: «I yi wɔyɛnyi mɔɔli falama han tɛmui mundun? I xa wɔyɛnyi luxi nɛ alɔ foye.

sentences.english: Does God give wrong decisions? or is the Ruler of all not upright in his judging?
sentences.susu: Ala nɔma nɔndi mafindide wule ra? Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi nɔma tinxinyi ifude?

sentences.english: If your children have done evil against him, then their punishment is from his hand.
sentences.susu: Xa i xa die yunubi nan nabaxi a ra, a e ɲaxankataxi na nan ma.

sentences.english: If you will make search for God with care, and put your request before the Ruler of all;
sentences.susu: Xa i tan Ala fenma, xa i Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi makulama,

sentences.english: If you are clean and upright; then he will certainly be moved to take up your cause, and will make clear your righteousness by building up your house again.
sentences.susu: xa yunubi mu na i ma, xa i tinxin, Ala a ɲɛngi sama nɛ i xɔn ma, a i rasabati i xa tinxinyi kui.

sentences.english: And though your start was small, your end will be very great.
sentences.susu: I harige dɔnxɔɛ fama dangide na singe ra.»

sentences.english: Put the question now to the past generations, and give attention to what has been searched out by their fathers:

sentences.english: (For we are but of yesterday, and have no knowledge, because our days on earth are gone like a shade:)

sentences.english: Will they not give you teaching, and say words of wisdom to you?
sentences.susu: E mu fahaamui fima xɛ i ma? E e xaxili xa masenyie tima i bɛ yi ki:

sentences.english: Will the river-plant come up in its pride without wet earth? will the grass get tall without water?
sentences.susu: Wofiri bulama xare ma? Xure i baare findima a ra ye mu dɛnnaxɛ?

sentences.english: When it is still green, without being cut down, it becomes dry and dead before any other plant.
sentences.susu: Hali a na a bili ma, a mu xabaxi, a lisima mafuren dangi ɲooge birin na.

sentences.english: So is the end of all who do not keep God in mind; and the hope of the evil-doer comes to nothing:

sentences.english: Whose support is cut off, and whose hope is no stronger than a spider's thread.

sentences.english: He is looking to his family for support, but it is not there; he puts his hope in it, but it comes to nothing.

sentences.english: He is full of strength before the sun, and his branches go out over his garden.

sentences.english: Truly, God will not give up him who is without sin, and will not take evil-doers by the hand.

sentences.english: The time will come when your mouth will be full of laughing, and cries of joy will come from your lips.

sentences.english: Your haters will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the sinner will not be seen again.
sentences.susu: I xɔnmixie fama lude yaagi kui, e xɔnyie fa bira.»

sentences.english: And Job made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa a yaabi,

sentences.english: Truly, I see that it is so: and how is it possible for a man to get his right before God?
sentences.susu: «N na birin kolonxi nɔndi ra. Ala nɔma nɔndi fide adama ma di?

sentences.english: If a man was desiring to go to law with him, he would not be able to give him an answer to one out of a thousand questions.

sentences.english: It is he who takes away the mountains without their knowledge, overturning them in his wrath:

sentences.english: Who is moving the earth out of its place, so that its pillars are shaking:

sentences.english: Who made the Bear and Orion, and the Pleiades, and the store-houses of the south:
sentences.susu: A tan nan tunbui birin sa, kankan na a yire.

sentences.english: Who does great things not to be searched out; yes, wonders without number.

sentences.english: See, he goes past me and I see him not: he goes on before, but I have no knowledge of him.

sentences.english: If he puts out his hand to take, by whom may it be turned back? who may say to him, What are you doing?

sentences.english: If I had sent for him to be present, and he had come, I would have no faith that he would give ear to my voice.
