sentences.english: He would not let me take my breath, but I would be full of bitter grief.
sentences.susu: A mu n luma n xa malabu, a bara n ma xɔnɛ xun masa a ɲaaxi ra

sentences.english: If it is a question of strength, he says, Here I am! and if it is a question of a cause at law, he says, Who will give me a fixed day?
sentences.susu: N mu nɔma a ra, barima a sɛnbɛ gbo n bɛ. Muxu nun Ala mu nɔma makiitide, barima kiitisa mu na muxu tagi.

sentences.english: Though I was in the right, he would say that I was in the wrong; I have done no evil; but he says that I am a sinner.
sentences.susu: Hali n sa tinxin nu, n dɛ mu nɔndi fima n ma. Hali yunubi mu na n ma nu, n dɛ kiiti rakanama nɛ n na.

sentences.english: I have done no wrong; I give no thought to what becomes of me; I have no desire for life.
sentences.susu: Yunubi na n ma? N mu a kolon N nimisaxi n ma duniɲɛigiri nan tun na.

sentences.english: It is all the same to me; so I say, He puts an end to the sinner and to him who has done no wrong together.
sentences.susu: N tan bɛ, a birin keren, barima Ala tinxintɔɛ nun tinxintare birin ɲaxankatama.

sentences.english: If death comes suddenly through disease, he makes sport of the fate of those who have done no wrong.
sentences.susu: Gbaloe na tinxintɔɛ li, Ala mu na tɔɔrɛ toma.

sentences.english: The land is given into the power of the evil-doer; the faces of its judges are covered; if not by him, then who has done it?
sentences.susu: Tinxintare na bɔxi nde sɔtɔ tinxintareya kui, Ala a niyama kiitisae xa tin na ra. Xa Ala mu a ra, nde a ra fa?

sentences.english: My days go quicker than a post-runner: they go in flight, they see no good.
sentences.susu: N ma simaya xulun gila bɛ, A ɲɔnma beenun n xa hɛɛri sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: They go rushing on like reed-boats, like an eagle dropping suddenly on its food.
sentences.susu: N ma simaya dangima alɔ kunkui, alɔ sɛgɛ naxan goroma tɔxɛyɔrɛ ma.

sentences.english: If I say, I will put my grief out of mind, I will let my face be sad no longer and I will be bright;
sentences.susu: N na a fala, ‹N xa nɛɛmu n ma mawa ma, n xa ba sunnunxi, n xa n sɛnbɛ so,›

sentences.english: I go in fear of all my pains; I am certain that I will not be free from sin in your eyes.
sentences.susu: n ma tɔɔrɛ nan birin luma n magaaxu ra. N a kolon i mu nɔndi fima n ma.

sentences.english: You will not let me be clear of sin! why then do I take trouble for nothing?
sentences.susu: N to bara yunubi sɔtɔ, n nɔndi fenma n yɛtɛ bɛ munfe ra?

sentences.english: If I am washed with snow water, and make my hands clean with soap;
sentences.susu: Hali n sa n maxa nɛ ye tinsexi ra, hali n sa n bɛlɛxɛe maxa xɔsi ba se ra,

sentences.english: Then you will have me pushed into the dust, so that I will seem disgusting to my very clothing.
sentences.susu: i n nagoroma nɛ boora, n xa raɲaaxu n ma dugie ma.

sentences.english: For he is not a man as I am, that I might give him an answer, that we might come together before a judge.
sentences.susu: Ala mu luxi alɔ adamadi, n nɔma naxan xilide kiiti ma, alako n xa n gbe fala, kiitisa xa kiiti sa muxu tagi.

sentences.english: There is no one to give a decision between us, who might have control over us.
sentences.susu: Kiitisa yo mu na naxan nɔma kiiti sade n nun Ala tagi.

sentences.english: Let him take away his rod from me and not send his fear on me:
sentences.susu: Ala xa a xa wuri bɔnbɔ ti se ba n xun ma, a xa a xa fe magaaxuxi ba n yi ra,

sentences.english: Then I would say what is in my mind without fear of him; for there is no cause of fear in myself.
sentences.susu: alako n xa nɔ wɔyɛnde a ra gaaxutareɲa kui. Kɔnɔ n ma fe to mu na ki xɛ, n xa lu n keren.»

sentences.english: My soul is tired of life; I will let my sad thoughts go free in words; my soul will make a bitter outcry.
sentences.susu: «N ma duniɲɛigiri bara raɲaaxu n nii ma. Na kui n xa n gbe fala. Xɔnɛ naxan na n furi kui, n xa na makɛnɛn.

sentences.english: I will say to God, Do not put me down as a sinner; make clear to me what you have against me.
sentences.susu: N bara a fala Ala bɛ, I naxa n suxu. I xa n nakolon i n suxuxi fe naxan ma.

sentences.english: What profit is it to you to be cruel, to give up the work of your hands, looking kindly on the design of evil-doers?
sentences.susu: N tɔɔrɔfe rafan i ma, n tan naxan findixi i xa daalise ra? Tinxintare waxɔnfe rafan i ma?

sentences.english: Have you eyes of flesh, or do you see as man sees?
sentences.susu: I fe to ki mu makuya adamadi fe to ki ra?

sentences.english: Are your days as the days of man, or your years like his,
sentences.susu: I xa simaya maniya adamadi gbe ra?

sentences.english: That you take note of my sin, searching after my wrongdoing,
sentences.susu: I n tɔɔrɔfe munfe ra? I na n ma yunubie fenfe munfe ra?

sentences.english: Though you see that I am not an evil-doer; and there is no one who is able to take a man out of your hands?
sentences.susu: I ɲan n ma tinxinyi kolon, i ɲan a kolon mixi yo mu n natangama i bɛlɛxɛ i.

sentences.english: Your hands made me, and I was formed by you, but then, changing your purpose, you gave me up to destruction.
sentences.susu: I tan nan n daaxi, i tan nan n sɔntɔma.

sentences.english: O keep in mind that you made me out of earth; and will you send me back again to dust?
sentences.susu: I xa ratu a ma a i n daaxi bɛndɛ nan na. I man wama n nagbilenfe mɛnni nɛ?

sentences.english: Was I not drained out like milk, becoming hard like cheese?
sentences.susu: I bara n yailan alɔ mixi naxan xiɲɛ yailanma donse fanyi ra.

sentences.english: By you I was clothed with skin and flesh, and joined together with bones and muscles.
sentences.susu: I bara n fate birin yailan, kiri, sube, xɔri, nun fasɛ.

sentences.english: You have been kind to me, and your grace has been with me, and your care has kept my spirit safe.
sentences.susu: I bara n ma simaya xɔn kuya, i bara hinnɛ n na, i bara i ɲɛngi sa n nii xɔn ma.»

sentences.english: But you kept these things in the secret of your heart; I am certain this was in your thoughts:
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ yakɔsi n bara a kolon naxan nu na i xaxili ma n ma fe ra.

sentences.english: That, if I did wrong, you would take note of it, and would not make me clear from sin:
sentences.susu: I bara wa n ma yunubi tofe, alako i xa tondi diɲɛde n ma.

sentences.english: That, if I was an evil-doer, the curse would come on me; and if I was upright, my head would not be lifted up, being full of shame and overcome with trouble.
sentences.susu: Xa yunubi na n ma, ɲaxankatɛ na n bɛ. Xa yunubi mu na n ma, n na yaagi kui, n mu nɔma n xunyi yati rakelide.

sentences.english: And that if there was cause for pride, you would go after me like a lion; and again put out your wonders against me:
sentences.susu: Xa n sa n xunyi rakeli, i n bɔnbɔma i sɛnbɛ magaaxuxi ra, alɔ yɛtɛ sɛnbɛma a rabama ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: That you would send new witnesses against me, increasing your wrath against me, and letting loose new armies on me.
sentences.susu: I xa xɔnɛ na xun masafe n ma fe ra, i xa ɲaxankatɛ bara gbo yɛ.

sentences.english: Why then did you make me come out of my mother's body? It would have been better for me to have taken my last breath, and for no eye to have seen me,
sentences.susu: I n naminixi n nga tɛɛgɛ i munfe ra? Xa n sa faxa naa nɛ nu, mixi yo mu nu n toma,

sentences.english: And for me to have been as if I had not been; to have been taken from my mother's body straight to my last resting-place.
sentences.susu: n mu baloma nu, n nu tongoma nɛ n nga tɛɛgɛ, n nagoro gaburi kui keren na.

sentences.english: Are not the days of my life small in number? Let your eyes be turned away from me, so that I may have a little pleasure,
sentences.susu: Naxan luxi n ma simaya ra, a mu gbo sɔnɔn. Yandi, i xa gbilen n fɔxɔ ra fa, sɛɛwɛ dondoronti xa lu n bɛ

sentences.english: Before I go to the place from which I will not come back, to the land where all is dark and black,
sentences.susu: beenu n xa siga aligiyama, dimi na dɛnnaxɛ. N mu gbilenma duniɲa ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: A land of thick dark, without order, where the very light is dark.
sentences.susu: Dimi xungbe na aligiyama. Adama xaxili ifuma naa. Mɛnni naiyalanyi yati nan findima dimi ra.»

sentences.english: Then Zophar the Naamathite made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Sofara Naamaka naxa a fala,

sentences.english: Are all these words to go unanswered? and is a man seen to be right because he is full of talk?
sentences.susu: «A mu lan mixi xa i xa yi masenyi gbegbe yaabi? Masenyi ratofanxi mu nɔndi fima masenyi ma.

sentences.english: Are your words of pride to make men keep quiet? and are you to make sport, with no one to put you to shame?
sentences.susu: I ɲɔxɔ a ma a mixi dunduma i xa wɔyɛnyie ma, i xa yo Ala ma, mixi yo mu i rayaagi?

sentences.english: You may say, My way is clean, and I am free from sin in your eyes.
sentences.susu: I naxɛ, ‹Sese mu luxi n ma lɔnni ra, n bara sɛniyɛn Ala ya i.›

sentences.english: But if only God would take up the word, opening his lips in argument with you;
sentences.susu: Xa Ala sa wɔyɛn i bɛ nu,

sentences.english: And would make clear to you the secrets of wisdom, and the wonders of his purpose!
sentences.susu: a a xa lɔnni gundo masenma nɛ i bɛ, naxan dangima adamadi xa fe to ki ra.

sentences.english: Are you able to take God's measure, to make discovery of the limits of the Ruler of all?
sentences.susu: I nɔma Ala xa tilinyi kolonde? I nɔma Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi xaxili birin fahaamude?

sentences.english: They are higher than heaven; what is there for you to do? deeper than the underworld, and outside your knowledge;
sentences.susu: Na lɔnni ite koore xa maite bɛ, a tilin aligiyama bɛ. I nɔma sode na kui?

sentences.english: Longer in measure than the earth, and wider than the sea.
sentences.susu: A kuya bɔxi bɛ, a xa gboe dangi baa ra.

sentences.english: If he goes on his way, shutting a man up and putting him to death, who may make him go back from his purpose?
sentences.susu: Xa Ala sa mixi suxu, a fa a makiiti, nɔndi luma na kanyi bɛ?

sentences.english: For in his eyes men are as nothing; he sees evil and takes note of it.
sentences.susu: Ala mixi ɲaaxie kolonma, a tinxintaree toma.

sentences.english: And so a hollow-minded man will get wisdom, when a young ass of the field gets teaching.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare mu nɔma findide lɔnnila ra, alɔ sofale fan to mu nɔma findide adamadi ra.

sentences.english: But if you put your heart right, stretching out your hands to him;
sentences.susu: Xa i tan i yɛtɛ ragbilen Ala ma, xa i i bɛlɛxɛ itala a bɛ,

sentences.english: If you put far away the evil of your hands, and let no wrongdoing have a place in your tent;
sentences.susu: xa i gbilen tinxintareya fɔxɔ ra, xa i a matanga i xa denbaya kui,

sentences.english: Then truly your face will be lifted up, with no mark of sin, and you will be fixed in your place without fear:
sentences.susu: na kui i xunnakeli sɔtɔma nɛ, i sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ, i limaniya a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: For your sorrow will go from your memory, like waters flowing away:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui i nɛɛmuma nɛ i xa tɔɔrɛ ma, alɔ xure naxan bara dangi a rakuya.

sentences.english: And your life will be brighter than day; though it is dark, it will become like the morning.
sentences.susu: I xa duniɲɛigiri yanbama nɛ alɔ soge, i xa dimi bama nɛ, a lu alɔ kuye na iba.

sentences.english: And you will be safe because there is hope; after looking round, you will take your rest in quiet;
sentences.susu: I bɔɲɛ a raxarama nɛ, xaxili tide lu i bɛ, fe ɲaaxi a makuyama nɛ i ra, i xi xɔli fanyi raba.

sentences.english: Sleeping with no fear of danger; and men will be desiring to have grace in your eyes;
sentences.susu: I na i sa, mixi yo mu i xa xi xɔli kanama i ma. Mixie fama nɛ i xa hinnɛ e ra.

sentences.english: But the eyes of the evil-doers will be wasting away; their way of flight is gone, and their only hope is the taking of their last breath.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ tinxintaree xa fe xun nakanama nɛ, e mu kisima, faxɛ nan e mamɛxi.»

sentences.english: And Job made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa a yaabi,

sentences.english: No doubt you have knowledge, and wisdom will come to an end with you.
sentences.susu: «Duniɲa xui nan na wo kɔn na. A luxi nɛ yi ki alɔ lɔnni birin na wo tan gbansan yi ra.

sentences.english: But I have a mind as well as you; I am equal to you: yes, who has not knowledge of such things as these?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan fan, xaxili na n bɛ alɔ wo tan. Wo mu fisa n bɛ de. Wo naxan falaxi, nde mu nɔma na kolonde?

sentences.english: It seems that I am to be as one who is a cause of laughing to his neighbour, one who makes his prayer to God and is answered! the upright man who has done no wrong is to be made sport of!
sentences.susu: N na Ala maxandi, alako n xa yaabi nde sɔtɔ a ra, tinxintɔɛ findi a booree bɛ mayele se ra.

sentences.english: In the thought of him who is in comfort there is no respect for one who is in trouble; such is the fate of those whose feet are slipping.
sentences.susu: Mixie naxee mu na tɔɔrɛ kui, e yoma tɔɔrɔmixi xa tɔɔrɛ ma. E a falama e nun na tɔɔrɛ nan lan.

sentences.english: There is wealth in the tents of those who make destruction, and those by whom God is moved to wrath are safe; even those whose god is their strength.
sentences.susu: Kɔntɔfili yo mu na muɲɛtie xɔnyi. Kuye batuie Ala xili maberema, kɔnɔ e bɔɲɛ saxi.

sentences.english: But put now a question to the beasts, and get teaching from them; or to the birds of the heaven, and they will make it clear to you;
sentences.susu: Maxɔrinyi ti subee ma wula i, e xa i ralɔnni. Xɔnie fan xa na masen i bɛ.

sentences.english: Or to the things which go flat on the earth, and they will give you wisdom; and the fishes of the sea will give you news of it.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi mato, na fan xa findi lɔnni ra i bɛ. Yɛxɛe maxɔrin baa ma, nee fan xa na masen i bɛ.

sentences.english: Who does not see by all these that the hand of the Lord has done this?
sentences.susu: E birin a kolon Alatala fɔxi nan na ki.

sentences.english: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all flesh of man.
sentences.susu: Daalise birin nii na a xɔnyɛ i, adamadi birin ɲɛngi fatanxi a tan nan na.

sentences.english: Are not words tested by the ear, even as food is tasted by the mouth?
sentences.susu: Adama xa a ɲɔxɔ sa yi masenyie xɔn ma, alɔ a dɛ a ɲɔxɔ sama donse xɔn ma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Old men have wisdom, and a long life gives knowledge.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni na forie yi ra, simaya xɔnkuye nan xaxili fima mixi ma.

sentences.english: With him there is wisdom and strength; power and knowledge are his.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni nun sɛnbɛ na Ala nan yi ra, marasi nun xaxili fanyi na a tan nan bɛ.

sentences.english: Truly, there is no building up of what is pulled down by him; when a man is shut up by him, no one may let him loose.
sentences.susu: Xa Ala se kana, a mu nɔma rafalade sɔnɔn. Xa a tan nan mixi balanxi, na kanyi mu minima.

sentences.english: Truly, he keeps back the waters and they are dry; he sends them out and the earth is overturned.
sentences.susu: Xa Ala kankan tunɛ ma, se birin xarama nɛ. Xa a a bɛɲin, a banbaran yɛ bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: With him are strength and wise designs; he who is guided into error, together with his guide, are in his hands;
sentences.susu: Sɛnbɛ nun nɔndi na a tan nan yi ra. Mixi naxan madaxuxi nun mixi madaxui, e birin a gbe.

sentences.english: He takes away the wisdom of the wise guides, and makes judges foolish;
sentences.susu: A nɔma marasimae suxude, a nɔma kiitisae xaxili ifude.

sentences.english: He undoes the chains of kings, and puts his band on them;
sentences.susu: Mangɛ yɔlɔnxɔnyi naxan saxi mixie ma, Ala na bama nɛ e ma, a a sa mangɛ tan ma.

sentences.english: He makes priests prisoners, overturning those in safe positions;
sentences.susu: Ala sɛrɛxɛdubɛe xaninma konyiya kui, a mangasanyi rabira.

sentences.english: He makes the words of responsible persons without effect, and takes away the good sense of the old;
sentences.susu: A masenyi bama marasimae yi, a forie xa lɔnni mafindima.

sentences.english: He puts shame on chiefs, and takes away the power of the strong;
sentences.susu: A kuntigie rayaagima, a sɛnbɛmae igoroma.

sentences.english: Uncovering deep things out of the dark, and making the deep shade bright;
sentences.susu: A gundoe makɛnɛnma, a dimi findi naiyalanyi ra.

sentences.english: Increasing nations, and sending destruction on them; making wide the lands of peoples, and then giving them up.
sentences.susu: A ɲamanɛe xun nakelima, a man e xun nakana. A e rasiga, a man e rafa.

sentences.english: He takes away the wisdom of the rulers of the earth, and sends them wandering in a waste where there is no way.
sentences.susu: A xaxili bama ɲamanɛe mangɛe yi ra, a e ralɔɛ gbengberenyi ma.

sentences.english: They go feeling about in the dark without light, wandering without help like those overcome with wine.
sentences.susu: E luma alɔ dɔnxuie naxee mu naiyalanyi toma, e luma alɔ siisilae kira ifuma naxee ma.»

sentences.english: Truly, my eye has seen all this, word of it has come to my ear, and I have knowledge of it.
sentences.susu: «Iyo, n ya bara na birin to, n tuli bara na mɛ.

sentences.english: The same things are in my mind as in yours; I am equal to you.
sentences.susu: Wo naxan kolon, n tan fan na kolon. Wo mu fisa n bɛ.

sentences.english: But I would have talk with the Ruler of all, and my desire is to have an argument with God.
sentences.susu: N tan wama nɛ gbansan, n xa wɔyɛn Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi ra, n wama n yɛtɛ nan xun mafalafe a bɛ.

sentences.english: But you put a false face on things; all your attempts to put things right are of no value.
sentences.susu: Wo tan bara n tɔɔɲɛgɛ. Wo mu faxi seri yo ra n bɛ.

sentences.english: If only you would keep quiet, it would be a sign of wisdom!
sentences.susu: Xa wo wo sabarixi nɛ nu, na nan fisa. Na nu nɔma findide nɛ lɔnni ra.

sentences.english: Give ear to the argument of my mouth, and take note of the words of my lips.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo tuli mati n ma masenyi ra, wo xa n xunmafala wɔyɛnyie ramɛ.

sentences.english: Will you say in God's name what is not right, and put false words into his mouth?
sentences.susu: Wo tan wama wɔyɛn tinxintaree nan falafe Ala xili ra? Wo wama wule nan falafe wo Marigi xili ra?

sentences.english: Will you have respect for God's person in this cause, and put yourselves forward as his supporters?
sentences.susu: Wo wama Ala malife nɛ? Wo wama Ala nan xun mafalafe?

sentences.english: Will it be good for you to be searched out by him, or have you the thought that he may be guided into error like a man?
sentences.susu: Wo munse rabama xa a sa wo sondonyie mato? Wo nɔma Ala madaxude alɔ wo mixi madaxuma ki naxɛ?

sentences.english: He will certainly put you right, if you have respect for persons in secret.
sentences.susu: N a kolon, a wo rakɔrɔsima nɛ xa wo tantanma wo xa gundoe kui.

sentences.english: Will not his glory put you in fear, so that your hearts will be overcome before him?
sentences.susu: Wo mu gaaxuma a sɛnbɛ ya ra? Wo mu gaaxuma a xa xɔnɛ ya ra?

sentences.english: Your wise sayings are only dust, and your strong places are only earth.
sentences.susu: Wo xa masenyie luma alɔ tɛ xube, wo makanta see sɛnbɛ mu na.

sentences.english: Keep quiet, and let me say what is in my mind, whatever may come to me.
sentences.susu: Wo wo sabari, wo a lu n xa wɔyɛn. Fe naxan n lima, na n lima nɛ.

sentences.english: I will take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand.
sentences.susu: N suusaxi n yɛtɛ raminide kɛnɛ ma munfe ra, hali na to nɔma findide nɛ faxɛ ra n bɛ?

sentences.english: Truly, he will put an end to me; I have no hope; but I will not give way in argument before him;
sentences.susu: Hali Ala n faxa, n nan n xaxili tima a tan nan na. N nan n yɛtɛ xun mafalama a tan nan ya i.

sentences.english: And that will be my salvation, for an evil-doer would not come before him,
sentences.susu: Na yati nɔma findide kisi ra n bɛ, barima tinxintare mu suusama tide a ya i.

sentences.english: Give ear with care to my words, and keep what I say in your minds.
sentences.susu: Wo n ma masenyie ramɛ, wo wo tuli mati e ra.»

sentences.english: See now, I have put my cause in order, and I am certain that I will be seen to be right.
sentences.susu: «Wo a lu n xa n gbe fala, n a kolon nɔndi luma nɛ n bɛ.

sentences.english: Is any one able to take up the argument against me? If so, I would keep quiet and give up my breath.
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma n ma yunubi masende n bɛ? Xa na raba, n dunduma nɛ, n tin faxafe ra.»

sentences.english: Only two things do not do to me, then I will come before your face:
sentences.susu: «Ala, fe firin gbansan naba n bɛ, alako n naxa nɔxun i ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: Take your hand far away from me; and let me not be overcome by fear of you.
sentences.susu: I xɔnyɛ ba n ma, i man xa ba n magaaxufe.

sentences.english: Then at the sound of your voice I will give answer; or let me put forward my cause for you to give me an answer.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui n xili fa, n i yaabima nɛ, xa na mu a ra n nɔma nɛ wɔyɛnde, i n yaabi.

sentences.english: What is the number of my evil-doings and my sins? give me knowledge of them.
sentences.susu: N ma yunubi nun n ma fe ɲaaxi xasabi lanxi munse ma? N ma yunubi nun n ma fe ɲaaxi masen n bɛ.

sentences.english: Why is your face veiled from me, as if I was numbered among your haters?
sentences.susu: I mɛɛxi n na munfe ra? I n findixi i yaxui ra munfe ra?

sentences.english: Will you be hard on a leaf in flight before the wind? will you make a dry stem go more quickly on its way?
sentences.susu: I wama sɛnbɛ xuri kanyi nan nasɛrɛnfe? I wama birafe mixi xurudi nan fɔxɔ ra?

sentences.susu: Gantanyi bara a sanyi suxu, a mu a bama naxan yi sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: The twisted cord is put secretly in the earth to take him, and the cord is placed in his way.
sentences.susu: Gantanyi luuti nu nɔxunxi bɛndɛ bun ma, gantanyi nu texi sankira xɔn ma.

sentences.english: He is overcome by fears on every side, they go after him at every step.
sentences.susu: Gaaxui bara a suxu a xa fe birin kui.

sentences.english: His strength is made feeble for need of food, and destruction is waiting for his falling footstep.
sentences.susu: Kaamɛ bara a suxu, a bara lu tɔɔrɛ kui.

sentences.english: His skin is wasted by disease, and his body is food for the worst of diseases.
sentences.susu: A fate bara ba a ma, a salonse na bɔrɔfe saya kira xɔn ma.

sentences.english: He is pulled out of his tent where he was safe, and he is taken away to the king of fears.
sentences.susu: A bara keli a xɔnyi a nu laxi dɛnnaxɛ ra, a na sigafe mangɛ magaaxuxi yire.

sentences.english: In his tent will be seen that which is not his, burning stone is dropped on his house.
sentences.susu: I nɔma lude a xa banxi kui, a gbe mu luxi sɔnɔn. Aligiyama bara findi a xɔnyi ra.

sentences.english: Under the earth his roots are dry, and over it his branch is cut off.
sentences.susu: A sankee bara xara, a salonyie bara lisi.

sentences.english: His memory is gone from the earth, and in the open country there is no knowledge of his name.
sentences.susu: Duniɲa mixie bara nɛɛmu a ma, e mu ratuma a xili ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: He is sent away from the light into the dark; he is forced out of the world.
sentences.susu: A bara keli naiyalanyi kui, a so dimi kui duniɲa fari ma.

sentences.english: He has no offspring or family among his people, and in his living-place there is no one of his name.
sentences.susu: Di mu a bɛ, i fa a i nɛ mamadi. A nu sabatixi dɛnnaxɛ, bɔnsɔɛ yo mu a bɛ mɛnni sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: At his fate those of the west are shocked, and those of the east are overcome with fear.
sentences.susu: Bɔnsɔɛ naxee sa fama, keli sogetede nun sogegorode, nee fama nɛ kaabade a xa xunnakanɛ ma, gaaxui fa e suxu.

sentences.english: Truly, these are the houses of the sinner, and this is the place of him who has no knowledge of God.
sentences.susu: Tinxintare xa maraɲɔnyi luma na ki nɛ, Ala kolontare xa fe rabama na ki nɛ.»

sentences.english: And Job made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa a yaabi,

sentences.english: How long will you make my life bitter, crushing me with words?
sentences.susu: «Wo fama n tɔɔrɔde han tɛmui mundun? Wo n bɔɲɛ halakima wo xa masenyi ra han tɛmui mundun?

sentences.english: Ten times now you have made sport of me; it gives you no sense of shame to do me wrong.
sentences.susu: A dɔxɔ fu nan yi ki wo n konbima, n tɔɔrɔfe mu wo yaagima?

sentences.english: And, truly, if I have been in error, the effect of my error is only on myself.
sentences.susu: Xa nɔndi na a ra, n na yunubi kui, awa, na yunubi luma n tan nan ma.

sentences.english: If you make yourselves great against me, using my punishment as an argument against me,
sentences.susu: Xa wo wama a masenfe n bɛ a wo fisa n bɛ, xa wo wama n ma tɔɔrɛ findife n ma yunubi ra,

sentences.english: Be certain that it is God who has done me wrong, and has taken me in his net.
sentences.susu: wo xa a kolon xɔnɛ naxan na n ma, na fatanxi Ala nan na, a tan nan n suxuxi a xa yɛlɛ ra.

sentences.english: Truly, I make an outcry against the violent man, but there is no answer: I give a cry for help, but no one takes up my cause.
sentences.susu: Xa n sa gbelegbele n ma xɔnɛ xa fe ra, n mu yaabi yo sɔtɔma. Xa n sa wa kiiti xa sa, kiiti tinxinxi yo mu sama.

sentences.english: My way is walled up by him so that I may not go by: he has made my roads dark.
sentences.susu: Ala bara kira ibolon n ya ra, n mu nɔma dangide, a bara n ma kira ifɔɔrɔ n ma.

sentences.english: He has put off my glory from me, and taken the crown from my head.
sentences.susu: A bara n xun nakana, a bara binyɛ birin ba n ma.

sentences.english: I am broken down by him on every side, and I am gone; my hope is uprooted like a tree.
sentences.susu: A bara n ma fe birin nabira. A bara n xaxili tide tala alɔ sansi bili talama ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: His wrath is burning against me, and I am to him as one of his haters.
sentences.susu: A bara xɔnɔ n ma a ɲaaxi ra, n bara findi a yaxui ra.

sentences.english: His armies come on together, they make their road high against me, and put up their tents round mine.
sentences.susu: A xa geresoe bara n nabilin, e na n gerefe, n mu nɔma n gide e ma.

sentences.english: He has taken my brothers far away from me; they have seen my fate and have become strange to me.
sentences.susu: A bara n ngaxakerenyie makuya n na, n kolonmae bara yensen yɛ.

sentences.english: My relations and my near friends have given me up, and those living in my house have put me out of their minds.
sentences.susu: N dɔxɔbooree bara n nabɛɲin, n dɛfanbooree bara n nabolo.

sentences.english: I am strange to my women-servants, and seem to them as one from another country.
sentences.susu: N ma xɔɲɛe nun n ma konyie, nee mu n kolon sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: At my cry my servant gives me no answer, and I have to make a prayer to him.
sentences.susu: N na n ma konyi xili, hali n a mayandi, a mu n ma xili ratinma.

sentences.english: My breath is strange to my wife, and I am disgusting to the offspring of my mother's body.
sentences.susu: N dɛ xiri bara raɲaaxu n ma ginɛ ma, n ma fe mu rafan n ngaxakerenyie ma.

sentences.english: Even young children have no respect for me; when I get up their backs are turned on me.
sentences.susu: Dimɛe yati yoma n ma.

sentences.english: All the men of my circle keep away from me; and those dear to me are turned against me.
sentences.susu: N gundo xiri boore bara n xɔn, n xanuntenyie bara n yanfa.

sentences.english: My bones are joined to my skin, and I have got away with my flesh in my teeth.
sentences.susu: N fate birin bara ba n ma, n xɔrie mini kɛnɛ ma. Sese mu luxi sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: Have pity on me, have pity on me, O my friends! for the hand of God is on me.
sentences.susu: N booree, wo kinikini n ma, yandi, wo kinikini n ma, barima Ala nan n bɔnbɔxi.

sentences.english: Why are you cruel to me, like God, for ever saying evil against me?
sentences.susu: Munfe ra wo n tɔɔrɔma alɔ Ala a rabaxi ki naxɛ? Wo mu nu wasa sinden?»

sentences.english: If only my words might be recorded! if they might be put in writing in a book!
sentences.susu: «Xa n ma wɔyɛnyie sɛbɛxi buki kui nu,

sentences.english: And with an iron pen and lead be cut into the rock for ever!
sentences.susu: xa e masolixi gɛmɛ ma wure ra nu, na tɛmui e buma nɛ nu abadan.

sentences.english: But I am certain that he who will take up my cause is living, and that in time to come he will take his place on the dust;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan a kolon n nakisima ɲiɲɛ na a ra. A fama wɔyɛnyi dɔnxɔɛ falade duniɲa ma.

sentences.english: And ... without my flesh I will see God;
sentences.susu: N fate na gɛ bɔrɔde, n tan yati fama nɛ Ala tode.

sentences.english: Whom I will see on my side, and not as one strange to me. My heart is broken with desire.
sentences.susu: N tan nan yati fama a tode n yae ra, a mu mataalima n bɛ. Na kui n bɔɲɛ sɛɛwama nɛ a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: If you say, How cruel we will be to him! because the root of sin is clearly in him:
sentences.susu: Wo tan naxee maxɔrinyi tima, ‹Won a tɔɔrɔfe munfe ra?› Wo fama n ma nɔndi kolonde.

sentences.english: Be in fear of the sword, for the sword is the punishment for such things, so that you may be certain that there is a judge.
sentences.susu: Wo xa gaaxu santidɛgɛma ya ra, barima ɲaxankatɛ wo sɔtɔma nɛ wo xa fe ɲaaxie ma. Na kui wo fama a kolonde a kiitisa nde na.»

sentences.english: Then Zophar the Naamathite made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Sofara Naamaka naxa a fala,

sentences.english: For this cause my thoughts are troubling me and driving me on.
sentences.susu: «I xa masenyi bara n tɔɔrɔ, fo n xa i yaabi.

sentences.english: I have to give ear to arguments which put me to shame, and your answers to me are wind without wisdom.
sentences.susu: N bara marakɔrɔsi nde mɛ naxan bara n xaxili ifu. N i yaabima n ma lɔnni ra na nan ma.

sentences.english: Have you knowledge of this from early times, when man was placed on the earth,
sentences.susu: I mu a kolon kabi adama naxa daa, a lu duniɲa ma,

sentences.english: That the pride of the sinner is short, and the joy of the evil-doer but for a minute?
sentences.susu: mixi ɲaaxie xa xunnakeli mu buma? E xa ɲɛlɛxinyi dunke?

sentences.english: Though he is lifted up to the heavens, and his head goes up to the clouds;
sentences.susu: Hali a xa fe gbo yɛ, hali a xunyi koore li,

sentences.english: Like the waste from his body he comes to an end for ever: those who have seen him say, Where is he?
sentences.susu: a fama sɔntɔde a lu alɔ se naxan tide mu na, a kolonmae nu fa maxɔrinyi ti, ‹A na minden?›

sentences.english: He is gone like a dream, and is not seen again; he goes in flight like a vision of the night.
sentences.susu: A dangima nɛ alɔ xiye.

sentences.english: The eye which saw him sees him no longer; and his place has no more knowledge of him.
sentences.susu: A kolonmae mu a toma sɔnɔn, a lɔɛma nɛ a xa mixie ma.

sentences.english: His children are hoping that the poor will be kind to them, and his hands give back his wealth.
sentences.susu: A xa die setaree kima see ra, e baba naxee muɲa. E baba xa naafuli gbilenma nɛ na mixie ma.

sentences.english: His bones are full of young strength, but it will go down with him into the dust.
sentences.susu: Sɛnbɛ naxan nu na a yi ra a fonike ra, na birin kanama nɛ, a findi bɛndɛ ra.

sentences.english: Though evil-doing is sweet in his mouth, and he keeps it secretly under his tongue;
sentences.susu: Fe ɲaaxi na rafan mixi ma, a fa na ragata a furi kui,

sentences.english: Though he takes care of it, and does not let it go, but keeps it still in his mouth;
sentences.susu: a mu a bɛɲin, a mu gbilen na fɔxɔ ra,

sentences.english: His food becomes bitter in his stomach; the poison of snakes is inside him.
sentences.susu: a xa donse findima pɔsɔnɛ nan na a furi kui.

sentences.english: He takes down wealth as food, and sends it up again; it is forced out of his stomach by God.
sentences.susu: A naafuli naxan donxi, a fama na bɔxunde. Ala yati na bama nɛ a furi kui.

sentences.english: He takes the poison of snakes into his mouth, the tongue of the snake is the cause of his death.
sentences.susu: A bɔximase xa xɔnɛ nan bɛsuma, biida nan a faxama.

sentences.english: Let him not see the rivers of oil, the streams of honey and milk.
sentences.susu: A harige naxan sɔtɔxi, naxan bara gbo yɛ alɔ xure,

sentences.english: He is forced to give back the fruit of his work, and may not take it for food; he has no joy in the profit of his trading.
sentences.susu: a na birin nagbilenma nɛ, a mu nɔma na sese donde. Na mu findima ɲɛlɛxinyi ra a bɛ,

sentences.english: Because he has been cruel to the poor, turning away from them in their trouble; because he has taken a house by force which he did not put up;
sentences.susu: barima a bara se ba tɔɔrɔmixie yi ra. A bara e xa banxie ba e yi ra, a mu naxee tixi.

sentences.english: There is no peace for him in his wealth, and no salvation for him in those things in which he took delight.
sentences.susu: Wasabali nan to nu a ra a xa milɛ kui, a harige keren mu ratangama.

sentences.english: He had never enough for his desire; for this cause his well-being will quickly come to an end.
sentences.susu: A to nu se birin maɲɔxunxi a yɛtɛ nan bɛ, a xa hɛɛri mu buma.

sentences.english: Even when his wealth is great, he is full of care, for the hand of everyone who is in trouble is turned against him.
sentences.susu: A nɛ na a xa fanyi tagi, tɔɔrɔ sin tɛmui nan na ki a ma.

sentences.english: God gives him his desire, and sends the heat of his wrath on him, making it come down on him like rain.
sentences.susu: A dɛge tɛmui, Ala fama a tɔɔrɔde a xa xɔnɛ ra, na tɔɔrɛ fa findi a xa donse ra.

sentences.english: He may go in flight from the iron spear, but the arrow from the bow of brass will go through him;
sentences.susu: Xa geresose lanmadi mu a tɔɔrɔ, geresose xungbe nan nawalima a xili ma.

sentences.english: He is pulling it out, and it comes out of his back; and its shining point comes out of his side; he is overcome by fears.
sentences.susu: Hali a tanbɛ tala e a sɔxɔxi naxan na, fe magaaxuxi gbɛtɛ fama nɛ a lide.

sentences.english: All his wealth is stored up for the dark: a fire not made by man sends destruction on him, and on everything in his tent.
sentences.susu: A xa naafuli birin luma dimi nan kui, tɛ fa na birin gan a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: The heavens make clear his sin, and the earth gives witness against him.
sentences.susu: Ala a xa yunubi makɛnɛn ma, adamadie na sare ragbilen a ma.

sentences.english: The produce of his house is taken away into another country, like things given into the hands of others in the day of wrath.
sentences.susu: A xa naafuli birin sigama nɛ Ala xa xɔnɛ lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: This is the reward of the evil man, and the heritage given to him by God.
sentences.susu: Ala na nan fima mixi ɲaaxi ma kɛ ra. Na bara findi Ala ɲanige ra na mixi mɔɔli bɛ.»

sentences.english: Then Job made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa a yaabi,

sentences.english: Give attention with care to my words; and let this be your comfort.
sentences.susu: «Wo wo tuli mati n ma masenyi ra. Wo xa na raba n bɛ.

sentences.english: Let me say what is in my mind, and after that, go on making sport of me.
sentences.susu: Wo diɲɛ n bɛ, n xa wɔyɛn. N na gɛ, wo fa yo n ma.

sentences.english: As for me, is my outcry against man? is it then to be wondered at if my spirit is troubled?
sentences.susu: N nan n xun mawaxi mixi nan xili ma? Fɔlɔ yi tɛmui ma, n diɲɛma munfe ra fa?

sentences.english: Take note of me and be full of wonder, put your hand on your mouth.
sentences.susu: Wo wo ya ti n na, wo xa n fate igbɛ. Wo mu kaabaxi xɛ n fate ma?

sentences.english: At the very thought of it my flesh is shaking with fear.
sentences.susu: N nan n maɲɔxun a ma, gaaxui nan n suxuma, n fate birin nu sɛrɛn n ma.»

sentences.english: Why is life given to the evil-doers? why do they become old and strong in power?
sentences.susu: «Munfe ra mixi ɲaaxie buma duniɲa ma? Munfe ra e findima xɛmɔxi sɛnbɛmae ra?

sentences.english: Their children are ever with them, and their offspring before their eyes.
sentences.susu: E xa die xun nakelima, e bɔnsɔɛe fan fe fanyi sɔtɔma e ya ɲiɲɛ ra.

sentences.english: Their houses are free from fear, and the rod of God does not come on them.
sentences.susu: E xa denbayae luma bɔɲɛsa kui, gaaxui yo mu e ma, Ala fan mu e tɔɔrɔma.

sentences.english: Their ox is ready at all times to give seed; their cow gives birth, without dropping her young.
sentences.susu: E xa tuurae sɛnbɛ gbo, e tema e xa ninge ginɛe ma, nee die barima, e furi mu birama.

sentences.english: They send out their young ones like a flock, and their children have pleasure in the dance,
sentences.susu: Na mixi ɲaaxie xa die fare boronma,

sentences.english: They make songs to the instruments of music, and are glad at the sound of the pipe.
sentences.susu: e sigi sama maxasee, kɔra, nun xule xui ra.

sentences.english: Their days come to an end without trouble, and suddenly they go down to the underworld.
sentences.susu: E xa simaya kamalima hɛɛri kui, e man fa faxa faxɛ sɔɔnɛyaxi ra.»

sentences.english: Though they said to God, Go away from us, for we have no desire for the knowledge of your ways.
sentences.susu: «A nun, e nu a falama nɛ Ala bɛ e xa simaya kui, ‹I makuya muxu ra, muxu mu wama i xa sɛriyɛ kolonfe.

sentences.english: What is the Ruler of all, that we may give him worship? and what profit is it to us to make prayer to him?
sentences.susu: Muxu Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi rabatuma munfe ra? A maxandife findima geeni mundun na muxu bɛ?›

sentences.english: Truly, is not their well-being in their power? (The purpose of the evil-doers is far from me.)
sentences.susu: N a kolon e harige mu nu fatanxi e yɛtɛ xa ra, n nan n makuyama mixi ɲaaxie xa marasi ra na nan ma.

sentences.english: How frequently is the light of the evil-doers put out, or does trouble come on them? how frequently does his wrath take them with cords?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ halaki mixi ɲaaxie lima tɛmui birin nɛ? Ala gbaloe gbegbe ragirima e ma a xa xɔnɛ kui?

sentences.english: How frequently are they as dry stems before the wind, or as grass taken away by the storm-wind?
sentences.susu: E xa fe kanama a gbe ra, alɔ maale lagi foye naxan na fanafananma?

sentences.english: You say, God keeps punishment stored up for his children. Let him send it on the man himself, so that he may have the punishment of it!
sentences.susu: Ala ɲaxankatɛ ragatama e xa die bɛ? Munfe ra a mu e tan yati ɲaxankatama?

sentences.english: Let his eyes see his trouble, and let him be full of the wrath of the Ruler of all!
sentences.susu: A lanma e tan yati xa e xa tɔɔrɛ to e ya ra, e tan yati xa Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi xa xɔnɛ kolon.

sentences.english: For what interest has he in his house after him, when the number of his months is ended?
sentences.susu: Xa mixi ɲaaxi gɛ faxade, a mu a xa denbaya xa tɔɔrɛ kolonma.

sentences.english: Is anyone able to give teaching to God? for he is the judge of those who are on high.
sentences.susu: Adamadi nɔma lɔnni nde fide Ala ma, mangɛya birin na naxan ma yaamari bun ma?

sentences.english: One comes to his end in complete well-being, full of peace and quiet:
sentences.susu: Mixi nde faxama bɔɲɛsa kui, a sɛnbɛ gbo, kɔntɔfili yo mu lu a ma,

sentences.english: His buckets are full of milk, and there is no loss of strength in his bones.
sentences.susu: a fate fan, a xɔrie xɔrɔxɔ gben.

sentences.english: And another comes to his end with a bitter soul, without ever tasting good.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi gbɛtɛ tan faxama tɔɔrɛ kui, a mu hɛɛri yo nɛmunnɛmun.

sentences.english: Together they go down to the dust, and are covered by the worm.
sentences.susu: Na mixi firinyi birin sama bɛndɛ nɛ, kuli fa e don.

sentences.english: See, I am conscious of your thoughts, and of your violent purposes against me;
sentences.susu: N wo xa maɲɔxunyie kolon a fanyi ra, wo wama nɔndi rakanafe n na naxee xafe ra.

sentences.english: For you say, Where is the house of the ruler, and where is the tent of the evil-doer?
sentences.susu: Wo naxɛ, ‹Kuntigi xa banxi na minden? Mixi ɲaaxi xɔnyi na di?›

sentences.english: Have you not put the question to the travellers, and do you not take note of their experience?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo mu maxɔrinyi tixi biyaasilae ma? Wo mu wo tuli matixi e xa dɛntɛgɛ ra?

sentences.english: How the evil man goes free in the day of trouble, and has salvation in the day of wrath?
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi mu gbaloe sɔtɔma gbaloe lɔxɔɛ, a ratangama nɛ na xɔnɛ ma.

sentences.english: Who will make his way clear to his face? and if he has done a thing, who gives him punishment for it?
sentences.susu: Nde tima a ya i a a makiiti? Nde a xa wali kobi sare ragbilenma a ma?

sentences.english: He is taken to his last resting-place, and keeps watch over it.
sentences.susu: Mixie a xaninma gaburi, e man fa binyɛ sa a ma mɛnni.

sentences.english: The earth of the valley covering his bones is sweet to him, and all men come after him, as there were unnumbered before him.
sentences.susu: Gaburi bɛndɛ mu a tɔɔrɔma, a binyɛ sɔtɔ ɲama gbegbe ra.

sentences.english: Why then do you give me comfort with words in which there is no profit, when you see that there is nothing in your answers but deceit?
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo n madunduma madundui fuyan na di? Madaxui masenyie nan tun na wo xa lɔnni masenyie kui.»

sentences.english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Elifasi Temanka naxa a fala,

sentences.english: Is it possible for a man to be of profit to God? No, for a man's wisdom is only of profit to himself.
sentences.susu: «Adama tide na Ala bɛ? Ade, adama lɔnnixi nɔma a yɛtɛ gbansan nan malide.

sentences.english: Is it of any interest to the Ruler of all that you are upright? or is it of use to him that your ways are without sin?
sentences.susu: I xa tinxinyi findima geeni mundun na Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi bɛ? I lufe nɔndi kui, na Ala malima di?

sentences.english: Is it because you give him honour that he is sending punishment on you and is judging you?
sentences.susu: Ala na i ɲaxankatafe i xa tinxinyi nan xa fe ra? A na kiiti ɲaaxi safe i ma na nan ma?

sentences.english: Is not your evil-doing great? and there is no end to your sins.
sentences.susu: I xa fe ɲaaxi mu gboxi xɛ? I xa yunubie mu wuyaxi xɛ han a dangi a i?

sentences.english: For you have taken your brother's goods when he was not in your debt, and have taken away the clothing of those who have need of it.
sentences.susu: I bara see rasuxu sɛɛkɛ ra i ngaxakerenyie yi ra. I bara e xa sosee yati ba e ma, i e mageli ti.

sentences.english: You do not give water to the tired traveller, and from him who has no food you keep back bread.
sentences.susu: I mu nu mixi kima ye ra, ye xɔli nu naxan ma, i mu nu kaamɛtɔɛ kima donse ra.

sentences.english: For it was the man with power who had the land, and the man with an honoured name who was living in it.
sentences.susu: I nu bɔxi soma sɛnbɛma nan yi ra, naa findi yɛtɛ igboe sabatide ra.

sentences.english: If I was glad because my wealth was great, and because my hand had got together a great store;

sentences.english: If, when I saw the sun shining, and the moon moving on its bright way,
sentences.susu: xa n bara n ya ti soge nun kike xa yanbɛ ra,

sentences.english: A secret feeling of worship came into my heart, and my hand gave kisses from my mouth;
sentences.susu: n fa nee batu n bɔɲɛ kui gundo ra, n nan n bɛlɛxɛ sunbu e xa binyɛ bun ma,

sentences.english: That would have been another sin to be rewarded with punishment by the judges; for I would have been false to God on high.
sentences.susu: Ala xa n ɲaxankata, barima na fe mɔɔli mu fan, n bara findi yanfante ra Ala mabiri.»

sentences.english: If I was glad at the trouble of my hater, and gave cries of joy when evil overtook him;
sentences.susu: «N bara ɲɛlɛxin n xɔnma xa tɔɔrɛ ra, n sɛɛwa a xa ɲaxankatɛ ra,

sentences.english: (For I did not let my mouth give way to sin, in putting a curse on his life;)
sentences.susu: n tan naxan mu nu tinma a dankade n dɛ ra, n xa na yunubi mɔɔli raba?

sentences.english: If the men of my tent did not say, Who has not had full measure of his meat?
sentences.susu: N ma xɔɲɛe birin mu nu a falama xɛ: ‹A n dɛ wasaxi sube ra›?

sentences.english: The traveller did not take his night's rest in the street, and my doors were open to anyone on a journey;
sentences.susu: N nu biyaasilae yigiyama nɛ alako e naxa xi tande.

sentences.english: If I kept my evil doings covered, and my sin in the secret of my breast,
sentences.susu: N bara n ma fe ɲaaxie nɔxun n bɔɲɛ kui alɔ adamadie darixi a ra ki naxɛ? Ade.

sentences.english: For fear of the great body of people, or for fear that families might make sport of me, so that I kept quiet, and did not go out of my door;
sentences.susu: N bara gaaxu ɲama xa wɔyɛnyi ra, xa na mu a ra n xabilɛ xa wɔyɛnyi ra, n fa lu n xɔnyi nɔxunyi kui n mu nɔndi fala? Ade.»

sentences.english: If only God would give ear to me, and the Ruler of all would give me an answer! or if what he has against me had been put in writing!
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi na naxan tinma a tuli matide n na, n ma masenyi dɔnxɔɛ nan na ki. Ala xa n yaabi. A naxan toma n ma, a xa na sɛbɛ,

sentences.english: Truly I would take up the book in my hands; it would be to me as a crown;
sentences.susu: n xa na dɔxɔ n xun ma, n xa a gbaku n kɔn ma.

sentences.english: I would make clear the number of my steps, I would put it before him like a prince! The words of Job are ended.
sentences.susu: N dɛntɛgɛ sama nɛ a bɛ, alɔ mixi dɛntɛgɛ sama mangɛ bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: If my land has made an outcry against me, or the ploughed earth has been in sorrow;
sentences.susu: Xa n ma bɔxi nde bara xɔnɔ n xili ma, xa mixi nde ya ye bara silɔn na,

sentences.english: If I have taken its produce without payment, causing the death of its owners;
sentences.susu: xa n bara donse nde don n mu a rawalima sare fi, xa n bara a kanyi tɔɔrɔ,

sentences.english: Then in place of grain let thorns come up, and in place of barley evil-smelling plants.
sentences.susu: mɛngi naxan na n ma bɔxi ma, na xa findi tunbe ra, n ma fundenyi xa findi ɲooge ɲaaxi ra.» Ayuba xa masenyi dɔnxɔɛ nan na ki.

sentences.english: So these three men gave no more answers to Job, because he seemed to himself to be right.
sentences.susu: Yi xɛmɛ saxanyie naxa ba Ayuba xa wɔyɛnyi yaabife, barima a nu a yɛtɛ findixi nɔndi falɛ nan na.

sentences.english: And Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was angry, burning with wrath against Job, because he seemed to himself more right than God;
sentences.susu: Na kui Elihu, Barakeeli Buusika xa di, naxan fatan Rama xabilɛ ra, a bɔɲɛ naxa te Ayuba xili ma, barima na nu a yɛtɛ findixi nɔndi falɛ nan na Ala ya i.

sentences.english: And he was angry with his three friends, because they had been unable to give him an answer, and had not made Job's sin clear.
sentences.susu: A bɔɲɛ naxa te a boore saxanyie xili ma, barima e mu nu nɔma Ayuba yaabide hali e to a kolonxi nɔndi mu nu a bɛ.

sentences.english: Now Elihu had kept quiet while Job was talking, because they were older than he;
sentences.susu: Na mixi saxanyie to nu mɔxi a bɛ, Elihu mamɛ ti na nan ma wɔyɛnfe ra Ayuba bɛ.

sentences.english: And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, he was very angry.
sentences.susu: Elihu nu bara a to, yaabi yo mu nu na yi mixi saxanyie yi ra fa. Na kui a bɔɲɛ naxa te.

sentences.english: And Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, made answer and said, I am young, and you are very old, so I was in fear, and kept myself from putting my knowledge before you.
sentences.susu: Elihu, Barakeeli Buusika xa di, naxa a fala, «Fonike nan n na, forie nan wo tan na. N gaaxu n ma marakolonyi sade wo ya i na nan ma.

sentences.english: I said to myself, It is right for the old to say what is in their minds, and for those who are far on in years to give out wisdom.
sentences.susu: N naxɛ, ‹Fori nan fata wɔyɛnde, a xa simaya xɔnkuye xa fe ra.›

sentences.english: But truly it is the spirit in man, even the breath of the Ruler of all, which gives them knowledge.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi nan xaxili fima adama ma.

sentences.english: It is not the old who are wise, and those who are full of years have not the knowledge of what is right.
sentences.susu: Simaya xɔnkuye gbansan xa mu xaxilimaya fima mixi ma, forie gbansan xa mu findixi nɔndi kanyie ra.

sentences.english: So I say, Give ear to me, and I will put forward my knowledge.
sentences.susu: Na kui n bara wo maxandi, wo xa wo tuli mati n ma marakolonyi ra.»

sentences.english: I was waiting for your words, I was giving ear to your wise sayings; while you were searching out what to say,
sentences.susu: «N bara wo xa masenyi raɲɔnyi mamɛ, n bara n tuli mati wo xa masenyi birin na, wo naxan falaxi Ayuba xa fe ra.

sentences.english: I was taking note; and truly not one of you was able to make clear Job's error, or to give an answer to his words.
sentences.susu: N bara wo xa masenyie ramɛ, kɔnɔ wo mu nɔxi Ayuba yaabide, wo mu nɔxi nɔndi makɛnɛnde a bɛ.

sentences.english: Take care that you do not say, Wisdom is here; God may overcome him, but not man.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa a fala de, ‹Won tan bara gɛ lɔnni sɔtɔde. Won xa lu Ala xa yi xɛmɛ rafahaamu, adamadi mu nɔma na rabade.›

sentences.english: I will not put forward words like these, or make use of your sayings in answer to him.
sentences.susu: Ayuba mu a xa masenyi tixi n tan xa xili ma. N fan man mu a yaabima wo xa masenyie ra.»

sentences.english: Fear has overcome them, they have no more answers to give; they have come to an end of words.
sentences.susu: «Limaniya bara ba wo yi ra. Yaabi yo mu na sɔnɔn wo naxan tima.

sentences.english: And am I to go on waiting while they have nothing to say? while they keep quiet and give no more answers?
sentences.susu: N bara wo xa masenyi dande to, yaabi yo mu minima wo dɛ kui fa.

sentences.english: I will give my answer; I will put forward my knowledge:
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi n xa n gbe fala, n tan fan xa n ma lɔnni masen kɔrɛ,

sentences.english: For I am full of words, I am unable to keep in my breath any longer:
sentences.susu: barima fe gbegbe na n furi kui. N xaxili na n tutunfe,

sentences.english: My stomach is like wine which is unable to get out; like skins full of new wine, it is almost burst.
sentences.susu: alɔ wɛni nɛɛnɛ naxan xufuxufufe, a wama a sase bulafe.

sentences.english: Let me say what is in my mind, so that I may get comfort; let me give answer with open mouth.
sentences.susu: N xa wɔyɛn alako n bɔɲɛ xa goro. N dɛ xa yaabi ti.

sentences.english: Let me not give respect to any man, or give names of honour to any living.
sentences.susu: N mu mixi yo rafisama a boore bɛ, n mu taamixiya rabama mixi yo bɛ.

sentences.english: For I am not able to give names of honour to any man; and if I did, my Maker would quickly take me away.
sentences.susu: N mu fata taamixiya ra, n na na raba, Ala n naboloma nɛ.»

sentences.english: And now, O Job, give ear to my words, and take note of all I say.
sentences.susu: «Yakɔsi Ayuba, i i tuli mati n ma masenyi ra, i xa n ma wɔyɛnyi ramɛ.

sentences.english: See, now my mouth is open, my tongue gives out words.
sentences.susu: N bara n dɛ rabi, n nɛnyi bara keli.

sentences.english: My heart is overflowing with knowledge, my lips say what is true.
sentences.susu: N ma masenyi kelixi n bɔɲɛ fiixɛ nan kui, nɔndi nan minima n dɛ i.

sentences.english: The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Ruler of all gives me life.
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili bara n daa, Ala Sɛnbɛ kanyi ɲɛngi bara n findi mixi ɲiɲɛ ra.

sentences.english: If you are able, give me an answer; put your cause in order, and come forward.
sentences.susu: Xa i nɔma n yaabide, i xa na raba.

sentences.english: See, I am the same as you are in the eyes of God; I was cut off from the same bit of wet earth.
sentences.susu: Won firin birin lan Ala ya i. N fan yailanxi bɛndɛ nan na.

sentences.english: Fear of me will not overcome you, and my hand will not be hard on you.
sentences.susu: Na kui i naxa gaaxu n ya ra.

sentences.english: But you said in my hearing, and your voice came to my ears:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i bara wɔyɛnyi nde fala, n naxan mɛxi n tuli ra.

sentences.english: I am clean, without sin; I am washed, and there is no evil in me:
sentences.susu: I bara a fala, ‹N sɛniyɛn, n mu yunubi rabaxi,

sentences.english: See, he is looking for something against me; in his eyes I am as one of his haters;
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ Ala man na fe nde tofe n na, n findixi a yaxui ra naxan ma.

sentences.english: He puts chains on my feet; he is watching all my ways.
sentences.susu: A bara n sanyi mabalan yɔlɔnxɔnyi kui, a nu fa n fɔxi birin igbɛ.›

sentences.english: Truly, in saying this you are wrong; for God is greater than man.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n xa a fala i bɛ, nɔndi mu i bɛ na fe kui, barima Ala gbo mixi bɛ.

sentences.english: Why do you put forward your cause against him, saying, He gives no answer to any of my words?
sentences.susu: I wama Ala rakiitife munfe ra? A mu yaabi fima a xa fe rabaxi birin ma.

sentences.english: For God gives his word in one way, even in two, and man is not conscious of it:
sentences.susu: Ala fe masenma won bɛ ki nde ra, kɔnɔ won mu won ɲɔxɔ sama na xɔn ma.

sentences.english: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep comes on men, while they take their rest on their beds;
sentences.susu: A nɔma wɔyɛnde xiye ra kɔɛ ra, mixi xima tɛmui naxɛ e xa sade ma.

sentences.english: Then he makes his secrets clear to men, so that they are full of fear at what they see;
sentences.susu: A nɔma adamadie tuli rabide na tɛmui, a e rakolon fee ra naxee kelixi a tan ma,

sentences.english: In order that man may be turned from his evil works, and that pride may be taken away from him;
sentences.susu: alako e xa kira ɲaaxi bɛɲin, a man xa e ratanga e yɛtɛ kan igbofe ma.

sentences.english: To keep back his soul from the underworld, and his life from destruction.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a e ratangama nɛ gaburi gbaloe ma, a e ratanga santidɛgɛma ma.

sentences.english: Pain is sent on him as a punishment, while he is on his bed; there is no end to the trouble in his bones;
sentences.susu: Ala man nɔma masenyi tide adamadi bɛ a xa tɔɔrɛ nde ra, naxan xɔnɛ soma han a xɔrie kui a xa fure dagi tagi.

sentences.english: He has no desire for food, and his soul is turned away from delicate meat;
sentences.susu: Donse yati fa raɲaaxu a ma, a mu nɔ a dɛgede.

sentences.english: His flesh is so wasted away, that it may not be seen, and his bones. ...
sentences.susu: A fate ba a ma, a xɔrie birin sa kɛnɛ ma.

sentences.english: And his soul comes near to the underworld, and his life to the angels of death.
sentences.susu: A makɔrɛ aligiyama ra, Sayamalekɛ fa a fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: If now there may be an angel sent to him, one of the thousands which there are to be between him and God, and to make clear to man what is right for him;
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ xa xɛɛra xunmafalama nde sa lu a bɛ malekɛ galie ya ma, naxan fama tinxin ki masende na kanyi bɛ,

sentences.english: And if he has mercy on him, and says, Let him not go down to the underworld, I have given the price for his life:
sentences.susu: Na kui, xɛɛra xunmafalama findima saabui fanyi ra a bɛ, Ala hinnɛ a ra, a a masen Ala bɛ, ‹A rakisi faxɛ ma, n bara a xunsare ba.›

sentences.english: Then his flesh becomes young again, and he comes back to the days of his early strength;
sentences.susu: Na kui, a fate man gbilenma dimɛdiɲa, a man fonike sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: He makes his prayer to God, and he has mercy on him; he sees God's face with cries of joy; he gives news of his righteousness to men;
sentences.susu: Adamadi na Ala hinnɛnte maxandi, a Ala yatagi toma nɛ sɛɛwɛ kui, Ala fa tinxinyi fi a ma.

sentences.english: He makes a song, saying, I did wrong, turning from the straight way, but he did not give me the reward of my sin.
sentences.susu: Na kanyi bɛɛti bama nɛ mixie ya i, a a fala, ‹N yunubi rabaxi nɛ, n tinxinyi madalin, kɔnɔ na sare mu ragbilenxi n ma a ki ma.

sentences.english: He kept my soul from the underworld, and my life sees the light in full measure.
sentences.susu: Ala bara n xɔrɛya, n tan naxan xun nu tixi aligiyama ra. A man bara gbilen naiyalanyi masen na n bɛ.›

sentences.english: Truly, God does all these things to man, twice and three times,
sentences.susu: Ala nan na rabama adama bɛ, keren, firin, han saxan,

sentences.english: Keeping back his soul from the underworld, so that he may see the light of life.
sentences.susu: alako a xa a ba faxɛ yi, a xa a lu naiyalanyi kui.»

sentences.english: Take note O Job, give ear to me; keep quiet, while I say what is in my mind.
sentences.susu: «Ayuba, i tuli mati n na, i xa i sabari, i xa n ma masenyi ramɛ.

sentences.english: If you have anything to say, give me an answer; for it is my desire that you may be judged free from sin.
sentences.susu: Xa yaabi nde na i bɛ, i xa na fala, barima n wama nɔndi fife i ma.

sentences.english: If not, give attention to me, and keep quiet, and I will give you wisdom.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa na mu a ra, i tuli mati n na, i xa i sabari alako i xa xaxili sɔtɔ n na.»

sentences.english: And Elihu made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Elihu naxa a masen,

sentences.english: Give ear, you wise, to my words; and you who have knowledge, give attention to me;
sentences.susu: «Lɔnnilae, wo wo tuli mati. Xaxilimae, wo n ma masenyi ramɛ,

sentences.english: For words are tested by the ear, as food is tasted by the mouth.
sentences.susu: barima tuli wɔyɛnyi sensima, alɔ nɛnyi donse sensima ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Let us make the decision for ourselves as to what is right; let us have the knowledge among ourselves of what is good.
sentences.susu: Won xa tinxinyi sugandi, won xa bira fe fanyi fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: For Job has said, I am upright, and it is God who has taken away my right;
sentences.susu: «Ayuba naxɛ, ‹N tinxin, kɔnɔ Ala mu nɔndi fixi n ma.

sentences.english: Though I am right, still I am in pain; my wound may not be made well, though I have done no wrong.
sentences.susu: Hali n to tinxinxi, a bara n lu alɔ wule falɛ. N mu yunubi yo rabaxi, kɔnɔ n na tɔɔrɛ ɲaaxi kui.›

sentences.english: What man is like Job, a man who freely makes sport of God,
sentences.susu: Nde yaagi sɔtɔxi dangi Ayuba ra?

sentences.english: And goes in the company of evil-doers, walking in the way of sinners?
sentences.susu: A bara a ɲɛrɛ tinxintareya kui, a bara lu fe ɲaaxi rabae ya ma.

sentences.english: For he has said, It is no profit to a man to take delight in God.
sentences.susu: A bara a fala, ‹Geeni mu na adamadi bɛ naxan birama Ala waxɔnfe fɔxɔ ra.›

sentences.english: Now then, you wise, take note; you men of knowledge, give ear to me. Let it be far from God to do evil, and from the Ruler of all to do wrong.
sentences.susu: Xaxilimae, wo wo tuli mati n na. Ala nun fe ɲaaxi tagi ikuya, Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi mu tinxintareya kolon.

sentences.english: For he gives to every man the reward of his work, and sees that he gets the fruit of his ways.
sentences.susu: A mixie xa fe rabaxi sare ragbilenma e ma, a kote dɔxɔma e xun ma e nun naxan lan.

sentences.english: Truly, God does not do evil, and the Ruler of all is not a false judge.
sentences.susu: Ala mu nɔma fe ɲaaxi rabade. Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi mu nɔma tinxinyi kanade.

sentences.english: Who put the earth into his care, or made him responsible for the world?
sentences.susu: Nde a ti a xa duniɲa yamari? Nde duniɲa taxuxi a ra?

sentences.english: If he made his spirit come back to him, taking his breath into himself again,
sentences.susu: Xa Ala mu a ɲɛngi saxi adamadie xɔn ma nu, a fa a xaxili nun a ɲɛngi ba e yi,

sentences.english: All flesh would come to an end together, and man would go back to the dust.
sentences.susu: adamadi birin faxama kerenyi nan na nu, e findi bɛndɛ ra.

sentences.english: If you are wise, take note of this; give ear to the voice of my words.
sentences.susu: Xa xaxili fanyi na i yi ra, i xa i tuli mati n ma masenyi ra.

sentences.english: How may a hater of right be a ruler? and will you say that the upright Ruler of all is evil?
sentences.susu: Tinxintare nɔma duniɲa yamaride? I Tinxintɔɛ Sɛnbɛma nan kalamuma?

sentences.english: He who says to a king, You are an evil-doer; and to rulers, You are sinners;
sentences.susu: I nɔma a falade mangɛ bɛ, ‹Mixi xuri di nan i ra?› I nɔma a falade kuntigie bɛ, ‹Wo ɲaaxu?›

sentences.english: Who has no respect for rulers, and who gives no more attention to those who have wealth than to the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
sentences.susu: Ala mu mangɛ rafisa mixie bɛ, a mu bannae rafisa setaree bɛ, barima a tan nan birin daaxi.

sentences.english: Suddenly they come to an end, even in the middle of the night: the blow comes on the men of wealth, and they are gone, and the strong are taken away without the hand of man.
sentences.susu: Faxɛ man e birin tɛrɛnnama nɛ. Ɲamae e xunyi ikelima, kɔɛ kui e birin sɔntɔ. Sɛnbɛmae yati faxama nɛ fɔyɔgɔntɔn.

sentences.english: For his eyes are on the ways of a man, and he sees all his steps.
sentences.susu: Ala adamadie xa kira birin matoma, a e fɔxi igbɛ.

sentences.english: There is no dark place, and no thick cloud, in which the workers of evil may take cover.
sentences.susu: Dimi mu na naxan nɔma tinxintaree nɔxunde.

sentences.english: For he does not give man a fixed time to come before him to be judged.
sentences.susu: Ala hayi mu na tɛmui xɔnkuye ma mixi makiitife ra.

sentences.english: He sends the strong to destruction without searching out their cause, and puts others in their place.
sentences.susu: A nɔma sɛnbɛmae xun nakanade mafurenyi ra, a fa mixi gbɛtɛe dɔxɔ e ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: For he has knowledge of their works, overturning them in the night, so that they are crushed.
sentences.susu: A na e xa fe ɲaaxi to, a nɔma e bade duniɲa ma kerenyi ra kɔɛ kui.

sentences.english: The evil-doers are broken by his wrath, he puts his hand on them with force before the eyes of all onlookers.
sentences.susu: A nɔma e bɔnbɔde alɔ mixi kobi ɲama ya xɔri,

sentences.english: Because they did not go after him, and took no note of his ways,
sentences.susu: barima e mɛɛxi a xa sɛriyɛ nan na, e a xa kira bɛɲin.

sentences.english: So that the cry of the poor might come up to him, and the prayer of those in need come to his ears.
sentences.susu: E bara a niya setare wa xui xa Ala li. Ala tɔɔrɔmixi malima.
Xa Ala a sabari, nde nɔma a kalamude? Xa Ala a nɔxun, nde nɔma a tode? Adamadi mu nɔma na ra, ɲamanɛe yati mu nɔma na ra.
Ala mu tinxintare luma mangɛya kui, alako a xa gantanyi te ɲama bɛ.
Na mixi mɔɔli mu a falama Ala bɛ, ‹N bara gbilen fe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra n ma ɲaxankatɛ xa fe ra.
N fe ɲaaxi naxan nabaxi, na masen n bɛ, n mu na rabama sɔnɔn?›
Ala lanma a xa a sare fi? I tan nan a matandife, n tan mu a ra, i tan nan yaabi tima.

sentences.english: Men of knowledge, and all wise men, hearing me, will say,
sentences.susu: Xaxilimae nun lɔnnilae naxee e tuli matixi n na, muxu birin bara lan yi ma:

sentences.english: Job's words do not come from knowledge; they are not the fruit of wisdom.
sentences.susu: Ayuba wɔyɛnfe xaxilitareɲa nan kui, lɔnni mu a yi.

sentences.english: May Job be tested to the end, because his answers have been like those of evil men.
sentences.susu: Ayuba xa ɲaxankata han a dande, barima a xa masenyie mu tinxin.

sentences.english: For in addition to his sin, he is uncontrolled in heart; before our eyes he makes sport of God, increasing his words against him.
sentences.susu: A xa yunubi xun nan tun masafe. A wɔyɛnma muxu bɛ yɛtɛ igboɲa ra, A a xa Ala matandi xun masama a xa wɔyɛnyi ra.»

sentences.english: And Elihu made answer and said,
sentences.susu: Elihu naxa a fala,

sentences.english: What profit is it to me, and how am I better off than if I had done wrong?
sentences.susu: I bara a maxɔrin, ‹Geeni mundun na n bɛ xa n mu yunubi rabama?›

sentences.english: I will make answer to you and to your friends:
sentences.susu: N tan nan i yaabima na ra, i tan nun i booree.

sentences.english: Let your eyes be turned to the heavens, and lifted up to see the skies; they are higher than you.
sentences.susu: Koore mato. Nuxui mu na i xun ma xɛ?

sentences.english: If you have done wrong, is he any the worse for it? and if your sins are great in number, what is it to him?

sentences.english: If you are upright, what do you give to him? or what does he take from your hand?
sentences.susu: Xa i tinxin, na findima geeni mundun na a tan bɛ?

sentences.english: Your evil-doing may have an effect on a man like yourself, or your righteousness on a son of man.
sentences.susu: I xa fe ɲaaxi nɔma adamadi nan gbansan tɔɔrɔde, adamadi naxan luxi alɔ i tan. I xa tinxinyi fan nɔma findide geeni ra adamadi nan gbansan bɛ.

sentences.english: Because the hand of the cruel is hard on them, men are making sounds of grief; they are crying out for help because of the arm of the strong.
sentences.susu: Mixie e wa xui mɛma barima fe ɲaaxi rabae wuya. Mixie xili tima na kobiɲa xa fe ra.

sentences.english: But no one has said, Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night;

sentences.english: Who gives us more knowledge than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the heaven?
sentences.susu: naxan lɔnni fima adamadie ma dangife subee ra naxee na duniɲa ma, dangife xɔnie ra naxee na kuye ma?›

sentences.english: There they are crying out because of the pride of the evil-doers, but he gives them no answer.
sentences.susu: Mixie xili tima, kɔnɔ a mu e yaabima fe ɲaaxi rabae xa yɛtɛ igboɲa xa fe ra.

sentences.english: But God will not give ear to what is false, or the Ruler of all take note of it;

sentences.english: How much less when you say that you do not see him; that the cause is before him, and you are waiting for him.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i tan nan a falaxi a i mu Ala toxi, i xa fe saxi a ya i, i na a mamɛfe tun.

sentences.english: And now ... ;

sentences.english: And Elihu went on to say,

sentences.english: I will get my knowledge from far, and I will give righteousness to my Maker.

sentences.english: For truly my words are not false; one who has all knowledge is talking with you.

sentences.english: Truly, God gives up the hard-hearted, and will not give life to the sinner.
sentences.susu: «Ala sɛnbɛ gbo, a mu yoma mixi yo ma. A sɛnbɛ gbo, a ɲanige fan.

sentences.english: Who gives in the evening the meat he is searching for, when his young ones are crying to God; when the young lions with loud noise go wandering after their food?
sentences.susu: Xaxae go, e xa die nɛ wama koore ma, i tan nan e baloma?»

sentences.english: Have you knowledge of the rock-goats? or do you see the roes giving birth to their young?
sentences.susu: «I wula i si di bari tɛmui kolon geyae fari? I bara xeli to di bari ra?

sentences.english: Is the number of their months fixed by you? or is the time when they give birth ordered by you?
sentences.susu: I e xa furi maxanin kike kɔnti kolon beenu e di bari waxati xa a li?

sentences.english: They are bent down, they give birth to their young, they let loose the fruit of their body.
sentences.susu: E na e sa, e di barima, alako e xa fulun e furi xa xɔnɛ ma.

sentences.english: Their young ones are strong, living in the open country; they go out and do not come back again.
sentences.susu: E xa die na mɔ, e keli e nga xun ma, e mu fa sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: Who has let the ass of the fields go free? or made loose the bands of the loud-voiced beast?
sentences.susu: «Nde luuti baxi sofale ma, a a rabɛɲin wula i?

sentences.english: To whom I have given the waste land for a heritage, and the salt land as a living-place.
sentences.susu: N tan nan wula findixi a xɔnyi ra n a lu yire, fɔxɛ sunbuxi bɛndɛ ra dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: He makes sport of the noise of the town; the voice of the driver does not come to his ears;
sentences.susu: Taa xa wundui mu rafan a ma, a mu tinma mixie xa a raɲɛrɛ.

sentences.english: He goes looking for his grass-lands in the mountains, searching out every green thing.
sentences.susu: A wula isama ɲooge fende a balose ra.»

sentences.english: Will the ox of the mountains be your servant? or is his night's resting-place by your food-store?
sentences.susu: «I nɔma sɛxɛ ninge rawalide? A kɔɛ radangima i xa gɔɔrɛ kui?

sentences.english: Will he be pulling your plough with cords, turning up the valleys after you?
sentences.susu: I nɔma a xiride sari ra, a xa bɔxi buxa i bɛ?

sentences.english: Will you put your faith in him, because his strength is great? will you give the fruit of your work into his care?
sentences.susu: I i yigi suxuma a sɛnbɛ gbe ra? I nɔma i xa wali xungbee taxude a ra?

sentences.english: Will you be looking for him to come back, and get in your seed to the crushing-floor?
sentences.susu: I nɔma a xɛɛde xɛ xabɛ, a xa i mali i xa baloe rasode?»

sentences.english: Is the wing of the ostrich feeble, or is it because she has no feathers,
sentences.susu: «Xɔni mɔɔli nde na na naxan gabutenyi dunkee ibɔnbɔma sɛɛwɛ kui, kɔnɔ e mu tofan gbongboe gabutenyie bɛ.

sentences.english: That she puts her eggs on the earth, warming them in the dust,
sentences.susu: A a xɛlɛe sama bɔxi ma, a e lu mɛyɛnyi bun ma alako wuyenyi xa lu e ma,

sentences.english: Without a thought that they may be crushed by the foot, and broken by the beasts of the field?
sentences.susu: a mu a maɲɔxun sube nde nɔma tide e fari, e bula.

sentences.english: She is cruel to her young ones, as if they were not hers; her work is to no purpose; she has no fear.
sentences.susu: A mu mɛɛnima a xa die ma, a luma alɔ a gbe mu e ra.

sentences.english: For God has taken wisdom from her mind, and given her no measure of knowledge.
sentences.susu: A na mɔɔli rabama barima Ala mu lɔnni nun xaxili fanyi fixi a ma.

sentences.english: When she is shaking her wings on high, she makes sport of the horse and of him who is seated on him.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a na a gi fɔlɔ, a soe ragie nun soe luma nɛ a xanbi ra.»

sentences.english: Do you give strength to the horse? is it by your hand that his neck is clothed with power?
sentences.susu: «I tan nan soe sɛnbɛ fima a ma? I tan nan a kɔnyi xabee rakuyama?

sentences.english: Is it through you that he is shaking like a locust, in the pride of his loud-sounding breath?
sentences.susu: I tan nan a niyama a xa nɔ tugande alɔ katoe, a birin magaaxu a xui ra?

sentences.english: He is stamping with joy in the valley; he makes sport of fear.
sentences.susu: A bɔxi iboronma a sanyi ra, a ɲɛlɛxinxi a sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: In his strength he goes out against the arms of war, turning not away from the sword.
sentences.susu: A mu gaaxuma sese ya ra, a mu a magbilenma santidɛgɛma ya i.

sentences.english: The bow is sounding against him; he sees the shining point of spear and arrow.
sentences.susu: Tanbɛe nun e sase gbakuxi a ma,

sentences.english: Shaking with passion, he is biting the earth; he is not able to keep quiet at the sound of the horn;
sentences.susu: a gbataxi tuganma, a xulun a gide gere yire.

sentences.english: When it comes to his ears he says, Aha! He is smelling the fight from far off, and hearing the thunder of the captains, and the war-cries.
sentences.susu: Gere sara na fe, a tan kelima nɛ fa keren na a gereso ki ma.»

sentences.english: Is it through your knowledge that the hawk takes his flight, stretching out his wings to the south?
sentences.susu: «I xa lɔnni bara a niya sɛgɛ xa a ɲɛrɛ koore ma sigafe ra yirefanyi ma?

sentences.english: Or is it by your orders that the eagle goes up, and makes his resting-place on high?
sentences.susu: I tan nan yaamari fima a ma a xa a tɛɛ sa yire itexi?

sentences.english: On the rock is his house, and on the mountain-top his strong place.
sentences.susu: Kɔɛ ra, a yigiyama gɛmɛ longori ra geyae fari. Mɛnni nan findixi a bɛ a makantade nan na.

sentences.english: From there he is watching for food; his eye sees it far off.
sentences.susu: A subee toma na yire makuye nɛ, a baloma naxee ra.

sentences.english: His young have blood for their drink, and where the dead bodies are, there is he to be seen.
sentences.susu: Sube xinde ɲɔxun a xa diyɔrɛe bɛ. Binbi lu dɛdɛ a na mɛnni.»
Alatala man naxa a masen Ayuba bɛ,

sentences.english: Will he who is protesting give teaching to the Ruler of all? Let him who has arguments to put forward against God give an answer.
sentences.susu: «I tan naxan Ala Sɛnbɛ Kanyi kalamuma, i suusama a rakiitide? Xa lɔnnila na i tan na, yaabi nde ti yi birin ma ba.»

sentences.english: And Job said in answer to the Lord,
sentences.susu: Ayuba naxa Alatala yaabi,

sentences.english: Truly, I am of no value; what answer may I give to you? I will put my hand on my mouth.
sentences.susu: «Mixi xuri di nan n na. N tan i yaabima munse ra? N bara n dɛ suxu n bɛlɛxɛ ra, n dundu yen.

sentences.english: I have said once, and even twice, what was in my mind, but I will not do so again.
sentences.susu: N wɔyɛn nɛ keren, n naxa wɔyɛn firin. Na xanbi, n mu sese sama na fari sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: Then the Lord made answer to Job out of the storm-wind, and said,
sentences.susu: Ala man naxa a masen Ayuba bɛ turunnaadɛ foye kui,

sentences.english: Get your strength together like a man of war: I will put questions to you, and you will give me the answers.
sentences.susu: «I i tagi xiri gben alɔ gbangbalanyi, n xa maxɔrinyi ndee ti i ma, i xa n yaabi.

sentences.english: Will you even make my right of no value? will you say that I am wrong in order to make clear that you are right?
sentences.susu: I mu laxi a ra n ma kiiti tinxin? I wama nɔndi bafe n yi ra nɛ, a xa lu i tan bɛ?

sentences.english: Have you an arm like God? have you a voice of thunder like his?
sentences.susu: I sɛnbɛ gbo Ala gbe bɛ? I xui magaaxu alɔ a gbe?

sentences.english: Put on the ornaments of your pride; be clothed with glory and power:
sentences.susu: Na kui, i i maxiri nɔrɛ nun xunnakeli ra ba, i xa tofan, i xa i sɛnbɛ masen.

sentences.english: Let your wrath be overflowing; let your eyes see all the sons of pride, and make them low.
sentences.susu: I xa i xa xɔnɛ magaaxuxi ramini ba, i yɛtɛ igboee xun nakana.

sentences.english: Send destruction on all who are lifted up, pulling down the sinners from their places.
sentences.susu: E birin kuntan, mixi ɲaaxie igbantu e yire.

sentences.english: Let them be covered together in the dust; let their faces be dark in the secret place of the underworld.
sentences.susu: Bɛndɛ radin e birin xun na, e balan gaburi kui.

sentences.english: Then I will give praise to you, saying that your right hand is able to give you salvation.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui n fan yɛtɛ yati i matɔxɔma nɛ, barima i yɛtɛ sɛnbɛ bara i rakisi.»

sentences.english: See now the Great Beast, whom I made, even as I made you; he takes grass for food, like the ox.
sentences.susu: «Mali mato ba a fanyi ra, na sube magaaxuxi n naxan daaxi alɔ n i fan daaxi ki naxɛ. A ɲooge donma alɔ ninge.

sentences.english: His strength is in his body, and his force in the muscles of his stomach.
sentences.susu: A sɛnbɛ gbe na a gungui nɛ, sɛnbɛ malanxi a furi kiri bun.

sentences.english: His tail is curving like a cedar; the muscles of his legs are joined together.
sentences.susu: A xuli sɛnbɛ gbo alɔ konde bili, a sanyi fasɛe wuya, e gadara.

sentences.english: His bones are pipes of brass, his legs are like rods of iron.
sentences.susu: A xɔrie luxi alɔ yɔxui, xa na mu a ra wure.

sentences.english: He is the chief of the ways of God, made by him for his pleasure.
sentences.susu: Ala xa daalise fisamante nan a ra, kɔnɔ a gaaxuma Ala xa santidɛgɛma ya ra.

sentences.english: He takes the produce of the mountains, where all the beasts of the field are at play.
sentences.susu: A a baloe fenma geyae kɔn sube xaaɲɛe ya ma.

sentences.english: He takes his rest under the trees of the river, and in the pool, under the shade of the water-plants.
sentences.susu: A xima niini bun ma, a a nɔxun dabonyie kui.

sentences.english: He is covered by the branches of the trees; the grasses of the stream are round him.
sentences.susu: A a malabuma wuri bilie niini bun ma, naxee na dabon dɛ ra.

sentences.english: Truly, if the river is overflowing, it gives him no cause for fear; he has no sense of danger, even if Jordan is rushing against his mouth.
sentences.susu: Dabonyi ye xa gboe mu a magaaxuma. Yurudɛn xure na banbaran yɛ, a mu a tɔɔrɔma.

sentences.english: Will anyone take him when he is on the watch, or put metal teeth through his nose?
sentences.susu: A ya rabixi nɔma suxude? A nɔma suxude gantanyi ra, a ɲɔɛ xa tunba?»

sentences.english: Is it possible for Leviathan to be pulled out with a fish-hook, or for a hook to be put through the bone of his mouth?
sentences.susu: «Mixi mu nɔma a ra, a xa toe gbansan findima gaaxui nan na.

sentences.english: Will you put a cord into his nose, or take him away with a cord round his tongue?
sentences.susu: Xa mixi mu suusama a ya ra, nde fa nɔma suusade n tan ya ra?

sentences.english: Will he make prayers to you, or say soft words to you?
sentences.susu: Nde n donixi se nde ra n naxan nagbilenma a ma? Duniɲa birin findixi n gbe nan na.

sentences.english: Will he make an agreement with you, so that you may take him as a servant for ever?
sentences.susu: N mu nɔma dundude na sɔɲɛ xa fe ma, a salonsee sɛnbɛ gbo, a man tofan.

sentences.english: Will you make sport with him, as with a bird? or put him in chains for your young women?
sentences.susu: A bura fɛɛrɛ na nde bɛ? Nde mu gaaxuma a ɲinyie ya ra?

sentences.english: Will the fishermen make profit out of him? will they have him cut up for the traders?
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma a dɛ rabide? A ɲinyi magaaxuxie a dɛ kui rafexi.

sentences.english: Will you put sharp-pointed irons into his skin, or fish-spears into his head?
sentences.susu: Xalee fatuxi a kiri ma alɔ sɔɔri xa wure lefa,

sentences.english: Only put your hand on him, and see what a fight you will have; you will not do it again!
sentences.susu: e xɛtɛnxi e bore ra, foye sode yati mu na e tagi

sentences.english: Truly, the hope of his attacker is false; he is overcome even on seeing him!
sentences.susu: e fatuxi e bore ma a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: He is so cruel that no one is ready to go against him. Who then is able to keep his place before me?
sentences.susu: A na ɲɛngi sɛnbɛ ra, yanbɛ nan luma mini ra, a yae fan luxi alɔ gɛɛsɛgɛ soge.

sentences.english: Who ever went against me, and got the better of me? There is no one under heaven!
sentences.susu: Tɛ yiriyiri minima a dɛ i, e fulefulee nu fa yensen yɛ kuye ma.

sentences.english: I will not keep quiet about the parts of his body, or about his power, and the strength of his frame.
sentences.susu: Tuuri nde minima a ɲɔɛ, na luxi nɛ alɔ fifa naxan dɔxɔxi tɛ ma, a satunfe.

sentences.english: Who has ever taken off his outer skin? who may come inside his inner coat of iron?
sentences.susu: A ɲɛngi findima tɛ ra, tɛ yiriyiri nu fa mini a dɛ i.

sentences.english: Who has made open the doors of his face? Fear is round about his teeth.
sentences.susu: Sɛnbɛ xutunxi a kɔnyi ra, birin gaaxuma a ya ra.

sentences.english: His back is made of lines of plates, joined tight together, one against the other, like a stamp.
sentences.susu: A kiri xɔrɔxɔ, a sɛnbɛ gbo.
