sentences.english: A woman who is full of grace is honoured, but a woman hating righteousness is a seat of shame: those hating work will undergo loss, but the strong keep their wealth.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ fanyie binyɛ sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ xɛmɛ ɲaaxi naafuli nan tun sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: The man who has mercy will be rewarded, but the cruel man is the cause of trouble to himself.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ fanyi ɲɛrɛ ki a malima nɛ, kɔnɔ xɛmɛ ɲaaxi tɔɔrɛ nan bɛndunma a yɛtɛ ma.

sentences.english: The sinner gets the payment of deceit; but his reward is certain who puts in the seed of righteousness.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi xa geeni fama nɛ a madaxude. Tinxintɔɛ tan xa geeni findima sare fanyi nan na a bɛ.

sentences.english: So righteousness gives life; but he who goes after evil gets death for himself.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ kisima nɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintare faxɛ nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: The uncontrolled are hated by the Lord, but those whose ways are without error are his delight
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛ ɲaaxi mu rafan Alatala ma, a wama tinxinyi nan xɔn.

sentences.english: Certainly the evil-doer will not go free from punishment, but the seed of the upright man will be safe.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi fama nɛ fe ɲaaxi sɔtɔde, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ tan kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: Like a ring of gold in the nose of a pig, is a beautiful woman who has no sense.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ tofanyi xaxilitare luma nɛ alɔ xurundɛ xɛɛma daaxi xɔsɛ ɲɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: The desire of the upright man is only for good, but wrath is waiting for the evil-doer.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ fama nɛ fe fanyi sɔtɔde, kɔnɔ xɔnɛ nan luma mixi ɲaaxi tan bɛ.

sentences.english: A man may give freely, and still his wealth will be increased; and another may keep back more than is right, but only comes to be in need.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan bɛlɛxɛ yelefu ki tide, a bannaya sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ mixi kumaxi tan findima setare nan na.

sentences.english: He who gives blessing will be made fat, but the curser will himself be cursed.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a harige itaxunma, a fama nɛ harige sɔtɔde. Ye xɔli mu luma mixi ma naxan a boore kima ye ra.

sentences.english: He who keeps back grain will be cursed by the people; but a blessing will be on the head of him who lets them have it for a price.
sentences.susu: Ɲama mixi dankama nɛ naxan tondima baloe matide, e dubama nɛ mixi bɛ naxan tinma ɲama xa nde sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: He who, with all his heart, goes after what is good is searching for grace; but he who is looking for trouble will get it.
sentences.susu: Fe fanyi rabae, fe fanyi sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ fe ɲaaxi rabae, fe ɲaaxi nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: He who puts his faith in wealth will come to nothing; but the upright man will be full of growth like the green leaf.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a xaxili tima a xa naafuli ra, a fama nɛ birade, tinxintɔɛ tan luma nɛ alɔ burɛxɛ naxan mu lisima.

sentences.english: The troubler of his house will have the wind for his heritage, and the foolish will be servant to the wise-hearted.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tɔɔrɛ bɛndunma a xa denbaya ma, fe fufafu nan fama findide a kɛ ra. Lɔnnitare fama lude nɛ lɔnnila xa yaamari bun ma.

sentences.english: The fruit of righteousness is a tree of life, but violent behaviour takes away souls.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛe kisima nɛ, lɔnnilae mixie masɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: If the upright man is rewarded on earth, how much more the evil-doer and the sinner!
sentences.susu: Xa tinxintɔɛ a sare sɔtɔ duniɲa ma, mixi ɲaaxi nun yunubitɔɛ fan a sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: A lover of training is a lover of knowledge; but a hater of teaching is like a beast.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo tinma marasi ra, na wama lɔnni nan xɔn, naxan tan mu tinma na ra, daxui nan a ra.

sentences.english: A good man has grace in the eyes of the Lord; but the man of evil designs gets punishment from him.
sentences.susu: Alatala hinnɛma nɛ mixi fanyi ra, a mixi kobi tan ɲaxankata.

sentences.english: No man will make himself safe through evil-doing; but the root of upright men will never be moved.
sentences.susu: Ɲaaxuɲa mu xili xungbe fima mixi ma, kɔnɔ sese mu a niyama tinxintɔɛ sankee xa tala.

sentences.english: A woman of virtue is a crown to her husband; but she whose behaviour is a cause of shame is like a wasting disease in his bones.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ fanyi findima a xa mɔri xa xunnakeli nan na, ginɛ ɲaaxi tan luma nɛ alɔ kuli naxan na ɲinyi kui.

sentences.english: The purposes of upright men are right, but the designs of evil-doers are deceit.
sentences.susu: Mixi tinxinxie xa maɲɔxunyi fan, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxi xa marasi mixi madaxuma nɛ.

sentences.english: The words of sinners are destruction for the upright; but the mouth of upright men is their salvation.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi xa wɔyɛnyi mixi faxama nɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ tan xa wɔyɛnyi mixi rakisima nɛ.

sentences.english: Evil-doers are overturned and never seen again, but the house of upright men will keep its place.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie xa fe fama nɛ kanade, kɔnɔ sese mu mixi tinxinxie xa denbayae toma.

sentences.english: A man will be praised in the measure of his wisdom, but a wrong-minded man will be looked down on.
sentences.susu: Ɲama lɔnnilae matɔxɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ bɔɲɛ ɲaaxi kanyie, e yoma nɛ nee ma.

sentences.english: He who is of low position and has a servant, is better than one who has a high opinion of himself and is in need of bread.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ magore, malima keren peti na naxan bɛ, a fisa yɛtɛ igboe bɛ, baloe mu na naxan yi ra.

sentences.english: An upright man has thought for the life of his beast, but the hearts of evil-doers are cruel.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ mɛɛnima nɛ a xa xuruse ma, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxi tan ya ixara.

sentences.english: He who does work on his land will not be short of bread; but he who goes after foolish men is without sense.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi rawali baloe sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ lɔnnitare birama fe fufafu nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: The resting-place of the sinner will come to destruction, but the root of upright men is for ever.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi harige fenma tinxintareya ra, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ sankee tan sigama bɔxi suxu ra nɛ.

sentences.english: In the sin of the lips is a net which takes the sinner, but the upright man will come out of trouble.
sentences.susu: Fe ɲaaxi findima gantanyi nan na mixi ɲaaxi bɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ a yɛtɛ ratangama nɛ na tɔɔrɛ ma.

sentences.english: From the fruit of his mouth will a man have good food in full measure, and the work of a man's hands will be rewarded.
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛn fanyi findima xunnakeli nan na mixi bɛ, alɔ mixi to a xa wali sare sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: The way of the foolish man seems right to him? but the wise man gives ear to suggestions.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnitare a maɲɔxunxi a a xaxili fan, lɔnnila tan marasi nan fenma.

sentences.english: A foolish man lets his trouble be openly seen, but a sharp man keeps shame secret.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnitare bɔɲɛ te rafura, lɔnnila tan mu konbi yaabima.

sentences.english: The breathing out of true words gives knowledge of righteousness; but a false witness gives out deceit.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ nɔndi nan falama a boore xun, kɔnɔ seede ba ɲaaxi wule nan tun madɔxɔma.

sentences.english: There are some whose uncontrolled talk is like the wounds of a sword, but the tongue of the wise makes one well again.
sentences.susu: Mixi dɛ wuyaxi xa wɔyɛnyi mixi maxɔnɔma nɛ alɔ santidɛgɛma, kɔnɔ lɔnnila tan xa wɔyɛnyi mixi nan nayalanma.

sentences.english: True lips are certain for ever, but a false tongue is only for a minute.
sentences.susu: Nɔndi falɛ xa masenyi mu masarama, kɔnɔ wule falɛ xa masenyi luma nɛ masara ra.

sentences.english: Deceit is in the heart of those whose designs are evil, but for those purposing peace there is joy.
sentences.susu: Maifui nan na mixi ɲaaxi bɔɲɛ kui, sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ, naxan gere raxubenma.

sentences.english: No trouble will come to upright men, but sinners will be full of evil.
sentences.susu: Fe ɲaaxi yo mu tinxintɔɛ lima, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxie na nan tun sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: False lips are hated by the Lord, but those whose acts are true are his delight.
sentences.susu: Alatala wule falɛe xɔnma nɛ, a hinnɛma nɛ nɔndi falɛe ra.

sentences.english: A sharp man keeps back his knowledge; but the heart of foolish men makes clear their foolish thoughts.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila a xa lɔnni masen tɛmui kolon, lɔnnitare tan a xa daxuɲa nan ifalama a xui itexi ra.

sentences.english: The hand of the ready worker will have authority, but he who is slow in his work will be put to forced work.
sentences.susu: Tunnabɛxilae findima mangɛe nan na, kɔnɔ tunnaxɔnɛe findima konyie ra.

sentences.english: Care in the heart of a man makes it weighted down, but a good word makes it glad.
sentences.susu: Kɔntɔfili luma nɛ mixi lahalɛ masara ra, wɔyɛn fanyi tan a bɔɲɛ rasɛɛwama nɛ.

sentences.english: The upright man is a guide to his neighbour, but the way of evil-doers is a cause of error to them.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ kira tinxinxi masenma nɛ a boore bɛ, mixi ɲaaxi tan a boore ralɔɛma nɛ.

sentences.english: He who is slow in his work does not go in search of food; but the ready worker gets much wealth.
sentences.susu: Koyinma tunnaxɔnɛ mu a xa tɔɔkɛ ganma, kɔnɔ tunnabɛxila mɛɛnima nɛ a sɔtɔsee ma.

sentences.english: In the road of righteousness is life, but the way of the evil-doer goes to death.
sentences.susu: Simaya na kira tinxinxi nan xɔn ma. Faxɛ mu fulama na kira ra.

sentences.english: A wise son is a lover of teaching, but the ears of the haters of authority are shut to sharp words.
sentences.susu: Di lɔnnila a tuli matima a baba xa marasi nan na, kɔnɔ xurutare mu a tuli matima marasi ra.

sentences.english: A man will get good from the fruit of his lips, but the desire of the false is for violent acts.
sentences.susu: Mixi fanyi xa wɔyɛnyie fe fanyi nan naminima, kɔnɔ yanfante tan wama gere nan xɔn.

sentences.english: He who keeps a watch on his mouth keeps his life; but he whose lips are open wide will have destruction.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a dɛ suxuma, a xun nakelima nɛ, naxan dɛ wuyaxi, na tan a xun nakanama nɛ.

sentences.english: The hater of work does not get his desires, but the soul of the hard workers will be made fat.
sentences.susu: Tunnaxɔnɛ xa fefe mu sɔɔnɛyama, kɔnɔ tunnabɛxi harige gbegbe sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: The upright man is a hater of false words: the evil-doer gets a bad name and is put to shame.
sentences.susu: Wule mu rafan tinxintɔɛ ma, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxi tan a yɛtɛ rayaagima nɛ.

sentences.english: Righteousness keeps safe him whose way is without error, but evil-doers are overturned by sin.
sentences.susu: Tinxinyi tinxintɔɛ makantama nɛ, fe ɲaaxi yunubitɔɛ tan nahalakima nɛ.

sentences.english: A man may be acting as if he had wealth, but have nothing; another may seem poor, but have great wealth.
sentences.susu: Mixi nde a yɛtɛ findima banna nan na, kɔnɔ sese mu a yi ra. Boore tan a yɛtɛ findima setare nan na, kɔnɔ harige gbegbe na a yi ra.

sentences.english: A man will give his wealth in exchange for his life; but the poor will not give ear to sharp words.
sentences.susu: Banna xa kɔbiri a xun sarama mixi kobie ma, kɔnɔ mixi kobie mu sese fenma setare ra.

sentences.english: There is a glad dawn for the upright man, but the light of the sinner will be put out.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ luxi nɛ alɔ lanpui dɛxɛxi, mixi ɲaaxi tan xa lanpui xubenma nɛ.

sentences.english: The only effect of pride is fighting; but wisdom is with the quiet in spirit.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboɲa gere nan nabulama, kɔnɔ marasi ramɛfe findima lɔnni nan na.

sentences.english: Wealth quickly got will become less; but he who gets a store by the work of his hands will have it increased.
sentences.susu: Harige naxan sɔtɔma tinxintareya kui, a sigama xurun na nɛ, kɔnɔ harige naxan sɔtɔma dɔyi dɔyi tinxinyi kui, na sigama gbo ra nɛ.

sentences.english: Hope put off is a weariness to the heart; but when what is desired comes, it is a tree of life.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi mu a waxɔnfe sɔtɔma, a tɔɔrɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ xa a sɔtɔ, a sɛɛwama nɛ duniɲɛigiri kui.

sentences.english: He who makes sport of the word will come to destruction, but the respecter of the law will be rewarded.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan yoma marasi ma, a na sare sɔtɔma nɛ, naxan tan marasi binyama, na fama nɛ sare fanyi sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning men away from the nets of death.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa marasi findima simaya nan na, a mixi ratangama gantanyi ɲaaxi ma.

sentences.english: Wise behaviour gets approval, but the way of the false is their destruction.
sentences.susu: Fahaamui findima hinnɛ nan na mixi bɛ, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxi tan xa kira xɔrɔxɔ.

sentences.english: A sharp man does everything with knowledge, but a foolish man makes clear his foolish thoughts.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima a xa lɔnni rawalima, kɔnɔ xaxilitare daxuɲa nan tun funfunma.

sentences.english: A man taking false news is a cause of trouble, but he who gives news rightly makes things well.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛra tinxintare findima tɔɔrɛ nan saabui ra, xɛɛra tinxinxi tan fama yalanyi nan na.

sentences.english: Need and shame will be the fate of him who is uncontrolled by training; but he who takes note of teaching will be honoured.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tondima marasi ra, a setareɲa nun yaagi sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ naxan marasi ramɛma, a binyɛ nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: To get one's desire is sweet to the soul, but to give up evil is disgusting to the foolish.
sentences.susu: A ɲɔxun, mixi waxɔnfe na raba a bɛ, kɔnɔ xaxilitare mu tinma gbilende a waxɔnfe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Go with wise men and be wise: but he who keeps company with the foolish will be broken.
sentences.susu: Mixi na lu xaxilima fɔxɔ ra, a fan xaxili sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ lɔnnitaree xa malan booreɲa, findima tɔɔrɛ nan tun na.

sentences.english: Evil will overtake sinners, but the upright will be rewarded with good.
sentences.susu: Yunubitɔɛ sare findima fe ɲaaxi nan na, tinxintɔɛ tan sare findima hɛɛri nan na.

sentences.english: The heritage of the good man is handed down to his children's children; and the wealth of the sinner is stored up for the upright man.
sentences.susu: Mixi fanyi kɛ luma a xa mamadie nan bɛ, yunubitɔɛ tan kɛ luma tinxintɔɛe nan bɛ.

sentences.english: There is much food in the ploughed land of the poor; but it is taken away by wrongdoing.
sentences.susu: Baloe gbegbe minima nɛ setare xa xɛ ma, kɔnɔ tinxintareya luma nɛ kasara ra.

sentences.english: He who keeps back his rod is unkind to his son: the loving father gives punishment with care.
sentences.susu: Babɛ naxan mu a xa di xuruma luxusinyi ra, na di mu rafan a ma. Babɛ naxan a xa di xuruma, na di rafan a ma.

sentences.english: The upright man has food to the full measure of his desire, but there will be no food for the stomach of evil-doers.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ wasama nɛ baloe ra, kɔnɔ tinxintare tan luma kaamɛ ra nɛ.

sentences.english: Wisdom is building her house, but the foolish woman is pulling it down with her hands.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ lɔnnila sɛnbɛ fima nɛ a xa denbaya ma, kɔnɔ ginɛ lɔnnitare a xa denbaya xun nakanama nɛ.

sentences.english: He who goes on his way in righteousness has before him the fear of the Lord; but he whose ways are twisted gives him no honour.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a ɲɛrɛma a tinxinxi ra, a gaaxuma nɛ Ala ya ra, kɔnɔ naxan a ɲɛrɛma tinxintareya ra, na nan yoma Ala ma.

sentences.english: In the mouth of the foolish man is a rod for his back, but the lips of the wise will keep them safe.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboe xa wɔyɛnyi findima bɔnbɔɛ nan na a bɛ, lɔnnila tan xa wɔyɛnyi a makantama nɛ.

sentences.english: Where there are no oxen, their food-place is clean; but much increase comes through the strength of the ox.
sentences.susu: Xa ninge mu bɔxi buxama, saga mu rafema. Ninge xa wali a niyama nɛ mixi xa baloe gbegbe sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: A true witness does not say what is false, but a false witness is breathing out deceit.
sentences.susu: Seede fanyi mu wule falama, seede ɲaaxi tan wule nan tun funfunma.

sentences.english: The hater of authority, searching for wisdom, does not get it; but knowledge comes readily to the open-minded man.
sentences.susu: Mixi mayele lɔnni fenma nɛ, kɔnɔ a mu a sɔtɔma. Lɔnni kolonfe mu xɔrɔxɔ xaxilima bɛ.

sentences.english: Go away from the foolish man, for you will not see the lips of knowledge.
sentences.susu: I xa i makuya xaxilitaree ra, barima i mu lɔnni yo sɔtɔma e ra.

sentences.english: The wisdom of the man of good sense makes his way clear; but the unwise behaviour of the foolish is deceit.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila a ɲɔxɔ sama nɛ a ɲɛrɛ ki xɔn ma, lɔnnitare tan a yɛtɛ madaxuma nɛ.

sentences.english: In the tents of those hating authority there is error, but in the house of the upright man there is grace.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare yoma yunubi tongofe ma, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ Ala xa hinnɛ nan fenma.

sentences.english: No one has knowledge of a man's grief but himself; and a strange person has no part in his joy.
sentences.susu: Mixi a yɛtɛ xa tɔɔrɛ kolon a bɔɲɛ kui, a mu a xa sɛɛwɛ masenma mixi gbɛtɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: The house of the sinner will be overturned, but the tent of the upright man will do well.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie xa denbaya halakima nɛ, tinxintɔɛe tan xa denbaya fanma nɛ.

sentences.english: There is a way which seems straight before a man, but its end is the ways of death.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲɔxɔ a ma a a ɲɛrɛ ki fan, a fa li kɔrɛ a na gbaloe kira nan xɔn ma.

sentences.english: Even while laughing the heart may be sad; and after joy comes sorrow.
sentences.susu: Mixi nɔma yelede a dɛ ra, a tɔɔrɔxi a bɔɲɛ kui. Sɛɛwɛ nɔma mafindide tɔɔrɛ ra.

sentences.english: He whose heart is turned away will have the reward of his ways in full measure; but a good man will have the reward of his doings.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi yo, mixi fanyi yo, e birin e xa wali sare sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: The simple man has faith in every word, but the man of good sense gives thought to his footsteps.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare lama nɛ mixi birin xa masenyi ra, kɔnɔ xaxilima kira matoma nɛ beenu a xa bira na fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: The wise man, fearing, keeps himself from evil; but the foolish man goes on in his pride, with no thought of danger.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima gaaxuma nɛ Ala ya ra, a fa gbilen fe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra, kɔnɔ xaxilitare tan soma nɛ na fe ɲaaxi kui mafuren.

sentences.english: He who is quickly angry will do what is foolish, but the man of good sense will have quiet.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan bɔɲɛ tema mafuren, a daxuɲa nan nabama. Mixi madaxui mu rafan mixi yo ma.

sentences.english: Foolish behaviour is the heritage of the simple, but men of good sense are crowned with knowledge.
sentences.susu: Daxuɲa findima nɛ xaxilitare kɛ ra, xaxilimae tan lɔnni nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: The knees of the evil are bent before the good; and sinners go down in the dust at the doors of the upright.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie fama nɛ e xinbi sinde tinxintɔɛe bun ma, e kantari nan fenma tinxintɔɛe xɔnyi.

sentences.english: The poor man is hated even by his neighbour, but the man of wealth has numbers of friends.
sentences.susu: Setare raɲaaxu birin ma, hali a dɔxɔboore, kɔnɔ banna rafan mixi gbegbe ma.

sentences.english: He who has no respect for his neighbour is a sinner, but he who has pity for the poor is happy.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan yoma a ngaxakerenyi ma, a bara yunubi sɔtɔ, kɔnɔ naxan kinikini tɔɔrɔmixi ma, na bara sɛɛwɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Will not the designers of evil come into error? But mercy and good faith are for the designers of good.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxee fe ɲaaxi maɲɔxunma, nee bɔnɔma nɛ. Kɔnɔ naxee fe fanyi maɲɔxunma, na kanyie marafanyi nun nɔndi nan toma.

sentences.english: In all hard work there is profit, but talk only makes a man poor.
sentences.susu: Geeni na wali birin kui, kɔnɔ wɔyɛnyi gbansan findima setareɲa nan na.

sentences.english: Their wisdom is a crown to the wise, but their foolish behaviour is round the head of the unwise.
sentences.susu: Bannaya nan na lɔnnila sare ra, daxuɲa nan tun luma lɔnnitare tan yi ra.

sentences.english: A true witness is the saviour of lives; but he who says false things is a cause of deceit.
sentences.susu: Seede nɔndi falɛ mixi nii ratangama nɛ, kɔnɔ wule falɛ mixi madaxuma tun.

sentences.english: For him in whose heart is the fear of the Lord there is strong hope: and his children will have a safe place.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan gaaxu Alatala ya ra, a tan nun a xa die luma nɛ kantari kui.

sentences.english: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, by which one may be turned from the nets of death.
sentences.susu: Alatala xa yaragaaxui simaya fima nɛ mixi ma, alako e xa ratanga gantanyi ma naxan findima faxɛ ra.

sentences.english: A king's glory is in the number of his people: and for need of people a ruler may come to destruction.
sentences.susu: Ɲama xa gboe findima mangɛ xa xunnakeli nan na, kɔnɔ ɲama xa xurunyi findima mangɛ xa xunnagore nan na.

sentences.english: He who is slow to be angry has great good sense; but he whose spirit is over-quick gives support to what is foolish.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima bɔɲɛ te xɔnɔ, kɔnɔ xaxilitare a xa daxuɲa masenma nɛ a xa bɔɲɛ te saabui ra.

sentences.english: A quiet mind is the life of the body, but envy is a disease in the bones.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛsa findima simaya nan na, kɔnɔ milɛ tan findima fure nan na.

sentences.english: He who is hard on the poor puts shame on his Maker; but he who has mercy on those who are in need gives him honour.
sentences.susu: Naxan setare tɔɔrɔma, na bara yo setare Daa Mangɛ ma, kɔnɔ naxan kinikini setare ma, na bara a Daa Mangɛ matɔxɔ.

sentences.english: The sinner is overturned in his evil-doing, but the upright man has hope in his righteousness.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi xa ɲaaxuɲa a xun nakanama nɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ kantari sɔtɔma nɛ hali faxɛ ya i.

sentences.english: Wisdom has her resting-place in the mind of the wise, but she is not seen among the foolish.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni na xaxilima bɔɲɛ kui, xaxilitare yati nɔma na tode.

sentences.english: By righteousness a nation is lifted up, but sin is a cause of shame to the peoples.
sentences.susu: Tinxinyi bɔxi rasigama nɛ yare, yunubi tan ɲama rayaagima nɛ.

sentences.english: The king has pleasure in a servant who does wisely, but his wrath is against him who is a cause of shame.
sentences.susu: Walikɛ lɔnnila rafan mangɛ ma, kɔnɔ a walikɛ yaagitare tan xɔnma nɛ.

sentences.english: By a soft answer wrath is turned away, but a bitter word is a cause of angry feelings.
sentences.susu: Yaabi bɔrɔxɔxi mixi bɔɲɛ ragoroma nɛ, kɔnɔ wɔyɛn xɔnɛ tan mixi bɔɲɛ ratema nɛ.

sentences.english: Knowledge is dropping from the tongue of the wise; but from the mouth of the foolish comes a stream of foolish words.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa wɔyɛnyi a niyama nɛ xaxili fanyi xa rafan mixie ma, kɔnɔ xaxilitare xa wɔyɛnyi daxuɲa nan tun masenma.

sentences.english: The eyes of the Lord are in every place, keeping watch on the evil and the good.
sentences.susu: Alatala mixi birin matoma, mixi ɲaaxi nun mixi fanyi.

sentences.english: A comforting tongue is a tree of life, but a twisted tongue is a crushing of the spirit.
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛn fanyi mixi rayalanma, kɔnɔ wɔyɛn xɔnɛ mixi xaxili tɔɔrɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: A foolish man puts no value on his father's training; but he who has respect for teaching has good sense.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare yoma nɛ a baba xa marasi ma, xaxilima tan na marasi nan suxuma.

sentences.english: In the house of the upright man there is a great store of wealth; but in the profits of the sinner there is trouble.
sentences.susu: Harige fanyi na tinxintɔɛ xɔnyi, kɔnɔ tɔɔrɛ gbansan nan findima tinxintare sare ra.

sentences.english: The lips of the wise keep knowledge, but the heart of the foolish man is not right.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnilae xa wɔyɛnyie xaxili fima nɛ mixi ma, kɔnɔ fe fanyi yo mu na lɔnnitaree bɔɲɛ kui.

sentences.english: The offering of the evil-doer is disgusting to the Lord, but the prayer of the upright man is his delight.
sentences.susu: Alatala mixi ɲaaxi xa sɛrɛxɛ xɔnma, kɔnɔ a tinxintɔɛ xa duba suxuma nɛ.

sentences.english: The way of the evil-doer is disgusting to the Lord, but he who goes after righteousness is dear to him.
sentences.susu: Alatala mixi ɲaaxi xa kira xɔnma, kɔnɔ mixi naxan birama tinxinyi fɔxɔ ra a rafan a ma.

sentences.english: There is bitter punishment for him who is turned from the way; and death will be the fate of the hater of teaching.
sentences.susu: Kira fanyi bɛɲinfe findima ɲaxankatɛ nan na. Xurutareɲa mixi xun tima faxɛ kira nan ma.

sentences.english: Before the Lord are the underworld and destruction: how much more, then, the hearts of the children of men!
sentences.susu: Alatala to fe birin kolon, hali naxan nabama aligiyama nun yahannama, a ibunadama bɔɲɛ fan kolon.

sentences.english: The hater of authority has no love for teaching: he will not go to the wise.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboe mu wama marasi xɔn ma, a mu sigama lɔnnila yire.

sentences.english: A glad heart makes a shining face, but by the sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛ sɛɛwaxi mixi lahalɛ fanma, kɔnɔ bɔɲɛ tɔɔrɔxi mixi lahalɛ kanama nɛ.

sentences.english: The heart of the man of good sense goes in search of knowledge, but foolish things are the food of the unwise.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima lɔnni nan fenma, kɔnɔ xaxilitare daxu wɔyɛnyi nan tun falama.

sentences.english: All the days of the troubled are evil; but he whose heart is glad has an unending feast.
sentences.susu: Hali misikiinɛ tɔɔrɔ a xa simaya kui, xa a bɔɲɛ sɛɛwaxi, na findima nɛ baloe ra a bɛ.

sentences.english: Better is a little with the fear of the Lord, than great wealth together with trouble.
sentences.susu: Setare Ala yaragaaxui, fan banna xaxili ifuxi bɛ.

sentences.english: Better is a simple meal where love is, than a fat ox and hate with it.
sentences.susu: Bande ɲiɲɛ donfe xanunteya kui, na fan sube donfe bɛ gbɛsɛnxɔnnɛya kui.

sentences.english: An angry man makes men come to blows, but he who is slow to get angry puts an end to fighting.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛ rate gere xɔrɛ isɔxɔma nɛ, bɔɲɛ ragore sɔnxɔɛ raxinbelima nɛ.

sentences.english: Thorns are round the way of the hater of work; but the road of the hard worker becomes a highway.
sentences.susu: Tunnaxɔnɛ xa kira mabalanxi tunbee nan na, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ xa kira ɲɛrɛ ɲɔxun.

sentences.english: A wise son makes a glad father, but a foolish man has no respect for his mother.
sentences.susu: Di lɔnnixi findima sɛɛwɛ nan na a baba bɛ, kɔnɔ di lɔnnitare yoma nɛ a nga ma.

sentences.english: Foolish behaviour is joy to the unwise; but a man of good sense makes his way straight.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitareɲa rafan lɔnnitare ma, kɔnɔ xaxilima xa kira tinxin.

sentences.english: Where there are no wise suggestions, purposes come to nothing; but by a number of wise guides they are made certain.
sentences.susu: Marasitareɲa wali kanama nɛ, kɔnɔ marasi gbegbe wali nan sɔɔnɛyama.

sentences.english: A man has joy in the answer of his mouth: and a word at the right time, how good it is!
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ naxan fata a boore yaabide. Wɔyɛnyi tide gbo naxan falaxi a fala ki ma nun a fala tɛmui ma.

sentences.english: Acting wisely is the way of life, guiding a man away from the underworld.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa kira a ratema nɛ koore ma, a a mali a xa aligiyama kira matanga.

sentences.english: The house of the man of pride will be uprooted by the Lord, but he will make safe the heritage of the widow.
sentences.susu: Alatala yɛtɛ igboe xa banxi rabirama nɛ, kɔnɔ a kaaɲɛ ginɛ xa bɔxi makantama nɛ.

sentences.english: Evil designs are disgusting to the Lord, but the words of the clean-hearted are pleasing.
sentences.susu: Maɲɔxun kobi raɲaaxu Alatala ma, kɔnɔ wɔyɛn fanyi tan sɛniyɛn.

sentences.english: He whose desires are fixed on profit is a cause of trouble to his family; but he who has no desire for offerings will have life.
sentences.susu: Milante findima nɛ tɔɔrɛ ra a xa denbaya bɛ, kɔnɔ naxan mu wama geeni tinxintare xɔn, na kanyi kisi nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: The heart of the upright gives thought to his answer; but from the mouth of the evil-doer comes a stream of evil things.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ fe matoma nɛ a fanyi ra beenu a xa yaabi nde fi, kɔnɔ fe ɲaaxi mafura minide mixi ɲaaxi dɛ i.

sentences.english: The Lord is far from sinners, but his ear is open to the prayer of the upright.
sentences.susu: Alatala makuya mixi ɲaaxie ra, kɔnɔ a a tuli matima tinxintɔɛe xa maxandi ra.

sentences.english: The light of the eyes is a joy to the heart, and good news makes the bones fat.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛra ya iyalanxi mixi bɔɲɛ rasɛɛwama nɛ, xɛɛraya fanyi sɛnbɛ nan fima mixi ma.

sentences.english: The man whose ear is open to the teaching of life will have his place among the wise.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a tuli matima kisi marasi ra, na kanyi luma nɛ lɔnnilae ya ma.

sentences.english: He who will not be controlled by training has no respect for his soul, but he who gives ear to teaching will get wisdom.
sentences.susu: Naxan tondima marasi ramɛde, na yoxi a yɛtɛ nan ma, kɔnɔ naxan tinma marasi ramɛde, na kanyi xa lɔnni nan xun masama.

sentences.english: The fear of the Lord is the teaching of wisdom; and a low opinion of oneself goes before honour.
sentences.susu: Ala xa yaragaaxui findima lɔnni nan na mixi bɛ. Yɛtɛ magore fama binyɛ nan na.

sentences.english: The designs of the heart are man's, but the answer of the tongue comes from the Lord.
sentences.susu: Adamadi natɛ tongoma a bɔɲɛ kui, kɔnɔ maragiri na Ala nan bɛlɛxɛ.

sentences.english: All a man's ways are clean to himself; but the Lord puts men's spirits into his scales.
sentences.susu: Adama tan bɛ, a xa kira birin fan, kɔnɔ kiiti sa mangɛ Ala a bɔɲɛ kolon.

sentences.english: Put your works into the hands of the Lord, and your purposes will be made certain.
sentences.susu: Wali birin taxu Alatala ra, alako a xa sɔɔnɛya.

sentences.english: The Lord has made everything for his purpose, even the sinner for the day of evil.
sentences.susu: Alatala fe birin yailanxi fe nde nan ma. Hali mixi ɲaaxi daaxi gbaloe lɔxɔɛ nan ma fe ra.

sentences.english: Everyone who has pride in his heart is disgusting to the Lord: he will certainly not go free from punishment.
sentences.susu: Alatala yɛtɛ igboe xɔnxi. Ɲaxankatɛ nan a mamɛfe.

sentences.english: By mercy and good faith evil-doing is taken away: and by the fear of the Lord men are turned away from evil.
sentences.susu: Yunubi xafarima hinnɛ nun dugutɛgɛya nan saabui ra. Alatala xa yaragaaxui mixi ratangama fe ɲaaxi nan ma.

sentences.english: When a man's ways are pleasing to the Lord, he makes even his haters be at peace with him.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲɛrɛ ki na rafan Alatala ma, a a niyama nɛ gere xa ɲɔn na kanyi nun a yaxuie tagi.

sentences.english: Better is a little with righteousness, than great wealth with wrongdoing.
sentences.susu: Se dondoronti sɔtɔxi tinxinyi ra na nan fisa se gbegbe sɔtɔxi bɛ tinxintareya kui.

sentences.english: A man may make designs for his way, but the Lord is the guide of his steps.
sentences.susu: Mixi natɛ tongoma a xa fe rabaxi ma, kɔnɔ na fee ragiri mangɛ na Alatala nan na.

sentences.english: Decision is in the lips of the king: his mouth will not go wrong in judging.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xa masenyi tide gbo, a xa kiiti xa tinxin.

sentences.english: True measures and scales are the Lord's: all the weights of the bag are his work.
sentences.susu: Alatala na sikeeli tinxinxi nan bɛ, a xa wali nan na se maniyase kamalixi ra.

sentences.english: Evil-doing is disgusting to kings: for the seat of the ruler is based on righteousness.
sentences.susu: Fe ɲaaxi mu rafan mangɛe ma, barima tinxinyi nan mangɛ kibanyi mabanbanma.

sentences.english: Lips of righteousness are the delight of kings; and he who says what is upright is dear to him.
sentences.susu: Mangɛe xa hinnɛ na tinxintɔɛe bɛ, nɔndi falɛ rafan e ma.

sentences.english: The wrath of the king is like those who give news of death, but a wise man will put peace in place of it.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xa bɔɲɛte mixi faxama nɛ, kɔnɔ lɔnnila fata mangɛ bɔɲɛ ragorode.

sentences.english: In the light of the king's face there is life; and his approval is like a cloud of spring rain.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xa ɲɛlɛxinyi findima simaya nan na, a xa hinnɛ luma nɛ alɔ nuxui naxee tunɛ ye raminima.

sentences.english: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! and to get knowledge is more to be desired than silver.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni sɔtɔɛ fan xɛɛma sɔtɔɛ bɛ, xaxili fanyi sɔtɔɛ fan gbeti sɔtɔɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: The highway of the upright is to be turned away from evil: he who takes care of his way will keep his soul.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ xa kira mu sigama fe ɲaaxi ma. Mixi naxan a ɲɛngi saxi a ɲɛrɛ ki xɔn ma, na kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: Pride goes before destruction, and a stiff spirit before a fall.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboɲa mixi nan xun nakanama, yɛtɛ iteya mixi nan nalɔɛma.

sentences.english: Better it is to have a gentle spirit with the poor, than to take part in the rewards of war with men of pride.
sentences.susu: Lufe yɛtɛ magoree ya ma, na fan naafuli itaxunfe bɛ yɛtɛ igboee ya ma.

sentences.english: He who gives attention to the law of right will get good; and whoever puts his faith in the Lord is happy.
sentences.susu: Hɛɛri na mixi bɛ naxan a ɲɛngi sama fe raba kie xɔn ma. Sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ naxan a xaxili tima Alatala ra.

sentences.english: The wise-hearted will be named men of good sense: and by pleasing words learning is increased.
sentences.susu: Mixi sabarixi findima xaxilima nan na. Wɔyɛn ɲɔxunmɛ xaxili fima nɛ mixi ma.

sentences.english: Wisdom is a fountain of life to him who has it; but the punishment of the foolish is their foolish behaviour.
sentences.susu: Xaxili fanyi simaya nan fima xaxilima ma, xaxilitareɲa findima ɲaxankatɛ nan na xaxilitare bɛ.

sentences.english: The heart of the wise man is the teacher of his mouth, and gives increased learning to his lips.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima a ɲɛngi sama a xa masenyi ma, alako lɔnni fanyi xa mini a dɛ kui.

sentences.english: Pleasing words are like honey, sweet to the soul and new life to the bones.
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛn fanyi findixi kumi nan na, naxan xaxili nun fate rayalanma.

sentences.english: There is a way which seems straight before a man, but its end is the ways of death.
sentences.susu: Adama a maɲɔxun nɛ a xa kira fanxi, kɔnɔ a raɲɔnyi a xun tima faxɛ nan na.

sentences.english: The desire of the working man is working for him, for his need of food is driving him on.
sentences.susu: Walikɛ xa kaamɛ nan a tutunma wali ma.

sentences.english: A good-for-nothing man is a designer of evil, and in his lips there is a burning fire.
sentences.susu: Fuyante fe ɲaaxi maɲɔxunma nɛ, a xa masenyi mixi gan.

sentences.english: A man of twisted purposes is a cause of fighting everywhere: and he who says evil secretly makes trouble between friends.
sentences.susu: Mixi kobi gere xɔrɛ isɔxɔma nɛ, naafixi dɛfanmae tagi isoma.

sentences.english: A violent man puts desire of evil into his neighbour's mind, and makes him go in a way which is not good.
sentences.susu: Mixi kobi a boore ratantanma nɛ, a na ti kira ɲaaxi xɔn ma.

sentences.english: He whose eyes are shut is a man of twisted purposes, and he who keeps his lips shut tight makes evil come about.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tɔnxuma masenma a ya nun a dɛ ra, a wama fe ɲaaxi nde nan nabafe.

sentences.english: The grey head is a crown of glory, if it is seen in the way of righteousness.
sentences.susu: Xunsɛxɛ fiixɛ findima binyɛ nan na, naxan sɔtɔma kira tinxinxi xɔn ma.

sentences.english: He who is slow to be angry is better than a man of war, and he who has control over his spirit than he who takes a town.
sentences.susu: Diɲɛ mixi fan geresoe bɛ, yɛtɛ suxui tide dangi taa suxufe ra.

sentences.english: A thing may be put to the decision of chance, but it comes about through the Lord.
sentences.susu: Mixi kanda bunma fe nde ma, kɔnɔ fe birin nagiri mangɛ na Alatala nan na.

sentences.english: Better a bit of dry bread in peace, than a house full of feasting and violent behaviour.
sentences.susu: Taami xuntunyi sɔtɔfe bɔɲɛsa kui na nan fisa sube gbegbe sɔtɔfe bɛ lantareya na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: A servant who does wisely will have rule over a son causing shame, and will have his part in the heritage among brothers.
sentences.susu: Walikɛ xaxilima sɛnbɛ gbo dangife wali kanyi xa di ra, naxan fe mayaagixi rabama. Na walikɛ mɔɔli tan kɛ sɔtɔma nɛ na denbaya kui.

sentences.english: The heating-pot is for silver and the oven-fire for gold, but the Lord is the tester of hearts.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛma nun gbeti matose na tɛ nan na, kɔnɔ Alatala nan adama bɔɲɛ matoma.

sentences.english: A wrongdoer gives attention to evil lips, and a man of deceit gives ear to a damaging tongue.
sentences.susu: Fe kobi raba wɔyɛn tinxintare ramɛma, a a tuli matima wule falɛ ra.

sentences.english: Whoever makes sport of the poor puts shame on his Maker; and he who is glad because of trouble will not go free from punishment.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan yoma setaree ma, na bara setare Daa Marigi yelebu. Mixi naxan yelema a boore xa tɔɔrɛ ma, na ɲaxankatɛ nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: Children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children is their fathers.
sentences.susu: Mamadie findixi forie xa sɛɛwɛ nan na, babae fan findixi e xa die xa sɛɛwɛ nan na.

sentences.english: Fair words are not to be looked for from a foolish man, much less are false lips in a ruler.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xa wɔyɛnyi mu lan xaxilitare dɛ i, wule mu lan mangɛ dɛ i.

sentences.english: An offering of money is like a stone of great price in the eyes of him who has it: wherever he goes, he does well.
sentences.susu: Ki tife naadɛe rabima nɛ, a fe birin sɔɔnɛyama nɛ.

sentences.english: He who keeps a sin covered is looking for love; but he who keeps on talking of a thing makes division between friends.
sentences.susu: Diɲɛfe konbi ma a marafanyi nan na gboma, kɔnɔ na ifalafe a xanuntenmae tagi isoma.

sentences.english: A word of protest goes deeper into one who has sense than a hundred blows into a foolish man.
sentences.susu: Tantanyi masenfe lɔnnila bɛ a fahaamui fima nɛ a ma, dangife lɔnnitare bɔnbɔfe luxusinyi ya kɛmɛ ra.

sentences.english: An uncontrolled man is only looking for trouble, so a cruel servant will be sent against him.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi naxan mangɛ matandima tun, sɔɔri kinikinitare nan xɛɛma a xili ma.

sentences.english: It is better to come face to face with a bear whose young ones have been taken away than with a foolish man acting foolishly.
sentences.susu: Naralanfe sube xaaɲɛ ra, naxan xa die baxi a yi, na fisa naralanfe xaxilitare ra, naxan ɲɛrɛma a xa xaxilitareɲa kui.

sentences.english: If anyone gives back evil for good, evil will never go away from his house.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan fe fanyi ɲɔxɔma fe ɲaaxi ra, fe ɲaaxi mu makuyama na xa banxi ra.

sentences.english: The start of fighting is like the letting out of water: so give up before it comes to blows.
sentences.susu: Gere fɔlɔfe luxi nɛ alɔ bogoni ibɔɔfe. Na kui beenun sɔnxɔɛ xa mini, keli naa.

sentences.english: He who gives a decision for the evil-doer and he who gives a decision against the upright, are equally disgusting to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan nɔndi fima fe kobi rabama, nun mixi naxan tinxintɔɛ tɔɔɲɛgɛma, e mu rafan Alatala ma.

sentences.english: How will money in the hand of the foolish get him wisdom, seeing that he has no sense?
sentences.susu: Hali kɔbiri lu lɔnnitare yi ra, a mu na rawalima lɔnni sɔtɔfe ra.

sentences.english: A friend is loving at all times, and becomes a brother in times of trouble.
sentences.susu: Mixi a dɛfanboore xanuma tɛmui birin, a a ngaxakerenyi malima a tɔɔrɔ tɛmui.

sentences.english: A man without sense gives his hand in an agreement, and makes himself responsible before his neighbour.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnitare naxan xaxili mu na, na nan gbansan taanima a boore bɛ.

sentences.english: The lover of fighting is a lover of sin: he who makes high his doorway is looking for destruction.
sentences.susu: Gere rafan mixi yo ma, yunubi fan nafan na kanyi ma. Mixi naxan a yɛtɛ igboma, xunnakanɛ nan a lima.

sentences.english: Nothing good comes to him whose heart is fixed on evil purposes: and he who has an evil tongue will come to trouble.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo madaxui tima, na mu hɛɛri sɔtɔma, Mixi yo wɔyɛn kobi falama, na tɔɔrɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: He who has an unwise son gets sorrow for himself, and the father of a foolish son has no joy.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo di lɔnnitare bari, na fama nɛ tɔɔrɔde. Mixi yo di xaxilitare sɔtɔ, na mu sɛɛwama.

sentences.english: A glad heart makes a healthy body, but a crushed spirit makes the bones dry.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛ sɛɛwaxi, seri fanyi na a ra, xaxili sunnunxi tan xɔrie nan xun nakanama.

sentences.english: A sinner takes an offering out of his robe, to get a decision for himself in a cause.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi see rasuxuma gundo ra, alako kiiti tinxinxi xa mafindi.

sentences.english: Wisdom is before the face of him who has sense; but the eyes of the foolish are on the ends of the earth.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni makɔrɛ xaxilima ra, kɔnɔ xaxilitare ya tixi fe makuyaxi nan na.

sentences.english: A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitter pain to her who gave him birth.
sentences.susu: Di xaxilitare findima tɔɔrɛ nan na a baba bɛ, a findi xɔnɛ ra a nga bɛ.

sentences.english: To give punishment to the upright is not good, or to give blows to the noble for their righteousness.
sentences.susu: A mu lan kɔbiri xa ba tinxintɔɛ yi ra, a mu lan kuntigi xa bɔnbɔ a xa tinxinyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: He who has knowledge says little: and he who has a calm spirit is a man of good sense.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima a dɛ nan suxuma, a bɔɲɛ mu tema.

sentences.english: Even the foolish man, when he keeps quiet, is taken to be wise: when his lips are shut he is credited with good sense.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare nɔma a maɲɔxunde lɔnnila ra xa a dunduxi, a nɔma a maɲɔxunde fahaamula ra xa a sabarixi.

sentences.english: He who keeps himself separate for his private purpose goes against all good sense.
sentences.susu: Booretare a waxɔnfe gbansan nan fenma, a yo marasi birin ma.

sentences.english: A foolish man has no pleasure in good sense, but only to let what is in his heart come to light.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare mu wama xaxili fanyi xɔn, a wama a yɛtɛ xa maɲɔxunyi nan tun masenfe.

sentences.english: When the evil-doer comes, a low opinion comes with him, and with the loss of honour comes shame.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie yoma mixie ma, e yoma e ma han e sa yaagi.

sentences.english: The words of a man's mouth are like deep waters: the fountain of wisdom is like a flowing stream.
sentences.susu: Adama xa wɔyɛnyi tilin alɔ baa, a lɔnni raminima naxan luxi alɔ dulonyi ye fanyi.

sentences.english: To have respect for the person of the evil-doer is not good, or to give a wrong decision against the upright.
sentences.susu: Nɔndi fife mixi ɲaaxi ma, a mu fan. A mu lanma tinxintɔɛ xa tɔɔɲɛgɛ.

sentences.english: A foolish man's lips are a cause of fighting, and his mouth makes him open to blows.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnitare sɔnxɔɛ xɔrɛ isɔxɔma, a bɔnbɔɛ sɔtɔma a dɛ saabui ra.

sentences.english: The mouth of a foolish man is his destruction, and his lips are a net for his soul.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare dɛ a xun nakanama nɛ, a nɛnyi findixi gantanyi nan na a nii bɛ.

sentences.english: The words of one who says evil of his neighbour secretly are like sweet food, and go down into the inner parts of the stomach.
sentences.susu: Naafixi xa masenyi luxi nɛ alɔ donse ɲɔxunmɛ, naxan goroma mixi furi kui.

sentences.english: He who does not give his mind to his work is brother to him who makes destruction.
sentences.susu: Tunnaxɔnɛ nun kasarɛ raba, nee nga keren, e baba keren.

sentences.english: The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the upright man running into it is safe.
sentences.susu: Alatala findixi kantari sɛnbɛma nan na, tinxintɔɛ luma naxan niini bun ma.

sentences.english: The property of a man of wealth is his strong town, and it is as a high wall in the thoughts of his heart.
sentences.susu: Naafuli findixi banna xa kantari nan na, a ɲɔxɔ a ma tɛtɛ na a ra naxan mu nɔma kanade.

sentences.english: Before destruction the heart of man is full of pride, and before honour goes a gentle spirit.
sentences.susu: Gbaloe na yɛtɛ igboɲa xanbi ra, kɔnɔ nɔrɛ na yɛtɛ magore fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: To give an answer before hearing is a foolish thing and a cause of shame.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan yaabi fima beenu a xa mixi xui ramɛ, a daxuɲa masenma nɛ, a a yɛtɛ rayaagi.

sentences.english: The spirit of a man will be his support when he is ill; but how may a broken spirit be lifted up?
sentences.susu: Xaxili limaniyaxi mixi malima nɛ a xa fure kui, kɔnɔ limaniya baxi naxan yi, na mu kelima sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: The heart of the man of good sense gets knowledge; the ear of the wise is searching for knowledge.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila katama se kolonde, a a tuli matima masenyi fanyi ra.

sentences.english: A man's offering makes room for him, letting him come before great men.
sentences.susu: Kira rabixi mixi bɛ naxan ki tima, mangɛe yati tofe sɔɔnɛyama nɛ na kanyi bɛ.

sentences.english: The man who first puts his cause before the judge seems to be in the right; but then his neighbour comes and puts his cause in its true light.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan singe a yɛtɛ xun mafalama fe kui, a luma nɛ alɔ nɔndi na a tan nan bɛ, kɔnɔ a kalamuti maxɔrinyi xɔrɔxɔɛ tima nɛ a ma.

sentences.english: The decision of chance puts an end to argument, parting the strong.
sentences.susu: Fe lufe Ala ma a sɔnxɔɛ ɲɔnma nɛ, a gere ɲɔn sɛnbɛmae tagi.

sentences.english: A brother wounded is like a strong town, and violent acts are like a locked tower.
sentences.susu: Mixi konbixi xa bɔɲɛ xɔrɔxɔɛ luma nɛ alɔ taa makantaxi. Na sɔnxɔɛ mɔɔli xɔrɔxɔ dangife geeli kondonyi ra.

sentences.english: With the fruit of a man's mouth his stomach will be full; the produce of his lips will be his in full measure.
sentences.susu: Adama xa masenyi nɔma a baloe fide a ma, a hayi fanma nɛ a xa wɔyɛnyi saabui ra.

sentences.english: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; and those to whom it is dear will have its fruit for their food.
sentences.susu: Faxɛ nun simaya fatanma mixi xa wɔyɛnyi nan na. Wɔyɛnla a sare sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: Whoever gets a wife gets a good thing, and has the approval of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ sɔtɔfe findixi hɛɛri nan na, naxan fatanxi Alatala ra.

sentences.english: The poor man makes requests for grace, but the man of wealth gives a rough answer.
sentences.susu: Setare mayandi tima, kɔnɔ se kanyi a yaabima a xɔrɔxɔɛ nan na.

sentences.english: There are friends who may be a man's destruction, but there is a lover who keeps nearer than a brother.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi booree wuya, na nɔma findide tɔɔrɛ ra a bɛ, kɔnɔ boore nde na na naxan fan a ngaxakerenyi bɛ.

sentences.english: Better is the poor man whose ways are upright, than the man of wealth whose ways are twisted.
sentences.susu: Setare tinxinxi fan xaxilitare wule falɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: Further, without knowledge desire is not good; and he who is over-quick in acting goes out of the right way.
sentences.susu: Gbatafe ra i mu naxan kolon, a mixi ratantanma nɛ.

sentences.english: By his foolish behaviour a man's ways are turned upside down, and his heart is bitter against the Lord.
sentences.susu: Adamadi a yɛtɛ xun nakanama nɛ a xa daxuɲa ra, kɔnɔ a fa a bɔɲɛ rate Alatala tan ma na xunnakanɛ xa fe ra.

sentences.english: Wealth makes a great number of friends; but the poor man is parted from his friend.
sentences.susu: Bannaya a niyama nɛ mixi xa boore gbegbe sɔtɔ, kɔnɔ setareɲa dɛfanbooreɲa kanama nɛ.

sentences.english: A false witness will not go without punishment, and the breather out of deceit will not go free.
sentences.susu: Tɔɔɲɛgɛti fama nɛ ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔde, wule falɛ mu kisima.

sentences.english: Great numbers will make attempts to get the approval of a ruler: and every man is the special friend of him who has something to give.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbegbe katama e yɛtɛ rafande kinikinintee ma, birin birama nɛ mixi fɔxɔ ra naxan ki tima.

sentences.english: All the brothers of the poor man are against him: how much more do his friends go far from him! ...
sentences.susu: Setare mu rafan a ngaxakerenyie yati ma, a mu rafan a booree fan ma. A na e maxandi, e mu e tuli matima a ra.

sentences.english: He who gets wisdom has love for his soul: he who keeps good sense will get what is truly good.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan xaxili fenma, a fe fanyi rabama nɛ a yɛtɛ bɛ. Mixi naxan fahaamui fenma, a xa fe sɔɔnɛyama nɛ.

sentences.english: A false witness will not go without punishment, and the breather out of deceit will be cut off.
sentences.susu: Tɔɔɲɛgɛti fama nɛ ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔde, halaki birama nɛ wule falɛ fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Material comfort is not good for the foolish; much less for a servant to be put over rulers.
sentences.susu: Naafuli mu lan xaxilitare yi ra, alɔ a to mu lan konyi fan xa kuntigie yaamari.

sentences.english: A man's good sense makes him slow to wrath, and the overlooking of wrongdoing is his glory.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila bɔɲɛ te xɔnɔ, a mu konbi ragbilenma. Na kui a binyɛ sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: The king's wrath is like the loud cry of a lion, but his approval is like dew on the grass.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xa xɔnɛ maniya yɛtɛ xaaɲɛ ra, a xa hinnɛ fan maniya xini ra burɛxɛ xinde ma.

sentences.english: A foolish son is the destruction of his father; and the bitter arguments of a wife are like drops of rain falling without end.
sentences.susu: Di xaxilitare kɔntɔfili nan bɛndunma a baba ma, ginɛ xa sɔnxɔɛ xunxuri luxi nɛ alɔ ye naxan luma mini ra fɛɲɛ yale di kui, a mu a itima.

sentences.english: House and wealth are a heritage from fathers, but a wife with good sense is from the Lord.
sentences.susu: Mixi banxi nun harige sɔtɔma e baba kɛ ra, kɔnɔ Ala nan ginɛ xaxilima fima xɛmɛ ma.

sentences.english: Hate of work sends deep sleep on a man: and he who has no industry will go without food.
sentences.susu: Tunnaxɔnɛ mixi luma nɛ xixɔli kui, a kaamɛ nan tun sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: He who keeps the law keeps his soul; but death will be the fate of him who takes no note of the word.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatuma, a a yɛtɛ ratangama nɛ faxɛ ma, kɔnɔ naxan mu a ɲɛngi sama a ɲɛrɛ ki xɔn ma, a faxama nɛ.

sentences.english: He who has pity on the poor gives to the Lord, and the Lord will give him his reward.
sentences.susu: Setare kife na maniyaxi Alatala donife nan na. Ala fama nɛ na doni ragbilende a ma.

sentences.english: Give your son training while there is hope; let not your heart be purposing his death.
sentences.susu: I xa fe birin naba i xa di xurufe ra alako a xa kisi, xa na mu a ra, a faxama nɛ.

sentences.english: A man of great wrath will have to take his punishment: for if you get him out of trouble you will have to do it again.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan luma xɔnɔ ra, a na sare fima nɛ. Xa i a mali keren, a man gbilenma nɛ na ma.

sentences.english: Let your ear be open to suggestion and take teaching, so that at the end you may be wise.
sentences.susu: I xa i tuli mati marasi ra, i xa tin e xa i xaran, alako i xa findi xaxilima ra.

sentences.english: A man's heart may be full of designs, but the purpose of the Lord is unchanging.
sentences.susu: Maɲɔxun gbegbe na mixi bɔɲɛ kui, kɔnɔ Alatala waxɔnfe nan kamalima.

sentences.english: The ornament of a man is his mercy, and a poor man is better than one who is false.
sentences.susu: Adamadi wama a boore xa dugutɛgɛɲa a ma. Setare fisa wule falɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: The fear of the Lord gives life: and he who has it will have need of nothing; no evil will come his way.
sentences.susu: Alatala xa yaragaaxui mixi rakisima nɛ. Na mixi na a sa kɔɛ ra, a mu hanmɛma tɔɔrɛ yo ra.

sentences.english: The hater of work puts his hand deep into the basin, and will not even take it to his mouth again.
sentences.susu: Tunnaxɔnɛ a donse tongoma nɛ a bɛlɛxɛ, kɔnɔ a mu wakilima a rasofe ra a dɛ i.

sentences.english: When blows overtake the man of pride, the simple will get sense; say sharp words to the wise, and knowledge will be made clear to him.
sentences.susu: Mixi mayele bɔnbɔ, alako xaxilitare xa xaxili sɔtɔ. Xaxilima na rasi, alako a xaxili xun xa masa.

sentences.english: He who is violent to his father, driving away his mother, is a son causing shame and a bad name.
sentences.susu: Di naxan a baba kasarama, a a nga keri, mixi rayaagixi na a ra.

sentences.english: A son who no longer gives attention to teaching is turned away from the words of knowledge.
sentences.susu: N ma di, xa i mu marasi ramɛma, i bara i yɛtɛ makuya fe kolonyi ra.

sentences.english: A good-for-nothing witness makes sport of the judge's decision: and the mouth of evil-doers sends out evil like a stream.
sentences.susu: Seede wule falɛ yoma sɛriyɛ nan ma, tinxintareya nan minima mixi ɲaaxi dɛ i.

sentences.english: Rods are being made ready for the man of pride, and blows for the back of the foolish.
sentences.susu: Mixi mayele ɲaxankatama nɛ, lɔnnitare bɔnbɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: Wine makes men foolish, and strong drink makes men come to blows; and whoever comes into error through these is not wise.
sentences.susu: Wɛni mixi rayaagima, beere mixi madaxuma nɛ. Siisila mu nɔma findide xaxilima ra.

sentences.english: The wrath of a king is like the loud cry of a lion: he who makes him angry does wrong against himself.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ bɔɲɛ texi maniya yɛtɛ xaaɲɛ ra. Mixi naxan mangɛ raxɔnɔma, na bara a yɛtɛ tɔɔrɔ.

sentences.english: It is an honour for a man to keep from fighting, but the foolish are ever at war.
sentences.susu: Mixi binyaxi mu tinma gere ra, kɔnɔ xaxilitare birama sɔnxɔɛ nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: The hater of work will not do his ploughing because of the winter; so at the time of grain-cutting he will be requesting food and will get nothing.
sentences.susu: Mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi mu yire buxama a waxati. Xɛ xaba tɛmui a baloe fenma nɛ, kɔnɔ a mu sese toma.

sentences.english: The purpose in the heart of a man is like deep water, but a man of good sense will get it out.
sentences.susu: Marasi tilin alɔ ye naxan na baa ma. Fahaamui kanyi na birin matoma nɛ.

sentences.english: Most men make no secret of their kind acts: but where is a man of good faith to be seen?
sentences.susu: Mixi gbegbe dugutɛgɛɲa falama e yɛtɛ xun ma, kɔnɔ dugutɛgɛ yati yati toma duniɲa ma?

sentences.english: An upright man goes on in his righteousness: happy are his children after him!
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ ɲɛrɛma tinxinyi nan na, sɛɛwɛ na a xa die bɛ.

sentences.english: A king on the seat of judging puts to flight all evil with his eyes.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ kiitisa fata mixi bɔɲɛ ɲaaxi tode.

sentences.english: Who is able to say, I have made my heart clean, I am free from my sin?
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma a falade, «Fe ɲaaxi yo mu n bɔɲɛ ma, n sɛniyɛnxi, yunubi yo mu na n ma?»

sentences.english: Unequal weights and unequal measures, they are all disgusting to the Lord.
sentences.susu: Sikeeli tinxintare mu rafan Alatala ma.

sentences.english: Even a child may be judged by his doings, if his work is free from sin and if it is right.
sentences.susu: Fonike xa ɲɛrɛ ki tinxinxi a bɔɲɛ ki masenma nɛ.

sentences.english: The hearing ear and the seeing eye are equally the Lord's work.
sentences.susu: Tuli naxan fe mɛma, ya naxan se toma, Alatala nan na birin daaxi.

sentences.english: Do not be a lover of sleep, or you will become poor: keep your eyes open, and you will have bread enough.
sentences.susu: Xixɔli naxa rafan i ma de, xa na mu a ra i findima setare nan na. I ya lanma a xa rasɛgɛ, alako i xa baloe sɔtɔ a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: A poor thing, a poor thing, says he who is giving money for goods: but when he has gone on his way, then he makes clear his pride in what he has got.
sentences.susu: Sareso nan a falama yulɛ bɛ, «Na sare mu fan n bɛ feo,» kɔnɔ a fa keli na xun ma a yɛtɛ matɔxɔfe ra.

sentences.english: There is gold and a store of corals: but the lips of knowledge are a jewel of great price.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛma nun gɛmɛ tofanyi gbegbe na duniɲa, kɔnɔ lɔnnila xa wɔyɛnyi tide gbo e birin bɛ.

sentences.english: Take a man's clothing if he makes himself responsible for a strange man, and get an undertaking from him who gives his word for strange men.
sentences.susu: Mixi xa sɛɛkɛ se rasuxu a naxan taani xɔɲɛ bɛ, xa na mu a ra a naxan taani langoe bɛ.

sentences.english: Bread of deceit is sweet to a man; but after, his mouth will be full of sand.
sentences.susu: Donse naxan sɔtɔ wule ra, a fɔlɛ a ɲɔxun, kɔnɔ a raɲɔnyi a luxi nɛ alɔ gɛmɛ xɔri i dɛ i.

sentences.english: Every purpose is put into effect by wise help: and by wise guiding make war.
sentences.susu: Marasi fanyi nan wali sɔɔnɛyama. Ɲama naxa gere so marasi xanbi.

sentences.english: He who goes about talking of the business of others gives away secrets: so have nothing to do with him whose lips are open wide.
sentences.susu: Naafixi lanlanteya kanama nɛ. I naxa la mixi ra naxan dɛ wuya.

sentences.english: If anyone puts a curse on his father or his mother, his light will be put out in the blackest night.
sentences.susu: Mixi na yo a nga nun a baba ma, a duniɲa igirima dimi nan kui.

sentences.english: A heritage may be got quickly at first, but the end of it will not be a blessing.
sentences.susu: Harige naxan sɔtɔma mafurenyi ra, na mu buma.

sentences.english: Do not say, I will give punishment for evil: go on waiting for the Lord, and he will be your saviour.
sentences.susu: I naxa a fala, «N nan n gbeɲɔxɔma nɛ.» I xaxili ti Alatala nan na, a i rakisima nɛ.

sentences.english: Unequal weights are disgusting to the Lord, and false scales are not good.
sentences.susu: Alatala mu wama maniya se tinxintare xɔn ma. Sikeeli tinxintare mu fan.

sentences.english: A man's steps are of the Lord; how then may a man have knowledge of his way?
sentences.susu: Alatala nan adamadi xun tima kira nde ra. Ibunadama tan mu nɔma na fahaamude.

sentences.english: It is a danger to a man to say without thought, It is holy, and, after taking his oaths, to be questioning if it is necessary to keep them.
sentences.susu: Laayidi tongofe Ala bɛ mafuren mafuren maɲɔxunyi gbegbe xanbi, na findixi gantanyi nan na adamadi bɛ.

sentences.english: A wise king puts evil-doers to flight, and makes their evil-doing come back on them.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ lɔnnila fata mixi ɲaaxie mayegetide, a ti e fari a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: The Lord keeps watch over the spirit of man, searching all the deepest parts of the body.
sentences.susu: Alatala xaxili fima adamadi ma, a findi a bɛ lanpui ra, alako a xa a yɛtɛ bɔɲɛ mato a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: Mercy and good faith keep the king safe, and the seat of his power is based on upright acts.
sentences.susu: Xanunteya nun dugutɛgɛɲa mangɛ kantama nɛ. Mangɛ kibanyi sabatima nɛ mangɛ xa xanunteya saabui ra.

sentences.english: The glory of young men is their strength, and the honour of old men is their grey hairs.
sentences.susu: Fonike sɛnbɛ findixi a xa xunnakeli nan na. Xɛmɔxi xunsɛxɛ fiixɛ findixi a xa binyɛ nan na.

sentences.english: By the wounds of the rod evil is taken away, and blows make clean the deepest parts of the body.
sentences.susu: Bɔnbɔɛ findixi kobiɲa seri nan na, luxusinyi adama xaxili matinxinma nɛ.

sentences.english: The king's heart in the hands of the Lord is like the water streams, and by him it is turned in any direction at his pleasure.
sentences.susu: Alatala nan mangɛ bɔɲɛ raɲɛrɛma, alɔ a xure raɲɛrɛma ki naxɛ a waxɔnki ra.

sentences.english: Every way of a man seems right to himself, but the Lord is the tester of hearts.
sentences.susu: Adamadi ɲɔxɔ a ma a xa kira birin tinxin, kɔnɔ Alatala nan mixi bɔɲɛ matoma sikeeli ra.

sentences.english: To do what is right and true is more pleasing to the Lord than an offering.
sentences.susu: Wo xa bira nɔndi nun tinxinyi fɔxɔ ra. Na rafan Alatala ma dangife sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: A high look and a heart of pride, ***of the evil-doer is sin.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboɲa nun fe ɲaaxi rabafe, na birin findixi yunubi nan na.

sentences.english: The purposes of the man of industry have their outcome only in wealth; but one who is over-quick in acting will only come to be in need.
sentences.susu: Wakilila harige xun masama nɛ, kɔnɔ gbata gbegbe findima tɔɔrɛ nan na.

sentences.english: He who gets stores of wealth by a false tongue, is going after what is only breath, and searching for death.
sentences.susu: Harige naxan sɔtɔxi wule ra, a mu buma, a mixi xaninma nɛ aligiyama.

sentences.english: By their violent acts the evil-doers will be pulled away, because they have no desire to do what is right.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie xun nakanama nɛ, barima e mu tinxinyi rabatuma.

sentences.english: Twisted is the way of him who is full of crime; but as for him whose heart is clean, his work is upright.
sentences.susu: Mixi kobi mu tinxin, kɔnɔ mixi fanyi a ɲɛrɛma kira tinxinxi xɔn ma.

sentences.english: It is better to be living in an angle of the house-top, than with a bitter-tongued woman in a wide house.
sentences.susu: Lufe ra banxi fari ma, a fisa lufe ra ginɛ geresoe sɛɛti ma banxi kui.

sentences.english: The desire of the evil-doer is fixed on evil: he has no kind feeling for his neighbour.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi wama fe ɲaaxi nan tun xɔn ma. A mu kinikinima mixi yo ma, hali dɔxɔboore.

sentences.english: When the man of pride undergoes punishment, the simple man gets wisdom; and by watching the wise he gets knowledge.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare na a to e mixi mayele ɲaxankatama, a xaxili di sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ xaxilima tan fahaamui sɔtɔma lɔnni nan kui.

sentences.english: The Upright One, looking on the house of the evil-doer, lets sinners be overturned to their destruction.
sentences.susu: Ala naxan tinxin, a mixi ɲaaxi matoma nɛ, a e xun nakana.

sentences.english: He whose ears are stopped at the cry of the poor, will himself get no answer to his cry for help.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tondima a tuli matide setare wa xui ra, a fan fama nɛ wade, mixi mu a tuli matima a ra.

sentences.english: By a secret offering wrath is turned away, and the heat of angry feelings by money in the folds of the robe.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛte kife gundo ra, a bɔɲɛ ragoroma nɛ. Mixi kife suturɛ ra, a xa xɔnɛ magoroma nɛ.

sentences.english: It is a joy to the good man to do right, but it is destruction to the workers of evil.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛrɛfe tinxinyi kui, na findixi sɛɛwɛ nan na tinxintɔɛ bɛ, kɔnɔ na ɲɛrɛ ki mɔɔli mu rafan mixi ɲaaxi ma.

sentences.english: The wanderer from the way of knowledge will have his resting-place among the shades.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan gbilenma kira fanyi fɔxɔ ra, na fama nɛ lude mixi faxaxie ya ma.

sentences.english: The lover of pleasure will be a poor man: the lover of wine and oil will not get wealth.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan birama a waxɔnfe gbansan fɔxɔ ra, na luma nɛ setareɲa kui. Mixi naxan wɛni nun donse fanyi tun fenma, na mu bannama.

sentences.english: The evil-doer will be given as a price for the life of the good man, and the worker of deceit in the place of the upright.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi findima tinxintɔɛ xunsare nan na, yanfante findi mixi fanyi xunsare ra.

sentences.english: It is better to be living in a waste land, than with a bitter-tongued and angry woman.
sentences.susu: Lufe ra gbengberenyi ma, a fisa lufe ra ginɛ fitinɛtɔɛ sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: There is a store of great value in the house of the wise, but it is wasted by the foolish man.
sentences.susu: Harige fanyi nun ture gbegbe na lɔnnila xɔnyi, kɔnɔ lɔnnitare bara a gbe birin don.

sentences.english: He who goes after righteousness and mercy will get life, righteousness, and honour.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan birama tinxinyi nun hinnɛ fɔxɔ ra, a simaya, kiiti fanyi, nun binyɛ sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: A wise man goes up into the town of the strong ones, and overcomes its strength in which they put their faith.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila nɔma nɛ nɔde taa makantaxi ra, a e xa tɛtɛ rabira e xaxili nu tixi naxan na.

sentences.english: He who keeps watch over his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan fata a dɛ suxude, na mu tɔɔrɔ ma.

sentences.english: The man of pride, lifted up in soul, is named high-hearted; he is acting in an outburst of pride.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboe yoma nɛ mixie ma, a fe birin suxuma na xaxili nan na.

sentences.english: The desire of the hater of work is death to him, for his hands will do no work.
sentences.susu: Mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi waxɔnfe a faxama nɛ, barima a mu tinma walide.

sentences.english: All the day the sinner goes after his desire: but the upright man gives freely, keeping nothing back.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔɛ birin mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi milama nɛ a waxɔnse ma. Tinxintɔɛ tan mixi kima a gbe se birin nan na.

sentences.english: The offering of evil-doers is disgusting: how much more when they give it with an evil purpose!
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi xa sɛrɛxɛ mu rafan Ala ma. Xa a sa a ba maɲɔxunyi kobi ra, Alatala xa xɔnɛ xun masama nɛ.

sentences.english: A false witness will be cut off, ...
sentences.susu: Seede wule falɛ halakima nɛ, kɔnɔ seede nɔndi falɛ xa simaya nan buma.

sentences.english: The evil-doer makes his face hard, but as for the upright, he gives thought to his way.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi a yatagi ifɔɔrɔma, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ fe tinxinxi nan nabama.

sentences.english: Wisdom and knowledge and wise suggestions are of no use against the Lord.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni yo mu na, fahaamui yo mu na, marasi yo mu na, naxan sɛnbɛ gbo Alatala bɛ.

sentences.english: The horse is made ready for the day of war, but power to overcome is from the Lord.
sentences.susu: Soe maxirima gere so lɔxɔɛ nɛ, kɔnɔ xunnakeli fatanma Alatala nan na.

sentences.english: A good name is more to be desired than great wealth, and to be respected is better than silver and gold.
sentences.susu: Xili fanyi fan naafuli bɛ, binyɛ tide dangi xɛɛma nun gbeti tide ra.

sentences.english: The man of wealth and the poor man come face to face: the Lord is the maker of them all.
sentences.susu: Banna nun setare birin lan, barima Alatala nan e birin daa.

sentences.english: The sharp man sees the evil and takes cover: the simple go straight on and get into trouble.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima na fe xɔrɔxɔɛ to, a a yɛtɛ nan natangama a ma. Xaxilitare tan na fe xɔrɔxɔɛ to, a soma a kui nɛ keren na, a fa ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: The reward of a gentle spirit and the fear of the Lord is wealth and honour and life.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ magore naxan gaaxuma Alatala ya ra, a bannaya, binyɛ, nun simaya sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: Thorns and nets are in the way of the twisted: he who keeps watch over his soul will be far from them.
sentences.susu: Tunbee nun gantanyie na tinxintare xa kira xɔn ma, kɔnɔ mixi naxan mɛɛnima a yɛtɛ ma, a a makuyama nɛ mɛnni ra.

sentences.english: If a child is trained up in the right way, even when he is old he will not be turned away from it.
sentences.susu: Fonike matinxin kira fanyi ra, alako a naxa gbilen na fɔxɔ ra a mɔ tɛmui.

sentences.english: The man of wealth has rule over the poor, and he who gets into debt is a servant to his creditor.
sentences.susu: Banna setare yamarima nɛ, doni tongoe fan findi donifa xa konyi ra.

sentences.english: By planting the seed of evil a man will get in the grain of sorrow, and the rod of his wrath will be broken.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi tɔɔrɛ nan sɔtɔma a sare ra, a sɛnbɛ fama nɛ kanade.

sentences.english: He who is kind will have a blessing, for he gives of his bread to the poor.
sentences.susu: Hinnɛnte barakama nɛ, barima a tɔɔrɔmixie kima a xa donse ra.

sentences.english: Send away the man of pride, and argument will go out; truly fighting and shame will come to an end.
sentences.susu: Mixi mayoe keri, alako ɲɔxɔnsɔsɔɛ xa ɲɔn. Na tɛmui gbɛsɛnxɔnnɛya nun konbie danma nɛ.

sentences.english: He whose heart is clean is dear to the Lord; for the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛ xa sɛniyɛnyi rafan mixi naxan ma, wɔyɛn fanyie nan minima na dɛ i, a fa findi mangɛ dɛfanboore ra.

sentences.english: The eyes of the Lord keep knowledge, but by him the acts of the false man will be overturned.
sentences.susu: Alatala nɔndi nan makantama, kɔnɔ a yanfante xa wɔyɛnyi xun nakanama nɛ.

sentences.english: The hater of work says, There is a lion outside: I will be put to death in the streets.
sentences.susu: Mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi nan a falama, «Yɛtɛ xaaɲɛxi na tande, n na mini kɛnɛ ma, a n faxama nɛ.»

sentences.english: The mouth of strange women is a deep hole: he with whom the Lord is angry will go down into it.
sentences.susu: Gantanyi nan na langoe ginɛ xa wɔyɛnyi ra. Alatala xɔnɔxi mixi naxan ma, na suxuma na gantanyi kui.

sentences.english: Foolish ways are deep-seated in the heart of a child, but the rod of punishment will send them far from him.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitareɲa naxan na dimɛdi bɔɲɛ kui, a bama xuru luxusinyi nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: He who is cruel to the poor for the purpose of increasing his profit, and he who gives to the man of wealth, will only come to be in need.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan setare tɔɔrɔma geeni nde xa fe ra, nun mixi naxan banna kima, na firinyi findima fuxarila nan na.

sentences.english: Let your ear be bent down for hearing my words, and let your heart give thought to knowledge.
sentences.susu: I i tuli mati lɔnnilae xa marasi ra, i bɔɲɛ rabi n ma masenyie bɛ.

sentences.english: For it is a delight to keep them in your heart, to have them ready on your lips.
sentences.susu: A lan i xa e ragata i sondonyi kui, e naxa makuya i dɛ ra.

sentences.english: So that your faith may be in the Lord, I have made them clear to you this day, even to you.
sentences.susu: N wama i rasife nɛ to lɔxɔɛ, alako i xa i yɛtɛ taxu Alatala ra.

sentences.english: Have I not put in writing for you thirty sayings, with wise suggestions and knowledge,
sentences.susu: N bara taali tongo saxan sɛbɛ i ma, naxee findixi marasi nun lɔnni ra i bɛ,

sentences.english: To make you see how certain are true words, so that you may give a true answer to those who put questions to you?
sentences.susu: alako i xa nɔndi xɔri yati kolon, i fan xa sa na iba i xɛɛma bɛ.

sentences.english: Do not take away the property of the poor man because he is poor, or be cruel to the crushed ones when they come before the judge:
sentences.susu: I naxa setare rahalaki i xa kɔbiri sɔtɔ, i naxa tɔɔrɔmixi tɔɔɲɛgɛ,

sentences.english: For the Lord will give support to their cause, and take the life of those who take their goods.
sentences.susu: barima Alatala tan e xun mafalama nɛ, a fa tɔɔrɔmixie yaxuie tɔɔrɔ.

sentences.english: Do not be friends with a man who is given to wrath; do not go in the company of an angry man:
sentences.susu: I naxa bira mixi bɔɲɛ gbe fɔxɔ ra, naxan xɔnɔxi tɛmui birin,

sentences.english: For fear of learning his ways and making a net ready for your soul.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra i fan darima nɛ na mɔɔli ra, na fa findi gantanyi ra i suxuma naxan na.

sentences.english: Be not one of those who give their hands in an agreement, or of those who make themselves responsible for debts:
sentences.susu: I naxa lu mixie ya ma naxee taanima e booree bɛ, naxee se dɔxɔma sɛɛkɛ ra mixie bɛ,

sentences.english: If you have nothing with which to make payment, he will take away your bed from under you.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra e i xa sade raminima nɛ i bun ma, a fa li kɔbiri mu na i yi ra i xa a fi.

sentences.english: Let not the old landmark be moved which your fathers have put in place.
sentences.susu: I naxa i babae xa naaninyi matɔnxuma saxi ba e yire de.

sentences.english: Have you seen a man who is expert in his business? he will take his place before kings; his place will not be among low persons.
sentences.susu: Walikɛ naxan fata a xa wali ra, mangɛe nan hayi luma a ma. A mu walima setaree bɛ.

sentences.english: When you take your seat at the feast with a ruler, give thought with care to what is before you;
sentences.susu: Wo nun kuntigi na dɔxɔ wo dɛgede, i xa i ɲɛngi sa i raba ki xɔn ma de.

sentences.english: And put a knife to your throat, if you have a strong desire for food.
sentences.susu: Xa kaamɛ na i ma, i naxa a gbegbe don.

sentences.english: Have no desire for his delicate food, for it is the bread of deceit.
sentences.susu: I naxa milɛ na donse fanyi ma, barima a nɔma i madaxude.

sentences.english: Take no care to get wealth; let there be an end to your desire for money.
sentences.susu: I naxa i yɛtɛ ratagan naafuli fenfe ma. Kɔbiri xɔli naxa findi i xaxili waxɔnfe birin na.

sentences.english: Are your eyes lifted up to it? it is gone: for wealth takes to itself wings, like an eagle in flight up to heaven.
sentences.susu: Xa i i ya ti bannaya ra, a lɔɛma i ma alɔ sɛgɛ naxan tema kuye ma ki naxɛ, a siga.

sentences.english: Do not take the food of him who has an evil eye, or have any desire for his delicate meat:
sentences.susu: I naxa mixi ɲaaxi xa taami don, i naxa mila a xa donse fanyi ma.

sentences.english: For as the thoughts of his heart are, so is he: Take food and drink, he says to you; but his heart is not with you.
sentences.susu: Na mixi mɔɔli wama i madaxufe nɛ. A a falama i bɛ, «I dɛge, i min,» kɔnɔ marafanyi yo mu na a bɔɲɛ kui i bɛ.

sentences.english: The food which you have taken will come up again, and your pleasing words will be wasted.
sentences.susu: I fama nɛ na donse bɔxunde, i xa wɔyɛn fanyi findi wɔyɛn fufafu ra.

sentences.english: Say nothing in the hearing of a foolish man, for he will put no value on the wisdom of your words.
sentences.susu: I naxa masenyi ti xaxilitare bɛ, barima a yoma nɛ i xa wɔyɛn fanyi birin ma.

sentences.english: Do not let the landmark of the widow be moved, and do not go into the fields of those who have no father;
sentences.susu: I naxa naaninyi tɔnxuma fori tala. I naxa so kiridie xa xɛ ra,

sentences.english: For their saviour is strong, and he will take up their cause against you.
sentences.susu: barima e xunmafalama sɛnbɛ gbo, a e gbeɲɔxɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: Give your heart to teaching, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
sentences.susu: I bɔɲɛ rabi xaranyi bɛ, i i tuli mati marasi fanyi ra.

sentences.english: Do not keep back training from the child: for even if you give him blows with the rod, it will not be death to him.
sentences.susu: I naxa tagan fonike matinxinde, xuru luxusinyi mu a faxama.

sentences.english: Give him blows with the rod, and keep his soul safe from the underworld.
sentences.susu: Xa i a xuru luxusinyi ra, i bara a nii makanta.

sentences.english: My son, if your heart becomes wise, I, even I, will be glad in heart;
sentences.susu: N ma di, xa lɔnni fanyi lu i bɔɲɛ kui, sɛɛwɛ bara lu n tan fan bɔɲɛ kui.

sentences.english: And my thoughts in me will be full of joy when your lips say right things.
sentences.susu: N bɔɲɛ ɲɛlɛxinma nɛ i xa wɔyɛn tinxinxie ra.

sentences.english: Have no envy of sinners in your heart, but keep in the fear of the Lord all through the day;
sentences.susu: I naxa yunubitɔɛe tɔɔnɛ, i xa gaaxu Alatala nan ya ra,

sentences.english: For without doubt there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
sentences.susu: alako i xa xunnakeli sɔtɔ yare.

sentences.english: Give ear, my son, and be wise, guiding your heart in the right way.
sentences.susu: N ma di, i tuli mati a fanyi ra, i xa xaxili sɔtɔ, i bɔɲɛ xa lu kira tinxinxi fari.

sentences.english: Do not be among those who give themselves to wine-drinking, or among those who make themselves full with meat:
sentences.susu: I naxa lu siisilae ya ma, xa na mu a ra naxee xa donse xɔli dangi a i.

sentences.english: For those who take delight in drink and feasting will come to be in need; and through love of sleep a man will be poorly clothed.
sentences.susu: Na mixi mɔɔlie findima nɛ setaree ra, e xa tunnaxɔnɛya a niyama nɛ dunkobi gbansan nagoro e ma.

sentences.english: Give ear to your father whose child you are, and do not keep honour from your mother when she is old.
sentences.susu: I i tuli mati i baba ra naxan i barixi, i naxa yo i nga ma a na fori.

sentences.english: Get for yourself that which is true, and do not let it go for money; get wisdom and teaching and good sense.
sentences.susu: Nɔndi, lɔnni, xaranyi, nun xaxili fanyi fen, i naxa mɛɛ e ra.

sentences.english: The father of the upright man will be glad, and he who has a wise child will have joy because of him.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ baba sɛɛwama nɛ, xaxilima baba ɲɛlɛxinma nɛ.

sentences.english: Let your father and your mother be glad, let her who gave you birth have joy.
sentences.susu: I xa fe birin naba alako i baba nun i nga xa sɛɛwa, i bari mixie xa lu ɲɛlɛxinyi kui.

sentences.english: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes take delight in my ways.
sentences.susu: N ma di, i i bɔɲɛ rabi n bɛ, i xa i ya ti n ɲɛrɛ ki misaali ra.

sentences.english: For a loose woman is a deep hollow, and a strange woman is a narrow water-hole.
sentences.susu: Langoe ginɛ findixi gantanyi nan na, ginɛ yɛnɛxi i rabirama nɛ.

sentences.english: Yes, she is waiting secretly like a beast for its food, and deceit by her is increased among men.
sentences.susu: Na ginɛ mɔɔli i yanfama nɛ alɔ muɲɛti, a a niyama nɛ xɛmɛ gbegbe xa findi yanfantee ra.

sentences.english: Who says, Oh! who says, Ah! who has violent arguments, who has grief, who has wounds without cause, whose eyes are dark?
sentences.susu: Nde tɔɔrɛ nun nimisɛ sɔtɔma? Nde luma gere nun kalamui ya ma? Nde bɔnbɔɛ fufafu sɔtɔma? Nde ya gbeelima nɛ soe?

sentences.english: Those who are seated late over the wine: those who go looking for mixed wine.
sentences.susu: Siisilae nan luma na mɔɔli sɔtɔfe ra, beere mɔɔli birin ɲɔxunxi naxee bɛ.

sentences.english: Keep your eyes from looking on the wine when it is red, when its colour is bright in the cup, when it goes smoothly down:
sentences.susu: I naxa i ya ti wɛni gbeeli ra, naxan min mu xɔnɔ.

sentences.english: In the end, its bite is like that of a snake, its wound like the wound of a poison-snake.
sentences.susu: A mixi xinma nɛ alɔ bɔximase, a i bun alɔ tali.

sentences.english: Your eyes will see strange things, and you will say twisted things.
sentences.susu: I yae see toma naxee mu na duniɲa, i xaxili ifuma nɛ.

sentences.english: Yes, you will be like him who takes his rest on the sea, or on the top of a sail-support.
sentences.susu: I luma nɛ fa alɔ xɛmɛ naxan saxi kunkui kui baa mɔrɔnyie fari.

sentences.english: They have overcome me, you will say, and I have no pain; they gave me blows without my feeling them: when will I be awake from my wine? I will go after it again.
sentences.susu: Siisila nan a falama, «E bara n bɔnbɔ, kɔnɔ sese mu n toxi. N xunuma mun tɛmui? N man wama beere nde xɔn.»

sentences.english: Have no envy for evil men, or any desire to be with them:
sentences.susu: I naxa mila mixi ɲaaxie ma, i naxa tin lufe e ya ma.

sentences.english: For the purposes of their hearts are destruction, and their lips are talking of trouble.
sentences.susu: E bɔɲɛ kobi, e xa wɔyɛnyi xɔrɔxɔ.
