sentences.english: The building of a house is by wisdom, and by reason it is made strong:
sentences.susu: Lɔnni banxi tima nɛ, xaxili fanyi denbaya rasabati a kui.

sentences.english: And by knowledge its rooms are full of all dear and pleasing things.
sentences.susu: Fe kolonyi a niyama nɛ e xa harige sɔtɔ, harige hagigɛ naxan maniyɛ mu na.

sentences.english: A wise man is strong; and a man of knowledge makes strength greater.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila sɛnbɛ gbo, xaxilima sɛnbɛ xun masama nɛ.

sentences.english: For by wise guiding you will overcome in war: and in a number of wise guides there is salvation.
sentences.susu: I hayi na marasima alako fe xa sɔɔnɛya, xunnakeli sɔtɔma marasimae nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: Wisdom is outside the power of the foolish: he keeps his mouth shut in the public place.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni xɔrɔxɔ xaxilitare bɛ, wɔyɛnyi yo mu na a naxan falama malanyi kui.

sentences.english: He whose purposes are bad will be named a man of evil designs.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan fe ɲaaxi xabuma, a xili nɛ kɔɔta ɲaaxi xabui.

sentences.english: The purpose of the foolish is sin: and the hater of authority is disgusting to others.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitareɲa findixi yunubi nan na. Adamadie mixi mayele xɔnma.

sentences.english: If you give way in the day of trouble, your strength is small.
sentences.susu: Xa limaniya bama i yi ra tɔɔrɛ kui, i sɛnbɛ mu gbo.

sentences.english: Be the saviour of those who are given up to death, and do not keep back help from those who are slipping to destruction.
sentences.susu: Mixie ratanga naxee na saya kira xɔn ma, e ba mixie yi ra naxee wama e faxafe.

sentences.english: If you say, See, we had no knowledge of this: does not the tester of hearts give thought to it? and he who keeps your soul, has he no knowledge of it? and will he not give to every man the reward of his work?
sentences.susu: Xa i a falama, «Muxu mu nu a kolon,» naxan bɔɲɛe ma fe kolon, a mu na toma? Naxan ɲɛngi saxi i xa simaya xɔn ma, na mu i furi ife kolon? A mu kankan sare ragbilenma a ma xɛ?

sentences.english: My son, take honey, for it is good; and the flowing honey, which is sweet to your taste:
sentences.susu: N ma di, kumi nde don, barima se ɲɔxunmɛ nan a ra, a fan i fate bɛ.

sentences.english: So let your desire be for wisdom: if you have it, there will be a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i xa a kolon xaxili luma nɛ alɔ kumi. Xa i a sɔtɔ, i xunnakeli lima nɛ yare, i xaxili tima naxan na, na mu kanama.

sentences.english: Do not keep a secret watch, O evil-doer, against the fields of the upright man, or send destruction on his resting-place:
sentences.susu: I naxa gantanyi itala tinxintɔɛ bɛ, i naxa a xɔnyi kana.

sentences.english: For an upright man, after falling seven times, will get up again: but trouble is the downfall of the evil.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ nɔma birade sanmaya solofere, a man keli. Kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxi birama nɛ tɔɔrɛ kui kerenyi ra.

sentences.english: Do not be glad at the fall of your hater, and let not your heart have joy at his downfall:
sentences.susu: I naxa ɲɛlɛxin i yaxui xa birɛ ra, i bɔɲɛ naxa rafan i ma i na a to tɔɔrɔ ra,

sentences.english: For fear that the Lord may see it, and it may be evil in his eyes, and his wrath may be turned away from him.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra Alatala i xa maɲɔxunyi kobi toma nɛ, a fa a xa xɔnɛ ragbilen i yaxui fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Do not be troubled because of evil-doers, or have envy of sinners:
sentences.susu: I naxa xɔnɔ fe ɲaaxi rabae ma, i naxa e tɔɔnɛ.

sentences.english: For there will be no future for the evil man; the light of sinners will be put out.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi mu fe fanyi lima yare, e xa lanpui fama nɛ xubende.

sentences.english: My son, go in fear of the Lord and the king: have nothing to do with those who are in high positions:
sentences.susu: N ma di, i xa gaaxu Alatala ya ra, i xa mangɛe binya, i naxa lu matandilae ya ma,

sentences.english: For their downfall will come suddenly; and who has knowledge of the destruction of those in high positions?
sentences.susu: barima halaki nan fama e ratɛrɛnnade. Nde a kolon Ala halaki naxan dusuma e xun na?

sentences.english: These are more sayings of the wise: To have respect for a person's position when judging is not good.
sentences.susu: Lɔnnila gbɛtɛe xa taalie nan ya: Wo naxa mixi rafisa a boore bɛ kiiti kui.

sentences.english: He who says to the evil-doer, You are upright, will be cursed by peoples and hated by nations.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a falama mixi ɲaaxi bɛ, «I tinxin,» ɲama birin fama nɛ na kanyi dankade, si birin xɔnɔma nɛ a ma.

sentences.english: But those who say sharp words to him will have delight, and a blessing of good will come on them.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan mixi ɲaaxi kalamuma nɔndi kui, na kanyi bara fe fanyi raba, a fama nɛ barakɛ sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: He gives a kiss with his lips who gives a right answer.
sentences.susu: Yaabi tinxinxi ɲɔxun nɛ alɔ xanuntenyi xa xɛɛbui.

sentences.english: Put your work in order outside, and make it ready in the field; and after that, see to the building of your house.
sentences.susu: Fɛntɛn i xa wali ma, i fe raba baloe sɔtɔfe ra, na tɛmui i fa denbaya rasabati.

sentences.english: Do not be a violent witness against your neighbour, or let your lips say what is false.
sentences.susu: I naxa i dɔxɔboore tɔɔɲɛgɛ. Wule naxa mini i dɛ kui.

sentences.english: Say not, I will do to him as he has done to me; I will give the man the reward of his work.
sentences.susu: I naxa a fala, «A naxan nabaxi n na, fo n fan na raba a ra, n a xa wali kobi sare ragbilenma nɛ a ma.»

sentences.english: I went by the field of the hater of work, and by the vine-garden of the man without sense;
sentences.susu: N bara dangi tunnaxɔnɛ nde xa xɛ ra, a nun xaxilitare nde xa sansi yire ra.

sentences.english: And it was all full of thorns, and covered with waste plants, and its stone wall was broken down.
sentences.susu: N tunbee nun ɲooge ɲaaxie nan tun to naa. Tɛtɛ fan nu biraxi.

sentences.english: Then looking at it, I gave thought: I saw, and I got teaching from it.
sentences.susu: N naxa na fe maɲɔxun han a naxa findi xaxili ra n bɛ:

sentences.english: A little sleep, a little rest, a little folding of the hands in sleep:
sentences.susu: Xixɔli na i suxu, i kinsɔn fɔlɔ, i i bɛlɛxɛe findigilin i ma,

sentences.english: So loss will come on you like an outlaw, and your need like an armed man.
sentences.susu: setareɲa fa dutun i ma alɔ muɲɛti ɲaaxi.

sentences.english: These are more wise sayings of Solomon, copied out by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
sentences.susu: Sulemani xa taali ndee nan ya, Yuda Mangɛ Xesekiya naxee sɛbɛ:

sentences.english: It is the glory of God to keep a thing secret: but the glory of kings is to have it searched out.
sentences.susu: Ala fee nɔxunma, mangɛe katama e fahaamude.

sentences.english: The heaven is high and the earth is deep, and the hearts of kings may not be searched out.
sentences.susu: Koore xa maiteya nun bɔxi xa tilinyi mu kolonma. Mangɛ sondon ma fe fan mu nɔma kolonde.

sentences.english: Take away the waste from silver, and a vessel will come out for the silver-worker.
sentences.susu: Xa gbeti gbi ba, a nɔma findide se tofanyi ra.

sentences.english: Take away evil-doers from before the king, and the seat of his power will be made strong in righteousness.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi ɲaaxi ba mangɛ rabilinyi, a xa mangɛya sabatima nɛ tinxinyi saabui ra.

sentences.english: Do not take glory for yourself before the king, and do not put yourself in the place of the great:
sentences.susu: I naxa i yɛtɛ igbo mangɛ ya xɔri, i naxa i yɛtɛ findi mixi xungbe ra.

sentences.english: For it is better to have it said to you, Come up here; than for you to be put down in a lower place before the ruler.
sentences.susu: A fisa kuntigi nan xa i xili i xa dɔxɔ yire nde, dinɛ a xa i rakeli mixi xungbe nde bɛ.

sentences.english: Do not be quick to go to law about what you have seen, for what will you do in the end, when your neighbour has put you to shame?
sentences.susu: I na fe nde to, i naxa gbata sigafe ra kiiti banxi, barima xa fe gbɛtɛ minima i mu naxan kolon, na nɔma i rayaagide i dɔxɔboore ya xɔri.

sentences.english: Have a talk with your neighbour himself about your cause, but do not give away the secret of another:
sentences.susu: Fe na so wo nun i dɔxɔboore tagi, i naxa mixi gbɛtɛ xa gundo makɛnɛn,

sentences.english: Or your hearer may say evil of you, and your shame will not be turned away.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra mixi nde na na kolon, a i rayaagima nɛ, i fa xili kanɛ sɔtɔ abadan.

sentences.english: A word at the right time is like apples of gold in a network of silver.
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛnyi falaxi a ki ma, a tofan alɔ xɛɛma nun gbeti.

sentences.english: Like a nose-ring of gold and an ornament of the best gold, is a wise man who says sharp words to an ear ready to give attention.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa marasi tide gbo xaxili fenyi bɛ, alɔ xurundɛ naxan yailanxi xɛɛma fanyi ra.

sentences.english: As the cold of snow in the time of grain-cutting, so is a true servant to those who send him; for he gives new life to the soul of his master.
sentences.susu: Dugutɛgɛ xɛɛra ɲɔxun a xɛɛma bɛ, alɔ foye fanyi naxan fama walikɛe ma xɛ xaba tɛmui.

sentences.english: As clouds and wind without rain, so is one who takes credit for an offering he has not given.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a falama a setaree kima, kɔnɔ a mu a rabama, na kanyi luxi nɛ alɔ nuxui nun foye naxan mu fama ye ra.

sentences.english: A judge is moved by one who for a long time undergoes wrongs without protest, and by a soft tongue even bone is broken.
sentences.susu: Tunnabɛxiya a niyama nɛ mangɛ xa natɛ masara, wɔyɛn ɲɔxunmɛ sɛnbɛ gbo han a nɔma xɔri ragirade.

sentences.english: If you have honey, take only as much as is enough for you; for fear that, being full of it, you may not be able to keep it down.
sentences.susu: I na kumi to, naxan i ralima, na nan kɔn. Xa a radangi yɛ, i a bɔxunma nɛ.

sentences.english: Let not your foot be frequently in your neighbour's house, or he may get tired of you, and his feeling be turned to hate.
sentences.susu: I naxa i dɔxɔboore xɔnyi sigafe radigan, xa na mu a ra i xa fe fama nɛ raɲaaxude a ma.

sentences.english: One who gives false witness against his neighbour is a hammer and a sword and a sharp arrow.
sentences.susu: I dɔxɔboore tɔɔɲɛgɛfe xɔnɔ alɔ santidɛgɛma xaaɲɛxi, alɔ tanbɛ rameluxi.

sentences.english: Putting one's faith in a false man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth and a shaking foot.
sentences.susu: I xaxili tife yanfante ra, na luxi nɛ alɔ ɲinyi kanaxi, alɔ sanyi mabɛnxi.

sentences.english: Like one who takes off clothing in cold weather and like acid on a wound, is he who makes melody to a sad heart.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan sigi sama mixi sunnunxi ya xɔri, na maniya mixi ra naxan xinbeli dugi bama furema ma xinbeli tɛmui. A xa sunnunyi xun nan tun masama alɔ mixi na gbɛngbɛ sa fi ya i.

sentences.english: If your hater is in need of food, give him bread; and if he is in need of drink, give him water:
sentences.susu: Xa kaamɛ na i yaxui ma, donse so a yi ra. Xa ye xɔli na a ma, ye so a yi ra, a xa a min.

sentences.english: For so you will put coals of fire on his head, and the Lord will give you your reward.
sentences.susu: Xa i na wali mɔɔli raba a bɛ, na luxi nɛ alɔ i bara tɛ wole dɔxɔ a xun ma. Alatala nan i gbeɲɔxɔma.

sentences.english: As the north wind gives birth to rain, so is an angry face caused by a tongue saying evil secretly.
sentences.susu: Foye naxan kelima kɔɔla ma, na fama nɛ tunɛ ra. Nɛnyi naxan naafixiya falama, na mixi yatagi i xɔnɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: It is better to be living in an angle of the house-top, than with a bitter-tongued woman in a wide house.
sentences.susu: Lufe ra banxi fari ma, na fisa lufe ra ginɛ fitinɛtɔɛ sɛɛti ma banxi kui.

sentences.english: As cold water to a tired soul, so is good news from a far country.
sentences.susu: Xibaaru fanyi naxan kelixi yire makuye, a maniya ye xinbeli ra mixi taganxi bɛ.

sentences.english: Like a troubled fountain and a dirty spring, is an upright man who has to give way before evil-doers.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ naxan natɛ tongoma, a xa bira mixi ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra, na maniyaxi ye dulonyi nan na naxan bara dunda, a ye mu fan sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: It is not good to take much honey: so he who is not looking for honour will be honoured.
sentences.susu: Kumi donfe a radangi a i, na mu fan. Binyɛ fenfe i yɛtɛ ra, na fan mu fan.

sentences.english: He whose spirit is uncontrolled is like an unwalled town which has been broken into.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan mu nɔma a yɛtɛ raxande a na xɔnɔ, na luxi nɛ alɔ taa kanaxi naxan tɛtɛ bara bira.

sentences.english: Like snow in summer and rain when the grain is being cut, so honour is not natural for the foolish.
sentences.susu: Kuye mu xinbelima sogofure ra, tunɛ mu fama maale xaba tɛmui, na ki a mu lan lɔnnitare xa binyɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: As the sparrow in her wandering and the swallow in her flight, so the curse does not come without a cause.
sentences.susu: Dankɛ mu mixi fanyi suxuma. Na fe luma nɛ alɔ xɔni naxan mu dɔxɔma, koyinma xa a gɔnɔ.

sentences.english: A whip for the horse, a mouth-bit for the ass, and a rod for the back of the foolish.
sentences.susu: Soe bɔnbɔma nɛ alako a xa a gi, karafoe rasoma nɛ sofale dɛ i alako mixi xa a raɲɛrɛ, xaxilitare fan xuruma nɛ wuri ra alako a xa matinxin.

sentences.english: Do not give to the foolish man a foolish answer, or you will be like him.
sentences.susu: I naxa xaxilitare yaabi a maɲɔxun ki ra, xa na mu a ra wo birin lan.

sentences.english: Give a foolish man a foolish answer, or he will seem wise to himself.
sentences.susu: I xa xaxilitare yaabi a maɲɔxun ki ma, xa na mu a ra a a yɛtɛ findima xaxilima nan na.

sentences.english: He who sends news by the hand of a foolish man is cutting off his feet and drinking in damage.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan xaxilitare xɛɛma masenyi nde tide, na bara a yɛtɛ tɔɔrɔ.

sentences.english: The legs of one who has no power of walking are hanging loose; so is a wise saying in the mouth of the foolish.
sentences.susu: Taali wɔyɛnyi naxan minima xaxilitare dɛ i, na luxi nɛ alɔ mabɛnyi sanyi naxan sɛnbɛ mu na.

sentences.english: Giving honour to a foolish man is like attempting to keep a stone fixed in a cord.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare binyafe luxi nɛ alɔ gɛmɛ safe laati kui.

sentences.english: Like a thorn which goes up into the hand of a man overcome by drink, so is a wise saying in the mouth of a foolish man.
sentences.susu: Taali wɔyɛnyi naxan minima xaxilitare dɛ i, na luxi nɛ alɔ luxusinyi naxan na siisila bɛlɛxɛ i.

sentences.english: Like an archer wounding all who go by, is a foolish man overcome by drink.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan wali soma xaxilitare yi ra, xa na mu a ra mixi yi ra a mu naxan kolon, na luxi nɛ alɔ sɔɔri naxan tanbɛ wolima ɲama mabiri.

sentences.english: Like a dog going back to the food which he has not been able to keep down, is the foolish man doing his foolish acts over again.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare naxan gbilenma a xa daxuɲa ma, na luxi nɛ alɔ bare naxan gbilenma a xa bɔxunyi don na.

sentences.english: Have you seen a man who seems to himself to be wise? There is more hope for the foolish than for him.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare fan fisa mixi bɛ naxan a yɛtɛ findixi lɔnnila ra. Fe sɔɔnɛyama nɛ na xaxilitare bɛ dangife na yɛtɛ igboe ra.

sentences.english: The hater of work says, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.
sentences.susu: Mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi nan a falama, «Yɛtɛ na kira ra, yɛtɛ na taa kui.»

sentences.english: A door is turned on its pillar, and the hater of work on his bed.
sentences.susu: Naadɛ rabima, a man nagalima, alɔ tunnaxɔnɛ naxan a ya rabima a xa sade ma, a man xi.

sentences.english: The hater of work puts his hand deep into the basin: lifting it again to his mouth is a weariness to him.
sentences.susu: Mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi a donse suxuma a bɛlɛxɛ ra, kɔnɔ a mu a rasoma a dɛ i tunnaxɔnɔya saabui ra.

sentences.english: The hater of work seems to himself wiser than seven men who are able to give an answer with good sense.
sentences.susu: Mixi tunnaxɔnɔxi a yɛtɛ rafisa xaxilima solofere bɛ naxee yaabi fima xaxilimaya ra.

sentences.english: He who gets mixed up in a fight which is not his business, is like one who takes a dog by the ears while it is going by.
sentences.susu: Dangi mixi naxan a yɛtɛ rasoma gere kui naxan mu a matoxi, na maniya mixi ra naxan bare suxuma a tulie ma.

sentences.english: As one who is off his head sends about flaming sticks and arrows of death,
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a boore madaxu, a fa a fala, «Bere nan nu a ra,» na maniya daxui ra naxan tɛ maxirima tanbɛ ma, a a woli.

sentences.english: So is the man who gets the better of his neighbour by deceit, and says, Am I not doing so in sport?
sentences.susu: <range>

sentences.english: Without wood, the fire goes out; and where there is no secret talk, argument is ended.
sentences.susu: Xa yege mu na, tɛ xubenma nɛ. Xa mixi keren a sabari, sɔnxɔɛ danma nɛ.

sentences.english: Like breath on coals and wood on fire, so a man given to argument gets a fight started.
sentences.susu: Tige findima nɛ tɛ wole ra, yege findi tɛ ra. Sɔnxɔla fan gere rabirama na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: The words of one who says evil of his neighbour secretly are like sweet food, they go down into the inner parts of the stomach.
sentences.susu: Naafixi xa masenyi luxi nɛ alɔ donse ɲɔxunmɛ, naxan goroma mixi furi kui.

sentences.english: Smooth lips and an evil heart are like a vessel of earth plated with silver waste.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi naxan wɔyɛn ɲɔxunmɛ falama, na luxi nɛ alɔ biriki to ɲaaxie se fiixɛ masoma naxee ma.

sentences.english: With his lips the hater makes things seem what they are not, but deceit is stored up inside him;
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi a boore madaxuma wɔyɛn ɲɔxunmɛ ra, kɔnɔ yanfanteya na a bɔɲɛ kui.

sentences.english: When he says fair words, have no belief in him; for in his heart are seven evils:
sentences.susu: Hali a wɔyɛnyi ɲɔxun, i naxa la a ra de, barima kobiɲa na a sondonyi kui.

sentences.english: Though his hate is covered with deceit, his sin will be seen openly before the meeting of the people.
sentences.susu: A xa xɔnnanteya nɔxunxi a xa mayendenyi saabui ra, kɔnɔ a xa kobiɲa fama nɛ minide kɛnɛ ma mixie tagi.

sentences.english: He who makes a hole in the earth will himself go falling into it: and on him by whom a stone is rolled the stone will come back again.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan yili gema gantanyi ra, a tan nan fama birade a kui. Mixi naxan gɛmɛ wolima, na gɛmɛ gbilenma a tan nan ma.

sentences.english: A false tongue has hate for those who have clean hearts, and a smooth mouth is a cause of falling.
sentences.susu: Wule falɛ tɔɔɲɛgɛtɔɛ nan xɔnma, Mixi naxan a boore matɔxɔma wule ra, na kasarɛ nan tun nabama.

sentences.english: Do not make a noise about tomorrow, for you are not certain what a day's outcome may be.
sentences.susu: I naxa i yɛtɛ matɔxɔ tina xa fe ra, barima i mu a kolon naxan fama rabade.

sentences.english: Let another man give you praise, and not your mouth; one who is strange to you, and not your lips.
sentences.susu: I naxa i yɛtɛ matɔxɔ, a lu mixi gbɛtɛ nan xa i matɔxɔ. Mixi gbɛtɛ xa matɔxɔɛ fisa i yɛtɛ xa matɔxɔɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: A stone has great weight, and sand is crushing; but the wrath of the foolish is of greater weight than these.
sentences.susu: Kote nan gɛmɛ ra, mɛyɛnyi fan binya, kɔnɔ xaxilitare xa gbɛsɛnxɔnnɛya xɔrɔxɔ a birin bɛ.

sentences.english: Wrath is cruel, and angry feeling an overflowing stream; but who does not give way before envy?
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛ xa te xɔrɔxɔ, xɔnɛ fan magaaxu, kɔnɔ nde nɔma tide tɔɔnɛ tan ya ra?

sentences.english: Better is open protest than love kept secret.
sentences.susu: Marakɔrɔsi raminife kɛnɛ ma mixi xa tantanyi xa fe ra, na fisa marakɔrɔsi nɔxunfe marafanyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: The wounds of a friend are given in good faith, but the kisses of a hater are false.
sentences.susu: I xanuntenyi xa marakɔrɔsi xɔnɔ, kɔnɔ la na ra. I yaxui tan i madaxuma nɛ wɔyɛnyi ɲɔxunmɛ ra.

sentences.english: The full man has no use for honey, but to the man in need of food every bitter thing is sweet.
sentences.susu: Mixi lugaxi mu wama hali kumi xɔn, kɔnɔ kaamɛtɔɛ tan, hali se xɔnɛ nan a ra, a ɲɔxun a bɛ.

sentences.english: Like a bird wandering from the place of her eggs is a man wandering from his station.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ naxan a makuyama a xɔnyi ra, na maniya xɔni ra naxan a makuyama a tɛɛ ra.

sentences.english: Oil and perfume make glad the heart, and the wise suggestion of a friend is sweet to the soul.
sentences.susu: Labundɛ nun surayi bɔɲɛ rasɛɛwama nɛ, alɔ i xanuntenyi xa marasi fanyi.

sentences.english: Do not give up your friend and your father's friend; and do not go into your brother's house in the day of your trouble: better is a neighbour who is near than a brother far off.
sentences.susu: I naxa i dɛfanboore rabolo, i naxa i baba dɛfanboore rabolo. I naxa i bariboore xili i xa tɔɔrɛ ma. I dɔxɔboore makɔrɛxi fisa i ngaxakerenyi makuyaxi bɛ.

sentences.english: My son, be wise and make my heart glad, so that I may give back an answer to him who puts me to shame.
sentences.susu: N ma di, bira lɔnni fɔxɔ ra alako n bɔɲɛ xa rafan n ma. Na kui n nɔma nɛ mixi yaabide naxan wama n nayaagife.

sentences.english: The sharp man sees the evil and takes cover: the simple go straight on and get into trouble.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima a yɛtɛ ratangama fe xɔrɔxɔɛ ma, kɔnɔ xaxilitare tan soma nɛ na kui, a fa ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Take a man's clothing if he makes himself responsible for a strange man, and get an undertaking from him who gives his word for strange men.
sentences.susu: Mixi xa sɛɛkɛ se rasuxu a naxan taani xɔɲɛ bɛ, xa na mu a ra a naxan taani langoe bɛ.

sentences.english: He who gives a blessing to his friend with a loud voice, getting up early in the morning, will have it put to his account as a curse.
sentences.susu: I na i dɔxɔboore xɛɛbu i xui itexi ra gɛɛsɛgɛ gbe ra, i bara a bɔɲɛ raɲaaxu a ma i tan mabiri.

sentences.english: Like an unending dropping on a day of rain is a bitter-tongued woman.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ fitinɛtɔɛ luxi nɛ alɔ tunɛ di naxan fɛɛɲɛnma fa ra.

sentences.english: He who keeps secret the secret of his friend, will get himself a name for good faith.
sentences.susu: Na ginɛ mɔɔli raxanfe, na maniyama foye raxanfe ra, a suxufe xɔrɔxɔ alɔ ture suxufe i bɛlɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: Iron makes iron sharp; so a man makes sharp his friend.
sentences.susu: Wure nan wure raluganma. Mixi a boore rakamalima nɛ.

sentences.english: Whoever keeps a fig-tree will have its fruit; and the servant waiting on his master will be honoured.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan mɛɛnima xɔrɛ bili ma, a a bogi donma nɛ. Mixi naxan mɛɛnima a karamɔxɔ ma, a binyɛ sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: Like face looking at face in water, so are the hearts of men to one another.
sentences.susu: Adama yatagi na ki naxɛ, na nan minima ye xɔɔra. Adama yati na ki naxɛ, na toma nɛ a bɔɲɛ kui.

sentences.english: The underworld and Abaddon are never full, and the eyes of man have never enough.
sentences.susu: Aligiyama mu wasama mixi faxaxie ra, adama fan mu wasama a waxɔnse ra.

sentences.english: The heating-pot is for silver and the oven-fire for gold, and a man is measured by what he is praised for.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛma nun gbeti matoma tɛ ra, kɔnɔ mixi makiitima a xili nan ma.

sentences.english: Even if a foolish man is crushed with a hammer in a vessel among crushed grain, still his foolish ways will not go from him.
sentences.susu: I na maale din, a lagi bama nɛ a ma, kɔnɔ xaxilitareɲa mu bama xaxilitare bɔɲɛ kui.

sentences.english: Take care to have knowledge about the condition of your flocks, looking well after your herds;
sentences.susu: I xa i xa xuruse birin kolon a fanyi ra, i xa mɛɛni e ma,

sentences.english: For wealth is not for ever, and money does not go on for all generations.
sentences.susu: barima bannaya mu buma tɛmui birin, xunnakeli fan mu buma abadan.

sentences.english: The grass comes up and the young grass is seen, and the mountain plants are got in.
sentences.susu: Xurusee na gɛ e balode ɲooge ra naxan toma fiili ma nun geya fari,

sentences.english: The lambs are for your clothing, and the he-goats make the value of a field:
sentences.susu: yɛxɛɛe xabe yailan dugi ra i bɛ, si kontonyi findi kɔbiri ra i xɛ sarama naxan na,

sentences.english: There will be goats' milk enough for your food, and for the support of your servant-girls.
sentences.susu: si xiɲɛ findi i xa denbaya nun i xa konyie balo se ra.

sentences.english: The evil man goes running away when no man is after him, but the upright are without fear, like the lion.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie luma nɛ gaaxui kui, e e gima nɛ hali mixi mu e fɔxɔ ra. Tinxintɔɛe tan mu gaaxuma, e suusa alɔ yɛtɛ.

sentences.english: Because of the sin of the land, its troubles are increased; but by a man of wisdom and knowledge they will be put out like a fire.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ die wuya ɲama matandila ya ma, kɔnɔ mangɛ xaxilima fata ɲama raxande.

sentences.english: A man of wealth who is cruel to the poor is like a violent rain causing destruction of food.
sentences.susu: Setare naxan a boore setaree tɔɔrɔma, na maniya tunɛ wunde ra naxan xɛ kanama.

sentences.english: Those who have no respect for the law give praise to the evil-doer; but such as keep the law are against him.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ matandi mixi ɲaaxi matɔxɔma nɛ, sɛriyɛ rabatui tan xɔnɔma nɛ mixi kobi ma.

sentences.english: Evil men have no knowledge of what is right; but those who go after the Lord have knowledge of all things.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie mu sɛriyɛ kolon, kɔnɔ Alatala fenmae a fahaamuma nɛ a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: Better is the poor man whose ways are upright, than the man of wealth whose ways are not straight.
sentences.susu: Setare tinxinxi fisa banna tinxintare bɛ.

sentences.english: He who keeps the law is a wise son, but he who keeps company with feasters puts shame on his father.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ batula findixi di xaxili fanyi nan na, kɔnɔ wasatare tan a baba rayaagima nɛ.

sentences.english: He who makes his wealth greater by taking interest, only gets it together for him who has pity on the poor.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a xa naafuli xun masama riba ra, a xa bannaya gbilenma nɛ kinikininte ma.

sentences.english: As for the man whose ear is turned away from hearing the law, even his prayer is disgusting.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tondima a tuli matide sɛriyɛ ra, Ala mu a xa duba suxuma feo.

sentences.english: Anyone causing the upright to go wandering in an evil way, will himself go down into the hole he has made; but the upright will have good things for their heritage.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tinxintɔɛe ratantanma, a birama a yɛtɛ kan xa gantanyi nan kui, tinxintɔɛ tan fa kɛ fanyi sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: The man of wealth seems to himself to be wise, but the poor man who has sense has a low opinion of him.
sentences.susu: Banna mixi ɲɔxɔ a ma a xa lɔnni gbo, kɔnɔ setare xaxilima nɔma nɛ na kanyi ra.

sentences.english: When the upright do well, there is great glory; but when evil-doers are lifted up, men do not let themselves be seen.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛe xun na rakeli, ɲama ɲɛlɛxinma nɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintare xun na rakeli, ɲama a nɔxunma nɛ.

sentences.english: He who keeps his sins secret will not do well; but one who is open about them, and gives them up, will get mercy.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a xa yunubie nɔxunma, a xa fe mu sɔɔnɛyama, kɔnɔ mixi naxan a tima a xa yunubie ra, a gbilen e fɔxɔ ra, Ala kinikinima a ma.

sentences.english: Happy is the man in whom is the fear of the Lord at all times; but he whose heart is hard will come into trouble.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ naxan gaaxuma Ala ya ra, kɔnɔ bɔɲɛ xɔrɔxɔɛ kanyi luma tɔɔrɛ nan kui.

sentences.english: Like a loud-voiced lion and a wandering bear, is an evil ruler over a poor people.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi naxan ɲama setare yamarima, a luxi nɛ alɔ yɛtɛ magaaxuxi nun wulai sube xaaɲɛ.

sentences.english: The prince who has no sense is a cruel ruler; but he who has no desire to get profit for himself will have long life.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ xaxilitare mixi tɔɔrɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ mangɛ naxan naafuli tinxintare xɔnma, na simaya xɔnkuye sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: One who has been the cause of a man's death will go in flight to the underworld: let no man give him help.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a kolon a bɔɲɛ kui a faxɛ tixi, na luma a gi ra nɛ han aligiyama. Mixi yo naxa na kanyi mali.

sentences.english: He whose ways are upright will be safe, but sudden will be the fall of him whose ways are twisted.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan ɲɛrɛma tinxinyi ra, na kisima nɛ, kɔnɔ filankafui tan birama nɛ kerenyi ra.

sentences.english: By ploughing his land a man will have bread in full measure; but he who goes after good-for-nothing persons will be poor enough.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a xa bɔxi rawalima, na baloe sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ naxan birama fe fufafu fɔxɔ ra, na setareɲa nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: A man of good faith will have great blessing, but one attempting to get wealth quickly will not go free from punishment.
sentences.susu: Mixi dugutɛgɛxi barakɛ sɔtɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ naxan gbatama bannaya ra, a ɲaxankatama nɛ.

sentences.english: It is not good to have respect for a man's position: for a man will do wrong for a bit of bread.
sentences.susu: A mu lan mixi xa mixi rafisa a boore bɛ, kɔnɔ mixi nde fe ɲaaxi rabama taami xuntunyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: He who is ever desiring wealth goes running after money, and does not see that need will come on him.
sentences.susu: Milante gbatama bannaya ra, kɔnɔ a mu a kolon a tɔɔrɛ nan tun sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: He who says words of protest to a man will later have more approval than one who says smooth words with his tongue.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan marasi xɔrɔxɔɛ fima mixi nde ma, na hinnɛ nan sɔtɔma dangife mixi ra naxan luma wɔyɛn ɲɔxunmɛ gbansan fala ra mixie bɛ.

sentences.english: He who takes from his father or his mother what is theirs by right, and says, It is no sin; is the same as a taker of life.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a baba nun a nga muɲama, a fa a fala «A mu ɲaaxu,» na bara findi kasarati ra.

sentences.english: He who is ever desiring profit is a cause of fighting; but he who puts his faith in the Lord will be made fat.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan milama harige ma, na findima geresoe nan na, kɔnɔ naxan bara a yɛtɛ taxu Alatala ra, na ɲan bara hɛɛri gbegbe sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: He whose faith is in himself is foolish; but everyone walking wisely will be kept safe.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan laxi a yɛtɛ kan xaxili ra, na bara findi xaxilitare ra, kɔnɔ mixi naxan ɲɛrɛma xaxili fanyi ra, na kanyi kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: He who gives to the poor will never be in need, but great curses will be on him who gives no attention to them.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan setare kima, na mu tɔɔrɔma, kɔnɔ naxan setare kumama, na dankɛ nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: When evil-doers are lifted up, men take cover; but when destruction overtakes them, the upright are increased.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie xun na rakeli, ɲama a nɔxunma nɛ, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxie na halaki, tinxintɔɛe tan xun nakelima nɛ.

sentences.english: A man hating sharp words and making his heart hard, will suddenly be broken and will not be made well again.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan tondima marakɔrɔsi ra, na kanyi ɲaxankatama nɛ kerenyi ra.

sentences.english: When the upright have power, the people are glad; when an evil man is ruler, grief comes on the people.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ na sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ, ɲama sɛɛwama nɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintare na findi mangɛ ra, ɲama tɔɔrɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: A man who is a lover of wisdom is a joy to his father: but he who goes in the company of loose women is a waster of wealth.
sentences.susu: Lɔnni rafan mixi naxan ma, na a baba rasɛɛwama nɛ, kɔnɔ naxan birama langoeɲa fɔxɔ ra, na ganma nɛ a harige ra.

sentences.english: A king, by right rule, makes the land safe; but one full of desires makes it a waste.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ bɔxi rasabatima tinxinyi nan na, kɔnɔ mangɛ naxan kɔbiri fenma a yɛtɛ bɛ, na bɔxi xun nakanama nɛ.

sentences.english: A man who says smooth things to his neighbour is stretching out a net for his steps.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a boore tamixiyama, a na yɛlɛ italafe a boore nan bɛ.

sentences.english: In the steps of an evil man there is a net for him, but the upright man gets away quickly and is glad.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi xa yunubi findixi gantanyi nan na a bɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛ xun nakelima nɛ sɛɛwɛ kui.

sentences.english: The upright man gives attention to the cause of the poor: the evil-doer gives no thought to it.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ katama nɛ tinxinyi xa raba setaree bɛ, kɔnɔ mixi ɲaaxi mu mɛɛnima setaree ma fefe ma.

sentences.english: Men of pride are the cause of violent acts in a town, but by wise men wrath is turned away.
sentences.susu: Mixi mayelee a niyama nɛ taakae xa xɔnɔ, kɔnɔ xaxilimae tan ɲama bɔɲɛ ragoroma nɛ.

sentences.english: If a wise man goes to law with a foolish man, he may be angry or laughing, but there will be no rest.
sentences.susu: Xa kiiti lu xaxilima nun xaxilitare tagi, na xaxilitare sɔnxɔɛ ratema nɛ tun, bɔɲɛsa xa kana.

sentences.english: Men of blood are haters of the good man, and evil-doers go after his soul.
sentences.susu: Faxɛtie tinxintɔɛ xɔnma, kɔnɔ mixi tinxinxie e boore makantama nɛ.

sentences.english: A foolish man lets out all his wrath, but a wise man keeps it back quietly.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare bɔɲɛ xa te mafura, kɔnɔ xaxilima tan a yɛtɛ suxuma nɛ.

sentences.english: If a ruler gives attention to false words, all his servants are evil-doers.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ na bira wule fɔxɔ ra, a xa mixi birin findima nɛ mixi ɲaaxie ra.

sentences.english: The poor man and his creditor come face to face: the Lord gives light to their eyes equally.
sentences.susu: Fe keren na setare nun mixi kobi tagi: Alatala nan e birin daa.

sentences.english: The king who is a true judge in the cause of the poor, will be safe for ever on the seat of his power.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxan setare makiitima nɔndi ra, na xa kibanyi mabanbanma nɛ abadan.

sentences.english: The rod and sharp words give wisdom: but a child who is not guided is a cause of shame to his mother.
sentences.susu: Di xurufe luxusinyi ra, na a niyama nɛ a xaxili sɔtɔ, kɔnɔ di lufe a yɛtɛ yi ra, na findima yaagi nan na a nga bɛ.

sentences.english: When evil men are in power, wrongdoing is increased; but the upright will have pleasure when they see their downfall.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie na sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ, yunubie gboma nɛ, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛe fama nɛ e xunnagore tode.

sentences.english: Give your son training, and he will give you rest; he will give delight to your soul.
sentences.susu: I xa di matinxin alako i xa lu bɔɲɛsa kui, a ɲɛrɛ ki xa i rasɛɛwa.

sentences.english: Where there is no vision, the people are uncontrolled; but he who keeps the law will be happy.
sentences.susu: Xa ɲama mu Ala xa fe toma, e birama e yɛtɛ waxɔnfe nan tun fɔxɔ ra. Sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ naxan Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatuma.

sentences.english: A servant will not be trained by words; for though the sense of the words is clear to him, he will not give attention.
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛnyi xa mu konyi matinxinma. Hali a na mɛ, a mu a rabatuma.

sentences.english: Have you seen a man who is quick with his tongue? There is more hope for a foolish man than for him.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare fisa mixi bɛ, naxan ɲɛngi mu sama a xa wɔyɛnyi xɔn ma.

sentences.english: If a servant is gently cared for from his early years, he will become a cause of sorrow in the end.
sentences.susu: Konyi naxan kanyi bara a kana kabi a dimɛdi tɛmui, na findima tɔɔrɛ nan na a kanyi bɛ.

sentences.english: An angry man is the cause of fighting, and a man given to wrath does much wrong.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛte nan gere raminima, a findi yunubie ra.

sentences.english: A man's pride will be the cause of his fall, but he who has a gentle spirit will get honour.
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igboɲa mixi rayaagima nɛ, kɔnɔ yɛtɛ magore mixi xun nakelima nɛ.

sentences.english: A man who takes part with a thief has hate for his soul; he is put under oath, but says nothing.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan kafuma muɲɛti ma, na bara a yɛtɛ gan. A a kolon dankɛ na seede tinxintare bɛ, kɔnɔ a nɔndi nɔxunma nɛ.

sentences.english: The fear of man is a cause of danger: but whoever puts his faith in the Lord will have a safe place on high.
sentences.susu: Gaaxufe mixi ya ra, na findima gantanyi nan na, kɔnɔ naxan a yɛtɛ taxuma Alatala ra, a kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: The approval of a ruler is desired by great numbers: but the decision in a man's cause comes from the Lord.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbegbe mangɛ xa hinnɛ fenma, kɔnɔ Alatala nan mixi birin makiitima nɔndi ra.

sentences.english: An evil man is disgusting to the upright, and he who is upright is disgusting to evil-doers.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxie raɲaaxu tinxintɔɛe ma, tinxintɔɛe raɲaaxu mixi ɲaaxie ma.

sentences.english: The words of Agur, the son of Jakeh, from Massa. The man says: I am full of weariness, O God, I am full of weariness; O God, I have come to an end:
sentences.susu: Yake xa di Aguru xa masenyi nan ya a naxan masenxi Itiyɛli nun Ukala bɛ:

sentences.english: For I am more like a beast than any man, I have no power of reasoning like a man:
sentences.susu: N ma lɔnni mu gbo alɔ booree, n mu gɛxi fahaamui gbegbe sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: I have not got wisdom by teaching, so that I might have the knowledge of the Holy One.
sentences.susu: N mu findixi lɔnnila ra, n mu lɔnni sɔtɔxi Ala xa Sɛniyɛntɔɛe xa fe ra.

sentences.english: Who has gone up to heaven and come down? who has taken the winds in his hands, prisoning the waters in his robe? by whom have all the ends of the earth been fixed? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if you are able to say?
sentences.susu: Nde texi koore, a man naxa goro? Nde foye malanxi a bɛlɛxɛe kui? Nde ye ragataxi a xa sosee kui? Nde duniɲa naaninyie saxi? A xili di? A xa di xili di? I na kolon?

sentences.english: Every word of God is tested: he is a breastplate to those who put their faith in him.
sentences.susu: Ala xa masenyi birin findixi nɔndi nan na, a findi kantari ra mixi bɛ naxan lama a ra.

sentences.english: Make no addition to his words, or he will make clear your error, and you will be seen to be false.
sentences.susu: I naxa se sa na masenyi xun ma, alako Ala naxa i suxu, a fa i xa wule to.

sentences.english: I have made request to you for two things; do not keep them from me before my death:
sentences.susu: N wama fe firin maxɔrinfe i ma beenun n xa faxa. I naxa tondi.

sentences.english: Put far from me all false and foolish things: do not give me great wealth or let me be in need, but give me only enough food:
sentences.susu: Madaxuɲa nun wule makuya n na. I naxa n findi setare ra, i naxa n findi banna ra. Baloe gbansan fi n ma, naxan n wasama.

sentences.english: For fear that if I am full, I may be false to you and say, Who is the Lord? or if I am poor, I may become a thief, using the name of my God wrongly.
sentences.susu: Xa n sa se gbegbe sɔtɔ, n gaaxuma nɛ n naxa nɛɛmu i ma, n fa a fala, «Nde na Alatala ra?» Xa n sa lu setareɲa fan kui, n gaaxuma nɛ n naxa muɲɛ ti, n fa i tan n Marigi Ala xili kana.

sentences.english: Do not say evil of a servant to his master, or he will put a curse on you, and you will get into trouble.
sentences.susu: I naxa konyi xili kana a kanyi bɛ, alako a naxa i danka, na haakɛ lu i ma.

sentences.english: There is a generation who put a curse on their father, and do not give a blessing to their mother.
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee e baba dankama, e e nga finsiriwali.

sentences.english: There is a generation who seem to themselves to be free from sin, but are not washed from their unclean ways.
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee e yɛtɛ findima sɛniyɛntɔɛe ra, kɔnɔ e mu nɔma sɛniyɛntareɲa bade e ma.

sentences.english: There is a generation, O how full of pride are their eyes! O how their brows are lifted up!
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee e yɛtɛ itema, e a maɲɔxun e dangi mixi birin na.

sentences.english: There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, their strong teeth like knives, for the destruction of the poor from the earth, and of those who are in need from among men.
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee na naxee luxi alɔ sube xaaɲɛe naxee wama setaree faxafe, e xa e ba duniɲa.

sentences.english: The night-spirit has two daughters, Give, give. There are three things which are never full, even four which never say, Enough:
sentences.susu: Di firin na nisi bɛ naxee a falama, «N ki, n ki.» Se saxan na na, xa na mu a ra, se naani, naxee mu wasama, naxee mu a falama, «Na lan.»

sentences.english: The underworld, and the woman without a child; the earth which never has enough water, and the fire which never says, Enough.
sentences.susu: E tan nan ya: aligiyama, ginɛ dibaritare, gbengberenyi, nun tɛ. Nee sese mu a falama, «Na lan.»

sentences.english: The eye which makes sport of a father, and sees no value in a mother when she is old will be rooted out by the ravens of the valley, and be food for the young eagles.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan yoma a baba ma, naxan mu a nga xui rabatuma, xaaxae kelima nɛ gulunba yire e a yae sakun, sɛgɛ yɔrɛe fa a donde.

sentences.english: There are three things, the wonder of which overcomes me, even four things outside my knowledge:
sentences.susu: Se saxan na na, xa na mu a ra, se naani, n mu naxee fahaamuma e xa tilinyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a snake on a rock; the way of a ship in the heart of the sea; and the way of a man with a girl.
sentences.susu: E tan nan ya: Sɛgɛ xa kira koore ma, bɔximase xa kira fanye fari, kunkui xa kira baa ma, xɛmɛ xa kira ginɛdimɛdi xɔnyi.

sentences.english: This is the way of a false wife; she takes food, and, cleaning her mouth, says, I have done no wrong.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ yɛnɛla xa wali nan ya: A na gɛ a dɛgede, a a dɛ raxa, a fa a fala, «N mu fe ɲaaxi yo rabaxi.»

sentences.english: For three things the earth is moved, and there are four which it will not put up with:
sentences.susu: Se saxan na na, xa na mu a ra, se naani, naxee mu nɔma lude duniɲa fari.

sentences.english: A servant when he becomes a king; a man without sense when his wealth is increased;
sentences.susu: E tan nan ya: Konyi findife mangɛ ra, xaxilitare findife banna ra,

sentences.english: A hated woman when she is married; and a servant-girl who takes the place of her master's wife.
sentences.susu: ginɛ maxanutare dɔxɔfe xɛmɛ taa, konyi ginɛ naxan findife a kanyi kɛ tongoe ra.

sentences.english: There are four things which are little on the earth, but they are very wise:
sentences.susu: Sube naani na naxee xurun duniɲa subee birin bɛ, kɔnɔ e xa lɔnni dangi a birin na.

sentences.english: The ants are a people not strong, but they put by a store of food in the summer;
sentences.susu: E tan nan ya: Dondoli naxan sɛnbɛ mu gbo, kɔnɔ e baloe fenma a fen waxati.

sentences.english: The conies are only a feeble people, but they make their houses in the rocks;
sentences.susu: Yere maniyɛ nde naxan sɛnbɛ mu gbo, kɔnɔ a yili gema gɛmɛ longori yigiya sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: The locusts have no king, but they all go out in bands;
sentences.susu: Mangɛ mu na katoe bɛ, kɔnɔ e e ɲɛrɛma xunlande ki ma.

sentences.english: You may take the lizard in your hands, but it is in kings' houses.
sentences.susu: Kasa naxan nɔma tongode bɛlɛxɛ ra, kɔnɔ a toma mangɛ xa banxi kui.

sentences.english: There are three things whose steps are good to see, even four whose goings are fair:
sentences.susu: Se saxan na na, xa na mu a ra, se naani, naxee ɲɛrɛ ki tofan.

sentences.english: The lion, which is strongest among beasts, not turning from his way for any;
sentences.susu: E tan nan ya: Yɛtɛ naxan sɛnbɛ gbo, a suusa sube birin bɛ,

sentences.english: The war-horse, and the he-goat, and the king when his army is with him.
sentences.susu: konkore naxan ɲɛrɛma a xun nakelixi ra, si kontonyi, nun mangɛ, sɔɔrie na naxan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: If you have done foolishly in lifting yourself up, or if you have had evil designs, put your hand over your mouth.
sentences.susu: Xa i bara i yɛtɛ igbo xaxilitareɲa kui, xa i bara wa fe ɲaaxi nde rabafe, i xa gbilen na fɔxɔ ra,

sentences.english: The shaking of milk makes butter, and the twisting of the nose makes blood come: so the forcing of wrath is a cause of fighting.
sentences.susu: barima xiɲɛ na bɔnbɔ, a binyama nɛ, ɲɔɛ na din, wuli minima nɛ, xɔnɛ xun na masa, a findima nɛ gere ra.

sentences.english: The words of Lemuel, king of Massa: the teaching which he had from his mother.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Lemuweli xa masenyi nan ya a nga naxan fi a ma marasi ra:

sentences.english: What am I to say to you, O Lemuel, my oldest son? and what, O son of my body? and what, O son of my oaths?
sentences.susu: N ma di, i tuli mati n na, n ma di fanyi, n naxan barixi, n naxan sɔtɔ Ala saabui ra.

sentences.english: Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to that which is the destruction of kings.
sentences.susu: I naxa i sɛnbɛ fi ginɛ ɲaaxie ma, naxee fata mangɛe ralɔɛde. I naxa bira na ginɛ mɔɔli fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to take wine, or for rulers to say, Where is strong drink?
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Lemuweli, a mu lanma mangɛe xa wɛni min. Beere xɔli mu lanma a xa mangɛ suxu,

sentences.english: For fear that through drinking they may come to have no respect for the law, wrongly judging the cause of those who are in trouble.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra e nɛɛmuma nɛ e yɛtɛ xa sɛriyɛ ma, e fa tɔɔrɔmixi yanfa.

sentences.english: Give strong drink to him who is near to destruction, and wine to him whose soul is bitter:
sentences.susu: Na minse mɔɔli xa so mixie nan yi, naxee na saya kira xɔn ma, alako e xa nɛɛmu e xa fe xɔrɔxɔɛ birin ma.

sentences.english: Let him have drink, and his need will go from his mind, and the memory of his trouble will be gone.
sentences.susu: Naxan wɛni minxi a nɛɛmuma nɛ a xa setareɲa ma, a mu ratuma a xa tɔɔrɛ ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: Let your mouth be open for those who have no voice, in the cause of those who are ready for death.
sentences.susu: I xa dɛtare xunmafala, i xa misikiinɛ mali.

sentences.english: Let your mouth be open, judging rightly, and give right decisions in the cause of the poor and those in need.
sentences.susu: I xui ramini, kiiti sa nɔndi ra. I xa tɔɔrɔmixi nun setare xunmafala.

sentences.english: Who may make discovery of a woman of virtue? For her price is much higher than jewels.
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma ginɛ fanyi sɔtɔde? A tide gbo diyaman bɛ.

sentences.english: The heart of her husband has faith in her, and he will have profit in full measure.
sentences.susu: A xa mɔri laxi a ra, a findixi harige fanyi nan na a bɛ tɛmui birin.

sentences.english: She does him good and not evil all the days of her life.
sentences.susu: A fe fanyi rabama a xa mɔri bɛ, a mu fe ɲaaxi yo rabama a ra a xa duniɲɛigiri kui.

sentences.english: She gets wool and linen, working at the business of her hands.
sentences.susu: A yɛxɛɛ xabe nun gɛsɛ fute fenma, a nee rafalama sosee ra. Na wali rafan a ma.

sentences.english: She is like the trading-ships, getting food from far away.
sentences.susu: A luma alɔ yulɛ xa kunkui, a sa baloe fenma yire makuye a fa a ra.

sentences.english: She gets up while it is still night, and gives meat to her family, and their food to her servant-girls.
sentences.susu: A kurunma nɛ alako a xa kuri so a xa denbaya bɛ, a man wali so a xa walikɛ ginɛe yi ra.

sentences.english: After looking at a field with care, she gets it for a price, planting a vine-garden with the profit of her work.
sentences.susu: A bɔxi matoma nɛ, a fa na sara. A geeni naxan sɔtɔma a na sarama sansi nan na, a a si.

sentences.english: She puts a band of strength round her, and makes her arms strong.
sentences.susu: A tunnabɛxi, a walima sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: She sees that her marketing is of profit to her: her light does not go out by night.
sentences.susu: A a kolon a xa wali sɔɔnɛyama nɛ. A lanpui radɛxɛma nɛ, a wali kɔɛ fan na.

sentences.english: She puts her hands to the cloth-working rod, and her fingers take the wheel.
sentences.susu: A yɛxɛɛ xabe findima nɛ gɛsɛ ra, a gɛsɛ findima sose ra.

sentences.english: Her hands are stretched out to the poor; yes, she is open-handed to those who are in need.
sentences.susu: A setare kima, a misikiinɛ malima.

sentences.english: She has no fear of the snow for her family, for all those in her house are clothed in red.
sentences.susu: A mu gaaxuma ɲɛmɛ ya ra, barima a xinbeli donma fanyie yailanxi a xa denbaya bɛ.

sentences.english: She makes for herself cushions of needlework; her clothing is fair linen and purple.
sentences.susu: A sade dugi yailanma, a dugi tofanyi dɛgɛma a yɛtɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: Her husband is a man of note in the public place, when he takes his seat among the responsible men of the land.
sentences.susu: Taa kuntigi nan a xa mɔri ra, a dɔxɔxi forie ya ma.

sentences.english: She makes linen robes and gets a price for them, and traders take her cloth bands for a price.
sentences.susu: A sosee dɛgɛma, a e mati. A bɛlɛtie fan yailanma, yulɛe nee wafuma a ma.

sentences.english: Strength and self-respect are her clothing; she is facing the future with a smile.
sentences.susu: A sɛnbɛ gbo, mixie a binyama. A mu gaaxuma fefe ma.

sentences.english: Her mouth is open to give out wisdom, and the law of mercy is on her tongue.
sentences.susu: A lɔnni masenma mixie bɛ, a man e xaran a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: She gives attention to the ways of her family, she does not take her food without working for it.
sentences.susu: A a ɲɛngi sama a xa denbaya xɔn ma, a mu walitareɲa kolon.

sentences.english: Her children get up and give her honour, and her husband gives her praise, saying,
sentences.susu: A xa die a matɔxɔma, a xa mɔri a tantuma yi wɔyɛnyi ra:

sentences.english: Unnumbered women have done well, but you are better than all of them.
sentences.susu: «Ginɛ fanyie na na de, kɔnɔ i maniyɛ mu na e ya ma.»

sentences.english: Fair looks are a deceit, and a beautiful form is of no value; but a woman who has the fear of the Lord is to be praised.
sentences.susu: Fate xa tofanyi mixi madaxuma nɛ, a mu buma. Tantui na ginɛ nan bɛ naxan gaaxuma Alatala ya ra.

sentences.english: Give her credit for what her hands have made: let her be praised by her works in the public place.
sentences.susu: Wo xa na ginɛ xa wali fanyi sare fi a ma, wo xa na ginɛ mɔɔli matɔxɔ taa kui.

sentences.english: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Dawuda xa di Darisalamu mangɛ xa kawandi nan ya:

sentences.english: All is to no purpose, said the Preacher, all the ways of man are to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Duniɲa findixi fe fufafu nan na. Duniɲa fee tide yo mu na, na birin findixi fuyan nan na. N tan kawandila xa masenyi nan nan ki.

sentences.english: What is a man profited by all his work which he does under the sun?
sentences.susu: Adamadi geeni mundun sɔtɔma a xa wali ma soge bun ma?

sentences.english: One generation goes and another comes; but the earth is for ever.
sentences.susu: Ndee faxama, ndee barima, duniɲa fan na kɛɲa keren lɔxɔɛ birin.

sentences.english: The sun comes up and the sun goes down, and goes quickly back to the place where he came up.
sentences.susu: Soge tema, a goroma, a man gbilen a texi dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: The wind goes to the south, turning back again to the north; circling round for ever.
sentences.susu: Foye fan minima, a sigama yirefanyi ma, a a mafindima kɔɔla ma. A na gɛ mafindide, a man gbilen a kelide.

sentences.english: All the rivers go down to the sea, but the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers go, there they go again.
sentences.susu: Xure birin xun tixi baa nan na, kɔnɔ baa mu rafema. Xuree kelima dɛnnaxɛ, e man gbilenma mɛnni nɛ.

sentences.english: All things are full of weariness; man may not give their story: the eye has never enough of its seeing, or the ear of its hearing.
sentences.susu: Fe birin ɲɛrɛma, a mu taganma, a mu masarama. Adama ya mu wasama fe matode, a tuli fan mu lugama fe ramɛde.

sentences.english: That which has been, is that which is to be, and that which has been done, is that which will be done, and there is no new thing under the sun.
sentences.susu: Naxan bara dangi nu, na nan man gbilenma a ra. Naxan bara raba nu, na nan man nabama. Fe nɛɛnɛ mu rabama duniɲa ma naxan ɲɔndɔn mu nu raba.

sentences.english: Is there anything of which men say, See, this is new? It has been in the old time which was before us.
sentences.susu: Fe nɛɛnɛ yo mu na naxan a niyama mixi xa a fala, «Yi mato, fe nɛɛnɛ na a ra!» N xa a fala wo bɛ, na fe mɔɔli ɲan nu na beenun won tan xa bari.

sentences.english: There is no memory of those who have gone before, and of those who come after there will be no memory for those who are still to come after them.
sentences.susu: Ɲama mu ratuma fe dangixi ma, fe naxan sa fama rabade, ɲama nɛɛmuma nɛ na fan na.

sentences.english: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: N tan Kawandila, n bara findi mangɛ ra Isirayila bɔxi ma Darisalamu.

sentences.english: And I gave my heart to searching out in wisdom all things which are done under heaven: it is a hard thing which God has put on the sons of men to do.
sentences.susu: N natɛ tongoxi nɛ, fe naxee birin nabafe yi duniɲa ma, n xa e mato a fanyi ra. Na kui n a to nɛ a Ala kote xɔrɔxɔɛ nan saxi adamadie fari.

sentences.english: I have seen all the works which are done under the sun; all is to no purpose, and desire for wind.
sentences.susu: N bara wali birin mato naxan nabama yi duniɲa ma. Fufafu na a birin na! Birafe na wali fɔxɔ ra, a luxi nɛ alɔ mixi na birafe foye nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: That which is bent may not be made straight, and that which is not there may not be numbered.
sentences.susu: Naxan kuntinxi, na mu nɔma matinxinde, naxan luxi, na mu nɔma kamalide.

sentences.english: I said to my heart, See, I have become great and am increased in wisdom more than any who were before me in Jerusalem — yes, my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.
sentences.susu: N naxa a maɲɔxun n yɛtɛ ma, a n tan bara lɔnni fen dangi Darisalamu mangɛ birin na, naxee singe fa n tan yara. N bara lɔnni nun fe kolonyi gbegbe sɔtɔ duniɲa xa fe ma.

sentences.english: And I gave my heart to getting knowledge of wisdom, and of the ways of the foolish. And I saw that this again was desire for wind.
sentences.susu: N naxa natɛ tongo n xa xaxilimaya nun xaxilitareɲa fan mato. Kɔnɔ n bara a to na fan luxi alɔ birafe foye nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Because in much wisdom is much grief, and increase of knowledge is increase of sorrow.
sentences.susu: Xaxilimaya nun kɔntɔfili nan ɲɛrɛma kira keren xɔn ma. Fe kolonyi gboma ki naxɛ, tɔɔrɛ fan gboma na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: I said in my heart, I will give you joy for a test; so take your pleasure — but it was to no purpose.
sentences.susu: N a fala nɛ n yɛtɛ bɛ, «N xa ɲɛlɛxinyi mato, n xa a kolon naxan fan.» N naxa a to a ɲɛlɛxinyi fan mu buma.

sentences.english: Of laughing I said, It is foolish; and of joy — What use is it?
sentences.susu: N naxa n yɛtɛ maxɔrin, «Yelefe tun mu findixi fe kamalixi ra. Ɲɛlɛxinyi tide na munse ra?»

sentences.english: I made a search with my heart to give pleasure to my flesh with wine, still guiding my heart with wisdom, and to go after foolish things, so that I might see what was good for the sons of men to do under the heavens all the days of their life.
sentences.susu: N naxa natɛ tongo n ma lɔnni fenfe kui, n xa ɲɛlɛxinyi fen wɛni ra. N nu wama a kolonfe munse munafanyi gbo adamadie bɛ e xa duniɲɛigiri kui.

sentences.english: I undertook great works, building myself houses and planting vine-gardens.
sentences.susu: N naxa wali xungbe ndee suxu alɔ banxi tife nun xɛ safe.

sentences.english: I made myself gardens and fruit gardens, planting in them fruit-trees of all sorts.
sentences.susu: N naxa yire tofanyie yailan naafuli kanyi e malabuma dɛnnaxɛ sansi tofanyie ya ma.

sentences.english: I made pools to give water for the woods with their young trees.
sentences.susu: N naxa ye yire ge naxee a niyama ye xa sa n ma sansie ma.

sentences.english: I got men-servants and women-servants, and they gave birth to sons and daughters in my house. I had great wealth of herds and flocks, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me.
sentences.susu: N naxa konyie sara, naxee bara die sɔtɔ naxee findixi n gbe ra, e fa lu n xɔnyi. N naxa xuruse gbegbe sɔtɔ, dangi Darisalamukae birin na naxee nu na beenu n xa bari.

sentences.english: I got together silver and gold and the wealth of kings and of countries. I got makers of song, male and female; and the delights of the sons of men — girls of all sorts to be my brides.
sentences.susu: N naxa gbeti, xɛɛma, nun naafuli mɔɔli birin sɔtɔ. N naxa yelibae sɔtɔ, a nun ginɛ gali adama waxɔnfe xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And I became great; increasing more than all who had been before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom was still with me.
sentences.susu: N naxa findi mixi xungbe ra dangife Darisalamukae birin na naxee nu na beenu n xa bari. N naxa na birin naba lɔnni fenfe ra.

sentences.english: And nothing which was desired by my eyes did I keep from them; I did not keep any joy from my heart, because my heart took pleasure in all my work, and this was my reward.
sentences.susu: N naxa n waxɔnfe mɔɔli birin fen, n mu tondi sese ra naxan nu rafanxi n ma. N ma wali yati nu rafanxi n ma, na nan findixi n ma geeni ra.

sentences.english: Then I saw all the works which my hands had made, and everything I had been working to do; and I saw that all was to no purpose and desire for wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n to n ma wali birin mato, n naxan nabaxi tɔɔrɛ kui, n naxa a to na birin fufafu. A nu luxi nɛ alɔ mixi naxan birama foye fɔxɔ ra a mu sese suxu.

sentences.english: And I went again in search of wisdom and of foolish ways. What may the man do who comes after the king? The thing which he has done before.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui n naxa n ɲɔxɔ sa xaxilimaya nun xaxilitareɲa xɔn ma. Naxan tima mangɛ ra n ɲɔxɔɛ ra, na fama munse rabade?

sentences.english: Then I saw that wisdom is better than foolish ways — as the light is better than the dark.
sentences.susu: N naxa a to xaxilimaya fan dangi xaxilitareɲa ra, alɔ naiyalanyi fan to fanxi dimi bɛ.

sentences.english: The wise man's eyes are in his head, but the foolish man goes walking in the dark; but still I saw that the same event comes to them all.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima se toma a ya ra, xaxilitare tan a ɲɛrɛma dimi nan kui. Kɔnɔ e firin birin faxama nɛ.

sentences.english: Then said I in my heart: As it comes to the foolish man, so will it come to me; so why have I been wise overmuch? Then I said in my heart: This again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra n naxa a maɲɔxun, xa n tan nun xaxilitare birin faxama nɛ, n ma xaxilimaya tide fa na munse ra? N naxa a fala n yɛtɛ bɛ, «Xaxilimaya fan fe fufafu nan a ra.»

sentences.english: Of the wise man, as of the foolish man, there is no memory for ever, seeing that those who now are will have gone from memory in the days to come. See how death comes to the wise as to the foolish!
sentences.susu: Xaxilima nun xaxilitare xa fe mu ratuma mixie ra, e nɛɛmuma nɛ e firin birin ma, e firin birin faxama nɛ.

sentences.english: So I was hating life, because everything under the sun was evil to me: all is to no purpose and desire for wind.
sentences.susu: Na kui duniɲɛigiri naxa raɲaaxu n ma, barima n bara a kolon n ma wali mu buma. A luxi nɛ alɔ mixi naxan birama foye fɔxɔ ra, e mu a suxu.

sentences.english: Hate had I for all my work which I had done, because the man who comes after me will have its fruits.
sentences.susu: N ma wali naxa raɲaaxu n ma, barima n bara a kolon fo n xa na birin lu mixi gbɛtɛ yi ra.

sentences.english: And who is to say if that man will be wise or foolish? But he will have power over all my work which I have done and in which I have been wise under the sun. This again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Na mixi findima xaxilima nan na, ka xaxilitare ra? Nde nɔma na kolonde? Kɔnɔ a tan yati nɔɛ sɔtɔma nɛ n ma wali birin xun ma! Fe fufafu nan na ki.

sentences.english: So my mind was turned to grief for all the trouble I had taken and all my wisdom under the sun.
sentences.susu: Na kui n naxa nimisa wali birin xa fe ra n naxan naba yi duniɲa ma.

sentences.english: Because there is a man whose work has been done with wisdom, with knowledge, and with an expert hand; but one who has done nothing for it will have it for his heritage. This again is to no purpose and a great evil.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan walixi lɔnni nun fatɛ ra, a fa na wali lu mixi nde yi ra naxan mu sese raba na wali kui, na findixi fe fufafu nan na naxan xɔrɔxɔ ki fanyi ra.

sentences.english: What does a man get for all his work, and for the weight of care with which he has done his work under the sun?
sentences.susu: Mixi geeni mundun sɔtɔma a xa wali nun a xa katɛ kui a naxan nabaxi yi duniɲa ma?

sentences.english: All his days are sorrow, and his work is full of grief. Even in the night his heart has no rest. This again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: A xa wali findixi tɔɔrɛ xɔrɔxɔɛ nan na a bɛ. Hali kɔɛ ra a bɔɲɛ mu malabuma. Fe fufafu nan na ki.

sentences.english: There is nothing better for a man than taking meat and drink, and having delight in his work. This again I saw was from the hand of God.
sentences.susu: A lanma mixi xa a dɛge, a xa a min, a xa a xa wali raba sɛɛwɛ kui. N bara a kolon na birin kelixi Ala nan ma.

sentences.english: Who may take food or have pleasure without him?
sentences.susu: Mixi mu nɔma a dɛgede, a fe fanyi kolon xa Ala mu a mali?

sentences.english: To the man with whom he is pleased, God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy; but to the sinner he gives the work of getting goods together and storing up wealth, to give to him in whom God has pleasure. This again is to no purpose and desire for wind.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan nafan Ala ma, Ala a kima xaxili fanyi, fahaamui, nun sɛɛwɛ nan na. Kɔnɔ xaxilitare tan, Ala a niyama nɛ a xa a harige birin so mixi gbɛtɛ yi ra naxan nafan Ala ma. Yi fan findixi fe fufafu nan na, alɔ mixi naxan birama foye fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: For everything there is a fixed time, and a time for every business under the sun.
sentences.susu: Tɛmui na fe birin ma, fe birin duniɲa ma, a xa waxati na na.

sentences.english: A time for birth and a time for death; a time for planting and a time for uprooting;
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na di barife ma, waxati nde na faxafe ma. Waxati nde na sansi sife ma, waxati nde na sansi xabafe ma.

sentences.english: A time to put to death and a time to make well; a time for pulling down and a time for building up;
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na faxɛ tife ma, waxati nde na dandan tife ma. Waxati nde na se kanafe ma, waxati nde na se yailanfe ma.

sentences.english: A time for weeping and a time for laughing; a time for sorrow and a time for dancing;
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na wafe ma, waxati nde na yelefe ma. Waxati nde na yaye raminife ma, waxati nde na fare boronfe ma.

sentences.english: A time to take stones away and a time to get stones together; a time for kissing and a time to keep from kissing;
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na gɛmɛe rayensenfe ma, waxati nde na gɛmɛe malanfe ma. Waxati nde na sunbu tife ma, waxati nde na a titareya ma.

sentences.english: A time for search and a time for loss; a time to keep and a time to give away;
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na se fenfe ma, waxati nde na a lufe ma. Waxati nde na se ragatafe ma, waxati nde na a wɔlɛfe ma.

sentences.english: A time for undoing and a time for stitching; a time for keeping quiet and a time for talk;
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na se ibɔɔfe ma, waxati nde na a dɛgɛfe ma. Waxati nde na wɔyɛnfe ma, waxati nde na dundufe ma.

sentences.english: A time for love and a time for hate; a time for war and a time for peace.
sentences.susu: Waxati nde na xanu tife ma, waxati nde na xɔn tife ma. Waxati nde na geresofe ma, waxati nde na saatafe ma.

sentences.english: What profit has the worker in the work which he does?
sentences.susu: Walikɛ geeni mundun sɔtɔma a xa katɛ kui?

sentences.english: I saw the work which God has put on the sons of man.
sentences.susu: N bara kote to Ala naxan dɔxɔxi adamadie xun.

sentences.english: He has made everything right in its time; but he has made their hearts without knowledge, so that man is unable to see the works of God, from the first to the last.
sentences.susu: A bara se birin natofan a waxati ma. A bara a niya adamadi xaxili xa siga abadan fe ma, hali a mu nɔ Ala xa walie kolonde keli a fɔlɛ ma han a raɲɔnyi.

sentences.english: I am certain that there is nothing better for a man than to be glad, and to do good while life is in him.
sentences.susu: N a kolon fefe mu na naxan fan adamadi bɛ, fo a sɛɛwa, a fe fanyi raba a xa duniɲɛigiri kui.

sentences.english: And for every man to take food and drink, and have joy in all his work, is a reward from God.
sentences.susu: Mixi a dɛgefe, a a min, a sɛɛwa a xa wali kui, na nan findixi Ala xa ki ra adamadi bɛ.

sentences.english: I am certain that whatever God does will be for ever. No addition may be made to it, nothing may be taken from it; and God has done it so that man may be in fear before him.
sentences.susu: N a kolon Ala xa wali birin buma nɛ abadan. Sese mu sama a xun ma, sese mu bama a ra. Ala fe rabama nɛ alako adamadi xa gaaxu a ya ra.

sentences.english: Whatever is has been before, and what is to be is now; because God makes search for the things which are past.
sentences.susu: Naxan na na, na ɲan nu na nu. Naxan fama rabade, na ɲan nu na nu. Adamadi naxan nabaxi, Ala fama nɛ na makiitide.

sentences.english: And again, I saw under the sun, in the place of the judges, that evil was there; and in the place of righteousness, that evil was there.
sentences.susu: N bara fe gbɛtɛ fan to yi duniɲa ma: Nɔndi mafindima wule ra, tinxinyi mafindima tinxintareya ra.

sentences.english: I said in my heart, God will be judge of the good and of the bad; because a time for every purpose and for every work has been fixed by him.
sentences.susu: N naxa a maɲɔxun n xaxili kui, Ala tinxintɔɛ nun tinxintare makiitima nɛ, barima fe birin a waxati na na.

sentences.english: I said in my heart, It is because of the sons of men, so that God may put them to the test and that they may see themselves as beasts.
sentences.susu: N man naxa a maɲɔxun n xaxili kui, Ala na mixie matofe nɛ, alako e xa a kolon daalise nan lanxi e ma alɔ wulai subee.

sentences.english: Because the fate of the sons of men and the fate of the beasts is the same. As is the death of one so is the death of the other, and all have one spirit. Man is not higher than the beasts; because all is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: E firin birin fama nɛ raɲɔnde yire keren, e firin birin faxama nɛ. E firin birin ɲɛngima ki keren, adama yo sube yo, e birin lan. Fe fufafu na na birin na.

sentences.english: All go to one place, all are of the dust, and all will be turned to dust again.
sentences.susu: E birin sigade keren. E kelixi bɛndɛ nɛ, e man gbilenma bɛndɛ nɛ.

sentences.english: Who is certain that the spirit of the sons of men goes up to heaven, or that the spirit of the beasts goes down to the earth?
sentences.susu: Nde a kolon xa mixi faxaxi xaxili tema koore nɛ, xa sube faxaxi xaxili goroma bɔxi nɛ?

sentences.english: So I saw that there is nothing better than for a man to have joy in his work — because that is his reward. Who will make him see what will come after him?
sentences.susu: N a kolon fefe mu na naxan fan adamadi bɛ, fo a sɛɛwa a xa wali kui. Na nan findixi Ala xa maragiri ra adamadi bɛ. Nde nɔma a masende a bɛ naxan fama rabade a dangi xanbi?

sentences.english: And again I saw all the cruel things which are done under the sun; there was the weeping of those who have evil done to them, and they had no comforter: and from the hands of the evil-doers there went out power, but they had no comforter.
sentences.susu: N man bara n xaxili rasiga ɲaxankatɛ birin ma, naxan na rabafe yi duniɲa ma. Mixi ɲaxankataxi na wafe, e madunduma yo mu na. Nɔɛ na mixie bɛ naxee na e ɲaxankatafe. E madunduma yo mu na.

sentences.english: So my praise was for the dead who have gone to their death, more than for the living who still have life.
sentences.susu: N bara a maɲɔxun, mixi faxaxi nan sɛɛwaxi dangife mixi baloxi ra.

sentences.english: Yes, happier than the dead or the living seemed he who has not ever been, who has not seen the evil which is done under the sun.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan mu barixi sinden, nee xa hɛɛri dangi mixi faxaxi nun mixi baloxi ra, barima e mu ɲaxankatɛ kolon naxan na rabafe yi duniɲa ma.

sentences.english: And I saw that the cause of all the work and of everything which is done well was man's envy of his neighbour. This again is to no purpose and a desire for wind.
sentences.susu: N bara a to, mixi walima e xunnakeli fenma milɛ kui. Yi fan findixi fe fufafu nan na, alɔ birafe foye fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: The foolish man, folding his hands, takes the flesh of his body for food.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare a bɛlɛxɛe findigilinxi a ma, a mu walima, han a xun nakana.

sentences.english: One hand full of rest is better than two hands full of trouble and desire for wind.
sentences.susu: Bɔɲɛsa dondoronti fisa katɛ gbegbe bɛ. Na katɛ luxi nɛ alɔ mixi naxan birama foye fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Then I came back, and I saw an example of what is to no purpose under the sun.
sentences.susu: N bara fe fufafu gbɛtɛ fan to yi duniɲa ma.

sentences.english: It is one who is by himself, without a second, and without son or brother; but there is no end to all his work, and he has never enough of wealth. For whom, then, am I working and keeping myself from pleasure? This again is to no purpose, and a bitter work.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ nde nu na naxan nu na a kerenyi ma, mixi yo mu nu na a bɛ. A nu walima tɛmui birin, kɔnɔ a mu wasa a xa naafuli ra. A naxa a yɛtɛ maxɔrin, «N na walife tɔɔrɛ kui nde bɛ?» Yi mɔɔli fan findixi fe fufafu nan na.

sentences.english: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their work.
sentences.susu: Mixi firin malanxi sɔɔnɛya dangife mixi ra naxan luma a keren. Na firinyie xa wali dangi na mixi kerenyi gbe ra.

sentences.english: And if one has a fall, the other will give him a hand; but unhappy is the man who is by himself, because he has no helper.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li keren bira, a boore a rakelima nɛ. Kɔnɔ mixi naxan birama, a malima mu na, na tɔɔrɔma nɛ a ɲaaxi ra.

sentences.english: So again, if two are sleeping together they are warm, but how may one be warm by himself?
sentences.susu: Na maniyaxi mixi firin nan na, naxee saxi e boore fɛ ma xinbeli tɛmui, e nu wuyenyi sɔtɔ e boore saabui ra. Kɔnɔ mixi naxan na a kerenyi ma, na xinbeli bama di?

sentences.english: And two attacked by one would be safe, and three cords twisted together are not quickly broken.
sentences.susu: Mixi ɲaaxi nɔma nɛ mixi keren na, kɔnɔ mixi firin tan tima nɛ a kanke. Luuti xɔri saxan malanxi mu bolonma mafuren.

sentences.english: A young man who is poor and wise is better than a king who is old and foolish and will not be guided by the wisdom of others.
sentences.susu: Misikiinɛ xa di naxan xaxili fan, a sɛnbɛ gbo mangɛ bɛ naxan mu fata marasi fanyi nun a ɲaaxi tagi rasade.

sentences.english: Because out of a prison the young man comes to be king, though by birth he was only a poor man in the kingdom.
sentences.susu: Na mixi mɔɔli nɔma minide geeli kui, a findi mangɛ ra. A barixi setareɲa nan kui, a fa mangɛya sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: I saw all the living under the sun round the young man who was to be ruler in place of the king.
sentences.susu: Duniɲa mixi birin saxanyi nan nabama, i na dangi mixi gbɛtɛ fa ti i ɲɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: There was no end of all the people, of all those whose head he was, but they who come later will have no delight in him. This again is to no purpose and desire for wind.
sentences.susu: Mixi wuyaxi dangixi nɛ beenun na kanyi xa bari. Mixi naxee fama a xanbi ra, a xa fe mu fama rafande e ma. Na fan findixi fe fufafu nan na, alɔ mixi naxan birafe foye fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Put your feet down with care when you go to the house of God, for it is better to give ear than to make the burned offerings of the foolish, whose knowledge is only of doing evil.
sentences.susu: I naxa gbata i dɛ rabide wɔyɛnyi xili ma, i naxa gbata laayidi tongode Ala bɛ, barima Ala tan na koore nɛ, kɔnɔ i tan na bɔxi nan ma. Awa, i xa wɔyɛnyi naxa wuya.

sentences.english: Be not unwise with your mouth, and let not your heart be quick to say anything before God, because God is in heaven and you are on the earth — so let not the number of your words be great.
sentences.susu: Alɔ xiye to kelima maɲɔxunyi gbegbe ma, xaxilitareɲa fan kelima dɛ wuya nan ma.

sentences.english: As a dream comes from much business, so the voice of a foolish man comes with words in great number.
sentences.susu: Xa i bara laayidi tongo Ala bɛ, i naxa dugundi a rakamalide. Xaxilitareɲa mu rafan Ala ma. A lanma i xa i xa laayidi rakamali.

sentences.english: When you take an oath before God, put it quickly into effect, because he has no pleasure in the foolish; keep the oath you have taken.
sentences.susu: Laayidi tongotareɲa fisa laayidi rakamalitareɲa bɛ.

sentences.english: It is better not to take an oath than to take an oath and not keep it.
sentences.susu: I naxa tin i xa wɔyɛnyi xa findi yunubi ra. I naxa a fala Ala xa xɛɛra bɛ, «N mu nu wama laayidi yati tongofe.» Na fe mɔɔli Ala raxɔnɔma nɛ, a a niya i xa wali xun xa rakana.

sentences.english: Let not your mouth make your flesh do evil. And say not before the angel, It was an error. So that God may not be angry with your words and put an end to the work of your hands.
sentences.susu: Xiye wuyaxi safe nun wɔyɛnyi tife findixi fe fufafu nan na. Na kui a lanma i xa gaaxu Ala ya ra.

sentences.english: Because much talk comes from dreams and things of no purpose. But let the fear of God be in you.
sentences.susu: I naxa tɛrɛnna xa a sa li i mixie toma taa kui naxee fuma misikiinɛe ma, e sɛriyɛ kana, e kiiti ɲaaxi sa tinxintɔɛe ma. Mangɛ a boore mangɛ nan malima, han a mangɛya xungbe sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: If you see the poor under a cruel yoke, and law and right being violently overturned in a country, be not surprised, because one authority is keeping watch on another and there are higher than they.
sentences.susu: E birin geenima xɛ samae nan saabui ra, hali mangɛ xungbe.

sentences.english: It is good generally for a country where the land is worked to have a king.
sentences.susu: Kɔbiri rafan mixi naxan ma, a mu wasama. Bannaya rafan naxan ma, a naafuli mu a ralima. Fe fufafu nan na ki.

sentences.english: He who has a love for silver never has enough silver, or he who has love for wealth, enough profit. This again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Harige gboma ki naxɛ, a donmae fan gboma na ki nɛ. Na kui munafanyi mundun na harige kanyi bɛ, ba a ya tife ra a harige ra?

sentences.english: When goods are increased, the number of those who take of them is increased; and what profit has the owner but to see them?
sentences.susu: Walikɛ luga ba, a mu luga ba, a xixɔli fanyi rabama nɛ. Kɔnɔ banna xa naafuli a niyama nɛ a mu xixɔli fanyi raba.

sentences.english: The sleep of a working man is sweet, if he has little food or much; but to him who is full, sleep will not come.
sentences.susu: N fe magaaxuxi nde rakɔrɔsixi yi duniɲa ma: Kankanfe bannaya ma han a banna tɔɔrɔ,

sentences.english: There is a great evil which I have seen under the sun — wealth kept by the owner to be his downfall.
sentences.susu: xa na mu a ra, bannaya lɔɛfe tɔɔrɛ nde saabui ra, a fa li banna xa di mu kɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And I saw the destruction of his wealth by an evil chance; and when he became the father of a son he had nothing in his hand.
sentences.susu: Adamadi mini ki naxɛ a nga tɛgɛ, a man gbilenma bɛndɛ a mageli ra na ki nɛ. A mu sese xaninma a xun ma a naxan sɔtɔ a xa wali kui.

sentences.english: As he came from his mother at birth, so does he go again; he gets from his work no reward which he may take away in his hand.
sentences.susu: Yi fe xɔrɔxɔ. Adamadi fa ki naxɛ yi duniɲa ma, a man sigama na ki nɛ. A xa katɛ findixi fe fufafu nan na.

sentences.english: And this again is a great evil, that in all points as he came so will he go; and what profit has he in working for the wind?
sentences.susu: A duniɲa igirima dimi nan kui, kɔntɔfili, tɔɔrɛ, nun bɔɲɛ maɲaaxui kui.

sentences.english: All his days are in the dark, and he has much sorrow, pain, disease, and trouble.
sentences.susu: Na kui n naxa a fahaamu a fan adama bɛ xa a a dɛge, a a min, a sɛɛwa a xa wali ra, a naxan nabama duniɲa ma a xa simaya kui, Ala naxan nagirixi a ma na nan findixi a xa geeni ra.

sentences.english: This is what I have seen: it is good and fair for a man to take meat and drink and to have joy in all his work under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; that is his reward.
sentences.susu: Xa Ala a ragiri mixi ma a xa harige sɔtɔ, a fa sɛɛwa na ra han a wasa, na bara findi Ala xa ki nan na.

sentences.english: Every man to whom God has given money and wealth and the power to have pleasure in it and to do his part and have joy in his work: this is given by God.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a mu kɔntɔfilima a xa simaya xa dunke xa fe ra, barima Ala bara a niya a bɔɲɛ xa lu sɛɛwɛ kui tun.

sentences.english: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is hard on men;
sentences.susu: N fe xɔrɔxɔɛ gbɛtɛ nan to yi duniɲa ma:

sentences.english: A man to whom God gives money, wealth, and honour so that he has all his desires but God does not give him the power to have joy of it, and a strange man takes it. This is to no purpose and an evil disease.
sentences.susu: Ala bannaya nun binyɛ ragirixi mixi nde ma han a wasa na birin na, kɔnɔ Ala fa a niya a mu xan a yi, a fa a lu mixi gbɛtɛ yi ra. Fe fufafu nan na ki naxan xɔrɔxɔ a gbe ra.

sentences.english: If a man has a hundred children, and his life is long so that the days of his years are great in number, but his soul takes no pleasure in good, and he is not honoured at his death; I say that a birth before its time is better than he.
sentences.susu: Hali mixi di kɛmɛ sɔtɔ, a naxa simaya xɔn kuye sɔtɔ, xa a mu nɔma sɛɛwade a harige ra, ɲama mu fa a ragata gaburi kui a ragata ki ma, diyɔrɛ naxan baxi a nga furi, na fisa na kanyi bɛ.

sentences.english: In wind it came and to the dark it will go, and with the dark will its name be covered.
sentences.susu: Na diyɔrɛ mu findima a ra, a kelima dimi nan kui, a xili yati mu falama.

sentences.english: Yes, it saw not the sun, and it had no knowledge; it is better with this than with the other.
sentences.susu: A mu soge xa naiyalanyi toxi, a mu sese kolonxi, kɔnɔ a xa fe fisa na naafuli kanyi bɛ,

sentences.english: And though he goes on living a thousand years twice over and does not see good, are not the two going to the same place?
