sentences.susu: hali naafuli kanyi fa lu duniɲa ma ɲɛ wulu firin sɛɛwɛtareɲa kui. E birin mu sigama aligiyama xɛ?

sentences.english: All the work of man is for his mouth, and still he has a desire for food.
sentences.susu: Mixi xa katɛ birin nabama furi fe nan ma fe ra, kɔnɔ a mu wasama feo.

sentences.english: What have the wise more than the foolish? and what has the poor man by walking wisely before the living?
sentences.susu: Munse luma xaxilima yi ra naxan mu na xaxilitare yi ra? Munse luma misikiinɛ bɛ xa a ɲɛrɛ ki fan a boore ya xɔri?

sentences.english: What the eyes see is better than the wandering of desire. This is to no purpose and a desire for wind.
sentences.susu: Se toxi fisa maɲɔxunyi bɛ? Fe fufafu nan na ki naxan luxi alɔ mixi naxan birafe foye fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: That which is, has been named before, and of what man is there is knowledge. He has no power against one stronger than he.
sentences.susu: Daalise birin ɲan bara xili sɔtɔ, adama naxan nu na, a ɲan bara kolon. Adama mu nɔma mixi ra naxan sɛnbɛ gbo a bɛ.

sentences.english: There are words without number for increasing what is to no purpose, but what is man profited by them?
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛnyi na gbo, fe fufafu fan gboma nɛ. A mu mixi yo malima.

sentences.english: Who is able to say what is good for man in life all the days of his foolish life which he goes through like a shade? who will say what is to be after him under the sun?
sentences.susu: Nde a kolon fe naxan fan adamadi bɛ a xa duniɲɛigiri kui, naxan dangima mafuren mafuren alɔ niini? Nde nɔma a falade a bɛ fe naxan nabama a faxa xanbi?

sentences.english: A good name is better than oil of great price, and the day of death than the day of birth.
sentences.susu: Xili fanyi fan dangi labundɛ fanyi ra. I faxa lɔxɔɛ fan dangi i bari lɔxɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: It is better to go to the house of weeping, than to go to the house of feasting; because that is the end of every man, and the living will take it to their hearts.
sentences.susu: Sofe kaaɲɛ banxi fisa sofe xulun banxi bɛ, barima faxɛ ragirixi adama birin bɛ. A lanma mixi baloxi xa ratu na ma.

sentences.english: Sorrow is better than joy; when the face is sad the mind gets better.
sentences.susu: Sunnunyi fisa yele bɛ, barima mixi bɔɲɛ fanyi sɔtɔma nɛ sunnunyi kui.

sentences.english: The hearts of the wise are in the house of weeping; but the hearts of the foolish are in the house of joy.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima a ɲɔxɔ rasigama nɛ faxɛ ma, xaxilitare tan na yelefe nan tui.

sentences.english: It is better to take note of the protest of the wise, than for a man to give ear to the song of the foolish.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa xurui fisa xaxilitare xa matɔxɔɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: Like the cracking of thorns under a pot, so is the laugh of a foolish man; and this again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare xa yele luxi nɛ alɔ bolee naxee mabulama tunde bun ma. Fe fufafu nan na ki.

sentences.english: The wise are troubled by the ways of the cruel, and the giving of money is the destruction of the heart.
sentences.susu: Kɔbiri tinxintare a niyama nɛ xaxilima xa findi xaxilitare ra, ye dɔxɔɛ a bɔɲɛ mafindima nɛ.

sentences.english: The end of a thing is better than its start, and a gentle spirit is better than pride.
sentences.susu: Fe raɲɔnyi fisa a fɔlɛ bɛ. Mixi sabarixi fisa yɛtɛ igboe bɛ.

sentences.english: Be not quick to let your spirit be angry; because wrath is in the heart of the foolish.
sentences.susu: I bɔɲɛ naxa gbata tede, barima xaxilitaree bɔɲɛ nan tema.

sentences.english: Say not, Why were the days which have gone by better than these? Such a question comes not from wisdom.
sentences.susu: I naxa lu a fala ra, «Singe dangi yakɔsi ra.» Xaxilimaya wɔyɛnyi mu na na ra.

sentences.english: Wisdom together with a heritage is good, and a profit to those who see the sun.
sentences.susu: Xaxilimaya luxi nɛ alɔ kɛ, a munafanyi na duniɲa mixi birin bɛ.

sentences.english: Wisdom keeps a man from danger even as money does; but the value of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to its owner.
sentences.susu: Xaxilimaya findixi mixi xa kantari nan na, kɔbiri fan findixi mixi xa kantari nan na, kɔnɔ xaxilimaya nan fisa, barima a xaxilima rakisima.

sentences.english: Give thought to the work of God. Who will make straight what he has made bent?
sentences.susu: Ala xa wali mato. A naxan madalin, nde nɔma na matinxinde?

sentences.english: In the day of wealth have joy, but in the day of evil take thought: God has put the one against the other, so that man may not be certain what will be after him.
sentences.susu: I xa sɛɛwa hɛɛri tɛmui. Tɔɔrɛ tɛmui na a li, i xa ratu a ma, a Ala nan na firinyi birin daaxi. Na kui adamadi mu nɔma a xa tina kolonde.

sentences.english: These two have I seen in my life which is to no purpose: a good man coming to his end in his righteousness, and an evil man whose days are long in his evil-doing.
sentences.susu: N ma simaya fufafu kui, n a toxi nɛ tinxintɔɛ nde faxa simaya dunke kui hali a to tinxinxi, tinxintare nde bu duniɲa hali a to mu tinxin.

sentences.english: Be not given overmuch to righteousness and be not over-wise. Why let destruction come on you?
sentences.susu: I naxa i yɛtɛ findi tinxintɔɛ ra, i naxa i yɛtɛ findi lɔnnila ra, xa na mu a ra i i yɛtɛ kanama nɛ.

sentences.english: Be not evil overmuch, and be not foolish. Why come to your end before your time?
sentences.susu: I naxa findi tinxintare ra, xa na mu a ra i faxama nɛ beenu i xa waxati xa a li.

sentences.english: It is good to take this in your hand and not to keep your hand from that; he who has the fear of God will be free of the two.
sentences.susu: A lanma i xa i ɲɔxɔ sa na marasi firinyi xɔn ma. Ala xa yaragaaxui xa fe sɔɔnɛyama nɛ na birin kui.

sentences.english: Wisdom makes a wise man stronger than ten rulers in a town.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa xaxilimaya a sɛnbɛ gboma nɛ dangi taa mangɛ fu ra.

sentences.english: There is no man on earth of such righteousness that he does good and is free from sin all his days.
sentences.susu: Tinxintɔɛ mu na yi duniɲa ma, naxan fe fanyi tun nabama, a mu yunubi yo raba.

sentences.english: Do not give ear to all the words which men say, for fear of hearing the curses of your servant.
sentences.susu: I naxa i tuli mati mixi xa wɔyɛnyi birin na, xa na mu a ra i fama i xa konyi xui mɛde a i dankama,

sentences.english: Your heart has knowledge how frequently others have been cursed by you.
sentences.susu: alɔ i tan yati bara a raba sanya wuyaxi mixie ra.

sentences.english: All this I have put to the test by wisdom; I said, I will be wise, but it was far from me.
sentences.susu: N na birin igbɛxi nɛ xaxilimaya ra. N naxa a fala, «N xa findi xaxilima ra,» kɔnɔ n mu nɔ.

sentences.english: Far off is true existence, and very deep; who may have knowledge of it?
sentences.susu: Xaxilimaya tan tilin, a makuya won na, nde nɔma a fahaamude?

sentences.english: I gave my mind to knowledge and to searching for wisdom and the reason of things, and to the discovery that sin is foolish, and that to be foolish is to be without one's senses.
sentences.susu: Na kui n naxa kata na kolonde, n xa so xaxilimaya kui, n xa fahaamui sɔtɔ, n xa a kolon tinxintareya findixi xaxilitareɲa nan na, xaxilitareɲa fan findixi daxuɲa nan na.

sentences.english: And I saw a thing more bitter than death, even the woman whose heart is full of tricks and nets, and whose hands are as bands. He with whom God is pleased will get free from her, but the sinner will be taken by her.
sentences.susu: N bara fe nde to naxan xɔnɔ dangi faxɛ ra. Ginɛ na a ra naxan findixi yɛlɛ ra, naxan bɔɲɛ findixi gantanyi ra, naxan bɛlɛxɛe luxi alɔ luuti balanxi. Mixi naxan nafan Ala ma, a kelima nɛ na ginɛ xun ma, kɔnɔ na ginɛ yunubitɔɛ nan masɔtɔma.

sentences.english: Look! this I have seen, said the Preacher, taking one thing after another to get the true account,
sentences.susu: N tan kawandila yi nan to n ma fe matoxi birin kui:

sentences.english: For which my soul is still searching, but I have it not; one man among a thousand have I seen; but a woman among all these I have not seen.
sentences.susu: N naxa xɛmɛ tinxinxi keren to xɛmɛ wulu ya ma, n naxa a fen han, kɔnɔ n mu ginɛ yo to ɲama ya ma naxan tinxin.

sentences.english: This only have I seen, that God made men upright, but they have been searching out all sorts of inventions.
sentences.susu: N yi nan gbansan to kɔrɛ: Ala adamadie daaxi nɛ e tinxinxi, kɔnɔ e tan naxa e yɛtɛ madaxu.

sentences.english: Who is like the wise man? and to whom is the sense of anything clear? A man's wisdom makes his face shining, and his hard face will be changed.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima maniyɛ mu na. Nde fata fe tilinxi fatanfaside? Xaxilima yatagi nɔrɔma a xa xaxilimaya saabui nan na, a lahalɛ masarama nɛ.

sentences.english: I say to you, Keep the king's law, from respect for the oath of God.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, a lanma wo xa mangɛ xa yaamari rabatu, barima wo bara wo rakali Ala ya xɔri.

sentences.english: Be not quick to go from before him. Be not fixed in an evil design, because he does whatever is pleasing to him.
sentences.susu: I naxa gbata kelide mangɛ ya xɔri. I naxa ti fefe xanbi ra naxan mu fan. Mangɛ a waxɔnfe nan nabama.

sentences.english: The word of a king has authority; and who may say to him, What is this you are doing?
sentences.susu: A lu ki yo ki, nɔɛ na mangɛ nan yi. Nde nɔma a matandide?

sentences.english: Whoever keeps the law will come to no evil: and a wise man's heart has knowledge of time and of decision.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan mangɛ xa yamari rabatuma, fe ɲaaxi yo mu a sɔtɔma. Xaxilima a ɲɛrɛ ki nun ɲɛrɛ waxati kolon.

sentences.english: For every purpose there is a time and a decision, because the sorrow of man is great in him.
sentences.susu: Fe birin lanma a xa raba a waxati nun a kɛɲa ma, hali na fa findima fe xɔrɔxɔɛ ra mixi bɛ.

sentences.english: No one is certain what is to be, and who is able to say to him when it will be?
sentences.susu: Mixi to mu a kolon fe naxee fama rabade, nde nɔma nee tagi rabade a bɛ?

sentences.english: No man has authority over the wind, to keep the wind; or is ruler over the day of his death. In war no man's time is free, and evil will not keep the sinner safe.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu nɔma a ɲɛngi yamaride, mixi yo mu nɔma a faxa lɔxɔɛ sugandide. Mixi mu nɔma kelide gere xun ma, tinxintareya mu fe kobi rabae bɛɲinma.

sentences.english: All this have I seen, and have given my heart to all the work which is done under the sun: there is a time when man has power over man for his destruction.
sentences.susu: N bara yi birin rakɔrɔsi duniɲa ma. N naxa mixi to a na a boore yamarife, a fa a yɛtɛ tɔɔrɔ na kui.

sentences.english: And then I saw evil men put to rest, taken even from the holy place; and they went about and were praised in the town because of what they had done. This again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: N naxa mixi ɲaaxie to naxee ragatama binyɛ kui, mixie nu naxee matɔxɔma hɔrɔmɔlingira yire taa kui. Fe fufafu nan na ki.

sentences.english: Because punishment for an evil work comes not quickly, the minds of the sons of men are fully given to doing evil.
sentences.susu: Xa fe kobi rabae mu ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔ a tɛmui, ɲama fan fama nɛ birade e waxɔnfe ɲaaxie fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his life is long, I am certain that it will be well for those who go in fear of God and are in fear before him.
sentences.susu: N a kolon hali fe kobi rabae gbilen fe ɲaaxi rabafe ra han sanmaya kɛmɛ, sɔɔnɛya tan nabama nɛ mixi bɛ naxan gaaxuma Ala ya ra, naxan luma a batu ra.

sentences.english: But it will not be well for the evil-doer; he will not make his days long like a shade, because he has no fear before God.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ fe mu sɔɔnɛyama mixi ɲaaxie bɛ naxee mu gaaxuma Ala ya ra, e xa simaya xɔn mu kuyama alɔ mixi niini.

sentences.english: There is a thing which is to no purpose done on the earth: that there are good men to whom is given the same punishment as those who are evil, and there are evil men who get the reward of the good. I say that this again is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Fe fufafu gbɛtɛ na na yi duniɲa ma: Fe xɔrɔxɔɛ naxan lan a xa dɔxɔ mixi ɲaaxi ma, na nan dɔxɔma tinxintɔɛ ma. Fe fanyi naxan lan a xa raba tinxintɔɛ bɛ, na nan nabama mixi ɲaaxi bɛ. N xa a fala wo bɛ, na fe mɔɔli findixi fe fufafu nan na.

sentences.english: So I gave praise to joy, because there is nothing better for a man to do under the sun than to take meat and drink and be happy; for that will be with him in his work all the days of his life which God gives him under the sun.
sentences.susu: Na kui a lanma adama xa sɛɛwa a xa duniɲɛigiri kui. Fe yo mu na naxan fisa yi bɛ: Mixi lanma e xa e dɛge, e xa e min, e xa sɛɛwa. Na ki a sɛɛwama nɛ a xa wali ra a xa duniɲɛigiri kui, Ala naxan fixi a ma duniɲa bɛndɛ fuɲi fari.

sentences.english: When I gave my mind to the knowledge of wisdom and to seeing the business which is done on the earth (and there are those whose eyes see not sleep by day or by night),
sentences.susu: N to natɛ tongo n xa fahaamui sɔtɔ adamadi xa wali xa fe ra, a naxan nabama kɔɛ nun yanyi,

sentences.english: Then I saw all the work of God, and that man may not get knowledge of the work which is done under the sun; because, if a man gives hard work to the search he will not get knowledge, and even if the wise man seems to be coming to the end of his search, still he will be without knowledge.
sentences.susu: n naxa Ala xa wali mato. Mixi yo mu nɔma sode fe birin kui naxan nabama duniɲa ma. Hali a kata han, a mu a kolonma feo. Hali xaxilima naxan a falama a bara gɛ na kolonde, a mu nɔma na kolonde yati yati.

sentences.english: All this I took to heart, and my heart saw it all: that the upright and the wise and their works are in the hand of God; and men may not be certain if it will be love or hate; all is to no purpose before them.
sentences.susu: N to n maɲɔxun na fe birin ma, n a toxi nɛ tinxintɔɛe, xaxilimae, nun e xa katɛ birin kelima Ala nan ma. Adamadi mu a kolon a fama naxan lide a yara, xanunteya xa na mu a ra xɔnnanteya. Na birin na Ala nan yi.

sentences.english: Because to all there is one event, to the upright man and to the evil, to the clean and to the unclean, to him who makes an offering and to him who makes no offering; as is the good so is the sinner; he who takes an oath is as he who has fear of it.
sentences.susu: Adamadi birin sigama nɛ aligiyama. Tinxintɔɛ ba, tinxintare ba, sɛniyɛntɔɛ ba, sɛniyɛntare ba, sɛrɛxɛba ba, sɛrɛxɛbatare ba. Mixi fanyi ba, mixi ɲaaxi ba e birin sigama nɛ aligiyama. Mixi naxan laayidi tongoma ba, mixi naxan mu suusama na tongode ba, e birin sigama nɛ aligiyama.

sentences.english: This is evil in all things which are done under the sun: that there is one fate for all, and the hearts of the sons of men are full of evil; while they have life their hearts are foolish, and after that — to the dead.
sentences.susu: Fe xɔrɔxɔɛ nan yi ki fe birin ya ma duniɲa ma: maraɲɔn ki keren nan na nee birin bɛ. Adamadie bɔɲɛ rafexi fe ɲaaxi nan na, e walima xaxilitareɲa nan na e xa duniɲɛigiri kui. Na dangi xanbi, e faxamixie lima nɛ aligiyama.

sentences.english: For him who is joined to all the living there is hope; a living dog is better than a dead lion.
sentences.susu: Mixi baloxi gbansan nɔma a xaxili tide fe nde ma. Bare ɲiɲɛ fisa yɛtɛ faxaxi bɛ.

sentences.english: The living are conscious that death will come to them, but the dead are not conscious of anything, and they no longer have a reward, because there is no memory of them.
sentences.susu: Naxee baloxi, nee a kolon a e faxama nɛ, kɔnɔ mixi faxaxie tan mu fefe kolon. Sare fi yo mu na e bɛ sɔnɔn, e xa fe yati bara nɛɛmu mixie ra.

sentences.english: Their love and their hate and their envy are now ended; and they have no longer a part for ever in anything which is done under the sun.
sentences.susu: E xa xanunteya, e xa xɔnnanteya, e waxɔnfe, nee birin bara ɲɔn. E tan gbe yo mu na yi duniɲa fee tan ya ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: Come, take your bread with joy, and your wine with a glad heart. God has taken pleasure in your works.
sentences.susu: Siga, i i dɛge sɛɛwɛ kui, i i xa wɛni min bɔɲɛ fanyi kui. Ala wama na nan xɔn i bɛ.

sentences.english: Let your clothing be white at all times, and let not your head be without oil.
sentences.susu: I xa sose fiixɛ ragoro i ma, i xa labundɛ fanyi sa i fate ma.

sentences.english: Have joy with the woman of your love all the days of your foolish life which he gives you under the sun. Because that is your part in life and in your work which you do under the sun.
sentences.susu: I xa duniɲa igiri sɛɛwɛ kui wo nun i xanuntenyi ginɛ. Ala bara yi simaya nan fi i ma. Hali a to dangima alɔ foye, hali a xɔrɔxɔ, Ala xa maragiri na a ra i bɛ.

sentences.english: Whatever comes to your hand to do with all your power, do it because there is no work, or thought, or knowledge, or wisdom in the place of the dead to which you are going.
sentences.susu: I nɔma wali naxan na, i xa na raba i sɛnbɛ birin na, barima i naxan nabama duniɲa ma, alɔ walife, fe matofe, fe fahaamufe, nun fe kolonfe, na sese mu na aligiyama i sigafe dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And again I saw under the sun that the reward goes not to him who is quick, or the fruits of war to the strong; and there is no bread for the wise, or wealth for men of learning, or respect for those who have knowledge; but time and chance come to all.
sentences.susu: N man bara fe gbɛtɛ to yi duniɲa ma: Naxan xulun dangi a boore ra, a mu gbata geenima tɛmui birin xɛ, naxan sɛnbɛ gbo dangi a boore ra, a mu gere geenima tɛmui birin xɛ, naxan xaxili fan a boore bɛ, a mu donse sɔtɔma tɛmui birin xɛ, naxan ma lɔnni dangi a boore ra, a mu naafuli sɔtɔma tɛmui birin xɛ, naxan xa fahaamui gbo a boore bɛ, a mu hinnɛ sɔtɔma tɛmui birin xɛ. Ala xa maragiri tan fe birin nabama a waxati nɛ.

sentences.english: Even man has no knowledge of his time; like fishes taken in an evil net, or like birds taken by deceit, are the sons of men taken in an evil time when it comes suddenly on them.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu a kolon fe fama a lide tɛmui naxɛ: Yɛxɛ suxuma nɛ yɛlɛ xɔrɔxɔɛ kui, xɔni suxuma nɛ gantanyi ra. Na ki fe xɔrɔxɔɛ adamadi tɛrɛnnama nɛ kerenyi ra.

sentences.english: This again I have seen under the sun as wisdom and it seemed great to me.
sentences.susu: N man bara yi xaxilimaya misaali to duniɲa ma naxan tide gbo.

sentences.english: There was a little town and the number of its men was small, and there came a great king against it and made an attack on it, building works of war round about it.
sentences.susu: Taa xuri nde nu na, mixi mu nu gbo dɛnnaxɛ. Mangɛ sɛnbɛma nde naxa na taa gere, a fa tede yailan na taa tɛtɛ bunyi.

sentences.english: Now there was in the town a poor, wise man, and he, by his wisdom, kept the town safe. But no one had any memory of that same poor man.
sentences.susu: Na taaka nde nu na, naxan findixi setare xaxilima ra. A naxa na taa rakisi a xa xaxilimaya saabui ra, kɔnɔ na dangi xanbi mixi yo mu ratu a xa fe ma.

sentences.english: Then I said, Wisdom is better than strength, but the poor man's wisdom is not respected, and his words are not given a hearing.
sentences.susu: Na kui n naxɛ, Xaxilimaya fisa ɲalamaya bɛ, kɔnɔ setare xa xaxilimaya maberema nɛ, mixi mu a xa masenyi suxuma.

sentences.english: The words of the wise which come quietly to the ear are noted more than the cry of a ruler among the foolish.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima xa masenyi raxaraxi ramɛfe, na fisa mangɛ xa sɔnxɔɛ rate bɛ xaxilitaree tagi.

sentences.english: Wisdom is better than instruments of war, but one sinner is the destruction of much good.
sentences.susu: Xaxilimaya fisa geresosee bɛ, kɔnɔ yunubitɔɛ keren gbansan nɔma fe fanyi gbegbe xun nakanade.

sentences.english: Dead flies make the oil of the perfumer give out an evil smell; more valued is a little wisdom than the great glory of the foolish.
sentences.susu: Tugitugi na faxa labundɛ xun ma, labundɛ xiri kanama nɛ. Xaxilitareɲa nan xui mɛma dangife xaxilimaya xui ra.

sentences.english: The heart of the wise man goes in the right direction; but the heart of a foolish man in the wrong.
sentences.susu: Xaxilima bɔɲɛ matinse, xaxilitare bɔɲɛ ɲaaxu.

sentences.english: And when the foolish man is walking in the way, he has no sense and lets everyone see that he is foolish.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare a xa xaxilitareɲa masenma nɛ birin bɛ a xa ɲɛrɛ kui.

sentences.english: If the wrath of the ruler is against you, keep in your place; in him who keeps quiet even great sins may be overlooked.
sentences.susu: Xa i xa mangɛ xɔnɔ i ma, i naxa keli i xa wali xun ma, i xa sabari fe xɔrɔxɔɛ rabɔrɔxɔma.

sentences.english: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, like an error which comes by chance from a ruler:
sentences.susu: N fe xɔrɔxɔɛ nde fan toxi yi duniɲa ma naxan kelixi mangɛ ma:

sentences.english: The foolish are placed in high positions, but men of wealth are kept low.
sentences.susu: A nɔɛ fima nɛ xaxilitare nde ma, banna nde tan mu nɔɛ yo sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: I have seen servants on horses, and rulers walking on the earth as servants.
sentences.susu: N bara konyi nde to a soe ragima, mangɛ nde fa a ɲɛrɛ a sanyi ra.

sentences.english: He who makes a hole for others will himself go into it, and for him who makes a hole through a wall the bite of a snake will be a punishment.
sentences.susu: Yili ge nɔma birade a xa yili gexi kui, mixi naxan yale tima tɛtɛ ma, bɔximase nɔma na fan xinde.

sentences.english: He who gets out stones from the earth will be damaged by them, and in the cutting of wood there is danger.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan gɛmɛ masolima, a nɔma a maxɔnɔde gɛmɛ ra. Mixi naxan yege bɔɔma, a nɔma a maxɔnɔde yege ra.

sentences.english: If the iron has no edge, and he does not make it sharp, then he has to put out more strength; but wisdom makes things go well.
sentences.susu: Xa beera kole torixi, a mu ralugan, na a niyama nɛ wali xa xɔrɔxɔ. Xaxilimaya xunnakeli fima mixi ma na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: If a snake gives a bite before the word of power is said, then there is no longer any use in the word of power.
sentences.susu: Xa bɔximase mixi xin beenun bɔximase suxuma xa a suxu, mixi naxan bɔximase suxuma, a mu geenima.

sentences.english: The words of a wise man's mouth are sweet to all, but the lips of a foolish man are his destruction.
sentences.susu: Hinnɛ gbegbe na xaxilima xa masenyi kui, kɔnɔ xaxilitare tan xa wɔyɛnyi a yɛtɛ bɔnɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: The first words of his mouth are foolish, and the end of his talk is evil crime.
sentences.susu: A xa masenyi fɔlɔma lɔnnitareɲa ra, a raɲɔn daxuɲa ra.

sentences.english: The foolish are full of words; man has no knowledge of what will be; and who is able to say what will be after him?
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare xa wɔyɛnyi wuya. Adamadi mu a kolon fe naxan fama fade. Nde a rakolonma fe ra naxan fama a lide?

sentences.english: The work of the foolish will be a weariness to him, because he has no knowledge of the way to the town.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare a yɛtɛ rataganma, hali taa kira, a mu a kolon.

sentences.english: Unhappy is the land whose king is a boy, and whose rulers are feasting in the morning.
sentences.susu: Ɲaxankatɛ na taa bɛ naxan xa mangɛ findixi fonike yɔrɛ ra, naxan xa kuntigie kurunma xulunyi tife ra.

sentences.english: Happy is the land whose ruler is of noble birth, and whose chiefs take food at the right time, for strength and not for feasting.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛlɛxinyi na taa bɛ naxan xa mangɛ fatanxi mangɛ bɔnsɔɛ ra, naxan xa kuntigie e dɛgema a waxati ma sɛnbɛ sɔtɔfe ra, e mu siisi.

sentences.english: When no work is done the roof goes in, and when the hands do nothing water comes into the house.
sentences.susu: Xa banxi kanyi tunnaxɔnɔ, banxi xunyi birama nɛ, xa a mu a findi tunnabɛxi ra, a xa banxi fama nɛ minide.

sentences.english: A feast is for laughing, and wine makes glad the heart; but by the one and the other money is wasted.
sentences.susu: Mixi donse rafalama nɛ alako a xa ɲɛlɛxin, a wɛni minma nɛ alako a xa sɛɛwa, a kɔbiri sɔtɔma nɛ alako a hayi birin xa fan.

sentences.english: Say not a curse against the king, even in your thoughts; and even secretly say not a curse against the man of wealth; because a bird of the air will take the voice, and that which has wings will give news of it.
sentences.susu: I naxa mangɛ danka hali i xa maɲɔxunyi kui, i naxa banna danka hali i xa konkoe kui, barima xɔni nde i xui xaninma nɛ, a na fala mixi nde bɛ.

sentences.english: Put out your bread on the face of the waters; for after a long time it will come back to you again.
sentences.susu: Taali ndee nan yi ki: Xa i taami woli ye ma, i fama nɛ a masɔtɔde lɔxɔɛ nde.

sentences.english: Give a part to seven or even to eight, because you have no knowledge of the evil which will be on the earth.
sentences.susu: I xa i xa sɔtɔse taxu mixi solofere ra, xa na mu a ra, mixi solomasaxan, barima i mu a kolon ɲaxankatɛ naxan fama duniɲa lide.

sentences.english: If the clouds are full of rain, they send it down on the earth; and if a tree comes down to the south, or the north, in whatever place it comes down, there it will be.
sentences.susu: Xa nuxui rafexi ye ra, tunɛ fama nɛ birade bɔxi ma. Xa wuri bira yire fanyi ma, xa a bira kɔɔla ma, a luma naa nɛ.

sentences.english: He who is watching the wind will not get the seed planted, and he who is looking at the clouds will not get in the grain.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo bɔnbɔ foye rabɛnfe ra, na mu sansi sima. Mixi yo bɔnbɔ nuxui matofe ra, na mu fama sansi xabade.

sentences.english: As you have no knowledge of the way of the wind, or of the growth of the bones in the body of her who is with child, even so you have no knowledge of the works of God who has made all.
sentences.susu: I mu ɲɛngi nun xɔrie rafala ki kolon furi ginɛ furi kui, i man mu Ala Daali Mangɛ xa wali fan kolon.

sentences.english: In the morning put your seed into the earth, and till the evening let not your hand be at rest; because you are not certain which will do well, this or that — or if the two will be equally good.
sentences.susu: I xa wakili kelife gɛɛsɛgɛ han nunmare sansi sife ra, barima i mu a kolon i xa wali mundun fama sɔɔnɛyade.

sentences.english: Truly the light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
sentences.susu: Naiyalanyi tofe ɲɔxun.

sentences.english: But even if a man's life is long and he has joy in all his years, let him keep in mind the dark days, because they will be great in number. Whatever may come is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: A lanma mixi xa sɛɛwa a xa simaya ra, kɔnɔ a naxa nɛɛmu dimi ma naxan nu na a xa simaya kui. Fe naxan birin fama, fe fufafu na a ra.

sentences.english: Have joy, O young man, while you are young; and let your heart be glad in the days of your strength, and go in the ways of your heart, and in the desire of your eyes; but be certain that for all these things God will be your judge.
sentences.susu: Fonike, i xa ɲɛlɛxin i xa fonikeya kui, i sondonyi xa sɛɛwa i xa fonikeya waxati kui. I xa bira i bɔɲɛ nun i waxɔnfe fɔxɔ ra, kɔnɔ i xa a kolon a Ala i makiitima nɛ na birin ma.

sentences.english: So put away trouble from your heart, and sorrow from your flesh; because the early years and the best years are to no purpose.
sentences.susu: Na kui kɔntɔfili makuya i ra, tɔɔrɛ keri i fɔxɔ ra. Fonikeya findixi fe fufafu nan na.

sentences.english: Let your mind be turned to your Maker in the days of your strength, while the evil days come not, and the years are far away when you will say, I have no pleasure in them;
sentences.susu: I xa ratu i Daali Marigi ma i xa fonikeya kui, beenun i nimisa lɔxɔɛ xa fa, beenun tɔɔrɛ waxati xa i li, i fa a fala, «Sɛɛwɛ yo mu na n bɛ sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, are not dark, and the clouds come not back after the rain;
sentences.susu: I xa ratu a ma beenun soge xa dimi, beenun kike nun tunbuie xa ifɔɔrɔ, beenun nuxui xa siga tunɛ bira xanbi.

sentences.english: In the day when the keepers of the house are shaking for fear, and the strong men are bent down, and the women who were crushing the grain are at rest because their number is small, and those looking out of the windows are unable to see;
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui banxi kantɛe sɛrɛnma nɛ, xɛmɛ ɲalamae e felenma nɛ, maale dinmae xurunma nɛ, mixi naxee se igbɛma e luma nɛ dimi kui,

sentences.english: When the doors are shut in the street, and the sound of the crushing is low, and the voice of the bird is soft, and the daughters of music will be made low;
sentences.susu: banxi naadɛe balanma nɛ, maale din xui danma nɛ, xɔni xui dunduma nɛ naxan nu mixie raxunuma,

sentences.english: And he is in fear of that which is high, and danger is in the road, and the tree is white with flower, and the least thing is a weight, and desire is at an end, because man goes to his last resting-place, and those who are sorrowing are in the streets;
sentences.susu: xɛmɛ fama nɛ gaaxude yire itexi ra, e fama nɛ gaaxude fe xɔrɔxɔɛ ra kira xɔn ma, xɛmɔxi xunsɛxɛ fama nɛ fiixɛde, katoe bama nɛ kasarɛ tife, seri mu dandanyi tima sɔnɔn. Na tɛmui mixi sigama nɛ a xa lingira dɔnxɔɛ, wa xui minima nɛ kirae xɔn ma.

sentences.english: Before ever the silver cord is cut, or the vessel of gold is broken, or the pot is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the water-hole;
sentences.susu: Na rabama nɛ beenun gbeti xa bolon, beenun xɛɛma tɔnbili xa kana, beenun fɛɲɛ xa ibɔɔ dulonyi ma, beenun ye bɛndun se xa kana kolonyi yire,

sentences.english: And the dust goes back to the earth as it was, and the spirit goes back to God who gave it.
sentences.susu: beenun adamadi xa gbilen bɛndɛ a daaxi naxɛ, a nii fan xa gbilen Ala ma naxan a raso a fate i.

sentences.english: All things are to no purpose, says the Preacher, all is to no purpose.
sentences.susu: N tan Kawandila xa a fala wo bɛ, «Fe fufafu nan na na birin na. A birin luxi nɛ alɔ foye!»

sentences.english: And because the Preacher was wise he still gave the people knowledge; searching out, testing, and putting in order a great number of wise sayings.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a kolon yi Kawandila findixi xaxilima nan na, naxan bara ɲama xaran. A bara taalie mato, a e yailan.

sentences.english: The Preacher made search for words which were pleasing, but his writing was in words upright and true.
sentences.susu: Yi Kawandila kata nɛ a xa masenyi fanyie nun sɛbɛli tinxinxie sɔtɔ naxee nɔndi masenma.

sentences.english: The words of the wise are pointed, and sayings grouped together are like nails fixed with a hammer; they are given by one guide.
sentences.susu: Xaxilimae xa masenyie luxi nɛ alɔ wuri rameluxi naxee xurusee raɲɛrɛma. Na masenyie malanxi luxi nɛ alɔ lantuma naxee mabanbanxi wuri ma. Na birin fatanxi Xuruse dɛmadonyi keren nan na.

sentences.english: And further, my son, take note of this: of the making of books there is no end, and much learning is a weariness to the flesh.
sentences.susu: N ma di, naxan dangi na masenyie ra, i xa i yɛtɛ ratanga na ma. Danyi mu na sɛbɛli yailanfe ma. Xaranyi gbegbe mixi rataganma nɛ.

sentences.english: This is the last word. All has been said. Have fear of God and keep his laws; because this is right for every man.
sentences.susu: A birin xundusuxi yi masenyi nan na: Won xa gaaxu Ala ya ra, won xa a xa yaamarie rabatu, barima adamadi xa wali lanma a xa findi na nan na.

sentences.english: God will be judge of every work, with every secret thing, good or evil.
sentences.susu: Won xa gaaxu Ala ya ra barima a tan nan mixi xa wali birin makiitima, hali fe naxan birin nɔxunxi, a findi a fanyi ra ba, a findi a ɲaaxi ra ba.

sentences.english: The song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
sentences.susu: Annabi Sulemani xa suuki fisamante nan ya:

sentences.english: Let him give me the kisses of his mouth: for his love is better than wine.
sentences.susu: «I xa n masunbu. I xa xanunteya ɲɔxun wɛni bɛ.

sentences.english: Sweet is the smell of your perfumes; your name is as perfume running out; so the young girls give you their love.
sentences.susu: I xiri ɲɔxunmɛ luxi nɛ alɔ labundɛ, naxan xiri fanyi minima. Na nan a ra i rafan ginɛdimɛ birin ma.

sentences.english: Take me to you, and we will go after you: the king has taken me into his house. We will be glad and full of joy in you, we will give more thought to your love than to wine: rightly are they your lovers.
sentences.susu: I xa n tongo, won xa siga. Mangɛ xa n xanin a xɔnyi. I xa fe na a niyama won xa lu sɛɛwɛ kui. I xa xanunteya ɲɔxun wɛni bɛ. Nɔndi na mixi bɛ i rafanxi naxan ma.»

sentences.english: I am dark, but fair of form, O daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
sentences.susu: «Darisalamu ginɛdimɛe, n kiri fɔɔrɔ, kɔnɔ n tofan alɔ Kedari xa kiri banxie, alɔ dugi naxee gbakuxi Annabi Sulemani xɔnyi.

sentences.english: Let not your eyes be turned on me, because I am dark, because I was looked on by the sun; my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vine-gardens; but my vine-garden I have not kept.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa n kiri fɔɔrɔxi mato, soge nan n fɔɔrɔxi. N nga xa di xɛmɛe nu xɔnɔxi n ma, e nu n xɛɛma e xa wɛni bilie rawalide. N mu nɔ n ɲɛngi sade n gbe xɔn ma.»

sentences.english: Say, O love of my soul, where you give food to your flock, and where you make them take their rest in the heat of the day; why have I to be as one wandering by the flocks of your friends?
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi, i xa a fala n bɛ i xurusee dɛ madonma dɛnnaxɛ, alako n naxa lu i fen na malabui tɛmui i booree xa xuruse gɔɔrɛe ya ma.»

sentences.english: If you have not knowledge, O most beautiful among women, go on your way in the footsteps of the flock, and give your young goats food by the tents of the keepers.
sentences.susu: «Ginɛ tofanyi fisamante, xa i mu na yire kolon, i xa n ma yɛxɛɛe fɔxi fen, i xa i gbee dɛ madon n ma gɔɔrɛ longori ra.

sentences.english: I have made a comparison of you, O my love, to a horse in Pharaoh's carriages.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi, i tofan alɔ Misira mangɛ xa soe, naxan a ragise bɛndunma.

sentences.english: Your face is a delight with rings of hair, your neck with chains of jewels.
sentences.susu: I xa tulirasoee bara i xɛrɛe ratofan, i kɔnyi rayabu kɔnmagore kui.

sentences.english: We will make you chains of gold with ornaments of silver.
sentences.susu: Won xa maratofan se gbɛtɛe fen, naxee yailanxi xɛɛma nun gbeti ra.»

sentences.english: While the king is seated at his table, my spices send out their perfume.
sentences.susu: «N ma labundɛ xiri nu mɛma, mangɛ xa xulunyi yire.

sentences.english: As a bag of myrrh is my well-loved one to me, when he is at rest all night between my breasts.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi maniyaxi se sase nan na, naxan gbakuxi n xiɲɛe tagi, se xiri fanyi saxi a kui.

sentences.english: My love is to me as a branch of the cypress-tree in the vine-gardens of En-gedi.
sentences.susu: A xiri luxi nɛ alɔ sansi fuge xiri, naxee kelixi wɛni bilie ya ma En Gedi bɔxi ma.»

sentences.english: See, you are fair, my love, you are fair; you have the eyes of a dove.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi, i tofan, i tofan. I yae rayabu alɔ ganbɛ.»

sentences.english: See, you are fair, my loved one, and a pleasure; our bed is green.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi, i tofan, i tofan. Won na dɛnnaxɛ, ɲooge fanyi bara findi won ma sade ra,

sentences.english: Cedar-trees are the pillars of our house; and our boards are made of fir-trees.
sentences.susu: sɛdiri wuri salonyie bara findi won ma banxi xunyi ra, sipirɛ wuri bara findi won ma banxi kanke ra.»

sentences.english: I am a rose of Sharon, a flower of the valleys.
sentences.susu: «N tan luma nɛ alɔ sansi fuge tofanyi, naxan mɔɔli toma Sarɔn gulunba yire.»

sentences.english: As the lily-flower among the thorns of the waste, so is my love among the daughters.
sentences.susu: «I tan luxi nɛ alɔ sansi fuge tofanyi tunbee ya ma. I tofan ginɛdimɛe birin bɛ.»

sentences.english: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, so is my loved one among the sons. I took my rest under his shade with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi luxi nɛ alɔ mangoe bili wondi kui. A fan sɛgɛtalae birin bɛ. N bara wa lufe a xa niini bun ma, a xa fe rafan n ma alɔ mangoe rafanma mixi ma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: He took me to the house of wine, and his flag over me was love.
sentences.susu: A bara n xanin a xɔnyi, a xa xanunteya bara findi ɲɛlɛxinyi ra n bɛ.»

sentences.english: Make me strong with wine-cakes, let me be comforted with apples; I am overcome with love.
sentences.susu: «Donse ɲɔxunmɛ so n yi, n ki mangoe, barima xanunteya naxan na n bɔɲɛ kui, a bara n sɛnbɛ ba n yi ra.

sentences.english: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand is round about me.
sentences.susu: N xunyi na n xanuntenyi bɛlɛxɛ, a na n mafurukufe a yirefanyi ra.»

sentences.english: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes of the field, do not let love be moved till it is ready.
sentences.susu: «Darisalamu ginɛdimɛe, n bara wo mayandi, tɔɔkɛ nun xeli xili ra naxee na wula i, wo naxa xanunteya raxunu, wo naxa a rakeli, beenu a wama a xɔn ma tɛmui naxɛ.»

sentences.english: The voice of my loved one! See, he comes dancing on the mountains, stepping quickly on the hills.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi xui na a ra, a na fafe a gi ra geyae fari.

sentences.english: My loved one is like a roe; see, he is on the other side of our wall, he is looking in at the windows, letting himself be seen through the spaces.
sentences.susu: A gima alɔ tɔɔkɛ, a tuganma alɔ xeli. A na be won ma tɛtɛ xanbi ra, a na be matofe wundɛri ra.

sentences.english: My loved one said to me, Get up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala n bɛ, ‹N xanuntenyi tofanyi, keli, i xa fa,

sentences.english: For, see, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
sentences.susu: barima ɲɛmɛ tɛmui bara dangi, tunɛ mu birama sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: The flowers are come on the earth; the time of cutting the vines is come, and the voice of the dove is sounding in our land;
sentences.susu: Sansi na bogife daaxa, ɲɛlɛxin waxati bara a li, xɔnie na e xui raminife won ma bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: The fig-tree puts out her green fruit and the vines with their young fruit give a good smell. Get up from your bed, my beautiful one, and come away.
sentences.susu: Xɔrɛ bili na bogife, wɛni bili na fugafe, a xiri fan. N xanuntenyi, keli, i xa fa.

sentences.english: O my dove, you are in the holes of the mountain sides, in the cracks of the high hills; let me see your face, let your voice come to my ears; for sweet is your voice, and your face is fair.
sentences.susu: N ma ginɛ, i naxa i nɔxun alɔ ganbɛ a nɔxunma gɛmɛe longori ra ki naxɛ. Mini, n wama i xui ɲɔxunmɛ mɛfe, n wama i yatagi tofanyi tofe.›»

sentences.english: Take for us the foxes, the little foxes, which do damage to the vines; our vines have young grapes.
sentences.susu: «Wo xulumasee suxu, naxee wama muxu xa wɛni bili fugaxie kanafe.»

sentences.english: My loved one is mine, and I am his: he takes his food among the flowers.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi findixi n gbe nan na, n fan findixi a gbe nan na. A a xa xurusee dɛ madonma sansi fugaxie ya ma.

sentences.english: Till the evening comes, and the sky slowly becomes dark, come, my loved one, and be like a roe on the mountains of Bether.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi, beenu kuye xa iba, i xa gbilen, i xa i gi alɔ tɔɔkɛ, i xa i gi geyae fari alɔ xeli.»

sentences.english: By night on my bed I was looking for him who is the love of my soul: I was looking for him, but I did not see him.
sentences.susu: «Kɔɛ ra n bara n xanuntenyi fen n ma sade ma, kɔnɔ n mu a toxi.

sentences.english: I will get up now and go about the town, in the streets and in the wide ways I will go after him who is the love of my soul: I went after him, but I did not see him.
sentences.susu: N naxa keli, n naxa mini taa kui, n xa n xanuntenyi to, kɔnɔ n mu a toxi.

sentences.english: The watchmen who go about the town came by me; to them I said, Have you seen him who is my heart's desire?
sentences.susu: N to taa kantamae li, n naxa e maxɔrin, ‹Wo bara n xanuntenyi to?›

sentences.english: I was but a little way from them, when I came face to face with him who is the love of my soul. I took him by the hands, and did not let him go, till I had taken him into my mother's house, and into the room of her who gave me birth.
sentences.susu: N to dangi e ra, n naxa n xanuntenyi li yire nde, n naxa a suxu, n mu a lu, n naxa a xanin n nga xɔnyi, a xa konkoe kui n barixi dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes of the field, let not love be moved till it is ready.
sentences.susu: «Darisalamu ginɛdimɛe, n bara wo mayandi, tɔɔkɛ nun xeli xili ra naxee na wula i, wo naxa xanunteya raxunu, wo naxa a rakeli, beenu a wama a xɔn ma tɛmui naxɛ.»

sentences.english: Who is this coming out of the waste places like pillars of smoke, perfumed with sweet spices, with all the spices of the trader?
sentences.susu: «Nde na fafe kelife gbengberen yire? A na xube ratefe alɔ tuuri. Na tuuri luxi nɛ alɔ surayi tuuri naxan xiri fan.

sentences.english: See, it is the bed of Solomon; sixty men of war are about it, of the army of Israel,
sentences.susu: Sulemani ragise na a ra, Isirayila xa sɔɔri gbangbalanyi tongo senni na a matife,

sentences.english: All of them armed with swords, trained in war; every man has his sword at his side, because of fear in the night.
sentences.susu: santidɛgɛma na e birin yi ra, e fata gere ra, e fata mixi makantade kɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: King Solomon made himself a bed of the wood of Lebanon.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Sulemani ragise na a ra, a yailanxi wuri fanyi ra naxan kelixi Liban.

sentences.english: He made its pillars of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it of ebony.
sentences.susu: A raxunmaxi xɛɛma, gbeti, nun dugi gbeeli ra. Darisalamu ginɛe nu bara dugi dɛgɛ Sulemani ragise raxunmafe ra, mangɛ xa marafanyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: Go out, O daughters of Jerusalem, and see King Solomon, with the crown which his mother put on his head on the day when he was married, and on the day of the joy of his heart.
sentences.susu: Siyon ginɛdimɛe, wo xa mangɛ Sulemani mato, mangɛ tɔnxuma na a xun ma, a nga naxan soxi a yi ra a xa futi xiri lɔxɔɛ. Na lɔxɔɛ a nu sɛɛwaxi ki fanyi ra.»

sentences.english: See, you are fair, my love, you are fair; you have the eyes of a dove; your hair is as a flock of goats, which take their rest on the side of Gilead.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi, i tofan, i tofan. I yae rayabu alɔ ganbɛ, e nɔxunxi mafelenyi kui. I xunsɛxɛ gbo. E luxi nɛ alɔ si gɔɔrɛ naxan goroma Galadi geya fari.

sentences.english: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep whose wool is newly cut, which come up from the washing; every one has two lambs, and there is not one without young.
sentences.susu: I ɲinyi fiixɛ alɔ yɛxɛɛ gɔɔrɛ naxan xabe maxabaxi, e kelixi maxade. I ɲinyi keren mu baxi, e birin na e boore sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: Your red lips are like a bright thread, and your mouth is fair of form; the sides of your head are like pomegranate fruit under your veil.
sentences.susu: I dɛ tofan, i dɛ kiri luxi nɛ alɔ luuti gbeeli. I xɛrɛ tofan alɔ mangoe naxan ixabaxi a tagi. E makotoxi i xa mafelenyi kui.

sentences.english: Your neck is like the tower of David made for a store-house of arms, in which a thousand breastplates are hanging, breastplates for fighting-men.
sentences.susu: I kɔnyi filinxi, a luxi alɔ Dawuda xa yire makantaxi itexi. I xa kɔnmagore maniyaxi sɔɔrie xa makantasee nan na, naxee gbakuxi sɔɔri banxi kanke.

sentences.english: Your two breasts are like two young roes of the same birth, which take their food among the lilies.
sentences.susu: I xiɲɛ firinyi luxi nɛ alɔ bole xa gulie, naxee e dɛ madonma sansie tofanyi tagi.

sentences.english: Till the evening comes, and the sky slowly becomes dark, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
sentences.susu: Soge na goro, kɔɛ naxa so, n tema nɛ labundɛ nun surayi na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: You are all fair, my love; there is no mark on you.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi, i tofan, sese mu luxi i xa tofanyi ra.

sentences.english: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon; see from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the places of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
sentences.susu: N ma ginɛ, won xa keli Liban, won xa keli Liban Amana geya fari, Seniri nun Xerimon geyae fari, yɛtɛe nun baratɛe na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: You have taken away my heart, my sister, my bride; you have taken away my heart, with one look you have taken it, with one chain of your neck!
sentences.susu: N ma ginɛ, i n sondonyi rasɛɛwama. N xunya, i na i ya ti n na, n bɔɲɛ ɲɛlɛxinma nɛ. I xa kɔnmagore tofe rafan n ma.

sentences.english: How fair is your love, my sister! How much better is your love than wine, and the smell of your oils than any perfume!
sentences.susu: N ma ginɛ, i xa xanunteya ɲɔxun n bɛ, dangife wɛni ra. A xiri fan dangife labundɛ ra.

sentences.english: Your lips are dropping honey; honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your clothing is like the smell of Lebanon.
sentences.susu: N ma ginɛ, i dɛ kiri ɲɔxun kumi bɛ, i nɛnyi ɲɔxun dangi kumi nun xiɲɛ ra. I xa dugi xiri luxi nɛ alɔ Liban xiri fanyi.»

sentences.english: A garden walled-in is my sister, my bride; a garden shut up, a spring of water stopped.
sentences.susu: «N ma ginɛ, i findixi n gbe nan na, alɔ sansi yire tɛtɛ rabilinxi naxan na. N xunya, i luxi nɛ alɔ n ma kɔlɔnyi, naxan balanxi, mixi gbɛtɛ mu nɔma ye bade naa.

sentences.english: The produce of the garden is pomegranates; with all the best fruits, henna and spikenard,
sentences.susu: I fan alɔ sansi yire sansi mɔɔli birin na dɛnnaxɛ, alɔ mangoe, laali, sansi xiri fanyi,

sentences.english: Spikenard and safron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.
sentences.susu: sansi fuge nerefunyi, wuri bili naxan fuɲi ɲɔxun, wuri bili naxan xiri fan, surayi mɔɔli birin kelixi naxee ma.

sentences.english: You are a fountain of gardens, a spring of living waters, and flowing waters from Lebanon.
sentences.susu: I luxi nɛ alɔ ye naxan minima bɔxi ma, naxan a niyama Liban sansi birin xa fan.»

sentences.english: Be awake, O north wind; and come, O south, blowing on my garden, so that its spices may come out. Let my loved one come into his garden, and take of his good fruits.
sentences.susu: «Foye fanyi xa fa kelife kɔɔla ma, kelife yire fanyi ma, alako n ma sansi xiri xa te. N xanuntenyi xa fa n yire, a xa sansi bogi fanyi don naxee findixi a gbe ra.»

sentences.english: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; to take my myrrh with my spice; my wax with my honey; my wine with my milk. Take meat, O friends; take wine, yes, be overcome with love.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi, n bara so n ma sansi yire. N xunya, n bara n ma surayi malan, n bara kumi don, n bara wɛni nun xiɲɛ min. N bara a fala n booree bɛ e fan xa e min, e xa xanunteya kolon.»

sentences.english: I am sleeping, but my heart is awake; it is the sound of my loved one at the door, saying, Be open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my very beautiful one; my head is wet with dew, and my hair with the drops of the night.
sentences.susu: «N nu na xife, kɔnɔ n bɔɲɛ mu xixi, a n xanuntenyi xui mɛxi, naxan nu bara naadɛ kɔnkɔn.» «N maaginɛ, n dɔxɔginɛ, naadɛ rabi n bɛ. N ma tɔɔkɛ ginɛ, naxan xa tofanyi maniyɛ mu na. Xini bara n xunyi xinbeli, a bara n xunsɛxɛ bunda.»

sentences.english: I have put off my coat; how may I put it on? My feet are washed; how may I make them unclean?
sentences.susu: «N ɲan nu bara n ma dugi ba, fo n man xa a ragoro n ma? N ɲan nu bara n sanyi maxa, fo n man xa ti bɔxi ma?

sentences.english: My loved one put his hand on the door, and my heart was moved for him.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi naxa a bɛlɛxɛ raso naadɛ longori ra, alako a xa a rabi. N bɔɲɛ naxa sɛɛwa a xa fe ra.

sentences.english: I got up to let my loved one in; and my hands were dropping with myrrh, and my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the lock of the door.
sentences.susu: N naxa keli alako n xa naadɛ rabi n xanuntenyi bɛ. Labundɛ nu na n bɛlɛxɛ ma, ture nu na n bɛlɛxɛsolee ma. Na birin naxa lu naadɛ rabi se ma.

sentences.english: I made the door open to my loved one; but my loved one had taken himself away, and was gone, my soul was feeble when his back was turned on me; I went after him, but I did not come near him; I said his name, but he gave me no answer.
sentences.susu: N naxa naadɛ rabi n xanuntenyi bɛ, kɔnɔ a ɲan nu bara siga. N bɔɲɛ naxa sunnun. N naxa a fen, kɔnɔ n mu a toxi. N naxa a xili, kɔnɔ a mu n ma xili ratinxi.

sentences.english: The keepers who go about the town overtook me; they gave me blows and wounds; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
sentences.susu: Taa kantamae to n to, e naxa n suxu, e n bɔnbɔ, e n ma xinbeli dugi muɲa.»

sentences.english: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you see my loved one, what will you say to him? That I am overcome with love.
sentences.susu: «Darisalamu ginɛdimɛe, n bara wo mayandi, xa wo bara n xanuntenyi to, wo xa a fala a bɛ a xɔli bara n suxu xanunteya xa fe ra.»

sentences.english: What is your loved one more than another, O fairest among women? What is your loved one more than another, that you say this to us?
sentences.susu: «Ginɛ tofanyi fisamante, i xanuntenyi fan a birin bɛ? I bara muxu mayandi barima a fan a birin bɛ?»

sentences.english: My loved one is white and red, the chief among ten thousand.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi kiri fiixɛ, a ragbeeli. A kolon ɲɔxun na xɛmɛ wulu fu ya ma.

sentences.english: His head is as the most delicate gold; his hair is thick, and black as a raven.
sentences.susu: A xunyi luxi nɛ alɔ xɛɛma fanyi, a xunsɛxɛ ifɔɔrɔxi alɔ xaxa fɔɔrɛ xabe.

sentences.english: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the water streams, washed with milk, and rightly placed.
sentences.susu: A yae rayabu alɔ ganbɛ naxee tixi xure dɛ ra, e fiixɛ alɔ xiɲɛ, e yanbama alɔ diyaman.

sentences.english: His face is as beds of spices, giving out perfumes of every sort; his lips like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
sentences.susu: A xɛrɛe luxi nɛ alɔ labundɛ yailande, a dɛ kiri maniyaxi sansi fuge tofanyi nan na, a xiri ɲɔxun.

sentences.english: His hands are as rings of gold ornamented with beryl-stones; his body is as a smooth plate of ivory covered with sapphires.
sentences.susu: A bɛlɛxɛ tofan alɔ bɛlɛxɛsolerasoe xɛɛma daaxi, diyaman na naxan ma. A fate luxi nɛ alɔ sili ɲinyi fiixɛ, gɛmɛ tofanyi mɔɔli nde, yee masoxi naxan ma.

sentences.english: His legs are as pillars of stone on a base of delicate gold; his looks are as Lebanon, beautiful as the cedar-tree.
sentences.susu: A sanyi sɛnbɛ gbo alɔ fanye fiixɛ, naxan tixi xɛɛma fari. A tofan alɔ Liban, a ite alɔ sɛdiri wuri bilie.

sentences.english: His mouth is most sweet; yes, he is all beautiful. This is my loved one, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: A dɛ iɲɔxun, a xa fe birin fan. Darisalamu ginɛdimɛe, n xanuntenyi na na ki nɛ, n dɛ fan boore nan a ra.»

sentences.english: Where is your loved one gone, O most fair among women? Where is your loved one turned away, that we may go looking for him with you?
sentences.susu: «Ginɛ tofanyi fisamante, i xanuntenyi sigaxi minden? A siga minden mabiri alako won birin xa a fen?»

sentences.english: My loved one is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to take food in the gardens, and to get lilies.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi bara siga a xa sansi yire, se xiri fanyi na dɛnnaxɛ, alako a xa a maɲɛrɛ, a xa sansi fuge tofanyi nde ba.

sentences.english: I am for my loved one, and my loved one is for me; he takes food among the lilies.
sentences.susu: N findixi n xanuntenyi gbe nan na, a fan findixi n gbe nan na. A luma a maɲɛrɛ ra sansi fuge tofanyie ya ma.»

sentences.english: You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, as fair as Jerusalem; you are to be feared like an army with flags.
sentences.susu: «N dɛ fan boore, i tofan alɔ Tirisa, i rayabu alɔ Darisalamu, i sɛnbɛ gbo alɔ Isirayila xa sɔɔrie.

sentences.english: Let your eyes be turned away from me; see, they have overcome me; your hair is as a flock of goats which take their rest on the side of Gilead.
sentences.susu: I naxa i ya ti n na, xa na mu a ra n xaxili ifuma nɛ. I xunsɛxɛe gbo. E luxi nɛ alɔ si gɔɔrɛ naxan goroma Galadi geya fari.

sentences.english: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep which come up from the washing; every one has two lambs, and there is not one without young.
sentences.susu: I ɲinyi fiixɛ alɔ yɛxɛɛ gɔɔrɛ naxan xabe maxabaxi, e kelixi naxee maxade. I ɲinyi keren mu baxi, e birin dɛɲɛxi.

sentences.english: Like pomegranate fruit are the sides of your head under your veil.
sentences.susu: I xɛrɛ tofan alɔ mangoe naxan ixabaxi a tagi. E nɔxunxi i xa mafelenyi bun ma.

sentences.english: There are sixty queens, and eighty servant-wives, and young girls without number.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ ginɛ tongo senni nɔma lude naa, mangɛ xa konyi ginɛ tongo solomasaxan fan lu naa, a nun a xa ginɛdimɛ tofanyi gbegbe naxan kɔnti mu kolon.

sentences.english: My dove, my very beautiful one, is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the dearest one of her who gave her birth. The daughters saw her, and gave her a blessing; yes, the queens and the servant-wives, and they gave her praises.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ ginɛ keren peti nan n yi naxan dangi e birin na. A keren nan na a nga bɛ, naxan nafanxi a ma dangife e birin na. Ginɛdimɛe, mangɛ ginɛe, nun mangɛ xa ginɛe, e birin a matɔxɔma yi wɔyɛnyi ra,

sentences.english: Who is she, looking down as the morning light, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, who is to be feared like an army with flags?
sentences.susu: ‹Nde na yi ginɛ ra, naxan yanbama alɔ subaxɛ naiyalanyi, naxan tofan alɔ kike, naxan fate yanbama alɔ soge, naxan mamirin alɔ tunbui gaali?›»

sentences.english: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the green plants of the valley, and to see if the vine was in bud, and the pomegranate-trees were in flower.
sentences.susu: «N wama gorofe sansi yire, alako n xa sansi nɛɛnɛ to gulunba kui, alako n xa a kolon xa wɛni bili bara bogi, xa mangoe bara fuga.

sentences.english: Before I was conscious of it, ...
sentences.susu: N mu nu a kolon xa n yɛtɛ fama tede n ma ɲama xa mangɛ ragise kui.»

sentences.english: How beautiful are your feet in their shoes, O king's daughter! The curves of your legs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a good workman:
sentences.susu: «Sulamika, i xa gbilen, i xa gbilen, alako muxu xa i mato.» «Munfe ra wo Sulamika matoma a fare boronfe ki naxɛ ɲama ya ma?»

sentences.english: Your stomach is a store of grain with lilies round it, and in the middle a round cup full of wine.
sentences.susu: «Mangɛ xa di, i sanyi tofan sankiri kui. I tagi bilinyi rayabu alɔ xunmase mixi naxan yailanxi.

sentences.english: Your two breasts are like two young roes of the same birth.
sentences.susu: I furi digilin, a rafexi fe fanyi ra, i tagi luxi alɔ mɛngi malanxi, a rabilinxi sansi fuge tofanyie ra.

sentences.english: Your neck is as a tower of ivory; your eyes like the waters in Heshbon, by the doorway of Bath-rabbim; your nose is as the tower on Lebanon looking over Damascus:
sentences.susu: I xiɲɛ firinyi luxi alɔ xeli xa gulie.

sentences.english: Your head is like Carmel, and the hair of your head is like purple, in whose net the king is prisoner.
sentences.susu: I kɔnyi filinxi, a luxi alɔ yire makantaxi itexi, naxan yailanxi sili ɲinyi ra. I yae luxi alɔ ye ragatadee Xɛsibɔn, Bati Rabimi naadɛ sɛɛti ma. I ɲɔɛ luxi alɔ Liban xa yire makantaxi, naxan ya rafindixi Damasi ma.

sentences.english: How beautiful and how sweet you are, O love, for delight.
sentences.susu: I xunyi luxi alɔ Karemele geya, i xunsɛxɛ luxi alɔ dugi gbeeli. Mangɛ mu nɔma a ya bade naxan na.

sentences.english: You are tall like a palm-tree, and your breasts are like the fruit of the vine.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi, i tofan, n xanuntenyi fanyi, i rafan n ma.

sentences.english: I said, Let me go up the palm-tree, and let me take its branches in my hands: your breasts will be as the fruit of the vine, and the smell of your breath like apples;
sentences.susu: I kuya alɔ tugi bili, i xiɲɛ misaalixi naxan bogie ra.

sentences.english: And the roof of your mouth like good wine flowing down smoothly for my loved one, moving gently over my lips and my teeth.
sentences.susu: N bara a fala n yɛtɛ bɛ, ‹N xa te na tugi kɔn na, n xa na bogi suxu.› I xiɲɛ misaalixi wɛni bili bogi nan na, i dɛ xiri ɲɔxun alɔ mangoe,

sentences.english: I am for my loved one, and his desire is for me.
sentences.susu: i dɛ rafan n ma dangife wɛni ra.» «Iyo, a maniyaxi wɛni nan na, naxan findixi n xanuntenyi gbe ra, won firin naxan minma.

sentences.english: Come, my loved one, let us go out into the field; let us take rest among the cypress-trees.
sentences.susu: N bara findi n xanuntenyi gbe ra, a xɔli na n tan nan ma.

sentences.english: Let us go out early to the vine-gardens; let us see if the vine is in bud, if it has put out its young fruit, and the pomegranate is in flower. There I will give you my love.
sentences.susu: N xanuntenyi, won xa mini daaxa, won xa kɔɛ radangi taa xunxurie kui.

sentences.english: The mandrakes give out a sweet smell, and at our doors are all sorts of good fruits, new and old, which I have kept for my loved one.
sentences.susu: Won kurunma nɛ sigafe ra wɛni bogi bili matode, won xa a to xa e fugaxi, won xa a mato xa mangoe fan fuge bara mini. Mɛnni n n ma xanunteya masenma nɛ i bɛ.

sentences.english: Oh that you were my brother, who took milk from my mother's breasts! When I came to you in the street, I would give you kisses; yes, I would not be looked down on.
sentences.susu: «Xa i findixi n taara xɛmɛma nan na nu, n nga xiɲɛ fixi naxan ma, n nu nɔma i masunbude mixi ya xɔri n mu yaagima na ra.

sentences.english: I would take you by the hand into my mother's house, and she would be my teacher. I would give you drink of spiced wine, drink of the pomegranate.
sentences.susu: N nu nɔma i xaninde n nga yire, i xa findi n karamɔxɔ ra, n fa wɛni fanyi nun mangoe ye so i yi ra.»

sentences.english: His left hand would be under my head, and his right hand about me.
sentences.susu: «N xunyi na n xanuntenyi bɛlɛxɛ, a na n mafurukufe a yirefanyi ra.

sentences.english: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, do not let love be moved till it is ready.
sentences.susu: Darisalamu ginɛdimɛe, n bara wo mayandi, wo naxa xanunteya raxunu, wo naxa a rakeli, beenu a wama a xɔn ma tɛmui naxɛ.»

sentences.english: Who is this, who comes up from the waste places, resting on her loved one? It was I who made you awake under the apple-tree, where your mother gave you birth; there she was in pain at your birth.
sentences.susu: «Nde na yi ginɛ ra naxan kelixi gbengberen yire, a a xanuntenyi bɛlɛxɛ suxuxi?» «N bara i raxunu mangoe bili bun ma, i nga tɔɔrɔxi i baride dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: Put me as a sign on your heart, as a sign on your arm; love is strong as death, and wrath bitter as the underworld: its coals are coals of fire; violent are its flames.
sentences.susu: N xa findi i keren gbe ra, alɔ i xa tɔnxuma naxan gbakuxi i kɔn ma, xa na mu a ra naxan nasoxi i bɛlɛxɛsole ra, barima xanunteya sɛnbɛ gbo dangife faxɛ ra. N wama i xɔn n yɛtɛ bɛ, alɔ aligiyama wama mixie xɔn ma ki naxɛ. Xanunteya sɛnbɛ gbo alɔ tɛ, Alatala naxan nadɛxɛxi, a mu xubenma.

sentences.english: Much water may not put out love, or the deep waters overcome it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would be judged a price not great enough.
sentences.susu: Baa ye mu nɔma xanunteya raxubende, xure ye mu nɔma a bade. Mixi naxan wama a harige birin masarafe xanunteya ra, mixi na kanyi mayelema nɛ.»

sentences.english: We have a young sister, and she has no breasts; what are we to do for our sister in the day when she is given to a man?
sentences.susu: «Xunya ginɛma na muxu yi ra, a mu mɔxi sinden, a xiɲɛe xurun. Muxu fama munse rabade a bɛ mixi na a fen tɛmui naxɛ?

sentences.english: If she is a wall, we will make on her a strong base of silver; and if she is a door, we will let her be shut up with cedar-wood.
sentences.susu: Xa a luxi alɔ tɛtɛ naxan balanxi, muxu a yɛnsɛma nɛ gbeti ra, kɔnɔ xa a luxi alɔ naadɛ naxan nabixi, muxu a balanma nɛ.»

sentences.english: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers; then was I in his eyes as one to whom good chance had come.
sentences.susu: «N tan luxi nɛ alɔ tɛtɛ naxan mu rabima, n xiɲɛe findixi yire makantaxie nan na. Na kui n bara findi n xanuntenyi xa bɔɲɛsa ra.

sentences.english: Solomon had a vine-garden at Baal-hamon; he let out the vine-garden to keepers; every one had to give a thousand bits of silver for its fruit.
sentences.susu: Wɛni sansi bili yire nu na Sulemani yi ra Bali Hamon. A naxa a taxu a xa walikɛe ra, naxee nu lanma e xa gbeti kɔbiri kole wulu fi na xa fe ra.

sentences.english: My vine-garden, which is mine, is before me: you, O Solomon, will have the thousand, and those who keep the fruit of them two hundred.
sentences.susu: N tan nan n ma wɛni bilie yire makantama. I bara gbeti kole wulu sɔtɔ, i xa walikɛe bara gbeti kole kɛmɛ firin sɔtɔ.»

sentences.english: You who have your resting-place in the gardens, the friends give ear to your voice; make me give ear to it.
sentences.susu: «I tan naxan na sansi yire, i booree wama i xui ramɛfe, kɔnɔ n tan nan na ramɛma.»

sentences.english: Come quickly, my loved one, and be like a roe on the mountains of spice.
sentences.susu: «N xanuntenyi, i xa i gi alɔ xeli, i xa i gi alɔ tɔɔkɛ tefe ra geyae fari, surayi ɲɔxunmɛ na dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: The vision of Isaiah, the son of Amoz, which he saw about Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
sentences.susu: Masenyi naxee goro Amosu xa di Esayi ma, Yudaya nun Darisalamu xa fe ra, Yudaya mangɛe Osiyasi, Yotami, Axasi, nun Xesekiya xa waxati.

sentences.english: Give ear, O heavens, and you, O earth, to the word which the Lord has said: I have taken care of my children till they became men, but their hearts have been turned away from me.
sentences.susu: Alatala nan masenyi tife, koore nun bɔxi birin xa e tuli mati a ra. Alatala naxɛ, «N bara die xuru, n e ramɔ, kɔnɔ e bara muruta n ma.

sentences.english: Even the ox has knowledge of its owner, and the ass of the place where its master puts its food: but Israel has no knowledge, my people give no thought to me.
sentences.susu: Ninge yati a kanyi kolon, sofale fan a kolon a kanyi donse sama a bɛ dɛnnaxɛ. Kɔnɔ Isirayila tan mu sese kolon, n ma ɲama mu sese fahaamuxi.»

sentences.english: O nation full of sin, a people weighted down with crime, a generation of evil-doers, false-hearted children: they have gone away from the Lord, they have no respect for the Holy One of Israel, their hearts are turned back from him.
sentences.susu: Ɲaxankatɛ na yi ɲama yunubitɔɛ bɛ, naxan yunubi kote xaninma, naxan findixi fe ɲaaxi rabae ra, naxan findixi di murutaxie ra. E bara mɛ Alatala ra, e Isirayila xa Sɛniyɛntɔɛ mabere, e e kobe raso a ra.

sentences.english: Why will you have more and more punishment? why keep on in your evil ways? Every head is tired and every heart is feeble.
sentences.susu: Wo na ɲaxankatɛ fenfe munfe ra? Wo tondixi gbilende Alatala ma munse ma? Wo bara fura wo xunyi ma, wo tɔɔrɔxi wo bɔɲɛ ma.

sentences.english: The body, from head to foot, is all diseased; it is a mass of open wounds, marks of blows, and broken flesh: the flow of blood has not been stopped, and no oil has been put on the wounds.
sentences.susu: Kelife wo sanyi ma han wo xunyi, wo xa fefe mu lanxi. Wo xa fie ya mu ixaxi, e mu maxirixi, ture yo mu saxi e ma.

sentences.english: Your country has become waste; your towns are burned with fire; as for your land, it is overturned before your eyes, made waste and overcome by men from strange lands.
sentences.susu: Wo xa bɔxi bara kana, wo xa taae bara gan. Si gbɛtɛe na wo xa daxamui donfe wo ya xɔri, e na a birin tongofe e yɛtɛ bɛ.

sentences.english: And the daughter of Zion has become like a tent in a vine-garden, like a watchman's house in a field of fruit, like a town shut in by armies.
sentences.susu: Siyoni taa na a kerenyi ma alɔ bage di xɛ tagi, alɔ leele naxan tixi mɛrɛ ma, alɔ taa naxan nabilinxi yaxuie ra.

sentences.english: If the Lord of armies had not kept some at least of us safe, we would have been like Sodom, and the fate of Gomorrah would have been ours.
sentences.susu: Xa Alatala Sɛnbɛma mu mixi ndee rakisi won bɛ nu, won bara lu nu alɔ Sodoma nun Gomora taae.

sentences.english: Give ear to the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; let your hearts be turned to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah.
sentences.susu: Wo wo tuli mati Alatala xa masenyi ra, wo tan naxee maniyaxi Sodoma kuntigie ra. Wo xa won Marigi Alatala xa sɛriyɛ ramɛ, wo tan naxee luxi alɔ Gomora ɲama.

sentences.english: What use to me is the number of the offerings which you give me? says the Lord; your burned offerings of sheep, and the best parts of fat cattle, are a weariness to me; I take no pleasure in the blood of oxen, or of lambs, or of he-goats.
sentences.susu: Alatala naxɛ, «N munse rabama wo xa sɛrɛxɛ wuyaxie ra? N bara luga yɛxɛ kontonyi sɛrɛxɛe ra, n bara luga xuruse bɔrɛgɛxie ture ra. Tuurae, yɛxɛɛe nun si kontonyie wuli mu rafan n ma.

sentences.english: At whose request do you come before me, making my house unclean with your feet?
sentences.susu: Nde wo xilixi fafe ra n ma hɔrɔmɔbanxi tɛtɛ kui, tife ra n ya i?

sentences.english: Give me no more false offerings; the smoke of burning flesh is disgusting to me, so are your new moons and Sabbaths and your holy meetings.
sentences.susu: Wo ba fafe hadiya fufafu ra. Surayi xiri mu rafan n ma fefe ma. Wo xa kike nɛɛnɛ salie, wo xa malabui lɔxɔɛe, wo xa malanyie, nun wo xa salie xungbee, e sese mu rafanxi n ma.

sentences.english: Your new moons and your regular feasts are a grief to my soul: they are a weight in my spirit; I am crushed under them.
sentences.susu: N wo xa kike nɛɛnɛ salie xɔnxi, wo xa sali birin bara n bɔɲɛ raɲaaxu n ma.

sentences.english: And when your hands are stretched out to me, my eyes will be turned away from you: even though you go on making prayers, I will not give ear: your hands are full of blood.
sentences.susu: Wo na wo bɛlɛxɛe itala sali kui tɛmui naxɛ, n na n ya ragalima nɛ alako n naxa fa a to. Hali wo maxandie bira e boore fɔxɔ ra, n mu e ramɛma, barima faxɛtie nan wo ra.

sentences.english: Be washed, make yourselves clean; put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; let there be an end of sinning;
sentences.susu: Wo lu fe fiixɛ kui, wo wo yɛtɛ rasɛniyɛn, wo ba yunubie rabafe n ya i.

sentences.english: Take pleasure in well-doing; let your ways be upright, keep down the cruel, give a right decision for the child who has no father, see to the cause of the widow.
sentences.susu: Wo wo matinkan fe fanyi rabade, wo lu tinxinyi kui, wo mixi kobie makiiti, wo kiridie nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe xun mafala.»

sentences.english: Come now, and let us have an argument together, says the Lord: how may your sins which are red like blood be white as snow? how may their dark purple seem like wool?
sentences.susu: Alatala naxɛ, «Wo fa, won xa wɔyɛn. Hali wo xa yunubie to bara wo manɔxɔ, wo nɔma fiixɛde fɔɛn. Hali e sa xɔsi nɛ alɔ garɛ gbeeli, e nɔma nɛ fiixɛde alɔ xuruse fiixɛ fate maxabe.

sentences.english: If you will give ear to my word and do it, the good things of the land will be yours;
sentences.susu: Xa wo tin wo tuli matide n na, wo yi bɔxi daxamui donma nɛ,

sentences.english: But if your hearts are turned against me, I will send destruction on you by the sword; so the Lord has said.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ xa wo sa tondi n natinmɛde, santidɛgɛma nan wo sɔntɔma.» Alatala xui nan na ki.

sentences.english: The upright town has become untrue; there was a time when her judges gave right decisions, when righteousness had a resting-place in her, but now she is full of those who take men's lives.
sentences.susu: Yi taa luxi nɛ alɔ ginɛ naxan nu dugutɛgɛxi a xa mɔri ma a fa mɛ a ra, a findi langoe ginɛ ra. A singe a nu tinxin a fanyi ra, kɔnɔ yakɔsi a bara findi faxati ra?

sentences.english: Your silver is no longer true metal, your wine is mixed with water.
sentences.susu: I xa gbeti bara findi se kanaxi ra, i xa wɛni bara sunbu ye ra.

sentences.english: Your chiefs have gone against the Lord, they have become friends of thieves; every one of them is looking for profit and going after rewards; they do not give right decisions for the child who has no father, and they do not let the cause of the widow come before them.
sentences.susu: I xa mangɛe bara muruta, e findi muɲɛtie ra, buɲa tinxintare rafan naxee ma. Na kui e mu kiridie malima, e mu kiiti fanyi sama kaaɲɛ ginɛ xa tɔɔrɛ xa fe ra.

sentences.english: For this reason the Lord, the Lord of armies, the Strong One of Israel, has said, I will put an end to my haters, and send punishment on those who are against me;
sentences.susu: Alatala Sɛnbɛma xui nan ya, na xa fe ra. Isirayila Marigi Ala Sɛnbɛma naxɛ, «N ɲaxankatɛ dɔxɔma nɛ n gerefae ma, n na n gbe ɲɔxɔ n yaxuie ma.

sentences.english: And my hand will again be on you, washing away what is unclean as with soap, and taking away all your false metal;
sentences.susu: N gbilenma nɛ n yi sa ra i ma a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra, n i rasɛniyɛn alɔ gbeti gbi bama ki naxɛ tɛ ra, alako i xa ba tinxintareya ma.

sentences.english: And I will give you judges again as at the first, and wise guides as in the past; then you will be named, The Town of Righteousness, the true town.
sentences.susu: N kiitisa tinxinxie tima nɛ wo xun alɔ singe, n marasima fanyie luma nɛ wo tagi alɔ tɛmui dangixi. Na dangi xanbi, i xili fama nɛ falade ‹Taa tinxinxi naxan dugutɛgɛxi.›»

sentences.english: Upright acts will be the price of Zion's forgiveness, and by righteousness will men be living there.
sentences.susu: Siyoni xun sarama nɛ tinxinyi ra, tuubi mixie kisima nɛ tinxinyi saabui ra.

sentences.english: But a common destruction will overtake sinners and evil-doers together, and those who have gone away from the Lord will be cut off.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ gbaloe goroma nɛ murutɛlae nun yunubitɔɛe ma, halaki lu mixie fɔxɔ ra, naxee e kobe soma Alatala ra.

sentences.english: For you will be put to shame because of the trees of your desire, and because of the gardens of your pleasure.
sentences.susu: Wo fama nɛ yaagide fɔtɔnyi ra wo nu kuye batuma dɛnnaxɛ. Wo yaagi belebele sɔtɔma nɛ na yiree xa fe ra.

sentences.english: For you will be like a tree whose leaves have become dry, and like a garden without water.
sentences.susu: Wo fama nɛ lude alɔ wuri bili lisixi, ye mu na naxan ma.

sentences.english: And the strong will be as food for the fire, and his work as a flame; and they will be burned together, with no one to put out the fire.
sentences.susu: Sɛnbɛma sɛnbɛ ɲɔnma nɛ, a tan nun a xa wali birin gan, a rakisima yo mu lu na.

sentences.english: The word which Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Amosu xa di Annabi Esayi xa masenyi nan ya Yuda nun Darisalamu xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And it will come about in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord will be placed on the top of the mountains, and be lifted up over the hills; and all nations will come to it.
sentences.susu: Waxati dɔnxɔɛ Alatala xa banxi tixi geya naxan fari, na fama nɛ lude geyae birin xun ma. Si birin e xun tima nɛ na yire itexi ra.

sentences.english: And the peoples will say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob: and he will give us knowledge of his ways, and we will be guided by his word; for out of Zion the law will go out, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Bɔnsɔɛ wuyaxi sigama nɛ naa, e a fala, «Wo fa, won xa te Alatala xa geya fari, Yaxuba Marigi Ala xa banxi na dɛnnaxɛ. A won xaranma nɛ a xa sɛriyɛ ra, alako won xa bira a xa kira fɔxɔ ra.» Alatala xa sɛriyɛ minima Siyoni geya ma, a xa masenyi fɔlɔma Darisalamu taa kui.

sentences.english: And he will be the judge between the nations, and the peoples will be ruled by his decisions: and their swords will be turned into plough-blades, and their spears into vine-knives: no longer will the nations be turning their swords against one another, and the knowledge of war will be gone for ever.
sentences.susu: Alatala nan kiiti sama ɲamanɛe tagi, a findi si wuyaxi tagi ibama ra. E fama e xa santidɛgɛmae xabude kerie nan na, e e xa tanbɛe findi wɔrɔtɛe ra. Gere ɲɔnma nɛ sie tagi, sɔɔriɲa mu matinkanma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: O family of Jacob, come, and let us go in the light of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Yaxuba bɔnsɔɛ, wo fa, won xa won ɲɛrɛ Alatala xa naiyalanyi ma.

sentences.english: For you, O Lord, have given up your people, the family of Jacob, because they are full of the evil ways of the east, and make use of secret arts like the Philistines, and are friends with the children of strange countries.
sentences.susu: Alatala, i bara i xa ɲama rabolo, barima e birama naamunyie fɔxɔ ra, naxee kelixi sogetede mabiri. Se matoe bara wuya naxee walima alɔ Filisitakae. I xa ɲama nun si Ala kolontaree bara lanyi xiri.

sentences.english: And their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end to their stores; their land is full of horses, and there is no end to their carriages.
sentences.susu: I xa ɲama bara xɛɛma nun gbeti gbegbe sɔtɔ, e xa naafuli mu ɲɔnma. E xa bɔxi bara rafe sɔɔri xa soee nun e ragisee ra.

sentences.english: Their land is full of images; they give worship to the work of their hands, even to that which their fingers have made.
sentences.susu: Kuyee toma nɛ yire birin. Kankan a xinbi sinma kuyee bɛ, e naxee masolixi e bɛlɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And the poor man's head is bent, and the great man goes down on his face: for this cause there will be no forgiveness for their sin.
sentences.susu: E felenma nɛ e bɛ, e e magoro e batufe ra. Na kui, i naxa diɲɛ e ma feo.

sentences.english: Go into a hole in the rock, covering yourselves with dust, in fear of the Lord, before the glory of his power.
sentences.susu: Wo wo nɔxun fanyee tagi bɔxi ma, alako wo xa wo makuya Alatala xa xɔnɛ ra, naxan fama a xa nɔrɛ makaabaxi kui.

sentences.english: The high looks of man will be put to shame, and the pride of men will be made low, and only the Lord will be lifted up in that day.
sentences.susu: Adamadi xa yɛtɛ igboya magoroma nɛ, mixie xa yɛtɛ iteya kuntin. Alatala keren nan a yɛtɛ itema na lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: For the day of the Lord of armies is coming on all the pride of men, and on all who are high and lifted up;
sentences.susu: Alatala Sɛnbɛma xa kiiti lɔxɔɛ fama yɛtɛ igboe bɛ. Naxee bara e yɛtɛ ite, Ala fama nɛ e ragorode.

sentences.english: And on all the high trees of Lebanon, and on all the strong trees of Bashan;
sentences.susu: A Liban sɛdiri bili nun Basan xa wuri bili itexi birin nagoroma nɛ.

sentences.english: And on all the high mountains, and on all the hills which are lifted up;
sentences.susu: A geya itexi fan bama nɛ.

sentences.english: And on every high tower, and on every strong wall;
sentences.susu: A mixie xa banxi makantaxie kanama nɛ, a e xa tɛtɛe rabira.

sentences.english: And on all the ships of Tarshish, and on all the fair boats.
sentences.susu: A e xa kunkui xungbee radulama nɛ.

sentences.english: And the high looks of man will be put to shame, and the pride of men will be made low: and only the Lord will be lifted up in that day.
sentences.susu: Alatala fama nɛ Adamadi xa yɛtɛ igboya ragorode, a mixie xa yɛtɛ iteya kuntin. Alatala keren nan a yɛtɛ itema na lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: And the images will never be seen again.
sentences.susu: Kuye fe birin kanama nɛ.

sentences.english: And men will go into cracks of the rocks, and into holes of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and before the glory of his power, when he comes out of his place, shaking the earth with his strength.
sentences.susu: Mixie e nɔxunma nɛ fɔnmɛe tagi gɛmɛ longori ra, e yili gema nɛ bɔxi kui, e fa e nɔxun Alatala xa xɔnɛ ma, naxan fama a xa nɔrɛ makaabaxi kui, a na keli bɔxi rasɛrɛnde tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: In that day men will put their images of silver and of gold, which they made for worship, in the keeping of the beasts of the dark places;
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ, mixie fama nɛ e xa kuye wɔlɛde bale nun tuukɛ ma, e nu naxee yailanxi xɛɛma nun gbeti ra e batufe ra.

sentences.english: To take cover in the cracks of the rocks, and in the holes of the hills, for fear of the Lord, and before the glory of his power, when he comes out of his place, shaking the earth with his strength.
sentences.susu: E e nɔxunma nɛ yilie nun fɔnmɛe kui fanye longori ra, e xa e makuya Alatala xa xɔnɛ ra, naxan fama a xa nɔrɛ makaabaxi kui, a na keli bɔxi rasɛrɛnde tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: Have no more to do with man, whose life is only a breath, for he is of no value.
sentences.susu: Wo ba wo yɛtɛ taxufe adamadi ra, ɲɛngi keren peti na naxan bɛ. Tide mundun na a ma?

sentences.english: For the Lord, the Lord of armies, is about to take away from Jerusalem and from Judah all their support; their store of bread and of water;
sentences.susu: Marigi Alatala Sɛnbɛma bara natɛ tongo Darisalamu nun Yudaya xun nakanafe ra. A xa baloe nun ye ba e yi ra,

sentences.english: The strong man and the man of war; the judge and the prophet; the man who has knowledge of secret arts, and the man who is wise because of his years;
sentences.susu: a xa e xa ɲalamae nun e xa sɔɔrie ragoro, a xa e xa kiitisae nun namiɲɔnmɛe rasabari, a xa e xa sematoe nun e xa forie makuya e boore ra,

sentences.english: The captain of fifty, and the man of high position, and the wise guide, and the wonder-worker, and he who makes use of secret powers.
sentences.susu: a xa e xa sɔɔri mangɛe, e xa marasimae, e xa walikɛ fanyie, nun e xa mixi kɔɔtaxi birin ba e yi ra.

sentences.english: And I will make children their chiefs, and foolish ones will have rule over them.
sentences.susu: N fama fonikee nan tide mangɛya ra e xun ma, dimɛe nan fama dɔxɔde e fari.

sentences.english: And the people will be crushed, every one by his neighbour; the young will be full of pride against the old, and those of low position will be lifted up against the noble.
sentences.susu: Kankan fuma nɛ a boore ma, fonikee tima nɛ xɛmɔxie kanke, fuyantee fan bagan mixi binyɛ ma.

sentences.english: When one man puts his hand on another in his father's house, and says, You have clothing, be our ruler and be responsible for us in our sad condition:
sentences.susu: Na kui, mixi nde a falama nɛ a bari boore nde bɛ, «Donma fanyi to na i tan yi ra, i xa findi muxu xa yarerati ra, i xa mangɛya tongo yi ɲaxasi kui.»

sentences.english: Then he will say with an oath, I will not be a helper, for in my house there is no bread or clothing: I will not let you make me a ruler of the people.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a ngaxakerenyi a yaabima nɛ, «Seriba mu na n na, donma nun donse yo mu na n ma banxi kui. Wo naxa n findi ɲama xa mangɛ ra.»

sentences.english: For Jerusalem has become feeble, and destruction has come on Judah, because their words and their acts are against the Lord, moving the eyes of his glory to wrath.
