sentences.susu: Yusufu to xunu, a naxa Marigi xa malekɛ xa yaamari rabatu, a a xa ginɛ xa futi xiri.

sentences.english: And he had no connection with her till she had given birth to a son; and he gave him the name Jesus.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a mu a kolon ginɛ ra han Mariyama xa di xɛmɛ bari xanbi. A naxa na di xili sa Isa.

sentences.english: Now when the birth of Jesus took place in Beth-lehem of Judaea, in the days of Herod the king, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
sentences.susu: Isa bari Bɛtɛlɛɛmu taa nan kui, Yudaya bɔxi ma, mangɛ Herode xa ɲamanɛ. Na waxati, karamɔxɔ ndee naxa fa Darisalamu keli sogetede biri ra,

sentences.english: Saying, Where is the King of the Jews whose birth has now taken place? We have seen his star in the east and have come to give him worship.
sentences.susu: e naxa maxɔrinyi ti, e naxɛ, «Yuwifie xa mangɛ naxan baxi baride, a na minden? Muxu faxi nɛ muxu xa fa suyidi a bɛ, barima muxu bara a xa tunbui to sogetede biri.»

sentences.english: And when it came to the ears of Herod the king, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Herode to na fe mɛ, a tan nun Darisalamuka birin naxa kɔntɔfili.

sentences.english: And he got together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, questioning them as to where the birth-place of the Christ would be.
sentences.susu: A naxa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe malan, a xa e maxɔrin Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi barima dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And they said to him, In Beth-lehem of Judaea; for so it is said in the writings of the prophet,
sentences.susu: E naxa a yaabi, «A barima Bɛtɛlɛɛmu taa nan kui, Yudaya bɔxi ma, barima namiɲɔnmɛ a sɛbɛxi,

sentences.english: You Beth-lehem, in the land of Judah, are not the least among the chiefs of Judah: out of you will come a ruler, who will be the keeper of my people Israel.
sentences.susu: ‹I tan Bɛtɛlɛɛmu, naxan na Yudaya bɔxi ma, i tide mu xurun Yudaya taa xungbee ya ma, barima mangɛ fama kelide i tan Bɛtɛlɛɛmu nɛ, naxan n ma Isirayila ɲama raɲɛrɛma, alɔ xuruse dɛmadonyi xurusee raɲɛrɛma ki naxɛ.›»

sentences.english: Then Herod sent for the wise men privately, and put questions to them about what time the star had been seen.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Herode naxa na karamɔxɔe xili gundo ra, a e maxɔrin tunbui minixi waxati naxan ma.

sentences.english: And he sent them to Beth-lehem and said, Go and make certain where the young child is; and when you have seen him, let me have news of it, so that I may come and give him worship.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, a naxa e xɛɛ Bɛtɛlɛɛmu yi xɛɛraya ra, «Wo siga, wo xa sa wakili yi diyɔrɛ fenfe ra. Wo na a to, wo xa fa n nakolon alako n fan xa sa suyidi a bɛ.»

sentences.english: And after hearing the king, they went on their way; and the star which they saw in the east went before them, till it came to rest over the place where the young child was.
sentences.susu: Karamɔxɔe to gɛ mangɛ xui ramɛde, e naxa siga. E man naxa tunbui to, e sa naxan to sogetede biri ra. Tunbui naxa ɲɛrɛ e ya ra han a naxa ti diyɔrɛ yire xun ma.

sentences.english: And when they saw the star they were full of joy.
sentences.susu: E to tunbui to, e naxa sɛɛwa ki fanyi ra.

sentences.english: And they came into the house, and saw the young child with Mary, his mother; and falling down on their faces they gave him worship; and from their store they gave him offerings of gold, perfume, and spices.
sentences.susu: E naxa so banxi kui, e naxa diyɔrɛ to a nga Mariyama yi ra. E naxa e magoro bɔxi, e suyidi diyɔrɛ bɛ. Na tɛmui, e naxa sanbasee ramini e xa kote kui, e xɛɛma, surayi fanyi, nun miri labundɛ fi diyɔrɛ ma.

sentences.english: And it was made clear to them by God in a dream that they were not to go back to Herod; so they went into their country by another way.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, Ala to nu bara e rakolon xiye kui a a mu lanma e xa gbilen Herode yire, e naxa gbilen e xa bɔxi ma kira gbɛtɛ ra.

sentences.english: And when they had gone, an angel of the Lord came to Joseph in a dream, saying, Get up and take the young child and his mother, and go into Egypt, and do not go from there till I give you word; for Herod will be searching for the young child to put him to death.
sentences.susu: Karamɔxɔe siga xanbi, Marigi xa malekɛ naxa mini Yusufu ma xiye kui, a a masen a bɛ, «Keli. Diyɔrɛ nun a nga xanin Misira bɔxi ma. Wo xa lu mɛnni han n wɔyɛnma i bɛ tɛmui naxɛ, barima Herode diyɔrɛ fenma nɛ alako a xa a faxa.»

sentences.english: So he took the young child and his mother by night, and went into Egypt;
sentences.susu: Yusufu naxa keli kɔɛ ra, a diyɔrɛ nun a nga xanin Misira.

sentences.english: And was there till the death of Herod; so that the word of the Lord through the prophet might come true, Out of Egypt have I sent for my son.
sentences.susu: E naxa lu mɛnni han Herode naxa faxa, alako Marigi naxan masen namiɲɔnmɛ saabui ra, a xa kamali, «N bara n ma di xili, a xa keli Misira.»

sentences.english: Then Herod, when he saw that he had been tricked by the wise men, was very angry; and he sent out, and put to death all the male children in Beth-lehem and in all the parts round about it, from two years old and under, acting on the knowledge which he had got with care from the wise men.
sentences.susu: Herode to a kolon a karamɔxɔe bara a madaxu, a bɔɲɛ naxa te a ɲaaxi ra. A naxa yaamari fi, di xɛmɛ birin xa faxa Bɛtɛlɛɛmu nun a rabilinyi birin, naxee mu nu ɲɛ saxan sɔtɔ sinden. A na natɛ tongo na karamɔxɔe xa tunbui to tɛmui nan ma.

sentences.english: Then the word of Jeremiah the prophet came true,
sentences.susu: Na kui, Annabi Yeremi xa masenyi naxa kamali,

sentences.english: In Ramah there was a sound of weeping and great sorrow, Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted for their loss.
sentences.susu: «Xui nde bara mɛ Rama, wa xui nun sunnunyi gbegbe na a ra. Raxele wama a xa die nan ma fe ra, a mu tinxi mixi yo xa a madundu barima die mu a bɛ sɔnɔn duniɲɛ.»

sentences.english: But when Herod was dead, an angel of the Lord came in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
sentences.susu: Herode to faxa, Marigi xa malekɛ naxa mini Yusufu ma xiye kui Misira bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: Saying, Get up and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: because they who were attempting to take the young child's life are dead.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen a bɛ, «Keli, diyɔrɛ nun a nga tongo, i xa gbilen e ra Isirayila bɔxi ma, barima naxee nu waxi diyɔrɛ faxafe, e bara faxa.»

sentences.english: And he got up, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.
sentences.susu: Yusufu naxa keli, a naxa diyɔrɛ nun a nga tongo, e gbilen Isirayila bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: But when it came to his ears that Archelaus was ruling over Judaea in the place of his father Herod, he was in fear of going there; and God having given him news of the danger in a dream, he went out of the way into the country parts of Galilee.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Yusufu to a mɛ a Araxelusi nan findixi Yudaya mangɛ ra a baba Herode ɲɔxɔɛ ra, a naxa gaaxu sode naa. Ala to wɔyɛn a ra xiye kui, a naxa siga Galile bɔxi ma,

sentences.english: And he came and was living in a town named Nazareth: so that the word of the prophets might come true, He will be named a Nazarene.
sentences.susu: a sa sabati Nasarɛti. Na raba nɛ alako namiɲɔnmɛe xa masenyi xa kamali, naxan a masenxi, «A xili falama nɛ, ‹Nasarɛtika.›»

sentences.english: And in those days John the Baptist came preaching in the waste land of Judaea,
sentences.susu: Na waxati Annabi Yaya Xunxa naxa kawandi ti fɔlɔ Yudaya gbengberen yire.

sentences.english: Saying, Let your hearts be turned from sin; for the kingdom of heaven is near.
sentences.susu: A nu a masen, «Wo tuubi, barima Ala xa mangɛya niini bara makɔrɛ.»

sentences.english: For this is he of whom Isaiah the prophet said, The voice of one crying in the waste land, Make ready the way of the Lord, make his roads straight.
sentences.susu: Annabi Esayi nu Annabi Yaya nan ma fe falafe, a to a masen, «Mixi nde a xui itema gbengberen yire, ‹Wo kira yailan Marigi bɛ, wo kirae matinxin a ya ra.›»

sentences.english: Now John was clothed in camel's hair, with a leather band about him; and his food was locusts and honey.
sentences.susu: Ɲɔxɔmɛ xabe donma nan nu ragoroxi Yaya ma, bɛlɛti kiri daaxi nu xirixi a tagi. A nu baloma katoe nun wula kumi nan na.

sentences.english: Then Jerusalem and all Judaea went out to him, and all the people from near Jordan;
sentences.susu: Darisalamukae, Yudayakae, nun mixi naxee birin nu sabatixi Yurudɛn xure rabilinyi, e nu sigama a yire.

sentences.english: And they were given baptism by him in the river Jordan, saying openly that they had done wrong.
sentences.susu: E nu e xa yunubie masenma kɛnɛ ma, Yaya fan nu e xunxama Yurudɛn xure xɔɔra Ala xa fe ra.

sentences.english: But when he saw a number of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, Offspring of snakes, at whose word are you going in flight from the wrath to come?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Annabi Yaya to Farisɛnie nun Saduseni gbegbe to fa ra e xa e xunxa ye xɔɔra, a naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo tan bɔximase bɔnsɔɛ! Nde wo rakolonxi wo xa wo gi Ala xa xɔnɛ ma naxan na fafe?

sentences.english: Let your change of heart be seen in your works:
sentences.susu: Wo xa fe fanyi nan naba naxan a masenma a wo bara tuubi.

sentences.english: And say not to yourselves, We have Abraham for our father; because I say to you that God is able from these stones to make children for Abraham.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa a fala wo yɛtɛ ma, ‹Iburahima nan na muxu benba ra,› barima Ala nɔma yi gɛmɛe mafindide Iburahima xa die ra.

sentences.english: And even now the axe is put to the root of the trees; every tree then which does not give good fruit is cut down, and put into the fire.
sentences.susu: Beera ɲan na wurie sanke ma a xa e bilie sɛgɛ. Wuri naxan yo mu bogi fanyi raminima, a sɛgɛma nɛ, a woli tɛ i.

sentences.english: Truly, I give baptism with water to those of you whose hearts are changed; but he who comes after me is greater than I, whose shoes I am not good enough to take up: he will give you baptism with the Holy Spirit and with fire:
sentences.susu: N tan wo xunxama ye nan xɔɔra wo xa tuubi xa fe ra, kɔnɔ naxan fama fade n xanbi ra, na sɛnbɛ gbo n tan bɛ. Na binyɛ mu na n tan yi ra hali a xa sankiri maxaninfe ra. A tan nan Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi ragoroma wo ma, a tan nan wo xunxama tɛ ra.

sentences.english: In whose hand is the instrument with which he will make clean his grain; he will put the good grain in his store, but the waste will be burned up in the fire which will never be put out.
sentences.susu: A xa segerenyi suxuxi a yi ra, a maale nun a lagi yegetima naxan na lɔnyi ma. A maale rasoma a xa bili kui, kɔnɔ a lagi tan ganma tɛ ra naxan mu xubenma.»

sentences.english: Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan, to be given baptism by him.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Isa naxa keli Galile, fafe ra Yaya yire Yurudɛn xure, alako Yaya xa a xunxa ye xɔɔra.

sentences.english: But John would have kept him back, saying, It is I who have need of baptism from you, and do you come to me?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Yaya mu nu tinxi na fe ra. A naxa a fala, «N tan nan hayi a ma i tan xa n xunxa ye xɔɔra, kɔnɔ i tan nan fa faxi n tan xa i xunxa ye xɔɔra?»

sentences.english: But Jesus made answer, saying to him, Let it be so now: because so it is right for us to make righteousness complete. Then he gave him baptism.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Yakɔsi, a xa raba yi ki, barima a lanma won xa fe birin naba a sɛriyɛ ki ma.» Na kui, Yaya naxa tin a ra.

sentences.english: And Jesus, having been given baptism, straight away went up from the water; and, the heavens opening, he saw the Spirit of God coming down on him as a dove;
sentences.susu: Isa xun to xa, a naxa te ye xɔɔra, koore naxa rabi, a naxa Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi to goro ra a ma alɔ ganbɛ.

sentences.english: And a voice came out of heaven, saying, This is my dearly loved Son, with whom I am well pleased.
sentences.susu: Xui nde naxa mɛ keli koore ma, a a masen, «N ma Di maxanuxi nan yi ki naxan n kɛnɛnxi ki fanyi ra.»

sentences.english: Then Jesus was sent by the Spirit into the waste land to be tested by the Evil One.
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili naxa Isa xun ti gbengberenyi ma alako Ibulisa xa sa kata a xa a ratantan.

sentences.english: And after going without food for forty days and forty nights, he was in need of it.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu bara sun xi tongo naani, kɔɛ nun yanyi, kaamɛ nu na a ma.

sentences.english: And the Evil One came and said to him, If you are the Son of God, give the word for these stones to become bread.
sentences.susu: Maratantanma to maso a ra, a naxa a fala a bɛ, «Xa Ala xa Di nan i ra, yaamari fi yi gɛmɛe xa findi taami ra.»

sentences.english: But he made answer and said, It is in the Writings, Bread is not man's only need, but every word which comes out of the mouth of God.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «A sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, ‹Mixi mu baloma taami gbansan xa ra. Ala xa masenyi birin findixi baloe nan na adama bɛ.›»

sentences.english: Then the Evil One took him to the holy town; and he put him on the highest point of the Temple and said to him,
sentences.susu: Ibulisa naxa a xanin Darisalamu, taa sɛniyɛnxi, a a ti Ala xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi fari, yire itexi.

sentences.english: If you are the Son of God, let yourself go down; for it is in the Writings, He will give his angels care over you; and, In their hands they will keep you up, so that your foot may not be crushed against a stone.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala a bɛ, «Xa Ala xa Di nan lanxi i ma, tugan, barima a sɛbɛxi, ‹Ala yaamari fima nɛ a xa malekɛe ma i xa fe ra,› ‹e e bɛlɛxɛe rasoma nɛ i bun ma, e i ralaxun alako i sanyi naxa din gɛmɛ ra.›»

sentences.english: Jesus said to him, Again it is in the Writings, You may not put the Lord your God to the test.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Iyo, kɔnɔ a man sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, ‹I naxa i Marigi Ala mato.›»

sentences.english: Again, the Evil One took him up to a very high mountain, and let him see all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them;
sentences.susu: Ibulisa man naxa a xanin geya itexi fari, a fa duniɲa mangɛya birin masen a bɛ, e nun e xa dariyɛ.

sentences.english: And he said to him, All these things will I give you, if you will go down on your face and give me worship.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala a bɛ, «N yi birin fima nɛ i ma xa i suyidi n bɛ, i n batu.»

sentences.english: Then said Jesus to him, Away, Satan: for it is in the Writings, Give worship to the Lord your God and be his servant only.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Sentanɛ, keli be! A sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, ‹I xa i Marigi Ala gbansan nan batu, i xa suyidi a keren nan bɛ.›»

sentences.english: Then the Evil One went away from him, and angels came and took care of him.
sentences.susu: Na wɔyɛnyi dangi xanbi, Ibulisa naxa keli a xun. Malekɛe naxa e maso Isa ra, e a sɛnbɛ so.

sentences.english: Now when it came to his ears that John had been put in prison, he went away to Galilee;
sentences.susu: Isa to a mɛ a Yaya bara sa geeli, a naxa gbilen Galile bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: And going away from Nazareth, he came and made his living-place in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the country of Zebulun and Naphtali:
sentences.susu: A naxa keli Nasarɛti taa kui, a sa sabati Kapɛrɛnamu, taa nde naxan nu na baa dɛ ra, Sabulon nun Nafatali bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: So that the word of the prophet Isaiah might come true,
sentences.susu: Na naxa raba alako Annabi Esayi xa masenyi xa kamali,

sentences.english: The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, by the way of the sea, the other side of Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
sentences.susu: «Sabulon nun Nafatali bɔxi, naxee na kira ra sigafe baa dɛ ra Yurudɛn naakiri, wo findixi Galile bɔxi nan na naxan na si gbɛtɛe bɛlɛxɛ.

sentences.english: The people who were in the dark saw a great light, and to those in the land of the shade of death did the dawn come up.
sentences.susu: Ɲamanɛ naxan dɔxɔxi dimi kui, e bara naiyalanyi belebele to. Naxee dɔxɔxi faxɛ xa dimi kui, naiyalanyi bara mini e bɛ.»

sentences.english: From that time Jesus went about preaching and saying, Let your hearts be turned from sin, for the kingdom of heaven is near.
sentences.susu: Keli na tɛmui ma, Isa naxa kawandi ti fɔlɔ, a nu a fala, «Wo tuubi, barima Ala xa mangɛya niini bara makɔrɛ.»

sentences.english: And when he was walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, whose other name was Peter, and Andrew, his brother, who were putting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu ɲɛrɛfe Galile baa dɛ ra, a naxa xɛmɛ firin to e na yɛlɛ wolife. Yɛxɛsuxuie nan nu e ra, Simɔn, naxan xili Piyɛri, a nun a xunya Andire.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo bira n fɔxɔ ra. Tɛmui dangixi wo nu yɛxɛ nan suxuma, kɔnɔ yakɔsi n a niyama wo xa nu mixie nan sɔtɔ n bɛ.»

sentences.english: And straight away they let go the nets and went after him.
sentences.susu: E naxa e xa yɛlɛe lu na keren na, e bira Isa fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And going on from there he saw two other brothers, James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, in the boat with their father, stitching up their nets; and he said, Come.
sentences.susu: E to siga, e naxa xɛmɛ firin gbɛtɛ to, Sebede xa di Yaki nun a xunya Yaya. E nu na yɛlɛe madɛgɛfe kunkui kui e baba Sebede fɛ ma. Isa naxa e xili,

sentences.english: And they went straight from the boat and their father and came after him.
sentences.susu: e fan naxa kunkui nun e baba lu na keren na, e bira Isa fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their Synagogues and preaching the good news of the kingdom, and making well those who were ill with any disease among the people.
sentences.susu: Na xanbi Isa naxa Galile bɔxi birin isa fɔlɔ. A nu mixie xaranma e xa salidee kui, a nu e kawandi Ala xa mangɛya niini xa xibaaru fanyi ra, a nu furema mɔɔli birin nayalan ɲama ya ma.

sentences.english: And news of him went out through all Syria; and they took to him all who were ill with different diseases and pains, those having evil spirits and those who were off their heads, and those who had no power of moving. And he made them well.
sentences.susu: A xili naxa te Siriya bɔxi birin ma. Mixie naxa fa furema mɔɔli birin na a xɔn ma. E nu fama mixie ra naxee nu na tɔɔrɔfe a ɲaaxi ra, ɲinnɛ nu naxee fɔxɔ ra, bira fure nu na naxee ma, a nun namatɛe. Isa nu e birin nayalanma.

sentences.english: And there went after him great numbers from Galilee and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judaea and from the other side of Jordan.
sentences.susu: Ɲama gbegbe naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra kelife Galile bɔxi ma, Taa Fu bɔxi, Darisalamu, Yudaya, nun bɔxi naxan na Yurudɛn naakiri ma.

sentences.english: And seeing great masses of people he went up into the mountain; and when he was seated his disciples came to him.
sentences.susu: Isa to ɲama to, a naxa te geya fari, a a magoro. A fɔxirabirɛe naxa e makɔrɛ a ra.

sentences.english: And with these words he gave them teaching, saying,
sentences.susu: A naxa masenyi ti fɔlɔ e bɛ.

sentences.english: Happy are the poor in spirit: for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
sentences.susu: «Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee e yɛtɛ magoroma, barima e fama nɛ sode Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: Happy are those who are sad: for they will be comforted.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee wama, barima e fama nɛ madundude.

sentences.english: Happy are the gentle: for the earth will be their heritage.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee diɲɛma, bɔxi findima e tan nan kɛ ra.

sentences.english: Happy are those whose heart's desire is for righteousness: for they will have their desire.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee wama tinxinyi xɔn, alɔ kaamɛtɔɛ wama donse xɔn ma ki naxɛ, barima e a sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: Happy are those who have mercy: for they will be given mercy.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee kinikinima e booree ma, barima Ala kinikinima nɛ e fan ma.

sentences.english: Happy are the clean in heart: for they will see God.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee bɔɲɛ fiixɛ, barima e Ala toma nɛ a xa fonisireya kui.

sentences.english: Happy are the peacemakers: for they will be named sons of God.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee lanyi fenma e nun mixie tagi, barima e xili falama nɛ Ala xa die.

sentences.english: Happy are those who are attacked on account of righteousness: for the kingdom of heaven will be theirs.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na mixie bɛ naxee ɲaxankataxi tinxinyi xa fe ra, barima e soma nɛ Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.»

sentences.english: Happy are you when men give you a bad name, and are cruel to you, and say all evil things against you falsely, because of me.
sentences.susu: «Sɛɛwɛ na wo bɛ e na wo konbi, e na wo ɲaxankata, e na wule nun fe kobi mɔɔli birin fala wo xun ma n ma fe ra.

sentences.english: Be glad and full of joy; for great is your reward in heaven: for so were the prophets attacked who were before you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ɲɛlɛxin, wo xa sɛɛwa, barima wo baraayi gboma nɛ ariyanna. Beenun wo xa bari, e namiɲɔnmɛe fan ɲaxankata na ki nɛ.»

sentences.english: You are the salt of the earth; but if its taste goes from the salt, how will you make it salt again? it is then good for nothing but to be put out and crushed under foot by men.
sentences.susu: «Wo maniyaxi fɔxɛ nan na yi duniɲa adamadie ya ma, kɔnɔ xa fɔxɛ mɛxɛmɛxɛnyi bara ba, a fa mɛxɛmɛxɛnma di? A tide yo mu na kɔrɛ, fo a woli tande, mixie ɲɛrɛ a fari.

sentences.english: You are the light of the world. A town put on a hill may be seen by all.
sentences.susu: Wo maniyaxi naiyalanyi nan na yi duniɲa adamadie ya ma. Taa naxan dɔxɔxi geya fari, na mu nɔma nɔxunde.

sentences.english: And a burning light is not put under a vessel, but on its table; so that its rays may be shining on all who are in the house.
sentences.susu: Lanpui mu radɛxɛma a xa dɔxɔ debe bun ma. A dɔxɔma lanpui dɔxɔse nan fari alako a xa banxi kui iyalan birin bɛ.

sentences.english: Even so let your light be shining before men, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
sentences.susu: Wo xa naiyalanyi fan xa yanba na ki adamadie ya ma, alako e xa wo xa kɛwali fanyie to, e wo Baba matɔxɔ naxan na ariyanna.»

sentences.english: Let there be no thought that I have come to put an end to the law or the prophets. I have not come for destruction, but to make complete.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa a maɲɔxun a n faxi nɛ n xa Tawureta Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa sɛriyɛ ba a i. N mu faxi e bade xɛ, n faxi nɛ alako n xa e rakamali.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, Till heaven and earth come to an end, not the smallest letter or part of a letter will in any way be taken from the law, till all things are done.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, danmi koore nun bɔxi na na, hali sigirɛ keren mu bama Ala xa sɛriyɛ ra, fo a birin kamali.

sentences.english: Whoever then goes against the smallest of these laws, teaching men to do the same, will be named least in the kingdom of heaven; but he who keeps the laws, teaching others to keep them, will be named great in the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.susu: Na kui, mixi yo Ala xa yaamari keren matandi, na yaamari xurun kiyoki, a man fa mixi gbɛtɛe ratantan na kui, a kanyi fan xili xurunma nɛ birin bɛ Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma. Kɔnɔ mixi yo Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatu, a mixi gbɛtɛe xaran na ra, na kanyi xunnakeli nan sɔtɔma Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: For I say to you, If your righteousness is not greater than the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never go into the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, xa wo xa tinxinyi mu dangi sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛnie gbe ra, wo mu soma Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma abadan.»

sentences.english: You have knowledge that it was said in old times, You may not put to death; and, Whoever puts to death will be in danger of being judged:
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon wo benbae yamari naxan na, ‹Wo naxa faxɛ ti. Faxɛti makiitima nɛ.›

sentences.english: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be in danger of being judged; and he who says to his brother, Raca, will be in danger from the Sanhedrin; and whoever says, You foolish one, will be in danger of the hell of fire.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan xa a fala wo bɛ, naxan yo bɔɲɛ na te a ngaxakerenyi xili ma, na kanyi makiitima nɛ. Naxan na a fala ngaxakerenyi bɛ, ‹I tan dugula›, na kanyi makiitima nɛ kiitisa xungbee ya i. Naxan na a fala a bɛ, ‹I tan xaxilitare!›, na kanyi wolima nɛ yahannama tɛ xɔɔra.»

sentences.english: If then you are making an offering at the altar and there it comes to your mind that your brother has something against you,
sentences.susu: «Na kui, xa wo bara siga sɛrɛxɛ bade, wo fa ratu a wo ngaxakerenyi xɔnɔxi wo ma fe nde ma,

sentences.english: While your offering is still before the altar, first go and make peace with your brother, then come and make your offering.
sentences.susu: wo xa wo xa sɛrɛxɛ lu sɛrɛxɛbade fɛ ma sinden, wo siga wo ngaxakerenyi yire. Wo xa lanyi xiri wo nun wo ngaxakerenyi tagi, wo fa gbilen wo xa sɛrɛxɛ bade.»

sentences.english: Come to an agreement quickly with him who has a cause against you at law, while you are with him on the way, for fear that he may give you up to the judge and the judge may give you to the police and you may be put into prison.
sentences.susu: «I xa kata wo nun i kalamuma xa lan sinnanyi ma, wo na kira xɔn ma tɛmui naxɛ. Xa na mu a ra a i xaninma kiitisa yire, kiitisa fan i so kɔsibili yi ra, na fan i sa geeli.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, You will not come out from there till you have made payment of the very last farthing.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala i bɛ, i mu minima mɛnni fo i kɔbiri birin fi han batanka dɔnxɔɛ.»

sentences.english: You have knowledge that it was said, You may not have connection with another man's wife:
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon wo benbae yamari naxan na, ‹Wo naxa yɛnɛ raba.›

sentences.english: But I say to you that everyone whose eyes are turned on a woman with desire has had connection with her in his heart.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan xa a fala wo bɛ, naxan yo a ya ti ginɛ nde ra milɛ kui, na kanyi bara gɛ yɛnɛ rabade a bɔɲɛ kui.

sentences.english: And if your right eye is a cause of trouble to you, take it out and put it away from you; because it is better to undergo the loss of one part, than for all your body to go into hell.
sentences.susu: Xa i yirefan ya findima i ratantanse ra, a ba na, a wɔlɛ. Fate yire nde bafe na, na fisa dinɛ i fate gundi birin wolife yahannama.

sentences.english: And if your right hand is a cause of trouble to you, let it be cut off and put it away from you; because it is better to undergo the loss of one part, than for all your body to go into hell.
sentences.susu: Xa i yirefan bɛlɛxɛ findima i ratantanse ra, a bolon, a wɔlɛ. Fate salonse nde bolonfe, na fisa dinɛ i fate gundi birin wolife yahannama.»

sentences.english: Again, it was said, Whoever puts away his wife has to give her a statement in writing for this purpose:
sentences.susu: «A man masenxi nɛ, ‹Naxan wama mɛɛfe a xa ginɛ ra, a xa fatan kɛɛdi so a yi ra.›

sentences.english: But I say to you that everyone who puts away his wife for any other cause but the loss of her virtue, makes her false to her husband; and whoever takes her as his wife after she is put away, is no true husband to her.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan xa a fala wo bɛ, naxan yo mɛɛ a xa ginɛ ra, xa a xa ginɛ mu yɛnɛ xa rabaxi, na kanyi bara a niya na ginɛ xa findi yɛnɛla ra a na dɔxɔ xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ xɔn ma tɛmui naxɛ. Xɛmɛ naxan fan na ginɛ dɔxɔma e mɛɛxi naxan na, a fan bara findi yɛnɛla ra.»

sentences.english: Again, you have knowledge that it was said in old times, Do not take false oaths, but give effect to your oaths to the Lord:
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon wo benbae yamari naxan na, ‹Wo naxa wo xa marakali kana, wo xa a rakamali nɛ Marigi bɛ.›

sentences.english: But I say to you, Take no oaths at all: not by the heaven, because it is the seat of God;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan xa a fala wo bɛ, wo naxa wo kali feo! Wo naxa wo kali koore ra, barima Ala xa kibanyi nan a ra.

sentences.english: Or by the earth, because it is the resting-place for his foot; or by Jerusalem, because it is the town of the great King.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo kali bɔxi ra, barima Ala sanyi tide na a ra. Wo naxa wo kali Darisalamu ra, barima Mangɛ Xungbe xa taa nan a ra.

sentences.english: You may not take an oath by your head, because you are not able to make one hair white or black.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo kali wo yɛtɛ xunyi ra, barima wo mu nɔma xunsɛxɛ keren nafugade, wo mu nɔma a fɔɔrɔde.

sentences.english: But let your words be simply, Yes or No: and whatever is more than these is of the Evil One.
sentences.susu: Wo xa nɔndi fala. Xa iyo nan a ra, wo xa a fala ‹iyo›. Xa ade nan a ra, wo xa a fala ‹ade›. Sese sa na xun ma, a fatanxi Sentanɛ nan ma.»

sentences.english: You have knowledge that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon wo yamari naxan na, ‹Wo xa ya ɲɔxɔ ya ra, wo xa ɲinyi ɲɔxɔ ɲinyi ra.›

sentences.english: But I say to you, Do not make use of force against an evil man; but to him who gives you a blow on the right side of your face let the left be turned.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan xa a fala wo bɛ, wo naxa mixi kobi gere. Xa mixi nde wo xɛrɛ garin, wo xa boore sɛɛti fan ti a bɛ.

sentences.english: And if any man goes to law with you and takes away your coat, do not keep back your robe from him.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde wama wo xaninfe kiiti banxi, alako a xa donma ba wo yi ra, wo xa wo xa guba fan lu a yi.

sentences.english: And whoever makes you go one mile, go with him two.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde wo karaxan wo xa a mati ɲɛrɛ kui kilo keren, wo xa a mati kilo firin.

sentences.english: Give to him who comes with a request, and keep not your property from him who would for a time make use of it.
sentences.susu: Naxan na i makula, i xa a ki. Naxan wama se nde yofufe i ma, i naxa tondi a bɛ.»

sentences.english: You have knowledge that it was said, Have love for your neighbour, and hate for him who is against you:
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon wo yamarixi naxan na, ‹Wo xa wo boore xanu, wo xa wo yaxui xɔn.›

sentences.english: But I say to you, Have love for those who are against you, and make prayer for those who are cruel to you;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan xa a fala wo bɛ, wo xa wo yaxuie xanu, wo xa Ala maxandi mixie bɛ naxee wo ɲaxankatama.

sentences.english: So that you may be the sons of your Father in heaven; for his sun gives light to the evil and to the good, and he sends rain on the upright man and on the sinner.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo findima wo Baba xa die ra naxan na ariyanna, naxan kuye ibama tinxintɔɛe nun tinxintaree bɛ, naxan tunɛ ragoroma mixi fanyie nun mixi kobie bɛ.

sentences.english: For if you have love for those who have love for you, what credit is it to you? do not the tax-farmers the same?
sentences.susu: Xa wo sa mixie gbansan nan xanuma, naxee wo fan xanuxi, wo baraayi mundun sɔtɔma na kui? Hali duuti maxili kobie na mɔɔli rabama.

sentences.english: And if you say, Good day, to your brothers only, what do you do more than others? do not even the Gentiles the same?
sentences.susu: Xa wo sa wo ngaxakerenyie gbansan nan xɛɛbuma, wo munfe rabafe naxan findi fe nɛɛnɛ ra na kui? Hali kaafirie na mɔɔli rabama.

sentences.english: Be then complete in righteousness, even as your Father in heaven is complete.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa tinxinyi nun marafanyi xa kamali, alɔ wo naxan toxi wo Baba ra naxan na ariyanna.»

sentences.english: Take care not to do your good works before men, to be seen by them; or you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa fe fanyi raba mixie ya tode ra e xa wo xa tinxinyi to, xa na mu a ra wo mu baraayi yo sɔtɔma wo Baba ra, naxan na ariyanna.

sentences.english: When then you give money to the poor, do not make a noise about it, as the false-hearted men do in the Synagogues and in the streets, so that they may have glory from men. Truly, I say to you, They have their reward.
sentences.susu: Na kui, i nɛ mixi kima, i naxa a sigi sa duniɲa birin bɛ alɔ filankafuie a rabama ki naxɛ salide nun taa ma, alako mixie xa e matɔxɔ. N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, e bara gɛ e xa wali sare birin sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: But when you give money, let not your left hand see what your right hand does:
sentences.susu: I nɛ mixi kima i yirefanyi ra, kɔɔla naxa a kolon.

sentences.english: So that your giving may be in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will give you your reward.
sentences.susu: I xa mixi ki suturɛ nan na. Na kui, i Baba Ala naxan gundo birin kolon, a fama nɛ na sare ragbilende i ma.»

sentences.english: And when you make your prayers, be not like the false-hearted men, who take pleasure in getting up and saying their prayers in the Synagogues and at the street turnings so that they may be seen by men. Truly I say to you, They have their reward.
sentences.susu: «Wo nɛ salima, wo naxa lu alɔ filankafuie naxee salima, e tixi salidee kui nun kira dɛ ra alako mixie xa e to. N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, e bara gɛ e xa wali sare birin sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: But when you make your prayer, go into your private room, and, shutting the door, say a prayer to your Father in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will give you your reward.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i tan nɛ salima, siga i xa banxi yire nde nɔxunyi kui, i naadɛ ragali, i Ala maxandi naxan mu toma. Na kui, i Baba Ala naxan gundo fe birin toxi, a fama nɛ i sare fide.»

sentences.english: And in your prayer do not make use of the same words again and again, as the Gentiles do: for they have the idea that God will give attention to them because of the number of their words.
sentences.susu: «Wo nɛ Ala maxandima, wo naxa wo xa wɔyɛnyi rawuya fufafu, alɔ kaafiri naxee laxi a ra a e xa duba suxuma e xa wɔyɛnyi radiganxie nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: So be not like them; because your Father has knowledge of your needs even before you make your requests to him.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa lu alɔ e tan, barima wo Baba Ala wo hayi kolon beenun wo xa a maxandi.»

sentences.english: Let this then be your prayer: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
sentences.susu: «Wo lan wo xa sali yi ki nɛ: ‹Muxu Baba naxan na ariyanna, duniɲa birin xa i xili sɛniyɛnxi kolon.

sentences.english: Let your kingdom come. Let your pleasure be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
sentences.susu: I xa mangɛya xa fa. I sago xa raba duniɲa ma, alɔ a rabama ariyanna ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Give us this day bread for our needs.
sentences.susu: Baloe fi muxu ma to lɔxɔɛ, muxu hayi na naxan ma.

sentences.english: And make us free of our debts, as we have made those free who are in debt to us.
sentences.susu: Diɲɛ muxu xa yunubie ma, alɔ muxu fan diɲɛxi mixie haakɛe ma ki naxɛ, naxee bara fe kobi niya muxu ra.

sentences.english: And let us not be put to the test, but keep us safe from the Evil One.
sentences.susu: I naxa muxu ti maratantanyi kira xɔn, i xa muxu ratanga Sentanɛ ma. I tan nan gbe na mangɛya, sɛnbɛ, nun binyɛ ra abadan. Amina.›»

sentences.english: For if you let men have forgiveness for their sins, you will have forgiveness from your Father in heaven.
sentences.susu: «Xa wo diɲɛ mixie haakɛe ma, wo Baba naxan na ariyanna, a fan diɲɛma nɛ wo ma,

sentences.english: But if you do not let men have forgiveness for their sins, you will not have forgiveness from your Father for your sins.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ xa wo mu diɲɛ mixie ma, wo Baba naxan na ariyanna, a fan mu diɲɛma wo xa yunubie ma.»

sentences.english: And when you go without food, be not sad-faced as the false-hearted are. For they go about with changed looks, so that men may see that they are going without food. Truly I say to you, They have their reward.
sentences.susu: «Wo nɛ sunyi suxuma, wo naxa wo yatagi ixɔnɔ alɔ filankafuie e yatagi ixɔnɔma ki naxɛ, mixie xa a kolon a e na sunyi. N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, e bara gɛ e xa wali sare birin sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: But when you go without food, put oil on your head and make your face clean;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i tan nɛ sunyi suxuma, i xa ture sa i xunyi ma, i i yatagi maxa,

sentences.english: So that no one may see that you are going without food, but your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will give you your reward.
sentences.susu: alako mixie naxa a kolon a i na sunyi. Na kui, i Baba Ala naxan mu toma, naxan man gundo fe birin toxi, a fama nɛ i sare fide.»

sentences.english: Make no store of wealth for yourselves on earth, where it may be turned to dust by worms and weather, and where thieves may come in by force and take it away.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa wo harige malan duniɲa ma, nimasee nun xɔrixɔri a xun nakanama dɛnnaxɛ, xa na mu a ra muɲɛtie nɔma a muɲade banxi kui dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: But make a store for yourselves in heaven, where it will not be turned to dust and where thieves do not come in to take it away:
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo harige malan ariyanna nɛ, nimasee nun xɔrixɔri mu kanari sama dɛnnaxɛ, muɲɛtie fan mu muɲɛ tima dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: For where your wealth is, there will your heart be.
sentences.susu: Wo harige na dɛnnaxɛ, wo bɔɲɛ fan luma naa nɛ.»

sentences.english: The light of the body is the eye; if then your eye is true, all your body will be full of light.
sentences.susu: «Ya nan na fate xa lanpui ra. Xa i ya fan, i fate birin iyalanma nɛ,

sentences.english: But if your eye is evil, all your body will be dark. If then the light which is in you is dark, how dark it will be!
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ xa i ya mu fan, i fate luma dimi nan kui. Na kui, xa i xa naiyalanyi bara findi dimi ra, na dimi ifɔɔrɔ de!»

sentences.english: No man is able to be a servant to two masters: for he will have hate for the one and love for the other, or he will keep to one and have no respect for the other. You may not be servants of God and of wealth.
sentences.susu: «Mixi yo mu nɔma lude marigi firin xa yaamari bun ma, barima a fama marigi keren xɔnde, a boore maxanu. A xirima keren na, a boore rabolo. Wo mu nɔma Ala nun naafuli batude tɛmui keren.»

sentences.english: So I say to you, Take no thought for your life, about food or drink, or about clothing for your body. Is not life more than food, and the body more than its clothing?
sentences.susu: «Na nan a toxi, n xa a fala wo bɛ, wo naxa kɔntɔfili baloe xa fe ra wo hayi na naxan ma yi duniɲɛigiri kui, xa na mu a ra, dugie xa fe ra wo naxee ragoroma wo fate ma. Wo xa duniɲɛigiri tide mu gbo donse bɛ? Wo fate tide mu gbo dugie bɛ?

sentences.english: See the birds of heaven; they do not put seeds in the earth, they do not get in grain, or put it in store-houses; and your Father in heaven gives them food. Are you not of much more value than they?
sentences.susu: Wo xɔnie mato koore ma. E mu sansi sima, e mu xɛ xabama, e mu donse ragatama bilie kui, kɔnɔ wo Baba naxan na ariyanna, a e baloma. Wo tan mu dangi na xɔnie ra?

sentences.english: And which of you by taking thought is able to make himself a cubit taller?
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma hali xi keren sade a xa simaya xun a xa kɔntɔfili saabui ra?

sentences.english: And why are you troubled about clothing? See the flowers of the field, how they come up; they do no work, they make no thread:
sentences.susu: Munfe ra wo kɔntɔfilima wo xa sosee xa fe ra? Wo sansi fuge tofanyie mato, e minima wula sansie ma ki naxɛ. E mu walima, e mu woligɛsɛ yailanma,

sentences.english: But I say to you that even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ n xa a fala wo bɛ, hali mangɛ Sulemani xa dariyɛ birin kui, a xa sosee mu nu tofan alɔ na sansi fuge keren.

sentences.english: But if God gives such clothing to the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is put into the oven, will he not much more give you clothing, O you of little faith?
sentences.susu: Xa Ala sansi mɛɛnima yi ki nɛ, sansi naxan na na to, tina a gan, a mu mɛɛnima wo fan ma? Wo xa danxaniya xurun!»

sentences.english: Then do not be full of care, saying, What are we to have for food or drink? or, With what may we be clothed?
sentences.susu: «Na kui, wo naxa kɔntɔfili a falafe ra, ‹Muxu munse donma? Muxu munse minma? Muxu munse ragoroma muxu ma?›

sentences.english: Because the Gentiles go in search of all these things: for your Father in heaven has knowledge that you have need of all these things:
sentences.susu: Kaafirie birama na fe mɔɔli nan tun fɔxɔ ra. Anun, wo Baba naxan na ariyanna, a a kolon wo hayi na na se birin ma.

sentences.english: But let your first care be for his kingdom and his righteousness; and all these other things will be given to you in addition.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa Ala xa mangɛya niini nun a xa tinxinyi nan singe fen, a na se dɔnxɔɛ birin fan fima nɛ wo ma.

sentences.english: Then have no care for tomorrow: tomorrow will take care of itself. Take the trouble of the day as it comes.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa kɔntɔfili tina xa fe ra, barima tina a ɲɔxɔ sama a yɛtɛ xɔn. Lɔxɔɛ birin nun a xa tɔɔrɛ nan a ra.»

sentences.english: Be not judges of others, and you will not be judged.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa wo yɛtɛ findi wo boore adama kɛwalie makiitima ra, alako kiiti naxa kana wo fan na Ala yi.

sentences.english: For as you have been judging, so you will be judged, and with your measure will it be measured to you.
sentences.susu: Wo mixi makiitima ki naxɛ, wo fan makiitima na ki nɛ. Wo maniyase naxan nawalima booree bɛ, na nan nawalima wo fan bɛ.

sentences.english: And why do you take note of the grain of dust in your brother's eye, but take no note of the bit of wood which is in your eye?
sentences.susu: Munfe ra i wuri fuɲi toma i ngaxakerenyi ya ma, a fa li i mu xebenyi toxi naxan na i tan yɛtɛ ya ma?

sentences.english: Or how will you say to your brother, Let me take out the grain of dust from your eye, when you yourself have a bit of wood in your eye?
sentences.susu: I nɔma a falade i ngaxakerenyi bɛ di, ‹A lu n xa wuri fuɲi ba i ya ma,› xa a sa li xebenyi nan na i tan yɛtɛ ya ma?

sentences.english: You false one, first take out the bit of wood from your eye, then will you see clearly to take out the grain of dust from your brother's eye.
sentences.susu: I tan filankafui, xebenyi nan singe ba i yɛtɛ ya ma. Na ba xanbi, i nɔma nɛ se igbɛde a fanyi ra, alako i xa wuri fuɲi ba i ngaxakerenyi fan ya ma.»

sentences.english: Do not give that which is holy to the dogs, or put your jewels before pigs, for fear that they will be crushed under foot by the pigs whose attack will then be made against you.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa se sɛniyɛnxi so baree yi ra, xa na mu a ra e e ya rafindima nɛ wo ma, e wo maxin. Wo naxa gɛmɛ tofanyie woli xɔsɛe bun ma, xa na mu a ra e e maboronma nan tui.»

sentences.english: Make a request, and it will be answered; what you are searching for you will get; give the sign, and the door will be open to you:
sentences.susu: «Wo maxandi ti, wo a sɔtɔma nɛ. Wo fenyi ti, wo a toma nɛ. Wo naadɛ kɔnkɔn, a rabima nɛ wo bɛ.

sentences.english: Because to everyone who makes a request, it will be given; and he who is searching will get his desire, and to him who gives the sign, the door will be open.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan birin maxandi tima, a a sɔtɔma nɛ. Mixi naxan fenyi tima, a a toma nɛ. Mixi naxan naadɛ kɔnkɔnma, a rabima nɛ a bɛ.»

sentences.english: Or which of you, if his son makes a request for bread, will give him a stone?
sentences.susu: «Babɛ mundun na wo ya ma naxan xa di taami maxɔrinma a ma, a sa gɛmɛ so a yi ra?

sentences.english: Or if he makes a request for a fish, will give him a snake?
sentences.susu: Xa na mu a ra, a bɔximase so a yi, a xa di na a maxɔrin yɛxɛ ma?

sentences.english: If you, then, being evil, are able to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who make requests to him?
sentences.susu: Xa wo tan mixi kobie fata se fanyie fide wo xa die ma, wo Baba Ala naxan na ariyanna, a dangi wo ra pon! A fe fanyie fima nɛ a maxandimae ma.»

sentences.english: All those things, then, which you would have men do to you, even so do you to them: because this is the law and the prophets.
sentences.susu: «Wo wama mixie xa naxan birin naba wo bɛ, wo fan xa na nan naba e bɛ. Tawureta Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa Kitaabuie birin nalanxi nan na ki.»

sentences.english: Go in by the narrow door; for wide is the door and open is the way which goes to destruction, and great numbers go in by it.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa so naadɛ ixutuxi nan na, barima naadɛ igbe mixi rasigama gbaloe nan ma. Kira naxan mixi xaninma gbaloe ma, a ɲɛrɛ mu xɔnɔ. Mixi gbegbe soma naadɛ igbe nan na, mixi gbegbe gbaloe kira nan suxuma.

sentences.english: For narrow is the door and hard the road to life, and only a small number make discovery of it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naadɛ ixutuxi rabima kisi nan ma. Kira naxan mixi xaninma kisi ma, a ɲɛrɛ xɔnɔ. Mixi mu gbo naxee na naadɛ nun na kira toma.»

sentences.english: Be on the watch for false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inside they are cruel wolves.
sentences.susu: «Wo wo yɛtɛ ratanga wule falɛe ma naxee e yɛtɛ findixi namiɲɔnmɛe ra. E fama wɔyɛnyi ɲɔxunmɛ ra wo ma, kɔnɔ e ɲanige mu fan feo!

sentences.english: By their fruits you will get knowledge of them. Do men get grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?
sentences.susu: Wo e kolonma e xa kɛwali nan ma. Kusu bama baagi bili kɔn na? Xɔrɛ bama tunbe bili ma?

sentences.english: Even so, every good tree gives good fruit; but the bad tree gives evil fruit.
sentences.susu: Sansi fanyi bogi fanyi nan naminima, sansi kobi fan bogi kobi nan naminima.

sentences.english: It is not possible for a good tree to give bad fruit, and a bad tree will not give good fruit.
sentences.susu: Sansi fanyi mu nɔma bogi kobi raminide, sansi kobi fan mu nɔma bogi fanyi raminide.

sentences.english: Every tree which does not give good fruit is cut down and put in the fire.
sentences.susu: Sansi naxan mu bogi fanyi raminima, a sɛgɛma nɛ, a woli tɛ i.

sentences.english: So by their fruits you will get knowledge of them.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo na mixie kolonma e xa kɛwali nan ma.»

sentences.english: Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will go into the kingdom of heaven; but he who does the pleasure of my Father in heaven.
sentences.susu: «Mixi naxee a falama n bɛ, ‹N Marigi, n Marigi,› e birin xa mu soma Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma, fo naxee n Baba sago rabama naxan na ariyanna.

sentences.english: A great number will say to me on that day, Lord, Lord, were we not prophets in your name, and did we not by your name send out evil spirits, and by your name do works of power?
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ mixi gbegbe a falama nɛ n bɛ, ‹Muxu Marigi, muxu Marigi, muxu mu wɔyɛn xɛ i xili ra? Muxu mu ɲinnɛe keri xɛ i xili ra? Muxu mu kaabanako gbegbe raba xɛ i xili ra?›

sentences.english: And then will I say to them, I never had knowledge of you: go from me, you workers of evil.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui n nee yaabima nɛ, ‹N mu wo kolon feo! Wo tan fe kobi rabae, wo keli n ya i.›»

sentences.english: Everyone, then, to whom my words come and who does them, will be like a wise man who made his house on a rock;
sentences.susu: «Na kui, mixi naxan na n ma masenyi ramɛ, a fa a rabatu, na kanyi maniya xaxilima ra naxan a xa banxi bili ti fanye ma.

sentences.english: And the rain came down and there was a rush of waters and the winds were driving against that house, but it was not moved; because it was based on the rock.
sentences.susu: Tunɛ naxa fa, xuree naxa banbaran yɛ, foye naxa mini a nu banxi mabɔnbɔ, kɔnɔ banxi mu bira, barima a nu tixi fanye nan fari.

sentences.english: And everyone to whom my words come and who does them not, will be like a foolish man who made his house on sand;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan n ma masenyi ramɛ, a mu a rabatu, na kanyi maniya mixi xaxilitare ra naxan a xa banxi tixi mɛyɛnyi fari.

sentences.english: And the rain came down and there was a rush of waters and the winds were driving against that house; and it came down and great was its fall.
sentences.susu: Tunɛ naxa fa, xuree naxa banbaran yɛ, foye naxa mini a nu banxi mabɔnbɔ, banxi fan naxa bira, a kana a ɲaaxi ra.»

sentences.english: And it came about, when Jesus had come to the end of these words, that the people were surprised at his teaching,
sentences.susu: Isa to gɛ yi fe birin masende, ɲama naxa kaaba a xa xaranyi ma,

sentences.english: for he was teaching as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
sentences.susu: barima a mu nu luxi alɔ e xa sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe. A tan nu wɔyɛnma mangɛ sɛnbɛ nan na.

sentences.english: And when he had come down from the mountain, great numbers of people came after him.
sentences.susu: Isa to goro geya fari, ɲama gbegbe naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And a leper came and gave him worship, saying, Lord, if it is your pleasure, you have power to make me clean.
sentences.susu: Kunɛ kanyi nde naxa a maso Isa ra, a suyidi a bɛ, a a fala a bɛ, «N Marigi, xa i tin, i nɔma n nasɛniyɛnde.»

sentences.english: And he put his hand on him, saying, It is my pleasure; be clean. And straight away he was made clean.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a bɛlɛxɛ itala, a a sa kunɛ kanyi ma, a a fala a bɛ, «N tinxi. Findi mixi sɛniyɛnxi ra.» Kunɛ fure naxa ba a ma keren na.

sentences.english: And Jesus said to him, See that you say nothing about this to anyone; but go and let the priest see you and make the offering which was ordered by Moses, for a witness to them.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a masen a bɛ, «I naxa yi fe fala mixi yo bɛ. Siga i sa i yɛtɛ dɛntɛgɛ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ bɛ, i sɛrɛxɛ ba alɔ Annabi Munsa a yamarixi ki naxɛ. Na findima seedeɲɔxɔya nan na e bɛ.»

sentences.english: And when Jesus was come into Capernaum, a certain captain came to him with a request,
sentences.susu: Isa to so Kapɛrɛnamu, sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati naxa fa a yire, a a maxandi,

sentences.english: Saying, Lord, my servant is ill in bed at the house, with no power in his body, and in great pain.
sentences.susu: «Marigi, n ma walikɛ saxi banxi, a bara namata, a ɲaxankataxi ki fanyi ra.»

sentences.english: And he said to him, I will come and make him well.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala a bɛ, «N xa siga, n xa sa a rayalan.»

sentences.english: And the captain in answer said, Lord, I am not good enough for you to come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant will be made well.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati naxa a yaabi, «Marigi, na binyɛ mu na n yi ra i tan xa so n ma banxi kui. I xa yaamari gbansan nan fi, n ma konyi yalanma nɛ.

sentences.english: Because I myself am a man under authority, having under me fighting men; and I say to this one, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
sentences.susu: N a kolon barima n fan na mangɛ ndee nan xa yaamari bun ma, sɔɔri ndee man na n fan yi, naxee na n ma yaamari bun ma. N na a fala sɔɔri nde bɛ, ‹Siga,› a sigama nɛ. N na a fala, ‹Fa,› a fama nɛ. N na n ma konyi nde yamari, ‹Yi fe raba,› a a rabama nɛ.»

sentences.english: And when these words came to the ears of Jesus he was surprised, and said to those who came after him, Truly I say to you, I have not seen such great faith, no, not in Israel.
sentences.susu: Isa to na sɔɔri xa masenyi mɛ, a naxa kaaba, a fa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, n mu yi danxaniya mɔɔli toxi Isirayila bɔxi dɛdɛ.

sentences.english: And I say to you that numbers will come from the east and the west, and will take their seats with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, mixi gbegbe fama nɛ keli sogetede nun sogegorode biri, e e dɛge e nun Iburahima, Isiyaga, nun Yaxuba Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: But the sons of the kingdom will be put out into the dark, and there will be weeping and cries of pain.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mangɛ xa die tan wolima nɛ tande dimi kui, wa nun ɲinyi raxinyi na dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to the captain, Go in peace; as your faith is, so let it be done to you. And the servant was made well in that hour.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Isa naxa a fala sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati bɛ, «Siga, a xa raba i bɛ alɔ i laxi a ra ki naxɛ.» Na waxati kerenyi yati, sɔɔri xa konyi naxa yalan.

sentences.english: And when Jesus had come into Peter's house, he saw his wife's mother in bed, very ill.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, Isa naxa siga Piyɛri xɔnyi. A naxa Piyɛri bitanyi ginɛma to, a saxi, a fate wolenxi ki fanyi.

sentences.english: And he put his hand on hers and the disease went from her, and she got up and took care of his needs.
sentences.susu: Isa to a bɛlɛxɛ suxu, fure naxa a bɛɲin keren na. A naxa keli, a fa kuri so e bɛ.

sentences.english: And in the evening, they took to him a number of people who had evil spirits; and he sent the spirits out of them with a word, and made well all who were ill;
sentences.susu: Nunmare tɛmui, e naxa fa mixi gbegbe ra Isa xɔn ma ɲinnɛ nu naxee fɔxɔ ra. A naxa ɲinnɛe keri a xa wɔyɛnyi ra, a furemae birin nayalan.

sentences.english: So that the word of Isaiah the prophet might come true: He himself took our pains and our diseases.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Annabi Esayi xa masenyi naxa kamali, naxan sɛbɛxi, «A naxa won ma tɔɔrɛ ba won ma, a won ma furee dɔxɔ a xun.»

sentences.english: Now when Jesus saw a great mass of people about him, he gave an order to go to the other side.
sentences.susu: Isa to ɲama gbegbe to a rabilinyi, a naxa a fɔxirabirɛe yamari e xa baa igiri.

sentences.english: And there came a scribe and said to him, Master, I will come after you wherever you go.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔ nde naxa a maso Isa ra, a a fala a bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, i siga dɛdɛ, n na i fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of heaven have a resting-place; but the Son of man has nowhere to put his head.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Xulumase xima a yili kui. Xɔni xima a tɛɛ kui. Kɔnɔ dɛdɛ mu na Adama xa Di bɛ a a xunyi sama dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: And another of the disciples said to him, Lord, let me first go and give the last honours to my father.
sentences.susu: A fɔxirabirɛ nde fan naxa a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, a lu n xa siga n baba ragatade sinden.»

sentences.english: But Jesus said to him, Come after me; and let the dead take care of their dead.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a yaabi, «Bira n fɔxɔ ra. A lu faxamixie xa e xa faxamixie ragata.»

sentences.english: And when he had got into a boat, his disciples went after him.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa baki kunkui kui, a fɔxirabirɛe naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And there came up a great storm in the sea, so that the boat was covered with the waves: but he was sleeping.
sentences.susu: Foye belebele naxa keli baa ma, mɔrɔnyi nu fa sa kunkui kui. Kɔnɔ Isa tan nu na xife.

sentences.english: And they came to him, and, awaking him, said, Help, Lord; destruction is near.
sentences.susu: A fɔxirabirɛe naxa fa a raxunu, e a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, won nakisi, won faxafe nɛ yi ki!»

sentences.english: And he said to them, Why are you full of fear, O you of little faith? Then he got up and gave orders to the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
sentences.susu: A naxa e yaabi, «Wo gaaxuxi munfe ra? Wo xa danxaniya xurun!» A naxa keli, a foye nun baa yamari, baa naxa xinbeli yen!

sentences.english: And the men were full of wonder, saying, What sort of man is this, that even the winds and the sea do his orders?
sentences.susu: A fɔxirabirɛe naxa kaaba, e e bore maxɔrin, «Mixi mɔɔli mundun lanxi yi ma? Hali foye nun baa, e a xui rabatuma.»

sentences.english: And when he had come to the other side, to the country of the Gadarenes, there came out to him from the place of the dead, two who had evil spirits, so violent that no man was able to go that way.
sentences.susu: E to naakiri li Gadara bɔxi ma, mixi firin naxa mini gaburi longori ra ɲinnɛe nu naxee fɔxɔ ra, e sa Isa ralan. E nu magaaxu ki fanyi, mixi yo ɲan mu nu nɔma dangide na biri.

sentences.english: And they gave a loud cry, saying, What have we to do with you, you Son of God? Have you come here to give us punishment before the time?
sentences.susu: E naxa sɔnxɔ, «Ala xa Di, i waxi munse xɔn ma muxu bɛ? I faxi be muxu ɲaxankatade nɛ beenun a lɔxɔɛ xa a li?»

sentences.english: Now there was, some distance away, a great herd of pigs taking their food.
sentences.susu: Xɔsɛ gali nu na e dɛmadonfe na longori.

sentences.english: And the evil spirits made strong prayers to him, saying, If you send us out, let us go into the herd of pigs.
sentences.susu: Ɲinnɛe naxa Isa mayandi, «Xa i sa muxu keri, muxu raso yi xɔsɛ gali.»

sentences.english: And he said to them, Go. And they came out, and went into the pigs; and the herd went rushing down a sharp slope into the sea and came to their end in the water.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo siga.» E naxa mini na xɛmɛ firinyie, e so na xɔsɛe i. Xɔsɛ gali birin naxa goro e gi ra tentenyi ra, e sa sin baa ma, e madula.

sentences.english: And their keepers went in flight to the town and gave an account of everything, and of the men who had the evil spirits.
sentences.susu: Naxee nu na xɔsɛe dɛmadonfe, e naxa e gi. E to so taa kui, e naxa dɛntɛgɛ sa fe ma naxan dangixi, e a fala taakae bɛ ɲinnɛe gbilenxi na xɛmɛ firin fɔxɔ ra ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And all the town came out to Jesus; and seeing him they made request that he would go away from their part of the country.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui taa birin naxa mini Isa ralande. E to a to, e naxa a mayandi a xa keli e xa bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: And he got into a boat and went across and came to his town.
sentences.susu: Isa to baki kunkui kui, a naxa baa igiri, a so a xɔnyi taa kui.

sentences.english: And they took to him a man stretched on a bed who had no power of moving; and Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the man who was ill, Son, take heart; you have forgiveness for your sins.
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee naxa fa namatɛ nde ra Isa xɔn ma, a saxi dagi ma. Isa to e xa danxaniya to, a naxa a fala namatɛ bɛ, «N ma di, limaniya tongo, i xa yunubie bara xafari.»

sentences.english: And some of the scribes said among themselves, This man has no respect for God.
sentences.susu: Na kui, sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔ ndee naxa a fala e bɔɲɛ ma, «Yi xɛmɛ na Ala rasɔtɔfe nɛ yi ki.»

sentences.english: And Jesus, having knowledge of what was in their minds, said, Why are your thoughts evil?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa to nu e xa maɲɔxunyi kolon, a naxa a masen e bɛ, «Munfe ra maɲɔxunyi kobie na wo bɔɲɛ ma?

sentences.english: For which is the simpler, to say, You have forgiveness for your sins; or to say, Get up and go?
sentences.susu: Wɔyɛnyi mundun sɔɔnɛya, a falafe ‹I xa yunubie bara xafari,› ka a falafe ‹Keli, i xa i ɲɛrɛ›?

sentences.english: But so that you may see that on earth the Son of man has authority for the forgiveness of sins, (then said he to the man who was ill,) Get up, and take up your bed, and go to your house.
sentences.susu: N xa a masen wo bɛ a Adama xa Di nɔma yunubi xafaride duniɲa ma.» Isa naxa a masen namatɛ bɛ, «Keli, i xa i xa dagi tongo, i xa siga i xɔnyi.»

sentences.english: And he got up and went away to his house.
sentences.susu: Namatɛ naxa keli, a siga a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: But when the people saw it they were full of fear, and gave glory to God who had given such authority to men.
sentences.susu: Ɲama to na to, e naxa gaaxu, e nu fa Ala matɔxɔ, naxan na sɛnbɛ mɔɔli fixi adamadie ma.

sentences.english: And when Jesus was going from there, he saw a man whose name was Matthew, seated at the place where taxes were taken; and he said to him, Come after me. And he got up and went after him.
sentences.susu: Isa to keli na, a naxa xɛmɛ nde to naxan xili Matiyu, a dɔxɔxi duuti maxilide. Isa naxa a fala a bɛ, «Bira n fɔxɔ ra.» Matiyu naxa keli, a bira a fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And it came about, when he was in the house taking food, that a number of tax-farmers and sinners came and took their places with Jesus and his disciples.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe nu na e dɛgefe Matiyu xɔnyi. Duuti maxilie nun yunubitɔɛ gbegbe naxa fa, e birin naxa e dɛge fɔlɔ yire keren.

sentences.english: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, Why does your Master take food with tax-farmers and sinners?
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie to na to, e naxa Isa fɔxirabirɛe maxɔrin, «Munfe ra wo karamɔxɔ nun duuti maxilie nun yunubitɔɛe e dɛgema yire keren?»

sentences.english: But on hearing this he said, Those who are well have no need of a medical man, but those who are ill.
sentences.susu: Isa to na mɛ, a naxa a fala, «Mixi yalanxi hayi mu na seriba ma. Furema nan hayi na seriba ma.

sentences.english: But go and take to heart the sense of these words, My desire is for mercy, not offerings: for I have come not to get the upright, but sinners.
sentences.susu: Wo siga, wo sa fahaamui sɔtɔ yi masenyi ma, ‹Hinnɛ rafan n ma dangife sɛrɛxɛ ra.› N mu faxi tinxintɔɛe xa xilide. N faxi yunubitɔɛe nan xilide.»

sentences.english: Then the disciples of John came to him, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees frequently go without food, but your disciples do not?
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Annabi Yaya fɔxirabirɛe naxa fa Isa yire, e a maxɔrin, «Munfe ra muxu tan nun Farisɛnie sunyi suxuma, kɔnɔ i fɔxirabirɛe tan mu sunma?»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to them, Will the friends of the newly-married man be sad as long as he is with them? But the days will come when he will be taken away from them, and then will they go without food.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Ginɛfenyi xa futixiri xulunyi, a booree nɔma sunnunde a na e fɛ ma tɛmui naxɛ? Lɔxɔɛ fama, ginɛfenyi bama nɛ e yi ra. Na waxati tan, e sunyi suxuma nɛ.

sentences.english: And no man puts a bit of new cloth on an old coat, for by pulling away from the old, it makes a worse hole.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu dugi fori lonpoma dugi nɛɛnɛ ra, xa na mu a ra na dugi nɛɛnɛ xuntunyi nan dugi fori ibɛndunma, dugi ibɔɔ dangi a singe ra.

sentences.english: And men do not put new wine into old wine-skins; or the skins will be burst and the wine will come out, and the skins are of no more use: but they put new wine into new wine-skins, and so the two will be safe.
sentences.susu: Mixi man mu wɛni nɛɛnɛ sama lɛbɛ fori kui, xa na mu a ra na wɛni nɛɛnɛ na funtu, wɛni lɛbɛ fori bulama nɛ, wɛni fili, a sase fan kana. Wɛni nɛɛnɛ sama lɛbɛ nɛɛnɛ nan kui, alako wɛni yo, wɛni sase yo, e birin xa ragata a fanyi ra.»

sentences.english: While he was saying these things to them, there came a ruler and gave him worship, saying, My daughter is even now dead; but come and put your hand on her, and she will come back to life.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu na na fee masenfe e bɛ, mangɛ nde naxa fa, a suyidi Isa bɛ, a a fala a bɛ, «N ma di ginɛ baxi faxade ya, kɔnɔ xa i siga, i naxa i bɛlɛxɛ sa a ma, a man kelima nɛ.»

sentences.english: And Jesus got up and went after him, and so did his disciples.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa keli, e nun a fɔxirabirɛe naxa bira na mangɛ fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And a woman, who for twelve years had had a flow of blood, came after him, and put her hand on the edge of his robe:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, ginɛ nde naxan xa kike wali mu nu a itima ɲɛ fu nun firin bun ma, a naxa fa Isa xanbi ra, a a bɛlɛxɛ din a xa donma sanbunyi ra,

sentences.english: Because, she said to herself, if I may but put my hand on his robe, I will be made well.
sentences.susu: barima a nu a falafe a yɛtɛ ma, «Xa n nɔ n bɛlɛxɛ dinde Isa xa donma gbansan na, n yalanma nɛ.»

sentences.english: But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, Daughter, take heart; your faith has made you well. And the woman was made well from that hour.
sentences.susu: Isa to a mafindi, a ginɛ to, a naxa a fala a bɛ, «N ma di, limaniya, i xa danxaniya bara i rayalan.» Keren na, ginɛ naxa yalan.

sentences.english: And when Jesus came into the ruler's house and saw the players with their instruments and the people making a noise,
sentences.susu: Isa to so mangɛ xɔnyi, a naxa ɲama li naa, e sɔnxɔfe, xule femae fan bara fa ɲɔn yire. A naxa a fala e bɛ,

sentences.english: He said, Make room; for the girl is not dead, but sleeping. And they were laughing at him.
sentences.susu: «Wo siga, barima yi ginɛdimɛdi mu faxaxi. A na xife nɛ.» E naxa yo a ma, e a mayele.

sentences.english: But when the people were sent out, he went in and took her by the hand; and the girl got up.
sentences.susu: A to ɲama ramini tande, a naxa so banxi kui. A naxa ginɛdimɛdi bɛlɛxɛ suxu, ginɛdimɛdi naxa keli.

sentences.english: And the news of it went out into all that land.
sentences.susu: Na xibaaru naxa yensen na yire birin na.

sentences.english: And when Jesus went on from there, two blind men came after him, crying out, Have mercy on us, you Son of David.
sentences.susu: Isa to keli mɛnni, dɔnxui firin naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra, e nu e xui ite a bɛ, «Dawuda xa Di, kinikini muxu ma!»

sentences.english: And when he had come into the house, the blind men came to him; and Jesus said to them, Have you faith that I am able to do this? They said to him, Yes, Lord.
sentences.susu: Isa to so banxi, dɔnxuie naxa e maso a ra. A naxa e maxɔrin, «Wo laxi a ra a n nɔma wo rayalande?» E naxa a yaabi, «Iyo, Marigi.»

sentences.english: Then he put his hand on their eyes, saying, As your faith is, let it be done to you.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a bɛlɛxɛe sa e ya ma, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo waxɔnfe xa raba wo bɛ alɔ wo laxi a ra ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And their eyes were made open. And Jesus said to them sharply, Let no man have knowledge of it.
sentences.susu: E yae naxa rabi keren na. Isa naxa a matintin e ra a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra, «Mixi yo naxa yi fe kolon.»

sentences.english: But they went out and gave news of him in all that land.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e to mini, e naxa siga Isa xa fe fala ra na bɔxi yire birin.

sentences.english: And while they were going away, there came to him a man without the power of talking, and with an evil spirit.
sentences.susu: Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe to nu kelife naa, mixi nde naxa fa xɛmɛ nde ra a xɔn ma ɲinnɛ nu bara naxan findi boboe ra.

sentences.english: And when the evil spirit had been sent out, the man had the power of talking: and they were all surprised, saying, Such a thing has never been seen in Israel.
sentences.susu: Isa to na ɲinnɛ keri, boboe naxa wɔyɛn. Ɲama naxa kaaba, e a fala, «Yi fe mɔɔli singe mu nu to Isirayila bɔxi ma.»

sentences.english: But the Pharisees said, By the ruler of evil spirits, he sends evil spirits out of men.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Farisɛnie tan naxa a fala, «A ɲinnɛe kerima ɲinnɛ mangɛ nan saabui ra.»

sentences.english: And Jesus went about all the towns and small places, teaching in their Synagogues and preaching the good news of the kingdom and making well all sorts of disease and pain.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa taae birin iɲɛrɛ, a xungbe nun a xuri. A nu mixie xaranma e xa salidee kui, a nu e kawandi Ala xa mangɛya xa xibaaru fanyi ra, a nu furema mɔɔli birin nayalan.

sentences.english: But when he saw all the people he was moved with pity for them, because they were troubled and wandering like sheep without a keeper.
sentences.susu: A nu ɲama toma tɛmui naxɛ, a nu kinikinima e ma, barima sɛnbɛ nun limaniya birin nu baxi e yi. E nu luxi nɛ alɔ yɛxɛɛ naxee makantama mu na.

sentences.english: Then he said to his disciples, There is much grain but not enough men to get it in.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Xɛ xaba wali belebele nan na, kɔnɔ walikɛe tan xurun.

sentences.english: Make prayer, then, to the Lord of the grain-fields, that he may send out workers to get in his grain.
sentences.susu: Wo xɛ kanyi maxandi alako a xa walikɛe rasanba a xa xɛ xabade.»

sentences.english: And he got together his twelve disciples and gave them the power of driving out unclean spirits, and of making well all sorts of disease and pain.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fɔxirabirɛ fu nun firinyie xili, a nɔɛ so e yi ra alako e xa nɔ ɲinnɛe keride mixie fɔxɔ ra, e man xa nɔ furema mɔɔli birin nayalande.

sentences.english: Now the names of the twelve are these: The first, Simon, who is named Peter, and Andrew, his brother; James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother;
sentences.susu: Na xɛɛra fu nun firinyi xilie nan ya: a singe, Simɔn, naxan man xili Piyɛri, nun a xunya Andire, Sebede xa di Yaki, nun a xunya Yaya,

sentences.english: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew, the tax-farmer; James, the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
sentences.susu: Filipu nun Barotolome, Tomasi nun Matiyu duuti maxili, Alifa xa di Yaki nun Tadayo,

sentences.english: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who was false to him.
sentences.susu: Simɔn naxan xili Seloti, nun Yudasi Isikariyoti naxan Isa yanfa.

sentences.english: These twelve Jesus sent out and gave them orders, saying, Do not go among the Gentiles, or into any town of Samaria,
sentences.susu: Isa naxa yi xɛmɛ fu nun firinyie xɛɛ yi yaamari ra: «Wo naxa siga mixie yire Yuwifie mu naxee ra, wo naxa so Samarikae xa taae kui.

sentences.english: But go to the wandering sheep of the house of Israel,
sentences.susu: Wo xa siga Isirayilakae nan xɔn, naxee luxi alɔ yɛxɛɛ lɔɛxie.

sentences.english: And, on your way, say, The kingdom of heaven is near.
sentences.susu: Wo xa kawandi ti kira xɔn a Ala xa mangɛya niini bara makɔrɛ.

sentences.english: Make well those who are ill, give life to the dead, make lepers clean, send evil spirits out of men; freely it has been given to you, freely give.
sentences.susu: Wo xa furemae rayalan, wo xa faxamixie rakeli, wo xa kunɛ kanyie rasɛniyɛn, wo xa ɲinnɛe keri. Wo kixi nɛ, wo mu sese fi. Wo fan xa mixi ki na ki.

sentences.english: Take no gold or silver or copper in your pockets;
sentences.susu: Wo naxa xɛɛma, gbeti, xa na mu a ra kɔbiri xanin wo xun ma.

sentences.english: Take no bag for your journey and do not take two coats or shoes or a stick: for the workman has a right to his food.
sentences.susu: Wo man naxa gbɔnfɔɛ, donma firin nde, sankiri, xa na mu a ra xuli xanin wo xun ma. A lanma baloe xa fi walikɛ ma.»

sentences.english: And into whatever town or small place you go, make search there for someone who is respected, and make his house your resting-place till you go away.
sentences.susu: «Wo na so taa naxan kui, wo xa mixi fanyi nde fen naxan wo yigiyama, wo lu naa han wo siga taa gbɛtɛ.

sentences.english: And when you go in, say, May peace be on this house.
sentences.susu: Wo na so mixie xɔnyi, wo xa e xɛɛbu.

sentences.english: And if the house is good enough, let your peace come on it: but if not, let your peace come back to you.
sentences.susu: Xa na fɔxɔɛ mixie fan, Ala xa wo xa duba suxu e xa fe ra. Kɔnɔ xa naakae mu fan, Ala naxa na duba suxu.

sentences.english: And whoever will not take you in, or give ear to your words, when you go out from that house or that town, put off its dust from your feet.
sentences.susu: Xa mixie mu tin wo rasɛnɛde, xa na mu a ra e tondi e tuli matide wo xa masenyi ra, wo nɛ kelima na banxi xa na mu a ra na taa kui, wo xa mɛnni bɛndɛ rakɔnkɔn wo sanyie ra.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, It will be better for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of God's judging than for that town.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, kiiti sa lɔxɔɛ, kiiti fanma Sodoma nun Gomora taakae ra dangife na taa mixie ra.»

sentences.english: See, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Be then as wise as snakes, and as gentle as doves.
sentences.susu: «Wo wo tuli mati, n na wo xɛɛfe nɛ alɔ yɛxɛɛ naxee soma wula baree tagi. Na kui, wo xa kɔɔta alɔ yere, wo yuge xa fan alɔ turunna xɔni.

sentences.english: But be on the watch against men: for they will give you up to the Sanhedrins, and in their Synagogues they will give you blows;
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo yɛtɛ matanga mixie ma, barima e wo soma nɛ kiitisae yi ra, e wo bɔnbɔma nɛ sɛbɛrɛ ra e xa salidee kui,

sentences.english: And you will come before rulers and kings because of me, for a witness to them and to the Gentiles.
sentences.susu: e wo xaninma nɛ gominae nun mangɛe yire n ma fe ra. Na kui, wo findima nɛ n ma seedee ra e tan bɛ, a nun si gbɛtɛe bɛ.

sentences.english: But when you are given up into their hands, do not be troubled about what to say or how to say it: for in that hour what you are to say will be given to you;
sentences.susu: E na wo so nee yi ra, wo naxa kɔntɔfili wo xa masenyi xa fe ra, wo naxan falama nun wo a falama ki naxɛ, barima na birin fima nɛ wo ma na waxati yati.

sentences.english: Because it is not you who say the words, but the Spirit of your Father in you.
sentences.susu: Wo tan xa mu wɔyɛnma, wo Baba Ala Xaxili nan wɔyɛnma wo saabui ra.»

sentences.english: And brother will give up brother to death, and the father his child: and children will go against their fathers and mothers, and put them to death.
sentences.susu: «Mixi fama a ngaxakerenyi yanfade, a a sa mixie bɛlɛxɛ, e xa a faxa. Babɛ fan na mɔɔli niyama a xa di ra, die fan kelima nɛ e barimae xili ma, e xa e faxa.

sentences.english: And you will be hated by all men because of my name: but he who is strong to the end will have salvation.
sentences.susu: Mixi birin fama wo xɔnde n xili xa fe ra, kɔnɔ naxan na wakili han a raɲɔnyi, na kanyi kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: But when they are cruel to you in one town, go in flight to another: for truly, I say to you, You will not have gone through the towns of Israel before the Son of man comes.
sentences.susu: Xa e wo ɲaxankata yire nde, wo xa wo gi, wo siga taa gbɛtɛ. N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, wo mu gɛma Isirayila taa birin iɲɛrɛde a fa lu Adama xa Di mu fa.»

sentences.english: A disciple is not greater than his master, or a servant than his lord.
sentences.susu: «Taalibi mu dangima a karamɔxɔ ra, konyi fan mu dangima a marigi ra.

sentences.english: It is enough for the disciple that he may be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have given the name Beelzebub to the master of the house, how much more to those of his house!
sentences.susu: A lanma taalibi xa lu alɔ a karamɔxɔ, konyi fan xa lu alɔ a marigi. Xa fɔxɔɛ xunyi xili fala ɲinnɛ Bɛlɛsɛbulu, e naxan falama a xa fɔxɔɛ mixie xun ma, a ɲan dangima na ra.»

sentences.english: Have, then, no fear of them: because nothing is covered which will not come to light, or secret which will not be made clear.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa gaaxu mixie ya ra, barima fefe nɔxunxi mu na naxan mu fama makɛnɛnde, gundo yo mu na naxan mu fama kolonde.

sentences.english: What I say to you in the dark, say in the light: and what comes to your ear secretly, say publicly from the house-tops.
sentences.susu: N naxan falama wo bɛ kɔɛ ra, wo xa na masen yanyi ra. Wo naxan mɛma makɔyikɔyi ra, wo xa duniɲa birin nakolon a ra.

sentences.english: And have no fear of those who put to death the body, but are not able to put to death the soul. But have fear of him who has power to give soul and body to destruction in hell.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa gaaxu mixie ya ra naxee nɔma mixi fate bɛndɛ nan tun faxade, a fa li e mu nɔma wo nii tan masɔtɔde. Wo xa gaaxu Ala nan ya ra, naxan nɔma fate bɛndɛ nun nii sɔntɔde yahannama.

sentences.english: Are not sparrows two a farthing? and not one of them comes to an end without your Father:
sentences.susu: Turunna firin xa mu sarama batanka keren na? Kɔnɔ hali xɔni di keren mu birama bɔxi ma xa wo Baba Ala sago mu a ra.

sentences.english: But the hairs of your head are all numbered.
sentences.susu: Wo xunsɛxɛ yati kɔntixi.

sentences.english: Then have no fear; you are of more value than a flock of sparrows.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo naxa gaaxu, barima wo tide gbo dangi turunna xɔni gali ra.»

sentences.english: To everyone, then, who gives witness to me before men, I will give witness before my Father in heaven.
sentences.susu: «Mixi yo naxan n kolonma a Marigi ra adamadie ya xɔri, n fan na kanyi kolonma n Baba ya xɔri ariyanna.

sentences.english: But if anyone says before men that he has no knowledge of me, I will say that I have no knowledge of him before my Father in heaven.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naxan na tondi n kolonde a Marigi ra adamadie ya ma, n fan tondima nɛ na kanyi rakolonde n Baba ra naxan na ariyanna.»

sentences.english: Do not have the thought that I have come to send peace on the earth; I came not to send peace but a sword.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa a maɲɔxun a n faxi bɔɲɛsa nan na duniɲa. N mu faxi bɔɲɛsa xa ra, n faxi santidɛgɛma nan na.

sentences.english: For I have come to put a man against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law:
sentences.susu: N faxi fatanyi nan na di xɛmɛ nun a baba tagi, di ginɛ nun a nga tagi, mamadi nun a mama tagi.

sentences.english: And a man will be hated by those of his house.
sentences.susu: Mixi ngaxakerenyie nan findima a yaxuie ra.

sentences.english: He who has more love for his father or mother than for me is not good enough for me; he who has more love for son or daughter than for me is not good enough for me.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan a baba nun a nga xanuma dangife n tan na, na kanyi mu daxa a xa lu n sɛɛti ma. Mixi naxan a xa di xanuma dangife n tan na, na kanyi mu daxa a xa lu n sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: And he who does not take his cross and come after me is not good enough for me.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi naxan mu tin tɔɔrɛ nun faxɛ ra, a mu bira n fɔxɔ ra, na kanyi mu daxa a xa lu n sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: He who has the desire to keep his life will have it taken from him, and he who gives up his life because of me will have it given back to him.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan wama a yɛtɛ rakisife, na kanyi lɔɛma nɛ. Naxan a yɛtɛ ralɔɛma n tan ma fe ra, na kanyi kisima nɛ.»

sentences.english: He who gives honour to you gives honour to me; and he who gives honour to me gives honour to him who sent me.
sentences.susu: «Mixi naxan na wo rasɛnɛ, a n tan nan nasɛnɛxi. Mixi naxan na n nasɛnɛ, a n xɛɛma nan nasɛnɛxi.

sentences.english: He who gives honour to a prophet, in the name of a prophet, will be given a prophet's reward; and he who gives honour to an upright man, in the name of an upright man, will be given an upright man's reward.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan na namiɲɔnmɛ rasɛnɛ a xa namiɲɔnmɛɲa ma, a baraayi sɔtɔma nɛ alɔ namiɲɔnmɛ. Mixi naxan na tinxintɔɛ rasɛnɛ a xa tinxinyi ma, a baraayi sɔtɔma nɛ alɔ tinxintɔɛ.

sentences.english: And whoever gives to one of these little ones a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you, he will not go without his reward.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan na hali ye xinbeli pɔɔti ya keren fi yi mixi xuri keren ma a to findixi n fɔxirabirɛ ra, n xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, na kanyi mu ganma a baraayi ra muku.»

sentences.english: And it came about that when Jesus had come to the end of giving these orders to his twelve disciples, he went away from there, teaching and preaching in their towns.
sentences.susu: Isa to gɛ yi yaamarie fide a fɔxirabirɛ fu nun firinyie ma, a naxa keli mɛnni, a siga Yuwifie xa taae alako a xa mixie xaran, a e kawandi.

sentences.english: Now when John had news in prison of the works of the Christ, he sent his disciples
sentences.susu: Annabi Yaya to Isa Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa fe mɛ geeli kui, a naxa a fɔxirabirɛ ndee xɛɛ Isa ma.
