sentences.english: So when the other servants saw what was done they were very sad, and came and gave word to their lord of what had been done.
sentences.susu: «A boore walikɛe to na to, e naxa kinikini. E naxa na birin dɛntɛgɛ sa mangɛ bɛ naxan nu e birin xun ma.

sentences.english: Then his lord sent for him and said, You evil servant; I made you free of all that debt, because of your request to me:
sentences.susu: Na kui, mangɛ naxa na walikɛ singe xili, a a fala a bɛ, ‹I tan walikɛ kobi! I to n mayandi, n tan diɲɛ nɛ i xa doni birin ma.

sentences.english: Was it not right for you to have mercy on the other servant, even as I had mercy on you?
sentences.susu: A di, a mu lanma xɛ nu i fan xa kinikini i boore ma, alɔ n kinikinixi i tan ma ki naxɛ?›

sentences.english: And his lord was very angry, and put him in the hands of those who would give him punishment till he made payment of all the debt.
sentences.susu: A xa mangɛ to xɔnɔ a ma, a naxa a so kɔsibilie yi, e xa a sa geeli, e xa a ɲaxankata han a xa gɛ doni birin fide.»

sentences.english: So will my Father in heaven do to you, if you do not everyone, from your hearts, give forgiveness to his brother.
sentences.susu: «N Baba naxan na ariyanna, a na nan niyama wo fan na, xa wo mu diɲɛ wo ngaxakerenyi ma wo bɔɲɛ birin na.»

sentences.english: And it came about that after saying these words, Jesus went away from Galilee, and came into the parts of Judaea on the other side of Jordan.
sentences.susu: Isa to gɛ yi fe birin masende, a naxa keli Galile bɔxi ma, a siga Yudaya bɔxi nde ma naxan nu na Yurudɛn naakiri ma.

sentences.english: And a great number went after him; and he made them well there.
sentences.susu: Ɲama gbegbe naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra naa, a fan naxa furemae rayalan.

sentences.english: And certain Pharisees came to him, testing him, and saying, Is it right for a man to put away his wife for every cause?
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie naxa fa a yire alako e xa gantanyi te a bɛ. E naxa a maxɔrin, «A daxa xɛmɛ xa mɛɛ a xa ginɛ ra fe birin ma?»

sentences.english: And he said in answer, Have you not seen in the Writings, that he who made them at the first made them male and female, and said,
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Kitaabui naxan masenxi wo mu nu a xaran? Fe fɔlɔ fɔlɛ ra, Daali Mangɛ naxa xɛmɛ nun ginɛ daa,

sentences.english: For this cause will a man go away from his father and mother, and be joined to his wife; and the two will become one flesh?
sentences.susu: a fa a masen, ‹Na kui, xɛmɛ kelima a baba nun a nga xun ma, a a xa ginɛ xa futi xiri, e firin findi keren na.›

sentences.english: So that they are no longer two, but one flesh. Then let not that which has been joined by God be parted by man.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi, mixi firin xa mu e ra sɔnɔn, e firin bara findi keren na. Ala bara naxee xiri e boore ra, adama naxa nee rafatan.»

sentences.english: They say to him, Why then did Moses give orders that a husband might give her a statement in writing and be free from her?
sentences.susu: E man naxa Isa maxɔrin, «Munfe ra fa Annabi Munsa a yamarixi, xɛmɛ naxan wama mɛɛfe a xa ginɛ ra, a lan a xa fatan kɛɛdi so a yi ra, a mɛɛ a ra?»

sentences.english: He says to them, Moses, because of your hard hearts, let you put away your wives: but it has not been so from the first.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Wo bɔɲɛe nan xɔrɔxɔ, na nan a niyaxi Annabi Munsa naxa fɛɛrɛ fi wo ma, wo xa nɔ mɛɛde wo xa ginɛe ra, kɔnɔ a mu nu na na ki xɛ a fɔlɛ ra.

sentences.english: And I say to you, Whoever puts away his wife for any other cause than the loss of her virtue, and takes another, is a false husband: and he who takes her as his wife when she is put away, is no true husband to her.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, naxan yo mɛɛ a xa ginɛ ra, xa a xa ginɛ mu yɛnɛ xa rabaxi, a fa ginɛ gbɛtɛ dɔxɔ, na xɛmɛ bara yɛnɛ raba.»

sentences.english: The disciples say to him, If this is the position of a man in relation to his wife, it is better not to be married.
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛe naxa a fala a bɛ, «Xa a na na ki nɛ xɛmɛ bɛ a xa ginɛ mabiri ra, hali a mu ginɛ dɔxɔ.»

sentences.english: But he said to them, Not all men are able to take in this saying, but only those to whom it is given.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Birin xa mu nɔma yi masenyi suxude, fo Ala a fɛɛrɛ fi naxan ma.

sentences.english: For there are men who, from birth, were without sex: and there are some who were made so by men: and there are others who have made themselves so for the kingdom of heaven. He who is able to take it, let him take it.
sentences.susu: Wo a kolon, xɛmɛ ndee bari ki nan a niyaxi e mu nɔma ginɛ dɔxɔde. Ndee na na e e banaxi nɛ. Ndee fan na, e natɛ nan tongoxi e naxa ginɛ dɔxɔ Ala xa wali xa fe ra. Mixi naxan nɔma yi masenyi suxude, a xa a suxu.»

sentences.english: Then some people took little children to him, so that he might put his hands on them in blessing: and the disciples said sharp words to them.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui mixie naxa fa dimɛdie ra Isa xɔn, alako a xa a bɛlɛxɛ sa e ma, a duba e bɛ. Kɔnɔ a fɔxirabirɛe naxa wɔyɛn na mixie ma.

sentences.english: But Jesus said, Let the little ones come to me, and do not keep them away: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Isa naxa a masen, «Wo a lu dimɛdie xa fa n yire. Wo naxa tɔnyi dɔxɔ e ma, barima naxee maniyaxi e ra, nee nan na Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.»

sentences.english: And he put his hands on them, and went away.
sentences.susu: A naxa a bɛlɛxɛ sa e ma, a duba e bɛ. Na xanbi, a naxa siga.

sentences.english: And one came to him and said, Master, what good thing have I to do, so that I may have eternal life?
sentences.susu: Sɛgɛtala nde naxa fa Isa xɔn, a a maxɔrin, «Karamɔxɔ, a lan n xa fe fanyi mundun naba alako n xa abadan kisi sɔtɔ?»

sentences.english: And he said to him, Why are you questioning me about what is good? One there is who is good: but if you have a desire to go into life, keep the rules of the law.
sentences.susu: Isa fan naxa a maxɔrin, «I n maxɔrinma fe fanyi ma munfe ra? Ala keren peti nan fan. Xa i wama i xa kisi, Ala xa sɛriyɛ nan nabatu.» Xɛmɛ naxa a maxɔrin, «Ala xa sɛriyɛ mundue?»

sentences.english: He says to him, Which? And Jesus said, Do not put anyone to death, Do not be untrue in married life, Do not take what is not yours, Do not give false witness,
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «I naxa faxɛ ti. I naxa yɛnɛ raba. I naxa muɲɛ ti. I naxa mixi tɔɔɲɛgɛ.

sentences.english: Give honour to your father and your mother: and, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
sentences.susu: I baba nun i nga binya. I xa i ngaxakerenyi xanu alɔ i yɛtɛ yati.»

sentences.english: The young man says to him, All these things have I done: what more is there?
sentences.susu: Sɛgɛtala naxa Isa yaabi, «N bara na birin nabatu. Munse fa luxi?»

sentences.english: Jesus said to him, If you have a desire to be complete, go, get money for your property, and give it to the poor, and you will have wealth in heaven: and come after me.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen a bɛ, «Xa i wama i xa gɛ kamalide i xa kɛwalie kui, siga, sa i sɔtɔse birin mati, i a kɔbiri fi setaree ma. Na kui, i fama bannaya sɔtɔde ariyanna. I na na raba, fa, i bira n fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: But hearing these words the young man went away sorrowing: for he had much property.
sentences.susu: Sɛgɛtala to na mɛ, a naxa siga sunnunyi kui, barima harige gbegbe nu na a yi ra.

sentences.english: And Jesus said to his disciples, Truly I say to you, It is hard for a man with much money to go into the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, naafuli kanyi sofe Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma a xɔrɔxɔ.

sentences.english: And again I say to you, It is simpler for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a man with much money to go into the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: N man xa a fala wo bɛ, ɲɔxɔmɛ so ɲɔxun sɛnbɛ yale ra, dinɛ bannamixi sofe Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.»

sentences.english: And the disciples, hearing this, were greatly surprised, saying, Who then may have salvation?
sentences.susu: E to na mɛ, Isa fɔxirabirɛe dɛ naxa ixara ki fanyi ra, e maxɔrinyi ti, «Nde, fa nɔma kiside?»

sentences.english: And Jesus, looking at them, said, With men this is not possible; but with God all things are possible.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e mato, a fa a masen, «Adama mu nɔma a yɛtɛ rakiside, kɔnɔ Ala tan nɔma fe birin na.»

sentences.english: Then Peter said to him, See, we have given up everything and have come after you; what then will we have?
sentences.susu: Na kui, Piyɛri naxa a fala a bɛ, «A mato, muxu bara keli se birin xun ma, muxu bira i fɔxɔ ra. Munse fa luma muxu bɛ?»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you that in the time when all things are made new, and the Son of man is seated in his glory, you who have come after me will be seated on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, duniɲa fe birin na masara a nɛɛnɛ ra, Adama xa Di naxa magoro a xa nɔrɛ kibanyi kui, wo tan n fɔxirabirɛe fan magoroma nɛ kibanyi fu nun firin kui, wo fa Isirayila bɔnsɔɛ fu nun firin makiiti.

sentences.english: And everyone who has given up houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or child, or land, for my name, will be given a hundred times as much, and have eternal life.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo naxan na sa keli a xa se nde xun ma n tan ma fe ra, a findi banxie ra ba, xunyae ba, taarae ba, baba ba, nga ba, bɔxie ba, na kanyi nee ɲɔxɔ kɛmɛ kɛmɛ nan sɔtɔma, a man abadan kisi sɔtɔ kɛ ra.

sentences.english: But a great number who are first will be last, and some who are last will be first.
sentences.susu: Yarerati wuyaxi fama findide xanbiratie ra, xanbirati fan findi yareratie ra.»

sentences.english: For the kingdom of heaven is like the master of a house, who went out early in the morning to get workers into his vine-garden.
sentences.susu: «Ala xa mangɛya misaalixi xɛ kanyi nan na, naxan mini subaxɛ ma alako a xa walikɛe tongo a xa xɛ walife ra.

sentences.english: And when he had made an agreement with the workmen for a penny a day, he sent them into his vine-garden.
sentences.susu: E to lan a ma fɛɛɲɛn keren xa wali sare xa findi gbeti kɔbiri kole keren na, xɛ kanyi naxa walikɛe xɛɛ a xa xɛ yire.

sentences.english: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others in the market-place doing nothing;
sentences.susu: A man to mini gɛɛsɛgɛ, soge to nu bara mate, a naxa walikɛ gbɛtɛe li, e tixi taa kui, wali yo mu e yi.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Go into the vine-garden with the others, and whatever is right I will give you. And they went to work.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala e bɛ, ‹Wo fan xa siga walide n ma xɛ ma. N wali sare tinxinxi fima nɛ wo ma.›

sentences.english: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did the same.
sentences.susu: E fan naxa siga. Xɛ kanyi man naxa mini yanyi tagi, a walikɛ gbɛtɛe man tongo. Nunmare, a man naxa mixi gbɛtɛe sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And about the eleventh hour he went out and saw others doing nothing; and he says to them, Why are you here all the day doing nothing?
sentences.susu: A dɔnxɔɛ ra, lɛɛri ndee beenu kɔɛ xa so, a naxa mini, a walikɛ gbɛtɛe li, e tixi. A naxa e maxɔrin, ‹Fɛɛɲɛn, wo tixi be, wo mu walife. Munfe ra?›

sentences.english: They say to him, Because no man has given us work. He says to them, Go in with the rest, into the vine-garden.
sentences.susu: E naxa a yaabi, ‹Mixi yo nan mu muxu tongoxi walide.› Xɛ kanyi naxa a fala e bɛ, ‹Wo fan xa siga walide n ma xɛ yire.›»

sentences.english: And when evening came, the lord of the vine-garden said to his manager, Let the workers come, and give them their payment, from the last to the first.
sentences.susu: «Nunmare to so, xɛ kanyi naxa a fala a xa walikɛ xunyi bɛ, ‹Walikɛe xili, i xa e sare fi. A fɔlɔ dɔnxɔɛ rasoe ma, a raɲɔn a singe ma.›

sentences.english: And when those men came who had gone to work at the eleventh hour, they were given every man a penny.
sentences.susu: Naxee wali fɔlɔxi lɛɛri ndee beenu kɔɛ xa so, kankan naxa gbeti kɔbiri kole keren sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Then those who came first had the idea that they would get more; and they, like the rest, were given a penny.
sentences.susu: Na kui, walikɛe naxee singe tongo, nee to fa e ɲɔxɔ a ma a e kɔbiri sɔtɔma dangi booree ra, kɔnɔ e fan naxa gbeti kɔbiri kole keren sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And when they got it, they made a protest against the master of the house,
sentences.susu: E to a rasuxu, e naxa wɔyɛn xɛ kanyi ma,

sentences.english: Saying, These last have done only one hour's work, and you have made them equal to us, who have undergone the hard work of the day and the burning heat.
sentences.susu: e a fala, ‹Yi walikɛ dɔnxɔɛe, e waxati keren gbansan nan walixi, kɔnɔ i bara wali sare fi e ma naxan nun muxu gbe lan. Anun, muxu tan nan fɛɛɲɛnxi wali ra soge xɔnɛ bun!›

sentences.english: But he in answer said to one of them, Friend, I do you no wrong: did you not make an agreement with me for a penny?
sentences.susu: A naxa mixi keren yaabi e ya ma, ‹N boore, n mu fefe kobi niyaxi i ra. Won mu lan gbeti kɔbiri kole keren xa ma?

sentences.english: Take what is yours, and go away; it is my pleasure to give to this last, even as to you.
sentences.susu: I gbe tongo, i siga. N tan nan waxi a xɔn yi walikɛ dɔnxɔɛ xa wali sare xa lan i gbe ma.

sentences.english: Have I not the right to do as seems good to me in my house? or is your eye evil, because I am good?
sentences.susu: N mu nɔma n waxɔnfe rabade n ma kɔbiri ra? Ka i tɔɔnɛxi nɛ n to fe fanyi rabaxi mixi gbɛtɛ nde bɛ?›

sentences.english: So the last will be first, and the first last.
sentences.susu: Na kui, xanbiratie fama findide yareratie ra, yareratie fan findi xanbiratie ra.»

sentences.english: And when Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples on one side, and said to them,
sentences.susu: Isa nun a xɛɛra fu nun firinyie to nu tefe Darisalamu, Isa naxa e xun lan, a fa a masen e doro bɛ kira xɔn ma,

sentences.english: See, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man will be given into the hands of the chief priests and scribes; and they will give orders for him to be put to death,
sentences.susu: «Wo a mato, won na tefe Darisalamu nɛ yi ki. Adama xa Di sama nɛ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe bɛlɛxɛ, e a makiiti a xa faxa,

sentences.english: And will give him up to the Gentiles to be made sport of and to be whipped and to be put to death on the cross: and the third day he will come back again from the dead.
sentences.susu: e a so kaafirie yi ra. E a mayelema nɛ, e a bɔnbɔ sɛbɛrɛ ra, e fa a mabanban wuri magalanbuxi ma, kɔnɔ a xa faxɛ xi saxan nde ma, a man kelima nɛ faxɛ ma.»

sentences.english: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, giving him worship and making a request of him.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui Sebede xa die nga naxa fa Isa yire, a nun a xa die. A naxa suyidi a bɛ, a xa a maxandi fe nde ma.

sentences.english: And he said to her, What is your desire? She says to him, Let my two sons be seated, the one at your right hand, and the other at your left, in your kingdom.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa ginɛ maxɔrin, «I wama munse xɔn?» A naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «I xa tin, i na i xa mangɛya sɔtɔ, n ma yi di firinyie xa dɔxɔ i sɛɛti ma, keren i yirefanyi ma, boore i kɔɔla ma.»

sentences.english: But Jesus made answer and said, You have no idea what you are requesting. Are you able to take of the cup which I am about to take?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen di firinyie bɛ, «Wo mu a kolon wo fe naxan maxɔrinfe. N fafe tɔɔrɛ naxan tode, wo tinma na ra?» E naxa a yaabi, «Iyo, muxu tinma a ra.»

sentences.english: They say to him, We are able. He says to them, Truly, you will take of my cup: but to be seated at my right hand and at my left is not for me to give, but it is for those for whom my Father has made it ready.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo fan yati fama ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔde alɔ n tan, kɔnɔ dɔxɔfe n yirefanyi nun n kɔɔla ma, na mu fatanma n tan xa ra. Na na mixie nan bɛ, n Baba naxee sugandixi.»

sentences.english: And when it came to the ears of the ten, they were angry with the two brothers.
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛ fu dɔnxɔɛe to na fe mɛ, e naxa xɔnɔ na ngaxakerenyi firin ma.

sentences.english: But Jesus said to them, You see that the rulers of the Gentiles are lords over them, and their great ones have authority over them.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa e xili a yire, a a masen e bɛ, «Ɲamanɛ mangɛe mixie yamarima a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra, e e sɛnbɛ raminima mixie ma alako e xa mangɛya xa kolon.

sentences.english: Let it not be so among you: but if anyone has a desire to become great among you, let him be your servant;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a naxa lu na ki wo tan tagi. Mixi naxan wama a tide xa gbo wo ya ma, a xa findi wo xa konyi nan na.

sentences.english: And whoever has a desire to be first among you, let him take the lowest place:
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan wama findife wo xa yarerati ra, a xa findi wo xa konyi nan na.

sentences.english: Even as the Son of man did not come to have servants, but to be a servant, and to give his life for the salvation of men.
sentences.susu: Wo xa lu nɛ alɔ Adama xa Di. A tan mu faxi xɛ mixie xa wali a tan bɛ. A faxi nɛ alako a tan nan xa wali mixie bɛ, a xa mixi gbegbe xunsara a xa faxɛ saabui ra.»

sentences.english: And when they were going out from Jericho, a great number went after him.
sentences.susu: Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe to mini Yeriko, ɲama gbegbe naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And two blind men seated by the wayside, when they had the news that Jesus was going by, gave a loud cry, saying, Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.
sentences.susu: Dɔnxui firin nu dɔxɔxi kira dɛ ra. E to a mɛ a Isa na dangife, e naxa e xui ramini, «Marigi, Dawuda xa Di, kinikini muxu ma!»

sentences.english: And the people gave them orders to be quiet; but they went on crying even louder, Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa wɔyɛn e ma, e xa e sabari, kɔnɔ e ɲan naxa e xui ite dangi a singe ra, «Marigi, Dawuda xa Di, kinikini muxu ma!»

sentences.english: And Jesus, stopping, sent for them, and said, What would you have me do to you?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa ti, a e xili, a e maxɔrin, «Wo wama n xa munse raba wo bɛ?»

sentences.english: They say to him, Lord, that our eyes may be open.
sentences.susu: E naxa a yaabi, «Marigi, muxu wama muxu yae xa se to.»

sentences.english: And Jesus, being moved with pity, put his fingers on their eyes: and straight away they were able to see, and went after him.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa kinikini e ma, a a bɛlɛxɛ sa e yae ma. Keren na, e yae naxa se to, e naxa bira Isa fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And when they were near Jerusalem, and had come to Beth-phage, to the Mountain of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
sentences.susu: Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe to makɔrɛ Darisalamu ra, e naxa Betifage li, Oliwi geya mabiri. Isa naxa a fɔxirabirɛ firin xɛɛ,

sentences.english: Saying to them, Go into the little town in front of you, and straight away you will see an ass with a cord round her neck, and a young one with her; let them loose and come with them to me.
sentences.susu: a a fala e bɛ, «Wo xa so taa kui naxan na yare. Wo nɛfɛ so naa, wo sofale ginɛ nde lima a xirixi naa, a xa di na a fɛ ma. Wo xa e fulun, wo fa e ra n xɔn ma.

sentences.english: And if anyone says anything to you, you will say, The Lord has need of them; and straight away he will send them.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde fa wo maxɔrin, wo xa a fala a bɛ, ‹Marigi nan hayi na e ma. A e ragbilenma ya.›»

sentences.english: Now this took place so that these words of the prophet might come true,
sentences.susu: Na rabaxi nɛ, alako namiɲɔnmɛ xa masenyi xa kamali, naxan a falama,

sentences.english: Say to the daughter of Zion, See, your King comes to you, gentle and seated on an ass, and on a young ass.
sentences.susu: «Wo a fala Siyoni di ginɛ bɛ, ‹A mato, i xa mangɛ na fafe i ma. A fama yɛtɛ magore kui, a dɔxɔxi sofale nun a yɔrɛ fari.›»

sentences.english: And the disciples went and did as Jesus had given them orders,
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛe naxa siga, e sa Isa xa xɛɛraya raba.

sentences.english: And got the ass and the young one, and put their clothing on them, and he took his seat on it.
sentences.susu: E to fa sofale nun sofale xa di ra, e naxa e xa donmae sa e fari, Isa fa a magoro sofale fari.

sentences.english: And all the people put their clothing down in the way; and others got branches from the trees, and put them down in the way.
sentences.susu: Ɲama gbegbe naxan nu na, e fan naxa e xa donmae itala kira xɔn ma, ndee fan naxa fɛnsɛ sɛgɛ, e nee fan sa kira xɔn ma Isa binyafe ra.

sentences.english: And those who went before him, and those who came after, gave loud cries, saying, Glory to the Son of David: A blessing on him who comes in the name of the Lord: Glory in the highest.
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxee nu ɲɛrɛfe Isa ya ra, a nun naxee nu ɲɛrɛfe a xanbi ra, e birin nu e xui itefe, e a fala, «Tantui na won Nakisima bɛ, Dawuda xa Di! Baraka na a bɛ naxan fafe Marigi xili ra! Tantui na won Nakisima bɛ naxan na koore ma!»

sentences.english: And when he came into Jerusalem, all the town was moved, saying, Who is this?
sentences.susu: Isa to so Darisalamu, taakae birin naxa kaaba, e nu maxɔrinyi ti, «Nde yi ki?»

sentences.english: And the people said, This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa e yaabi, «Annabi Isa nan yi ki, naxan kelixi Nasarɛti, Galile bɔxi ma.»

sentences.english: And Jesus went into the Temple and sent out all who were trading there, overturning the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those trading in doves.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa so hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, a sarematie nun saresoe birin keri naxee nu na na. A naxa kɔbiri masarɛe xa teebilie a nun ganbɛ matie xa dɔxɔsee rabira,

sentences.english: And he said to them, It is in the Writings, My house is to be named a house of prayer, but you are making it a hole of thieves.
sentences.susu: a a masen e bɛ, «A sɛbɛxi, ‹N ma banxi xili falama nɛ, salide banxi,› kɔnɔ wo tan bara a findi muɲɛtie dɔxɔde ra.»

sentences.english: And the blind and the broken in body came to him in the Temple, and he made them well.
sentences.susu: Dɔnxuie nun namatɛe naxa fa Isa xɔn hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, a naxa nee rayalan.

sentences.english: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the works of power which he did, and the children crying out in the Temple, Glory to the son of David, they were angry and said to him,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe tan naxa xɔnɔ ki fanyi e to Isa xa kaabanakoe to, e man to dimɛe to e xui itema hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, «Tantui na won Nakisima bɛ, Dawuda xa Di!»

sentences.english: Have you any idea what these are saying? And Jesus said to them, Yes: have you not seen in the Writings, From the lips of children and babies at the breast you have made your praise complete?
sentences.susu: E naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «I mu e xui mɛxi?» Isa naxa e yaabi, «Iyo. Wo fan mu nu a xaran Kitaabui kui a to sɛbɛxi, ‹I bara a niya dimɛdie nun diyɔrɛe xa i matɔxɔ?›»

sentences.english: And he went away from them, and went out of the town to Bethany, and was there for the night.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, Isa naxa keli e xun taa kui, a siga Betani, a kɔɛ radangi naa.

sentences.english: Now in the morning when he was coming back to the town, he had a desire for food.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, Isa to nu gbilenfe taa kui, kaamɛ naxa a suxu.

sentences.english: And seeing a fig-tree by the wayside, he came to it, and saw nothing on it but leaves only; and he said to it, Let there be no fruit from you from this time forward for ever. And straight away the fig-tree became dry and dead.
sentences.susu: A to xɔrɛ bili nde to kira ra, a naxa a maso a ra kɔnɔ a mu bogi yo to a kɔn na, fo a burɛxɛe. Isa naxa a fala xɔrɛ bili bɛ, «I tan mu bogima sɔnɔn!» Xɔrɛ bili naxa xara keren na.

sentences.english: And when the disciples saw it they were surprised, saying, How did the fig-tree become dry in so short a time?
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛe to na to, e naxa kaaba, e a maxɔrin, «Yi xɔrɛ bili xaraxi a ikɔrɛxi ra di?»

sentences.english: And Jesus in answer said to them, Truly I say to you, If you have faith, without doubting, not only may you do what has been done to the fig-tree, but even if you say to this mountain, Be taken up and put into the sea, it will be done.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, xa danxaniya na wo bɛ, wo mu siikɛ, wo nɔma nɛ yi fe mɔɔli nabade n naxan nabaxi xɔrɛ bili ra. Kɔnɔ dangi na ra, xa wo a fala yi geya bɛ, ‹Keli be, i sa sin baa ma,› a rabama nɛ.

sentences.english: And all things, whatever you make request for in prayer, having faith, you will get.
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra, xa danxaniya na wo bɛ, wo fefe maxandi Ala ma, wo a sɔtɔma nɛ.»

sentences.english: And when he had come into the Temple, the chief priests and those in authority over the people came to him while he was teaching, and said, By what authority do you do these things? and who gave you this authority?
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa so hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui. A to nu na mixie xaranfe, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie, nun Yuwifie xa forie naxa fa a yire, e a maxɔrin, «I yi fee rabama nde xa yaamari ma? Nde yi sɛnbɛ fixi i ma?»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to them in answer, I will put one question to you, and if you give me the answer, I will say by what authority I do these things.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «N fan xa wo maxɔrin fe keren ma. Xa wo n yaabi, n a falama nɛ wo bɛ n yi fee rabama naxan ma yaamari ma.

sentences.english: The baptism of John, where did it come from? from heaven or from men? And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, If we say, From heaven; he will say to us, Why then did you not have faith in him?
sentences.susu: Yaya nu mixie xunxama ye xɔɔra nde xa yaamari ma? Ala nan a xɛɛxi ba, ka adama?» Na kui, e naxa so wɔyɛnfe e bore tagi, «Xa won na a yaabi, won naxɛ, ‹Ala,› a a falama nɛ won bɛ, ‹Munfe ra wo mu fa la a ra?›

sentences.english: But if we say, From men; we are in fear of the people, because all take John to be a prophet.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa won na a yaabi, won naxɛ, ‹Adama,› won gaaxuma nɛ ɲama ya ra, barima birin Yaya maɲɔxunxi namiɲɔnmɛ nan na.»

sentences.english: And they made answer and said, We have no idea. Then he said to them, And I will not say to you by what authority I do these things.
sentences.susu: Na kui, e naxa Isa yaabi, «Muxu mu a kolon.» A fan naxa a masen e bɛ, «N fan mu a falama wo bɛ n yi fee rabama naxan ma yaamari ma.»

sentences.english: But how does it seem to you? A man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go and do work today in the vine-garden.
sentences.susu: «Wo yi taali toxi di? Di xɛmɛ firin nu na xɛmɛ nde yi. A naxa a fala di singe bɛ, ‹N ma di, siga i sa wali xɛ ma to.›

sentences.english: And he said in answer, I will not: but later, changing his decision, he went.
sentences.susu: Di naxa a yaabi, ‹N tondi.› Kɔnɔ na dangi xanbi, a xaxili naxa masara, a siga walide.

sentences.english: And he came to the second and said the same. And he made answer and said, I go, sir: and went not.
sentences.susu: Babɛ to na yaamari fi a xa di firin nde fan ma, a naxa a yaabi, ‹N Baba, awa, n sigafe.› Kɔnɔ a mu siga.

sentences.english: Which of the two did his father's pleasure? They say, The first. Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you, that tax-farmers and loose women are going into the kingdom of God before you.
sentences.susu: Yi mixi firinyie ya ma, nde a baba sago rabaxi?» E naxa a yaabi, «Na di singe.» Isa man naxa a masen e bɛ, «N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, duuti maxilie nun langoee singe soma wo bɛ Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you had no faith in him, but the tax-farmers and the loose women had faith in him: and you, when you saw it, did not even have regret for your sins, so as to have faith in him.
sentences.susu: Annabi Yaya fa nɛ kira tinxinxi masende wo bɛ, wo mu fa la a ra. Kɔnɔ duuti maxilie nun langoee tan la nɛ a ra. Hali wo to na to, wo mu tin natɛ masarade, wo xa la a ra.»

sentences.english: Give ear to another story. A master of a house made a vine garden, and put a wall round it, and made a place for crushing out the wine, and made a tower, and let it out to field-workers, and went into another country.
sentences.susu: «Wo wo tuli mati taali gbɛtɛ fan na. Xɛ kanyi nde naxa wɛni bilie si. A naxa tɛtɛ rabilin bɔxi ra, a baye ti, a yili ge wɛni bogi bunduma dɛnnaxɛ. Na xanbi, a naxa na hɛri bɔxi rawalie ma, a fa biyaasi.

sentences.english: And when the time for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the workmen, to get the fruit.
sentences.susu: Wɛni bogi ba tɛmui to a li, bɔxi kanyi naxa konyi ndee xɛɛ bɔxi rawalie xɔn ma, e xa a gbe wɛni bogi so a yi ra.

sentences.english: And the workmen made an attack on his servants, giving blows to one, putting another to death, and stoning another.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ bɔxi rawalie naxa na konyie suxu. E naxa keren bɔnbɔ, e boore faxa, e boore magɔnɔ gɛmɛe ra.

sentences.english: Again, he sent other servants more in number than the first: and they did the same to them.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi kanyi man naxa konyi gbɛtɛe xɛɛ dangi a singe ra. Bɔxi rawalie naxan naba booree ra, e naxa na raba nee fan na.

sentences.english: But after that he sent his son to them, saying, They will have respect for my son.
sentences.susu: A dɔnxɔɛ ra, bɔxi kanyi naxa a maɲɔxun, a a fala, ‹E n ma di tan binyama nɛ.› Na kui, a naxa a xa di xɛɛ bɔxi rawalie xɔn ma.

sentences.english: But when the workmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is he who will one day be the owner of the property; come, let us put him to death and take his heritage.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e to bɔxi kanyi xa di to, e naxa a fala e bore bɛ, ‹Yi nan na kɛ tongoma ra. Wo fa, won xa a faxa alako a kɛ xa findi won gbe ra.›

sentences.english: And they took him and, driving him out of the vine-garden, put him to death.
sentences.susu: E to a suxu, e naxa sa a xanin tɛtɛ xanbi ra, e a faxa.»

sentences.english: When, then, the lord of the vine-garden comes, what will he do to those workmen?
sentences.susu: «Na kui, bɔxi kanyi na siga e yire, a munse rabama na bɔxi rawalie ra?»

sentences.english: They say to him, He will put those cruel men to a cruel death, and will let out the vine-garden to other workmen, who will give him the fruit when it is ready.
sentences.susu: E naxa Isa yaabi, «A na bɔxi hɛrie sɔntɔma nɛ a ɲaaxi ra, a a xa bɔxi so bɔxi hɛri gbɛtɛe yi, naxee a mabiri soma a yi ra a waxati ma.»

sentences.english: Jesus says to them, Did you never see in the Writings, The stone which the builders put on one side, the same has been made the chief stone of the building: this was the Lord's doing, and it is a wonder in our eyes?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Wo mu nu yi masenyi xaran Kitaabui kui? ‹Banxitie mɛɛ gɛmɛ naxan na, a bara findi tuxui gɛmɛ hagigɛ ra. Marigi fɔxi nan a ra. Fe makaabaxi nan ya won bɛ.›»

sentences.english: For this reason I say to you, The kingdom of God will be taken away from you, and will be given to a nation producing the fruits of it.
sentences.susu: «Na nan a toxi, n xa a fala wo bɛ, wo bama nɛ Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma, si gbɛtɛ fa raso naa naxan birama Ala xa yaamarie fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Any man falling on this stone will be broken, but he on whom it comes down will be crushed to dust.
sentences.susu: Naxan na bira yi gɛmɛ ma, a kanyi magirama nɛ gbɛsɛxu. Yi gɛmɛ na bira naxan fan ma, a kanyi butuxunma nɛ.»

sentences.english: And when his stories came to the ears of the chief priests and the Pharisees, they saw that he was talking of them.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun Farisɛnie to a xa taalie mɛ, e naxa a kolon a Isa nu na wɔyɛnfe e tan nan ma fe ra.

sentences.english: And though they had a desire to take him, they were in fear of the people, because in their eyes he was a prophet.
sentences.susu: E nu katafe e xa a suxu, kɔnɔ e nu gaaxuxi ɲama ya ra, barima ɲama nu laxi a ra, a namiɲɔnmɛ nan na Isa ra.

sentences.english: And Jesus, talking to them again in stories, said:
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa so wɔyɛnfe e bɛ taalie ra. A naxa a masen,

sentences.english: The kingdom of heaven is like a certain king, who made a feast when his son was married,
sentences.susu: «Ala xa mangɛya misaalixi mangɛ nan na, naxan xulunyi ti a xa di xa futi xirife ma, donse fanyi gbegbe donma dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And sent out his servants to get in the guests to the feast: and they would not come.
sentences.susu: A naxa a xa konyie xɛɛ e xa mixie xili, yi fe binyɛ nu bara ragbilen naxee ma, kɔnɔ na mixie mu tin fade.

sentences.english: Again he sent out other servants, with orders to say to the guests, See, I have made ready my feast: my oxen and my fat beasts have been put to death, and all things are ready: come to the feast.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ man naxa konyi gbɛtɛe xɛɛ, e xa a fala na mixi maxilixie bɛ, ‹Wo ya ti, donse bara gɛ rafalade, n bara n ma ninge bɔrɔgɛxie faxa, fe birin bara gɛ yailande. Wo fa n ma di xa futixiri xulunyi.›

sentences.english: But they gave no attention, and went about their business, one to his farm, another to his trade:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e mu xɛɛrae danxun. Ndee naxa siga e xa xɛ yire, ndee fan naxa siga e xa yulɛya rabade.

sentences.english: And the rest put violent hands on his servants, and did evil to them, and put them to death.
sentences.susu: Naxee lu, e naxa mangɛ xa konyie suxu, e e ɲaxankata, e e faxa.»

sentences.english: But the king was angry; and he sent his armies, and those who had put his servants to death he gave to destruction, burning down their town with fire.
sentences.susu: «Mangɛ naxa xɔnɔ, a a xa sɔɔrie xɛɛ, a e xa na faxatie birin faxa, e e xa taa gan.

sentences.english: Then he said to his servants, The feast is ready but the guests were not good enough.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, a naxa a fala a xa konyie bɛ, ‹N ma di xa futixiri xulunyi xa fe birin bara gɛ yailande. Donsee birin nafalaxi, kɔnɔ mixi naxee nu maxilixi, a mu daxa e xa na binyɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Go then to the cross-roads, and get all those whom you see to come to the bride-feast.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa siga taa kui, wo sa mixie xili wo naxee yo toma naa, e xa fa n ma di xa futixiri xulunyi.›

sentences.english: And those servants went out into the streets, and got together all those whom they came across, bad and good: and the feast was full of guests.
sentences.susu: Konyie naxa mini kirae ma, e naxa mixi birin xili e xa fa. Mixi fanyi yo, mixi kobi yo, e birin naxa fa futixiri xulunyi, mangɛ xɔnyi naxa rafe ɲama ra.»

sentences.english: But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who had not on a guest's robe;
sentences.susu: «Mangɛ to so na mixi maxilixie ya ma, a naxa xɛmɛ nde to xulunyi donma mu nu ragoroxi naxan ma.

sentences.english: And he says to him, Friend, how came you in here not having a guest's robe? And he had nothing to say.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹N ma di, i soxi be di, i to mu maxirixi a xulunyi ki ma?› Kɔnɔ xɛmɛ mu nɔ yaabi yo fide.

sentences.english: Then the king said to the servants, Put cords round his hands and feet and put him out into the dark; there will be weeping and cries of sorrow.
sentences.susu: Na kui, mangɛ naxa a fala a xa walikɛe bɛ, ‹Wo a sanyie nun a bɛlɛxɛe xiri, wo a woli tande dimi kui, wa nun ɲin maxinyi na dɛnnaxɛ.›

sentences.english: For out of all to whom the good news has come, only a small number will get salvation.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbegbe maxilixi, kɔnɔ naxee sugandixi, e xurun.»

sentences.english: Then the Pharisees went and had a meeting to see how they might make use of his words to take him.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, Farisɛnie naxa sa e malan, e natɛ tongo e gantanyi tema Isa bɛ ki naxɛ, e xa a masɔtɔ wɔyɛnyi kui.

sentences.english: And they sent to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Master, we see that you are true, and that you are teaching the true way of God, and have no fear of anyone, because you have no respect for a man's position.
sentences.susu: E naxa e fɔxirabirɛe nun Herode xa mixi ndee xɛɛ Isa xɔn. Nee naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, muxu a kolon nɔndi falɛ nan i ra. I mixie xaranma Ala xa kira ra a nɔndi ki ma. I mu gaaxuma mixi yo xɔn, barima i mu mixi rafisama e booree bɛ.

sentences.english: Give us, then, your opinion of this: Is it right to give tax to Caesar, or not?
sentences.susu: Na kui, a fala muxu bɛ, i a toxi di? A lanma ka a mu lanma muxu xa duuti fi Rɔma mangɛ ma?»

sentences.english: But Jesus saw their trick and said, Oh false ones, why are you attempting to put me in the wrong?
sentences.susu: Isa to nu e xaxili kobi kolon, a naxa e yaabi, «Wo tan filankafuie, wo katafe n masɔtɔde munfe ra?

sentences.english: Let me see the tax money. And they gave him a penny.
sentences.susu: Wo kɔbiri kole masen n bɛ duuti fima naxan na.» E naxa gbeti kole ramini a bɛ.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Whose is this image and name on it?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e maxɔrin, «Nde xili nun nde misaali na yi kɔbiri kole ma yi ki?»

sentences.english: They say to him, Caesar's. Then he said to them, Give to Caesar the things which are Caesar's, and to God the things which are God's.
sentences.susu: E naxa a yaabi, «Rɔma Mangɛ.» A fan naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo mangɛ gbe ragbilen mangɛ ma, wo Ala fan gbe ragbilen Ala ma.»

sentences.english: And hearing it, they were full of wonder, and went away from him.
sentences.susu: E to a xa yaabi mɛ, e naxa kaaba. E naxa keli a xun, e siga.

sentences.english: On the same day there came to him the Sadducees, who say that there is no coming back from the dead: and they put a question to him, saying,
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛ kerenyi, Sadusenie naxa fa Isa xɔn. E tan nan a falama a faxamixie mu kelima faxɛ ma. E naxa Isa maxɔrin,

sentences.english: Master, Moses said, If a man, at the time of his death, has no children, let his brother take his wife, and get a family for his brother;
sentences.susu: «Karamɔxɔ, Annabi Munsa a masen nɛ, ‹Xa xɛmɛ nde taara faxa, a naxa a xa ginɛ lu a mu di yo bari, a na xunya nan na ginɛ dɔxɔma, alako a xa bɔnsɔɛ fi a taara ma.›

sentences.english: Now there were among us seven brothers; and the first was married and at his death, having no seed, gave his wife to his brother;
sentences.susu: Na kui, xɛmɛ nde naxa di xɛmɛ solofere sɔtɔ muxu ya ma be. A xa di singe naxa ginɛ dɔxɔ, a faxa, a mu bɔnsɔɛ yo lu. A xanbiratoe naxa a xa kaaɲɛ ginɛ tongo,

sentences.english: In the same way the second and the third, up to the seventh.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ na fan naxa faxa, a mu bɔnsɔɛ yo lu. Na nan man naba na fan xanbiratoe ra, a nun na mixi naani dɔnxɔɛ birin. E birin naxa faxa, e sese mu bɔnsɔɛ lu.

sentences.english: And last of all the woman came to her end.
sentences.susu: A dɔnxɔɛ ra, ginɛ fan naxa faxa.

sentences.english: When they come back from the dead, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? because they all had her.
sentences.susu: Na kui, marakeli lɔxɔɛ, na ginɛ to dɔxɔxi yi mixi solofere birin xɔn ma, a findima nde gbe ra?»

sentences.english: But Jesus said to them in answer, You are in error, not having knowledge of the Writings, or of the power of God.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Wo na tantanyi kui, barima wo mu Kitaabui kolon, wo mu Ala sɛnbɛ fan kolon.

sentences.english: For when they come back from the dead there are no husbands and wives, but they are as the angels in heaven.
sentences.susu: Mixie na keli faxɛ ma marakeli lɔxɔɛ, xɛmɛ mu ginɛ dɔxɔma, ginɛ fan mu dɔxɔma xɛmɛ xɔn. E luma nɛ alɔ malekɛe na ariyanna ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: But about the dead coming back to life, have you no knowledge of what was said to you by God in the Writings:
sentences.susu: A falafe tan, a faxamixie mu kelima faxɛ ma, Ala naxan masen wo bɛ, wo mu nu a xaran?

sentences.english: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead but of the living.
sentences.susu: A a masen nɛ, ‹N tan nan na Marigi Alatala ra, Iburahima, Isiyaga, nun Yaxuba naxan batuma.› Faxamixie xa mu Ala batuma, fo mixi ɲiɲɛ.»

sentences.english: And the people hearing it were surprised at his teaching.
sentences.susu: Ɲama to Isa xa yaabi mɛ, e naxa kaaba a xa fasari ma.

sentences.english: But the Pharisees, hearing how the mouths of the Sadducees had been stopped, came together;
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie to a mɛ a Isa nu bara Sadusenie dɛ balan yaabi fanyi ra, e naxa e malan.

sentences.english: And one of them, a teacher of the law, put a question to him, testing him, and saying,
sentences.susu: Ala xa sɛriyɛ lɔnnila nde nu na e ya ma. Na naxa kata Isa masɔtɔde maxɔrinyi ra, a naxɛ,

sentences.english: Master, which is the chief rule in the law?
sentences.susu: «Karamɔxɔ, yaamari mundun tide gbo a birin bɛ Tawureta Munsa kui?»

sentences.english: And he said to him, Have love for the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «‹I xa i Marigi Ala xanu i bɔɲɛ birin na, i nii birin na, a nun i xaxili birin na.›

sentences.english: This is the first and greatest rule.
sentences.susu: Na nan tide gbo, a findi yaamari singe nan na Ala xa sɛriyɛ birin ya ma.

sentences.english: And a second like it is this, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
sentences.susu: A firin nde maniya na singe ra, ‹I xa i ngaxakerenyi xanu alɔ i i yɛtɛ xanuxi ki naxɛ.›

sentences.english: On these two rules all the law and the prophets are based.
sentences.susu: Tawureta Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa sɛriyɛ birin gbakuxi yi yaamari firin nan na.»

sentences.english: Now while the Pharisees were together, Jesus put a question to them, saying,
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie to nu malanxi naa, Isa naxa e fan maxɔrin,

sentences.english: What is your opinion of the Christ? whose son is he? They say to him, The Son of David.
sentences.susu: «Wo Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa fe toxi di? Nde xa di a ra?» E naxa a yaabi, «Dawuda nan xa di a ra.»

sentences.english: He says to them, How then does David in the Spirit give him the name of Lord, saying,
sentences.susu: Isa fa e maxɔrin, «Munfe ra fa, Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra, Dawuda yɛtɛ naxa Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xili ‹N Marigi›? A tan Dawuda naxa a masen,

sentences.english: The Lord said to my Lord, Be seated at my right hand, till I put under your feet all those who are against you?
sentences.susu: ‹Marigi bara a masen n Marigi bɛ, “I magoro n yirefanyi ma, han beemanun n xa i yaxuie ragoro i sanyi bun.”›»

sentences.english: If David then gives him the name of Lord, how is he his son?
sentences.susu: «Xa Dawuda yɛtɛ yati naxɛ a bɛ ‹N Marigi›, a tan Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi nɔma findide Dawuda xa di ra di?»

sentences.english: And no one was able to give him an answer, and so great was their fear of him, that from that day no one put any more questions to him.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu nɔ yaabi yo fide. Fɔlɔ na lɔxɔɛ ma, mixi yo mu suusa maxɔrinyi tide Isa ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: Then Jesus said to the people and to his disciples:
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen ɲama nun a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ,

sentences.english: The scribes and the Pharisees have the authority of Moses;
sentences.susu: «Sɛbɛlitie nun Farisɛnie mixie xaranma Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ nan na.

sentences.english: All things, then, which they give you orders to do, these do and keep: but do not take their works as your example, for they say and do not.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa nu e xui rabatu, wo ɲɛrɛ a ma. Kɔnɔ wo naxa e wali fɔxi tan naba de, barima e naxan falama, e mu na xa rabama.

sentences.english: They make hard laws and put great weights on men's backs; but they themselves will not put a finger to them.
sentences.susu: E kote binyee raxirima, e e sa mixie fari, kɔnɔ e tan mu tinma e malide hali e bɛlɛxɛsole keren na.

sentences.english: But all their works they do so as to be seen by men: for they make wide their phylacteries, and the edges of their robes,
sentences.susu: E e xa kɛwalie birin nabama alako mixie xa e to. E e xa sɛbɛe rabelebelema e naxee xirima e tigi nun e bɛlɛxɛ ra. Luuti dɛnbɛxie naxee singanma donma sanbunyi ra Ala xa fe ma, e nee rakuyama han a dangi a i.

sentences.english: And the things desired by them are the first places at feasts, and the chief seats in the Synagogues,
sentences.susu: E na siga e dɛgede mixi xɔnyi malanyi na dɛnnaxɛ, xa na mu e na so salide banxi, binyɛ dɔxɔde rafan e ma ki fanyi.

sentences.english: And words of respect in the market-places, and to be named by men, Teacher.
sentences.susu: E na siga taa kui, a rafan e ma mixie xa e xɛɛbu binyɛ ra, e na a fala e bɛ, ‹Karamɔxɔ.›»

sentences.english: But you may not be named Teacher: for one is your teacher, and you are all brothers.
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ mixie naxa a fala wo tan bɛ ‹Karamɔxɔ,› barima karamɔxɔ keren peti nan na wo bɛ, wo fan birin findixi ngaxakerenmae nan na.

sentences.english: And give no man the name of father on earth: because one is your Father, who is in heaven.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa yi duniɲa adamadi xili ‹N Baba,› barima Babɛ keren peti nan na wo bɛ, wo Baba naxan na ariyanna.

sentences.english: And you may not be named guides: because one is your Guide, even Christ.
sentences.susu: Mixie man naxa a fala wo tan bɛ ‹Mangɛ,› barima Mangɛ keren peti nan na wo bɛ, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: But let the greatest among you be your servant.
sentences.susu: Naxan na mixi xungbe ra wo ya ma, a xa findi wo xa walikɛ nan na.

sentences.english: And whoever makes himself high will be made low, and whoever makes himself low will be made high.
sentences.susu: Naxan na a yɛtɛ igbo, a xa fe fama nɛ igorode. Naxan a yɛtɛ magoroma, a xa fe fama nɛ itede.»

sentences.english: But a curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! because you are shutting the kingdom of heaven against men: for you do not go in yourselves, and those who are going in, you keep back.
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛni filankafuie, barima wo naadɛ balanma mixie ya ra alako e naxa so Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma. Na kui, wo tan yɛtɛ mu soma, wo man mu tinma mixi gbɛtɛe fan xa so naa naxee waxi sofe.»
<range>

sentences.english: A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you go about land and sea to get one disciple and, having him, you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛni filankafuie! Wo baa igirima, wo bɔxi birin isa alako wo xa mixi keren naso wo xa dinɛ, kɔnɔ a na so, wo a findima yahannama di nan na, naxan kobi dɔxɔ firin wo tan na.»

sentences.english: A curse is on you, blind guides, who say, Whoever takes an oath by the Temple, it is nothing; but whoever takes an oath by the gold of the Temple, he is responsible.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan yarerati dɔnxuie! Wo a falama, ‹Xa mixi a kali hɔrɔmɔbanxi ra, fefe mu a ra, hali a kanyi mu a xui rakamali. Kɔnɔ xa mixi a kali xɛɛma ra naxan na hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, fo a kanyi xa a xui rakamali teku.›

sentences.english: You foolish ones and blind: which is greater, the gold, or the Temple which makes the gold holy?
sentences.susu: Wo tan dɔnxui xaxilitaree! Mundun tide gbo, xɛɛma, ka hɔrɔmɔbanxi naxan xɛɛma findixi se sɛniyɛnxi ra?

sentences.english: And, Whoever takes an oath by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever takes an oath by the offering which is on it, he is responsible.
sentences.susu: Wo man a falama, ‹Xa mixi nde a kali sɛrɛxɛbade ra, fefe mu a ra hali a kanyi mu a xui rakamali. Kɔnɔ xa mixi a kali sɛrɛxɛ ra naxan na sɛrɛxɛbade fari, fo a kanyi xa a xui rakamali teku.›

sentences.english: You blind ones: which is greater, the offering, or the altar which makes the offering holy?
sentences.susu: Wo tan dɔnxuie! Mundun tide gbo, sɛrɛxɛ, ka sɛrɛxɛbade naxan sɛrɛxɛ findixi se sɛniyɛnxi ra?

sentences.english: He, then, who takes an oath by the altar, takes it by the altar and by all things on it.
sentences.susu: Na kui, naxan yo na a kali sɛrɛxɛbade ra, a bara a kali na ra, a nun sɛrɛxɛ fan naxan birin saxi a fari.

sentences.english: And he who takes an oath by the Temple, takes it by the Temple and by him whose house it is.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo na a kali hɔrɔmɔbanxi ra, a bara a kali na ra, a nun naxan fan sabatixi a kui.

sentences.english: And he who takes an oath by heaven, takes it by the seat of God, and by him who is seated on it.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo na a kali ariyanna ra, a bara a kali Ala xa kibanyi ra, a nun naxan fan magoroxi a kui.»

sentences.english: A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you make men give a tenth of all sorts of sweet-smelling plants, but you give no thought to the more important things of the law, righteousness, and mercy, and faith; but it is right for you to do these, and not to let the others be undone.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛni filankafuie! Wo sansi xunxurie farilɛ bama, alɔ salaxui, suloɲi, nun digiyanyi, kɔnɔ fe naxee findixi a hagigɛe ra Ala xa sɛriyɛ kui, alɔ tinxinyi, kinikini, nun danxaniya, wo gbilenxi nee nan fɔxɔ ra. A lanma nɛ nu wo xa na sɛriyɛ hagigɛe rabatu, wo man mu nɛɛmu na sɛriyɛ xunxurie dɔnxɔɛe ma.

sentences.english: You blind guides, who take out a fly from your drink, but make no trouble over a camel.
sentences.susu: Yarerati dɔnxuie! Wo minse rasɛnsɛnma kuli di xa fe ra, wo fa ɲɔxɔmɛ gundi gerun!»

sentences.english: A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the plate, but inside they are full of violent behaviour and uncontrolled desire.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛnie filankafuie! Wo pɔɔti nun pileti fari maxama, kɔnɔ e kui rafexi balose naxan na, wo a sɔtɔxi muɲɛ nun wasatareya nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: You blind Pharisee, first make clean the inside of the cup and of the plate, so that the outside may become equally clean.
sentences.susu: I tan farisɛni dɔnxui! Pɔɔti nun pileti kui rasɛniyɛn sinden, na tɛmui a fari fan sɛniyɛnma nɛ.»

sentences.english: A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you are like the resting-places of the dead, which are made white, and seem beautiful on the outside, but inside are full of dead men's bones and of all unclean things.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛni filankafuie! Wo maniyaxi gaburie nan na, naxee fari ratofanxi, kɔnɔ e kui rafexi faxamixi xɔrie nun sɛniyɛntareɲa mɔɔli birin na.

sentences.english: Even so you seem to men to be full of righteousness, but inside you are all false and full of wrongdoing.
sentences.susu: Wo fan, mixi na wo to, e wo maɲɔxunma tinxintɔɛe nan na, kɔnɔ wo bɔɲɛ kui rafexi filankafuiɲa nun kobiɲa ra.»

sentences.english: A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! because you put up buildings for housing the dead bodies of the prophets, and make fair the last resting-places of good men, and say,
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun Farisɛni filankafuie! Wo gaburi fanyie yailanma namiɲɔnmɛe bɛ, wo tinxintɔɛe xa gaburie raxunmama,

sentences.english: If we had been living in the days of our fathers, we would not have taken part with them in the blood of the prophets.
sentences.susu: wo a fala, ‹Xa muxu nu na duniɲa ma muxu benbae waxati, muxu mu kafuma e ma nu namiɲɔnmɛe faxafe ra.›

sentences.english: So that you are witnesses against yourselves that you are the sons of those who put the prophets to death.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo bara seedeɲɔxɔya ba wo yɛtɛ xili ma, a falafe ra a wo findixi namiɲɔnmɛ faxɛe xa die nan na.

sentences.english: Make full, then, the measure of your fathers.
sentences.susu: Wo wo benbae xa kɛwalie rakamali yire!

sentences.english: You snakes, offspring of snakes, how will you be kept from the punishment of hell?
sentences.susu: Wo tan bɔximase bɔnsɔɛ, wo ratangama yahannama ma di?»

sentences.english: For this reason, I send you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: some of them you will put to death and put on the cross, and to some of them you will give blows in your Synagogues, driving them from town to town;
sentences.susu: «Na kui, n xa a fala wo bɛ, n fafe namiɲɔnmɛe, lɔnnilae, nun karamɔxɔe xɛɛde wo yire, kɔnɔ wo ndee faxama nɛ, wo ɲan nee ndee mabanbanma nɛ wuri magalanbuxie ma. Wo ndee bɔnbɔma nɛ sɛbɛrɛ ra wo xa salidee kui, e man siga taa yo kui, wo birama e fɔxɔ ra e ɲaxankatafe ra.

sentences.english: So that on you may come all the blood of the upright on the earth, from the blood of upright Abel to the blood of Zachariah, son of Barachiah, whom you put to death between the Temple and the altar.
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra, tinxintɔɛe xa wuli naxan ifilixi duniɲɛ, a birin luma wo tan nan ma, kelife Habila ma dɔxɔ Berekiya xa di Sakari ra, wo naxan faxa hɔrɔmɔbanxi nun sɛrɛxɛbade tagi.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, All these things will come on this generation.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, yi ɲaxankatɛ birin fama nɛ to mixie sɔtɔde.»

sentences.english: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, putting to death the prophets, and stoning those who are sent to her! Again and again would I have taken your children to myself as a bird takes her young ones under her wings, and you would not!
sentences.susu: «Darisalamu, Darisalamu, taa naxan namiɲɔnmɛe faxama, naxan Ala xa xɛɛrae magɔnɔma. Sanmaya wuyaxi n bara wa i xa die malanfe n yire, alɔ tɔxɔɛ a xa die rasoma a gabutenyi bun ma ki naxɛ, kɔnɔ wo naxa tondi!

sentences.english: See, your house is made waste.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Ala bara keli wo xa banxi xun ma.

sentences.english: For I say to you, You will not see me from this time till you say, A blessing on him who comes in the name of the Lord.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, wo mu n toma sɔnɔn, han wo a falama tɛmui naxɛ, ‹Baraka na mixi bɛ naxan fafe Marigi xili ra!›»

sentences.english: And Jesus went out of the Temple, and on the way his disciples came to him, pointing out the buildings of the Temple.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa mini hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui. A nu sigafe tɛmui naxɛ, a fɔxirabirɛe naxa e maso a ra, e wɔyɛn a bɛ a xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi mato a nun banxie naxee na a rabilinyi, e ti ki to tofanxi.

sentences.english: But he, answering, said to them, See you not all these things? truly I say to you that here there will not be one stone resting on another, which will not be pulled down.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo yi birin toxi? N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, yi gɛmɛ keren mu fama lude a boore fari be, a birin nabirama nɛ.»

sentences.english: And while he was seated on the Mountain of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, Make clear to us, when will these things be? and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the world?
sentences.susu: Isa nu magoroxi Oliwi geya fari tɛmui naxɛ, a fɔxirabirɛe naxa siga a yire, e a maxɔrin e doro ma, «Na fe sa rabama mun tɛmui? A man sa kolonma tɔnxuma mundun ma a i fa waxati nun duniɲa raɲɔnyi bara makɔrɛ?»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to them in answer, Take care that you are not tricked.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Wo mɛnni wo yɛtɛ ma, mixi yo naxa fa wo ratantan.

sentences.english: For people will come in my name, saying, I am the Christ; and a number will be turned from the true way through them.
sentences.susu: Mixi wuyaxi fama n xili falade e yɛtɛ xun ma a falafe ra, ‹N tan nan na Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi ra.› Na kui, e fama mixi gbegbe ratantande.»

sentences.english: And news will come to you of wars and talk of wars: do not be troubled, for these things have to be; but it is still not the end.
sentences.susu: «Wo gere fe mɛma nɛ, wo gere ndee xili mɛ, kɔnɔ wo naxa kɔntɔfili, barima fo na fe mɔɔlie xa raba. Na xa mu findima duniɲa raɲɔnyi ra sinden.

sentences.english: For nation will be moved against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and men will be without food, and the earth will be shaking in different places;
sentences.susu: Sie kelima nɛ e boore xili ma, ɲamanɛe e boore gere. Kaamɛ sinma nɛ bɔxi wuyaxi ma, bɔxi fan sɛrɛn yire gbegbe.

sentences.english: But all these things are the first of the troubles.
sentences.susu: Na fe birin findima mantɔɔrɔlie fɔlɛ nan na.»

sentences.english: Then they will be cruel to you, and will put you to death: and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.
sentences.susu: «Na tɛmui, mixie wo soma nɛ mangasanyi yi, e xa wo ɲaxankata, e wo faxa. Sie birin wo xɔnma nɛ n xili xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And numbers of people will be turned from the right way, and will give one another up and have hate for one another.
sentences.susu: Danxaniyatɔɛ gbegbe birama nɛ tantanyi kui na waxati, e e booree yanfa xɔnnanteya kui.

sentences.english: And a number of false prophets will come, causing error.
sentences.susu: Wule falɛ gbegbe fan e yɛtɛ findima nɛ namiɲɔnmɛe ra, e mixi gbegbe ratantan.

sentences.english: And because wrongdoing will be increased, the love of most people will become cold.
sentences.susu: Kobiɲa gboma nɛ han mixi gbegbe xa xanunteya xinbeli,

sentences.english: But he who goes through to the end will get salvation.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ naxan na a tunnabɛxi han a raɲɔnyi, na kanyi kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: And this good news of the kingdom will be given through all the world for a witness to all nations; and then the end will come.
sentences.susu: Ala xa mangɛya niini xibaaru fanyi kawandima nɛ duniɲa birin kui, a findi seedeɲɔxɔya ra sie birin bɛ. Na xanbi, duniɲa raɲɔnyi fama a lide.»

sentences.english: When, then, you see in the holy place the unclean thing which makes destruction, of which word was given by Daniel the prophet (let this be clear to the reader),
sentences.susu: «Wo tan naxee na yi xaranfe, wo wo tuli mati de! Wo na se haramuxi ɲaaxi to kasarɛ na naxan xanbi ra, a tixi yire sɛniyɛnxi kui, Annabi Daniyɛli naxan ma fe fala,

sentences.english: Then let those who are in Judaea go in flight to the mountains:
sentences.susu: wo tan naxee na Yudaya, wo lanma wo xa wo gi geyae fari.

sentences.english: Let not him who is on the house-top go down to take anything out of his house:
sentences.susu: Naxan na tande, a naxa so sese tongode a xa banxi kui.

sentences.english: And let not him who is in the field go back to get his coat.
sentences.susu: Naxan na xɛ ma, a naxa gbilen a xa xinbeli donma tongode.

sentences.english: But it will be hard for women who are with child and for those with babies at the breast in those days.
sentences.susu: Na waxati findima gbaloe nan na furuginɛe nun dingɛe bɛ!

sentences.english: And say a prayer that your flight may not be in the winter, or on a Sabbath.
sentences.susu: Wo Ala maxandi na naxa wo li ɲɛmɛ tɛmui, xa na mu a ra malabu lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: Because in those days there will be great sorrow, such as there has not been from the start of the world till now, or ever will be.
sentences.susu: Barima tɔɔrɛ a lima na waxati ma naxan maniyɛ singe mu nu to kabi duniɲa daa, a man mu gbilenma to ra abadan.

sentences.english: And if those days had not been made short there would have been no salvation for any, but because of the saints those days will be made short.
sentences.susu: Xa Marigi mu a ragirixi nu nde xa ba na xi kɔnti ra, adama yo mu kisima nu. Kɔnɔ a nde bama a kɔnti ra mixi sugandixie nan ma fe ra.»

sentences.english: Then if any man says to you, See, here is the Christ, or, Here; do not put faith in him;
sentences.susu: «Na waxati, xa mixi nde sa a fala wo bɛ, ‹A mato, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi na be›, xa na mu a ra, ‹Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi na mɛnni›, wo naxa la a ra.

sentences.english: For there will come up false Christs, and false prophets, who will do great signs and wonders; so that if possible even the saints might be tricked.
sentences.susu: Barima wule falɛe fama Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xili falade e yɛtɛ xun, xa na mu e e yɛtɛ findi namiɲɔnmɛe ra. E fama tɔnxuma makaabaxie nun kaabanakoe rabade alako e xa Ala xa mixi sugandixie ratantan, xa e sa nɔma.

sentences.english: See, I have made it clear to you before it comes about.
sentences.susu: Wo wo tuli ti, n bara a masen wo bɛ beenun a waxati xa a li.»

sentences.english: If, then, they say to you, See, he is in the waste land; go not out: See, he is in the inner rooms; put no faith in it.
sentences.susu: «Na kui, xa e sa a fala wo bɛ, ‹A mato, a sa na wula i›, wo naxa siga de! Xa e sa a fala wo bɛ, ‹A mato, a na banxi kui be›, wo naxa la a ra de!

sentences.english: Because as in a thunderstorm the bright light coming from the east is seen even in the west; so will be the coming of the Son of man.
sentences.susu: Adama xa Di na fa, a luma nɛ alɔ seyamakɔnyi naxan yanbama koore ma kelife sogetede han sogegorode.

sentences.english: Wherever the dead body is, there will the eagles come together.
sentences.susu: ‹Binbi na lu dɛnnaxɛ, yubɛe sa e malanma mɛnni nɛ.›»

sentences.english: But straight away, after the trouble of those days, the sun will be made dark and the moon will not give her light and the stars will come down from heaven and the powers of heaven will be moved:
sentences.susu: «Na ɲaxankatɛ waxati dangi xanbi, ‹soge ifɔɔrɔma nɛ, kike yanbɛ bama nɛ, tunbuie birama nɛ bɔxi, se naxan birin na koore ma e sɛrɛnma nɛ.›»

sentences.english: And then the sign of the Son of man will be seen in heaven: and then all the nations of the earth will have sorrow, and they will see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
sentences.susu: «Na tɛmui, Adama xa Di xa tɔnxuma minima nɛ koore ma. Duniɲa bɔnsɔɛ birin sunnunma nɛ. E Adama xa Di toma nɛ fa ra nuxui kui sɛnbɛ nun nɔrɛ ra.

sentences.english: And he will send out his angels with a great sound of a horn, and they will get his saints together from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
sentences.susu: A a xa malekɛe xɛɛma nɛ han duniɲa dande, e xa sa a xa mixi sugandixie malan sara xui ra keli duniɲa tunxun naani birin ma.»

sentences.english: Now take an example from the fig-tree: when her branch has become soft and puts out its leaves, you are certain that the summer is near;
sentences.susu: «Wo xɔrɛ bili mato misaali ra, wo xa xaxili sɔtɔ. A salonyi na ɲingi, a burɛxɛ nɛɛnɛ mini, wo a kolonma ɲɛmɛ tɛmui bara makɔrɛ.

sentences.english: Even so, when you see all these things, you may be certain that he is near, even at the doors.
sentences.susu: Adama xa Di fafe fan na na ki nɛ. Wo na yi fe birin to, wo xa a kolon a a bara makɔrɛ, a ɲan tixi naadɛ ra.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, This generation will not come to an end till all these things are complete.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, to mixie mu dangima fo na fe birin naba.

sentences.english: Heaven and earth will come to an end, but my words will not come to an end.
sentences.susu: Koore nun bɔxi dangima nɛ, kɔnɔ n ma masenyi tan mu dangima abadan, a mu kanama muku.»

sentences.english: But of that day and hour no one has knowledge, not even the angels in heaven, or the Son, but the Father only.
sentences.susu: «Mixi yo mu a kolon yi fee sa rabama lɔxɔɛ nun waxati yo ma. Hali malekɛ naxee na ariyanna, e mu a kolon, Ala xa Di fan mu a kolon, fo Baba Ala keren peti.

sentences.english: And as were the days of Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of man.
sentences.susu: Adama xa Di fa lɔxɔɛ luma nɛ alɔ Annabi Nuha xa waxati.

sentences.english: Because as in those days before the overflowing of the waters, they were feasting and taking wives and getting married, till the day when Noah went into the ark,
sentences.susu: Beenun na banbaranyi belebele xa duniɲa li, mixie nu e dɛgema, e nu e minma, e nu ginɛe dɔxɔma, e nu e xa die fima xɛmɛe ma, han Annabi Nuha so kunkui kui lɔxɔ naxɛ.

sentences.english: And they had no care till the waters came and took them all away; so will be the coming of the Son of man.
sentences.susu: E mu nu kɔntɔfilixi fefe ra, han banbaranyi naxa e li, a e birin xanin. Adama xa Di fafe fan nabama na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: Then two men will be in the field; one is taken, and one let go;
sentences.susu: Xa xɛmɛ firin na xɛ ma na waxati, keren tongoma nɛ, boore lu naa.

sentences.english: Two women will be crushing grain; one is taken, and one let go.
sentences.susu: Xa ginɛ firin na se dinfe mulunyi keren kui, keren tongoma nɛ, boore lu naa.

sentences.english: Be watching, then! for you have no knowledge on what day your Lord will come.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo naxa yanfa, barima wo mu wo Marigi fa lɔxɔɛ kolon.

sentences.english: But be certain of this, that if the master of the house had had knowledge of the time when the thief was coming, he would have been watching, and would not have let his house be broken into.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a fahaamu a fanyi ra, xa banxi kanyi a kolon nɛ nu muɲɛti fama tɛmui naxɛ kɔɛ kui, a mu xima nu, alako muɲɛti naxa nɔ sode a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: Be ready then; for at a time which you have no thought of the Son of man will come.
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra, wo fan xa wo tagi ixiri, wo naxa yanfa, barima Adama xa Di fama waxati nan ma wo ɲɔxɔ mu naxan ma.»

sentences.english: Who is the true and wise servant, whom his lord has put over those in his house, to give them their food at the right time?
sentences.susu: «Nde luma alɔ konyi naxan findixi xaxilima dugutɛgɛ ra? A marigi bara a ti a xa banxi walikɛe birin xun ma, a xa donsee taxun e ra a waxati.

sentences.english: A blessing on that servant, who will be doing so when his lord comes.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛlɛxinyi na na konyi bɛ, naxan marigi a lima na wali ra.

sentences.english: Truly, I say to you, he will put him over all he has.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, na marigi a harige birin taxuma nɛ na konyi ra.»

sentences.english: But if that evil servant says in his heart, My lord is a long time in coming;
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ xa na konyi findi a kobi ra, a a falama nɛ a yɛtɛ ma, ‹N marigi buma nɛ fafe ra,›

sentences.english: And is cruel to the other servants, taking his pleasure with those who are overcome with wine;
sentences.susu: a fa a boore konyie bɔnbɔ fɔlɔ, a nu lu a dɛge ra, a a min, e nun siisilae.

sentences.english: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he is not looking for him, and in an hour of which he has no knowledge,
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde fama, a tan konyi mu naxan kolon, a ɲɔxɔ man mu lɔxɔɛ naxan ma, a marigi gbilenma nɛ.

sentences.english: And will have him cut in two, and will give him a part in the fate of the false ones: there will be weeping and cries of sorrow.
sentences.susu: A na fa, a na konyi ɲaxankatama nɛ a ɲaaxi ra, konyi gbaloe sɔtɔ e nun filankafuie, a woli wa nun ɲin maxinyi na dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins, the friends of the bride, who took their lights, and went out with the purpose of meeting the husband.
sentences.susu: «Na waxati, Ala xa mangɛya luma nɛ alɔ ginɛdimɛdi mixi fu, naxee e xa lanpuie tongo sigafe ra ginɛdɔxɔɛ ralande, e xa sa lan a xa futi xiri ma.

sentences.english: And five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
sentences.susu: Na ginɛdimɛdie ya ma, suuli, xaxilitaree, suuli, xaxilimae.

sentences.english: For the foolish, when they took their lights, took no oil with them.
sentences.susu: Naxee findi xaxilitaree ra, e naxa e xa lanpuie xanin, kɔnɔ e mu ture xanin e xun naxan sama lanpuie kui.

sentences.english: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lights.
sentences.susu: Naxee tan findi xaxilimae ra, kankan naxa ture bitirɛ xanin a xun, a nun e xa lanpuie.»

sentences.english: Now the husband was a long time in coming, and they all went to sleep.
sentences.susu: «Ginɛdɔxɔɛ to bu fafe ra, xi xɔli naxa ginɛdimɛdie suxu, e naxa xi.

sentences.english: But in the middle of the night there is a cry, The husband comes! Go out to him.
sentences.susu: Kɔɛ tagi, sɔnxɔɛ xui naxa mini, ‹Ginɛdɔxɔɛ bara fa! Wo sa a ralan!›

sentences.english: Then all those virgins got up, and made ready their lights.
sentences.susu: Ginɛdimɛdie naxa keli, e e xa lanpuie yailan.

sentences.english: And the foolish said to the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lights are going out.
sentences.susu: Xaxilitaree naxa a fala xaxilimae bɛ, ‹Wo muxu ki wo xa ture nde ra, barima muxu xa lanpuie na xubenfe.›

sentences.english: But the wise made answer, saying, There may not be enough for us and you; it would be better for you to go to the traders and get oil for yourselves.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xaxilimae naxa e yaabi, ‹Ade, a mu won birin nalima. Wo siga ture matie xɔn wo xa sa wo gbe sara.›

sentences.english: And while they went to get oil, the master came; and those who were ready went in with him to the feast: and the door was shut.
sentences.susu: Nee to siga ture sarade, ginɛdɔxɔɛ naxa fa. Ginɛdimɛdi naxee nu bara ture sa e xa lanpuie kui, nee tan naxa bira a fɔxɔ ra, e so futixiri xulunyi, naadɛ fa balan e xanbi ra.»

sentences.english: After that the other virgins came, saying, Lord, Lord, let us in.
sentences.susu: «Na dangi xanbi, ginɛdimɛdi xaxilitaree fan naxa fa, e a fala, ‹Marigi, marigi, naadɛ rabi muxu bɛ.›

sentences.english: But he made answer and said, Truly I say to you, I have no knowledge of you.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a naxa e yaabi, ‹N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, n mu wo kolon.›»

sentences.english: Keep watch, then, because you are not certain of the day or of the hour.
sentences.susu: «Na kui, wo naxa yanfa, barima wo mu na lɔxɔɛ nun na waxati kolon.»

sentences.english: For it is as when a man, about to take a journey, got his servants together, and gave them his property.
sentences.susu: «A luma nɛ alɔ xɛmɛ nde naxan nu fafe biyaaside. A naxa a xa konyie xili, a a harige taxu e ra.

sentences.english: And to one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one; to everyone as he was able; and he went on his journey.
sentences.susu: A naxa xɛɛma kilo suuli so konyi keren yi, a firin so boore yi, a keren so a saxan nde yi ra. A to kankan bɛrɛ so a yi, a naxa biyaasi.»

sentences.english: Straight away he who had been given the five talents went and did trade with them, and made five more.
sentences.susu: «Xɛɛma kilo suuli taxu konyi naxan na, a naxa siga keren na, a xa sa na harige rawali. A naxa xɛɛma kilo suuli gbɛtɛ sɔtɔ geeni ra.

sentences.english: In the same way he who had been given the two got two more.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛma kilo firin taxu konyi naxan na, a fan naxa na harige rawali, a xɛɛma kilo firin gbɛtɛ sɔtɔ geeni ra.

sentences.english: But he who was given the one went away and put it in a hole in the earth, and kept his lord's money in a secret place.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xɛɛma kilo keren taxu konyi naxan na, a tan naxa sa yili ge, a a marigi xa kɔbiri nɔxun na kui.»

sentences.english: Now after a long time the lord of those servants comes, and makes up his account with them.
sentences.susu: «A to bu han, konyie marigi naxa gbilen e yire alako e xa dɛntɛgɛ sa a bɛ.

sentences.english: And he who had the five talents came with his other five talents, saying, Lord, you gave into my care five talents: see, I have got five more.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛma kilo suuli taxu konyi naxan na, a naxa fa a marigi harige ra, a a fala, ‹N marigi, i xɛɛma kilo suuli nan taxu n na. A mato, n bara kilo suuli man sa a xun geeni ra.›

sentences.english: His lord said to him, Well done, good and true servant: you have been true in a small thing, I will give you control over great things: take your part in the joy of your lord.
sentences.susu: A marigi naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹I nuwali. Konyi dugutɛgɛ nan i ra, walikɛ fanyi. N to harige dondoronti taxu i ra, i mu lanlanteya kana, n fa harige gbegbe nan taxuma i ra. Fa n xɔnyi, wo nun i marigi xa lu sɛɛwɛ kui.›»

sentences.english: And he who had the two talents came and said, Lord, you gave into my care two talents: see, I have got two more.
sentences.susu: «Na xanbi, xɛɛma kilo firin taxu konyi naxan na, a fan naxa fa, a a fala, ‹N marigi, i xɛɛma kilo firin nan taxu n na. A mato, n bara kilo firin man sa a xun geeni ra.›

sentences.english: His lord said to him, Well done, good and true servant: you have been true in a small thing, I will give you control over great things: take your part in the joy of your lord.
sentences.susu: A marigi naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹I nuwali. Konyi dugutɛgɛ nan i ra, walikɛ fanyi. N to harige dondoronti taxu i ra, i mu lanlanteya kana, n fa harige gbegbe nan taxuma i ra. Fa n xɔnyi, wo nun i marigi xa lu sɛɛwɛ kui.›»

sentences.english: And he who had had the one talent came and said, Lord, I had knowledge that you are a hard man, getting in grain where you have not put seed, and making profits for which you have done no work:
sentences.susu: «A dɔnxɔɛ ra, xɛɛma kilo keren taxu konyi naxan na, a fan naxa fa, a a fala, ‹N marigi, n a kolon i xa fe maxɔrɔxɔ. I sansi xabama, i mu naxan garansan. I sansi bogi bama, i mu naxan si.

sentences.english: And I was in fear, and went away, and put your talent in the earth: here is what is yours.
sentences.susu: N gaaxu nɛ. N naxa sa i xa xɛɛma kilo keren nɔxun yili kui. A mato, a tan nan yi ki. I harige sese mu lɔɛxi.›

sentences.english: But his lord in answer said to him, You are a bad and unready servant; if you had knowledge that I get in grain where I did not put seed, and make profits for which I have done no work,
sentences.susu: A marigi naxa a yaabi, ‹I tan konyi kobi tunnaxɔnɛ! I nu a kolon a n sansi xabama, n mu naxan garansan, n man sansi bogi bama, n mu naxan si?

sentences.english: Why, then, did you not put my money in the bank, and at my coming I would have got back what is mine with interest?
sentences.susu: A lan nɛ nu i n ma kɔbiri so kɔbiri rawalie yi ra, alako n na fa i yire tɛmui naxɛ, i n harige ragbilen n ma, geeni saxi a xun ma.

sentences.english: Take away, then, his talent and give it to him who has the ten talents.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xɛɛma kilo rasuxu a yi, wo a so konyi yi ra, xɛɛma kilo fu na naxan yi,

sentences.english: For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have more: but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
sentences.susu: barima a na naxan yo yi ra, a gbe xun masama nɛ, a gbo ki fanyi. Kɔnɔ a mu na naxan yi ra, hali naxan di na a yi, na yati bama nɛ a yi ra.

sentences.english: And put out the servant who is of no profit into the outer dark: there will be weeping and cries of sorrow.
sentences.susu: Wo yi konyi fufafu woli tande dimi kui, wa nun ɲin maxinyi na dɛnnaxɛ.›»

sentences.english: But when the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then will he be seated in his glory:
sentences.susu: «Adama xa Di na fa a xa nɔrɛ kui, a nun a xa malekɛe, a a magoroma nɛ a xa kibanyi nɔrɔxi kui.

sentences.english: And before him all the nations will come together; and they will be parted one from another, as the sheep are parted from the goats by the keeper.
sentences.susu: Si birin malanma nɛ a ya ra. A mixi mayegetima nɛ alɔ xuruse dɛmadonyi yɛxɛɛe nun sie mayegetima ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And he will put the sheep on his right, but the goats on the left.
sentences.susu: A yɛxɛɛe tima nɛ a yirefanyi ma, a sie fan ti a kɔɔla ma.»

sentences.english: Then will the King say to those on his right, Come, you who have the blessing of my Father, into the kingdom made ready for you before the world was:
sentences.susu: «Na tɛmui, mangɛ a falama nɛ mixie bɛ naxee na a yirefanyi ma, ‹Wo fa, n Baba naxee barakaxi. Wo fa mangɛya sɔtɔ wo kɛ ra, mangɛya naxan yailanxi wo bɛ kabi duniɲa fɔlɛ.

sentences.english: For I was in need of food, and you gave it to me: I was in need of drink, and you gave it to me: I was wandering, and you took me in;
sentences.susu: Barima kaamɛ to nu n ma, wo naxa n ki donse. Ye xɔli to nu n ma, wo naxa n ki ye. Xɔɲɛ to nu n na, wo naxa n yigiya.

sentences.english: I had no clothing, and you gave it to me: when I was ill, or in prison, you came to me.
sentences.susu: N mageli to nu a ra, wo naxa dugie fi n ma. N to nu furaxi, wo naxa fa mɛɛni n ma. N to nu saxi geeli, wo naxa fa n yire matode.›»

sentences.english: Then will the upright make answer to him, saying, Lord, when did we see you in need of food, and give it to you? or in need of drink, and give it to you?
sentences.susu: «Na tɛmui, tinxintɔɛe a maxɔrinma nɛ, ‹Marigi, muxu i to kaamɛ kui mun tɛmui, muxu fa i ki donse, xa na mu ye xɔli ra, muxu fa i ki ye?

sentences.english: And when did we see you wandering, and take you in? or without clothing, and give it to you?
sentences.susu: Muxu i to xɔɲɛya ra mun tɛmui, muxu fa i yigiya, xa na mu i mageli ra, muxu fa dugie fi i ma?

sentences.english: And when did we see you ill, or in prison, and come to you?
sentences.susu: Muxu i furaxi to mun tɛmui, xa na mu i saxi geeli, muxu fa siga i yire matode?›

sentences.english: And the King will make answer and say to them, Truly I say to you, Because you did it to the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ e yaabima nɛ, ‹N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, wo naxan yo raba n ngaxakerenyi mixi xuri nde bɛ, wo a rabaxi n tan nan bɛ.›»

sentences.english: Then will he say to those on the left, Go from me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire which is ready for the Evil One and his angels:
sentences.susu: «Na xanbi, a a falama nɛ mixie bɛ naxee na a kɔɔla ma, ‹Wo wo makuya n na, wo tan mixi dankaxie, wo sa so tɛ xɔɔra naxan yailanxi Ibulisa nun a xa malekɛe bɛ, naxan mu xubenma abadan.

sentences.english: For I was in need of food, and you gave it not to me; I was in need of drink, and you gave it not to me:
sentences.susu: Barima kaamɛ to nu n ma, wo mu n ki donse. Ye xɔli to nu n ma, wo mu n ki ye.

sentences.english: I was wandering, and you took me not in; without clothing, and you gave me no clothing; ill, and in prison, and you came not to me.
sentences.susu: Xɔɲɛ to nu n na, wo mu n yigiya. N mageli to nu a ra, wo mu dugie fi n ma. N furaxi to nu a ra, n man to nu saxi geeli, wo mu fa mɛɛnide n ma.›»

sentences.english: Then will they make answer, saying, Lord, when did we see you in need of food or drink, or wandering, or without clothing, or ill, or in prison, and did not take care of you?
sentences.susu: «Na tɛmui, e fan a maxɔrinma nɛ, ‹Marigi, muxu i to mun tɛmui kaamɛ na i ma, xa na mu ye xɔli, xa na mu i findixi xɔɲɛ ra, xa na mu i mageli ra, xa na mu i furaxi, xa na mu i saxi geeli, muxu fa tondi i malide?›

sentences.english: Then will he make answer to them, saying, Truly I say to you, Because you did it not to the least of these, you did it not to me.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ e yaabima nɛ, ‹N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, wo mu naxan yo raba n ngaxakerenyi mixi xuri nde bɛ, wo tondixi a rabade n tan nan bɛ.›

sentences.english: And these will go away into eternal punishment; but the upright into eternal life.
sentences.susu: Ɲaxankatɛ nan nagataxi na mixie bɛ abadan, kɔnɔ tinxintɔɛe tan abadan kisi nan sɔtɔma.»

sentences.english: And when Jesus had come to the end of all these words, he said to his disciples,
sentences.susu: Isa to gɛ yi fe birin masende, a naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ,

sentences.english: After two days is the Passover, and the Son of man will be given up to the death of the cross.
sentences.susu: «Wo a kolon, xi firin nan luxi Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali xa a li. Na tɛmui, Adama xa Di sama nɛ mixie bɛlɛxɛ e xa a banban wuri magalanbuxi ma.»

sentences.english: Then the chief priests and the rulers of the people came together in the house of the high priest, who was named Caiaphas.
