sentences.english: A man went out to put in seed, and while he was doing it, some was dropped by the wayside and it was crushed under foot, and was taken by the birds of heaven.
sentences.susu: «Xɛ rawali nde nan mini sansi xɔri garansande. A to nu sansi xɔri garansanma, a xɔri ndee naxa bira sankira xɔn, mixie naxa nee maboron, xɔnie man fa e don gbiki.

sentences.english: And some went on the rock, and when it came up it became dry and dead because it had no water.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri nde fan naxa bira gɛmɛ yire. A to bula, a naxa ragan barima ye mu nu na a bɛ.

sentences.english: And some went among thorns, and the thorns came up with it and it had no room for growth.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri ndee fan naxa bira tunbe kunsie tagi. Tunbe kunsie naxa gbo, e sansie ixɛtɛn, e e kana.

sentences.english: And some falling on good earth, came up and gave fruit a hundred times as much. And with these words he said in a loud voice, He who has ears, let him give ear.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri nde fan naxa bira bɛndɛ fanyi ma. Na xɔri keren keren birin sansie to te, e naxa e tɔnsɔɛ ramini, xɔri kɛmɛ kɛmɛ.» Isa to gɛ na wɔyɛnyi ra, a naxa a xui ite, a a fala, «Xa wo tuli fe mɛma, wo wo tuli mati yi masenyi ra.»

sentences.english: And his disciples put questions to him about the point of the story.
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛe to a maxɔrin a xa na taali ya iba e bɛ,

sentences.english: And he said, To you is given knowledge of the secrets of the kingdom of God; but to the others, they are given in stories, so that seeing, they may not see, and though they give hearing, the sense will not be clear to them.
sentences.susu: a naxa e yaabi, «Ala bara fahaamui fi wo ma wo xa a xa mangɛya niini gundo kolon, kɔnɔ mixi gbɛtɛe tan a mɛma taali wɔyɛnyie nan na, alako ‹E xa fe to, kɔnɔ e naxa a igbɛ. E xa fe mɛ, kɔnɔ e naxa a fahaamu.›»

sentences.english: Now this is the point of the story: The seed is the word of God.
sentences.susu: «Na taali wɔyɛnyi ya ibama yi ki nɛ. Sansi xɔri misaalixi Ala xa masenyi nan na.

sentences.english: Those by the side of the road are those who have given hearing; then the Evil One comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not have faith and get salvation.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri naxee bira kira xɔn, nee misaalixi mixie nan na naxee bara Ala xa masenyi mɛ, kɔnɔ Ibulisa nan fama fa, a a ba e bɔɲɛ ma, alako e naxa fa danxaniya, e kisi.

sentences.english: And those on the rock are those who with joy give hearing to the word; but having no root, they have faith for a time, and when the test comes they give up.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri naxee bira gɛmɛ yire, nee misaalixi mixi nan na naxee Ala xa masenyi mɛma, e a suxu sɛɛwɛ ra. Kɔnɔ sanke to mu na e bɛ, e xa danxaniya mu buma. Maratantanyi waxati na a li, e mu xanma.

sentences.english: And those which went among thorns are those who have given hearing, and go on their way, but they are overcome by cares and wealth and the pleasures of life, and they give no fruit.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri naxee bira tunbe kunsie tagi, nee misaalixi mixie nan na naxee Ala xa masenyi mɛma, kɔnɔ kɔntɔfili, bannaya, nun yɛtɛ rafan fee nan a niyama e mu gɛ e bogi raminide Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: And those in the good earth are those who, having given ear to the word, keep it with a good and true heart, and in quiet strength give fruit.
sentences.susu: Sansi xɔri naxee bira bɛndɛ fanyi tan ma, nee misaalixi mixie nan na naxee Ala xa masenyi mɛma, e a ragata e bɔɲɛ fanyi ma tinxinyi kui, e e bogi ramini Ala bɛ tunnabɛxiya kui.»

sentences.english: No man, when the light is lighted, puts a cover over it, or puts it under a bed, but he puts it on its table, so that those who come in may see the light.
sentences.susu: «Mixi yo mu lanpui radɛxɛma, a man fa fɛɲɛ felen a xun na, xa na mu a ra a a raso sade bunyi. A a dɔxɔma lanpui dɔxɔse nan fari alako naxee soma banxi, e xa a tɛ dɛxɛ to.

sentences.english: For nothing is put out of view which will not be made clear, and nothing is secret of which the knowledge will not come to light.
sentences.susu: Fe nɔxunxi birin fama kolonde. Gundo birin makɛnɛnma nɛ.

sentences.english: So take care how you give hearing, for to him who has will be given, and from him who has not will be taken even what he seems to have.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, wo lan wo xa wo tuli mati a fanyi ra. Fahaamui kanyi xa fahaamui xun masama, kɔnɔ fahaamutare, hali a naxan di maɲɔxunxi a gbe ra, na fama bade a yi ra.»

sentences.english: And his mother and his brothers came to him, and they were not able to get near him because of the great number of people.
sentences.susu: Isa nga nun a xunya xɛmɛmae naxa siga a yire, kɔnɔ e mu nu nɔma makɔrɛde a ra ɲama xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And someone said to him, Your mother and your brothers are outside desiring to see you.
sentences.susu: Mixi nde naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «I nga nun i xunyae na tande, e wama i tofe.»

sentences.english: But he said to them in answer, My mother and my brothers are those who have knowledge of the word of God and do it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a yaabi, «Mixi naxee Ala xa masenyi ramɛma, e a rabatu, nee nan findixi n nga nun n xunyae ra.»

sentences.english: Now it came about on one of those days that he got into a boat with his disciples; and he said to them, Let us go over to the other side of the water: and they put out the boat.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde, Isa naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Won xɛɛ baa naakiri ma.» E birin naxa baki kunkui kui, e siga.

sentences.english: But while they were sailing he went to sleep: and a storm of wind came down on the sea, and the boat became full of water and they were in danger.
sentences.susu: Na ɲɛrɛ kui, Isa naxa xi. Foye belebele naxa keli baa ma, kunkui naxa rafe fɔlɔ ye ra. Gbaloe nu bara makɔrɛ e ra.

sentences.english: Then they came to him and, awaking him out of his sleep, said, Master, Master, destruction is near. And he, when he was awake, gave orders to the wind and the rolling waves, and the storm came to an end, and all was calm.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a fɔxirabirɛe naxa fa Isa raxunu e a fala a bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, karamɔxɔ, won faxafe nɛ yi ki!» Isa to xunu, a naxa wɔyɛn foye nun mɔrɔnyie ma, a e yaamari. Foye nun mɔrɔnyie naxa a iti, baa naxa raxara.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Where is your faith? And fear and wonder overcame them, and they said to one another, Who then is this, who gives orders even to the winds and the water and they do what he says?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa fa a fɔxirabirɛe maxɔrin, «Wo xa danxaniya na minden?» E fan naxa gaaxu, e kaaba, e nu a fala e bore bɛ, «Nde lanxi yi ma? Hali foye nun baa, a e yamarima, e a xui rabatu.»

sentences.english: And they came to the country of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.
sentences.susu: Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe to so Gadara bɔxi ma, dɛnnaxɛ na Galile naakiri ma,

sentences.english: And when he had come to the land, there came to him a certain man from the town who had evil spirits; and for a long time he had had no clothing on, and was not living in a house but in the place of the dead.
sentences.susu: Isa to goro xare ma, a naxa ɲinnɛe kanyi li naa. Singe a nu sabatixi taa kui, kɔnɔ kabi tɛmui xɔnkuye a sabatixi gaburi yire a mageli ra.

sentences.english: And when he saw Jesus, he gave a loud cry and went down on the earth before him and in a loud voice said, What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Do not be cruel to me.
sentences.susu: A to Isa to, a naxa gbelegbele, a sa bira a bun ma, a a fala a xui itexi ra, «Isa, i tan Ala Xili Xungbe Kanyi xa Di, i wama munse xɔn ma n bɛ? N bara i mayandi, i naxa n ɲaxankata.»

sentences.english: For he gave an order to the evil spirit to come out of the man. For frequently it would take a grip of him: and he was kept under control, and prisoned with chains; but parting the chains in two, he would be sent by the driving of the evil spirit into waste places.
sentences.susu: A na fala nɛ, barima Isa nu bara ɲinnɛ yamari a xa gbilen na xɛmɛ fɔxɔ ra. Sanmaya wuyaxi, mixie nu bara yɔlɔnxɔnyi sa a sanyie nun a bɛlɛxɛe ma, alako a naxa a maxɔnɔ, kɔnɔ ɲinnɛ nu luma yɔlɔnxɔnyie bolon na, a fa a rakonkon wula ra.

sentences.english: And Jesus said to him, What is your name? And he said, Legion; for a number of spirits had gone into him.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a maxɔrin, «I xili di?» A naxa a yaabi, «N xili nɛ Gali.» A na fala nɛ barima ɲinnɛ gbegbe nan nu a fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And they made a request to him that he would not give them an order to go away into the deep.
sentences.susu: Ɲinnɛe naxa Isa mayandi alako a naxa e rasanba yahannama.

sentences.english: Now there was a great herd of pigs in that place, getting food on the mountain: and the evil spirits made a request to him that he would let them go into the pigs, and he let them.
sentences.susu: Xɔsɛ gali nu na e dɛmadonfe geya nde ma. Ɲinnɛe naxa Isa mayandi a xa tin e xa sa so na xɔsɛe. Isa to tin,

sentences.english: And the evil spirits came out of the man and went into the pigs: and the herd went rushing down a sharp slope into the water and came to destruction.
sentences.susu: ɲinnɛe naxa gbilen na xɛmɛ fɔxɔ ra, e sa so xɔsɛe. Xɔsɛe naxa goro e gi ra tentenyi ra, e sin baa ma. E birin naxa madula, e faxa.

sentences.english: And when the men who took care of them saw what had come about, they went quickly and gave news of it in the town and the country.
sentences.susu: Xɔsɛ dɛmadonyie to na fe to, e naxa siga e gi ra, e sa a fala taakae nun daaxakae bɛ,

sentences.english: And they went out to see what had taken place, and they came to Jesus and saw the man out of whom the evil spirits had gone, seated, clothed and with full use of his senses, at the feet of Jesus; and fear came on them.
sentences.susu: mixie fan naxa siga e xa sa a mato naxan nabaxi. E to Isa yire li, e naxa xɛmɛ fan li naa, ɲinnɛe nu bara keri naxan fɔxɔ ra, a dɔxɔxi Isa bun ma, sose ragoroxi a ma, a bara yalan. Na naxa e ragaaxu.

sentences.english: And those who had seen it gave them an account of how the man who had the evil spirits was made well.
sentences.susu: Naxee nu bara a to Isa ɲinnɛe keri xɛmɛ fɔxɔ ra ki naxɛ, e naxa a tagi raba birin bɛ.

sentences.english: And all the people of the country of the Gerasenes made a request to him to go away from them; for they were in great fear: and he got into a boat and went back.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, Gadarakae birin naxa Isa mayandi a xa keli e xɔnyi, barima gaaxui nu bara e suxu ki fanyi. Na kui, Isa naxa baki kunkui kui, a xa gbilen.

sentences.english: But the man from whom the evil spirits had gone out had a great desire to be with him, but he sent him away, saying,
sentences.susu: Ɲinnɛ kerixi xɛmɛ naxan fɔxɔ ra, a naxa Isa mayandi a e birin xa lu a ra. Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a ragbilen, a a masen a bɛ,

sentences.english: Go back to your house and let them have news of all the great things which God has done for you. And he went away, giving word through all the town of the great things which Jesus had done for him.
sentences.susu: «Gbilen i xɔnyi. Ala fe naxan birin nabaxi i bɛ, sa na dɛntɛgɛ sa.» Xɛmɛ naxa siga, a sa na taa birin isa. Isa naxan nabaxi a bɛ, a naxa sa na tagi raba birin bɛ.

sentences.english: And when Jesus went back, the people were glad to see him, for they were all waiting for him.
sentences.susu: Isa to gbilen naakiri ma, ɲama birin nu a mamɛfe. E naxa a ralan.

sentences.english: Then there came a man named Jairus, who was a ruler in the Synagogue: and he went down at the feet of Jesus, desiring him to come to his house;
sentences.susu: Salide yarerati nde naxa fa a xɔn naxan nu xili Yayiru. A naxa fa a suyidi Isa bɛ, a a mayandi a xa siga a xɔnyi,

sentences.english: For he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was near to death. But while he was on his way, the people were pushing to be near him.
sentences.susu: barima a xa di ginɛ kerenyi nu fa na faxafe nɛ. A ɲɛ kɔnti nu bara ɲɛ fu nun firin ɲɔndɔn li. Isa to nu sigafe Yayiru xɔnyi, ɲama gbegbe nu na a xɛtɛnfe.

sentences.english: And a woman, who had had a flow of blood for twelve years, and had given all her money to medical men, and not one of them was able to make her well,
sentences.susu: Ginɛ nde nu na e ya ma naxan xa kike wali mu nu a itima ɲɛ fu nun firin bun ma, mixi yo mu nɔ a dandande.

sentences.english: Came after him and put her hand on the edge of his robe, and straight away the flowing of her blood was stopped.
sentences.susu: Na ginɛ naxa fa Isa xanbi ra, a a bɛlɛxɛ din a xa donma sanbunyi ra. Keren na, a xa kike wali naxa dan.

sentences.english: And Jesus said, Who was touching me? And when they all said, It is not I, Peter and those who were with him said, Master, the people are pushing round you on every side.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa maxɔrinyi ti, «Nde dinxi n na?» Birin to a fala a e tan mu a ra, Piyɛri naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, ɲama i rabilinxi, birin nan i xɛtɛnfe!»

sentences.english: But Jesus said, Someone was touching me, for I had the feeling that power had gone out from me.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a masen, «Mixi nde bara din n na, barima n a kolon sɛnbɛ nde bara mini n fate.»

sentences.english: And when the woman saw that she was not able to keep it secret, she came, shaking with fear, and falling down before him she made clear before all the people the reason for her touching him, and how she was made well straight away.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ to a kolon a a mu nu nɔma a nɔxunde, a naxa fa a sɛrɛnma, a suyidi Isa bɛ. A a bɛlɛxɛ dinxi a ra fe naxan ma, a man yalanxi a ikɔrɛxi ra ki naxɛ, a naxa na birin tagi raba ɲama ya xɔri.

sentences.english: And he said to her, Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen a bɛ, «N ma di ginɛ, i xa danxaniya bara i rayalan. Siga bɔɲɛsa kui.»

sentences.english: While he was still talking, someone came from the house of the ruler of the Synagogue, saying, Your daughter is dead; do not go on troubling the Master.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu wɔyɛnfe, mixi nde naxa fa kelife salide yarerati xɔnyi, a a fala a tan Yayiru bɛ, «I xa di ginɛ bara faxa. I naxa karamɔxɔ tɔɔrɔ sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: But Jesus at these words said to him, Have no fear, only have faith, and she will be made well.
sentences.susu: Isa to a mɛ, a naxa a masen Yayiru bɛ, «I naxa gaaxu. I xa danxaniya tun. I xa di kisima nɛ.»

sentences.english: And when he came to the house he did not let any man go in with him, but only Peter and John and James, and the father of the girl and her mother.
sentences.susu: Isa to Yayiru xɔnyi li, a mu tin mixi yo xa so banxi kui fo Piyɛri, Yaya, Yaki, di ginɛ baba nun a nga.

sentences.english: And all the people were weeping and crying for her; but he said, Do not be sad, for she is not dead, but sleeping.
sentences.susu: Isa to a to birin nu wafe di ginɛ xa fe ra sunnunyi kui, a naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo naxa wa. Yi di ginɛ mu faxaxi xɛ, a na xife nɛ.»

sentences.english: And they were laughing at him, being certain that she was dead.
sentences.susu: Ɲama naxa yo Isa ma, e a mayele, barima e nu a kolon a tɛmɛdi bara faxa.

sentences.english: But he, taking her hand, said to her, My child, get up.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa tɛmɛdi bɛlɛxɛ suxu, a a fala a bɛ a xui itexi ra, «N ma di, keli!»

sentences.english: And her spirit came back to her and she got up straight away: and he gave orders that food was to be given to her.
sentences.susu: A nii naxa gbilen a i, a keli keren na. Isa naxa a fala e bɛ e xa donse fi a ma.

sentences.english: And her father and mother were full of wonder, but he gave orders to them to say nothing about it to anyone.
sentences.susu: Tɛmɛdi barimae dɛ nu ixaraxi, kɔnɔ Isa naxa a matintin e ra fa a fala, a fe naxan nabaxi, e naxa a fala mixi yo bɛ.

sentences.english: And getting the twelve together, he gave them power and authority over all evil spirits and over diseases, to make them well.
sentences.susu: Isa to a fɔxirabirɛ fu nun firinyie malan, a naxa sɛnbɛ nun nɔɛ fi e ma alako e xa nɔ ɲinnɛe keride mixie fɔxɔ ra, e man xa nɔ furema mɔɔli birin nayalande.

sentences.english: And he sent them out to be preachers of the kingdom of God, and to make well those who were ill.
sentences.susu: A naxa e xɛɛ mixie kawandide Ala xa mangɛya niini xa masenyi ra, e man xa furemae rayalan.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Take nothing for your journey, no stick or bag or bread or money, and do not take two coats.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo nɛ biyaasima, wo naxa sese xanin wo xun ma, alɔ xuli, gbɔnfɔɛ, taami, kɔbiri, xa na mu a ra donma firin nde.

sentences.english: And if you go into a house, let that house be your resting-place till you go away.
sentences.susu: Wo na so banxi naxan kui, wo xa yigiya mɛnni nɛ han wo sa sigama taa gbɛtɛ tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: And if any people will not take you in, when you go away from that town, put off its dust from your feet for a witness against them.
sentences.susu: Xa na taakae mu wo rasɛnɛ, wo xa keli naa. Wo xa mɛnni bɛndɛ rakɔnkɔn wo sanyie ra, a xa findi seedeɲɔxɔya ra e bɛ, wo bara e rabolo.»

sentences.english: And they went away, journeying through all the towns, preaching the good news and making people free from diseases in all places.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Isa fɔxirabirɛe naxa siga, e sa taae birin isa. E nu mixie kawandima Ala xa xibaaru fanyi ra, e nu furemae rayalan yire birin.

sentences.english: Now Herod the king had news of all these things: and he was in doubt, because it was said by some people that John had come back from the dead;
sentences.susu: Galile mangɛ Herode to fe birin mɛ naxee nu rabafe a xa bɔxi ma, a naxa ifu Isa xa fe ra, barima ndee nu a falama a Yaya Xunxa nan kelixi faxɛ ma,

sentences.english: And by some, that Elijah had come; and by others, that one of the old prophets had come back to life.
sentences.susu: ndee a fala a Annabi Eliya nan gbilenxi, ndee a fala a namiɲɔnmɛ gbɛtɛ naxan nu na duniɲɛ tɛmui dangixi, na nan man kelixi.

sentences.english: And Herod said, I put John to death: but who is this, of whom such stories are given to me? And he had a desire to see him.
sentences.susu: Herode naxa a fala, «Yaya tan, n bara na xunyi bolon a dɛ i. Kɔnɔ nde fa yi tan na, n naxan xa fe mɛma yi ki?» Na kui, a naxa so katafe a xa Isa to.

sentences.english: And the twelve, when they came back, gave him an account of what they had done. And he took them with him and went away from the people to a town named Beth-saida.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛrae to gbilen, e fe naxee rabaxi, e naxa a birin dɛntɛgɛ sa Isa bɛ. A fan naxa e xanin Betesayida e xa lu e xati ma yire keren.

sentences.english: But the people, getting news of it, went after him: and he was pleased to see them, and gave them teaching about the kingdom of God, and made those well who were in need of it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ ɲama to a kolon, e naxa bira Isa fɔxɔ ra. A fan naxa e ralan, a wɔyɛn e bɛ Ala xa mangɛya niini xa fe ra, a furemae rayalan.

sentences.english: And the day went on; and the twelve came to him and said, Send these people away so that they may go into the towns and the country round about and get resting-places and food for themselves, for we are in a waste place.
sentences.susu: Nunmare to so fɔlɔ, Isa fɔxirabirɛ fu nun firinyie naxa e maso a ra, e a fala a bɛ, «Ɲama rayensen alako e xa sa so taae nun daaxae naxee na be rabilinyi, e xa sa yigiyadee nun donsee fen, barima won na wula nɛ yi ki.»

sentences.english: But he said, Give them food yourselves. And they said, We have only five cakes of bread and two fishes, if we do not go and get food for all these people.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo tan nan xa donse fi e ma.» A fɔxirabirɛe naxa a yaabi, «Sese mu na muxu yi bafe taami suuli nun yɛxɛ firin na. Ka muxu tan nan xa siga donse sarade yi ɲama birin bɛ?»

sentences.english: For there were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them be seated in groups, about fifty to a group.
sentences.susu: Mixie naxee nu na naa, xɛmɛe kɔnti naxa siga han wulu suuli ɲɔndɔn. Isa naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Wo a fala mixie bɛ e xa dɔxɔ e tongo suuli suuli ma.»

sentences.english: And they did so, and made them all be seated.
sentences.susu: E fan naxa a raba na ki, e mixi birin nadɔxɔ.

sentences.english: And he took the five cakes of bread and the two fishes and, looking up to heaven, he said words of blessing over them, and when they had been broken, he gave them to the disciples to give to the people.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa na taami suuli nun na yɛxɛ firin tongo, a a ya rate koore ma, a fa Ala nuwali sa. A naxa taamie igira, a fa e so a fɔxirabirɛe yi ra, alako e xa e itaxun ɲama ma.

sentences.english: And they all took the food and had enough; and they took up of the broken bits which were over, twelve baskets full.
sentences.susu: Ɲama birin naxa e dɛge han e wasa. Donse dɔnxɔɛ xuntunyie to matongo, debe fu nun firin nan nafe.

sentences.english: And it came about that when he was in prayer, by himself, and the disciples were with him, he put a question to them, saying, Who do the people say I am?
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde Isa nu na Ala maxandife a xati ma. A fɔxirabirɛe fan nu na naa. A naxa e maxɔrin, a naxɛ, «Mixie munse falama n ma fe ra? Nde lanxi n ma?»

sentences.english: And they, answering, said, John the Baptist; but others say Elijah; and others, that one of the old prophets has come back.
sentences.susu: E naxa a yaabi, «Ndee a falama, Annabi Yaya Xunxa. Ndee a falama, Annabi Eliya. Ndee a falama, namiɲɔnmɛ gbɛtɛ naxan faxa waxati dangixi, na nan man kelixi.»

sentences.english: And he said, But who do you say that I am? And Peter, answering, said, The Christ of God.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa e maxɔrin, «Kɔnɔ wo tan naxɛ di? Nde n na?» Piyɛri naxa a yaabi, «Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi nan na i ra.»

sentences.english: But he gave them special orders, not to say this to any man;
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a matintin e ra, a e yamari, e naxa a xa fe fala mixi yo bɛ.

sentences.english: Saying, The Son of man will undergo much and be put on one side by the rulers and the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and be put to death, and on the third day he will come back to life.
sentences.susu: A man naxa a masen e bɛ, «Fo Adama xa Di xa tɔɔrɛ gbegbe sɔtɔ. Yuwifie xa forie, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie, nun sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe mu fama lade a ra, e a faxama nɛ, kɔnɔ a man xa keli faxɛ ma a xi saxan nde.»

sentences.english: And he said to them all, If any man has a desire to come after me, let him give up all, and take up his cross every day, and come after me.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen birin bɛ, «Xa mixi wa birafe n fɔxɔ ra, a xa tondi a yɛtɛ ma, a xa tin tɔɔrɛ nun faxɛ ra lɔxɔɛ birin, a bira n fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: For whoever has a desire to keep his life will have it taken from him, but whoever gives up his life because of me, will keep it.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan wama a yɛtɛ rakisife, na kanyi lɔɛma nɛ. Naxan a yɛtɛ ralɔɛma n tan ma fe ra, na kanyi kisima nɛ.

sentences.english: For what profit will a man have if he gets all the world, but undergoes loss or destruction himself?
sentences.susu: Duniɲa birin sɔtɔɛ munse fanma mixi ma, xa a sigama yahannama?

sentences.english: For if any man has a feeling of shame because of me or of my words, the Son of man will have shame because of him when he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo yaagima n tan nun n ma wɔyɛnyi xa fe ra, n tan Adama xa Di fama a nɔrɛ kui tɛmui naxɛ nun a Baba Ala nun a xa malekɛ sɛniyɛnxie xa nɔrɛ, n fan yaagima nɛ na kanyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: But truly I say to you, Some of those who are here now will have no taste of death till they see the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, mixi ndee tixi wo ya ma be, naxee mu faxama fo e Ala xa mangɛya niini to.»

sentences.english: And about eight days after he had said these things, he took Peter and John and James with him and went up into the mountain for prayer.
sentences.susu: Yi masenyi dangi xanbi xi solomasaxan ɲɔndɔn, Isa naxa Piyɛri, Yaya, nun Yaki xanin geya fari Ala maxandide.

sentences.english: And while he was in prayer, his face was changed and his clothing became white and shining.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu Ala maxandife, a yatagi naxa masara. A xa dugie fan naxa fiixɛ alɔ naiyalanyi.

sentences.english: And two men, Moses and Elijah, were talking with him;
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, Annabi Munsa nun Annabi Eliya naxa mini e ma, e nun Isa naxa wɔyɛn.

sentences.english: Who were seen in glory and were talking of his death which was about to take place in Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: E mini nɔrɛ xungbe nan kui, e nu wɔyɛnfe Isa bɛ a xa faxɛ xa fe ma, naxan nu fafe kamalide Darisalamu.

sentences.english: Now Peter and those who were with him were overcome with sleep: but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men who were with him.
sentences.susu: Xi xɔli nu bara nɔ Piyɛri nun a booree ra, kɔnɔ e to xunu, e naxa Isa xa nɔrɛ to, a nun na xɛmɛ firin naxee nu na a fɛ ma.

sentences.english: And when they were about to go away from him, Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah: having no knowledge of what he was saying.
sentences.susu: Na xɛmɛ firinyie to nu kelife Isa xun, Piyɛri naxa a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, fe fanyi na a ra muxu to na be yi ki. Muxu xa lingira saxan yailan, keren i gbe, keren Annabi Munsa gbe, keren Annabi Eliya gbe.» Piyɛri mu nu a kolonxi a nu sese naxan falafe.

sentences.english: And while he said these things, the shade of a cloud came over them, and they were full of fear when they went into the cloud.
sentences.susu: A to nu na wɔyɛnfe, nuxui naxa goro e ma. Piyɛri nun a booree naxa gaaxu e to a to nuxui bara din e ma.

sentences.english: And there was a voice from the cloud saying, This is my Son, the man of my selection; give ear to him.
sentences.susu: Xui nde naxa mini nuxui kui, a a masen, «N ma Di nan ya, n ma Mixi Sugandixi. Wo wo tuli mati a ra.»

sentences.english: And after the voice was gone they saw that Jesus was by himself. And they kept quiet, and said nothing at that time to anyone of the things which they had seen.
sentences.susu: Na xui to gɛ wɔyɛnde, e naxa Isa to a keren. A fɔxirabirɛe fe naxan toxi e ya ra, e naxa dundu a fe ma, e mu a fala mixi yo bɛ na waxati.

sentences.english: And on the day after, when they came down from the mountain, a great band of people came to him.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe naxa goro geya fari, ɲama gbegbe naxa fa a ralande.

sentences.english: And a man from among them, crying out, said, Master, I make a request to you, give a thought to my son, for he is my only child:
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, xɛmɛ nde naxa a xui ite ɲama tagi Isa mayandife ra, «Karamɔxɔ, yandi, fa n ma di xɛmɛ mato, barima yi di kerenyi nan na n bɛ!

sentences.english: And see, a spirit takes him, and suddenly he gives a cry, twisted in pain and streaming at the lips, and when it goes away from him at last, he is marked as from blows.
sentences.susu: A mato, ɲinnɛ nan na a fɔxɔ ra. A na keli a ra, a sɔnxɔma nɛ, a a raketun a ra, n ma di dɛxunfɛ nu fa mini. A mu a bɛɲinma mafuren, fo a gɛ a rahalakide.

sentences.english: And I made a request to your disciples to send it out of him, but they were not able to do it.
sentences.susu: N bara i fɔxirabirɛe mayandi e xa yi ɲinnɛ keri a fɔxɔ ra, kɔnɔ e mu nɔxi.»

sentences.english: And Jesus said, O generation without faith and false in heart, how long will I have to be with you and put up with you? let your son come here.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Wo tan bɔnsɔɛ danxaniyatare, wo kobi. N xa lu wo sɛɛti ma han mun tɛmui? N xa ti wo bun ma han mun lɔxɔɛ? Wo fa na di ra n xɔn.»

sentences.english: And while he was coming, he was pushed violently down and twisted by the evil spirit. But Jesus gave sharp orders to the unclean spirit, and made the boy well, and gave him back to his father.
sentences.susu: A ɲan mu nu Isa yire li sinden, ɲinnɛ naxa di rabira bɔxi ma, a a raketun a ra. Kɔnɔ Isa to ɲinnɛ yamari, di naxa yalan, Isa fa a ragbilen a baba ma.

sentences.english: And they were full of wonder at the great power of God. But while they were all wondering at all the things which he did, he said to his disciples,
sentences.susu: Ɲama birin naxa kaaba Ala xa sɛnbɛ ma. Birin to nu kaabaxi Isa wali fɔxi birin ma, a naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ,

sentences.english: Let these words go deep into your ears, for the Son of man will be given up into the hands of men.
sentences.susu: «Wo tan xa yi masenyi nan namɛ a fanyi ra: Adama xa Di sama nɛ mixie bɛlɛxɛ.»

sentences.english: But this saying was not clear to them and its sense was kept secret from them so that they were not able to see it: and they had fear of questioning him about it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e mu na wɔyɛnyi fahaamu, barima a nu bara nɔxun e ma alako e naxa a kolon. E man mu suusa Isa maxɔrinde a ma.

sentences.english: Now there was a discussion among them about which of them would be the greatest.
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛe naxa so wɔyɛnyi kui, e xa a kolon naxan tide gbo e ya ma.

sentences.english: But when Jesus saw the reasoning of their hearts, he took a small child and put him by his side,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa to nu e bɔɲɛ ma fe kolon, a naxa dimɛdi nde tongo, a a ti a fɛ ma.

sentences.english: And said to them, Whoever gives honour to this child in my name, gives honour to me: and whoever gives honour to me, gives honour to him who sent me: for whoever is least among you all, that man is great.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen e bɛ, «Mixi yo naxan yi dimɛdi mɔɔli rasɛnɛma n xili ra, na kanyi bara n tan yɛtɛ yati rasɛnɛ. Mixi yo naxan n tan nasɛnɛ, na kanyi bara n xɛɛma fan nasɛnɛ. Naxan findixi mixi xuri ra wo birin ya ma, a tan nan tide gbo.»

sentences.english: And John, answering, said, Master, we saw a man driving out evil spirits in your name, and we did not let him do it, because he was not one of us.
sentences.susu: Yaya naxa a yaabi, «Karamɔxɔ, muxu bara xɛmɛ nde to a ɲinnɛ kerima mixi fɔxɔ ra i xili saabui ra. Muxu bara kata a xa ba na ma, barima a mu biraxi won fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: But Jesus said to him, Let him do it, for he who is not against you is for you.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yamari, «Wo naxa a ratɔn, barima xa naxan mu kelixi wo xili ma, na tan na wo tan na bɛ.»

sentences.english: And it came about that when the days were near for him to be taken up, his face was turned to go to Jerusalem,
sentences.susu: Waxati to nu bara makɔrɛ Isa xa te koore, a naxa natɛ tongo a xa Darisalamu kira suxu.

sentences.english: And he sent men before: and they came to a small town of Samaria to make ready for him.
sentences.susu: A naxa mixi ndee xɛɛ a ya ra. E to siga, e naxa so Samari taa nde e xa sa yigiya nde fen a bɛ.

sentences.english: But they would not have him there, because he was clearly going to Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naakae mu tin a rasɛnɛde barima a nu sigafe Darisalamu nɛ.

sentences.english: And when his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, Lord, may we send fire from heaven and put an end to them?
sentences.susu: A fɔxirabirɛe Yaya nun Yaki to na fe to, e naxa a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, muxu xa yaamari fi tɛ xa goro keli koore, a xa e ratɔn?»

sentences.english: But turning round he said sharp words to them.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a ya rafindi e ma, a wɔyɛn xɔrɔxɔɛ fala e bɛ.

sentences.english: And they went to another small town.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, e naxa siga taa gbɛtɛ.

sentences.english: And when they were on the way, a certain man said to him, I will come after you wherever you go.
sentences.susu: E to nu kira xɔn ma, xɛmɛ nde naxa fa a fala Isa bɛ, «I siga dɛdɛ, n na i fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to him, Foxes have holes and the birds of the air have resting-places, but the Son of man has nowhere to put his head.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Xulumase xima yili kui. Xɔni xima a tɛɛ kui. Kɔnɔ dɛdɛ mu na Adama xa Di bɛ a a xunyi sama dɛnnaxɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said to another, Come after me. But he said, Lord, let me first go and give the last honours to my father.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a masen mixi gbɛtɛ nde bɛ, «Bira n fɔxɔ ra.» Kɔnɔ a kanyi naxa a yaabi, «Marigi, a lu n xa siga, n xa sa n baba ragata sinden.»

sentences.english: But he said to him, Let the dead take care of their dead; it is for you to go and give news of the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «A lu faxamixie nan xa e xa faxamixie ragata. I tan xa siga, i xa sa mixie kawandi Ala xa mangɛya niini ra.»

sentences.english: And another man said, I will come with you, Lord, but first let me say a last good-day to those who are at my house.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbɛtɛ fan naxa a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, n birama nɛ i fɔxɔ ra, kɔnɔ a lu n xa siga n xɔnyi, n xa sa n ɲungu n ma mixie ma.»

sentences.english: But Jesus said, No man, having put his hand to the plough and looking back, is good enough for the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a yaabi, «Mixi yo naxan saari suxuma a nu fa a xanbi mato, a kanyi mu daxa a xa wali suxu Ala xa mangɛya niini bɛ.»

sentences.english: Now after these things, the Lord made selection of seventy others and sent them before him, two together, into every town and place where he himself was about to come.
sentences.susu: Yi fee dangi xanbi, Marigi naxa mixi gbɛtɛe sugandi, mixi tongo solofere a nun firin. A naxa e xɛɛ firin firin na, e xa siga a ya ra taa birin kui a nun yire birin a tan yɛtɛ nu fafe sigade dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And he said to them, There is much grain ready to be cut, but not enough workers: so make prayer to the Lord of the grain-fields that he will send workers to get in the grain.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen e bɛ, «Xɛ xaba wali belebele nan na, kɔnɔ walikɛe tan xurun. Wo xɛ kanyi maxandi alako a xa walikɛe rasanba a xa xɛ xabade.

sentences.english: Go on your way: see, I send you out like lambs among wolves.
sentences.susu: Wo siga. N na wo xɛɛfe nɛ alɔ yɛxɛɛyɔrɛ naxee soma wula baree tagi.

sentences.english: Take no bag for money or for food, and no shoes; say no word to any man on the way.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa kɔbiri, gbɔnfɔɛ, xa na mu a ra sankiri xanin wo xun ma. Wo naxa bu mixie xɛɛbu ra kira xɔn ma.»

sentences.english: And whenever you go into a house, first say, Peace be to this house.
sentences.susu: «Wo nu so banxi naxan kui, beenun wo xa se gbɛtɛ fala wo xa a masen sinden, ‹Ala xa bɔɲɛsa fi yi fɔxɔɛ ma.›

sentences.english: And if a son of peace is there, your peace will be with him: but if not, it will come back to you again.
sentences.susu: Xa bɔɲɛsa mixi nde sabatixi naa, Ala wo xa duba suxuma nɛ a bɛ, kɔnɔ xa na mixi mɔɔli mu na, Ala wo xa duba ragbilenma wo tan nan ma.

sentences.english: And keep in that same house, taking what food and drink they give you: for the worker has a right to his reward. Do not go from house to house.
sentences.susu: Wo xa lu na banxi kerenyi nan kui. E se naxan soma wo yi ra, wo xa a don, wo xa a min, barima a lanma walikɛ xa a sare sɔtɔ. Wo naxa keli na banxi kui wo xa sa yigiya banxi gbɛtɛ.»

sentences.english: And into whatever town you go, if they take you in, take whatever food is given to you:
sentences.susu: «Wo nu so taa naxan yo kui e naxa wo rasɛnɛ, e na naxan so wo yi ra, wo xa na don.

sentences.english: And make well those in it who are ill and say to them, The kingdom of God is near to you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa na furemae rayalan, wo a masen naakae bɛ, ‹Ala xa mangɛya niini bara makɔrɛ wo ra.›

sentences.english: But if you go into a town where they will not have you, go out into the streets of it and say,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo nu so taa naxan yo kui e mu wo rasɛnɛ, wo xa siga taa tagi nɛ, wo a masen mixie bɛ,

sentences.english: Even the dust of your town, which is on our feet, we put off as a witness against you; but be certain of this, that the kingdom of God is near.
sentences.susu: ‹Hali wo xa taa xube naxan kankanxi muxu sanyie ra, muxu bara a rakɔnkɔn a xa findi seedeɲɔxɔya ra naxan baxi wo xili ma. Kɔnɔ wo xa a kolon nɛ, a Ala xa mangɛya niini bara makɔrɛ.›

sentences.english: I say to you, It will be better in that day for Sodom than for that town.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, kiiti sa lɔxɔɛ, kiiti fanma Sodoma bɛ dangife na taa ra.»

sentences.english: A curse is on you, Chorazin! A curse is on you, Beth-saida! For if such works of power had been done in Tyre and Sidon as have been done in you, they would have been turned from their sins, in days gone by, seated in the dust.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, Korasinkae! Gbaloe na wo fan bɛ, Betesayidakae! Kaabanako naxee raba wo tagi, xa nee sa raba Tire nun Sidɔn nɛ nu, a a lima e tan bara tuubi nu a rakuya, e dɔxɔ sunnun donma ragoroxi e ma, e tɛ xube maso e ma e xa tuubi tɔnxuma ra.

sentences.english: But it will be better for Tyre and Sidon, in the day of judging, than for you.
sentences.susu: Kiiti sa lɔxɔɛ xɔrɔxɔma wo tan ma dangi Tirekae nun Sidɔnkae ra.

sentences.english: And you, Capernaum, were you not lifted up to heaven? you will go down to hell.
sentences.susu: I tan Kapɛrɛnamu go, i ɲɔxɔ a ma a i tema han ariyanna kui? Ade, i ragoroma nɛ han yahannama.»

sentences.english: Whoever gives ear to you, gives ear to me; and whoever is against you, is against me; and whoever is against me, is against him who sent me.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Naxan na a tuli mati wo ra, a kanyi a tuli matixi n tan nan na. Naxan na tondi lade wo ra, na kanyi tondixi lade n tan nan na. Naxan na tondi lade n tan na, na kanyi tondixi lade n xɛɛma nan na.»

sentences.english: And the seventy came back with joy, saying, Lord, even the evil spirits are under our power in your name.
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛ tongo solofere a nun firin naxa gbilen sɛɛwɛ kui, e a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, muxu na yaamari fi i xili ra, hali ɲinnɛe, e muxu xui rabatuma.»

sentences.english: And he said, I was watching for Satan, falling from heaven like a star.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «N bara Sentanɛ to bira ra keli koore ma alɔ seyamakɔnyi.

sentences.english: See, I have given you power to put your feet on snakes and evil beasts, and over all the strength of him who is against you: and nothing will do you damage.
sentences.susu: A mato, n bara nɔɛ fi wo ma wo xa ɲɛrɛ bɔximase nun tali ma, n nɔɛ fi wo ma yaxui Sentanɛ xa sɛnbɛ birin xun. Na birin kui, sese mu wo toma.

sentences.english: Do not be glad, however, because you have power over spirits, but because your names are recorded in heaven.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo naxa sɛɛwa xɛ ɲinnɛe to wo xui rabatuma. Wo xa sɛɛwa nɛ barima wo xili sɛbɛxi ariyanna.»

sentences.english: In that same hour he was full of joy in the Holy Spirit and said, I give praise to you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have kept these things secret from the wise and the men of learning, and have made them clear to little children: for so, O Father, it was pleasing in your eyes.
sentences.susu: Na waxati, Isa naxa sɛɛwa Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra, a a fala, «Baba Ala, koore nun bɔxi Marigi, n bara i tantu i to yi fee nɔxunxi lɔnnilae nun xaxilimae ma, i e masen dimɛdie bɛ. Iyo, n Baba, n bara i tantu barima i kɛnɛn fe nan ya.»

sentences.english: All things have been given to me by my Father: and no one has knowledge of the Son, but only the Father: and of the Father, but only the Son, and he to whom the Son will make it clear.
sentences.susu: «N Baba bara fe birin taxu n na. Mixi yo mu Ala xa Di kolon, fo Baba Ala. Mixi yo mu Baba Ala kolon, fo Ala xa Di, a nun Ala xa Di nu tin a masende naxan bɛ.»

sentences.english: And, turning to the disciples, he said privately, Happy are the eyes which see the things you see:
sentences.susu: A naxa a ya rafindi fɔxirabirɛe ma, a a fala e bɛ e xati ma, «Sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ, naxan fee toma wo ya naxan toxi!

sentences.english: For I say to you that numbers of prophets and kings have had a desire to see the things which you see, and have not seen them, and to have knowledge of the things which have come to your ears, and they had it not.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, namiɲɔnmɛ nun mangɛ wuyaxi bara wa e xa fee to wo na naxee tofe, kɔnɔ e mu a to. E bara wa e xa fee mɛ wo na naxee mɛfe, kɔnɔ e mu a mɛ.»

sentences.english: And a certain teacher of the law got up and put him to the test, saying, Master, what have I to do so that I may have eternal life?
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde, sɛriyɛ lɔnnila nde to nu wama Isa matofe, a naxa ti, a a fala a bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, a lanma n xa munse raba alako n xa abadan kisi sɔtɔ?»

sentences.english: And he said to him, What does the law say, in your reading of it?
sentences.susu: Isa fan naxa a maxɔrin, «Munse sɛbɛxi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ kui? I a fahaamuxi di?»

sentences.english: And he, answering, said, Have love for the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind; and for your neighbour as for yourself.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ lɔnnila naxa a yaabi, «I xa Ala xanu i bɔɲɛ birin na, i nii birin na, i sɛnbɛ birin na, a nun i xaxili birin na. I man xa i ngaxakerenyi xanu alɔ i i yɛtɛ xanuxi ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said, You have given the right answer: do this and you will have life.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala a bɛ, «I xa yaabi fan. Xa i na raba, i kisima nɛ.»

sentences.english: But he, desiring to put himself in the right, said to Jesus, And who is my neighbour?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ sɛriyɛ lɔnnila to nu wama a tan xa kolon tinxintɔɛ ra, a man naxa Isa maxɔrin, «Kɔnɔ nde findixi n ngaxakerenyi ra?»

sentences.english: And Jesus, answering him, said, A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he got into the hands of thieves, who took his clothing and gave him cruel blows, and when they went away, he was half dead.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa wɔyɛnyi tongo, a a yaabi, «Xɛmɛ nde nu na kira xɔn kelife Darisalamu gorofe ra Yeriko. Muɲɛtie naxa dutun a ma, e a xa dugie birin ba a ma, e a bɔnbɔ, e a lu alɔ faxamixi.

sentences.english: And by chance a certain priest was going down that way: and when he saw him, he went by on the other side.
sentences.susu: A naxa a li, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ nde nan nu fafe na kira xɔn ma. A to na xɛmɛ to saxi kira ra, a naxa dangi kira sɛɛti boore ra.

sentences.english: And in the same way, a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, went by on the other side.
sentences.susu: Na mɔɔli man na, Lewi di nde fan naxa fa kira xɔn ma. A to na li, a xɛmɛ to saxi kira ra, a fan naxa dangi kira sɛɛti boore ra.»

sentences.english: But a certain man of Samaria, journeying that way, came where he was, and when he saw him, he was moved with pity for him,
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ Samarika nde fan naxa fa a xa biyaasi kui, a na xɛmɛ li kira ra. A to a to, a naxa kinikini ki fanyi.

sentences.english: And came to him and put clean linen round his wounds, with oil and wine; and he put him on his beast and took him to a house and took care of him.
sentences.susu: A to a maso a ra, a naxa ture nun wɛni sa a xa fie ma, a e maxiri. A naxa a tongo, a a sa a xa sofale fari. A naxa a xanin yigiya banxi nde kui, a mɛɛni a ma.

sentences.english: And the day after he took two pennies and gave them to the owner of the house and said, Take care of him; and if this money is not enough, when I come again I will give you whatever more is needed.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, a naxa gbeti kɔbiri kole firin so na yigiya banxi kanyi yi ra, a a fala a bɛ, ‹Mɛɛni yi xɛmɛ ma. Xa i kɔbiri ba a xa fe ra dangi yi ra, n man nɛ dangima be n na kɔbiri ragbilenma i ma.›»

sentences.english: Which of these three men, in your opinion, was neighbour to the man who came into the hands of thieves?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa fa sɛriyɛ lɔnnila maxɔrin, «Yi mixi saxanyi ya ma, nde findixi ngaxakerenyi ra na xɛmɛ bɛ muɲɛtie dutun naxan ma?»

sentences.english: And he said, The one who had mercy on him. And Jesus said, Go and do the same.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ lɔnnila naxa a yaabi, «Naxan kinikini a ma.» Isa naxa a masen a bɛ, «I fan xa na mɔɔli nan naba.»

sentences.english: Now, while they were on their way, he came to a certain town; and a woman named Martha took him into her house.
sentences.susu: Isa nun a fɔxirabirɛe to so taa nde kui, ginɛ nde naxa e yigiya naxan xili Marata.

sentences.english: And she had a sister, by name Mary, who took her seat at the Lord's feet and gave attention to his words.
sentences.susu: A xunya ginɛma fan nu na naxan nu xili Mariyama. Na naxa sa dɔxɔ Marigi sɛɛti ma, a a tuli mati a xa masenyi ra,

sentences.english: But Martha had her hands full of the work of the house, and she came to him and said, Lord, is it nothing to you that my sister has let me do all the work? Say to her that she is to give me some help.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ Marata tan ya koto nu mɔxi a xa xɔɲɛe bun tife ra. Na kui, Marata naxa sa a fala Isa bɛ, «Marigi, i mu n xunya toxi? A bara wali birin lu n tan keren ma. Wɔyɛn a bɛ, a xa fa n mali.»

sentences.english: But the Lord, answering, said to her, Martha, Martha, you are full of care and troubled about such a number of things:
sentences.susu: Marigi naxa a yaabi, «Marata, Marata, i kɔntɔfilixi, i man ya koto mɔxi fe gbegbe ma,

sentences.english: Little is needed, or even one thing only: for Mary has taken that good part, which will not be taken away from her.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ i hayi na fe keren peti nan ma. Mariyama tan, a tan nan fe fanyi sugandixi. Na man mu bama a yi feo!»

sentences.english: And it came about that he was in prayer in a certain place, and when he came to an end, one of his disciples said to him, Lord, will you give us teaching about prayer, as John did to his disciples?
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde, Isa nu na Ala maxandife yire nde. A to gɛ, a fɔxirabirɛ nde naxa a fala a bɛ, «Marigi, muxu tinkan Ala maxandide alɔ Yaya a fɔxirabirɛe tinkanxi ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said to them, When you say your prayers, say, Father, may your name be kept holy and your kingdom come.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo nɛ Ala maxandima, wo xa a fala, ‹Baba Ala, duniɲa birin xa i xili sɛniyɛnxi kolon. I xa mangɛya niini xa fa.

sentences.english: Give us every day bread for our needs.
sentences.susu: Baloe fi muxu ma lɔxɔɛ birin, muxu hayi na naxan ma.

sentences.english: May we have forgiveness for our sins, as we make free all those who are in debt to us. And let us not be put to the test.
sentences.susu: Diɲɛ muxu xa yunubie ma, barima muxu fan diɲɛma mixie haakɛ ma, naxan yo bara fe kobi niya muxu ra. I naxa muxu ti maratantanyi kira xɔn.›»

sentences.english: And he said to them, Which of you, having a friend, would go to him in the middle of the night and say to him, Friend, let me have three cakes of bread;
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a masen e bɛ, «Xa a sa li, wo ya ma mixi nde naxa siga a boore nde xɔn kɔɛ tagi, a a fala a bɛ, ‹N boore, taami saxan doni n bɛ,

sentences.english: Because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to put before him;
sentences.susu: barima xɔɲɛ nde nan faxi n bɛ keli biyaasi, a fa li donse yo mu na n naxan soma a yi.›»

sentences.english: And he, from inside the house, would say in answer, Do not be a trouble to me; the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; it is not possible for me to get up and give to you?
sentences.susu: «Xa a sa li go, banxi kanyi a yaabi, ‹Ba n tɔɔrɔfe! Naadɛ balanxi, n tan nun n ma die birin saxi. N mu nɔma kelide fa n xa taami so i yi!›

sentences.english: I say to you, Though he will not get up and give to him, because he is his friend, still, if he keeps on making his request, he will get up and give him as much as he has need of.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, banxi kanyi mu kelima a xa a boore mali e xa dɔxɔbooreya ma. Kɔnɔ a boore xa lixirinyi tan, na nan a niyama banxi kanyi xa keli, a a boore hayi birin fan.»

sentences.english: And I say to you, Make requests, and they will be answered; what you are searching for, you will get; when you give the sign, the door will be open to you.
sentences.susu: «N xa a fala wo bɛ, wo maxandi ti, wo a sɔtɔma nɛ. Wo fenyi ti, wo a toma nɛ. Wo naadɛ kɔnkɔn, a rabima nɛ wo bɛ.

sentences.english: For to everyone who makes a request, it will be given; and he who is searching will get his desire; and to him who gives the sign, the door will be open.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan birin maxandi tima, a a sɔtɔma nɛ. Mixi naxan se fenma, a a toma nɛ. Mixi naxan naadɛ kɔnkɔnma, a rabima nɛ a bɛ.»

sentences.english: And which of you, being a father, will give a stone to his son, who makes request for bread? or for a fish, will give him a snake?
sentences.susu: «Baba mundun na wo ya ma naxan xa di yɛxɛ maxɔrinma a ma, a sa bɔximase so a yi ra?

sentences.english: Or for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
sentences.susu: Xa a sa tɔxɛlɛ nan maxɔrin wo ma, wo nɔma tali sode a yi ra?

sentences.english: If, then, you who are evil are able to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who make request to him?
sentences.susu: Xa wo tan mixi kobie fata se fanyie fide wo xa die ma, Baba Ala naxan na ariyanna, a dangi wo ra pon! A a Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi fima nɛ a maxandimae ma.»

sentences.english: And he was sending an evil spirit out of a man who was without the power of talking. And it came about that when the spirit had gone the man had the power of talking; and the people were full of wonder.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa ɲinnɛ nde keri xɛmɛ fɔxɔ ra naxan nu bara a kanyi findi boboe ra. Isa to na ɲinnɛ keri, boboe naxa wɔyɛn, ɲama naxa kaaba.

sentences.english: But some of them said, He sends out evil spirits by Beelzebul, the ruler of evil spirits.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi ndee nu na e ya ma, nee a fala, «A ɲinnɛe kerima ɲinnɛ mangɛ Bɛlɛsɛbulu nan saabui ra.»

sentences.english: And others, testing him, were looking for a sign from heaven from him.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbɛtɛe naxa gantanyi sa a ya ra a maxɔrinfe ra Ala xa tɔnxuma nde ma.

sentences.english: But he, having knowledge of their thoughts, said to them, Every kingdom in which there is division is made waste; and a house in which there is division comes to destruction.
sentences.susu: Isa to e xa maɲɔxunyi birin kolon, a naxa a masen e bɛ, «Lantareya na mangɛya naxan kui, a mu buma. Denbaya lantaree fan, e kanama nɛ.

sentences.english: If, then, Satan is at war with himself, how will he keep his kingdom? because you say that I send evil spirits out of men by the help of Beelzebul.
sentences.susu: Sentanɛ xa mangɛya nɔma bude xa lantareya na a kui? Wo naxɛ a n ɲinnɛ kerima Bɛlɛsɛbulu saabui nan na.

sentences.english: And if I, by Beelzebul, send out evil spirits, by whose help do your sons send them out? so let them be your judges.
sentences.susu: Xa n tan ɲinnɛe kerima Bɛlɛsɛbulu nan saabui ra, wo tan xa mixie fa e kerima nde saabui ra? Na kui, e tan nan yati wo makiitima.

sentences.english: But if I, by the finger of God, send out evil spirits, then the kingdom of God has overtaken you.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa n tan ɲinnɛ kerima Ala sɛnbɛ nan saabui ra, Ala xa mangɛya niini yati nan bara wo li.»

sentences.english: When the strong man armed keeps watch over his house, then his goods are safe:
sentences.susu: «Xa sɛnbɛma a xa banxi kantama geresose ra, a harige birin na kantari nan kui.

sentences.english: But when one who is stronger makes an attack on him and overcomes him, he takes away his instruments of war, in which he had put his faith, and makes division of his goods.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ na fa naxan sɛnbɛ gbo a bɛ, a nɔma nɛ a ra, a a xa geresosee ba a yi a nu laxi naxee ra, a a harige birin itaxun mixi gbɛtɛe ra.»

sentences.english: He who is not with me is against me, and he who will not give me help in getting people together is driving them away.
sentences.susu: «Mixi naxan mu n fɔxɔ ra, a tixi n kanke nɛ. Naxan mu n malima mixi sɔtɔde, a na mixie rayensenfe nɛ.»

sentences.english: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of a man, goes through dry places, looking for rest; and when he does not get it, he says, I will go back to my house from which I came.
sentences.susu: «Ɲinnɛ na gbilen mixi fɔxɔ ra, a sigama yire maxare lingira gbɛtɛ fende, kɔnɔ a mu a toma. Na tɛmui a a falama a yɛtɛ bɛ, ‹N xa gbilen n ma banxi kui n kelixi dɛnnaxɛ.›

sentences.english: And when he comes, he sees that it has been made fair and clean.
sentences.susu: A na gbilen mɛnni, a a lima nɛ na banxi makɔxi, a raxunmaxi a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: Then he goes and gets seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they go in, and take their places there: and the last condition of that man is worse than the first.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, a sigama nɛ a sa fa ɲinnɛ solofere gbɛtɛe ra naxee ɲaaxu a bɛ, e birin so na banxi kui, e sabati naa. Na kui, na mixi xa fe ɲaaxuma nɛ dangife singe ra.»

sentences.english: And it came about that when he said these things, a certain woman among the people said in a loud voice, Happy is the body which gave you birth, and the breasts from which you took milk.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu yi fee falafe, ginɛ nde naxa a xui ite ɲama tagi, «Sɛɛwɛ na ginɛ bɛ naxan i bari, a xiɲɛ fi i ma!»

sentences.english: But he said, More happy are they who give hearing to the word of God and keep it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a yaabi, «Sɛɛwɛ na mixie nan bɛ naxee Ala xa masenyi ramɛma, e a rabatu.»

sentences.english: And when a great number of people came together to him, he said, This generation is an evil generation: it is looking for a sign and no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah.
sentences.susu: Ɲama to nu Isa xɛtɛnfe, Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «To mixie kobi. E wama tɔnxuma makaabaxi tofe, kɔnɔ tɔnxuma yo mu fima e ma bafe Annabi Yunusa xa tɔnxuma ra.

sentences.english: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will the Son of man be to this generation.
sentences.susu: Annabi Yunusa findi tɔnxuma ra Ninewekae bɛ ki naxɛ, Adama xa Di fan findima tɔnxuma ra na ki nɛ yi waxati mixie bɛ.

sentences.english: The queen of the South will come up on the day of judging and give her decision against the men of this generation: for she came from the ends of the earth to give ear to the wisdom of Solomon; and now something greater than Solomon is here.
sentences.susu: Kiiti lɔxɔɛ, Seeba mangɛ ginɛ fan tima nɛ e nun to mixie, a seedeɲɔxɔya ba wo xili ma, barima a tan fa nɛ kelife yire makuye Sulemani xa lɔnni ramɛde, a fa li naxan na wo yire yi ki be, a tide gbo Sulemani bɛ.

sentences.english: The men of Nineveh will come up in the day of judging and give their decision against this generation: for they were turned away from their sins at the preaching of Jonah; but now something greater than Jonah is here.
sentences.susu: Kiiti sa lɔxɔɛ, Ninewekae fan kiiti tinxinxi sama nɛ yi waxati mixie ma, barima Ninewekae tuubi Yunusa xa kawandi nan saabui ra, kɔnɔ yakɔsi mixi nde na be naxan xa fe gbo Annabi Yunusa bɛ.»

sentences.english: No man, when the light has been lighted, puts it in a secret place, or under a vessel, but on its table, so that those who come in may see the light.
sentences.susu: «Mixi yo mu lanpui radɛxɛma a man fa a nɔxun yire nde, xa na mu a ra a debe felen a xun. A a dɔxɔma lanpui dɔxɔse nan fari alako naxee soma banxi, e xa a tɛ dɛxɛ to.»

sentences.english: The light of the body is the eye: when your eye is true, all your body is full of light; but when it is evil, your body is dark.
sentences.susu: «I ya nan na i fate xa lanpui ra. Xa i ya fan, i fate birin iyalanma nɛ, kɔnɔ xa i ya mu fan, i fate luma dimi nan kui.

sentences.english: So take care that the light which is in you is not dark.
sentences.susu: Na kui, i maɲɔxun ki fanyi xa naiyalanyi naxan na i bɔɲɛ kui mu findixi dimi ra.

sentences.english: If, then, all your body is light, with no part of it dark, it will be completely full of light, as when a flame with its bright shining gives you light.
sentences.susu: Xa i fate birin iyalanxi, dɛdɛ mu fa na dimi kui, a birin luma nɛ naiyalanyi kui alɔ lanpui dɛxɛ na ti i ma.»

sentences.english: Now, while he was talking, a Pharisee made a request that he would come to a meal with him; and he went in and took his seat at the meal.
sentences.susu: Isa to gɛ wɔyɛnde, Farisɛni nde naxa Isa maxɔrin e xa sa e dɛge. Isa to so Farisɛni xɔnyi, a naxa a magoro.

sentences.english: And when the Pharisee saw it, he was surprised because he came to the meal without first washing himself.
sentences.susu: Farisɛni naxa kaaba, a to a to Isa mu a bɛlɛxɛ raxa Yuwifie xa naamunyi ki ma beenun a xa a dɛge.

sentences.english: And the Lord said to him, You Pharisees make the outside of the cup and the plate clean; but inside you are thieves and full of evil.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Marigi naxa a fala a bɛ, «Wo tan Farisɛnie, wo pɔɔti nun pileti fari maxama e xa rasɛniyɛn, kɔnɔ mixi see muɲafe nun sɛniyɛntareɲa nan tun na wo bɔɲɛ ma.

sentences.english: O you foolish ones! did not he who made the outside in the same way make the inside?
sentences.susu: Wo tan xaxilitaree! Wo mu a kolon Ala naxan se fari daa, a tan nan mixi bɔɲɛ fan daa?

sentences.english: But if you give to the poor such things as you are able, then all things are clean to you.
sentences.susu: Xa wo setare ki baloe ra naxan na wo xa piletie kui, wo xa fe birin nasɛniyɛnma nɛ.»

sentences.english: But a curse is on you, Pharisees! for you make men give a tenth of every sort of plant, and give no thought to right and the love of God; but it is right for you to do these things, and not let the others be undone.
sentences.susu: «Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan Farisɛnie! Wo sansi xunxurie birin farilɛ bama, alɔ salaxui nun gbɛngbɛ, kɔnɔ wo gbilenxi tinxinyi nun Ala xanufe fɔxɔ ra. A lanma nɛ nu wo xa na sɛriyɛ hagigɛe rabatu, wo man mu nɛɛmu boore sɛriyɛ xunxurie fan ma.

sentences.english: A curse is on you, Pharisees! for your desires are for the most important seats in the Synagogues and for words of respect said to you in the market-place.
sentences.susu: Gbaloe na wo bɛ, wo tan Farisɛnie! Barima a rafanxi wo ma, wo xa dɔxɔ binyɛ yire salide banxi kui, mixie man xa nu wo xɛɛbu taa kui binyɛ xɛɛbuie ra.

sentences.english: A curse is on you! for you are like the resting-places of dead men, which are not seen, and men go walking over them without knowledge of it.
sentences.susu: Gbaloe na wo bɛ, barima wo maniyaxi gaburie nan na naxee mu matɔnxumaxi, mixie ɲɛrɛma naxan fari e mu a kolon!»

sentences.english: And one of the teachers of the law, answering, said to him, Master, in saying this, you give a bad name to us as to them.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ lɔnnila nde naxa a fala a bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, i to yi fee falama yi ki, i na muxu fan nasɔtɔfe nɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said, A curse is on you, teachers of the law! for while other men are crushed under the weight of the rules you make for them, you yourselves do not put so much as one finger to them.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Gbaloe na wo fan bɛ, wo tan sɛriyɛ lɔnnilae! Barima wo kote dɔxɔma mixi xun ma naxan xanin xɔnɔ ki fanyi, kɔnɔ wo tan mu tinma e malide hali wo bɛlɛxɛsole keren na.

sentences.english: A curse is on you! for you make resting-places for the bodies of the prophets, but your fathers put them to death.
sentences.susu: Gbaloe na wo bɛ, barima wo gaburi fanyie yailanma namiɲɔnmɛe bɛ, a fa li wo benbae nan e faxa!

sentences.english: So you are witnesses and give approval to the work of your fathers; for they put them to death and you make their last resting-places.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo bara findi wo benbae xa kɛwalie seede ra, e xa na kɛwalie man bara wo kɛnɛn, barima e tan bara namiɲɔnmɛe faxa, wo fan na namiɲɔnmɛe xa gaburie raxunmama.

sentences.english: For this reason the wisdom of God has said, I will send them prophets and teachers, and to some of them they will give death and cruel pains;
sentences.susu: Na nan a ra, Ala xa lɔnni fan a masenxi nɛ, ‹N namiɲɔnmɛe nun xɛɛrae rasanbama nɛ e ma, e tan ndee faxa, e ndee ɲaxankata.›

sentences.english: So that punishment may come on this generation for the blood of all the prophets which was given from the earliest days;
sentences.susu: Na kui, namiɲɔnmɛe birin wuli naxan filixi kabi duniɲa fɔlɛ, yi waxati mixie nan a sare fima,

sentences.english: From the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who was put to death between the altar and the Temple. Yes, I say to you, It will come on this generation.
sentences.susu: kelife Habila wuli ma han Sakari, naxan faxa sɛrɛxɛbade nun hɔrɔmɔbanxi tagi. Iyo, n xa a fala wo bɛ, to mixie nan a birin sare fima.

sentences.english: A curse is on you, teachers of the law! for you have taken away the key of knowledge: you did not go in yourselves, and you got in the way of those who were going in.
sentences.susu: Gbaloe na wo bɛ sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe, barima wo bara saabi tongo naxan lan a xa lɔnni naadɛ rabi. Kɔnɔ wo mu soma, wo man mu tinma mixi gbɛtɛ fan xa so naa.»

sentences.english: And when he had come out of that place, the scribes and the Pharisees came round him angrily, questioning him about more things;
sentences.susu: Isa to keli naa, Farisɛnie nun sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe naxa ti fɔlɔ a kanke a xɔnɛ ra. E naxa maxɔrinyi mɔɔli birin ti a ma,

sentences.english: And watching him, for a chance to get something from his words which might be used against him.
sentences.susu: alako e xa a suxu tantanyi nde kui.

sentences.english: At that time, when thousands of the people had come together, in such numbers that they were crushing one another, he said first to his disciples, Have nothing to do with the leaven of the Pharisees, which is deceit.
sentences.susu: Yi fee nu dangife tɛmui naxɛ, mixi wulu wulu nan nu bara e malan, han e nu e bore maboronfe. Isa wɔyɛn fɔlɔ a fɔxirabirɛe nan singe bɛ, a naxɛ, «Wo wo yɛtɛ ratanga Farisɛnie xa lɛbini ma, naxan findixi filankafuiɲa ra.

sentences.english: But nothing is covered up, which will not come to light, or secret, which will not be made clear.
sentences.susu: Fefe nɔxunxi mu na naxan mu fama makɛnɛnde, gundo yo mu na naxan mu fama kolonde.

sentences.english: So, whatever you have said in the dark, will come to men's hearing in the light, and what you have said secretly inside the house, will be made public from the house-tops.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo naxan yo falama kɔɛ ra, a mɛma nɛ yanyi ra. Wo fefe makɔyikɔyima banxi kui, duniɲa birin fama rakolonde a ra kɛnɛ ma.»

sentences.english: And I say to you, my friends, Have no fear of those who may put the body to death, and are able to do no more than that.
sentences.susu: «N booree, n xa a fala wo bɛ, wo naxa gaaxu mixie ya ra naxee nɔma mixi fate bɛndɛ faxade, kɔnɔ e mu nɔma fefe ra na xanbi ra.

sentences.english: But I will make clear to you of whom you are to be in fear: of him who after death has power to send you to hell; yes, truly I say, Have fear of him.
sentences.susu: N xa a masen wo bɛ, a lan wo xa gaaxu naxan ya ra. Wo xa gaaxu Ala nan ya ra, barima a tan nan mixi faxama, a tan nan man nɔma mixi wolide yahannama. Iyo, n xa a fala wo bɛ, a lanma wo xa gaaxu a tan nan ya ra.»

sentences.english: Are not five sparrows given in exchange for two farthings? and God has every one of them in mind.
sentences.susu: «Turunna suuli xa mu sarama batanka firin na? Kɔnɔ Ala tan mu nɛɛmuma e sese ma.

sentences.english: But even the hairs of your head are numbered. Have no fear: you are of more value than a flock of sparrows.
sentences.susu: Hali xunsɛxɛ naxan na wo xunyi ma, Ala a birin kɔnti kolon. Wo naxa gaaxu, barima wo munafanyi gbo dangi turunna xɔni gali ra.»

sentences.english: And I say to you that to everyone who gives witness to me before men, the Son of man will give witness before the angels of God.
sentences.susu: «N xa a fala wo bɛ, mixi yo naxan n kolonma a Marigi ra adamadie ya ma, n tan Adama xa Di fan na kanyi kolonma nɛ Ala xa malekɛe ya i.

sentences.english: But if anyone says before men that he has no knowledge of me, I will say that I have no knowledge of him before the angels of God.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naxan na tondi n kolonde adamadie ya i, n fan tondima nɛ na kanyi kolonde Ala xa malekɛe ya i.»

sentences.english: And if anyone says a word against the Son of man, he will have forgiveness: but for him who says evil words against the Holy Spirit, there will be no forgiveness.
sentences.susu: «Mixi naxan birin wɔyɛn kobi falama Adama xa Di xa fe ra, na yunubi nɔma nɛ xafaride na kanyi bɛ, kɔnɔ mixi naxan Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi rasɔtɔma, na yunubi tan mu nɔma xafaride na kanyi bɛ.»

sentences.english: And when they take you before the Synagogues and the authorities and the rulers, take no thought about what answers you will give, or what you will say:
sentences.susu: «E na wo xanin salide kiitisae yire, xa na mu a ra mangasanyi xɔn, wo naxa kɔntɔfili wo e yaabima ki naxɛ, xa na mu a ra wo naxan masenma e bɛ,

sentences.english: For the Holy Spirit will make clear to you in that very hour what to say.
sentences.susu: barima Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi wo rakolonma nɛ na waxati yati ma, a lan wo xa naxan fala.»

sentences.english: And one of the people said to him, Master, give an order to my brother to make division of the heritage with me.
sentences.susu: Mixi nde naxa a fala Isa bɛ ɲama tagi, «Karamɔxɔ, a fala n taara bɛ a xa muxu kɛ itaxun, a n gbe so n yi.»

sentences.english: But he said, Man, who made me a judge or a maker of decisions for you?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a yaabi, «Nde n findixi kiitisa ra wo xun ma, xa na mu a ra wo kɛ taxunma ra?»

sentences.english: And he said to them, Take care to keep yourselves free from the desire for property; for a man's life is not made up of the number of things which he has.
sentences.susu: A man naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo a i ki fanyi, wo wo yɛtɛ ratanga xɔyife se mɔɔli birin ma, barima i banna kiyoki, duniɲɛigiri tide mu kelima se sɔtɔɛ xa ma.»

sentences.english: And he said to them, in a story, The land of a certain man of great wealth was very fertile:
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, Isa naxa yi taali sa e bɛ, «Xɛmɛ bannaxi nde xa xɛ naxa fan ki fanyi.

sentences.english: And he said to himself, What is to be done? for I have no place in which to put all my fruit.
sentences.susu: A naxa a maɲɔxun a yɛtɛ ma, ‹N munse rabama, barima yire mu n bɛ n nɔma n ma donse birin nagatade dɛnnaxɛ?›

sentences.english: And he said, This I will do: I will take down my store-houses and make greater ones, and there I will put all my grain and my goods.
sentences.susu: A naxa natɛ tongo, ‹N yi nan nabama. N na n ma bilie rabirama nɛ, n gbɛtɛe ti naxee gbo e bɛ. N na n ma donse nun n ma se birin malanma nee nan kui.

sentences.english: And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have a great amount of goods in store, enough for a number of years; be at rest, take food and wine and be happy.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui n na a falama nɛ n yɛtɛ bɛ, N bara se gbegbe ragata naxan buma ɲɛ wuyaxi. N xa n malabu fa, n xa n dɛge, n xa n min, n xa ɲɛlɛxin.›

sentences.english: But God said to him, You foolish one, tonight I will take your soul from you, and who then will be the owner of all the things which you have got together?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Ala naxa a masen a bɛ, ‹I tan xaxilitare! To kɔɛ yati ra, i nii bama nɛ i fate. I naxan birin malanxi, a fa luma nde bɛ?›

sentences.english: So that is what comes to the man who gets wealth for himself, and has not wealth in the eyes of God.
sentences.susu: A na na ki nɛ mixi bɛ naxan se malanma a yɛtɛ bɛ, kɔnɔ a mu bannaxi Ala bɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said to his disciples, For this reason I say to you, Take no thought for your life, about what food you will take, or for your body, how it may be clothed.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi Isa naxa a masen a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Na nan a toxi, n xa a fala wo bɛ, wo naxa kɔntɔfili baloe xa fe ra wo hayi na naxan ma yi duniɲɛigiri kui, xa na mu a ra, dugie xa fe ra wo naxee ragoroma wo fate ma.

sentences.english: Is not life more than food, and the body than its clothing?
sentences.susu: Wo xa duniɲɛigiri tide gbo donse bɛ, wo fate tide gbo dugie bɛ.

sentences.english: Give thought to the ravens; they do not put seeds into the earth, or get together grain; they have no store-houses or buildings; and God gives them their food: of how much greater value are you than the birds!
sentences.susu: Wo wo maɲɔxun xaaxae ma. E mu sansi sima, e mu xɛ xabama. Saga nun bili sese mu e yi, kɔnɔ Ala e rabaloma. Wo tan tide gbo xɔnie bɛ pon!

sentences.english: And which of you by taking thought is able to make himself any taller?
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma hali xi keren sade a xa simaya xun a xa kɔntɔfilife saabui ra?

sentences.english: If, then, you are not able to do even that which is least, why are you troubled about the rest?
sentences.susu: Xa wo mu nɔma na fe lanma ra, wo fa kɔntɔfilima fe gbɛtɛe ra munfe ra?»

sentences.english: Give thought to the flowers: they do no work, they make no thread; and still I say to you, Even Solomon, in all his glory, was not clothed like one of these.
sentences.susu: «Wo wula sansi fuge tofanyie mato e minima ki naxɛ. E mu walima, e mu woligɛsɛ yailanma, kɔnɔ n xa a fala wo bɛ, hali mangɛ Sulemani xa dariyɛ birin kui, a xa sosee mu nu tofan alɔ na sansi fuge keren.

sentences.english: But if God gives such clothing to the grass in the field, which today is living, and tomorrow will be burned in the oven, how much more will he give clothing to you, O men of little faith?
sentences.susu: Xa Ala wula sansi mɛɛnima yi ki nɛ, naxan na na to, tina a gan, a mɛɛnima nɛ wo tan ma dangi na ra pon! Wo xa danxaniya xurun.

sentences.english: And do not give overmuch thought to your food and drink, and let not your mind be full of doubts.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo xaxili birin ti donse nun minse ra. Wo naxa kɔntɔfili.

sentences.english: For the nations of the world go in search of all these things: but your Father has knowledge that you have need of them.
sentences.susu: Kaafiri birin birama na fe mɔɔli nan tun fɔxɔ ra. Kɔnɔ wo tan Baba Ala a kolon, a wo hayi na na see ma.

sentences.english: But let your chief care be for his kingdom, and these other things will be given to you in addition.
sentences.susu: Wo xa Ala xa mangɛya niini singe fen. Wo hayi na naxan birin ma, a na fan fima nɛ wo ma.»

sentences.english: Have no fear, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
sentences.susu: «Wo naxa gaaxu, wo tan naxee luxi alɔ n ma xuruse gɔɔrɛ lanma, barima a bara wo Baba Ala kɛnɛn a xa mangɛya niini fi wo ma.

sentences.english: Give what property you have in exchange for money, and give the money to the poor; make for yourselves money-bags which will not get old, wealth stored up in heaven which will be yours for ever, where thieves will not come nor worms put it to destruction.
sentences.susu: Se naxan na wo yi ra, wo xa sa a mati, wo a kɔbiri fi setaree ma. Wo xa kɔbiri bɔɔtɔ sɔtɔ naxan mu kanama, wo harige sɔtɔ naxan mu ɲɔnma, naxan na ariyanna, muɲɛti mu dɛnnaxɛ lima, nimasee fan mu kanari sama dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: For where your wealth is, there will your heart be.
sentences.susu: Wo harige na dɛnnaxɛ, wo bɔɲɛ fan luma mɛnni nɛ.»

sentences.english: Be ready, dressed as for a journey, with your lights burning.
sentences.susu: «Wo tagi ixirixi nan xa lu a ra, wo xa lanpuie radɛxɛxi.

sentences.english: And be like men who are looking for their lord, when he comes back from the bride-feast; so that when he comes to the door, it will be open to him quickly.
sentences.susu: Wo xa lu nɛ alɔ mixi naxee e marigi mamɛfe kelife futixiri xulunyi. A na fa, a naadɛ kɔnkɔn, e a rabima nɛ a bɛ keren na.

sentences.english: Happy are those servants who are watching when the lord comes; truly I say to you, he will make himself their servant and, placing them at the table, he will come out and give them food.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na konyie bɛ, marigi naxee lima e mu xixi a fa tɛmui. N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, marigi yati fama a tagi ixiride, a fa magorode fen a xa na konyie bɛ, a fa e bun ti.

sentences.english: And if he comes in the second division of the night or in the third, and they are watching for him, happy are those servants.
sentences.susu: Sɛɛwɛ na e bɛ, marigi naxee lima e mu xixi, hali a gbilen kɔɛ tagi, xa na mu a ra a ɲan dangi na ra.»

sentences.english: But be certain of this, that if the master of the house had had knowledge of the time when the thief was coming, he would have been watching, and would not have let his house be broken into.
sentences.susu: «Wo xa a fahaamu a fanyi ra, xa banxi kanyi a kolon nɛ nu muɲɛti fama tɛmui naxɛ, a mu a luma muɲɛti xa so a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: So be ready: for the Son of man is coming at a time when you are not looking for him.
sentences.susu: Wo fan, wo xa wo tagi ixiri, wo naxa yanfa, barima Adama xa Di fama waxati nan ma wo ɲɔxɔ mu naxan ma.»

sentences.english: And Peter said to him, Lord, are these words said to us only, or to all men?
sentences.susu: Piyɛri naxa a maxɔrin, «Marigi, i yi taali saxi muxu tan nan bɛ, ka birin bɛ?»

sentences.english: And the Lord said, Who then is the wise and responsible servant whom his lord will put in control of his family, to give them their food at the right time?
sentences.susu: Marigi naxa a yaabi, «Nde luma alɔ walikɛ xunmati naxan findixi xaxilima dugutɛgɛ ra? A marigi a tima a xa banxi walikɛe birin xun ma, a xa donse taxun e ra a waxati.

sentences.english: Happy is that servant who, when his lord comes, is doing so.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛlɛxinyi na na konyi bɛ, naxan marigi a lima na wali ra.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, he will put him in control of all his goods.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, na marigi a harige birin taxuma nɛ na konyi ra.

sentences.english: But if that servant says to himself, My lord is a long time coming; and goes about giving blows to the men-servants and the women-servants, feasting and taking overmuch wine;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa li go, na konyi a fala a yɛtɛ bɛ, ‹N marigi buma nɛ fafe ra›, a fa marigi xa konyi xɛmɛe nun konyi ginɛe bɔnbɔ, a xulunyi ti, a siisi?

sentences.english: The lord of that servant will come at a time when he is not looking for him, and at an hour when he is not ready for him, and he will have him cut in two and will give him his part in the fate of those who have no faith;
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde fama, a tan konyi mu naxan kolon, a ɲɔxɔ mu saxi naxan ma, a marigi gbilenma nɛ. A na fa, a na konyi ɲaxankatama nɛ a ɲaaxi ra, konyi gbaloe sɔtɔ e nun kaafirie.»

sentences.english: And the servant who had knowledge of his lord's desires and was not ready for him and did not do as he was ordered, will be given a great number of blows;
sentences.susu: «Konyi naxan a marigi sago kolon, kɔnɔ a mu a tagi ixiri, a man mu a sago raba, a fama nɛ bɔnbɔɛ gbegbe sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: But he who, without knowledge, did things for which punishment is given, will get only a small number of blows. The man to whom much is given, will have to give much; if much is given into his care, of him more will be requested.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naxan mu a marigi sago kolon, xa a bara fe raba a lanma a xa bɔnbɔ naxan ma, a mu bɔnbɔɛ gbegbe sɔtɔma. A gbegbe bara so naxan yi, a gbegbe man maxɔrinma nɛ a ma. A gbegbe bara taxu naxan na, na gbegbe man maxɔrinma nɛ a ma, nde man fa sa na xun.»

sentences.english: I came to send a fire on the earth, and it may even now have been lighted.
sentences.susu: «N faxi tɛ nan sade bɔxi ma. A rafanma n ma xa a ɲan bara dɛxɛ!

sentences.english: But there is a baptism which I have to undergo; and how am I kept back till it is complete!
sentences.susu: Fo n xa tɔɔrɛ belebele sɔtɔ. N bɔɲɛ mu sama fo na kamali tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: Is it your opinion that I have come to give peace on earth? I say to you, No, but division:
sentences.susu: Wo ɲɔxɔ a ma a n faxi bɔɲɛsa nan na duniɲa? Ade, n faxi fatanyi nan na.

sentences.english: For from this time, a family of five in one house will be on opposite sides, three against two and two against three.
sentences.susu: Keli yi waxati ma, xa mixi suuli na denbaya kui, gere luma mixi saxan nun mixi firin tagi.

sentences.english: They will be at war, the father against his son, and the son against his father; mother against daughter, and daughter against mother; mother-in-law against daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.
sentences.susu: Baba a xa di xɛmɛ gerema nɛ, di xɛmɛ fan a baba gere. Nga a xa di ginɛ gerema nɛ, di ginɛ fan a nga gere. Mama a xa mamadi gerema nɛ, mamadi fan a mama gere.»

sentences.english: Then he said to the people, When you see a cloud coming up in the west, straight away you say, There will be rain; and so it is.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a fala ɲama bɛ, «Wo na nuxui to a malan na sogegorode, wo a falama keren na, ‹Tunɛ nan kelixi,› a fa li na nan man yati rabama.

sentences.english: And when you see a south wind blowing, you say, There will be heat; and so it is.
sentences.susu: Foye na keli kɔɔla ma, wo a falama, ‹Kuye ifurama nɛ,› a fa li na nan man yati rabama.

sentences.english: O false ones! the face of the earth and the heaven is clear to you; how is it that the signs of these times are not as clear to you?
sentences.susu: Wo tan filankafuie! Wo fata bɔxi nun koore ɲingi kui kolonde, kɔnɔ munfe ra wo mu fata yi waxati fee tan tagi rabade?»

sentences.english: And why are you, in your hearts, unable to be judges of what is right?
sentences.susu: «Munfe ra wo tan yɛtɛ mu fe matoma, wo xa a kolon naxan findixi tinxinyi ra?

sentences.english: For if anyone has a cause at law against you, and you are going with him before the ruler, make an attempt, on the way, to come to an agreement with him, for if you do not, he may take you before the judge and the judge will give you up to the police, and they will put you in prison.
sentences.susu: Xa wo nun i kalamu mixi na sigafe kiitisa yire, kata wo xa lanyi xiri kira xɔn, xa na mu a ra a i bɛndunma nɛ han kiitisa xɔn, kiitisa fan i so kɔsibili yi ra, kɔsibili i sa geeli.

sentences.english: I say to you, You will not come out of it till you have made payment to the very last farthing.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala i bɛ, i mu minima mɛnni fo i kɔbiri birin fi han batanka dɔnxɔɛ.»

sentences.english: Now some people who were there at that time, gave him an account of how the blood of some Galilaeans had been mixed by Pilate with their offerings.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, mixi ndee naxa dɛntɛgɛ sa Isa bɛ a mangɛ Pilati bara Galileka ndee faxa, a e wuli masunbu e xa sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: And he, in answer, said to them, Are you of the opinion that these Galilaeans were worse than all other Galilaeans, because these things were done to them?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Wo a maɲɔxunxi nɛ a na mixie tɔɔrɔxi nɛ na ki barima e xa yunubi dangi Galileka booree ra?

sentences.english: I say to you, It is not so: but if your hearts are not changed, you will all come to the same end.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ na mu a ra feo! Kɔnɔ xa wo mu tuubi, wo birin halakima nɛ alɔ e tan.

sentences.english: Or those eighteen men who were crushed by the fall of the tower of Siloam, were they worse than all the other men living in Jerusalem?
sentences.susu: Na Darisalamuka fu nun solomasaxanyi go, Silɔmu koore banxi bira naxee ma? Wo ɲɔxɔ a ma a na tɔɔrɛ e lixi nɛ yunubitɔɛe nan to e ra dangi Darisalamuka boore birin na?

sentences.english: I say to you, It is not so: but if your hearts are not changed, you will all come to an end in the same way.
