sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ na mu a ra feo! Kɔnɔ xa wo mu tuubi, wo birin sɔntɔma nɛ alɔ e tan.»

sentences.english: And he made up this story for them: A certain man had a fig-tree in his garden, and he came to get fruit from it, and there was no fruit.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa yi taali masen e bɛ. «Xɔrɛ bili to nu sixi xɛmɛ nde xa bɔxi ma, a naxa siga a xa sa a bogi ba, kɔnɔ a mu sese to a kɔn na.

sentences.english: And he said to the gardener, See, for three years I have been looking for fruit from this tree, and I have not had any: let it be cut down; why is it taking up space?
sentences.susu: Na kui, a naxa a fala a xa walikɛ bɛ, ‹A mato, a ɲɛ saxan nan yi ki n fama xɔrɛ bogi fende yi xɔrɛ bili kɔn na, n mu se to. A side bara findi bɔxi makanaxi nan na! A sɛgɛ!›

sentences.english: And he said, Lord, let it be for this year, and I will have the earth turned up round it, and put animal waste on it, to make it fertile:
sentences.susu: Walikɛ naxa a yaabi, ‹Marigi, i man xa diɲɛ toofare xa dangi, alako n xa a rabilinyi buxa, n ɲaɲɛ sa a ma.

sentences.english: And if, after that, it has fruit, it is well; if not, let it be cut down.
sentences.susu: Xa a bogi tamuna, awa. Xa a mu bogi, i a sɛgɛ.›»

sentences.english: And he was teaching in one of the Synagogues on the Sabbath.
sentences.susu: Malabu lɔxɔ nde ma, Isa nu na kawandi tife salide nde kui.

sentences.english: And there was a woman who had had a disease for eighteen years; she was bent, and was not able to make herself straight.
sentences.susu: A naxa ginɛ nde li naa ɲinnɛ nu bara naxan kuntin a ra. Kabi ɲɛ fu nun solomasaxan a mu nu nɔma a rakelide feo!

sentences.english: And when Jesus saw her, he said to her, Woman, you are made free from your disease.
sentences.susu: Isa to a to, a naxa a xili, a a fala a bɛ, «N nga, i bara fulun yi fure ma to.»

sentences.english: And he put his hands on her, and she was made straight, and gave praise to God.
sentences.susu: Isa to a bɛlɛxɛ sa a ma, ginɛ naxa a rakeli keren na, a so Ala matɔxɔfe.

sentences.english: And the ruler of the Synagogue was angry because Jesus had made her well on the Sabbath, and he said to the people, There are six days in which men may do work: so come on those days to be made well, and not on the Sabbath.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa to a rayalanxi malabu lɔxɔɛ nɛ, salide xunmati naxa xɔnɔ a ma, a a fala ɲama bɛ, «Xi senni nan na a daxa mixi xa wali naxan kui. Wo xa fa marayalanyi fende na lɔxɔɛe nɛ, kɔnɔ wo naxa fa malabu lɔxɔɛ tan ma.»

sentences.english: But the Lord gave him an answer and said, O you false men! do you not, every one of you, on the Sabbath, let loose his ox and his ass and take it to the water?
sentences.susu: Marigi naxa a yaabi, «Wo tan filankafuie! Malabu lɔxɔɛ ma, wo birin mu wo xa ninge xa na mu wo xa sofale fulunma xɛ a xiride, wo a xanin ye minde?

sentences.english: And is it not right for this daughter of Abraham, who has been in the power of Satan for eighteen years, to be made free on the Sabbath?
sentences.susu: Iburahima xa di nan yi ginɛ ra, kɔnɔ Sentanɛ bara a xiri kabi ɲɛ fu nun solomasaxan. A mu lanma n xa a fan fulun malabu lɔxɔɛ ma?»

sentences.english: And when he said these things, those who were against him were shamed, and all the people were full of joy because of the great things which were done by him.
sentences.susu: A to na fala, a yaxui birin naxa yaagi, kɔnɔ ɲama tan naxa sɛɛwa a xa kaabanako fe birin na.

sentences.english: Then he said, What is the kingdom of God like? what comparison may I make of it?
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a masen e bɛ, «Ala xa mangɛya maniyaxi munse ra? N nɔma a misaalide tali wɔyɛnyi mundun na?

sentences.english: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his garden, and it became a tree, and the birds of heaven made their resting-places in its branches.
sentences.susu: A luxi nɛ alɔ konde xɔri xurudi xɛmɛ naxan si a xa bɔxi ma. A naxa te, a findi wuri bili ra, xɔnie fa e tɛɛ sa a kɔn na.»

sentences.english: And again he said, What is the kingdom of God like?
sentences.susu: A man naxa a masen, «N xa Ala xa mangɛya misaali munse ra?

sentences.english: It is like leaven, which a woman put into three measures of meal, and it was all leavened.
sentences.susu: A luxi nɛ alɔ lɛbini, ginɛ naxan sa farin busali tagi xun ma, na fa farin birin nate.»

sentences.english: And he went on his way, through towns and country places, teaching and journeying to Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Isa nu sigama kawandi ti ra taae birin kui, a xungbe nun a xuri. Na birin, a nu na Darisalamu kira nan xɔn.

sentences.english: And someone said to him, Lord, will only a small number have salvation? And he said to them,
sentences.susu: Mixi nde naxa a maxɔrin, «Marigi, nɔndi nan a ra, a mixi gbegbe mu kisima?» A naxa a yaabi,

sentences.english: Do your best to go in by the narrow door, for I say to you, A number will make the attempt to go in, but will not be able to do so.
sentences.susu: «Wo kata wo xa so naadɛ ixutuxi nan na, barima n xa a fala wo bɛ, mixi wuyaxi katama nɛ sode naa, kɔnɔ e mu nɔma.

sentences.english: When the master of the house has got up, and the door has been shut, and you, still outside, give blows on the door, saying, Lord, let us in; he will make answer and say, I have no knowledge of where you come from.
sentences.susu: A waxati a lima banxi kanyi kelima nɛ a naadɛ balan. Wo tan fama nɛ tide tande wo nu naadɛ kɔnkɔn na, wo a fala, ‹Marigi, naadɛ rabi muxu bɛ.› Na tɛmui, a wo yaabima nɛ, ‹N mu wo kolon, n mu wo kelide kolon.›

sentences.english: Then you will say, We have taken food and drink with you, and you were teaching in our streets.
sentences.susu: Wo man a falama nɛ a bɛ, ‹I mixie xaranxi muxu xɔnyi nɛ, won birin nan won dɛgexi, won birin nan won min.›

sentences.english: But he will say, Truly, I have no knowledge of you or where you come from; go away from me, you workers of evil.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a wo yaabima nɛ, ‹N xa a fala wo bɛ, n mu wo kolon, n mu wo kelide kolon. Wo keli n ya i, wo tan fe kobi rabae!›

sentences.english: There will be weeping and cries of sorrow when you see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are shut outside.
sentences.susu: Iburahima, Isiyaga, Yaxuba, nun namiɲɔnmɛ birin, wo e toma nɛ Ala xɔnyi ariyanna, kɔnɔ wo tan naminima tande, wa nun ɲinyi raxinyi na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And they will come from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south, and take their places in the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: Mixie kelima sogetede nun sogegorode, e keli kɔɔla nun yirefanyi biri, e e dɛge Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: And the last will be first, and the first will be last.
sentences.susu: Na kui, xanbiratie findima nɛ yareratie ra, yareratie fan findi xanbiratie ra.»

sentences.english: At that time, certain Pharisees came to him and said, Go away from this place, because Herod's purpose is to put you to death.
sentences.susu: Na waxati ma, Farisɛni ndee naxa fa Isa xɔn, e a fala a bɛ, «I xa keli be. Siga yire gbɛtɛ, barima Herode wama i faxafe.»

sentences.english: And he said, Go and say to that fox, I send out evil spirits and do works of mercy today and tomorrow, and on the third day my work will be complete.
sentences.susu: A naxa e yaabi, «Wo siga, wo sa a fala na xulumase kɔɔtaxi bɛ, n na ɲinnɛe kerife mixie fɔxɔ ra, n na mixie rayalanfe, to a nun tina. Xi saxan nde ma, n gɛma nɛ n ma wali ra.

sentences.english: But I have to go on my way today and tomorrow and the third day, for it is not right for a prophet to come to his death outside Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ fo n xa n ɲɛrɛ to, tina nun tina bora, barima a mu lanma tan namiɲɔnmɛ xa faxa fo Darisalamu.»

sentences.english: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, putting to death the prophets, and stoning those who were sent to her! again and again would I have taken your children to myself, as a bird takes her young ones under her wings, but you would not!
sentences.susu: «Darisalamu, Darisalamu, taa naxan namiɲɔnmɛe faxama, naxan Ala xa xɛɛrae magɔnɔma. Sanmaya wuyaxi n bara wa i xa die malanfe n yire, alɔ tɔxɔɛ a xa die rasoma a gabutenyi bun ma ki naxɛ, kɔnɔ wo naxa tondi!

sentences.english: Now see, your house is waste, and I say to you, You will not see me again till you say, A blessing on him who comes in the name of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Ala bara keli wo xa banxi xun ma. N xa a fala wo bɛ, wo mu n toma sɔnɔn, han wo a falama tɛmui naxɛ, ‹Baraka na a bɛ naxan fafe Marigi xili ra!›»

sentences.english: And it came about that when he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees on the Sabbath, to have a meal, they were watching him.
sentences.susu: Malabu lɔxɔ nde ma, Isa to nu a dɛgefe Farisɛni kuntigi nde xɔnyi, e birin nu Isa rabɛnfe nɛ.

sentences.english: And a certain man was there who had a disease.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ nde nu na naa naxan fate nu mafuntuxi.

sentences.english: And Jesus, answering, said to the scribes and Pharisees, Is it right to make people well on the Sabbath or not?
sentences.susu: Na kui, Isa naxa Farisɛnie nun sɛriyɛ lɔnnilae maxɔrin, «A daxa ka a mu daxa furema xa rayalan malabu lɔxɔɛ ma?»

sentences.english: But they said nothing. And he made him well and sent him away.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e mu sese fala. Isa naxa a bɛlɛxɛ sa furema ma, a a rayalan, a a ragbilen a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Which of you, whose ox or ass has got into a water-hole, will not straight away get him out on the Sabbath?
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, Isa man naxa e maxɔrin, «Xa a sa li go, wo xa di, xa na mu wo xa ninge bara bira gulunba ra malabu lɔxɔɛ ma, wo mu a ratema xɛ keren na?»

sentences.english: And they had no answer to that question.
sentences.susu: E mu nɔ na yaabi yo fide.

sentences.english: And he gave teaching in the form of a story to the guests who came to the feast, when he saw how they took the best seats; saying to them,
sentences.susu: Isa to a rakɔrɔsi xɔɲɛe nu magorode fanyie nan tongoma e yɛtɛ bɛ, a naxa yi taali wɔyɛnyi fala e bɛ,

sentences.english: When you get a request to come to a feast, do not take the best seat, for a more important man than you may be coming,
sentences.susu: «Mixi na i xili a xa xulunyi, i naxa magorode fanyi fen, barima xa mixi fa naxan tide gbo i bɛ,

sentences.english: And then the giver of the feast will come to you and say, Give your place to this man; and you, with shame, will have to take the lowest seat.
sentences.susu: i yatigi a falama nɛ i bɛ, ‹I xa dɔxɔse so na mixi binye yi ra.› Na kui, i kelima nɛ yaagi ra sigafe dɔxɔse gbɛtɛ fende, binyɛ mu na dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: But when you come, go and take the lowest seat, so that when the giver of the feast comes, he may say to you, Friend, come up higher; and then you will have honour in the eyes of all the others who are there.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi na i xili a xa xulunyi, i xa magorode binyɛtare nan tongo. Na kui, xa i yatigi bara fa, a a falama nɛ i bɛ, ‹N boore, sa magorode fanyi nan tongo yare.› Na findima binyɛ nan na i bɛ mixie birin ya ma wo nun naxee dɔxɔxi naa.

sentences.english: For every man who gives himself a high place will be put down, but he who takes a low place will be lifted up.
sentences.susu: Naxan yo na a yɛtɛ igbo, a fama nɛ igorode. Naxan yo na a yɛtɛ magoro, a xa fe itema nɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said to the master of the house, When you give a feast, do not send for your friends and your brothers and your family or your neighbours who have wealth, for they may give a feast for you, and so you will get a reward.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala xulunyi kanyi bɛ, «Xa a li i xulunyi tima, i naxa i booree, i baribooree, i barenyie, nun i dɔxɔboore bannaxie gbansan xa xili, barima e nɔma nɛ i xa wali fanyi birin nagbilende i ma.

sentences.english: But when you give a feast, send for the poor and the blind and those who are broken in body:
sentences.susu: Donse fanyie na rafala i xɔnyi, a lanma i xa setaree, mabɛnyie, namatɛe, nun dɔnxuie nan xili e xa fa e dɛge.

sentences.english: And you will have a blessing, because they will not be able to give you any payment, and you will get your reward when the upright come back from the dead.
sentences.susu: Na kui, i findima sɛɛwatɔɛ nan na, barima fɛɛrɛ mu e tan bɛ e xa i xa na fe fanyi ragbilen i ma, kɔnɔ i fama nɛ a sare sɔtɔde mixi tinxinxie rakelima faxɛ ma lɔxɔ naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And, hearing these words, one of those who were at table with him said to him, Happy is the man who will be a guest in the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ nde Isa nun naxan nu a dɛgefe, a to na fe mɛ, a naxa a fala a bɛ, «Sɛɛwɛ na mixi bɛ naxan fama a dɛgede Ala xɔnyi ariyanna!»

sentences.english: And he said to them, A certain man gave a great feast, and sent word of it to a number of people.
sentences.susu: Isa fan naxa a masen a bɛ, «Xɛmɛ nde naxa mixi gbegbe rakolon, a e xa fa a xɔnyi, e xa e dɛge a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: And when the time had come, he sent his servants to say to them, Come, for all things are now ready.
sentences.susu: A tɛmui to a li, a naxa a xa konyi xɛɛ mixie xilide, yi fe binyɛ nu bara ragbilen naxee ma, a xa a fala, ‹Wo fa, fe birin bara gɛ yailande.›

sentences.english: And they all gave reasons why they were not able to come. The first said to him, I have got a new field, and it is necessary for me to go and see it: I am full of regret that I am unable to come.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e birin naxa e yɛtɛ maxandi. A singe naxɛ, ‹N baxi xɛ nan sarade, fo n xa sa a mato. Diɲɛ n bɛ.›

sentences.english: And another said, I have got some cattle, and I am going to make a test of them: I am full of regret that I am unable to come.
sentences.susu: Boore fan naxɛ, ‹N baxi ninge firin dɔxɔ suuli nan sarade, fo n xa sa e mato. Diɲɛ n bɛ.›

sentences.english: And another said, I have been married, and so I am not able to come.
sentences.susu: Gbɛtɛ fan naxɛ, ‹N baxi ginɛ nan dɔxɔde. N mu nɔma fade.›»

sentences.english: And the servant came back and gave his master an account of these things. Then the master of the house was angry and said to the servant, Go out quickly into the streets of the town and get the poor, the blind, and those who are broken in body.
sentences.susu: «Konyi to gbilen a marigi xɔnyi, a naxa na fee dɛntɛgɛ sa a bɛ. Na kui, banxi kanyi naxa xɔnɔ, a a fala a xa konyi bɛ, ‹Siga mafuren, i sa setaree, mabɛnyie, dɔnxuie, nun namatɛe xili naxee na taa kui yire birin. I xa fa e ra n xɔnyi be.›»

sentences.english: And the servant said, Lord, your orders have been done, and still there is room.
sentences.susu: «Konyi man to gbilen a naxa a fala, ‹Marigi, n bara i xa yaamari raba, kɔnɔ han ya dɔxɔde luxi i xa banxi kui.›

sentences.english: And the lord said to the servant, Go out into the roads and the fields, and make them come in, so that my house may be full.
sentences.susu: Banxi kanyi naxa a fala a xa konyi bɛ, ‹I man xa mini, i sa taa fari yire birin isa. I xa fe birin naba mixie xa fa, n ma banxi xa rafe.

sentences.english: For I say to you that not one of those who were requested to come will have a taste of my feast.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala i bɛ, mixi naxee singe xilixi, e tan sese mu e dɛgema n xɔnyi feo!›»

sentences.english: Now a great number of people went with him.
sentences.susu: Isa man to nu kira ra, ɲama gbegbe nu a fɔxɔ ra. A naxa a ya rafindi e ma, a a masen e bɛ,

sentences.english: And turning round, he said to them, If any man comes to me, and has not hate for his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even for his life, he may not be my disciple.
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi wa birafe n fɔxɔ ra, fo a xa n xanu nɛ dangi a baba ra, a nga ra, a taara ra, a xunya ra, a xa ginɛ ra, a xa die ra, nun a yɛtɛ yati fan na. Xa na mu a ra, a kanyi mu nɔma findide n fɔxirabirɛ ra.

sentences.english: Whoever does not take up his cross and come after me may not be my disciple.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi mu a yɛtɛ waxɔnfe gere, a fa tin n waxɔnfe ra, a mu nɔma findide n fɔxirabirɛ ra.»

sentences.english: For which of you, desiring to put up a tower, does not first give much thought to the price, if he will have enough to make it complete?
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi nde sa wa koore banxi xungbe tife wo ya ma, fo a xa dɔxɔ nɛ sinden, a a mato kɔbiri xasabi naxan nɔma na banxi tide, alako a xa a kolon xa a xa fɛɛrɛ nɔma na wali raɲɔnde.

sentences.english: For fear that if he makes a start and is not able to go on with it to the end, all who see it will be laughing at him,
sentences.susu: Xa na mu a ra, a kanyi na banxi kɔɔrin a mu fa nɔ a raɲɔnde, mixie nu na to, e a mayelema nɛ,

sentences.english: And saying, This man made a start at building and is not able to make it complete.
sentences.susu: e a fala, ‹Yi xɛmɛ bara banxi ti fɔlɔ, kɔnɔ a mu nɔxi a raɲɔnde.›»

sentences.english: Or what king, going to war with another king, will not first take thought if he will be strong enough, with ten thousand men, to keep off him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
sentences.susu: «Xa mangɛ nde wa minife e nun mangɛ gbɛtɛ xa gere, fo a xa dɔxɔ nɛ sinden, a a maɲɔxun xa a xa sɔɔri mixi wulu fu nɔma tide mangɛ boore xa sɔɔri mixi wulu mɔxɔɲɛn kanke.

sentences.english: Or while the other is still a great distance away, he sends representatives requesting conditions of peace.
sentences.susu: Xa a bara a kolon a e mu nɔma, beemanun mangɛ boore nun a xa sɔɔrie xa makɔrɛ, a xɛɛra nan nasigama a ma alako lanyi nan xa xiri e tagi.

sentences.english: And so whoever is not ready to give up all he has may not be my disciple.
sentences.susu: Na kui, xa mixi yo na wo ya ma naxan mu nɔma mɛɛde fe birin na n tan ma fe ra, a kanyi mu nɔma findide n fɔxirabirɛ ra.»

sentences.english: For salt is good, but if the taste goes from it, of what use is it?
sentences.susu: «Fɔxɛ fan, kɔnɔ xa fɔxɛ mɛxɛmɛxɛnyi bara ba, a fa mɛxɛmɛxɛnma di?

sentences.english: It is no good for the land or for the place of waste; no one has a use for it. He who has ears, let him give ear.
sentences.susu: A mu fan xɛ bɛ, a mu fan ɲaɲɛ ra. A wɔlɛma nɛ tun. Xa naxan tuli fe mɛma, a xa a tuli mati yi masenyi ra.»

sentences.english: Now all the tax-farmers and sinners came near to give ear to him.
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde, duuti maxilie nun yunubitɔɛe birin nu e makɔrɛfe Isa ra e xa e tuli mati a ra.

sentences.english: And the Pharisees and scribes were angry, saying, This man gives approval to sinners, and takes food with them.
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie nun sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe naxa so a mafalafe, e nu a fala, «Yi xɛmɛ yunubitɔɛe rasɛnɛma, a man a dɛgema e xɔnyi.»

sentences.english: And he made a story for them, saying,
sentences.susu: Na kui, Isa naxa yi taali wɔyɛnyi masen e bɛ,

sentences.english: What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if one of them gets loose and goes away, will not let the ninety-nine be in the waste land by themselves, and go after the wandering one, till he sees where it is?
sentences.susu: «Xa mixi nde na wo ya ma, yɛxɛɛ kɛmɛ na naxan yi ra, keren fa lɔɛ e tagi, a mu yɛxɛɛ tongo solomanaani nun solomanaani luma e dɛmadonde, a siga na kerenyi fende han a sa a to?

sentences.english: And when he has got it again, he takes it in his arms with joy.
sentences.susu: A na a to, a ɲɛlɛxinma nɛ ki fanyi, a a sa a tunkie ma.

sentences.english: And when he gets back to his house, he sends for his neighbours and friends, saying to them, Be glad with me, for I have got back my sheep which had gone away.
sentences.susu: A na so a xɔnyi, a a xanuntenyie nun a dɔxɔbooree xilima nɛ, a a fala e bɛ, ‹Wo fa, won birin xa sɛɛwa, barima n bara n ma yɛxɛɛ to, naxan nu bara lɔɛ!›

sentences.english: I say to you that even so there will be more joy in heaven when one sinner is turned away from his wrongdoing, than for ninety-nine good men, who have no need of a change of heart.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n xa a fala wo bɛ, sɛɛwɛ gboma nɛ ariyanna yunubitɔɛ tuubixi keren xa fe ra, dangife tinxintɔɛ tongo solomanaani nun solomanaani ra naxee hayi mu tuubi ma.»

sentences.english: Or what woman, having ten bits of silver, if one bit has gone from her hands, will not get a light, and go through her house, searching with care till she sees it?
sentences.susu: «Xa a sa li gbeti kɔbiri kole fu na ginɛ nde yi ra, keren fa lɔɛ a yi, a mu lanpui radɛxɛma xɛ, a banxi makɔ, a na kɔbiri kole fen han a a to?

sentences.english: And when she has it again, she gets her friends and neighbours together, saying, Be glad with me, for I have got back the bit of silver which had gone from me.
sentences.susu: A na a to, a a xanuntenyie nun a dɔxɔbooree xilima nɛ, a a fala e bɛ, ‹Wo fa, won birin xa sɛɛwa, barima n bara n ma gbeti kɔbiri kole to naxan nu bara lɔɛ n ma!›

sentences.english: Even so, I say to you, There is joy among the angels of God, when one sinner is turned away from his wrongdoing.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n xa a fala wo bɛ, sɛɛwɛ na Ala xa malekɛe xɔnyi yunubitɔɛ keren gbansan tuubife ma.»

sentences.english: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a masen, «Xɛmɛ nde nu na, di xɛmɛ firin nu naxan yi ra.

sentences.english: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me that part of your property which will be mine. And he made division of his goods between them.
sentences.susu: A xa di firin nde naxa a fala a baba bɛ, ‹Won ma denbaya harige sɛɛti so n yi ra, naxan lanma a xa findi n gbe ra.› Na kui, babɛ naxa a harige itaxun a xa di xɛmɛ firinyie ma.»

sentences.english: And not long after, the younger son got together everything which was his and took a journey into a far-away country, and there all his money went in foolish living.
sentences.susu: «A mu bu di firin nde naxa a xa se birin malan, a fa biyaasi ɲamanɛ makuye. A naxa a harige makana mɛnni, fuyanteya kui.

sentences.english: And when everything was gone, there was no food to be had in that country, and he was in need.
sentences.susu: A birin to ɲɔn, kaamɛ fan naxa sin na ɲamanɛ ma a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra, sese mu lu na di yi ra.

sentences.english: And he went and put himself into the hands of one of the people of that country, and he sent him into his fields to give the pigs their food.
sentences.susu: A to siga wali fende naaka nde xɔn, na naxa a xɛɛ xɔsɛe dɛmadonde.

sentences.english: And so great was his need that he would have been glad to take the pigs' food, and no one gave him anything.
sentences.susu: Wuri bogi naxan nu soma xɔsɛe yi, a tan nu wama na nan donfe, kɔnɔ mixi yo mu tin a kide nde ra.»

sentences.english: But when he came to his senses, he said, What numbers of my father's servants have bread enough, and more, while I am near to death here through need of food!
sentences.susu: «Na kui, a naxa xaxili sɔtɔ fa, a a fala a yɛtɛ bɛ, ‹N baba xa walikɛ birin lugama a fanyi ra, e donse dɔnxɔɛ lu, a fa li n tan na faxafe kaamɛ nan na be!

sentences.english: I will get up and go to my father, and will say to him, Father, I have done wrong, against heaven and in your eyes:
sentences.susu: Fo n xa gbilen n baba xɔnyi, n xa a fala a bɛ, N baba, n bara yunubi sɔtɔ Ala ra, n bara haakɛ sɔtɔ i fan na.

sentences.english: I am no longer good enough to be named your son: make me like one of your servants.
sentences.susu: A mu daxa sɔnɔn n xa findi i xa di ra. I xa n findi i xa walikɛ nan na.›

sentences.english: And he got up and went to his father. But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with pity for him and went quickly and took him in his arms and gave him a kiss.
sentences.susu: A naxa keli, a siga a baba xɔn.» «Beenun a xa naa li, a baba naxa sa a to fa ra, a makuyaxi a ra sinden. A baba naxa kinikini ki fanyi. A naxa a gi, a sa a xa di ralan, a a masunbu.

sentences.english: And his son said to him, Father, I have done wrong, against heaven and in your eyes: I am no longer good enough to be named your son.
sentences.susu: Di naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹N baba, n bara yunubi sɔtɔ Ala ra, n bara haakɛ sɔtɔ i fan na. A mu daxa sɔnɔn n xa findi i xa di ra.›»

sentences.english: But the father said to his servants, Get out the first robe quickly, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet:
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ a baba naxa a fala a xa konyie bɛ, ‹Wo wo xulun, wo fa guba fanyi ra, wo a ragoro a ma. Wo bɛlɛxɛrasoe so a bɛlɛxɛ ra, wo sankiri so a sanyi.

sentences.english: And get the fat young ox and put it to death, and let us have a feast, and be glad.
sentences.susu: Wo fa ninge turaxi ra, wo a faxa. Won xa won dɛge, won xa xulunyi ti,

sentences.english: For this, my son, who was dead, is living again; he had gone away from me, and has come back. And they were full of joy.
sentences.susu: barima n ma yi di nu bara lu alɔ a nu faxaxi nɛ, kɔnɔ a nii man bara gbilen a i. A nu bara lɔɛ, kɔnɔ a man bara to.› Na kui, e naxa xulunyi ti fɔlɔ.»

sentences.english: Now the older son was in the field: and when he came near the house, the sounds of music and dancing came to his ears.
sentences.susu: «Na waxati, di singe nu na xɛ ma. A to nu sofe, a a makɔrɛ banxi ra, a naxa xulunyi xui mɛ.

sentences.english: And he sent for one of the servants, questioning him about what it might be.
sentences.susu: A naxa konyi nde xili, a a maxɔrin, ‹Munse rabaxi yi ki?›

sentences.english: And he said to him, Your brother has come; and your father has had the young ox put to death because he has come back safely.
sentences.susu: Na naxa a yaabi, ‹I xunya nan faxi. I baba bara ninge turaxi faxa, barima a man bara a xa di masɔtɔ a yalanxi.›

sentences.english: But he was angry and would not go in; and his father came out and made a request to him to come in.
sentences.susu: Di singe naxa xɔnɔ, a tondi sode banxi. A baba naxa mini, a so a mayandife,

sentences.english: But he made answer and said to his father, See, all these years I have been your servant, doing your orders in everything: and you never gave me even a young goat so that I might have a feast with my friends:
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ a xa di naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹A mato, kabi ɲɛ wuyaxi n tan walima i bɛ alɔ i xa konyi, n mu i xa yaamari matandi hali keren. Kɔnɔ na birin kui, hali si lanma, i mu nu a fi n ma, muxu nun n booree xa xulun di ti.

sentences.english: But when this your son came, who has been wasting your property with bad women, you put to death the fat young ox for him.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i xa di tan to faxi, naxan i harige birin makanaxi e nun langoe ginɛe ra, i ninge turaxi nan faxaxi a tan bɛ!›»

sentences.english: And he said to him, Son, you are with me at all times, and all I have is yours.
sentences.susu: «A baba naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹N ma di, i tan na n fɛ ma tɛmui birin. Se naxan birin na n yi, i tan nan gbe a ra.

sentences.english: But it was right to be glad and to have a feast; for this your brother, who was dead, is living again; he had gone away and has come back.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a lan nɛ won xa sɛɛwa, won xulunyi ti, barima i xunya nu bara lu alɔ a nu faxaxi nɛ, kɔnɔ a nii man bara gbilen a i. A nu lɔɛxi nɛ, kɔnɔ a man bara to.›»

sentences.english: And another time he said to the disciples, There was a certain man of great wealth who had a servant; and it was said to him that this servant was wasting his goods.
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Xɛmɛ bannaxi nde nu bara a xa fe birin taxu a xa walikɛ xunmati ra, a xa a raɲɛrɛ. Lɔxɔ nde, a naxa a mɛ, a na walikɛ xunmati nu na a harige makanafe.

sentences.english: And he sent for him and said, What is this which is said about you? give me an account of all you have done, for you will no longer be the manager of my property.
sentences.susu: A naxa a xili, a a maxɔrin, ‹N nanse mɛxi i xa fe ra? I xa i xa wali dɛntɛgɛ sa n bɛ, barima n bara xunmati wali ba i yi ra.›

sentences.english: And the servant said to himself, What am I to do now that my lord takes away my position? I have not enough strength for working in the fields, and I would be shamed if I made requests for money from people in the streets.
sentences.susu: Walikɛ xunmati naxa a fala a yɛtɛ bɛ, ‹N munse rabama fa? N ma mangɛ bara n namini walide. Sɛnbɛ mu n yi n xa siga yire buxade, n man yaagima nɛ kulɛ matide.

sentences.english: I have come to a decision what to do, so that when I am put out of my position they will take me into their houses.
sentences.susu: N bara fa a kolon n naxan nabama, alako n ma wali na ba n yi, mixie xa nu n nasɛnɛ e xɔnyi.›»

sentences.english: And sending for every one who was in debt to his lord he said to the first, What is the amount of your debt to my lord?
sentences.susu: «A naxa a marigi xa donitie birin xili keren keren yi ra. Naxan singe fa, a naxa a maxɔrin, ‹N marigi xa yeri na i ma?›

sentences.english: And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said, Take your account straight away and put down fifty.
sentences.susu: Na naxa a yaabi, ‹Oliwi ture sunbui ya kɛmɛ.› Walikɛ xunmati naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹I xa i xa kɛɛdi tongo mafuren, dɔxɔ, i a sɛbɛ tongo suuli.›

sentences.english: Then he said to another, What is the amount of your debt? And he said, A hundred measures of grain. And he said to him, Take your account and put down eighty.
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, a naxa a fala gbɛtɛ bɛ, ‹I tan go? Yeri na i ma?› Na naxa a yaabi, ‹Maale busali wulu keren.› A naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹I fan xa kɛɛdi tongo, i xa a sɛbɛ kɛmɛ solomasaxan.›

sentences.english: And his lord was pleased with the false servant, because he had been wise; for the sons of this world are wiser in relation to their generation than the sons of light.
sentences.susu: Na kui, na walikɛ xunmati tinxintare xa mangɛ naxa a matɔxɔ, a to kɔɔta rabaxi.» «Yi duniɲa mixi naxee ɲɛrɛma dimi kui, e kɔɔta e booree mabiri, dangife mixie ra naxee ɲɛrɛma naiyalanyi kui.

sentences.english: And I say to you, Make friends for yourselves through the wealth of this life, so that when it comes to an end, you may be taken into the eternal resting-places.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, wo xa dɛfanɲa fen yi duniɲa tinxintare xa naafuli saabui ra. Na naafuli na ɲɔn, wo fama rasɛnɛde banxie kui naxee mu kanama abadan.»

sentences.english: He who is true in a little, is true in much; he who is false in small things, is false in great.
sentences.susu: «Naxan mu lanlanteya kanama fe xurudi kui, a mu lanlanteya kanama fe xungbe fan kui. Naxan mu tinxin fe xurudi kui, a mu tinxinma fe xungbe fan kui.

sentences.english: If, then, you have not been true in your use of the wealth of this life, who will give into your care the true wealth?
sentences.susu: Xa wo bara lanlanteya kana yi duniɲa tinxintare xa naafuli fe kui, nde fa lama wo ra a xa ariyanna bannaya taxu wo ra?

sentences.english: And if you have not been true in your care of the property of other people, who will give you that which is yours?
sentences.susu: Xa wo bara lanlanteya kana se taxuxi xa fe kui, nde fa wo gbe soma wo yi?»

sentences.english: No man may be a servant to two masters: for he will have hate for the one and love for the other; or he will keep to the one and have no respect for the other. You may not be servants of God and of wealth.
sentences.susu: «Konyi yo mu nɔma lude marigi firin xa yaamari bun ma, barima a fama marigi keren xɔnde, a boore maxanu. A xirima nɛ keren na, a boore rabolo. Wo mu nɔma Ala nun naafuli rabatude.»

sentences.english: And the Pharisees, who had a great love of money, hearing these things, were making sport of him.
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie, kɔbiri nu rafanxi naxee ma, e fan naxa e tuli mati na fe birin na, e nu Isa mayele.

sentences.english: And he said, You take care to seem right in the eyes of men, but God sees your hearts: and those things which are important in the opinion of men, are evil in the eyes of God.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo wama wo yɛtɛ masenfe tinxintɔɛe nan na adamadie ya i, kɔnɔ Ala wo bɔɲɛ ma fe kolon. Naxan tide gbo mixie bɛ, Ala na xɔnxi.»

sentences.english: The law and the prophets were till John: but then came the preaching of the kingdom of God, and everyone makes his way into it by force.
sentences.susu: «Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa Kitaabuie nan kawandi han Yaya xa waxati. Keli na tɛmui ma, Ala xa mangɛya niini xa xibaaru fanyi nan kawandima fa, mixie fe birin nan nabafe, alako e xa so Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: But heaven and earth will come to an end before the smallest letter of the law may be dropped out.
sentences.susu: Koore nun bɔxi lɔɛma nɛ beenun sigirɛ keren xa ba Ala xa sɛriyɛ ra.»

sentences.english: Everyone who puts away his wife and takes another, is a false husband: and he who is married to a woman whose husband has put her away, is no true husband to her.
sentences.susu: «Xɛmɛ yo mɛɛ a xa ginɛ ra, a sa gbɛtɛ dɔxɔ, a kanyi bara yɛnɛ raba. Naxan na ginɛ dɔxɔ xɛmɛ bara mɛɛ naxan na, a fan bara yɛnɛ raba.»

sentences.english: Now there was a certain man of great wealth, who was dressed in fair clothing of purple and delicate linen, and was shining and glad every day.
sentences.susu: «Xɛmɛ bannaxi nde nu na, naxan nu luma a maxiri ra dugi sare xɔrɔxɔɛe ra. Tɛmui birin, a nu xulunyi nan tife. Lɔxɔ yo lɔxɔ, a nu lugama donse ɲɔxunmɛ nan na.

sentences.english: And a certain poor man, named Lazarus, was stretched out at his door, full of wounds,
sentences.susu: Misikiinɛ nde nu saxi yi banna xa tɛtɛ sode dɛ ra, naxan nu xili Lasaru. Suurie nu na a fate birin ma.

sentences.english: Desiring the broken bits of food which came from the table of the man of wealth; and even the dogs came and put their tongues on his wounds.
sentences.susu: A nu wama donse xuntunyi ndee nan sɔtɔfe naxee nu birama na banna xa teebili ra. A to nu saxi naa, baree nan nu fama a yire, e nu a xa suurie makɔn.»

sentences.english: And in time the poor man came to his end, and angels took him to Abraham's breast. And the man of wealth came to his end, and was put in the earth.
sentences.susu: «Lɔxɔ nde misikiinɛ naxa laaxira, malekɛe naxa sa a xanin Annabi Iburahima yire. Na banna xɛmɛ fan naxa faxa, a ragata,

sentences.english: And in hell, being in great pain, lifting up his eyes he saw Abraham, far away, and Lazarus on his breast.
sentences.susu: a siga yahannama. A xa ɲaxankatɛ kui mɛnni, a naxa a ya rate a sa Annabi Iburahima to yire makuye, e nun Lasaru.

sentences.english: And he gave a cry and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus, so that he may put the end of his finger in water and put it on my tongue, for I am cruelly burning in this flame.
sentences.susu: A naxa a xui ramini, ‹N baba Iburahima, kinikini n ma! Yandi, Lasaru xɛɛ n yire, a xa a bɛlɛxɛsole rasin ye xɔɔra, a n nɛnyi maxinbeli, barima n na yi tɛ naxan xɔɔra, a n ɲaxankatafe a ɲaaxi ra!›»

sentences.english: But Abraham said, Keep in mind, my son, that when you were living, you had your good things, while Lazarus had evil things: but now, he is comforted and you are in pain.
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ Annabi Iburahima naxa a yaabi, ‹N ma di, i xa i ratu, i tan bara fe fanyi sɔtɔ i xa duniɲɛigiri kui, kɔnɔ Lasaru tan tɔɔrɛ nan sɔtɔ. Yakɔsi, a tan bara madundu be, i tan na ɲaxankatafe.

sentences.english: And in addition, there is a deep division fixed between us and you, so that those who might go from here to you are not able to do so, and no one may come from you to us.
sentences.susu: Sa na birin xun, gulunba belebele nan saxi won tagi, alako mixi naxa nɔ kelide be sigafe ra i yire, mixi man naxa nɔ kelide mɛnni girife ra muxu fan yire.›»

sentences.english: And he said, Father, it is my request that you will send him to my father's house;
sentences.susu: «Na kui, banna naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹Awa n baba, n bara i mayandi, i xa Lasaru xɛɛ n baba xɔnyi,

sentences.english: For I have five brothers; and let him give them an account of these things, so that they may not come to this place of pain.
sentences.susu: barima xunya suuli nan na n bɛ. A xa sa e rasi, alako e naxa fa be, yi ɲaxankatɛ ma.›

sentences.english: But Abraham said, They have Moses and the prophets; let them give ear to what they say.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Annabi Iburahima naxa a yaabi, ‹Annabi Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa Kitaabuie na e yi. E xa e tuli mati nee xa masenyie ra.›

sentences.english: And he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone went to them from the dead, their hearts would be changed.
sentences.susu: Banna naxa a fala, ‹N baba Iburahima, na mu sɔɔnɛyama, kɔnɔ xa mixi nde keli faxamixie ya ma sigafe ra e xɔn, e tuubima nɛ.›

sentences.english: And he said to him, If they will not give attention to Moses and the prophets, they will not be moved even if someone comes back from the dead.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Annabi Iburahima naxa a masen a bɛ, ‹Xa e mu Annabi Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xui ramɛma, hali mixi keli faxɛ ma, e mu lama a ra.›»

sentences.english: And he said to his disciples, It is necessary for causes of trouble to come about, but unhappy is he by whom they come.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Maratantanyi fafe mu kanama, kɔnɔ ɲaxankatɛ na mixi bɛ naxan findima na saabui ra.

sentences.english: It would be well for him if a great stone was put round his neck and he was dropped into the sea, before he made trouble for any of these little ones.
sentences.susu: A fisa na kanyi bɛ gɛmɛ binye xa xiri a kɔnyi ra, a rasin baa ma, beemanun a xa yi mixi xuri keren natantan.

sentences.english: Give attention to yourselves: if your brother does wrong, say a sharp word to him; and if he has sorrow for his sin, let him have forgiveness.
sentences.susu: Wo mɛɛni wo yɛtɛ ma de!» «Xa i ngaxakerenyi bara haakɛ sɔtɔ i ra, wɔyɛn a bɛ. Xa a tuubi, i xa diɲɛ a ma.

sentences.english: And if he does you wrong seven times in a day, and seven times comes to you and says, I have regret for what I have done; let him have forgiveness.
sentences.susu: Xa a haakɛ sɔtɔ i mabiri sanmaya solofere lɔxɔɛ keren bun, a tuubixi man gbilen i madiɲɛde sanmaya solofere, fo i xa diɲɛ a ma.»

sentences.english: And the twelve said to the Lord, Make our faith greater.
sentences.susu: Xɛɛrae naxa a fala Marigi bɛ, «Muxu xa danxaniya xun masa!»

sentences.english: And the Lord said, If your faith was only as great as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this tree, Be rooted up and planted in the sea; and it would be done.
sentences.susu: Marigi naxa e yaabi, «Xa danxaniya na wo bɛ nu, hali a xurun alɔ yɛntɛn xɔri, wo nɔma nɛ a falade yi konde bili bɛ, ‹Tala be, i sa sin baa ma,› a wo xui rabatuma nɛ.»

sentences.english: But which of you, having a servant who is ploughing or keeping sheep, will say to him, when he comes in from the field, Come now and be seated and have a meal,
sentences.susu: «Xa a sa li konyi na mixi nde yi wo tagi, na konyi na keli yire buxade xa na mu xurusee dɛmadonde, a kanyi nɔma a falade a bɛ keren na, ‹Fa, i fa i magoro, i i dɛge›?

sentences.english: Will he not say, Get a meal for me, and make yourself ready and see to my needs till I have had my food and drink; and after that you may have yours?
sentences.susu: Ade, wo a falama a bɛ, ‹N ma donse rafala. I xa i xa donma masara alako i xa fa donse nun ye ra n bɛ. I na gɛ na ra, i fan nɔma i dɛgede.›

sentences.english: Does he give praise to the servant because he did what was ordered?
sentences.susu: Mixi mu a xa konyi tantuma yaamari rabatufe ma.

sentences.english: In the same way, when you have done all the things which are given you to do, say, There is no profit in us, for we have only done what we were ordered to do.
sentences.susu: Wo tan fan, wo na gɛ fe birin nabade wo yamarixi naxan na, wo xa a fala nɛ, ‹Konyi nan tun na muxu ra. Muxu muxu xa wali gbansan nan nabaxi.›»

sentences.english: And it came about that when they were on the way to Jerusalem he went through Samaria and Galilee.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu Darisalamu kira xɔn, a naxa dangi Samari nun Galile bɔxi tagi.

sentences.english: And when he went into a certain small town he came across ten men who were lepers, and they, keeping themselves at a distance,
sentences.susu: A to so taa nde kui, kunɛ kanyi fu naxa fa a xɔn. E naxa sa ti e ndedi makuyaxi a ra,

sentences.english: Said, in loud voices, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
sentences.susu: e e xui ite a bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ Isa, kinikini muxu ma!»

sentences.english: And when he saw them he said, Go, and let the priests see you. And, while they were going, they were made clean.
sentences.susu: A to e to, a naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo siga, wo sa wo yɛtɛ masen sɛrɛxɛdubɛe bɛ.» Na kui, e nu sigafe tɛmui naxɛ, e naxa yalan.

sentences.english: And one of them, when he saw that he was clean, turning back, gave praise to God in a loud voice;
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, mixi keren e ya ma, a to a to a yalanxi, a naxa gbilen Ala matɔxɔ ra a xui itexi ra.

sentences.english: And, falling down on his face at the feet of Jesus, he gave the credit to him; and he was a man of Samaria.
sentences.susu: A naxa suyidi Isa bɛ, a a tantu. Samarika nan nu a ra.

sentences.english: And Jesus said, Were there not ten men who were made clean? where are the nine?
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala a bɛ, «Mixi fu xa mu rayalan? Na solomanaanie tan go?

sentences.english: Have not any of them come back to give glory to God, but only this one from a strange land?
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu gbilen Ala tantude fo yi Samarika?»

sentences.english: And he said to him, Get up, and go on your way; your faith has made you well.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a fala a bɛ, «Keli, i siga. I xa danxaniya bara i rakisi.»

sentences.english: And when the Pharisees put questions to him about when the kingdom of God would come, he gave them an answer and said, The kingdom of God will not come through observation:
sentences.susu: Farisɛnie to Isa maxɔrin, a Ala xa mangɛya niini fama mun tɛmui, a naxa e yaabi, «Mixi mu Ala xa mangɛya niini fa tɛmui kolonma.

sentences.english: And men will not say, See, it is here! or, There! for the kingdom of God is among you.
sentences.susu: Mixie mu a falama xɛ de, ‹A mato, a tan nan ya,› xa na mu a ra, ‹A tan nan sa na ki›, barima Ala xa mangɛya niini na wo ya ma nɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said to his disciples, The time will come when you will have a great desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, but you will not see it.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui, Isa naxa a fala a fɔxirabirɛe bɛ, «Waxati fama nɛ, Adama xa Di to xɔli wo suxuma nɛ, a xa lu wo ya ma hali lɔxɔ keren peti, kɔnɔ wo mu a toma.

sentences.english: And if they say to you, See, it is there! or, It is here! do not go away, or go after them.
sentences.susu: Mixie a falama nɛ wo bɛ, ‹A mato, a tan nan sa na ki,› xa na mu a ra, ‹A tan nan yi ki!› Wo naxa wo gi na matode, wo naxa bira nee fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: For as in a thunderstorm the bright light is seen from one end of the sky to the other, so will the Son of man be when his time comes.
sentences.susu: A fa lɔxɔɛ, Adama xa Di luma nɛ alɔ seyamakɔnyi naxan minima, kuye birin yanba.

sentences.english: But first, he will have to undergo much and be put on one side by this generation.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ beenun na lɔxɔɛ xa a li, fo a xa tɔɔrɛ gbegbe sɔtɔ. To mixie mu lama a ra.

sentences.english: And as it was in the days of Noah, so will it be in the day of the Son of man.
sentences.susu: Adama xa Di fa lɔxɔɛ luma nɛ alɔ Annabi Nuha xa waxati.

sentences.english: They were feasting and taking wives and getting married, till the day of the overflowing of the waters, when Noah went into the ark, and they all came to destruction.
sentences.susu: Mixie nu e dɛgema, e nu e minma, e nu ginɛe dɔxɔma, e nu e xa die fima xɛmɛe ma, han Annabi Nuha so kunkui kui lɔxɔ naxɛ. Banbaranyi belebele to din bɔxi ma, e birin naxa sɔntɔ.

sentences.english: In the same way, in the days of Lot; they were feasting and trading, they were planting and building;
sentences.susu: Na nan man naba Loti xa waxati. Mixie nu e dɛgema, e nu e minma, e nu sare matima, e nu sansi sima, e nu banxie tima.

sentences.english: But on the day when Lot went out of Sodom, fire came down from heaven and destruction came on them all.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Loti keli Sodoma lɔxɔ naxɛ, tɛ nun sooda ye nu goroma nɛ kelife koore ma alɔ tunɛ, birin naxa sɔntɔ.

sentences.english: So will it be in the day of the revelation of the Son of man.
sentences.susu: A man sa rabama na ki nɛ Adama xa Di na makɛnɛn lɔxɔ naxɛ.»

sentences.english: On that day, if anyone is on the roof of the house, and his goods are in the house, let him not go down to take them away; and let him who is in the field not go back to his house.
sentences.susu: «Na lɔxɔɛ, naxan na tande, a naxa so a harige tongode banxi kui. Naxan na xɛ ma, a fan naxa gbilen a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: Keep in mind Lot's wife.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu nɛ Loti xa ginɛ ma.

sentences.english: If anyone makes an attempt to keep his life, it will be taken from him, but if anyone gives up his life, he will keep it.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo katafe a yɛtɛ ratangade, na kanyi lɔɛma nɛ, kɔnɔ mixi yo a yɛtɛ ralɔɛma, na kanyi ratangama nɛ.

sentences.english: I say to you, In that night there will be two men sleeping in one bed, and one will be taken away and the other let go.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, na tɛmui ma, xa mixi firin saxi sade keren ma kɔɛ ra, mixi keren tongoma nɛ, boore lu naa.

sentences.english: Two women will be crushing grain together; one will be taken away and the other let go.
sentences.susu: Xa ginɛ firin na se dinfe mulunyi keren kui, keren tongoma nɛ, boore lu naa.»
<range>

sentences.english: And they, answering him, said, Where, Lord? And he said to them, Where the body is, there will the eagles come together.
sentences.susu: E naxa a maxɔrin, «Marigi, na rabama minden?» A naxa e yaabi, «Binbi na lu dɛnnaxɛ, yubɛe sa e malanma mɛnni nɛ.»

sentences.english: And he made a story for them, the point of which was that men were to go on making prayer and not get tired;
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, Isa naxa yi taali wɔyɛnyi masen e bɛ e xa a kolon a fo e xa Ala maxandi tɛmui birin tunnabɛxi kui.

sentences.english: Saying, There was a judge in a certain town, who had no fear of God or respect for man:
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen, «Kiitisa nde nu na taa nde kui, naxan mu nu gaaxuma Ala ya ra, a gbe fe man mu nu mixi yo xa fe ma.

sentences.english: And there was a widow in that town, and she kept on coming to him and saying, Give me my right against the man who has done me wrong.
sentences.susu: Kaaɲɛ ginɛ nde fan nu na na taa kui, naxan nu luma fa ra kiitisa xɔn, a nu a fala, ‹Kiiti tinxinxi sa n tan nun n yaxui tagi.›

sentences.english: And for a time he would not: but later, he said to himself, Though I have no fear of God or respect for man,
sentences.susu: A naxa bu na ki, kiitisa mu tin a bɛ, kɔnɔ lɔxɔ nde a naxa a fala a yɛtɛ bɛ, ‹Nɔndi na a ra, n tan mu gaaxuma Ala ya ra, n gbe fe man mu mixi yo xa fe ma.

sentences.english: Because this widow is a trouble to me, I will give her her right; for if not, I will be completely tired out by her frequent coming.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yi kaaɲɛ ginɛ tan na n bɔɲɛ raɲaaxufe n ma. N xa kiiti tinxinxi so a yi ra, alako a xa ba fafe n xɔn, a naxa fa n tɔɔrɔ.›»

sentences.english: And the Lord said, Give ear to the words of the evil judge.
sentences.susu: Na kui, Marigi naxa a masen, «Wo yi kiitisa kobi xui ramɛ.

sentences.english: And will not God do right in the cause of his saints, whose cries come day and night to his ears, though he is long in doing it?
sentences.susu: Ala mu kiiti tinxinxi soma xɛ a xa mixi sugandixie yi ra, naxee a maxandima kɔɛ nun yanyi? A buma e malife ra?

sentences.english: I say to you that he will quickly do right in their cause. But when the Son of man comes, will there be any faith on earth?
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, a kiiti tinxinxi soma e yi ra mafuren. Kɔnɔ Adama xa Di na fa, a danxaniya lima nɛ duniɲa ma?»

sentences.english: And he made this story for some people who were certain that they were good, and had a low opinion of others:
sentences.susu: Isa man naxa yi taali wɔyɛnyi masen mixi ndee bɛ naxee nu laxi e yɛtɛ ra, a tinxintɔɛe nan na e tan na dangi booree ra e yoxi naxee ma.

sentences.english: Two men went up to the Temple for prayer; one a Pharisee, and the other a tax-farmer.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen, «Xɛmɛ firin naxa siga Ala maxandide hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui. Keren nu findixi Farisɛni nan na, boore, duuti maxili.

sentences.english: The Pharisee, taking up his position, said to himself these words: God, I give you praise because I am not like other men, who take more than their right, who are evil-doers, who are untrue to their wives, or even like this tax-farmer.
sentences.susu: Farisɛni naxa ti, a Ala maxandi a bɔɲɛ ma, a nu a i, ‹Ala, n bara i tantu barima n mu luxi alɔ mixi gbɛtɛe, naxee findixi muɲɛtie, fe kobi rabae, nun yɛnɛlae ra. N bara i tantu barima n mu luxi alɔ yi duuti maxili.

sentences.english: Twice in the week I go without food; I give a tenth of all I have.
sentences.susu: N sunma sanmaya firin lɔxun keren bun ma, n man farilɛ fima n sɔtɔse birin na.›

sentences.english: The tax-farmer, on the other hand, keeping far away, and not lifting up even his eyes to heaven, made signs of grief and said, God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ duuti maxili tan naxa ti a xati ma. A ɲan mu nu suusama a xa a ya rate koore ma. A nu a bɛlɛxɛ saxi a kanke ma, a nu a fala, ‹Ee, Ala! Kinikini n ma, barima yunubitɔɛ nan n na!›»

sentences.english: I say to you, This man went back to his house with God's approval, and not the other: for everyone who makes himself high will be made low and whoever makes himself low will be made high.
sentences.susu: «N xa a fala wo bɛ, yi mixi firin to gbilen e xɔnyi, na duuti maxili nan nu tinxinxi Ala ya i, barima mixi yo a yɛtɛ igbo, a kanyi fama nɛ igorode. Kɔnɔ mixi naxan a yɛtɛ magoroma, a xa fe itema nɛ.»

sentences.english: And they took their children to him, so that he might put his hands on them: but when the disciples saw it, they said sharp words to them
sentences.susu: Mixie nu fafe dimɛdie ra Isa xɔn, alako a xa a bɛlɛxɛ sa e ma. A fɔxirabirɛe to na to, e naxa wɔyɛn na mixie ma.

sentences.english: But Jesus sent for them, saying, Let the children come to me, and do not keep them away, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa e xili, a a masen e bɛ, «Wo a lu dimɛdie xa fa n yire. Wo naxa tɔnyi dɔxɔ e ma, barima naxee maniyaxi e ra, e tan nan soma Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.

sentences.english: Truly I say to you, Whoever does not put himself under the kingdom of God like a little child, will not come into it at all.
sentences.susu: N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, mixi naxan mu tinma Ala xa mangɛya niini ra alɔ dimɛdi, na kanyi mu soma Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma feo!»

sentences.english: And a certain ruler put a question to him, saying, Good Master, what have I to do so that I may have eternal life?
sentences.susu: Mangɛ nde naxa Isa maxɔrin, «Karamɔxɔ fanyi, a lan n xa munse raba alako n xa abadan kisi sɔtɔ kɛ ra?»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to him, Why do you say that I am good? No one is good, but only God.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen a bɛ, «Munfe ra i n xilima karamɔxɔ fanyi? Mixi yo mu fan. Ala keren peti nan fan.

sentences.english: You have knowledge of what the law says: Do not be untrue to your wife, Do not put anyone to death, Do not take what is not yours, Do not give false witness, Give honour to your father and mother.
sentences.susu: I sɛriyɛ kolon: ‹I naxa yɛnɛ raba. I naxa faxɛ ti. I naxa muɲɛ ti. I naxa mixi tɔɔɲɛgɛ. I baba nun i nga binya.›»

sentences.english: And he said, All these things I have done from the time when I was a boy.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa Isa yaabi, «N bara na birin nabatu kafi n dimɛdi tɛmui.»

sentences.english: And Jesus, hearing it, said to him, One thing you still have need of; get money for your goods, and give it away to the poor, and you will have wealth in heaven; and come after me.
sentences.susu: Isa to na mɛ, a naxa a fala a bɛ, «Fe keren nan fa luxi i xa fe. Siga, se naxan birin na i yi ra, sa a mati, i a kɔbiri fi setaree ma. Na kui, i fama bannaya sɔtɔde ariyanna. I na na raba, fa, i bira n fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: But at these words he became very sad, for he had great wealth.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a to na mɛ, a naxa sunnun, barima a nu bannaxi ki fanyi.

sentences.english: And Jesus, looking at him, said, How hard it is for those who have wealth to get into the kingdom of God!
sentences.susu: Isa to a sunnunxi to, a naxa a masen a bɛ, «Sofe Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma, a xɔrɔxɔ naafuli kanyie bɛ ki fanyi!

sentences.english: It is simpler for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a man who has much money to come into the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: Ɲɔxɔmɛ so ɲɔxun sɛnbɛ yale ra, dinɛ bannamixi sofe ra Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma.»

sentences.english: And those who were present said, Then who may have salvation?
sentences.susu: Mixi naxee a xui mɛ, e naxa a maxɔrin, «Nde fa nɔma kiside?»

sentences.english: But he said, Things which are not possible with man are possible with God.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «Mixie mu nɔma naxan na, Ala tan nɔma na ra.»

sentences.english: And Peter said, See, we have given up what is ours to come after you.
sentences.susu: Piyɛri naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «A mato, muxu bara keli muxu xa se birin xun ma, muxu bira i fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: And he said to them, Truly I say to you, There is no man who has given up house or wife or brothers or father or mother or children, because of the kingdom of God,
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «N xa nɔndi fala wo bɛ, mixi yo naxan na keli a xa se nde xun ma Ala xa mangɛya niini xa fe ra, a findi banxi ra ba, ginɛ ba, ngaxakerenyie ba, barimae ba, die ba,

sentences.english: Who will not get much more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.
sentences.susu: na kanyi a ɲɔxɔɛ wuyaxi sɔtɔma nɛ yi duniɲa ma, a man fa abadan kisi sɔtɔ aligiyama.»

sentences.english: And he took with him the twelve and said to them, Now we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things which were said by the prophets will be done to the Son of man.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a xa xɛɛra fu nun firinyie xun lan, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo a mato, won na tefe Darisalamu nɛ yi ki. Namiɲɔnmɛe fe naxee sɛbɛxi Adama xa Di xa fe ra, a birin fama nɛ kamalide naa.

sentences.english: For he will be given up to the Gentiles, and will be made sport of and put to shame:
sentences.susu: A sama nɛ kaafirie bɛlɛxɛ, e a mayele, e a konbi, e dɛye bɔxun a ma.

sentences.english: And he will be given cruel blows and put to death, and on the third day he will come back to life.
sentences.susu: E na gɛ a bɔnbɔde sɛbɛrɛ ra, e a faxama nɛ, kɔnɔ a xa faxɛ xi saxan nde, a man kelima nɛ faxɛ ma.»

sentences.english: But they did not take in the sense of any of these words, and what he said was not clear to them, and their minds were not able to see it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa fɔxirabirɛe mu na sese fahaamu. Na masenyi bara findi wɔyɛnyi nɔxunxi ra e bɛ, e mu naxan kui kolon.

sentences.english: And it came about that when he got near Jericho, a certain blind man was seated by the side of the road, making requests for money from those who went by.
sentences.susu: Isa to makɔrɛ Yeriko ra, dɔnxui nde nu dɔxɔxi kira dɛ ra kulɛ matide.

sentences.english: And hearing the sound of a great number of people going by, he said, What is this?
sentences.susu: A to ɲama xui mɛ kira ra, a naxa maxɔrinyi ti, «Munse rabaxi?»

sentences.english: And they said to him, Jesus of Nazareth is going by.
sentences.susu: E naxa a fala a bɛ, «Isa Nasarɛtika nan dangife.»

sentences.english: And he said in a loud voice, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a naxa gbelegbele, «Isa, Dawuda xa Di, kinikini n ma!»

sentences.english: And those who were in front made protests and said to him, Be quiet: but he said all the more, O Son of David, have mercy on me.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxee nu yare, e naxa wɔyɛn a ma a a xa sabari, kɔnɔ a tan ɲan naxa so a xui itefe dangi singe ra, «Dawuda xa Di, kinikini n ma!»

sentences.english: And Jesus, stopping, gave orders that he was to come to him, and when he came near, he said to him,
sentences.susu: Isa naxa ti, a a fala mixie bɛ e xa fa dɔnxui ra a xɔn. Dɔnxui to a maso a ra, Isa naxa a maxɔrin,

sentences.english: What would you have me do for you? And he said, Lord, that I may be able to see again.
sentences.susu: «I wama n xa munse raba i bɛ?» A naxa a yaabi, «Marigi, n wama n ya xa se to.»

sentences.english: And Jesus said, See again: your faith has made you well.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen a bɛ, «Se to. I xa danxaniya bara i rayalan.»

sentences.english: And straight away he was able to see, and he went after him, giving glory to God; and all the people when they saw it gave praise to God.
sentences.susu: A ya naxa se to keren na, a fa bira Isa fɔxɔ ra Ala matɔxɔ ra. Ɲama birin to na to, e fan naxa Ala matɔxɔ.

sentences.english: And he went into Jericho, and when he was going through it,
sentences.susu: Isa to so Yeriko, a nu taa iɲɛrɛfe.

sentences.english: A man, named Zacchaeus, who was the chief tax-farmer, and a man of wealth,
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ nde nu na naxan nu xili Sakɛyɛ. Duuti maxilie kuntigi nan nu a ra, a bannaxi.

sentences.english: Made an attempt to get a view of Jesus, and was not able to do so, because of the people, for he was a small man.
sentences.susu: A nu katafe nɛ a xa Isa kolon, kɔnɔ a mu nu nɔma a tode ɲama xa fe ra, barima mixi dunke nan nu a ra.

sentences.english: And he went quickly in front of them and got up into a tree to see him, for he was going that way.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a naxa a gi yare, a sa te wuri bili kɔn na alako a xa Isa to dangi ra.

sentences.english: And when Jesus came to the place, looking up, he said to him, Zacchaeus, be quick and come down, for I am coming to your house today.
sentences.susu: Isa to a yire li, a naxa a ya rate, a a fala a bɛ, «Sakɛyɛ, goro mafuren, barima n sa yigiyama i xɔnyi nɛ to.»

sentences.english: And he came down quickly, and took him into his house with joy.
sentences.susu: Sakɛyɛ naxa a xulun gorode, a Isa rasɛnɛ ɲɛlɛxinyi kui.

sentences.english: And when they saw it, they were all angry, saying, He has gone into the house of a sinner.
sentences.susu: Mixie to na to, e birin naxa so Isa mafalafe, e nu a fala, «A bara sa yigiya yunubitɔɛ xɔnyi.»

sentences.english: And Zacchaeus, waiting before him, said to the Lord, See, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone wrongly, I give him back four times as much.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Sakɛyɛ naxa ti, a a fala Isa bɛ, «Marigi, n bara natɛ tongo, n xa n sɔtɔse tagi fima nɛ fuxarilae ma. Xa a sa li n bara se ba naxan yi funmaya ra, n a ragbilenma nɛ a kanyi ma dɔxɔ naani.»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, for even he is a son of Abraham.
sentences.susu: Isa fan naxa a masen a xa fe ra, «Yi fɔxɔɛ bara kisi sɔtɔ to, barima Iburahima xa di nan na yi xɛmɛ fan na.

sentences.english: For the Son of man came to make search for those who are wandering from the way, and to be their Saviour.
sentences.susu: Adama xa Di bara fa a xa mixi lɔɛxie fen, a xa e rakisi.»

sentences.english: And while they were giving ear to these words, he made another story for them, because he was near Jerusalem, and because they were of the opinion that the kingdom of God was coming straight away.
sentences.susu: Isa to nu bara makɔrɛ Darisalamu ra, ɲama ɲɔxɔ nu a ma, a Ala xa mangɛya niini fafe makɛnɛnde nɛ keren na. Na kui, mixie to nu Isa xui ramɛfe, a naxa yi taali wɔyɛnyi masen e bɛ.

sentences.english: So he said, A certain man of high birth went into a far-away country to get a kingdom for himself, and to come back.
sentences.susu: «Kuntigi nde naxa sa biyaasi yire makuye, alako mangɛ xungbe naxan nu sabatixi naa, a xa a tan kuntigi xɔnyi mangɛya so a yi, a man xa gbilen a xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And he sent for ten of his servants and gave them ten pounds and said to them, Do business with this till I come.
sentences.susu: Beenun a xa siga, a naxa a xa konyi mixi fu xili, a gbeti kɔbiri kole kɛmɛ so e birin yi ra, a fa a fala e bɛ, ‹Wo yulɛya raba yi kɔbiri ra beenun n fa tɛmui.›»

sentences.english: But his people had no love for him, and sent representatives after him, saying, We will not have this man for our ruler.
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ a to mu nu rafanxi a xɔnyi mixi ndee ma, e fan naxa xɛɛrae xɛɛ mangɛ xungbe ma, e xa a fala, ‹Muxu mu wama a xɔn yi xɛmɛ xa findi mangɛ ra muxu xun ma.›»

sentences.english: And when he came back again, having got his kingdom, he gave orders for those servants to whom he had given the money to come to him, so that he might have an account of what business they had done.
sentences.susu: «Na xɛmɛ to mangɛya sɔtɔ, a naxa gbilen a xɔnyi. A naxa yaamari fi na konyie xa xili, a nu bara kɔbiri so naxee yi, alako a xa a kolon e geeni naxan sɔtɔxi yulɛya kui.

sentences.english: And the first came before him, saying, Lord, your pound has made ten pounds.
sentences.susu: Konyi singe naxa fa, a dɛntɛgɛ sa, a naxɛ, ‹N marigi, i i xa gbeti kɔbiri kole kɛmɛ naxan so nɛ n yi, a ɲɔxɔɛ dɔxɔ fu bara sa a xun geeni ra.›

sentences.english: And he said to him, You have done well, O good servant: because you have done well in a small thing you will have authority over ten towns.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a fala a bɛ, ‹I nuwali! Konyi fanyi nan i ra! I to mu lanlanteya kana fe xuri kui, n bara mangɛya so i yi taa fu xun ma.›»

sentences.english: And another came, saying, Your pound has made five pounds.
sentences.susu: «Konyi firin nde naxa fa, a dɛntɛgɛ sa, a naxɛ, ‹N Marigi, i i xa gbeti kɔbiri kole kɛmɛ naxan so nɛ n yi, a ɲɔxɔɛ dɔxɔ suuli bara sa a xun geeni ra.›

sentences.english: And he said, You will be ruler over five towns.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a fala na fan bɛ, ‹N bara mangɛya so i fan yi taa suuli xun ma!›»

sentences.english: And another came, saying, Lord, here is your pound, which I put away in a cloth;
sentences.susu: «Konyi gbɛtɛ fan naxa fa, a dɛntɛgɛ sa, a naxɛ, ‹N marigi, a mato, i xa gbeti kɔbiri kole kɛmɛ nan ya. N sa a ragata dunkobi nan kui,

sentences.english: Because I was in fear of you, for you are a hard man: you take up what you have not put down, and get in grain where you have not put seed.
sentences.susu: barima n gaaxu nɛ i ya ra. Xɛmɛ nan i ra, i xa fe maxɔrɔxɔ. I se tongoma i gbe mu naxan na. I xɛ xabama i mu naxan garansan.›

sentences.english: He said to him, By the words of your mouth you will be judged, you bad servant. You had knowledge that I am a hard man, taking up what I have not put down and getting in grain where I have not put seed;
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa a yaabi, ‹I tan konyi kobi, n i makiitima i yɛtɛ kan xui nan yati ma! A di, i mu a fala a i nu a kolon a n ma fe maxɔrɔxɔ? I naxɛ, a n se tongoma n gbe mu naxan na, n xɛ xabama n mu naxan garansan.

sentences.english: Why then did you not put my money in a bank, so that when I came I would get it back with interest?
sentences.susu: Munfe a to i mu n ma kɔbiri so kɔbiri rawalie yi ra, alako n na fa, i a ragbilen n ma geeni saxi a xun?›

sentences.english: And he said to the others who were near, Take the pound away from him, and give it to the man who has ten.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala mixie bɛ naxee nu tixi na, ‹Wo na gbeti kɔbiri kole kɛmɛ rasuxu a yi, wo a so boore yi naxan gbeti kɔbiri kole wulu keren sɔtɔxi.›

sentences.english: And they say to him, Lord, he has ten pounds.
sentences.susu: E naxa a fala mangɛ bɛ, ‹Marigi, gbeti kɔbiri kole wulu keren ɲan na a yi!›

sentences.english: And I say to you that to everyone who has, more will be given, but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
sentences.susu: A naxa e yaabi, ‹N xa a fala wo bɛ, a na naxan yo yi ra, a gbe xun masama nɛ. Kɔnɔ a mu na naxan yi ra, hali naxan di na a yi, na yati bama nɛ a yi ra.

sentences.english: And as for those who were against me, who would not have me for their ruler, let them come here, and be put to death before me.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n yaxuie tan, naxee mu nu wama n xa findi mangɛ ra e xun ma, wo fa e ra be, wo e faxa n ya xɔri.›»

sentences.english: And when he had said this, he went on in front of them, going up to Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Isa to gɛ na masenyi ra, a naxa siga yare, sigafe ra Darisalamu.

sentences.english: And it came about that when he got near Beth-phage and Bethany by the mountain which is named the Mountain of Olives, he sent two of the disciples,
sentences.susu: A to makɔrɛ Betifage nun Betani taae ra, Oliwi geya fɛ ma, a naxa a fɔxirabirɛe mixi firin xɛɛ,

sentences.english: Saying, Go into the little town in front of you, and on going in you will see a young ass fixed with a cord, on which no man has ever been seated; let him loose and take him.
sentences.susu: a a fala e bɛ, «Wo xa so taa kui naxan na yare. Wo nɛfɛ so naa, wo sofale lanma lima a xirixi naa, mixi mu nu dɔxɔ naxan fari. Wo xa a fulun, wo fa a ra be.

sentences.english: And if anyone says to you, Why are you taking him? say, The Lord has need of him.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde fa wo maxɔrin, ‹Wo a fulunfe munfe ra› wo xa a yaabi, ‹Marigi nan hayi na a ma.›»

sentences.english: And those whom he sent went away, and it was as he said.
sentences.susu: E to siga xɛɛraya rabade, e naxa fe birin li alɔ Isa a fala e bɛ ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And when they were getting the young ass, the owners of it said to them, Why are you taking the young ass?
sentences.susu: E nu na sofale lanma fulunfe tɛmui naxɛ, a kanyie naxa e maxɔrin, «Wo yi sofale fulunfe munfe ra?»

sentences.english: And they said, The Lord has need of him.
sentences.susu: E naxa a masen, «Marigi nan hayi na a ma.»

sentences.english: And they took him to Jesus, and they put their clothing on the ass, and Jesus got on to him.
sentences.susu: E to sofale xanin Isa xɔn, e naxa e xa donmae sa a fari, e fa Isa mali a xa a magoro a ma.

sentences.english: And while he went on his way they put their clothing down on the road in front of him.
sentences.susu: A to nu sigama, mixie nu e xa donmae italama kira xɔn ma, Isa binyafe ra.

sentences.english: And when he came near the foot of the Mountain of Olives, all the disciples with loud voices gave praise to God with joy, because of all the great works which they had seen;
sentences.susu: A to nu makɔrɛfe Darisalamu ra, a gorofe Oliwi geya ra, a fɔxirabirɛ gali birin naxa sɛɛwa, e so Ala matɔxɔfe e xui itexi ra kaabanako birin xa fe ra e nu bara naxee to.

sentences.english: Saying, A blessing on the King who comes in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.
sentences.susu: E nu a falafe nɛ, «Baraka na Mangɛ bɛ naxan fafe Marigi xili ra! Bɔɲɛsa na ariyanna, matɔxɔɛ na Ala bɛ han koore ma!»

sentences.english: And some of the Pharisees among the people said to him, Master, make your disciples be quiet.
sentences.susu: Farisɛni nde naxee nu na ɲama tagi, e naxa a fala Isa bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, wɔyɛn i fɔxirabirɛe bɛ!»

sentences.english: And he said in answer, I say to you, if these men keep quiet, the very stones will be crying out.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa e yaabi, «N xa a fala wo bɛ, xa e tan e sabari, gɛmɛe yati fama nɛ e xui raminide.»

sentences.english: And when he got near and saw the town, he was overcome with weeping for it,
sentences.susu: Isa to makɔrɛ Darisalamu ra, a naxa na taa to, a naxa wa fɔlɔ naa xa fe ra,

sentences.english: Saying, If you, even you, had knowledge today, of the things which give peace! but you are not able to see them.
sentences.susu: a a masen, «I tan Darisalamu, to tan, hali i fan a kolon nɛ nu fee naxee bɔɲɛsa fima! Kɔnɔ na bara nɔxun i ma.

sentences.english: For the time will come when your attackers will put a wall round you, and come all round you and keep you in on every side,
sentences.susu: Tɛmui fama a lide, wo yaxuie bɛndɛ malanma nɛ taa tɛtɛ fari ma alako e xa nɔ sode taa kui. E fama wo rabilinde maraxɛtɛnyi ra.

sentences.english: And will make you level with the earth, and your children with you; and there will not be one stone resting on another in you, because you did not see that it was your day of mercy.
sentences.susu: E fama i tan Darisalamu rabirade, e i xa die sɔntɔ. I xa banxie tixi gɛmɛe naxee ra, keren mu luma a boore fari. Yi birin fama i tan Darisalamu lide barima Ala to faxi kisi ra i xɔn, i mu a kolonxi.»

sentences.english: And he went into the Temple and put out those who were trading there,
sentences.susu: Isa to so hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, a naxa sarematie keri fɔlɔ,

sentences.english: Saying to them, It has been said, My house is to be a house of prayer, but you have made it a hole of thieves.
sentences.susu: a a fala e bɛ, «A sɛbɛxi, ‹N ma banxi xili falama nɛ, salide banxi,› kɔnɔ wo tan bara a findi muɲɛtie dɔxɔde ra.»

sentences.english: And every day he was teaching in the Temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people were attempting to put him to death;
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ yo lɔxɔ Isa nu mixie kawandima hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie, sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe, nun ɲama yareratie nu na fɛɛrɛ fenfe e nɔma Isa faxade ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: But they were not able to do anything, because the people all kept near him, being greatly interested in his words.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e mu nu fɛɛrɛ yo kolon barima ɲama birin nu a tuli matixi a ra.

sentences.english: And it came about on one of those days, when he was teaching the people in the Temple and preaching the good news,
sentences.susu: Lɔxɔ nde, Isa to nu mixie kawandife hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, a nu Ala xa xibaaru fanyi masenfe e bɛ, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie, sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe, nun Yuwifie xa forie naxa fa a yire,

sentences.english: That the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people came to him and said, Make clear to us by what authority you do these things and who gave you this authority.
sentences.susu: e a maxɔrin, «A fala muxu bɛ, i yi fee rabama nde xa yaamari ma? Nde yi sɛnbɛ fixi i ma?»

sentences.english: And in answer he said to them, I will put a question to you, and do you give me an answer:
sentences.susu: A naxa e yaabi, «N fan xa wo maxɔrin fe keren ma. Wo a fala n bɛ,

sentences.english: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or of men?
sentences.susu: Yaya to nu mixie xunxama ye xɔɔra, Ala nan a xɛɛxi ba, ka adama?»

sentences.english: And they said among themselves, If we say, From heaven; he will say, Why did you not have faith in him?
sentences.susu: E fan naxa so wɔyɛnfe e bore tagi, «Xa won na a yaabi, ‹Ala,› a a falama nɛ won bɛ, ‹Munfe ra wo mu fa la a ra?›

sentences.english: But if we say, Of men; we will be stoned by the people, for they are certain that John was a prophet.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa won na a yaabi, ‹Adama,› ɲama birin won magɔnɔma nɛ e xa won faxa, barima e laxi a ra a namiɲɔnmɛ nan nu Yaya ra.»

sentences.english: And they made answer that they had no idea where it came from.
sentences.susu: Na kui, e naxa a yaabi a e mu a kolon naxan yo Yaya xɛɛxi.

sentences.english: And Jesus said, And I will not make clear to you by what authority I do these things.
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «N fan mu a falama wo bɛ n yi fee rabama naxan ma yaamari ma.»

sentences.english: And he gave the people this story: A man made a vine-garden and gave the use of it to some field-workers and went into another country for a long time.
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, Isa naxa so yi taali wɔyɛnyi masenfe ɲama bɛ. «Xɛmɛ nde naxa wɛni bilie si. A naxa na hɛri bɔxi rawalie ma, a fa biyaasi xɔnkuye ramini.

sentences.english: And at the right time he sent a servant to the workers to get part of the fruit from the vines; but the workmen gave him blows and sent him away with nothing.
sentences.susu: Wɛni bogi ba tɛmui to a li, bɔxi kanyi naxa konyi nde xɛɛ bɔxi rawalie xɔn ma, e xa wɛni bogi nde so a yi ra. Kɔnɔ bɔxi rawalie naxa na konyi bɔnbɔ, e a ragbilen a bɛlɛxɛ igeli ra.

sentences.english: And he sent another servant, and they gave blows to him in the same way, and put shame on him, and sent him away with nothing.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi kanyi man naxa konyi gbɛtɛ xɛɛ. E naxa na fan bɔnbɔ, e a konbi a mayaagixi ra, e a ragbilen a bɛlɛxɛ igeli ra.

sentences.english: And he sent a third, and they gave him wounds and put him out.
sentences.susu: Bɔxi kanyi naxa a saxan nde man xɛɛ. E naxa na fan maxɔnɔ, e a keri.»

sentences.english: And the lord of the garden said, What am I to do? I will send my dearly loved son; they may give respect to him.
sentences.susu: «Na kui, bɔxi kanyi naxa a fala, ‹N munse rabama fa? N xa n ma di maxanuxi nan xɛɛ. Tɛmunde, e fama na tan binyade.›

sentences.english: But when the workmen saw him, they said to one another, This is he who will one day be the owner of the property: let us put him to death and the heritage will be ours.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ bɔxi rawalie to a to, e naxa a fala e bore bɛ, ‹Yi nan na kɛ tongoma ra. Won na a faxa alako kɛ xa findi won gbe ra.›

sentences.english: And driving him out of the garden they put him to death. Now what will the lord do to these workmen?
sentences.susu: Bɔxi rawalie naxa a ramini bɔxi ra, e sa a faxa.» «Na bɔxi kanyi munse rabama fa?

sentences.english: He will come and put them to destruction and give the garden to others. And when he said this, they said, May it not be so.
sentences.susu: A sigama nɛ naa, a na bɔxi rawalie faxa, a a xa bɔxi so mixi gbɛtɛe yi.» Ɲama to na masenyi mɛ, e naxa a fala, «Astɔfulahi!»

sentences.english: But he, looking on them, said, Is it not in the Writings, The stone which the builders put on one side, the same has become the chief stone of the building?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa naxa a ya ti e ra, a e maxɔrin, «Yi naxan sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, a fa fasarima di? ‹Banxitie mɛɛ gɛmɛ naxan na, a bara findi tuxui gɛmɛ hagigɛ ra.›»

sentences.english: Everyone falling on that stone will be broken, but the man on whom the stone comes down will be crushed to dust.
sentences.susu: «Naxan birama na gɛmɛ ma, a igirama nɛ. Na gɛmɛ birama naxan ma, na fan butuxunma nɛ.»

sentences.english: And the chief priests and the scribes made attempts to get their hands on him in that very hour; and they were in fear of the people, for they saw that he had made up this story against them.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔe nun sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie naxa a kolon a Isa yi taali wɔyɛnyi masenxi e tan nan bɛ. E naxa kata e xa a suxu keren na, kɔnɔ e gaaxu ɲama nan ya ra.

sentences.english: And they kept watch on him, and sent out secret representatives, who were acting the part of good men, in order that they might get something from his words, on account of which they might give him up to the government and into the power of the ruler.
sentences.susu: E nu wama nɛ e xa a sa gomina bɛlɛxɛ, a xa lu a tan nan xa nɔɛ bun ma. Na kui, e naxa Isa rabɛn, e mixi ndee xɛɛ a yire e xa e yɛtɛ findi tinxintɔɛe ra, e xa sa Isa masɔtɔ a xa wɔyɛnyi kui.

sentences.english: And they put a question to him, saying, Master, we are certain that your teaching and your words are right, and that you have no respect for a man's position, but you are teaching the true way of God:
sentences.susu: Na kui, e naxa Isa maxɔrin yi masenyi ma, «Karamɔxɔ, muxu a kolon i xa masenyi tinxin. I mu mixi e rafisama e bore bɛ, i Ala xa kira masenma a nɔndi ki ma.

sentences.english: Is it right for us to make payment of taxes to Caesar or not?
sentences.susu: A lanma ka a mu lanma muxu xa duuti fi Rɔma mangɛ ma?»

sentences.english: But he saw through their trick and said to them,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa to nu e xa kɔɔta kolon, a naxa e yaabi,

sentences.english: Let me see a penny. Whose image and name are on it? And they said, Caesar's.
sentences.susu: «Wo gbeti kɔbiri kole masen n bɛ. Nde xili nun misaali na a ma?» E naxa a yaabi, «Rɔma Mangɛ.»

sentences.english: And he said, Then give to Caesar the things which are Caesar's, and to God the things which are God's.
sentences.susu: A naxa a masen e bɛ, «Wo mangɛ gbe ragbilen mangɛ ma, wo Ala fan gbe ragbilen Ala ma.»

sentences.english: And they were not able to get anything from these words before the people: but they were full of wonder at his answer, and said nothing.
sentences.susu: Nee fan mu nɔ a masɔtɔde a xa wɔyɛnyi kui, ɲama birin ya xɔri. Fo e to kaaba a xa yaabi ma, e sabari.

sentences.english: And some of the Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no coming back from the dead; and they said to him,
sentences.susu: Sadusenie, naxee a falama a faxamixie mu kelima faxɛ ma, e naxa fa yi maxɔrinyi ra Isa xɔn ma,

sentences.english: Master, Moses said that if a man's brother comes to his end, having a wife, but no children, his brother is to take the wife, and get a family for his brother.
sentences.susu: «Karamɔxɔ, Annabi Munsa yi nan sɛbɛxi muxu bɛ Kitaabui kui, ‹Xa xɛmɛ nde taara faxa, a naxa a xa ginɛ lu a mu di yo bari, a na xunya nan na ginɛ dɔxɔma, alako a xa bɔnsɔɛ fi a taara ma.›

sentences.english: Now there were seven brothers, and the first had a wife and came to his end, having no children;
sentences.susu: Na kui, xɛmɛ nde naxa di xɛmɛ solofere sɔtɔ. A xa di singe naxa ginɛ dɔxɔ, a faxa, a mu bɔnsɔɛ yo lu.

sentences.english: And the second;
sentences.susu: A xanbiratoe naxa na kaaɲɛ ginɛ tongo, kɔnɔ a fan naxa faxa.

sentences.english: And the third took her; and in the same way, all the seven, without having any children, came to their end.
sentences.susu: Na nan man naba na fan xanbiratoe ra, a nun na di solofere birin na. E birin naxa faxa, e sese mu bɔnsɔɛ lu.

sentences.english: And last of all, the woman came to her end.
sentences.susu: A dɔnxɔɛ ra, ginɛ fan naxa faxa.

sentences.english: When they come back from the dead, whose wife will she be? for all the seven had her.
sentences.susu: Na kui, marakeli lɔxɔɛ, na ginɛ to dɔxɔxi yi mixi solofere birin xɔn ma, a sa findima nde gbe ra?»

sentences.english: And Jesus said to them, The sons of this world are married and have wives;
sentences.susu: Isa naxa a masen e bɛ, «Yi duniɲɛigiri kui, xɛmɛ ginɛ dɔxɔma, ginɛ fan dɔxɔma xɛmɛ xɔn.

sentences.english: But those to whom is given the reward of the world to come, and to come back from the dead, have no wives, and are not married;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxee binyɛ sɔtɔma e xa keli faxɛ ma, e xa sa so waxati kui naxan sa fama, e tan xɛmɛe mu ginɛe dɔxɔma, ginɛe fan mu dɔxɔma xɛmɛe xɔn.

sentences.english: And death has no more power over them, for they are equal to the angels, and are sons of God, being of those who will come back from the dead.
sentences.susu: E mu faxama sɔnɔn, barima e luma nɛ alɔ malekɛe. E to bara keli faxɛ ma, e findima Ala xa die nan na.»

sentences.english: But even Moses made it clear that the dead come back to life, saying, in the story of the burning thorn-tree, The Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
sentences.susu: «Kɔnɔ a falafe tan, a faxamixie kelima faxɛ ma, Annabi Munsa yati na masen nɛ Kitaabui kui wuri bili xa fe falaxi dɛnnaxɛ, a to Marigi xili fala, ‹N tan nan na Marigi Alatala ra, Iburahima, Isiyaga, nun Yaxuba naxan batuma.›

sentences.english: Now he is not the God of the dead but of the living: for all men are living to him.
sentences.susu: Faxamixie xa mu Ala batuma, fo a mixi ɲiɲɛ. Mixi yo findi Ala batui ra, na kanyi ɲiɲɛ nan a ra.»

sentences.english: And some of the scribes, in answer to this, said, Master, you have said well.
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔ ndee naxa a fala a bɛ, «Karamɔxɔ, i xa masenyi fan,»

sentences.english: And they had fear of putting any more questions to him.
sentences.susu: barima Sadusenie mu suusa maxɔrinyi yo tide a ma sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: And he said to them, Why do they say that the Christ is the son of David?
