sentences.susu: Yuwifi nun Girɛkika naxee birin nu sabatixi Efɛsɛ, e naxa na fe kolon. Gaaxui naxa e birin suxu. Marigi Isa xili dariyɛ naxa mate.

sentences.english: And a number of those who had faith came and made a public statement of their sins and all their acts.
sentences.susu: Danxaniyatɔɛ wuyaxi naxa fa, e naxa e ti e xa yunubie ra, e naxa e xa fe ɲaaxi birin fala kɛnɛ ma.

sentences.english: And a great number of those who were experts in strange arts took their books and put them on the fire in front of everyone: and when the books were valued they came to fifty thousand bits of silver.
sentences.susu: Duuree fan naxa fa e xa bukie ra, e naxa e gan birin ya xɔri. E naxa bukie sare kɔnti, kɔbiri kole wulu tongo suuli nan nu a ra.

sentences.english: So the word of the Lord was increased very greatly and was full of power.
sentences.susu: Marigi xa masenyi nu yiriwama na ki nɛ sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: Now after these things were ended, Paul came to a decision that when he had gone through Macedonia and Achaia he would go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I have a desire to see Rome.
sentences.susu: Yi fee to dangi, Pɔlu naxa natɛ tongo a xa siga Darisalamu. Na biyaasi kui fo a xa Masedon nun Akayi bɔxi ibolon. A naxa a fala, «N na siga Darisalamu, fo n xa Rɔma fan li.»

sentences.english: And having sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, into Macedonia, he himself went on living in Asia for a time.
sentences.susu: A naxa a malima firin xɛɛ Masedon, Timote nun Erasito, kɔnɔ a tan naxa lu Asi sinden.

sentences.english: And about that time a great outcry took place about the Way.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui sɔnxɔɛ xungbe naxa raba naa Marigi xa kira xa fe ma.

sentences.english: For there was a certain man named Demetrius, a silver-worker, who made silver boxes for the images of Diana, and gave no small profit to the workmen;
sentences.susu: Xabui nde, naxan xili Demetiri, a nu ala Aritemi xa salide misaali lanmadi yailanma gbeti ra. Na xabui mɔɔlie nu kɔbiri gbegbe sɔtɔma na wali kui.

sentences.english: Whom he got together, with other workmen of the same trade, and said to them, Men, it is clear that from this business we get our wealth.
sentences.susu: A naxa a walibooree malan, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo a kolon, won baloxi yi wali nan kui.

sentences.english: And you see, for it has come to your ears, that not only at Ephesus, but almost all through Asia, this Paul has been teaching numbers of people and turning them away, saying that those are not gods who are made by men's hands:
sentences.susu: Wo bara a to, wo bara a mɛ, yi Pɔlu bara mixi gbegbe madaxu Asi bɔxi birin ma, Efɛsɛ gbansan xa mu a ra. A naxɛ a alae naxee rafalaxi mixie bɛlɛxɛ ra, a ala mu e ra.

sentences.english: And there is danger, not only that our trade may be damaged in the opinion of men, but that the holy place of the great goddess Diana may be no longer honoured, and that she to whom all Asia and the world give worship, will be put down from her high position.
sentences.susu: Na kui won ma wali fama nɛ xili ɲaaxi sɔtɔde. Won ma ala Aritemi xa salide fan xun nakanama nɛ. Nde bama nɛ Aritemi xa binyɛ ra Asi bɔxi nun duniɲa ma.»

sentences.english: And hearing this, they were very angry, crying out and saying, Great is Diana of Ephesus.
sentences.susu: A to na fala, e naxa xɔnɔ, e naxa so sɔnxɔɛ ratefe, «Efɛsɛkae xa ala Aritemi nan gbo.»

sentences.english: And the town was full of noise and trouble, and they all came running into the theatre, having taken by force Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia who were journeying in company with Paul.
sentences.susu: Taa birin ya naxa iso. E naxa Gayu nun Arisitaraki, Pɔlu ɲɛrɛboore Masedonkae, xanin malande xungbe kui.

sentences.english: And when Paul was about to go in to the people, the disciples did not let him.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa wa sigafe naa, kɔnɔ Isa fɔxirabirɛe mu tin.

sentences.english: And some of the rulers of Asia, being his friends, sent to him, requesting him seriously not to put himself in danger by going into the theatre.
sentences.susu: A booree Asikae xunmatie fan naxa xɛɛra ti Pɔlu ma, e a mayandi a naxa siga malan yire.

sentences.english: And some said one thing, and some another: for there was no order in the meeting; and most of them had no idea why they had come together.
sentences.susu: Ndee nu sɔnxɔma e gbe ki ma. Booree fan sɔnxɔma e gbe ki. Lantareya nu na malanyi ya ma. Mixi wuyaxi mu nu a kolon e malanxi fe naxan ma.

sentences.english: Then they took Alexander out from among the people, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander, making a sign with his hand, was about to make a statement to the people in answer:
sentences.susu: Awa, Yuwifie naxa Alesandire tutun yare a xa wɔyɛn. A naxa ɲama masabari a bɛlɛxɛ ra alako a xa masenyi ti.

sentences.english: But when they saw that he was a Jew, all of them with one voice went on crying out for about two hours, Great is Diana of Ephesus.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ, e to a kolon a Yuwifi nan a ra, e birin nalanxi naxa sɔnxɔɛ rate lɛɛri firin bun ma. E naxɛ, «Efɛsɛkae xa ala Aritemi nan gbo.»

sentences.english: And when the chief secretary had got the people quiet, he said, Men of Ephesus, is any man without knowledge that the town of Ephesus is the keeper of the holy place of the great Diana, who was sent down from Jupiter?
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, taa kuntigi nde naxa ɲama masabari, a naxa a fala, «Efɛsɛkae, duniɲa birin a kolon a Efɛsɛ taa nan Aritemi xa salide kantama a nun Aritemi maniyɛ, naxan goroxi keli koore ma.

sentences.english: So then, because these things may not be doubted, it would be better for you to be quiet, and do nothing unwise.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu na matandima. A lanma wo xa dundu. Wo naxa gbata fefe rabade.

sentences.english: For you have taken these men, who are not doing damage to the holy place or talking against our goddess.
sentences.susu: Wo bara fa yi mixie ra be, kɔnɔ e mu Aritemi muɲa, e mu a konbi.

sentences.english: If, then, Demetrius and the workmen who are with him have a protest to make against any man, the law is open to them, and there are judges; let them put up a cause at law against one another.
sentences.susu: Xa Demetiri nun a walibooree wama mixi nde kalamufe, e xa na masen kiitisae bɛ kiiti lɔxɔɛe.

sentences.english: But if any other business is in question, let it be taken up in the regular meeting.
sentences.susu: Xa wo wama fe gbɛtɛ nan xɔn, na fan ya ibama won ma malan lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: For, truly, we are in danger of being made responsible for this day's trouble, there being no cause for it: and we are not able to give any reason for this coming together.
sentences.susu: E nɔma won suxude won ma bɔɲɛte ma naxan dangixi to, barima nɔndi yo mu na won bɛ yi malanyi rabafe ma.» A to gɛ, a naxa malanyi rayensen.

sentences.english: And after the noise had come to an end, Paul, having sent for the disciples and given them comfort, went away from them to Macedonia.
sentences.susu: Sɔnxɔɛ to bara ɲɔn, Pɔlu naxa Isa fɔxirabirɛe malan e rasife ma. A to a ɲungu e ma, a naxa siga Masedon.

sentences.english: And when he had gone through those parts and given them much teaching, he came into Greece.
sentences.susu: A naxa na bɔxi isa, a nu Isa fɔxirabirɛe rasi marasi wuyaxi ra. Na dangi xanbi, a naxa siga Girɛki bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: And when he had been there three months, because the Jews had made a secret design against him when he was about to take ship for Syria, he made a decision to go back through Macedonia.
sentences.susu: A to lu naa kike saxan, a naxa wa sigafe Siriya kunkui kui, kɔnɔ Yuwifie nu bara yanfanteya yailan a xili ma. Na kui, a naxa natɛ tongo a xa gbilen Masedon kira ra.

sentences.english: And Sopater of Beroea, the son of Pyrrhus, and Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia, went with him as far as Asia.
sentences.susu: Naxee a mati han Asi nee nan yi ki: Sopateri, Beereka Pirusi xa di, Arisitaraki nun Sekondu Tɛsalonikikae, Gayu Deribeka nun Timote, Tikike nun Tirofimo Asikae.

sentences.english: But these had gone before, and were waiting for us at Troas.
sentences.susu: Nee naxa ti yare, e naxa sa muxu mamɛ Tiroyasi.

sentences.english: And we went away from Philippi by ship after the days of unleavened bread, and came to them at Troas in five days; and we were there for seven days.
sentences.susu: Taami Lɛbinitare Sali lɔxɔɛ dangi xanbi, muxu naxa baki kunkui kui Filipi. Beenun xi suuli, muxu naxa e li Tiroyasi. Muxu naxa lu naa xi solofere.

sentences.english: And on the first day of the week, when we had come together for the holy meal, Paul gave them a talk, for it was his purpose to go away on the day after; and he went on talking till after the middle of the night.
sentences.susu: Sande lɔxɔɛ muxu naxa malan taami igirafe ra. Pɔlu naxa kawandi ti Isa fɔxirabirɛe bɛ han kɔɛ tagi. A lan nɛ a xa siga kuye na iba.

sentences.english: And there were a number of lights in the room where we had come together.
sentences.susu: Lanpui gbegbe nu na na koore banxi kui, muxu nu malanxi dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And a certain young man named Eutychus, who was seated in the window, went into a deep sleep; and while Paul went on talking, being overcome by sleep, he had a fall from the third floor, and was taken up dead.
sentences.susu: Sɛgɛtala nde naxan xili Eyutiki nu dɔxɔxi wundɛri ra. Pɔlu xa kawandi xɔn to kuya, xi xɔli naxa a suxu a fanyi ra, a bira bɔxi ma kelife banxi dɛki saxan nde. E naxa a li, a bara faxa.

sentences.english: And Paul went down and, falling on him, took him in his arms and said, Do not be troubled, for his life is in him.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu to goro, a naxa a felen a xun. A naxa a tongo, a a fala e bɛ, «Wo naxa kɔntɔfili, barima a mu faxaxi.»

sentences.english: And when he had gone up, and had taken the broken bread, he went on talking to them for a long time, even till dawn, and then he went away.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu to te, a naxa taami igira, a naxa a don. A man naxa wɔyɛn han gɛɛsɛgɛ. Na gɛɛsɛgɛ, a naxa siga.

sentences.english: And they took the boy in, living, and were greatly comforted.
sentences.susu: Danxaniyatɔɛe naxa sɛgɛtala xanin a ɲiɲɛ ra bɔɲɛsa kui.

sentences.english: But we, going before him by ship, went to Assos with the purpose of taking Paul in there: for so he had given orders, because he himself was coming by land.
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa kunkui bɛla rakeli sigafe ra Asosi Pɔlu ya ra alɔ muxu lanxi a ma ki naxɛ. A naxa wa sigafe a sanyi ra.

sentences.english: And when he came up with us at Assos, we took him in the ship and went on to Mitylene.
sentences.susu: A to muxu li Asosi, muxu naxa a baki kunkui kui sigafe Mitilɛni.

sentences.english: And going from there by sea, we came on the day after opposite Chios, and touching at Samos on the day after that, we came on the third day to Miletus.
sentences.susu: Keli mɛnni, muxu naxa siga baa kira ra. Na fan kuye iba, muxu naxa Kiyo li. Na xanbi, muxu naxa siga han Samosi. Na lɔxɔɛ kuye iba, muxu naxa Mileto li.

sentences.english: For Paul's purpose was to go past Ephesus, so that he might not be kept in Asia; for he was going quickly, in order, if possible, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu nu bara natɛ tongo a xa dangi Efɛsɛ mabiri alako a naxa bu Asi bɔxi ma. A nu gbataxi a xa so Darisalamu Xɛ Xabɛ Sali lɔxɔɛ xa a sa sɔɔnɛyama a bɛ.

sentences.english: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus for the rulers of the church.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu to Mileto li, a naxa xɛɛra ti a Efɛsɛ danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama kuntigie xa fa.

sentences.english: And when they had come, he said to them, You yourselves have seen what my life has been like all the time from the day when I first came into Asia,
sentences.susu: E to fa a yire, a naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo a kolon n ɲɛrɛxi wo tagi ki naxɛ. Kabi n so Asi,

sentences.english: Doing the Lord's work without pride, through all the sorrow and troubles which came on me because of the evil designs of the Jews:
sentences.susu: n Marigi xa wali raba yɛtɛ magoroe nan kui. N yaye bara mini, n bara tɔɔrɔ Yuwifie xa wali ɲaaxi saabui ra.

sentences.english: And how I kept back nothing which might be of profit to you, teaching you publicly and privately,
sentences.susu: Wo a kolon a n mu wo munafan se yo nɔxun wo ma. N bara kawandi ti wo bɛ kɛnɛ ma nun wo xa banxie kui.

sentences.english: Preaching to Jews and to Greeks the need for a turning of the heart to God, and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.
sentences.susu: N nu a falama nɛ Yuwifie nun Girɛkikae bɛ e xa togondiya Ala ma, e xa danxaniya won Marigi Isa, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi ma.»

sentences.english: And now, as you see, I am going to Jerusalem, a prisoner in spirit, having no knowledge of what will come to me there:
sentences.susu: «Yakɔsi Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi wama nɛ n xa siga Darisalamu, kɔnɔ n mu a kolon naxan sigama n sɔtɔde naa.

sentences.english: Only that the Holy Spirit makes clear to me in every town that prison and pains are waiting for me.
sentences.susu: Taa birin kui Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi bara n nakolon a geeli nun tɔɔrɛ fama nɛ n lide naa.

sentences.english: But I put no value on my life, if only at the end of it I may see the work complete which was given to me by the Lord Jesus, to be a witness of the good news of the grace of God.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n nii tide yo mu na n bɛ. N xa n ma xɛɛraya rakamali, n Marigi Isa naxan taxuxi n na. N xa findi Ala xa hinnɛ seedeɲɔxɔya ba ra, naxan findixi xibaaru fanyi ra.»

sentences.english: And now I am conscious that you, among whom I have gone about preaching the kingdom, will not see my face again.
sentences.susu: «Yakɔsi n a kolon wo mu n yatagi toma sɔnɔn, wo tan naxee birin wo tuli matixi n ma kawandi ra, Ala xa mangɛya niini xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And so I say to you this day that I am clean from the blood of all men.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, n a falama wo bɛ to, wo xa kote yo mu na n xun,

sentences.english: For I have not kept back from you anything of the purpose of God.
sentences.susu: barima n bara Ala sago birin masen wo bɛ, n mu sese nɔxun wo ma.

sentences.english: Give attention to yourselves, and to all the flock which the Holy Spirit has given into your care, to give food to the church of God, for which he gave his blood.
sentences.susu: Awa, wo xa mɛɛni wo yɛtɛ ma a nun danxaniyatɔɛ birin, Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi wo findixi naxee xa xunmati ra, alako wo xa mɛɛni Marigi xa danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama ma, a naxan sɔtɔxi a yɛtɛ wuli ra. Wo xa e kanta alɔ xurusee dɛmadonyi gɔɔrɛ kantama ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: I am conscious that after I am gone, evil wolves will come in among you, doing damage to the flock;
sentences.susu: N na kolon, n na siga, mixi ɲaaxie fama nɛ sode wo tagi, alɔ wula baree soma gɔɔrɛ ya ma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And from among yourselves will come men who will give wrong teaching, turning away the disciples after them.
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee soma wo tagi, e xa xaranyi ɲaaxi ti alako e xa Isa fɔxirabirɛe bɛndun e ma.

sentences.english: So keep watch, having in mind that for three years without resting I was teaching every one of you, day and night, with weeping.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo mɛɛni. Wo xa ratu yi ɲɛ saxanyi bun ma n mu wo kawandife iti kɔɛ nun yanyi. N na birin nabaxi yaye nan kui.»

sentences.english: And now, I give you into the care of God and the word of his grace, which is able to make you strong and to give you your heritage among all the saints.
sentences.susu: «Awa yakɔsi, n wo taxuma Ala ra nun a xa hinnɛ masenyi ra, naxan nɔma sɛnbɛ nun kɛ fanyi fide sɛniyɛntɔɛ birin ma.

sentences.english: I have had no desire for any man's silver or gold or clothing.
sentences.susu: N mu nu wama wo xa kɔbiri xa xɔn, xa na mu a ra wo xa xɛɛma, wo xa sosee.

sentences.english: You yourselves have seen that with these hands I got what was necessary for me and those who were with me.
sentences.susu: Wo yɛtɛ yati a kolon a n wali yi bɛlɛxɛe nan na alako n xa balo n nun n ɲɛrɛbooree.

sentences.english: In all things I was an example to you of how, in your lives, you are to give help to the feeble, and keep in memory the words of the Lord Jesus, how he himself said, There is a greater blessing in giving than in getting.
sentences.susu: N bara a masen wo bɛ mɔɔli birin na, a won lan nɛ won xa wali alako won xa setaree mali. Wo xa ratu Marigi Isa xa wɔyɛnyi ma, a naxɛ, ‹Ɲɛlɛxinyi na ki nan kui, dangife a sɔtɔfe ra.›»

sentences.english: And having said these words, he went down on his knees in prayer with them all.
sentences.susu: A to gɛ wɔyɛnde, a naxa a xinbi sin, e birin naxa Ala maxandi.

sentences.english: And they were all weeping, falling on Paul's neck and kissing him,
sentences.susu: E birin naxa so wafe. E naxa findigilin Pɔlu kɔnyi ma, e a masunbu.

sentences.english: Being sad most of all because he had said that they would not see his face again. And so they went with him to the ship.
sentences.susu: E sunnun nɛ barima a bara a fala e mu nɔma a tode sɔnɔn. E naxa a mati han kunkui dɛ ra.

sentences.english: And after parting from them, we put out to sea and came straight to Cos, and the day after to Rhodes, and from there to Patara:
sentences.susu: Muxu to fatan, muxu naxa siga keren na Kosi kunkui kui. Na kuye iba, muxu naxa siga Rodi. Muxu to keli Rodi, muxu naxa siga Patara.

sentences.english: And as there was a ship going to Phoenicia, we went in it.
sentences.susu: Muxu to kunkui to naa, naxan nu baa igirife sigafe Fenisiya biri ra, muxu naxa baki na kui.

sentences.english: And when we had come in view of Cyprus, going past it on our left, we went on to Syria, and came to land at Tyre: for there the goods which were in the ship had to be taken out.
sentences.susu: Muxu to bara Sipiri suri to, muxu naxa dangi na ra kɔɔla ma, sigafe Siriya biri ra. Muxu naxa ti Tire alako kote xa ragoro.

sentences.english: And meeting the disciples we were there for seven days: and they gave Paul orders through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa Isa fɔxirabirɛe ndee li naa. Muxu naxa xi solofere radangi e xɔnyi. Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi naxa goro Isa fɔxirabirɛe ma, e xa a fala Pɔlu bɛ a naxa te Darisalamu.

sentences.english: And when these days came to an end, we went on our journey; and they all, with their wives and children, came with us on our way till we were out of the town: and after going on our knees in prayer by the sea,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xi solofere kamali lɔxɔɛ, muxu naxa kira tongo sigafe ra. E birin naxa muxu mati, a nun e xa ginɛe nun e xa die ra, han taa fari ma. Muxu naxa muxu xinbi sin baa dɛ ra Ala maxandife ra.

sentences.english: We said our last words to one another, and got into the ship, and they went back to their houses.
sentences.susu: Ɲungui to ɲɔn, muxu naxa baki kunkui kui. Booree tan naxa gbilen e xɔnyi.

sentences.english: And journeying by ship from Tyre we came to Ptolemais; and there we had talk with the brothers and were with them for one day.
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa keli Tire sigafe ra Pitolomayi. Muxu naxa ngaxakerenyie xɛɛbu mɛnni, muxu naxa fɛɛɲɛn naa.

sentences.english: And on the day after, we went away and came to Caesarea, where we were guests in the house of Philip, the preacher, who was one of the seven.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, muxu naxa siga Sesare, Filipu xibaaru fanyi kawandila xɔnyi, naxan nu na mixi sugandixi solofere ya ma.

sentences.english: And he had four daughters, virgins, who were prophets.
sentences.susu: A xa di ginɛ naani nu na naxee mu nu dɔxɔ xɛmɛ taa. E nu namiɲɔnmɛ wali rabama.

sentences.english: And while we were waiting there for some days, a certain prophet, named Agabus, came down from Judaea.
sentences.susu: Muxu to bara xi wuyaxi raba naa, Ala xa namiɲɔnmɛ naxan xili Agabu, naxa fa muxu xɔnyi kelife Yudaya.

sentences.english: And he came to us, and took the band of Paul's clothing, and putting it round his feet and hands, said, The Holy Spirit says these words, So will the Jews do to the man who is the owner of this band, and they will give him up into the hands of the Gentiles.
sentences.susu: A naxa Pɔlu xa bɛlɛti tongo, a naxa a yɛtɛ kan sanyie nun a bɛlɛxɛe xiri. A naxa a fala, «Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi yi nan masenxi. Xɛmɛ naxan gbe yi bɛlɛti ra, Yuwifie a xirima yi mɔɔli nan na Darisalamu, e a so mixie yi ra naxee findi si gbɛtɛe ra.»

sentences.english: And hearing these things, we and those who were living in that place made request to him not to go to Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Muxu to na mɛ, muxu nun naakae naxa Pɔlu maxandi a naxa te Darisalamu.

sentences.english: Then Paul said, What are you doing, weeping and wounding my heart? for I am ready, not only to be a prisoner, but to be put to death at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
sentences.susu: A naxa muxu yaabi, «Munfe ra wo wama n bɔɲɛ maɲaaxufe wo yaye ra? N bara tin e xa n xiri Darisalamu, e xa n faxa, Marigi Isa xili xa fe ra.»

sentences.english: And as he might not be moved we did no more, saying, Let the purpose of God be done.
sentences.susu: A to mu tin muxu xui suxude, muxu mu tin a karaxande. Muxu naxa a fala, «Marigi sago xa raba.»

sentences.english: And after these days we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.
sentences.susu: Na lɔxɔɛe to dangi, muxu naxa muxu yailan, muxu naxa te Darisalamu.

sentences.english: And some of the disciples from Caesarea went with us, taking a certain Mnason of Cyprus, one of the early disciples, in whose house we were to be living.
sentences.susu: Isa fɔxirabirɛe ndee Sesarekae naxa muxu mati. E naxa muxu xanin Menason Sipirika xɔnyi, naxan findixi Isa fɔxirabirɛ ra a rakuya. A naxa muxu yigiya.

sentences.english: And when we came to Jerusalem, the brothers were pleased to see us.
sentences.susu: Muxu to so Darisalamu, Isa fɔxirabirɛe naxa muxu rasɛnɛ ɲɛlɛxinyi ra.

sentences.english: And on the day after, Paul went with us to James, and all the rulers of the church were present.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, muxu nun Pɔlu naxa siga Yaki xɔnyi. Danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama kuntigi birin naxa e malan naa.

sentences.english: And when he had said how glad he was to see them, he gave them a detailed account of the things which God had done through his work among the Gentiles.
sentences.susu: A to gɛ e xɛɛbude, Pɔlu naxa a xa wali dɛntɛgɛ sa Ala naxan nabaxi si gbɛtɛe tagi a saabui ra.

sentences.english: And hearing it, they gave praise to God; and they said to him, You see, brother, what thousands there are among the Jews, who have the faith; and they all have a great respect for the law:
sentences.susu: E to na mɛ, e naxa Ala matɔxɔ. E naxɛ, «Muxu ngaxakerenyi, i bara a to Yuwifi wulu wuyaxi bara danxaniya, kɔnɔ e man e tunnabɛxixi birafe Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And they have had news of you, how you have been teaching all the Jews among the Gentiles to give up the law of Moses, and not to give circumcision to their children, and not to keep the old rules.
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee bara a fala e bɛ a i Yuwifie xaranma, naxee na si gbɛtɛe ya ma, a e xa gbilen Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛe fɔxɔ ra, a e naxa e xa die sunna, a e naxa bira Yuwifie xa naamunyie fɔxɔ ra.»

sentences.english: What then is the position? They will certainly get news that you have come.
sentences.susu: «Won na ma di? Siikɛ yo mu na, ɲama a kolonma nɛ a i bara fa.

sentences.english: Do this, then, which we say to you: We have four men who have taken an oath;
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, muxu naxan falama i bɛ i xa a raba. Mixi naani na muxu ya ma, naxee bara laayidi tongo Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: Go with these, and make yourself clean with them, and make the necessary payments for them, so that they may be free from their oath: and everyone will see that the statements made about you are not true, but that you put yourself under rule, and keep the law.
sentences.susu: I xa kafu e ma, wo birin xa wo yɛtɛ rasɛniyɛn, i man xa e sare fi, e xa e xunyi bi. Na na a ra birin a kolonma a mixie naxan falaxi i xun ma, wule na a ra. E xa a kolon i fan biraxi Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But as to the Gentiles who have the faith, we sent a letter, giving our decision that they were to keep themselves from offerings made to false gods, and from blood, and from the flesh of animals put to death in ways against the law, and from the evil desires of the body.
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa natɛ tongo, muxu man fa na sɛbɛ. Danxaniyatɔɛe naxee keli si gbɛtɛe ma, e naxa sube don naxan baxi sɛrɛxɛ ra kuyee bɛ, nun sube yufaxie. E naxa wuli fan min. E man naxa yɛnɛ fan naba.»

sentences.english: Then Paul took the men, and on the day after, making himself clean with them, he went into the Temple, giving out the statement that the days necessary for making them clean were complete, till the offering was made for every one of them.
sentences.susu: Awa na kuye iba, Pɔlu naxa na mixie tongo, e naxa e yɛtɛ rasɛniyɛn. Na xanbi a naxa so hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, a xa a masen, marasɛniyɛnyi rakamalima lɔxɔɛ naxan ma, a nun sɛrɛxɛ naxan bama kankan bɛ.

sentences.english: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews from Asia, seeing him in the Temple, got the people together and put their hands on him,
sentences.susu: Na xi solofere raɲɔnyi, Yuwifie Asikae to Pɔlu to hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, e naxa ɲama birin ya iso, e man naxa Pɔlu suxu.

sentences.english: Crying out, Men of Israel, come to our help: this is the man who is teaching all men everywhere against the people and the law and this place: and in addition, he has taken Greeks into the Temple, and made this holy place unclean.
sentences.susu: E nu sɔnxɔɛ rate, «Isirayilakae, wo muxu mali! Na xɛmɛ nan yi ki naxan kawandi ɲaaxi rabama yire birin mixi birin bɛ, Yuwifie, nun Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ, nun yi hɔrɔmɔbanxi xa fe ra. A man bara Girɛkikae raso hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui. Na bara yi yire sɛniyɛnxi findi yire sɛniyɛntare ra.»

sentences.english: For they had seen him before in the town with Trophimus of Ephesus, and had the idea that Paul had taken him with him into the Temple.
sentences.susu: E na fala nɛ barima e nu bara Pɔlu nun Tirofimo Efɛsɛka to e boore fɔxɔ ra taa kui. E naxa a maɲɔxun a Pɔlu a raso nɛ hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui.

sentences.english: And all the town was moved, and the people came running together and put their hands on Paul, pulling him out of the Temple: and then the doors were shut.
sentences.susu: Taa kui birin ya naxa iso. Mixie naxa fa e gi ra keli yire birin. E naxa Pɔlu suxu, e naxa mini a bubu ra tande ma. E naxa naadɛe ragali keren na.

sentences.english: And while they were attempting to put him to death, news came to the chief captain of the band that all Jerusalem was out of control.
sentences.susu: E nu wama Pɔlu faxafe nɛ. Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa a kolon Darisalamu birin ya isoxi.

sentences.english: And straight away he took some armed men and went quickly down to them: and the Jews, seeing them, gave no more blows to Paul.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa sɔɔrie nun e xa xunmatie tongo, e siga Pɔlu fɔxɔ ra keren na. Ɲama to sɔɔrie to, e naxa ba Pɔlu bɔnbɔfe.

sentences.english: Then the chief captain came near and took him, and gave orders for him to be put in chains, questioning them as to who he was and what he had done.
sentences.susu: Awa, sɔɔri mangɛ naxa yaamari fi e xa a xiri yɔlɔnxɔnyi firin na. A naxa maxɔrinyi ti fa nde a ra, nun a munfe rabaxi.

sentences.english: And some said one thing and some another, among the people: and as he was not able to get a knowledge of the facts because of the noise, he gave orders for Paul to be taken into the army building.
sentences.susu: Ɲama sɛɛti nde sɔnxɔma e gbe ki, booree fan sɔnxɔma e gbe ki. A to mu nɔ fe fiixɛ sɔtɔde e ra sɔnxɔɛ xa fe ra, a naxa a fala e xa Pɔlu xanin sɔɔri banxi kui.

sentences.english: And when he came on to the steps, he was lifted up by the armed men, because of the force of the people;
sentences.susu: Pɔlu to ti banxi dɛ ra, sɔɔrie naxa a tongo ɲama xa ɲaaxui ma,

sentences.english: For a great mass of people came after them, crying out, Away with him!
sentences.susu: barima mixi gali nan nu biraxi e fɔxɔ ra, e nu fa a fala e xui itexi ra, «A xa faxa!»

sentences.english: And when Paul was about to be taken into the building, he said to the chief captain, May I say something to you? And he said, Have you a knowledge of Greek?
sentences.susu: E wama a rasofe sɔɔri banxi kui tɛmui naxɛ, Pɔlu naxa sɔɔri mangɛ maxɔrin, «I nɔma n sago sade n xa fe nde fala i bɛ?» Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa a yaabi, «I Girɛki xui mɛma?

sentences.english: Are you by chance the Egyptian who, before this, got the people worked up against the government and took four thousand men of the Assassins out into the waste land?
sentences.susu: I tan xa mu na Misiraka ra, naxan mixie ya iso yi dɔnxɔɛ ra, a naxa suute wulu naani xanin wula kui?»

sentences.english: But Paul said, I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, which is not an unimportant town: I make a request to you to let me say a word to the people.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a yaabi, «Yuwifi nan n na, Tariseka. Na taa xungbe a munafanyi gbo Silisi bɔxi ma. N sago sa n xa wɔyɛn yi gali bɛ.»

sentences.english: And when he let him do so, Paul, from the steps, made a sign with his hand to the people, and when they were all quiet, he said to them in the Hebrew language,
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ to a sago sa, Pɔlu tixi banxi tede dɛ ra, a naxa mixie masabari a bɛlɛxɛ ra. Kuye naxa bolon yen! Pɔlu naxa wɔyɛn Eburu xui.

sentences.english: My brothers and fathers, give ear to the story of my life which I now put before you.
sentences.susu: «N ngaxakerenyie, n babae, wo xa wo tuli mati n na, n xa n yɛtɛ kan xun mafala.»

sentences.english: And, hearing him talking in the Hebrew language, they became the more quiet, and he said,
sentences.susu: E to a mɛ a Eburu xui falama, e naxa dundu dangi singe ra. Pɔlu naxa a fala,

sentences.english: I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia by birth, but I had my education in this town at the feet of Gamaliel, being trained in the keeping of every detail of the law of our fathers; given up to the cause of God with all my heart, as you are today.
sentences.susu: «Yuwifi nan n na, n barixi Tarise nɛ, Silisi bɔxi ma, kɔnɔ n mɔxi be nɛ. Gamaliyɛli naxa n xaran alako n xa bira won babae xa sɛriyɛ fɔxɔ ra. Ala xa fe nu n bɔɲɛ suxuma alɔ a wo fan suxuma ki naxɛ to.

sentences.english: And I made attacks on this Way, even to death, taking men and women and putting them in prison.
sentences.susu: N mixie tɔɔrɔ nɛ han n naxa e faxa, naxee nu biraxi Isa xa kira fɔxɔ ra. N naxa ginɛe nun xɛmɛe suxu, n naxa e sa geeli kui.

sentences.english: Of which the high priest will be a witness, and all the rulers, from whom I had letters to the brothers; and I went into Damascus, to take those who were there as prisoners to Jerusalem for punishment.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi nun diinɛ forie birin na n seedee ra. E naxa kɛɛdie so n yi ra katarabi e ngaxakerenyie ma Damasi alako n na danxaniyatɔɛe to, n xa e xiri, n xa fa e ra Darisalamu, n xa e ɲaxankata.»

sentences.english: And it came about that while I was on my journey, coming near to Damascus, about the middle of the day, suddenly I saw a great light from heaven shining round me.
sentences.susu: «N to makɔrɛ Damasi ra yanyi tagi, yanbɛ xungbe naxa goro n ma kelife koore ma.

sentences.english: And when I went down on the earth, a voice came to my ears saying to me, Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me so cruelly?
sentences.susu: N naxa bira bɔxi. N naxa xui mɛ naxan nu a falama n bɛ, ‹Sɔlu, Sɔlu, munfe ra i n ɲaxankatama?›

sentences.english: And I, answering, said, Who are you; Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are attacking.
sentences.susu: N naxa a yaabi, ‹Nde i ra, Marigi?› A naxa n yaabi, ‹Isa Nasarɛtika nan n na, i naxan ɲaxankatafe.›

sentences.english: And those who were with me saw the light, but the voice of him who was talking to me came not to their ears.
sentences.susu: Naxee nu na n fɔxɔ ra, e naxa yanbɛ to, kɔnɔ naxan nu wɔyɛnfe, e mu na tan xui mɛ. Awa, n naxa a fala,

sentences.english: And I said, What have I to do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Get up, and go into Damascus; and it will be made clear to you what you have to do.
sentences.susu: ‹N xa munse raba, Marigi?› Marigi naxa a fala n bɛ, ‹Keli, i siga Damasi. Mɛnni a fama falade i bɛ i lan i xa naxan naba.›

sentences.english: And because I was unable to see because of the glory of that light, those who were with me took me by the hand, and so I came to Damascus.
sentences.susu: N mu nu se toma na yanbɛ xa naiyalanyi saabui ra. Naxee nu na n fɔxɔ ra, e naxa n bɛlɛxɛ rasuxu han Damasi.»

sentences.english: And one Ananias, a God-fearing man, who kept the law, and of whom all the Jews in that place had a high opinion,
sentences.susu: «Awa, xɛmɛ nde naxan xili Ananiyasi, mixi tinxinxi na a ra Ala xa sɛriyɛ ki ma, naxan nafanxi Damasi Yuwifie ma,

sentences.english: Came to my side and said, Brother Saul, let your eyes be open. And in that very hour I was able to see him.
sentences.susu: a naxa fa n yire. A naxa a fala, ‹N ngaxakerenyi Sɔlu, to ti.› N ya naxa rabi keren na, n naxa se birin to.

sentences.english: And he said, You have been marked out by the God of our fathers to have knowledge of his purpose, and to see the Upright One and to give ear to the words of his mouth.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala, ‹Won babae Marigi Ala bara i sugandi i xa a sago kolon, i xa Tinxintɔɛ to, nun i xa a wɔyɛnyi mɛ a tan yati dɛ ra,

sentences.english: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and of what has come to your ears.
sentences.susu: barima i findima a xa seede nan na mixi birin ya i, i fee naxee toxi nun i naxee mɛxi.

sentences.english: And now, why are you waiting? get up, and have baptism, for the washing away of your sins, giving worship to his name.
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi, i munse mamɛfe? Keli, i xa i xunxa ye xɔɔra, i xa yunubi xa ba i ma, i xa Marigi xili maxandi.›»

sentences.english: And it came about that when I had come back to Jerusalem, while I was at prayer in the Temple, my senses became more than naturally clear,
sentences.susu: «N naxa gbilen Darisalamu. N to nu na Ala maxandife hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, n naxa laamatunyi to.

sentences.english: And I saw him saying to me, Go out of Jerusalem straight away because they will not give hearing to your witness about me.
sentences.susu: Marigi naxa a fala n bɛ, ‹I xa mini mafuren Darisalamu, barima e mu tinma i xa seedeya ra n ma fe ra.›

sentences.english: And I said, Lord, they themselves have knowledge that I went through the Synagogues putting in prison and whipping all those who had faith in you:
sentences.susu: N naxa a fala, ‹Marigi, e yati a kolon a n nu sigama salidee kui danxaniyatɔɛe fende alako n xa e sa geeli, n man xa e bɔnbɔ.

sentences.english: And when Stephen your witness was put to death, I was there, giving approval, and looking after the clothing of those who put him to death.
sentences.susu: E to nu i xa seede Etiyɛn faxama, n tan yati nu na, n nu ɲɛlɛxinxi na ra. N tan nan man nu booree xa dugie suxuxi.›

sentences.english: And he said to me, Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.
sentences.susu: Awa, Marigi naxa a fala n bɛ, ‹Siga, n i xɛɛma yire makuye si gbɛtɛe ma.›»

sentences.english: And they gave him a hearing as far as this word; then with loud voices they said, Away with this man from the earth; it is not right for him to be living.
sentences.susu: E naxa e tuli mati a xa masenyi birin na, han a yi wɔyɛnyi falaxi tɛmui naxɛ. E fa gbelegbele, «Wo yi xɛmɛ faxa. A mu lan a xa balo.»

sentences.english: And while they were crying out, and pulling off their clothing, and sending dust into the air,
sentences.susu: E naxa sɔnxɔɛ rate, e nu e xa donmae rate e ma, e nu xube ite kuye i.

sentences.english: The chief captain gave orders for him to be taken into the army building, saying that he would put him to the test by whipping, so that he might have knowledge of the reason why they were crying out so violently against him.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa a fala a e xa Pɔlu raso sɔɔri banxi kui, e man xa a bɔnbɔ luxusinyi ra alako e xa a kolon ɲama sɔnxɔma fe naxan ma.

sentences.english: And when they had put leather bands round him, Paul said to the captain who was present, Is it the law for you to give blows to a man who is a Roman and has not been judged?
sentences.susu: E to nu a xirife alako e xa a bɔnbɔ, Pɔlu naxa sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati maxɔrin naxan nu tixi naa, «Sɛriyɛ na wo yi ra naxan a masenxi a wo xa Rɔmaka bɔnbɔ luxusinyi ra hali a mu makiitixi?»

sentences.english: And hearing this, the man went to the chief captain and gave him an account of it, saying, What are you about to do? for this man is a Roman.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri kɛmɛ xunmati to na mɛ, a naxa sa sɔɔri mangɛ rakolon. A naxɛ, «Yi xɛmɛ Rɔmaka lasiri na a ra. Won na ma di?»

sentences.english: And the chief captain came to him and said, Give me an answer, are you a Roman? And he said, Yes.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa fa, a naxa Pɔlu maxɔrin, «A fala n bɛ xa Rɔmaka na i ra?» Pɔlu naxa a yaabi, «Iyo xɛ.»

sentences.english: And the chief captain said, I got Roman rights for myself at a great price. And Paul said, But I had them by birth.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ man naxa a fala, «N tan naafuli gbegbe nan baxi, n fa findi Rɔmaka lasiri ra.» Pɔlu naxa a fala a bɛ, «N tan barixi lasiriya nan kui nɛ.»

sentences.english: Then those who were about to put him to the test went away: and the chief captain was in fear, seeing that he was a Roman, and that he had put chains on him.
sentences.susu: Kabi na raba, naxee nu wama a bɔnbɔfe alako a xa wɔyɛn, e birin naxa e magbilen. Sɔɔri mangɛ yɛtɛ naxa gaaxu a kolonfe ra Pɔlu Rɔmaka na a ra, a naxan xiri yɔlɔnxɔnyi ra.

sentences.english: But on the day after, desiring to have certain knowledge of what the Jews had to say against him, he made him free, and gave orders for the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to come together, and he took Paul and put him before them.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, sɔɔri mangɛ to wa a kolonfe a fiixɛ ra Yuwifie Pɔlu kalamuxi fe naxan ma, a naxa a fulun. A naxa yaamari fi, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun Yuwifi kiitisae birin xa malan. A naxa Pɔlu ragoro, a ti e tagi.

sentences.english: And Paul, looking fixedly at the Sanhedrin, said, My brothers, my life has been upright before God till this day.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a ya ti Yuwifi kiitisae ra. A naxa a masen, «N ngaxakerenyie, n naxan nabaxi han to, n a rabaxi n bɔɲɛ fiixɛ nan na Ala ya xɔri»

sentences.english: And the high priest, Ananias, gave orders to those who were near him to give him a blow on the mouth.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi, Ananiyasi naxa mixie yaamari, naxee nu na a fɛ ma, e xa a dɛ ragarin.

sentences.english: Then Paul said to him, God will give blows to you, you whitewashed wall: are you here to be my judge by law, and by your orders am I given blows against the law?
sentences.susu: Awa, Pɔlu naxa a fala a bɛ, «Ala nan fama i tan bɔnbɔde. I luxi nɛ alɔ banxi naxan fari fiixɛ kɔnɔ a kui nɔxɔxi. I bara wa n makiitife kiiti sɛriyɛ ra, kɔnɔ i to yaamari fixi e xa n bɔnbɔ, i bara sɛriyɛ matandi.»

sentences.english: And those who were near said, Do you say such words against God's high priest?
sentences.susu: Naxee nu na a fɛ ma, e naxa a fala a bɛ, «I Ala xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi nan konbima yi ki!»

sentences.english: And Paul said, Brother, I had no idea that he was the high priest: for it has been said, You may not say evil about the ruler of your people.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a fala, «N ngaxakerenyie, n mu nu a kolon xa sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi na a ra, barima a sɛbɛxi, ‹I naxa wɔyɛn kobi fala ɲama mangɛ bɛ.›»

sentences.english: But when Paul saw that half of them were Sadducees and the rest Pharisees, he said in the Sanhedrin, Brothers, I am a Pharisee, and the son of Pharisees: I am here to be judged on the question of the hope of the coming back from the dead.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu to a kolon Sadusenie nun Farisɛnie nu na Yuwifi kiitisae xa malanyi kui, a naxa a fala a xui itexi ra, «N ngaxakerenyie, Farisɛni nan n na. N baba fan Farisɛni nan nu a ra. To n na kiiti banxi barima n laxi a ra Ala fama won nakelide faxɛ ma kiiti lɔxɔɛ.»

sentences.english: And when he had said this, there was an argument between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and a division in the meeting.
sentences.susu: A to na fala, boore matandi naxa lu Farisɛnie nun Sadusenie tagi. Ɲama naxa itaxun.

sentences.english: For the Sadducees say that there is no coming back from the dead, and no angels or spirits: but the Pharisees have belief in all these.
sentences.susu: Sadusenie tan bɛ, mixi mu kelima faxɛ ma. E man mu laxi malekɛe nun ɲinnɛe xa fe ra. Kɔnɔ Farisɛnie tan la nee birin xa fe ra.

sentences.english: And there was a great outcry: and some of the scribes on the side of the Pharisees got up and took part in the discussion, saying, We see no evil in this man: what if he has had a revelation from an angel or a spirit?
sentences.susu: Sɔnxɔɛ xungbe naxa mini. Sɛriyɛ karamɔxɔ ndee Farisɛnie tagi e naxa wɔyɛn xɔrɔxɔɛ fala. E naxɛ, «Muxu mu fefe ɲaaxi yo rakɔrɔsixi yi xɛmɛ ma. Tɛmunde ɲinnɛ nde, xa na mu a ra malekɛ nde, nan wɔyɛnxi a ra.»

sentences.english: And when the argument became very violent, the chief captain, fearing that Paul would be pulled in two by them, gave orders to the armed men to take him by force from among them, and take him into the army building.
sentences.susu: Sɔnxɔɛ to nu sigama gbo ra, sɔɔri mangɛ naxa gaaxu e fa Pɔlu faxafe. A naxa sɔɔrie ragoro e xa Pɔlu tongo e tagi, e xa a xanin sɔɔri banxi kui.

sentences.english: And the night after, the Lord came to his side and said, Be of good heart, for as you have been witnessing for me in Jerusalem, so will you be my witness in Rome.
sentences.susu: Na kɔɛ ra, Marigi naxa mini Pɔlu ma. A naxa a fala a bɛ, «I xa limaniya barima i findima n ma seede nan na Rɔma alɔ i a rabaxi Darisalamu ki naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And when it was day, the Jews came together and put themselves under an oath that they would take no food or drink till they had put Paul to death.
sentences.susu: Kuye to iba, Yuwifie naxa lanyi xiri kali ra, e naxa e dɛge, e naxa e min sinden, a fo e xa Pɔlu faxa.

sentences.english: And more than forty of them took this oath.
sentences.susu: Naxee na lanyi xiri, e nu dangi mixi tongo naani ra.

sentences.english: And they came to the chief priests and the rulers and said, We have taken a great oath to take no food till we have put Paul to death
sentences.susu: E naxa a masen sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun forie bɛ, «Muxu bara muxu kali Ala ra, muxu mu sese donma sinden fo muxu xa Pɔlu faxa.

sentences.english: So now, will you and the Sanhedrin make a request to the military authorities to have him sent down to you, as if you were desiring to go into the business in greater detail; and we, before ever he gets to you, will be waiting to put him to death.
sentences.susu: Awa, yakɔsi, wo tan nun Yuwifi kiitisae xa mangɛ mayandi a xa fa a ra alako wo xa a xa fe mato a fanyi ra. Na kui, muxu tan a faxama kira ra.»

sentences.english: But Paul's sister's son had word of their design, and he came into the army building and gave news of it to Paul.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu maaginɛ xa di naxa na yanfɛ kolon. A naxa siga sɔɔri banxi kui, a naxa na birin masen Pɔlu bɛ.

sentences.english: And Paul sent for a captain and said, Take this young man to your chief, for he has news for him.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati nde xili, a naxɛ, «Yi sɛgɛtala xanin sɔɔri mangɛ xɔn ma, alako a xa fe nde fala a bɛ.»

sentences.english: So he took him to the chief captain and said, Paul, the prisoner, made a request to me to take this young man to you, for he has something to say to you.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri kɛmɛ xunmati naxa sɛgɛtala tongo, a naxa a xanin sɔɔri mangɛ xɔn ma. A naxɛ, «Pɔlu, geelimani nan n xilixi, a naxa n mayandi a n xa fa yi sɛgɛtala ra i xɔn ma, a xa fe nde masen i bɛ.»

sentences.english: And the chief took him by the hand and, going on one side, said to him privately, What is it you have to say to me?
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa sɛgɛtala tongo, e naxa e mamini. Mangɛ naxɛ, «I wama munse falafe n bɛ?»

sentences.english: And he said, The Jews are in agreement together to make a request to you for Paul to be taken, on the day after this, into the Sanhedrin, to be questioned in greater detail.
sentences.susu: A naxa a yaabi, «Yuwifie bara lan a ma, e xa i maxandi i xa Pɔlu xanin Yuwifi kiitisae yire, alako e man xa maxɔrinyi nde ti a ma.

sentences.english: But do not give way to them, for more than forty of them are waiting for him, having taken an oath not to take food or drink till they have put him to death: and now they are ready, waiting for your order.
sentences.susu: I naxa i tuli mati e ra, barima mixi tongo naani nun nde bara yanfɛ xiri a xun e ya ma. E bara e kali a e mu sese donma, e mu sese minma a fo e na Pɔlu faxa tɛmui naxɛ. Yakɔsi e bara gɛ e yailande, e fa i sago nan mamɛfe.»

sentences.english: So the chief captain let the young man go, saying to him, Do not say to anyone that you have given me word of these things.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa sɛgɛtala rabolo, a naxa tɔnyi dɔxɔ a ma, fa fala, a fe naxan falaxi a bɛ, a naxa na fala mixi yo bɛ.

sentences.english: And he sent for two captains and said, Make ready two hundred men, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, to go to Caesarea, at the third hour of the night:
sentences.susu: A naxa sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati firin xili, a naxa a fala e bɛ, «Wo sɔɔri kɛmɛ firin yailan, sɔɔri soe ragie tongo solofere, nun xali woli kɛmɛ firin. Wo xa e yailan sigafe ra Sesare to kɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: And get beasts so that they may put Paul on them, and take him safely to Felix, the ruler.
sentences.susu: Wo xa soe nde yailan Pɔlu bɛ, alako a xa mangɛ Felisi li hɛɛri kui.»

sentences.english: And he sent a letter in these words:
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mangɛ naxa yi fe sɛbɛ bataaxɛ ra.

sentences.english: Claudius Lysias, to the most noble ruler, Felix, peace be with you.
sentences.susu: «N tan Kilɔdi Lisiya, i tan Mangɛ Felisi mafanxi, n bara i xɛɛbu.

sentences.english: This man was taken by the Jews, and was about to be put to death by them, when I came on them with the army and took him out of danger, having knowledge that he was a Roman.
sentences.susu: Yi xɛmɛ Yuwifie nan a suxuxi. E naxa wa a faxafe. N to a kolon a Rɔmaka na a ra, n nun sɔɔrie naxa fa, muxu naxa a ba e yi.

sentences.english: And, desiring to get at the reason for their attack on him, I took him down to their Sanhedrin:
sentences.susu: N to wa a kolonfe e a suxuxi naxan ma, n naxa siga a ra e xa kiitisae yire.

sentences.english: Then it became clear to me that it was a question of their law, and that nothing was said against him which might be a reason for prison or death.
sentences.susu: N naxa a li e a kalamuxi e xa sɛriyɛ xa fe nan ma, kɔnɔ a mu fe kobi yo rabaxi a lanma a xa faxa naxan ma, xa na mu a ra a xa sa geeli kui.

sentences.english: And when news was given to me that a secret design was being made against the man, I sent him straight away to you, giving orders to those who are against him to make their statements before you.
sentences.susu: N to bara a mɛ a Yuwifie bara gali malan a xili ma, n naxa a rasanba i ma keren na. N a kalamumae rakolonma e yɛtɛ kan xa sa a kalamu i xɔn a xa fe ra. Wo salamu.»

sentences.english: So the armed men, as they were ordered, took Paul and came by night to Antipatris.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔrie naxa Pɔlu tongo alɔ e yamarixi ki naxɛ. E naxa a xanin kɔɛ ra han Antipatiri.

sentences.english: But on the day after, they sent the horsemen on with him, and went back to their place:
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, sɔɔrie naxa gbilen sɔɔri banxi. Soe ragie naxa Pɔlu tongo.

sentences.english: And they, when they came to Caesarea, gave the letter to the ruler, and took Paul before him.
sentences.susu: E to so Sesare, soe ragie naxa bataaxɛ nun Pɔlu so mangɛ yi ra.

sentences.english: And after reading it, he said, What part of the country do you come from? And, hearing that he was from Cilicia,
sentences.susu: Mangɛ to gɛ bataaxɛ xarande, a naxa Pɔlu maxɔrin a keli dɛnnaxɛ. A to bara a mɛ a Silisika na a ra, a naxa a fala,

sentences.english: I will give hearing to your cause, he said, when those who are against you have come. And he gave orders for him to be kept in Herod's Praetorium.
sentences.susu: «N fama nɛ i makiitide i tɔɔɲɛgɛlae na fa tɛmui naxɛ.» A naxa yaamari fi e xa Pɔlu xanin geeli banxi Herode naxan tixi.

sentences.english: And after five days, the high priest, Ananias, came with certain of the rulers, and an expert talker, one Tertullus; and they made a statement to Felix against Paul.
sentences.susu: Xi suuli dangi xanbi, Ananiyasi, naxan findixi sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi ra, nun forie naxa fa e nun xunmafalɛ nde, naxan xili Teritulo. E naxa Pɔlu kalamu mangɛ xɔn ma.

sentences.english: And when he had been sent for, Tertullus, starting his statement, said, Because by you we are living in peace, and through your wisdom wrongs are put right for this nation,
sentences.susu: E to Pɔlu xili, Teritulo naxa so a tɔɔɲɛgɛfe yi masenyi ra. «Felisi mangɛ fanyi, yi bɔxi birin dɔxɔxi bɔɲɛsa kui i xa fe kolonyi nun i xa xaxili fanyi nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: In all things and in all places we are conscious of our great debt to you, most noble Felix.
sentences.susu: I bara muxu rasɛɛwa hɛɛri xungbe ra.

sentences.english: But, so that I may not make you tired, I make a request to you of your mercy, to give hearing to a short statement.
sentences.susu: N mu wama i rabufe, kɔnɔ n bara i maxandi i xa i tuli mati muxu xa masenyi ra dondoronti.

sentences.english: For this man, in our opinion, is a cause of trouble, a maker of attacks on the government among Jews through all the empire, and a chief mover in the society of the Nazarenes:
sentences.susu: Muxu bara a to yi xɛmɛ mixi ɲaaxi na a ra. A Yuwifie tagi isoma naxee na duniɲa birin. A tan nan na Isa Nasarɛtika xa ɲama xunyi ra.

sentences.english: Who, in addition, was attempting to make the Temple unclean: whom we took,
sentences.susu: A man naxa wa hɔrɔmɔbanxi maberefe. Muxu naxa a suxu. Muxu naxa wa a makiitife muxu xa sɛriyɛ ki ma,
kɔnɔ sɔɔri mangɛ Lisiya naxa fa, a naxa a ba muxu yi sɛnbɛ xungbe ra.

sentences.english: And from whom you will be able, by questioning him yourself, to get knowledge of all the things which we say against him.
sentences.susu: A naxa a kalamulae yaamari e xa fa i xɔn ma. Xa i fan Pɔlu maxɔrin, i fama a kolonde muxu a suxuxi fe naxan ma.»

sentences.english: And the Jews were in agreement with his statement, saying that these things were so.
sentences.susu: Yuwifie naxa tin na masenyi ra, e fan naxa a fala a na na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: Then when the ruler had given him a sign to make his answer, Paul said, Because I have knowledge that you have been a judge over this nation for a number of years, I am glad to make my answer:
sentences.susu: Mangɛ naxa Pɔlu yaamari a fan xa wɔyɛn. Pɔlu naxa a masen a bɛ, «N a kolon, yi bɔxi makiitima nan i ra kabi ɲɛ wuyaxi. Na kui, n nan ma fe xunmafalama nɛ i bɛ lanlanteya kui.

sentences.english: Seeing that you are able to make certain of the fact that it is not more than twelve days from the time when I came up to Jerusalem for worship;
sentences.susu: Xi fu nun firin mu dangi kabi n naxa siga Darisalamu salide.

sentences.english: And they have not seen me in argument with any man in the Temple, or working up the feelings of the people, in the Synagogues or in the town:
sentences.susu: E mu nu muxu nun mixi li sɔnxɔ ra hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, xa na mu a ra salide xunxurie kui. N mu sɔnxɔɛ ratexi taa kui, n mu gali kui isoxi.

sentences.english: And they are not able to give facts in support of the things which they say against me now.
sentences.susu: E mu nɔma sese masende, e n kalamuma naxan ma.

sentences.english: But this I will say openly to you, that I do give worship to the God of our fathers after that Way, which to them is not the true religion: but I have belief in all the things which are in the law and in the books of the prophets:
sentences.susu: N naxan masenma i bɛ na nan ya. N nan n benbae Marigi Ala nan batuma alɔ Isa xa kira a masenxi ki naxɛ, e a falama kira naxan bɛ a wule kira. Naxan sɛbɛxi Tawureta Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa Kitaabui kui, n la na birin na.

sentences.english: Hoping in God for that which they themselves are looking for, that there will be a coming back from the dead for upright men and wrongdoers.
sentences.susu: N laxi Ala xa masenyi ra naxan masenxi a tinxintɔɛe nun tinxintare birin fama nɛ kelide faxɛ ma. Yuwifie fan laxi na ra.

sentences.english: And in this, I do my best at all times to have no reason for shame before God or men.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi n nan n yɛtɛ karaxanma alako n xa n ma simaya radangi bɔɲɛ fiixɛ kui Ala nun mixie tagi.

sentences.english: Now after a number of years I came to give help and offerings to my nation:
sentences.susu: N mu nu na be ɲɛ wuyaxi bun ma, kɔnɔ yakɔsi n faxi harige nde ra n bɔnsɔɛ bɛ. N fan faxi sɛrɛxɛ bade Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: And having been made clean, I was in the Temple, but not with a great number of people, and not with noise: but there were certain Jews from Asia,
sentences.susu: E n lixi na tɛmui nɛ hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, n sɛniyɛnxi, gali mu na n fɔxɔ ra, sɔnxɔɛ yo fan mu keli n saabui ra.

sentences.english: And it would have been better if they had come here to make a statement, if they have anything against me.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Yuwifi nde naxee keli Asi bɔxi ma, e mu tin n ma fe ra. E tan xa e yɛtɛ masen i bɛ, xa fe nde na e bɛ n ma fe ra.

sentences.english: Or let these men here present say what wrongdoing was seen in me when I was before the Sanhedrin,
sentences.susu: Xa na mu a ra naxee na be, e xa a masen i bɛ e n toxi fe ɲaaxi naxan xun, n to siga Yuwifi kiitisae yire.

sentences.english: But only this one thing which I said among them in a loud voice, I am this day being judged on the question of the coming back from the dead.
sentences.susu: N wɔyɛnyi naxan falaxi e tagi na nan ya: ‹Wo n makiitima nɛ to barima n laxi a ra Ala fama nɛ mixi faxaxie rakelide.›»

sentences.english: But Felix, who had a more detailed knowledge of the Way, put them off, saying, When Lysias, the chief captain, comes down, I will give attention to your business.
sentences.susu: Felisi naxan nu Isa xa kira kolon a fanyi ra, a naxa e xa fe sa sinden. A naxɛ, «Mangɛ Lisiya na fa, n wo xa fe matoma.»

sentences.english: And he gave orders to the captain to keep Paul under his control, and to let him have everything he had need of; and not to keep his friends from coming to see him.
sentences.susu: A naxa sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati yamari a xa Pɔlu kanta, a naxa a tɔɔrɔ, a man naxa a xa mixi yo ratɔn fe fanyi rabafe ra a bɛ.

sentences.english: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was of the Jews by birth, and sent for Paul, and gave hearing to him about faith in Christ Jesus.
sentences.susu: Xi ndee to dangi, Felisi nun a xa ginɛ Dirusila, naxan na Yuwifi ra, e naxa fa. Felisi naxa Pɔlu xili kawandi rabade Isa Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa fe ra. Pɔlu naxa danxaniya xa fe fala e bɛ Isa ma,

sentences.english: And while he was talking about righteousness and self-control and the judging which was to come, Felix had great fear and said, Go away for the present, and when the right time comes I will send for you.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ a xa masenyi to nu binyaxi tinxinyi ma, nun yɛtɛ xurufe ma, nun Ala xa kiiti naxan fama, Felisi naxa gaaxu. A naxɛ, «Siga sinden. N na n yɛtɛ masɔtɔ tɛmui naxɛ, n man i xilima.»

sentences.english: For he was hoping that Paul would give him money: so he sent for him more frequently and had talk with him.
sentences.susu: A man nu waxi nɛ Pɔlu xa kɔbiri fi a ma. A nu a xilima na nan ma tɛmui birin, e xa sa e bore to.

sentences.english: But after two years Porcius Festus took the place of Felix, who, desiring to have the approval of the Jews, kept Paul in chains.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛ firin to dangi, Felisi masarama naxa fa, Pɔrusu Fɛsitu. Felisi to wa a yɛtɛ mafanfe Yuwifie bɛ, a naxa Pɔlu lu geeli kui.

sentences.english: So Festus, having come into that part of the country which was under his rule, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
sentences.susu: Fɛsitu naxa xi saxan naba Sesare. Na xanbi, a naxa te Darisalamu.

sentences.english: And the chief priests and the chief men of the Jews made statements against Paul,
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi nun Yuwifi kuntigie naxa Pɔlu kalamu Fɛsitu bɛ.

sentences.english: Requesting Festus to give effect to their design against him, and send him to Jerusalem, when they would be waiting to put him to death on the way.
sentences.susu: E naxa Fɛsitu mayandi a xa fa a ra Darisalamu. E nu wama nɛ e xa a faxa kira ra.

sentences.english: But Festus, in answer, said that Paul was being kept in prison at Caesarea, and that in a short time he himself was going there.
sentences.susu: Fɛsitu naxa e yaabi, «Pɔlu makantaxi Sesare. A gbegbe mu luxi n tan fan xa siga naa.

sentences.english: So, he said, let those who have authority among you go with me, and if there is any wrong in the man, let them make a statement against him.
sentences.susu: Wo xa yarerati ndee xa n mati, wo xa Pɔlu kalamu naa xa a bara sa fe ɲaaxi nde raba.»

sentences.english: And when he had been with them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the day after, he took his place on the judge's seat, and sent for Paul.
sentences.susu: Fɛsitu mu se sa xi solomasaxan fari, xa na mu a ra xi fu Darisalamu, a naxa goro Sesare. Na kuye iba, a naxa dɔxɔ a xa kiiti kibanyi ma. A naxa yaamari fi e xa fa Pɔlu ra.

sentences.english: And when he came, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem came round him, and made all sorts of serious statements against him, which were not supported by the facts.
sentences.susu: A to fa, Yuwifie naxee fa keli Darisalamu, e naxa a rabilin. E naxa tɔɔɲɛgɛ gbegbe sa a xun, e mu nu nɔma naxan masende nɔndi ra.

sentences.english: Then Paul, in his answer to them, said, I have done no wrong against the law of the Jews, or against the Temple, or against Caesar.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa so a yɛtɛ xunmafalafe, a nu a fala, «N mu fe ɲaaxi yo rabaxi Yuwifie xa sɛriyɛ ra, xa na mu hɔrɔmɔbanxi ra, xa na mu a ra Rɔma mangɛ ra.»

sentences.english: But Festus, desiring to get the approval of the Jews, said to Paul, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and be judged before me there in connection with these things?
sentences.susu: Fɛsitu to wa a yɛtɛ mafanfe Yuwifie xɔn, a naxa Pɔlu maxɔrin, «I wama tefe Darisalamu i xa sa makiiti yi fee ma n ya xɔri?»

sentences.english: And Paul said, I am before the seat of Caesar's authority where it is right for me to be judged: I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you are well able to see.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a yaabi, «N lanma n xa makiiti mangasanyi xa kiiti banxi nan kui, n tixi dɛnnaxɛ yi ki. N mu fe kobi yo rabaxi Yuwifie ra. I fan na kolon a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: If, then, I am a wrongdoer and there is a cause of death in me, I am ready for death: if it is not as they say against me, no man may give me up to them. Let my cause come before Caesar.
sentences.susu: Xa n bara fe ɲaaxi raba a lanma n xa faxa naxan ma, n mu tondima n xa faxa, kɔnɔ xa e naxan falama wule na a ra, a mu lan mixi yo xa n so e yi ra. Mangɛ xungbe xa sa n makiiti Rɔma.»

sentences.english: Then Festus, having had a discussion with the Jews, made answer, You have said, Let my cause come before Caesar; to Caesar you will go.
sentences.susu: Fɛsitu to wɔyɛn a rasimae ra, a naxa a fala Pɔlu bɛ, «I bara wa sigafe mangɛ xungbe xɔn. Awa, i sigama nɛ.»

sentences.english: Now when some days had gone by, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea and went to see Festus.
sentences.susu: Xi nde to dangi, mangɛ Agiripa nun Berinisi naxa so Sesare Fɛsitu xɛɛbude.

sentences.english: And as they were there for some days, Festus gave them Paul's story, saying, There is a certain man here who was put in prison by Felix:
sentences.susu: E to bara xi wuyaxi radangi naa, Fɛsitu naxa Pɔlu xa fe fala mangɛ Agiripa bɛ. A naxɛ, «Felisi bara geelimani nde lu be.

sentences.english: Against whom the chief priests and the rulers of the Jews made a statement when I was at Jerusalem, requesting me to give a decision against him.
sentences.susu: N nu na Darisalamu tɛmui naxɛ, sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie nun Yuwifie forie naxa a kalamu, e man naxa wa a xa faxa.

sentences.english: To whom I gave answer that it is not the Roman way to give a man up, till he has been face to face with those who are attacking him, and has had a chance to give an answer to the statements made against him.
sentences.susu: N naxa e yaabi a Rɔmakae xa sɛriyɛ mu mixi faxama, fo a xa a gbe fala kalamusae bɛ kiitisa ya xɔri.

sentences.english: So, when they had come together here, straight away, on the day after, I took my place on the judge's seat and sent for the man.
sentences.susu: Na fe nan e rafaxi be. N fan mu dugundi. Na kuye iba, n naxa dɔxɔ n ma kiiti banxi. N naxa yaamari fi e xa fa na xɛmɛ ra.

sentences.english: But when they got up they said nothing about such crimes as I had in mind:
sentences.susu: Kalamusae to e dɛntɛgɛ, e mu fe ɲaaxi yo fala a xun ma, n nu naxee maɲɔxunxi.

sentences.english: But had certain questions against him in connection with their religion, and about one Jesus, now dead, who, Paul said, was living.
sentences.susu: E nu xɔrɔxɔma e xa diinɛ nan ma fe ra, a nun Isa xa fe ra. E naxɛ a bara faxa, kɔnɔ Pɔlu naxɛ a baloxi.

sentences.english: And as I had not enough knowledge for the discussion of these things, I made the suggestion to him to go to Jerusalem and be judged there.
sentences.susu: Awa, n to mu a kolon a lan n xa naxan naba, n naxa a maxɔrin xa a wama sigafe Darisalamu, a xa makiiti naa.

sentences.english: But when Paul made a request that he might be judged by Caesar, I gave orders for him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Pɔlu naxa wa a xa fe xaninfe mangɛ xungbe xɔn ma. Na tɛmui n naxa yaamari fi e xa a kanta han n a rasanbama mangɛ xungbe ma tɛmui naxɛ.»

sentences.english: And Agrippa said to Festus, I have a desire to give the man a hearing myself. Tomorrow, he said, you may give him a hearing.
sentences.susu: Agiripa naxa a fala Fɛsitu bɛ, «N fan wama n tuli matife na xɛmɛ ra.» Fɛsitu naxa a yaabi, «Tina, i a xui mɛma.»

sentences.english: So on the day after, when Agrippa and Bernice in great glory had come into the public place of hearing, with the chief of the army and the chief men of the town, at the order of Festus, Paul was sent for.
sentences.susu: Awa, na kuye iba, Agiripa nun Berinisi naxa so malan yire e nun taa kuntigie. E nu maxirixi a fanyi ra. Fɛsitu xa yaamari ma, e naxa fa Pɔlu ra.

sentences.english: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all those who are present here with us, you see this man, about whom all the Jews have made protests to me, at Jerusalem and in this place, saying that it is not right for him to be living any longer.
sentences.susu: Fɛsitu naxa a fala, «Mangɛ Agiripa nun wo tan naxee birin na be, wo bara yi xɛmɛ to Yuwifi naxan birin kalamuxi n xɔn Darisalamu nun be. E naxɛ a a xa faxa.

sentences.english: But, in my opinion, there is no cause of death in him, and as he himself has made a request to be judged by Caesar, I have said that I would send him.
sentences.susu: N tan bɛ, a mu fefe rabaxi a lan a xa faxa naxan ma, kɔnɔ a tan yati bara mayandi ti sigafe ra mangɛ xungbe xɔnyi Rɔma. Awa, n fan bara tin na ra.

sentences.english: But I have no certain account of him to send to Caesar. So I have sent for him to come before you, and specially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the business has been gone into, I may have something to put in writing.
sentences.susu: N mu fe xɔri yo sɔtɔxi naxan sɛbɛma mangɛ xungbe ma a xa fe ra. Na na a ra, n a raminixi wo ya i, a gbengbenyi i tan mangɛ Agiripa, alako won na gɛ a maxɔrinde n xa a kolon a lanma n xa naxan sɛbɛ.

sentences.english: For it seems to me against reason to send a prisoner without making clear what there is against him.
sentences.susu: N mu nɔma geelimani rasanbade mangɛ ma, n mu a masen a naxan nabaxi.»

sentences.english: And Agrippa said to Paul, You may put your cause before us. Then Paul, stretching out his hand, made his answer, saying:
sentences.susu: Agiripa naxa a fala Pɔlu bɛ, «I xa i yɛtɛ xun mafala.» Pɔlu to a bɛlɛxɛ ite, a naxa a yɛtɛ rafiixɛ yi masenyi ra.

sentences.english: In my opinion I am happy, King Agrippa, to be able to give my answer before you today to all these things which the Jews say against me:
sentences.susu: «Mangɛ Agiripa, to n ɲɛlɛxinxi n ma fe rafiixɛfe ra Yuwifie n kalamuxi naxan ma.

sentences.english: The more so, because you are expert in all questions to do with the Jews and their ways: so I make my request to you to give me a hearing to the end.
sentences.susu: I e xa diinɛ nun e xa sɛriyɛ kolon ki fanyi ra. Awa yandi, i xa i tuli mati n na.

sentences.english: All the Jews have knowledge of my way of life from my early years, as it was from the start among my nation, and at Jerusalem;
sentences.susu: Kabi n dimɛdi tɛmui, n nu na Darisalamu n bɔnsɔɛ ya ma. Yuwifi birin n ɲɛrɛ ki kolon

sentences.english: And they are able to say, if they would give witness, that I was living as a Pharisee, in that division of our religion which is most regular in the keeping of the law.
sentences.susu: a rakuya. E man a kolon Farisɛni nan nu n na diinɛla tagi naxee xa fe maxɔrɔxɔ. E nɔma na seedeɲɔxɔya bade.

sentences.english: And now I am here to be judged because of the hope given by God's word to our fathers;
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi, e n nakiitife barima n laxi Ala xa laayidi ra a naxan tongoxi muxu benbae bɛ,

sentences.english: For the effecting of which our twelve tribes have been working and waiting night and day with all their hearts. And in connection with this hope I am attacked by the Jews, O king!
sentences.susu: muxu bɔnsɔɛ fu nun firinyi naxan mamɛfe. E Ala batuma tɛmui birin, kɔɛ nun yanyi. N laxi na laayidi nan na. Mangɛ, Yuwifie n kalamuxi na nan ma.

sentences.english: Why, in your opinion, is it outside belief for God to make the dead come to life again?
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma lade a ra a Ala mixi faxaxie rakelima?»

sentences.english: For I, truly, was of the opinion that it was right for me to do a number of things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
sentences.susu: «N tan kata nɛ kira mɔɔli birin na n xa Isa Nasarɛtika xili kana.

sentences.english: And this I did in Jerusalem: and numbers of the saints I put in prison, having had authority given to me from the chief priests, and when they were put to death, I gave my decision against them.
sentences.susu: N na nan naba Darisalamu. Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie naxa tin n xa sɛniyɛntɔɛ wuyaxi sa geeli kui. N man naxa tin e xa faxa.

sentences.english: And I gave them punishment frequently, in all the Synagogues, forcing them to say things against God; and burning with passion against them, I went after them even into far-away towns.
sentences.susu: N nu sigama salide banxie kui alako n xa e tɔɔrɔ, e xa gbilen e xa danxaniya fɔxɔ ra. N ma xɔnɛ kui, n nu e tɔɔrɔ hali taa gbɛtɛe kui.»

sentences.english: Then, when I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and orders of the chief priests,
sentences.susu: «Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigie naxa tin n xa siga Damasi na fe ma.

sentences.english: In the middle of the day, on the road I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining round me and those who were journeying with me.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ, yanyi tagi n naxa yanbɛ to kira xɔn ma kelife koore, n tan nun n booree rabilinyi. A yanbɛ nu dangi soge ra.

sentences.english: And when we had all gone down on the earth, a voice came to me, saying in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me so cruelly? It is hard for you to go against the impulse which is driving you.
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa bira bɔxi ma. N naxa xui nde mɛ naxan nu a falama n bɛ Eburu xui, ‹Sɔlu, Sɔlu, munfe ra i n ɲaxankatama? Na fe xɔrɔxɔma nɛ i bɛ.›

sentences.english: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus, whom you are attacking.
sentences.susu: N naxa a yaabi, ‹Marigi, nde i ra?› Marigi naxa n yaabi, ‹Isa nan n na, i naxan ɲaxankatafe.

sentences.english: But get up on your feet: for I have come to you for this purpose, to make you a servant and a witness of the things in which you have seen me, and of those in which you will see me;
sentences.susu: Keli, ti i sanyie xun na. N minixi nɛ i ma alako n xa i findi walikɛ nun seede ra fee ma i naxee toxi nun i fama naxee tode.

sentences.english: And I will keep you safe from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,
sentences.susu: N i ratangama nɛ Yuwifie ma nun si gbɛtɛe ma, n i xɛɛma naxee ma, alako i xa e yae rabi,

sentences.english: To make their eyes open, turning them from the dark to the light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may have forgiveness of sins and a heritage among those who are made holy by faith in me.
sentences.susu: e xa mini dimi kui, e xa so naiyalanyi kui. E xa keli Sentanɛ xa nɔɛ bun, e xa so Ala xa mangɛya niini bun ma. Na kui, e xa yunubi xafarima nɛ, e man fama nɛ kɛ sɔtɔde sɛniyɛntɔɛe ya ma naxee danxaniyaxi n ma.›»

sentences.english: So, then, King Agrippa, I did not go against the vision from heaven;
sentences.susu: «Na kui, mangɛ Agiripa, n mu tondi na xɛɛraya ra naxan keli koore ma.

sentences.english: But I went about, first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, and through all the country of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, preaching a change of heart, so that they, being turned to God, might give, in their works, the fruits of a changed heart.
sentences.susu: N naxa na kawandi ti Damasi, Darisalamu, Yudaya, nun si gbɛtɛe tagi. N naxa a masen e bɛ e xa tuubi, e xa danxaniya Ala ma, nun e xa wali fanyi raba naxan e xa togondiya masenma.»

sentences.english: For this reason, the Jews took me in the Temple, and made an attempt to put me to death.
sentences.susu: «Yuwifie naxa n suxu hɔrɔmɔbanxi kui, e waxi n faxafe na nan ma.

sentences.english: And so, by God's help, I am here today, witnessing to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would come about;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ, Ala tantu, n baloxi a tan nan saabui ra han to. N naxa na seedeɲɔxɔya ba dimɛe nun forie birin bɛ. N mu fefe gbɛtɛ falaxi fo namiɲɔnmɛe nun Annabi Munsa nu naxee falama a e fama nɛ rabade.

sentences.english: That the Christ would go through pain, and being the first to come back from the dead, would give light to the people and to the Gentiles.
sentences.susu: E naxa a masen Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi tɔɔrɔma nɛ, a singe nan kelima faxamixie ya ma, a nun a Yuwifie nun si gbɛtɛe kawandima kisi ra.»

sentences.english: And when he made his answer in these words, Festus said in a loud voice, Paul, you are off your head; your great learning has made you unbalanced.
sentences.susu: A to nu wɔyɛnfe a yɛtɛ rafiixɛfe ra, Fɛsitu naxa a fala a xui itexi ra, «Pɔlu, i daxu! I xa fe gbegbe kolonyi bara i findi daxui ra.»

sentences.english: Then Paul said, I am not off my head, most noble Festus, but my words are true and wise.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a yaabi, «Fɛsitu mafanxi, daxui mu na n na. N nɔndi nun lɔnni nan masenfe.

sentences.english: For the king has knowledge of these things, to whom I am talking freely; being certain that all this is common knowledge to him; for it has not been done in secret.
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Agiripa tan yi fee kolon. N yi birin falama a tan nan bɛ, barima a ɲan a kolon, a a mu raba gundo xa kui.»

sentences.english: King Agrippa, have you faith in the prophets? I am certain that you have.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a fala Agiripa bɛ, «Mangɛ Agiripa, i laxi namiɲɔnmɛe ra? I la e ra, n na kolon.»

sentences.english: And Agrippa said to Paul, A little more and you will be making me a Christian.
sentences.susu: Agiripa naxa a fala Pɔlu bɛ, «A gbe mu luxi i xa n fan findi Isayanka ra!»

sentences.english: And Paul said, It is my prayer to God that, in little or great measure, not only you, but all those hearing me today might be even as I am, but for these chains.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a yaabi, «A fa findi yakɔsi ra, xa na mu tɛmui gbɛtɛ, n Marigi maxandima nɛ alako i tan yo, a nun naxan birin n xui ramɛfe be to, wo fan xa lu alɔ n tan, ba yi yɔlɔnxɔnyi ra naxan na n ma.»

sentences.english: And the king and the ruler and Bernice and those who were seated with them got up;
sentences.susu: Mangɛ Agiripa, mangɛ Fɛsitu, Berinisi, nun naxee birin nu dɔxɔxi e sɛɛti ma, e naxa keli.

sentences.english: And when they had gone away they said to one another, This man has done nothing which might give cause for death or prison.
sentences.susu: E to nu sigama, e naxa a fala e bore bɛ, «Yi xɛmɛ mu fefe rabaxi a lanma a xa faxa naxan ma, xa na mu a ra a lanma a xa sa geeli kui naxan ma.»

sentences.english: And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been made free, if he had not put his cause before Caesar.
sentences.susu: Agiripa naxa a fala Fɛsitu bɛ, «Yi xɛmɛ nu lan a xa bɛɲin, kɔnɔ a bara maxandi ti Mangɛ Xungbe xa a makiiti.»

sentences.english: And when the decision had been made that we were to go by sea to Italy, they gave Paul and certain other prisoners into the care of a captain named Julius, of the Augustan band.
sentences.susu: E to natɛ tongo muxu xa baki kunkui kui sigafe ra Itali, e naxa Pɔlu nun geelimani ndee so sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati yi ra naxan xili Yuliyusi, naxan na mangɛ xungbe xa sɔɔrie ya ma.

sentences.english: And we went to sea in a ship of Adramyttium which was sailing to the sea towns of Asia, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
sentences.susu: Muxu nun Arisitaraki, naxan keli Tɛsaloniki Masedon bɔxi ma, naxa baki kunkui kui naxan keli Adiramiti. A nu lan a xa dangi Asi sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: And on the day after, we came to Sidon; and Julius was kind to Paul, and let him go to see his friends and take a rest.
sentences.susu: Na kuye iba, muxu naxa kilɔn Sidɔn. Yuliyusi, naxan nu a ɲɔxɔ saxi Pɔlu xɔn ma a fanyi ra, a naxa a sago sa a xa siga a booree xɔnyi biyaasi fandɛ fende.

sentences.english: And sailing again from there, we went on under cover of Cyprus, because the wind was against us.
sentences.susu: Muxu to keli naa, muxu naxa dangi Sipiri suri ma, barima foye mu nu tinxi muxu bɛ.

sentences.english: And having gone across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia we came to Myra, in Lycia.
sentences.susu: Muxu to Silisi nun Panfiliya baa igiri, muxu naxa so Mira, Lisi bɔxi ma.

sentences.english: And there the captain came across a ship of Alexandria, sailing for Italy, and put us in it.
sentences.susu: Mɛnni, sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati naxa kunkui to naxan keli Alesandire, a sigafe Itali. Muxu naxa baki na kui.

sentences.english: And when we had gone on slowly for a long time, and had had hard work getting across to Cnidus, for the wind was against us, we went under cover of Crete, in the direction of Salmone;
sentences.susu: Xi wuyaxi bun ma kunkui nu tɔɔrɔma ɲɛrɛde. Kata nun kata muxu fa Sinidi li kɔnɔ foye mu tin muxu xa kilɔn naa. Na nan a to muxu naxa dangi Kirɛti suri laabe ra, Salemone sɛɛti ma.

sentences.english: And sailing down the side of it, as well as we were able, we came to a certain place named Fair Havens, near which was the town of Lasea.
sentences.susu: Naa iɲɛrɛfe nu xɔrɔxɔ. Muxu naxa yire nde li, naxan xili Wafu Tofanyi, Laseya fɛ ma.

sentences.english: And as a long time had gone by, and the journey was now full of danger, because it was late in the year, Paul put the position before them,
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa bu naa. Ɲɛrɛ man nu xɔrɔxɔ barima sunyi tɛmui nu bara dangi.

sentences.english: Saying, Friends, I see that this journey will be one of great damage and loss, not only to the goods and the ship, but to ourselves.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, Pɔlu naxa a fala, «N biyaasibooree, n bara a kolon won ma ɲɛrɛ fama nɛ xɔrɔxɔde. Kotee, kunkui, nun mixie fama nɛ tɔɔrɔde.»

sentences.english: But the captain gave more attention to the master and the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri kɛmɛ xunmati naxa a tuli mati kɛpini nun kunkui kanyi xa wɔyɛnyi ra, a tondi Pɔlu xa marasi ra.

sentences.english: And as the harbour was not a good one in which to be for the winter, the greater number of them were for going out to sea, in order, if possible, to put in for the winter at Phoenix, a harbour of Crete, looking to the north-east and south-east.
sentences.susu: Mixi gbegbe naxa wa Feniki life, barima e nu na wafu dɛnnaxɛ, mɛnni mu nu fan ɲɛmɛ radangide ra. Feniki, Kirɛti suri wafu nan a ra, naxan ya rafindixi sogegorode biri ma. E naxa wa e xa ɲɛmɛ radangi naa.

sentences.english: And when the south wind came softly, being of the opinion that their purpose might be effected, they let the ship go and went sailing down the side of Crete, very near to the land.
sentences.susu: Foye di nde naxa mini keli kɔɔla ma. E naxa a maɲɔxun a biyaasi bara fan. E naxa hanga bɛndun, e kunkui radangi Kirɛti suri fɛ ma.

sentences.english: But after a little time, a very violent wind, named Euraquilo, came down from it with great force.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ na tɛmui foye xungbe, naxan xili Yurakilɔn, a naxa fa keli suri ma.

sentences.english: And when the ship got into the grip of it, and was not able to make headway into the wind, we gave way, and went before it.
sentences.susu: Foye naxa kunkui tutun, han kunkui mu nu nɔma matinxinde. Muxu naxa muxu raxara foye yi ra.

sentences.english: And, sailing near the side of a small island named Cauda, we were able, though it was hard work, to make the ship's boat safe:
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa dangi suri lanmadi laabe ra, naxan xili Kiloda. Muxu naxa tɔɔrɔ kunkui lanma masɔtɔfe ra.

sentences.english: And having got it up, they put cords under and round the ship; but fearing that they might be pushed on to the Syrtis, they let down the sails and so went running before the wind.
sentences.susu: E to gɛ a ratede, e naxa luuti mafilin kunkui ma. E to nu gaaxuxi dɔxɔfe ra Sirite bɛnki ma, e naxa bɛla ragoro, foye nu fa siga muxu ra.

sentences.english: And, still fighting the storm with all our strength, the day after they made a start at getting the goods out of the ship;
sentences.susu: Foye naxa muxu bɔnbɔ a fanyi ra. Na kuye iba, muxu naxa kote nde woli baa ma.

sentences.english: And on the third day, they let all the sailing apparatus go over the side.
sentences.susu: Xi saxan to dangi, muxu yati naxa kunkui isee birin nagoro ye ma.

sentences.english: And as we had not seen the sun or stars for a long time, and a great storm was on us, all hope of salvation was gone.
sentences.susu: Xi wuyaxi naxa dangi, soge mu na, tunbuie mu na, foye sɛnbɛ nu gboma nan tui. Muxu mu nu laxi muxu kisife ra sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: And when they had been without food for a long time, Paul got up among them and said, Friends, it would have been better if you had given attention to me and not gone sailing out from Crete, to undergo this damage and loss.
sentences.susu: Kabi xi wuyaxi muxu mu nu donse donma. Awa Pɔlu naxa ti mixie tagi, a naxa a fala e bɛ, «N booree, xa wo wo tuli mati n na nu, won mu kelima Kirɛti nu, won mu yi kasarɛ nun lɔsi sɔtɔma nu.

sentences.english: But now, I say to you, be of good heart, for there will be no loss of life, but only of the ship.
