sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yakɔsi, n wo rasima nɛ, wo xa limaniya, barima mixi yo mu faxama wo ya ma, kunkui nan gbansan kasarama.

sentences.english: For this night there came to my side an angel of the God who is my Master and whose servant I am,
sentences.susu: N Marigi Ala, n walima naxan bɛ, a xa malekɛ nde bara mini n ma yi kɔɛ ra.

sentences.english: Saying, Have no fear, Paul, for you will come before Caesar, and God has given to you all those who are sailing with you.
sentences.susu: A naxa a fala n bɛ, ‹Pɔlu, i naxa gaaxu, fo i xa ti nɛ mangɛ xungbe ya i. Ala bara tin i biyaasiboore birin natangade.›

sentences.english: And so, O men, be of good heart, for I have faith in God that it will be as he said to me.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, wo xa limaniya barima n laxi Ala xa masenyi ra.

sentences.english: But we will be sent on to a certain island.
sentences.susu: Won fama suri nde lide.»

sentences.english: But when the fourteenth day came, while we were going here and there in the Adriatic sea, about the middle of the night the sailors had an idea that they were getting near land;
sentences.susu: Kɔɛ fu nun naani nde, muxu naxa Adiriyatike baa li. Na kɔɛ tagi kunkui raɲɛrɛ naxa sogi a muxu bara makɔrɛ bɔxi nde ra.

sentences.english: And they let down the lead, and saw that the sea was a hundred and twenty feet deep; and after a little time they did it again and it was ninety feet.
sentences.susu: E to ye tilinyi maniyase ragoro, e naxa kanke ya mɔxɔɲɛn sɔtɔ. E to makuya dondoronti, e man naxa a ragoro, e naxa kanke ya fu nun suuli sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Then, fearing that by chance we might come on to the rocks, they let down four hooks from the back of the ship, and made prayers for the coming of day.
sentences.susu: E to gaaxu garinde fanye nde ra, e naxa hanga naani woli kunkui xanbi ra. E naxa gbata kuye ibafe ra.

sentences.english: Then the sailors made attempts secretly to get away from the ship, letting down a boat as if they were about to put down hooks from the front of the ship;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ kunkui raɲɛrɛe nu wama kelife kunkui xun. E naxa kunkui lanma ragoro baa ma alɔ e na hangae nan nagorofe kunkui ya ra.

sentences.english: But Paul said to the captain and his men, If you do not keep these men in the ship, you will not be safe.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa a fala sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati nun sɔɔrie bɛ, «Xa yi mixie mu lu kunkui kui, wo mu nɔma kiside.»

sentences.english: Then the armed men, cutting the cords of the boat, let her go.
sentences.susu: Awa, sɔɔrie naxa kunkui lanma luuti bolon, e naxa a rabɛɲin a xa siga.

sentences.english: And when dawn was near, Paul gave them all orders to take food, saying, This is the fourteenth day you have been waiting and taking no food.
sentences.susu: Beenun kuye xa iba, Pɔlu naxa e birin nasi e xa donse don. A naxa a fala e bɛ, «A xi fu nun naani nan to wo mamɛ tife, wo mu tinxi wo dɛgede.

sentences.english: So I make request to you to take food; for this is for your salvation: not a hair from the head of any of you will come to destruction.
sentences.susu: N bara wo rasi wo xa donse don, barima na nan fan wo fate bɛ. Mixi yo mu halakima, hali wo xunsɛxɛ keren mu lɔɛma.»

sentences.english: And when he had said this and had taken bread, he gave praise to God before them all, and took a meal of the broken bread.
sentences.susu: A to na fala, a naxa taami tongo, a Ala nuwali sa e birin ya xɔri, a taami igira, a naxa a don fɔlɔ.

sentences.english: Then they all took heart and did the same.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui e birin naxa limaniya, e fan naxa so taami donfe.

sentences.english: And we were, in the ship, two hundred and seventy-six persons.
sentences.susu: Muxu mixi kɛmɛ firin mixi tongo solofere a nun senni nan nu na kunkui kui.

sentences.english: And when they had had enough food, they made the weight of the ship less, turning the grain out into the sea.
sentences.susu: E to wasa donse ra, e naxa farin woli baa ma alako kunkui xa yelebu.

sentences.english: And when it was day, they had no knowledge of the land, but they saw an inlet of the sea with a floor of sand, and they had the idea of driving the ship up on to it if possible.
sentences.susu: Kuye to iba, e mu a kolon e na dɛnnaxɛ, kɔnɔ e naxa bɔxi nde to. E naxa natɛ tongo e xa kata kunkui rasigade naa.

sentences.english: So cutting away the hooks, and letting them go into the sea, and freeing the cords of the guiding-blades, and lifting up the sail to the wind, they went in the direction of the inlet.
sentences.susu: E naxa hangae fulun, e xa sin baa ma. E naxa fɛya luutie fan bolon. E naxa yare bɛla rate, e xa e xun sa xare ma.

sentences.english: And coming to a point between two seas, they got the ship to land; and the front part was fixed in the sand and not able to be moved, but the back part was broken by the force of the waves.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e naxa bɛnki li, kunkui naxa kankan. Kunkui xunyi to kankan, mɔrɔnyi naxa a xɔrɛ kana sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: Then the armed men were for putting the prisoners to death, so that no one would get away by swimming.
sentences.susu: Sɔɔrie naxa lan geelimanie faxafe ma, alako e naxa ye masa, e e gi.

sentences.english: But the captain, desiring to keep Paul safe, kept them from their purpose, and gave orders that those who had knowledge of swimming were to go off the ship and get first to land:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ sɔɔrie kɛmɛ xunmati, naxan nu wama Pɔlu rakisife, a naxa e ratɔn. A naxa yaamari fi e ma a naxee fata ye masade, e singe xa bagan ye ma alako e xa xare masɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And the rest, some on boards and some on things from the ship. And so it came about that they all got safe to land.
sentences.susu: Booree xa gbaku xebenyie ra, xa na mu a ra kunkui xuntunyie ra. E birin naxa xare masɔtɔ hɛɛri kui.

sentences.english: And when we were safe, we made the discovery that the island was named Melita.
sentences.susu: Muxu to xare masɔtɔ, muxu naxa a kolon a na suri xili Malita.

sentences.english: And the simple people living there were uncommonly kind to us, for they made a fire for us, and took us in, because it was raining and cold.
sentences.susu: Malitakae naxa sɛɛwa muxu ra ki fanyi ra. E naxa muxu birin malan tɛ xungbe fɛ ma, e nu naxan xuruxi, barima tunɛ nu fafe nun xinbeli gbegbe ra.

sentences.english: But when Paul had got some sticks together and put them on the fire, a snake came out, because of the heat, and gave him a bite on the hand.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu to bolee matongo safe tɛ i, bɔximase naxa mini na tɛ wuyenyi xa fe ra, a naxa a bɛlɛxɛ xin.

sentences.english: And when the people saw it hanging on his hand, they said to one another, Without doubt this man has put someone to death, and though he has got safely away from the sea, God will not let him go on living.
sentences.susu: Malitakae to bɔximase to, a bara a bɛlɛxɛ xin a singanxi a ra, e naxa a fala e bore bɛ, «Nɔndi ra, niba nan yi mixi ra, barima haakɛ mu tinxi a xa balo, hali a to tangaxi baa ma.»

sentences.english: But shaking off the beast into the fire, he got no damage.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa bɔximase ralisan tɛ, sese mu a to.

sentences.english: But they had the idea that they would see him becoming ill, or suddenly falling down dead; but after waiting a long time, and seeing that no damage came to him, changing their opinion, they said he was a god.
sentences.susu: Na mixie nu mamɛ tife nɛ a xinde xa funtu, xa na mu a ra a xa faxa keren na, kɔnɔ sese mu a to. E to mamɛ ti, e naxa e xa maɲɔxunyi masara. E naxa a fala ala nde nan a ra.

sentences.english: Now near that place there was some land, the property of the chief man of the island, who was named Publius; who very kindly took us into his house as his guests for three days.
sentences.susu: Suri kuntigi xungbe, naxan xili Pubiliyu, naxa muxu yigiya a fanyi ra a xɔnyi xi saxan bun ma.

sentences.english: And the father of Publius was ill, with a disease of the stomach; to whom Paul went, and put his hands on him, with prayer, and made him well.
sentences.susu: Pubiliyu baba nu saxi, a furaxi, mangafaxɛ nu na a ma. Pɔlu to a makɔrɛ a ra, a naxa a bɛlɛxɛ sa a ma, a Ala maxandi, a naxa a rayalan.

sentences.english: And when this took place, all the others in the island who had diseases came and were made well.
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, suri furema gbɛtɛe naxa fa, Pɔlu naxa e fan nayalan.

sentences.english: Then they gave us great honour, and, when we went away, they put into the ship whatever things we were in need of.
sentences.susu: E naxa muxu binya a fanyi ra. Muxu to keli sigade, e naxa fandɛ fi muxu ma.

sentences.english: And after three months we went to sea in a ship of Alexandria sailing under the sign of the Dioscuri, which had been at the island for the winter.
sentences.susu: Muxu to kike saxan nadangi naa, muxu naxa baki kunkui kui, naxan keli Alesandire. A nu bara ɲɛmɛ radangi suri ma. Tɔnxuma nu a ma naxan findixi kuye masolixi firinyi ra.

sentences.english: And going into the harbour at Syracuse, we were waiting there for three days.
sentences.susu: Muxu to so kilɔn Sirakusi, muxu naxa lu naa xi saxan.

sentences.english: And from there, going about in a curve, we came to Rhegium: and after one day a south wind came up and on the day after we came to Puteoli:
sentences.susu: Muxu to keli naa, muxu naxa siga Regiyo baa dɛ ra. Foye to keli yirefanyi ma na kuye iba, muxu naxa xi firin ɲɛrɛ raba han Pusoli.

sentences.english: Where we came across some of the brothers, who kept us with them for seven days; and so we came to Rome.
sentences.susu: Muxu naxa ngaxakerenyie li naa naxee muxu mayandi xi solofere radangife ra e xɔnyi. Na tɛmui muxu siga nɛ han Rɔma.

sentences.english: And the brothers, when they had news of us, came out from town as far as Appii Forum and the Three Taverns to have a meeting with us: and Paul, seeing them, gave praise to God and took heart.
sentences.susu: Muxu ngaxakerenyi Rɔmakae, naxee muxu xa fe mɛ, e naxa fa muxu ralande, keli Rɔma han Apiyusi malan yire nun taa naxan xili Banxi Saxanyie. Pɔlu to e to a naxa Ala nuwali sa, a naxa limaniya.

sentences.english: And when we came into Rome, they let Paul have a house for himself and the armed man who kept watch over him.
sentences.susu: Muxu to so Rɔma, sɔɔri mixi kɛmɛ xunmati naxa geelimanie so mangɛ yi ra, kɔnɔ a naxa Pɔlu lu a kerenyi ma, a nun sɔɔri keren naxan a kantama.

sentences.english: Then after three days he sent for the chief men of the Jews: and when they had come together, he said to them, My brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the ways of our fathers, I was given, a prisoner from Jerusalem, into the hands of the Romans.
sentences.susu: Xi saxan to dangi, Pɔlu naxa Yuwifi kuntigie xili. E to malan, a naxa yi wɔyɛnyi ti e bɛ, «N ngaxakerenyie, hali n to mu fefe rabaxi won ma mixie ra, nun won benbae xa naamunyie ra, Yuwifie bara n sa geeli kui Darisalamu, na xanbi e man fa n so Rɔmakae yi ra.

sentences.english: Who, when they had put questions to me, were ready to let me go free, because there was no cause of death in me.
sentences.susu: E to gɛ n maxɔrinde, e nu wama n nabolofe nɛ, barima e mu sese toxi n faxama naxan ma.

sentences.english: But when the Jews made protest against it, I had to put my cause into Caesar's hands; not because I have anything to say against my nation.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Yuwifie mu tin. Na ma, n naxa mangɛ xungbe xa kiiti maxandi, kɔnɔ n mu wa n bɔnsɔɛ nan kalamufe.

sentences.english: But for this reason I sent for you, to see and have talk with you: for because of the hope of Israel I am in these chains.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, n naxa wa wo tofe alako n xa wɔyɛn wo ra, barima Isirayilakae xaxili tixi xɛɛra naxan na, na xa fe nan a toxi e yi yɔlɔnxɔnyi saxi n ma.»

sentences.english: And they said to him, We have not had letters from Judaea about you, and no one of the brothers has come to us here to give an account or say any evil about you.
sentences.susu: E naxa a yaabi, «Muxu mu bataaxɛ yo sɔtɔxi i xa fe ra keli Yudaya. Won ngaxakerenyi yo mu faxi fe ɲaaxi falade i xa fe ra.

sentences.english: But we have a desire to give hearing to your opinion: for as to this form of religion, we have knowledge that in all places it is attacked.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ, muxu wama a kolonfe nɛ i naxan maɲɔxunxi, barima muxu a kolon e yi diinɛ xa fe ibaxantinma yire birin.»

sentences.english: And when a day had been fixed, they came to his house in great numbers; and he gave them teaching, giving witness to the kingdom of God, and having discussions with them about Jesus, from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning till evening.
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa lɔxɔɛ keren so e yi. Mixi wuyaxi to fa a xɔnyi, Pɔlu naxa Ala xa mangɛya seedeɲɔxɔya ba. A naxa Isa xa fe masen e bɛ Tawureta Munsa nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa Kitaabui saabui ra keli gɛɛsɛgɛ han nunmare.

sentences.english: And some were in agreement with what he said, but some had doubts.
sentences.susu: Ndee naxa la a ra, kɔnɔ booree mu danxaniya.

sentences.english: And they went away, for there was a division among them after Paul had said this one thing: Well did the Holy Spirit say by the prophet Isaiah to your fathers,
sentences.susu: E to nu fatanma lantareya kui, Pɔlu naxa yi masenyi sa a fari, «Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi a fala nɛ wo benbae bɛ nɔndi ki ma Annabi Esayi saabui ra. A naxɛ,

sentences.english: Go to this people and say, Though you give ear, you will not get knowledge; and seeing, you will see, but the sense will not be clear to you:
sentences.susu: ‹Siga yi mixie xɔn ma, i xa a fala e bɛ: “Wo a mɛma wo tulie ra, kɔnɔ wo mu a fahaamuma. Wo a toma wo yae ra, kɔnɔ wo mu a igbɛma.”

sentences.english: For the heart of this people has become fat and their ears are slow in hearing and their eyes are shut; for fear that they might see with their eyes and give hearing with their ears and become wise in their hearts and be turned again to me, so that I might make them well.
sentences.susu: Barima yi mixie sondonyi bara xɔrɔxɔ. E bara e tulie dɛsɛ. E bara e yae raxi, alako e naxa a to e yae ra, e naxa a mɛ e tulie ra, e naxa a fahaamu e xaxili ra. Xa na mu a ra e e sondonyi mafindima nɛ, alako Ala xa e rayalan.›»

sentences.english: Be certain, then, that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and they will give hearing.
sentences.susu: «Awa, wo xa a kolon a Ala xa kisi bara rasanba si gbɛtɛe ma. E fama e tuli matide a ra.»
A to na fala, Yuwifie naxa siga xɔrɔxɔɛ kui e booree tagi.

sentences.english: And for the space of two years, Paul was living in the house of which he had the use, and had talk with all those who went in to see him,
sentences.susu: Pɔlu naxa lu banxi nde kui ɲɛ firin, a nu a sare fi. Naxee birin nu fama a tode, a nu e birin nasɛnɛma.

sentences.english: Preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ without fear, and no orders were given that he was not to do so.
sentences.susu: A nu Ala xa mangɛya niini xa fe nan kawandima a nun Marigi Isa xa fe, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi. A naxa na birin naba limaniya ra, mixi yo mu a tɔɔrɔ.

sentences.english: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, an Apostle by the selection of God, given authority as a preacher of the good news,
sentences.susu: N tan Pɔlu nan yi ki, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa xa konyi di. Ala bara n xili n xa findi a xa xɛɛra ra, a n sugandi n xa a xa xibaaru fanyi rayensen yɛ.

sentences.english: Of which God had given word before by his prophets in the holy Writings,
sentences.susu: Tɛmui dangixi, Ala nu bara a xa yi xibaaru fanyi laayidi a xa namiɲɔnmɛe xui ra Kitaabui sɛniyɛnxi kui.

sentences.english: About his Son who, in the flesh, came from the family of David,
sentences.susu: Yi xibaaru fanyi findixi a xa Di nan xa fe ra, naxan bari Dawuda bɔnsɔɛ kui a adama ki ma.

sentences.english: But was marked out as Son of God in power by the Holy Spirit through the coming to life again of the dead; Jesus Christ our Lord,
sentences.susu: Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi fan bara a masen sɛnbɛ ra a Ala xa Di na a ra. A na masen a xa marakeli nan saabui ra faxɛ ma. Won Marigi nan na Isa ra, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: Through whom grace has been given to us, sending us out to make disciples to the faith among all nations, for his name:
sentences.susu: A tan nan saabui a niyaxi Ala hinnɛxi muxu ra muxu xa findi xɛɛrae ra a xili xa fe ra, alako si birin xa danxaniya a ma, e xa bira a fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: Among whom you in the same way have been marked out to be disciples of Jesus Christ:
sentences.susu: Wo fan na na ya ma, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa wo tan naxee xilixi.

sentences.english: To all those who are in Rome, loved by God, marked out as saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
sentences.susu: N yi sɛbɛfe wo tan Rɔmakae nan ma Ala naxee xanuxi, a naxee xilixi wo xa findi a xa sɛniyɛntɔɛe ra. Won Baba Ala nun a xa Mixi Sugandixi Marigi Isa xa hinnɛ nun bɔɲɛsa fi wo ma.

sentences.english: First of all, I give praise to my God through Jesus Christ for you all, because news of your faith has gone into all the world.
sentences.susu: A fɔlɛ ra, n nan n Marigi Ala tantuma nɛ wo birin xa fe ra a xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa saabui ra, barima wo xa danxaniya xili bara din duniɲa birin na.

sentences.english: For God is my witness, whose servant I am in spirit in the good news of his Son, that you are at all times in my memory and in my prayers,
sentences.susu: N Marigi Ala, n naxan batuma n nii birin na n to a xa Di xa xibaaru fanyi rayensenma, a tan a kolon a n na nɔndi nan falafe wo bɛ. A tan nan n seede ra, fa a fala, n a maxandima wo bɛ tɛmui birin.

sentences.english: And that I am ever making prayers that God will give me a good journey to you.
sentences.susu: N man Ala maxandima, xa a sago na a ra, a xa a niya n xa nɔ sigade wo xɔnyi fa.

sentences.english: For I have a strong desire to see you, and to give you some grace of the spirit, so that you may be made strong;
sentences.susu: Barima wo to xɔli na n ma ki fanyi, alako n xa nɔ wo sɛnbɛ sode Ala xa ki ndee ra.

sentences.english: That is to say, that all of us may be comforted together by the faith which is in you and in me.
sentences.susu: A xɔli n ma won xa won bore ralimaniya won ma danxaniya saabui ra, won birin xa sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ won bore ra.

sentences.english: You may be certain, my brothers, that it has frequently been in my mind to come to you (but till now I was kept from it), so that I might have some fruit from you in the same way as I have had it from the other nations.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, n wama wo xa a kolon a sanmaya wuyaxi nan yi ki n bara natɛ tongo n xa siga wo xɔnyi n xa sa n ma wali tide nde to wo tagi alɔ n a toxi ki naxɛ ɲamanɛ gbɛtɛe tagi, kɔnɔ han to a mu sɔɔnɛya n bɛ.

sentences.english: I have a debt to Greeks and to the nations outside; to the wise and to those who have no learning.
sentences.susu: Fo n xa wɔyɛn mixi birin bɛ, taa idɔxɔɛe nun daaxa idɔxɔɛe, xaran mixie nun xarantaree.

sentences.english: For which reason I have the desire, as far as I am able, to give the knowledge of the good news to you who are in Rome.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra a xɔli n ma ki fanyi n xa xibaaru fanyi kawandi wo tan Rɔmakae fan bɛ.

sentences.english: For I have no feeling of shame about the good news, because it is the power of God giving salvation to everyone who has faith, to the Jew first, and then to the Greek.
sentences.susu: N mu yaagima Marigi xa xibaaru fanyi masende mixi yo bɛ, barima a tan nan saabui a niyama Ala danxaniyatɔɛ birin nakisima. Yi kisi fixi Yuwifie nan singe ma, a fa fi si gbɛtɛe fan ma.

sentences.english: For in it there is the revelation of the righteousness of God from faith to faith: as it is said in the holy Writings, The man who does righteousness will be living by his faith.
sentences.susu: Yi xibaaru fanyi bara a makɛnɛn a tinxinyi naxan kelima Ala ma a sɔtɔma danxaniya nan tun saabui ra, alɔ a sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui ki naxɛ: «Mixi tinxinxi kisima danxaniya nan saabui ra.»

sentences.english: For there is a revelation of the wrath of God from heaven against all the wrongdoing and evil thoughts of men who keep down what is true by wrongdoing;
sentences.susu: Ala xa xɔnɛ goroma keli koore tinxintaree nun kaafirie xili ma. Yi mixie nɔndi nɔxunma e xa tinxintareya saabui ra.

sentences.english: Because the knowledge of God may be seen in them, God having made it clear to them.
sentences.susu: Anun mixi nɔma naxan kolonde Ala xa fe kui, a fiixɛxi e bɛ fɔɛn, barima Ala bara a makɛnɛn e bɛ.

sentences.english: For from the first making of the world, those things of God which the eye is unable to see, that is, his eternal power and existence, are fully made clear, he having given the knowledge of them through the things which he has made, so that men have no reason for wrongdoing:
sentences.susu: Kabi duniɲa daa tɛmui, Ala naxan mu toma, a naxa a yɛtɛ masen. Adamadi birin nɔma a kolonde a Ala na na yati, naxan sɛnbɛ mu danma, barima yi bara makɛnɛn e bɛ a fiixɛ ra a xa wali fɔxi saabui ra. Na kui, tinxintaree mu nɔma sese falade naxan kiiti fanma e bɛ,

sentences.english: Because, having the knowledge of God, they did not give glory to God as God, and did not give praise, but their minds were full of foolish things, and their hearts, being without sense, were made dark.
sentences.susu: barima hali e to Ala kolonxi, e bara tondi a tantude, e tondi a binyade a xa mangɛya kui. E xaxili bara bira fe fufafu fɔxɔ ra, e bɔɲɛ bara lu dimi kui.

sentences.english: Seeming to be wise, they were in fact foolish,
sentences.susu: E e yɛtɛ matɔxɔma e xa xaxilimaya ra, kɔnɔ e bara findi daxuie ra.

sentences.english: And by them the glory of the eternal God was changed and made into the image of man who is not eternal, and of birds and beasts and things which go on the earth.
sentences.susu: E bara tondi Ala batude naxan na na abadan, e kuye masolixie batu naxee misaalixi adamadi ra naxan faxama, a nun naxee misaalixi xɔni, sube, nun bubuse ra.

sentences.english: For this reason God gave them up to the evil desires of their hearts, working shame in their bodies with one another:
sentences.susu: Na nan a niya Ala naxa e rabolo e xa yunubi fee kui, e bɔɲɛ kɛnɛnyi ma. Na kui, e naxa fe mayaagixie raba e bore ra.

sentences.english: Because by them the true word of God was changed into that which is false, and they gave worship and honour to the thing which is made, and not to him who made it, to whom be blessing for ever. So be it.
sentences.susu: E naxa Ala xa nɔndi masara wule ra, e man fa daali batu, beenun e xa Daali Mangɛ nan batu, a tan naxan lan a xa batu abadan. Amina.

sentences.english: For this reason God gave them up to evil passions, and their women were changing the natural use into one which is unnatural:
sentences.susu: Na na a ra Ala naxa e rabolo e xa bira e waxɔnfe mayaagixie fɔxɔ ra. E xa ginɛe naxa e nun xɛmɛ xa kafuɲɔxɔya masara ginɛ firin xa kafuɲɔxɔya ra.

sentences.english: And in the same way the men gave up the natural use of the woman and were burning in their desire for one another, men doing shame with men, and getting in their bodies the right reward of their evil-doing.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛe fan naxa mɛɛ ginɛe xa kafuɲɔxɔya ra, e fa bira e boore xɛmɛe kafuɲɔxɔya fɔxɔ ra. E naxa fe mayaagixie raba e bore ra, e e xa wali kobi sare sɔtɔ naxan daxa.

sentences.english: And because they had not the mind to keep God in their knowledge, God gave them up to an evil mind, to do those things which are not right;
sentences.susu: E to tondi Ala kolonde Ala ra, a naxa e rabolo e yɛtɛ kan xaxili kobie yi, e nu fee raba naxee mu radaxa.

sentences.english: Being full of all wrongdoing, evil, desire for the goods of others, hate, envy, putting to death, fighting, deceit, cruel ways, evil talk, and false statements about others;
sentences.susu: E bɔɲɛ rafexi tinxintareya mɔɔli birin na: wali kobi rabafe, wasatareya, ɲaaxuɲa. Milanteya, mixi faxafe, mixi tagi isofe, mixi mayendenfe, nun ya ixareya mu ɲɔnma e tagi.

sentences.english: Hated by God, full of pride, without respect, full of loud talk, given to evil inventions, not honouring father or mother,
sentences.susu: Naafixie, mixi mafalɛe, Ala yaxuie, konbitie, yɛtɛ igboee nun dɛ igboee nan e ra. E fe kobie xabuma naxee singe mu nu kolon, e ɲan mu e barimixie danxunma.

sentences.english: Without knowledge, not true to their undertakings, unkind, having no mercy:
sentences.susu: Xaxilitare, dugutɛgɛ yanfɛ, kinikinitare, nun hinnɛtare nan na e ra.

sentences.english: Who, though they have knowledge of the law of God, that the fate of those who do these things is death, not only go on doing these things themselves, but give approval to those who do them.
sentences.susu: Ala xa sɛriyɛ a masenxi nɛ, a naxee na fee rabama, faxɛ nan daxaxi e bɛ. Hali e to na kolon, e na fe haramuxie nan yati rabama, e man mixi ralimaniyama naxee fan na fe mɔɔli rabama.

sentences.english: So you have no reason, whoever you are, for judging: for in judging another you are judging yourself, for you do the same things.
sentences.susu: Na kui, xa i mixi yuge makiitima, diɲɛ yo mu na i bɛ, i findi mixi yo ra. I nɛ i boore yuge makiitima, i na i yɛtɛ nan safe geeli, barima i tan naxan mixi yuge makiitima, wo birin wali kobi keren nan xun ma.

sentences.english: And we are conscious that God is a true judge against those who do such things.
sentences.susu: Won birin a kolon a Ala xa kiiti tinxin a na yi mixi mɔɔlie xa wali kobie sare fi.

sentences.english: But you who are judging another for doing what you do yourself, are you hoping that God's decision will not take effect against you?
sentences.susu: I tan naxan mixi yuge makiitima, a man fa li wo birin na wali kobi keren nan xun ma, i ɲɔxɔ a ma a i fama tangade Ala xa kiiti ma?

sentences.english: Or is it nothing to you that God had pity on you, waiting and putting up with you for so long, not seeing that in his pity God's desire is to give you a change of heart?
sentences.susu: Ka i yoxi nɛ Ala ma ba, a xa fanyi nun a xa diɲɛ nun a xa bɔɲɛ bɛxi to gboxi? I mu a kolon a Ala a xa fanyi nan masenma i bɛ alako i xa tuubi?

sentences.english: But by your hard and unchanged heart you are storing up wrath for yourself in the day of the revelation of God's judging in righteousness;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i to i tuli xɔrɔxɔxi, i tondi tuubide, i na Ala xa xɔnɛ nan nagbofe i yɛtɛ xili ma kiiti sa lɔxɔɛ, Ala xa kiiti tinxinxi makɛnɛnma tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: Who will give to every man his right reward:
sentences.susu: Ala kankan xa wali sare fima nɛ.

sentences.english: To those who go on with good works in the hope of glory and honour and salvation from death, he will give eternal life:
sentences.susu: Naxee e tunnabɛxi wali fanyi rabafe ma, e xunnakeli, yigi, nun kisi fen Ala ra, Ala kisi fima nɛ e ma.

sentences.english: But to those who, from a love of competition, are not guided by what is true, will come the heat of his wrath,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naxee e yɛtɛ kɛnɛnfe tun nabama, e tondi nɔndi nun tinxinyi ra, e bira fe kobi fɔxɔ ra, Ala xa xɔnɛ nun gbaloe nan tun nagataxi e bɛ.

sentences.english: Trouble and sorrow on all whose works are evil, to the Jew first and then to the Greek;
sentences.susu: Ɲaxankatɛ nun bɔɲɛkanɛ nan luma adamadi birin bɛ naxee fe kobi rabama, a fɔlɔ Yuwifie ma, a sa dɔxɔ si gbɛtɛe ra.

sentences.english: But glory and honour and peace to all whose works are good, to the Jew first and then to the Greek:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xunnakeli, binyɛ, nun bɔɲɛsa luma mixi birin bɛ naxee fe fanyi rabama, a fɔlɔ Yuwifie ma, a sa dɔxɔ si gbɛtɛe ra,

sentences.english: For one man is not different from another before God.
sentences.susu: barima Ala tan mu mixi yo rafisa a boore bɛ.

sentences.english: All those who have done wrong without the law will get destruction without the law: and those who have done wrong under the law will have their punishment by the law;
sentences.susu: Yunubitɔɛe naxee birin mu Ala xa sɛriyɛ kolon Annabi Munsa naxan fixi, e bɔnɔma nɛ, kɔnɔ e mu makiitima na sɛriyɛ ra. Yunubitɔɛe naxee sɛriyɛ kolon Annabi Munsa naxan fixi, e tan nan makiitima na sɛriyɛ ra.

sentences.english: For it is not the hearers of the law who will be judged as having righteousness before God, but only the doers:
sentences.susu: Naxee e tuli matima Ala xa sɛriyɛ ra, nee xa mu findixi tinxintɔɛe ra Ala ya i. Naxee Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatuma, nee nan findima tinxintɔɛe ra.

sentences.english: For when the Gentiles without the law have a natural desire to do the things in the law, they are a law to themselves;
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa mu Ala xa sɛriyɛ so si gbɛtɛe yi, naxee mu findi Yuwifie ra. Kɔnɔ e na Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatu tɛmui naxɛ e yɛtɛ ɲanige ma, e bara a kolon a lanma e xa naxan naba, hali e to mu Ala xa sɛriyɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Because the work of the law is seen in their hearts, their sense of right and wrong giving witness to it, while their minds are at one time judging them and at another giving them approval;
sentences.susu: E bara a masen a Ala xa sɛriyɛ sɛbɛxi e bɔɲɛ ma. Won a kolon a nɔndi na a ra barima e xaxili e rasima, «Yi ɲanige mu fan,» xa na mu, «Yi ɲanige nan fan.»

sentences.english: In the day when God will be a judge of the secrets of men, as it says in the good news of which I am a preacher, through Jesus Christ.
sentences.susu: A rabama na ki nɛ, Ala nɛ kiiti sama lɔxɔ naxɛ a xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa saabui ra, a mixie gundo birin makiiti. N xibaaru fanyi naxan kawandima, a na nan masenxi.

sentences.english: But as for you who have the name of Jew, and are resting on the law, and take pride in God,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ i tan naxɛ a Yuwifi nan na i ra. I xaxili tixi Munsa xa Sɛriyɛ nan na. I a maɲɔxunxi a i kisima na nan saabui ra. I to bara Ala kolon, na na a ra i i yɛtɛ igboma.

sentences.english: And have knowledge of his desires, and are a judge of the things which are different, having the learning of the law,
sentences.susu: I Ala sago kolon. I fata fe fanyi sugandide barima i Ala xa sɛriyɛ xaranxi.

sentences.english: In the belief that you are a guide to the blind, a light to those in the dark,
sentences.susu: I laxi a ra a i tan nan findixi dɔnxuie raɲɛrɛma ra, a i tan nan findixi tɛ radɛxɛ ra mixie bɛ naxee na dimi kui.

sentences.english: A teacher of the foolish, having in the law the form of knowledge and of what is true;
sentences.susu: I laxi a ra a i tan nan findixi xaxilitaree rasima nun dimɛe karamɔxɔe ra, barima lɔnni nun nɔndi birin na i yi ra i to diinɛ sɛriyɛ kolonxi.

sentences.english: You who give teaching to others, do you give it to yourself? you who say that a man may not take what is not his, do you take what is not yours?
sentences.susu: I tan naxan boore xaranma, i mu i yɛtɛ xaranma! I tan naxan mixie tuli ibama muɲɛ tife ra, i muɲɛ tima!

sentences.english: You who say that a man may not be untrue to his wife, are you true to yours? you who are a hater of images, do you do wrong to the house of God?
sentences.susu: I tan naxan a falama a mixie naxa yɛnɛ raba, i yɛnɛ rabama! I tan naxan yele na kuye batufe ra, i kuye batude see muɲama!

sentences.english: You who take pride in the law, are you doing wrong to the honour of God by behaviour which is against the law?
sentences.susu: I tan naxan i yɛtɛ igboma i to Ala xa sɛriyɛ kolonxi, i na Ala yelebufe nɛ na ki, i na a xa sɛriyɛ matandife!

sentences.english: For the name of God is shamed among the Gentiles because of you, as it is said in the holy Writings.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, a sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, «Si gbɛtɛe Ala bɛxuma wo tan Isirayilakae xa fe ra.»

sentences.english: It is true that circumcision is of use if you keep the law, but if you go against the law it is as if you had it not.
sentences.susu: Sunnɛ tide na na nɛ xa i sa Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatuxi. Kɔnɔ xa i sa a xa sɛriyɛ matandima, i xa sunnɛ bara findi i bɛ sunnatareya ra.

sentences.english: If those who have not circumcision keep the rules of the law, will it not be credited to them as circumcision?
sentences.susu: Na kui, xa a sa li sunnatare sa ɲɛrɛ Ala xa sɛriyɛ ma, a a rabatu, a xa sunnatareya mu findima a bɛ sunnɛ xa ra?

sentences.english: And they, by their keeping of the law without circumcision, will be judges of you, by whom the law is broken though you have the letter of the law and circumcision.
sentences.susu: Naxee mu sunnaxi e fate bɛndɛ ma, kɔnɔ e Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatuxi, nee wali ki nan fama i makiitide. Mixi sunnaxi nan i ra, Ala xa sɛriyɛ sɛbɛxi na i yi, kɔnɔ i Ala xa sɛriyɛ matandima.

sentences.english: The true Jew is not one who is only so publicly, and circumcision is not that which may be seen in the flesh:
sentences.susu: I naxan masenma kɛnɛ ma mixie ya i, na xa mu i findixi Yuwifi ra. Tɔnxuma naxan toma i fate ma, na xa mu a masenxi a i sunnaxi yati.

sentences.english: But he is a Jew who is a secret one, whose circumcision is of the heart, in the spirit and not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.
sentences.susu: Mixi findife Yuwifi ra, na kolonma bɔɲɛ nan ma. Sunnɛ yɛtɛ yɛtɛ fan, sunnɛ na a ra naxan sɔtɔma bɔɲɛ ma, Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra. A mu kelima diinɛ sɛriyɛ sɛbɛxi xa ma. Sunnɛ na mixi naxan bɔɲɛ ma, a xa matɔxɔɛ mu kelima mixi xa ma, a kelima Ala nan ma.

sentences.english: How then is the Jew better off? or what profit is there in circumcision?
sentences.susu: Tide mundun fa na findife Yuwifi ra? Sunnɛ tide na na yire?

sentences.english: Much in every way: first of all because the words of God were given to them.
sentences.susu: Iyo, yi fee tide gbo ki fanyi. A fɔlɛ ra, Ala a xa masenyi taxu Yuwifie nan na.

sentences.english: And if some have no faith, will that make the faith of God without effect?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa li go, ndee na e ya ma e kobe rasoxi Ala ra, na nɔma a niyade Ala fan xa a kobe raso e ra?

sentences.english: In no way: but let God be true, though every man is seen to be untrue; as it is said in the Writings, That your words may be seen to be true, and you may be seen to be right when you are judged.
sentences.susu: Astɔfulahi. Adamadi birin findixi wule falɛ nan na, kɔnɔ a xa kolon a Ala nɔndi kanyi mu nɔma wule falade. A sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui: «Na kui, i xa wɔyɛnyi findima nɔndi nan na. Kiiti luma i tan nan bɛ tɛmui birin.»

sentences.english: But if the righteousness of God is supported by our wrongdoing what is to be said? is it wrong for God to be angry (as men may say)?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa won ma tinxintareya fa a masenma nɛ mixie bɛ a Ala tinxin, won fa na ma di? Ala na xɔnɔ won ma, won xa a fala a mu tinxin? (N wɔyɛnfe nɛ alɔ mixie wɔyɛnma ki naxɛ.)

sentences.english: In no way: because if it is so, how is God able to be the judge of all the world?
sentences.susu: Astɔfulahi! Xa Ala mu tinxin, a duniɲa makiitima di?

sentences.english: But if, because I am untrue, God being seen to be true gets more glory, why am I to be judged as a sinner?
sentences.susu: Nde nɔma a falade, «Xa n ma wule Ala xa nɔndi makɛnɛnma duniɲa bɛ alako Ala xa tantui sɔtɔ, munfe ra a fa n findima yunubitɔɛ ra?»

sentences.english: Let us not do evil so that good may come (a statement which we are falsely said by some to have made), because such behaviour will have its right punishment.
sentences.susu: Won ɲan xa a fala, «Won xa fe ɲaaxi raba alako a xa sa findi fe fanyi ra.» Muxu xili kanɛe na nan falama muxu xun ma, a muxu xa masenyi nan na ki. Kɔnɔ Ala na e makiiti, e fan e sare sɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: What then? are we worse off than they? In no way: because we have before made it clear that Jews as well as Greeks are all under the power of sin;
sentences.susu: Won munse falama fa? Won xa a fala a won tan Yuwifie tinxin dangi si gbɛtɛe ra? Ade, na mu a ra feo, barima alɔ won ɲan bara a to, Yuwifie ba, si gbɛtɛe ba, birin na yunubi nan xa nɔɛ bun ma.

sentences.english: As it is said in the holy Writings, There is not one who does righteousness;
sentences.susu: A sɛbɛxi: «Mixi yo mu tinxin, hali mixi keren.

sentences.english: Not one who has the knowledge of what is right, not one who is a searcher after God;
sentences.susu: Fe kolonyi yo mu na, mixi yo mu Ala fenfe.

sentences.english: They have all gone out of the way, there is no profit in any of them; there is not one who does good, not so much as one:
sentences.susu: Birin bara kira fanyi bɛɲin, e birin xun bara rakana. Mixi yo mu na naxan fe fanyi rabama, hali mixi keren, a mu na.

sentences.english: Their throat is like an open place of death; with their tongues they have said what is not true: the poison of snakes is under their lips:
sentences.susu: E dɛ findixi gaburi dɛ ibixi nan na, e nɛnyi findixi mixi mayenden se nan na. Bɔximase xɔnɛ nan minima e dɛ kiri ra,

sentences.english: Whose mouth is full of curses and bitter words:
sentences.susu: dankɛ nun wɔyɛn xɔnɛ nan e dɛ rafexi.

sentences.english: Their feet are quick in running after blood;
sentences.susu: E sanyi xulun wuli raminife ra,

sentences.english: Destruction and trouble are in their ways;
sentences.susu: e dangi dɛdɛ, e kanari nun nimisɛ nan luma e xanbi ra.

sentences.english: And of the way of peace they have no knowledge:
sentences.susu: E mu bɔɲɛsa kira kolon,

sentences.english: There is no fear of God before their eyes.
sentences.susu: e mu Ala yaragaaxui kolon.»

sentences.english: Now, we have knowledge that what the law says is for those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and all men may be judged by God:
sentences.susu: Won a kolon Ala xa sɛriyɛ naxan birin masenxi, a a masenxi mixie nan bɛ naxee na a xa sɛriyɛ nɔɛ bun ma, alako dɛ birin xa balan, sɛriyɛ xa birin suxu Ala ya i.

sentences.english: Because by the works of the law no man is able to have righteousness in his eyes, for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
sentences.susu: Na kui, adamadi yo mu findima tinxintɔɛ ra Ala ya i sɛriyɛ rabatufe saabui ra, barima sɛriyɛ tan yunubi nan tun makɛnɛnma, adamadi xa a kolon a yunubitɔɛ na a ra.

sentences.english: But now without the law there is a revelation of the righteousness of God, to which witness is given by the law and the prophets;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yakɔsi, tinxinyi bara makɛnɛn naxan mu kelima sɛriyɛ rabatufe ma. A kelima Ala yɛtɛ nan ma, alɔ a sɛbɛxi sɛriyɛ nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa Kitaabuie kui ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: That is, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, to all those who have faith; and one man is not different from another,
sentences.susu: Yi tinxinyi naxan kelima Ala ma a sɔtɔma danxaniya nan saabui ra, birin a sɔtɔ naxee danxaniyaxi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa ma. Ala mu mixi yo rafisaxi a boore bɛ,

sentences.english: For all have done wrong and are far from the glory of God;
sentences.susu: barima birin findixi yunubitɔɛ nan na, birin bara gan Ala xa nɔrɛ ra,

sentences.english: And they may have righteousness put to their credit, freely, by his grace, through the salvation which is in Christ Jesus:
sentences.susu: birin tinxinyi sɔtɔma Ala xa hinnɛ nan tun saabui ra. Ala adama kima yi tinxinyi ra won xunsarama Isa nan saabui ra, a xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: Whom God has put forward as the sign of his mercy, through faith, by his blood, to make clear his righteousness when, in his pity, God let the sins of earlier times go without punishment;
sentences.susu: Ala a tan nan findi sɛrɛxɛ ra, a wuli raminixi nɛ alako naxee na danxaniya a ma, e xa yunubie xa xafari. Yi a masenxi nɛ a Ala tinxin, barima a xa diɲɛ kui, a nu bara adamadie xa yunubie lu na e mu makiiti, e naxee rabaxi waxati dangixi.

sentences.english: And to make clear his righteousness now, so that he might himself be upright, and give righteousness to him who has faith in Jesus.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yi waxati Ala bara a xa tinxinyi masen alako birin xa a kolon a a tinxin, e man xa a kolon a a tan nan tinxinyi fima mixi ma naxan danxaniyaxi Isa ma.

sentences.english: What reason, then, is there for pride? It is shut out. By what sort of law? of works? No, but by a law of faith.
sentences.susu: Na kui, mixi fa a yɛtɛ igboma munse xa fe ra? Fefe! Munfe ra? Mixi nɔma a yɛtɛ matɔxɔde a to diinɛ sɛriyɛ rabatuxi? Ade, barima tinxinyi sɔtɔma danxaniya nan tun saabui ra.

sentences.english: For this reason, then, a man may get righteousness by faith without the works of the law.
sentences.susu: Won a kolon a danxaniya nan mixi matinxinma Ala ya i, sɛriyɛ xa kɛwalie xa mu a ra.

sentences.english: Or is God the God of Jews only? is he not in the same way the God of Gentiles? Yes, of Gentiles:
sentences.susu: Ka Ala findixi Yuwifie gbansan nan Marigi Ala ra? Si gbɛtɛe fan Marigi Ala xa mu a ra? Iyo, si gbɛtɛe fan Marigi Ala nan yati a ra,

sentences.english: If God is one; and he will give righteousness because of faith to those who have circumcision, and through faith to those who have not circumcision.
sentences.susu: barima Ala keren peti na a ra. A tan nan mixi sunnaxie matinxinma a ya i danxaniya saabui ra, a man tinxinyi fima sunnataree fan ma na danxaniya kerenyi nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: Do we, then, through faith make the law of no effect? in no way: but we make it clear that the law is important.
sentences.susu: Won fa na ma di? Won xa a fala a Ala xa sɛriyɛ tide mu na won to danxaniyaxi Isa ma? Astɔfulahi! Won ɲan bara Ala xa sɛriyɛ tide ramini.

sentences.english: What, then, may we say that Abraham, our father after the flesh, has got?
sentences.susu: Won xa misaali tongo Iburahima ma, won tan Yuwifie benba. A munse kolon yi xa fe ra?

sentences.english: For if Abraham got righteousness by works, he has reason for pride; but not before God.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li nu Iburahima findi tinxintɔɛ ra a xa wali nan saabui ra, a nu nɔma a yɛtɛ matɔxɔde, kɔnɔ Ala tan ya i mu a ra.

sentences.english: But what does it say in the holy Writings? And Abraham had faith in God, and it was put to his account as righteousness.
sentences.susu: Kitaabui munse falaxi na xa fe ra? «Iburahima naxa danxaniya Ala ma, Ala naxa na findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ.»

sentences.english: Now, the reward is credited to him who does works, not as of grace but as a debt.
sentences.susu: Walikɛ na a sare sɔtɔ, na mu findima a bɛ ki xa ra, barima a xa wali sare na a ra a lanma a xa naxan sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: But to him who without working has faith in him who gives righteousness to the evil-doer, his faith is put to his account as righteousness.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan xaxili mu tixi a xa wali ra, naxan danxaniyaxi Marigi ma naxan mixi kobi findima tinxintɔɛ ra, Ala na kanyi xa danxaniya findima a bɛ tinxinyi nan na.

sentences.english: As David says that there is a blessing on the man to whose account God puts righteousness without works, saying,
sentences.susu: Dawuda fan a masen nɛ a hɛɛri na mixi bɛ Ala bara naxan findi tinxintɔɛ ra a ya i, bafe a xa walie ra:

sentences.english: Happy are those who have forgiveness for their wrongdoing, and whose sins are covered.
sentences.susu: «Hɛɛri na mixie bɛ, Ala bara diɲɛ naxee xa wali kobie ma, naxee xa yunubie bara xafari.

sentences.english: Happy is the man against whom no sin is recorded by the Lord.
sentences.susu: Hɛɛri na mixi bɛ, Ala mu naxan xa yunubi rabaxi maxɔrinma.»

sentences.english: Is this blessing, then, for the circumcision only, or in the same way for those who have not circumcision? for we say that the faith of Abraham was put to his account as righteousness.
sentences.susu: Na kui, yi hɛɛri naxan ma fe falaxi, mixi sunnaxie gbansan nan a sɔtɔma, ka mixi sunnataree fan nɔma a sɔtɔde? Won ɲan bara a fala a Iburahima to danxaniya Ala ma, Ala a xa danxaniya nan findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ.

sentences.english: How, then, was it judged? when he had circumcision, or when he had it not? Not when he had it, but when he did not have it:
sentences.susu: Na rabaxi a bɛ mun tɛmui? A to nu sunnaxi ba, ka a to mu nu sunnaxi? Ala na rabaxi a bɛ tɛmui naxɛ, Iburahima mu nu sunnaxi.

sentences.english: And he was given the sign of circumcision as a witness of the faith which he had before he underwent circumcision: so that he might be the father of all those who have faith, though they have not circumcision, and so that righteousness might be put to their account;
sentences.susu: Na xanbi, a naxa sunna alako a xa findi tɔnxuma ra naxan a masenma a Ala bara a xa danxaniya findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ beenun a xa sunna. Na kui, a naxa findi danxaniyatɔɛ birin benba ra naxee mu sunnaxi, Ala bara naxee xa danxaniya findi tinxinyi ra e bɛ.

sentences.english: And the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who keep to the way of that faith which our father Abraham had before he underwent circumcision.
sentences.susu: A tan nan findixi mixi sunnaxie fan benba ra naxee mu e xaxili tima e xa sunnɛ ra, kɔnɔ naxee man ɲɛrɛma danxaniya kui alɔ won benba Iburahima ɲɛrɛ ki naxɛ beenun a xa sunna.

sentences.english: For God's word, that the earth would be his heritage, was given to Abraham, not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
sentences.susu: Ala laayidi tongo nɛ Iburahima nun a bɔnsɔɛ bɛ, a e fama duniɲa sɔtɔde kɛ ra. Kɔnɔ na laayidi mu keli a xa diinɛ sɛriyɛ rabatufe xa ma. A kelixi tinxinyi nan ma a naxan sɔtɔ danxaniya saabui ra.

sentences.english: For if they who are of the law are the people who get the heritage, then faith is made of no use, and the word of God has no power;
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li nu sɛriyɛ rabatufe nan a niyama mixie xa findi kɛtongoe ra, danxaniya tide yo mu luma na fa, Ala xa laayidi fan bara kana na tɛmui.

sentences.english: For the outcome of the law is wrath; but where there is no law it will not be broken.
sentences.susu: Barima sɛriyɛ fama Ala xa xɔnɛ nan na, kɔnɔ sɛriyɛ mu na dɛnnaxɛ, sɛriyɛ matandi fan mu na.

sentences.english: For this reason it is of faith, so that it may be through grace; and so that the word of God may be certain to all the seed; not only to that which is of the law, but to that which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,
sentences.susu: Na kui, Ala xa laayidi sɔtɔma danxaniya nan saabui ra, alako a xa findi Ala xa hinnɛ ra Iburahima xa die birin bɛ, birin xa a sɔtɔ. A mu findima sɛriyɛ rabatumae gbansan xa gbe ra, kɔnɔ birin gbe na a ra naxee danxaniyaxi alɔ Iburahima. A bara findi won birin benba ra

sentences.english: (As it is said in the holy Writings, I have made you a father of a number of nations) before him in whom he had faith, that is, God, who gives life to the dead, and to whom the things which are not are as if they were.
sentences.susu: alɔ a sɛbɛxi ki naxɛ, «N bara i findi si gbegbe benba ra.» A findixi won benba ra Ala nan ya i, a danxaniya naxan ma, naxan nii rasoma faxamixie fate, naxan se birin daaxi.

sentences.english: Who without reason for hope, in faith went on hoping, so that he became the father of a number of nations, as it had been said, So will your seed be.
sentences.susu: Iburahima to danxaniya, a naxa la a ra a Ala fama a xa laayidi rakamalide alɔ a falaxi a bɛ ki naxɛ, «I bɔnsɔɛ wuyama yi ki nɛ.» A naxa a xaxili ti na ra hali a ya to mu nu tixi sese ra naxan a masenma a bɛ a na fe fama nɛ rakamalide. Na kui, a naxa findi si gbegbe benba ra.

sentences.english: And not being feeble in faith though his body seemed to him little better than dead (he being about a hundred years old) and Sarah was no longer able to have children:
sentences.susu: Iburahima nu bara simaya ɲɛ kɛmɛ ɲɔndɔn sɔtɔ, a xa simaya nu bara xurun, a xa ginɛ Sara fan mu nu nɔma di baride sɔnɔn. Kɔnɔ hali a to na birin fahaamu, sese mu ba Iburahima xa danxaniya ra.

sentences.english: Still, he did not give up faith in the undertaking of God, but was made strong by faith, giving glory to God,
sentences.susu: A mu siikɛ Ala xa laayidi ma, a xa danxaniya ɲan naxa sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ, a nu Ala batu.

sentences.english: And being certain that God was able to keep his word.
sentences.susu: A nu laxi a ra feo, a Ala nɔma a xa laayidi rakamalide.

sentences.english: For which reason it was put to his account as righteousness.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra «Ala naxa na findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ.»

sentences.english: Now, it was not because of him only that this was said,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Kitaabui naxan masenxi a falafe ra, «Ala naxa na findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ,» na mu sɛbɛ Iburahima gbansan xa bɛ.

sentences.english: But for us in addition, to whose account it will be put, if we have faith in him who made Jesus our Lord come back again from the dead,
sentences.susu: A sɛbɛxi won tan nan fan yati bɛ, won tan naxee danxaniyaxi Ala ma naxan won Marigi Isa rakeli faxɛ ma. Ala won fan ma danxaniya findima nɛ tinxinyi ra won bɛ.

sentences.english: Who was put to death for our evil-doing, and came to life again so that we might have righteousness.
sentences.susu: Won Marigi faxa won ma yunubie nan ma fe ra, a man naxa keli faxɛ ma, alako won xa findi tinxintɔɛe ra Ala ya i.

sentences.english: For which reason, because we have righteousness through faith, let us be at peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
sentences.susu: Na kui won to bara findi tinxintɔɛe ra Ala ya i danxaniya saabui ra, lanyi nun bɔɲɛsa bara lu won nun Ala tagi won Marigi Isa saabui ra, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: Through whom, in the same way, we have been able by faith to come to this grace in which we now are; and let us have joy in hope of the glory of God.
sentences.susu: Won ma danxaniya Marigi Isa ma, na bara won naso Ala xa hinnɛ kui won fa sabatixi naxan ma. Won sɛɛwaxi nan fa a ra won xaxili to tixi Ala xa nɔrɛ ra.

sentences.english: And not only so, but let us have joy in our troubles: in the knowledge that trouble gives us the power of waiting;
sentences.susu: Dangi na fan na, won man sɛɛwama won ma tɔɔrɛ kui, barima won a kolon a tɔɔrɛ duluxɔtɔya nan naminima.

sentences.english: And waiting gives experience; and experience, hope:
sentences.susu: Won ma tunnabɛxi fan a niyama nɛ won xa yuge fanyi sɔtɔ naxan Ala kɛnɛnma. Na yuge mɔɔli fan a niyama nɛ won xa won xaxili ti Ala ra.

sentences.english: And hope does not put to shame; because our hearts are full of the love of God through the Holy Spirit which is given to us.
sentences.susu: Won man mu yaagima won xaxili to tixi Ala ra, barima Ala bara a xa xanunteya xɛlɛ won bɔɲɛ kui a Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra a bara naxan fi won ma.

sentences.english: For when we were still without strength, at the right time Christ gave his life for evil-doers.
sentences.susu: Waxati to kamali, won sɛnbɛ yo mu nu na tɛmui naxɛ, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi naxa faxa yunubitɔɛe bɛ.

sentences.english: Now it is hard for anyone to give his life even for an upright man, though it might be that for a good man someone would give his life.
sentences.susu: A xɔrɔxɔ ki fanyi mixi diɲɛfe a nii ma tinxin mixi xa fe ra. Kɔnɔ tɛmunde, mixi nde fan nɔma limaniyade a xa faxamixi fanyi nde bɛ.

sentences.english: But God has made clear his love to us, in that, when we were still sinners, Christ gave his life for us.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Ala a xa xanunteya masenxi won bɛ yi nan na: Won nu findixi yunubitɔɛe ra tɛmui naxɛ, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi naxa diɲɛ a nii ma won ma fe ra.

sentences.english: Much more, if we now have righteousness by his blood, will salvation from the wrath of God come to us through him.
sentences.susu: Na kui, won to bara findi tinxintɔɛe ra Ala ya i Isa xa sɛrɛxɛ saabui ra, won xa a kolon a man mu taganma won nakiside Ala xa gbaloe ma.

sentences.english: For if, when we were haters of God, the death of his Son made us at peace with him, much more, now that we are his friends, will we have salvation through his life;
sentences.susu: Barima won nu findixi Ala yaxuie ra tɛmui naxɛ, a xa Di xa faxɛ saabui naxa won tagi yailan, yakɔsi won nun Ala tagi to bara yailan, won a kolon a won nakisima nɛ a xa Di xa kisi saabui ra.

sentences.english: And not only so, but we have joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we are now at peace with God.
sentences.susu: Na man fari, won sɛɛwaxi nɛ Ala ra a xa Mixi Sugandixi Marigi Isa saabui ra, naxan bara won nun Ala tagi yailan.

sentences.english: For this reason, as through one man sin came into the world, and death because of sin, and so death came to all men, because all have done evil:
sentences.susu: Na kui, yunubi naxa so duniɲa mixi keren saabui ra. Faxɛ fan naxa so duniɲa yunubi xa fe ra, a din mixi birin na barima adamadie birin bara yunubi raba.

sentences.english: Because, till the law came, sin was in existence, but sin is not put to the account of anyone when there is no law to be broken.
sentences.susu: Yunubi nu na duniɲa ma beenun Ala xa a xa sɛriyɛ fi Annabi Munsa ma, kɔnɔ xa sɛriyɛ mu na, yunubi fan mu na mixi yo ma.

sentences.english: But still death had power from Adam till Moses, even over those who had not done wrong like Adam, who is a picture of him who was to come.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ faxɛ tan nu na duniɲa ma, keli won benba Adama ma han Annabi Munsa, hali na mixie xa yunubi to mu nu luxi alɔ won benba Adama gbe naxan Ala xui yati matandi. Adama nu misaalixi mixi nan na naxan nu fafe.

sentences.english: But the free giving of God is not like the wrongdoing of man. For if, by the wrongdoing of one man death came to numbers of men, much more did the grace of God, and the free giving by the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, come to men.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Ala won kixi naxan na, na nun Benba Adama xa yunubi keren mu a ra. Iyo, adamadi gbegbe faxaxi yi mixi keren xa yunubi nan saabui ra, kɔnɔ Ala xa hinnɛ dangi na ra ki fanyi, barima a adamadie kixi a xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa naxan na, na bara mixi gbegbe rakisi a xa hinnɛ saabui ra.

sentences.english: And the free giving has not the same effect as the sin of one: for the effect of one man's sin was punishment by the decision of God, but the free giving had power to give righteousness to wrongdoers in great number.
sentences.susu: Adama xa yunubi nun Ala adamadie kixi naxan na, e fɔxi tagi ikuya. Mixi keren xa yunubi to makiiti, gbaloe nan fa. Kɔnɔ Ala adamadie kixi naxan na, a fa mixi gbegbe xa yunubi raba xanbi nɛ, a fa fɛɛrɛ ra mixi matinxinma ki naxɛ Ala ya i.

sentences.english: For, if by the wrongdoing of one, death was ruling through the one, much more will those to whom has come the wealth of grace and the giving of righteousness, be ruling in life through the one, even Jesus Christ.
sentences.susu: Mixi keren xa yunubi raba naxa a niya faxɛ xa nɔ duniɲa ra, kɔnɔ Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa wali fɔxi dangi na ra pon! Adamadie naxee bara Ala xa hinnɛ sɔtɔ naxan dande mu na, a nun a xa tinxinyi a won kixi naxan na, nee nɔɛ sɔtɔma kisi kui mixi keren nan saabui ra, naxan findi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa ra.

sentences.english: So then, as the effect of one act of wrongdoing was that punishment came on all men, even so the effect of one act of righteousness was righteousness of life for all men.
sentences.susu: Na kui, mixi keren xa yunubi naxa a niya adamadie birin xa lu yunubi xa gbaloe bun ma, kɔnɔ mixi keren xa wali tinxinxi nan man tinxinyi nun kisi fima adamadie birin ma.

sentences.english: Because, as numbers of men became sinners through the wrongdoing of one man, even so will great numbers get righteousness through the keeping of the word of God by one man.
sentences.susu: Alɔ mixi keren to Ala xa yaamari matandi, adamadi birin naxa findi yunubitɔɛe ra na mixi kerenyi saabui ra, adamadi gbegbe man findima tinxintɔɛe ra Ala ya i mixi keren nan fan saabui ra a to Ala xa yaamari rabatu.

sentences.english: And the law came in addition, to make wrongdoing worse; but where there was much sin, there was much more grace:
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛ fi nɛ yunubi xa gbo. Kɔnɔ yunubi to gbo, Ala xa hinnɛ naxa gbo ki fanyi dangi na ra!

sentences.english: That, as sin had power in death, so grace might have power through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
sentences.susu: Na kui, yunubi xa nɔɛ findixi faxɛ nan na, kɔnɔ Ala xa hinnɛ xa nɔɛ findima tinxinyi nan na alako mixi xa kisi abadan. Na birin nabama won Marigi Isa nan saabui ra, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: What may we say, then? are we to go on in sin so that there may be more grace?
sentences.susu: Won fa munse falama fa? Won man xa nu lu yunubi raba ra, alako Ala xa hinnɛ xun xa masa?

sentences.english: In no way. How may we, who are dead to sin, be living in it any longer?
sentences.susu: Astɔfulahi! Won bara won kobe so yunubi ra alɔ faxamixi a kobe soma duniɲa ra ki naxɛ. Won man fa nɔma ɲɛrɛde yunubi kui di?

sentences.english: Or are you without the knowledge that all we who had baptism into Christ Jesus, had baptism into his death?
sentences.susu: Won tan birin naxee bara won xunxa ye xɔɔra, won nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa nan fa a ra fa. Wo mu a kolon a won xunxafe ye xɔɔra na bara misaali Isa xa faxɛ ra?

sentences.english: We have been placed with him among the dead through baptism into death: so that as Christ came again from the dead by the glory of the Father, we, in the same way, might be living in new life.
sentences.susu: Won xunxafe ye xɔɔra saabui ra, won nun Marigi Isa bara faxa, won man bara sa gaburi a sɛɛti ma. Yi rabaxi nɛ alako won fan xa duniɲɛigiri nɛɛnɛ tongo, alɔ Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi keli faxamixie tagi ki naxɛ Baba Ala sɛnbɛ makaabaxi saabui ra.

sentences.english: For, if we have been made like him in his death, we will, in the same way, be like him in his coming to life again;
sentences.susu: Na kui, xa won nun Marigi Isa bara findi keren na won won xunxaxi ye xɔɔra tɛmui naxɛ a xa faxɛ ma misaali ra, won man fama nɛ rakelide faxɛ ma alɔ a tan.

sentences.english: Being conscious that our old man was put to death on the cross with him, so that the body of sin might be put away, and we might no longer be servants to sin.
sentences.susu: Won xa a kolon a won ma fe fori bara banban wuri magalanbuxi ma a nun Marigi Isa ra, alako won yuge fori xa masara naxan nu yunubi rabama, won naxa findi yunubi xa konyie ra sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: Because he who is dead is free from sin.
sentences.susu: Barima xa mixi bara faxa, a kanyi bara gbilen yunubi rabafe fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But if we are dead with Christ, we have faith that we will be living with him;
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi, xa won bara faxa won nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi, won man laxi a ra a won kisima nɛ won nun a tan,

sentences.english: Having knowledge that because Christ has come back from the dead, he will never again go down to the dead; death has no more power over him.
sentences.susu: barima won a kolon a Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi to bara rakeli faxɛ ma na ki a mu faxama sɔnɔn. Faxɛ xa nɔɛ yo mu na a fari sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: For his death was a death to sin, but his life now is a life which he is living to God.
sentences.susu: A to faxa, yunubi mu sese nɔma a ra sɔnɔn. A to bara rakeli faxɛ ma, a fa kisixi Ala nan bɛ.

sentences.english: Even so see yourselves as dead to sin, but living to God in Christ Jesus.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa wo yɛtɛ to faxamixi ra yunubi tan mabiri. Wo man to kisixi, wo bara findi Ala nan xa kisi mixi ra a xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa saabui ra.

sentences.english: For this cause do not let sin be ruling in your body which is under the power of death, so that you give way to its desires;
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi a mu lan yunubi xa nɔ wo nii ra sɔnɔn, alako wo naxa bira wo nii waxɔnfe kobie fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: And do not give your bodies to sin as the instruments of wrongdoing, but give yourselves to God, as those who are living from the dead, and your bodies as instruments of righteousness to God.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo fate rabolo yunubi yi, a xa findi fe kobi rabase ra. Wo xa wo yɛtɛ birin sa Ala sagoe alɔ mixi naxee kelixi faxɛ ma, e kisi. Wo fate birin xa findi tinxinyi rabase nan na Ala bɛ

sentences.english: For sin may not have rule over you: because you are not under law, but under grace.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo naxa a lu yunubi xa nɔ wo ra, barima sɛriyɛ xa nɔɛ mu wo fari sɔnɔn. Wo fa na Ala xa hinnɛ nan kui.

sentences.english: What then? are we to go on in sin because we are not under law but under grace? Let it not be so.
sentences.susu: Won fa na ma di? Sɛriyɛ xa nɔɛ to mu won fari sɔnɔn won to fa na Ala xa hinnɛ nan kui, won xa yunubi raba yire? Astɔfulahi!

sentences.english: Are you not conscious that you are the servants of him to whom you give yourselves to do his desire? if to sin, the end being death, or if to do the desire of God, the end being righteousness.
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon a wo na wo yɛtɛ findi mixi nde xa konyi ra, fo wo xa a xa yaamari birin nabatu? Wo mu a kolon a wo na naxan xa yaamari rabatu, na nan findixi wo marigi ra, a na fa findi yunubi ra naxan wo xaninma faxɛ ma, xa na mu a findi Ala ra naxan wo xaninma kisi ma?

sentences.english: But praise be to God that though you were the servants of sin, you have now given yourselves freely to that form of teaching under which you were placed;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Ala tantu! Wo tan naxee nu findixi yunubi xa konyie ra, nɔndi to kawandi wo bɛ, wo na nan nabatufe fa wo bɔɲɛ birin na.

sentences.english: And being made free from sin you have been made the servants of righteousness.
sentences.susu: Wo bara xɔrɛya yunubi xa konyiya ma, wo fa findixi Ala xa konyie nan na, alako wo xa bira tinxinyi fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: I am using words in the way of men, because your flesh is feeble: as you gave your bodies as servants to what is unclean, and to evil to do evil, so now give them as servants to righteousness to do what is holy.
sentences.susu: N wɔyɛnfe nɛ wo bɛ alɔ mixie wɔyɛnma ki naxɛ, alako wo xa fahaamui sɔtɔ. Singe ra nu, wo nu wo yɛtɛ findixi yunubi xa konyie nan na, wo xa wali kobie nu siga xun masa ra tun. Kɔnɔ yakɔsi, wo xa findi tinxinyi nan xa konyie ra, wo lu sɛniyɛnyi kira xɔn.

sentences.english: When you were servants of sin you were free from righteousness.
sentences.susu: Wo to nu na yunubi xa konyiya kui, tinxinyi xa nɔɛ yo mu nu na wo fari.

sentences.english: What fruit had you at that time in the things which are now a shame to you? for the end of such things is death.
sentences.susu: Wo nu ɲɛrɛma fe kobi naxee kui, wo fa yaagixi naxee ra to, nee munse fanxi wo ma? Faxɛ gbansan nan fama na fe mɔɔlie xanbi ra.

sentences.english: But now, being free from sin, and having been made servants to God, you have your fruit in that which is holy, and the end is eternal life.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yakɔsi, wo to bara mini yunubi xa konyiya kui, wo findi Ala xa konyie ra, wo sɛniyɛnyi nan sɔtɔfe yi ki naxan a niyama wo xa kisi abadan.

sentences.english: For the reward of sin is death; but what God freely gives is eternal life in Jesus Christ our Lord.
sentences.susu: Barima yunubi sare findixi faxɛ nan na, kɔnɔ Ala xa ki findixi a xa hinnɛ nan na: Won xa kisi abadan won Marigi Isa saabui ra, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: Is it not clear, my brothers (I am using an argument to those who have knowledge of the law), that the law has power over a man as long as he is living?
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo to sɛriyɛ kolon, wo mu a kolon a sɛriyɛ xa nɔɛ na mixi fari han a xa simaya dande gbansan nɛ?

sentences.english: For the woman who has a husband is placed by the law under the power of her husband as long as he is living; but if her husband is dead, she is free from the law of the husband.
sentences.susu: Na kui, ginɛ naxan xa futi bara xiri, a na futi sɛriyɛ bun ma han a xa mɔri xa simaya dan tɛmui nɛ. Kɔnɔ xa a xa mɔri xa simaya dan, na futi sɛriyɛ fan bara dan.

sentences.english: So if, while the husband is living, she is joined to another man, she will get the name of one who is untrue to her husband: but if the husband is dead, she is free from the law, so that she is not untrue, even if she takes another man.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li a xa mɔri na duniɲa ma, a tan fa dɔxɔ xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ xɔn, a bara findi yɛnɛla ra. Kɔnɔ xa a xa mɔri faxa, a fan bara fulun na futi sɛriyɛ ma. Hali a dɔxɔ xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ xɔn ma kɔrɛ, yɛnɛla mu a ra.

sentences.english: In the same way, my brothers, you were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might be joined to another, even to him who came again from the dead, so that we might give fruit to God.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, a na na ki nɛ wo fan bɛ. Wo fan bara lu alɔ faxamixie sɛriyɛ tan mabiri, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa faxɛ saabui ra. Wo fa findixi gbɛtɛ nan gbe ra, a tan naxan kelixi faxamixie tagi, alako won xa wali fanyi raba Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: For when we were in the flesh, the evil passions which came into being through the law were working in our bodies to give the fruit of death.
sentences.susu: Barima, won to nu ɲɛrɛma won yɛtɛ waxɔnfe kobie ma, sɛriyɛ nu won bɔɲɛ ratema yunubi rabafe ma. Won to nu biraxi na waxɔnfe kobie fɔxɔ ra, nee nu won xun tixi faxɛ nan na.

sentences.english: But now we are free from the law, having been made dead to that which had power over us; so that we are servants in the new way of the spirit, not in the old way of the letter.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yakɔsi fa, won bara xɔrɛya sɔtɔ sɛriyɛ xa konyiya ma, won lu alɔ faxamixie sɛriyɛ tan mabiri. Na kui, won mu fa walima Ala bɛ a kɛɲa fori xa ma sɔnɔn, alɔ won to nu na sɛriyɛ sɛbɛxi xa nɔɛ bun ma tɛmui naxɛ. Won fa walima Ala bɛ a kɛɲa nɛɛnɛ nan na, Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra.

sentences.english: What then is to be said? is the law sin? in no way. But I would not have had knowledge of sin but for the law: for I would not have been conscious of desire if the law had not said, You may not have a desire for what is another's.
sentences.susu: Won fa na ma di? Sɛriyɛ findixi yunubi nan na? Astɔfulahi! Sɛriyɛ nan a niya n xa yunubi kolon, barima n mu milanteya kolonma nu xa sɛriyɛ xa mu a fala n bɛ nu, «I naxa mila.»

sentences.english: But sin, taking its chance through that which was ordered by the law, was working in me every form of desire: because without the law sin is dead.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yunubi naxa fɛɛrɛ sɔtɔ yaamari ra, a milanteya mɔɔli birin naso n bɔɲɛ ma, barima sɛriyɛ mu na dɛnnaxɛ, yunubi fan mu luma naa.

sentences.english: And there was a time when I was living without the law: but when the law gave its orders, sin came to life and put me to death;
sentences.susu: Singe ra n nu baloxi sɛriyɛtareya nan kui, kɔnɔ sɛriyɛ to fa, yunubi naxa balo n bɔɲɛ kui fa, a n findi faxamixi ra.

sentences.english: And I made the discovery that the law whose purpose was to give life had become a cause of death:
sentences.susu: Yaamari naxan nu lan a xa findi kisi ra, na naxa findi n bɛ faxɛ ra,

sentences.english: For I was tricked and put to death by sin, which took its chance through the law.
sentences.susu: barima yunubi to fɛɛrɛ sɔtɔ yaamari ra, a naxa n mayenden, a n faxa yaamari saabui ra.

sentences.english: But the law is holy, and its orders are holy, upright, and good.
sentences.susu: Na kui, sɛriyɛ sɛniyɛn, yaamari fan sɛniyɛn, a tinxin, a man fan.

sentences.english: Was then that which is good, death to me? In no way. But the purpose was that sin might be seen to be sin by working death to me through that which is good; so that through the orders of the law sin might seem much more evil.
sentences.susu: Won xa a fala fa, a fe fanyi bara findi faxɛ ra n bɛ? Astɔfulahi! Yunubi nan findixi faxɛ ra n bɛ fe fanyi saabui ra, alako yunubi xa makɛnɛn yunubi ra, a xa mini a yunubi ki yati ma yaamari saabui ra.

sentences.english: For we are conscious that the law is of the spirit; but I am of the flesh, given into the power of sin.
sentences.susu: Won a kolon a sɛriyɛ kelixi Ala nan ma, kɔnɔ n tan findixi adamadi nan na, yunubi xa konyi.

sentences.english: And I have no clear knowledge of what I am doing, for that which I have a mind to do, I do not, but what I have hate for, that I do.
sentences.susu: N naxan nabama, n mu a ya yo kolon, barima n wama n xa naxan naba, n mu na xa rabama. N fe naxan xɔnxi, n na nan yati rabama.

sentences.english: But, if I do that which I have no mind to do, I am in agreement with the law that the law is good.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li n fe rabama n mu wama n xa naxan naba, na a masenma nɛ a n bara la a ra a sɛriyɛ fan.

sentences.english: So it is no longer I who do it, but the sin living in me.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n tan yɛtɛ yati xa mu yi fe rabafe. Yunubi naxan na n bɔɲɛ ma, na nan a rabafe,

sentences.english: For I am conscious that in me, that is, in my flesh, there is nothing good: I have the mind but not the power to do what is right.
sentences.susu: barima n a kolon, a fe fanyi yo mu na n bɔɲɛ ma n yɛtɛ fate bɛndɛ tan kɛɲa ma. Natɛ na n bɛ n xa fe fanyi raba, kɔnɔ nɔɛ mu na n bɛ n xa a raba.

sentences.english: For the good which I have a mind to do, I do not: but the evil which I have no mind to do, that I do.
sentences.susu: N wama fe fanyi naxan nabafe, n mu na xa rabama. N mu wama fe kobi naxan nabafe, n na nan yati rabama.

sentences.english: But if I do what I have no mind to do, it is no longer I who do it, but the sin living in me.
sentences.susu: Na kui, xa a sa li n fe rabama n mu wama naxan nabafe, n tan yɛtɛ yati xa mu a rabafe. Yunubi naxan na n bɔɲɛ ma, na nan na a rabafe.

sentences.english: So I see a law that, though I have a mind to do good, evil is present in me.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n yi fe nan toxi n ma duniɲɛigiri kui: N na wa fe fanyi rabafe, n mu nɔma fefe ra fo fe kobi.

sentences.english: In my heart I take pleasure in the law of God,
sentences.susu: N bɔɲɛ tan kui, Ala xa sɛriyɛ rafan n ma,

sentences.english: But I see another law in my body, working against the law of my mind, and making me the servant of the law of sin which is in my flesh.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ n fe gbɛtɛ nan toma n ma, naxan a niyama n xa yunubi raba. Yi fe naxan n xaninma yunubi ma, a sɛriyɛ gerema naxan nafan n xaxili ma, a n findi a xa konyi ra.

sentences.english: How unhappy am I! who will make me free from the body of this death?
sentences.susu: N ɲaxankataxi mato! Nde nɔma n nakiside yi fate bɛndɛ xa nɔɛ ma naxan na n xaninfe faxɛ ma?

sentences.english: I give praise to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So with my mind I am a servant to the law of God, but with my flesh to the law of sin.
sentences.susu: Tantui xa rasiga Ala ma naxan won nakisima won Marigi Isa saabui ra, a xa Mixi Sugandixi! Na kui, n xaxili tan ma, n bara findi Ala xa sɛriyɛ xa konyi ra, kɔnɔ n fate bɛndɛ tan ma, n findixi sɛriyɛ xa konyi nan na naxan n natutunma yunubi ma.

sentences.english: For this cause those who are in Christ Jesus will not be judged as sinners.
sentences.susu: Na kui, kiiti mu kanama mixie ra sɔnɔn naxee danxaniyaxi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa ma, naxee na Isa i,

sentences.english: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the law of sin and death.
sentences.susu: barima Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi xa sɛriyɛ naxan kisi fima, a bara won namini yunubi nun faxɛ xa sɛriyɛ xa nɔɛ bun ma Marigi Isa saabui ra.

sentences.english: For what the law was not able to do because it was feeble through the flesh, God, sending his Son in the image of the evil flesh, and as an offering for sin, gave his decision against sin in the flesh:
sentences.susu: Diinɛ sɛriyɛ mu nɔ naxan na, barima mixi waxɔnfe kobi nu bara a rahalaki, Ala tan na nan nabaxi. A naxa mixi xa yunubi sɛnbɛ xun nakana a to a xa Di xɛɛ yunubitɔɛ fate bɛndɛ maniyɛ ra a xa findi yunubi sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: So that what was ordered by the law might be done in us, who are living, not in the way of the flesh, but in the way of the Spirit.
sentences.susu: Na rabaxi nɛ, alako sɛriyɛ tinxinyi naxan masenxi, a xa nɔ rakamalide won bɛ, won tan naxee mu ɲɛrɛfe adama waxɔnfe kobi ma, won tan naxee na ɲɛrɛfe Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi ma.

sentences.english: For those who are living in the way of the flesh give their minds to the things of the flesh, but those who go in the way of the Spirit, to the things of the Spirit.
sentences.susu: Naxee ɲɛrɛma adama waxɔnfe ma, e xaxili rafexi adama waxɔnfe nan na. Kɔnɔ naxee ɲɛrɛma Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi ma, e tan nafexi Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi waxɔnfe nan na.

sentences.english: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace:
sentences.susu: Naxee e xaxili luxi fe kobi rabafe ma, e xun tixi faxɛ nan na. Kɔnɔ naxee e xaxili luxi Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi xa fe ma, e kisi nun bɔɲɛsa nan sɔtɔma.

sentences.english: Because the mind of the flesh is opposite to God; it is not under the law of God, and is not able to be:
sentences.susu: Naxee e xaxili luxi e yɛtɛ waxɔnfe yi, e findixi Ala yaxuie nan na. E mu Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatuma, e ɲan mu nɔma a rabatude.

sentences.english: So that those who are in the flesh are not able to give pleasure to God.
sentences.susu: Naxee biraxi e yɛtɛ waxɔnfe fɔxɔ ra, e xa fe mu nɔma Ala kɛnɛnde.

sentences.english: You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if the Spirit of God is in you. But if any man has not the Spirit of Christ he is not one of his.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo tan mu na wo yɛtɛ sagoe sɔnɔn. Xa Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi sabatixi wo i, wo fa na Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi nan sagoe. Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Xaxili mu na naxan yo yi ra, na kanyi mu findixi Isa gbe ra.

sentences.english: And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.
sentences.susu: Xa wo nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi bara findi keren na, wo fate bɛndɛ tan faxama yunubi nan ma fe ra, kɔnɔ Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi tan wo rakisima nɛ barima wo bara matinxin Ala ya i.

sentences.english: But if the Spirit of him who made Jesus come again from the dead is in you, he who made Christ Jesus come again from the dead will in the same way, through his Spirit which is in you, give life to your bodies which now are under the power of death.
sentences.susu: Ala nan Isa rakeli faxamixie tagi. Xa a tan Ala Xaxili nan sabatixi wo i, a tan naxan a xa Mixi Sugandixi rakeli faxɛ ma, a man fama nɛ wo fate bɛndɛ rakiside a Xaxili saabui ra naxan sabatixi wo i.

sentences.english: So then, my brothers, we are in debt, not to the flesh to be living in the way of the flesh:
sentences.susu: Na kui, n ngaxakerenyie, doni nde na won ma, kɔnɔ a mu na won ma won yɛtɛ fate bɛndɛ xa sɛɛti xɛ. A mu lan won man xa lu a sagoe sɔnɔn won man xa a waxɔnfe kobi raba.

sentences.english: For if you go in the way of the flesh, death will come on you; but if by the Spirit you put to death the works of the body, you will have life.
sentences.susu: Xa wo ɲɛrɛ fate bɛndɛ waxɔnfe kobie ma, wo faxama nɛ, kɔnɔ xa wo gbilen e fɔxɔ ra Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra, wo kisima nɛ,

sentences.english: And all those who are guided by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
sentences.susu: barima Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi mixi naxee birin naɲɛrɛma, e tan findixi Ala xa die nan na.

sentences.english: For you did not get the spirit of servants again to put you in fear, but the spirit of sons was given to you, by which we say, Abba, Father.
sentences.susu: Ala mu xaxili fixi wo ma naxan man wo findima gaaxui xa konyie ra. A a yɛtɛ Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi nan fixi wo ma naxan wo findixi a xa die ra, naxan a niyama won xa nɔ won xui itede Ala ma, won na a xili, «N Ba, n Ba!»

sentences.english: The Spirit is witness with our spirit that we are children of God:
sentences.susu: Na kui, Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi nun won yɛtɛ xaxili a masenma a won findixi Ala xa die nan na.

sentences.english: And if we are children, we have a right to a part in the heritage; a part in the things of God, together with Christ; so that if we have a part in his pain, we will in the same way have a part in his glory.
sentences.susu: Anun, won to findixi a xa die ra, won bara findi Ala xa kɛtongoe ra, won nun a xa Mixi Sugandixi. Barima, xa won tɔɔrɔ a xa tɔɔrɛ, won man fama nɛ xunnakeli sɔtɔde alɔ a tan.

sentences.english: I am of the opinion that there is no comparison between the pain of this present time and the glory which we will see in the future.
sentences.susu: N laxi a ra won tɔɔrɛ naxan tima yi duniɲa ma yi ki, a nun won fama xunnakeli naxan sɔtɔde, e tagi ikuya ki fanyi! E ɲan mu nɔma sade e boore ma.

sentences.english: For the strong desire of every living thing is waiting for the revelation of the sons of God.
sentences.susu: Daali birin mamɛ tife waxati ra, Ala a xa die makɛnɛnma tɛmui naxɛ,

sentences.english: For every living thing was put under the power of change, not by its desire, but by him who made it so, in hope
sentences.susu: barima duniɲa birin na Sentanɛ xa nɔɛ bun ma, tide yo mu naxan ma. Na mu kelixi duniɲa yɛtɛ xa ma, a kelixi Ala nan ma. Kɔnɔ na birin kui xaxili tide luxi birin bɛ.

sentences.english: That all living things will be made free from the power of death and will have a part with the free children of God in glory.
sentences.susu: Waxati fama fade daali fulunma tɛmui naxɛ kanari xa konyiya bun, a fan xɔrɛya nun xunnakeli sɔtɔ a nun Ala xa die ra.

sentences.english: For we are conscious that all living things are weeping and sorrowing in pain together till now.
sentences.susu: Won a kolon, a kabi a fɔlɛ han to, daali birin na a kui iwafe nɛ tɔɔrɛ kui, alɔ ginɛ di furi na keli a ra.

sentences.english: And not only so, but we who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we have sorrow in our minds, waiting for the time when we will take our place as sons, that is, the salvation of our bodies.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ daali gbansan xa mu a ra. Hali won tan naxee bara Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi sɔtɔ a xa ki singe ra, won tan yati na won kui iwafe, han Ala won findima a xa die ra tɛmui naxɛ, a won fate nɔrɔ.

sentences.english: For our salvation is by hope: but hope which is seen is not hope: for who is hoping for what he sees?
sentences.susu: Won xaxili to ti a ra, na nan a ra won bara kisi, kɔnɔ won xaxili man tixi a ra. Kɔnɔ xa mixi ya fe to a xaxili nu tixi naxan na, na kanyi mu a xaxili tima na ra sɔnɔn. Mixi nɔma a xaxili tide fe nde ra a ɲan bara naxan sɔtɔ?

sentences.english: But if we have hope for that which we see not, then we will be able to go on waiting for it.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa won xaxili tixi fe nde ra won mu naxan toxi sinden, won na mamɛma tunnabɛxi nan kui.

sentences.english: And in the same way the Spirit is a help to our feeble hearts: for we are not able to make prayer to God in the right way; but the Spirit puts our desires into words which are not in our power to say;
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi fan fama nɛ won malide won ma sɛnbɛtareya kui. Won mu a kolon a lan won xa maxandi naxan naba, kɔnɔ Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi nan Ala maxandima won bɛ mayandi xui ra naxan mu nɔma masarade wɔyɛnyi ra.

sentences.english: And he who is the searcher of hearts has knowledge of the mind of the Spirit, because he is making prayers for the saints in agreement with the mind of God.
sentences.susu: Anun, Ala, naxan won bɔɲɛ ma fe kolon, a a Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi xa maxandie kolon, barima Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi maxandi tima sɛniyɛntɔɛe bɛ Ala sagoe nan ma.

sentences.english: And we are conscious that all things are working together for good to those who have love for God, and have been marked out by his purpose.
sentences.susu: Won man a kolon a Ala walima fe birin kui a xanuntenyie xa munafanyi nan bɛ, a bara naxee xili a yɛtɛ sagoe ma.

sentences.english: Because those of whom he had knowledge before they came into existence, were marked out by him to be made like his Son, so that he might be the first among a band of brothers:
sentences.susu: Barima Ala bara mixi naxee sugandi, a nu e kolon kabi fe fɔlɔ fɔlɛ, a naxa a ragiri e ma e xa findi a xa Di maniyɛe ra, alako a xa Di tan xa findi di singe ra a ngaxakerenyi gbegbe tagi.

sentences.english: And those who were marked out by him were named; and those who were named were given righteousness; and to those to whom he gave righteousness, in the same way he gave glory.
