sentences.susu: Ala bara a ɲanige a xa hinnɛ kui, n xa wali suxu a bɛ. Na misaalixi banxi ti wali nan na. N bara lu alɔ banxiti. N tan nan banxi kɔɔrinma, boore biriki dɔxɔ. Kɔnɔ kankan xa mɛɛni a wali ki ma.

sentences.english: For there is no other base for the building but that which has been put down, which is Jesus Christ.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo mu nɔma fe gbɛtɛ findide na banxi bunyi ra, bafe Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa ra.

sentences.english: But on the base a man may put gold, silver, stones of great price, wood, dry grass, cut stems;
sentences.susu: Mixi naxee banxi tima na bunyi fari xɛɛma ra, xa na mu a ra gbeti, xa na mu a ra gɛmɛ tofanyi, xa na mu a ra wuri, xa na mu a ra sɛxɛ fanyi, xa na mu a ra sɛxɛ fori ra. Kankan xa wali matoma nɛ.

sentences.english: Every man's work will be made clear in that day, because it will be tested by fire; and the fire itself will make clear the quality of every man's work.
sentences.susu: Kiiti lɔxɔɛ na wali birin makɛnɛnma nɛ. Na kiiti luma nɛ alɔ tɛ naxan fama kankan xa wali makɛnɛnde.

sentences.english: If any man's work comes through the test, he will have a reward.
sentences.susu: Xa banxiti xa wali sa na tɛ imini, a fama nɛ wali sare sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: If the fire puts an end to any man's work, it will be his loss: but he will get salvation himself, though as by fire.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa li a xa wali naxa gan na tɛ ra, a tɔɔrɔma nɛ. A fama nɛ kiside alɔ mixi naxan natangaxi tɛ ma.

sentences.english: Do you not see that you are God's holy house, and that the Spirit of God has his place in you?
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon wo findixi Ala xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi nan na? Ala Xaxili sabatixi wo bɔɲɛ i.

sentences.english: If anyone makes the house of God unclean, God will put an end to him; for the house of God is holy, and you are his house.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde Ala xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi kana, Ala na kanyi fan kanama nɛ, barima a xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi sɛniyɛn. Wo tan nan findixi na hɔrɔmɔbanxi ra.

sentences.english: Let no man have a false idea. If any man seems to himself to be wise among you, let him become foolish, so that he may be wise.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo yɛtɛ madaxu. Xa mixi nde a yɛtɛ findixi lɔnnila ra duniɲa ki ma, a xa a yɛtɛ magoro alako a xa lɔnni yati kolon.

sentences.english: For the wisdom of this world is foolish before God. As it is said in the holy Writings, He who takes the wise in their secret designs:
sentences.susu: Yi duniɲa mixie xa lɔnni findixi daxuɲa nan na Ala bɛ. A sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, «Ala gantanyi tema nɛ lɔnnilae bɛ e yɛtɛ xa lɔnni nan na.»

sentences.english: And again, The Lord has knowledge of the reasonings of the wise, that they are nothing.
sentences.susu: A man sɛbɛxi, «Marigi a kolon duniɲa mixie xa lɔnni findixi fe fufafu nan na.»

sentences.english: So let no one take pride in men. For all things are yours;
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo xaxili ti mixi yo ra, barima e findixi wo malima nan na.

sentences.english: Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; all are yours;
sentences.susu: Pɔlu yo, Apolosi yo, Kefasi yo, e birin findixi wo malima nan na. Fe naxan birin na duniɲa, fe naxan birin na wo xa duniɲɛigiri kui, fe naxan birin na na, a nun fe naxan birin sa fama, hali faxɛ, na birin na na wo tan nan malife ra.

sentences.english: And you are Christ's; and Christ is God's.
sentences.susu: Wo tan na Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi nan bɛ, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi fan na Ala nan bɛ.

sentences.english: Let us be judged as servants of Christ, and as those who are responsible for the secret things of God.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, wo xa a kolon muxu tan findixi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa walikɛe nan na, Ala xa gundoe taxuxi naxee ra.

sentences.english: And it is right for such servants to be safe persons.
sentences.susu: Xa fe nde taxuxi mixi ra, a lanma a xa na rawali a rawali ki ma.

sentences.english: But it is a small thing to me that I am judged by you or by man's judging; I am not even a judge of myself.
sentences.susu: Xa wo wama n makiitife, xa na mu a ra kiitisa gbɛtɛ wama n makiitife, fefe mu a ra. N mu n yɛtɛ yati makiitima.

sentences.english: For I am not conscious of any wrong in myself; but this does not make me clear, for it is the Lord who is my judge.
sentences.susu: N tan bɛ, n mu fe ɲaaxi yo rabaxi, kɔnɔ n yɛtɛ makiitife tan mu findixi tinxinyi ra n bɛ. N Marigi nan findixi n ma kiitisa ra.

sentences.english: For this reason let there be no judging before the time, till the Lord comes, who will make clear the secret things of the dark, and the designs of the heart; and then will every man have his praise from God.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo naxa kiiti yo sa beenun Marigi xa kiiti waxati. A tan nan fe makɛnɛnma naxan nɔxunxi dimi kui. A tan nan ɲanige makɛnɛnma naxan na mixi bɔɲɛ ma. Na waxati, Ala mixie matɔxɔma e xa wali bɛrɛ nan na.

sentences.english: My brothers, it is because of you that I have taken Apollos and myself as examples of these things, so that in us you might see that it is not wise to go farther than what is in the holy Writings, so that no one of you may be lifted up against his brother.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, n bara misaali nde masen wo bɛ n tan nun Apolosi xa fe ra, alako wo xa yi sɛbɛli fahaamu, «Wo naxa yaamari sɛbɛxi matandi.» Na kui, wo naxa wo yɛtɛ igbo lufe ra mixi nde xanbi ra.

sentences.english: For who made you better than your brother? or what have you that has not been given to you? but if it has been given to you, what cause have you for pride, as if it had not been given to you?
sentences.susu: Nde i findixi fisamante ra? Munse na i yi ra, i mu naxan sɔtɔxi Ala saabui ra? Xa wo na sɔtɔxi Ala nan saabui ra, munfe ra wo wo yɛtɛ igboma alɔ a fatanxi wo tan nan na?

sentences.english: For even now you are full, even now you have wealth, you have been made kings without us: truly, I would be glad if you were kings, so that we might be kings with you.
sentences.susu: A luxi alɔ wo bara wo waxɔnfe birin sɔtɔ muxu xanbi, wo bara banna, wo bara findi mangɛe ra. Xa a sa na na ki nɛ, na birin xa sɔɔnɛya wo bɛ, alako muxu fan xa lu wo sɛɛti ma mangɛya kui.

sentences.english: For it seems to me that God has put us the Apostles last of all, as men whose fate is death: for we are put on view to the world, and to angels, and to men.
sentences.susu: A luxi n bɛ alɔ Ala bara a ragiri muxu tan xɛɛrae ma, muxu xa findi xanbiratie ra, alɔ mixie e naxee faxama duniɲa birin ya tode ra, malekɛe nun adamadie ya xɔri.

sentences.english: We are made to seem foolish for Christ, but you are wise in Christ; we are feeble, but you are strong; you have glory, but we have shame.
sentences.susu: A luxi alɔ muxu bara daxu Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa fe ra, kɔnɔ wo tan bara findi xaxilimae ra a xa fe ra. Muxu sɛnbɛ bara ɲɔn, kɔnɔ wo tan gbe xun bara masa. Muxu bara mayele sɔtɔ, kɔnɔ wo tan bara binyɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Even to this hour we are without food, drink, and clothing, we are given blows and have no certain resting-place;
sentences.susu: Han ya muxu tɔɔrɔma kaamɛ nun ye xɔli ma. Dugi mu na muxu yi ra. Mixie muxu bɔnbɔma, e bara muxu findi mixi rabɛɲinxie ra.

sentences.english: And with our hands we do the hardest work: when they give us curses we give blessings, when we undergo punishment we take it quietly;
sentences.susu: Muxu baloxi muxu yɛtɛ xa wali nan na. Mixie na muxu konbi, muxu dubama nɛ e bɛ. Mixie na muxu ɲaxankata, muxu diɲɛma nɛ e ma.

sentences.english: When evil things are said about us we give gentle answers: we are made as the unclean things of the world, as that for which no one has any use, even till now.
sentences.susu: Mixie na muxu xili kana, muxu wɔyɛn fanyi falama nɛ e bɛ. Han ya muxu tide mu na duniɲa mixie bɛ, muxu bara lu e bɛ alɔ mixi fufafu.

sentences.english: I am not saying these things to put you to shame, but so that, as my dear children, you may see what is right.
sentences.susu: N mu wama wo ifufe nɛ, kɔnɔ n wama wo rasife nɛ alɔ n ma di maxanuxie.

sentences.english: For even if you had ten thousand teachers in Christ, you have not more than one father: for in Christ Jesus I have given birth to you through the good news.
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma karamɔxɔ gbegbe sɔtɔde Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa fe ra, kɔnɔ n keren peti nan findixi wo baba ra, naxan bara Inyila Isa masen wo bɛ, wo xa danxaniya Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi ma.

sentences.english: So my desire is that you take me as your example.
sentences.susu: N ma marasi nan ya wo bɛ: Wo xa bira n ma misaali nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: For this cause I have sent Timothy to you, who is my dear and true child in the Lord; he will make clear to you my ways in Christ, even as I am teaching everywhere in every church.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, n bara Timote xɛɛ wo yire, alako a xa wo ratu n naɲɛrɛ ki ma Isa xa fe kui, n danxaniyatɔɛ ɲamae birin xaranma naxan na yire birin. N ma di maxanuxi Timote danxaniyaxi Marigi keren nan ma.

sentences.english: Now some are full of pride, as if I was not coming to you.
sentences.susu: Ndee bara e yɛtɛ igbo wo ya ma. E ɲɔxɔ a ma n mu sigama wo yire,

sentences.english: But I will come to you in a short time, if it is pleasing to the Lord, and I will take note, not of the word of those who are full of pride, but of the power.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ, xa Ala tin, a gbe mu luxi n xa wo xɔnyi li. Na tɛmui n fama a kolonde xa na yɛtɛ igboe xa wɔyɛnyi fama findide nɔndi ra.

sentences.english: For the kingdom of God is not in word but in power.
sentences.susu: Ala xa mangɛya mu findixi wɔyɛnyi gbansan xa ra, a findixi sɛnbɛ yati nan na.

sentences.english: What is your desire? is my coming to be with punishment, or is it to be in love and a gentle spirit?
sentences.susu: Wo wama munse xɔn? N xa siga wo xɔnyi luxusinyi ra, ka n xa siga xanunteya nun diɲɛ ra?

sentences.english: It is said, in fact, that there is among you a sin of the flesh, such as is not seen even among the Gentiles, that one of you has his father's wife.
sentences.susu: N bara a mɛ a fe ɲaaxi mɔɔli nde na wo ya ma, naxan mu toma hali kaafirie ya ma. A xɛmɛ nde luma a baba xa ginɛ kolon na ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: And in place of feeling sorrow, you are pleased with yourselves, so that he who has done this thing has not been sent away from among you.
sentences.susu: A nu lan nɛ yi fe xa wo bɔɲɛ tɔɔrɔ, wo fa na kanyi ramini wo tagi, kɔnɔ wo na wo yɛtɛ igbofe tun.

sentences.english: For I myself, being present in spirit though not in body, have come to a decision about him who has done this thing;
sentences.susu: Hali n tan mu na wo yire, n xaxili tan na wo tagi. N ɲan bara na kanyi makiiti

sentences.english: In the name of our Lord Jesus, when you have come together with my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
sentences.susu: Marigi Isa xili nun a sɛnbɛ ra. N na wo xanbi ra.

sentences.english: That this man is to be handed over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may have forgiveness in the day of the Lord Jesus.
sentences.susu: Yi mixi mɔɔli xa so Sentanɛ yi ra, na fe ɲaaxi xun xa rakana yakɔsi, alako na kanyi nii xa kisi Marigi xa lɔxɔɛ.

sentences.english: This pride of yours is not good. Do you not see that a little leaven makes a change in all the mass?
sentences.susu: Yɛtɛ igbofe mu fan. Wo mu a kolon lɛbini siyadi farin gbegbe ratema nɛ?

sentences.english: Take away, then, the old leaven, so that you may be a new mass, even as you are without leaven. For Christ has been put to death as our Passover.
sentences.susu: Wo lɛbini fori ba wo ya ma, alako wo xa lu alɔ farin nɛɛnɛ lɛbini mu saxi naxɛ i. A nɔndi ki ma wo na na ki nɛ. Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi bara findi won ma sɛrɛxɛ ra, naxan misaalixi yɛxɛɛ ra naxan kɔn naxabama Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali.

sentences.english: Let us then keep the feast, not with old leaven, and not with the leaven of evil thoughts and acts, but with the unleavened bread of true thoughts and right feelings.
sentences.susu: Won xa na sali raba sɛniyɛnyi kui. Won xa fe kobi nun fe ɲaaxi ba won ya ma, alɔ lɛbini fori bama won ma banxie kui ki naxɛ na sali. Nɔndi nun bɔɲɛ fiixɛ xa lu won yi ra. Na kui won misaalima taami lɛbinitare nan na.

sentences.english: In my letter I said to you that you were not to keep company with those who go after the desires of the flesh;
sentences.susu: N bara a sɛbɛ wo ma bataaxɛ kui, wo nun yɛnɛlae naxa lu dɛfanbooreya kui.

sentences.english: But I had not in mind the sinners who are outside the church, or those who have a desire for and take the property of others, or those who give worship to images; for it is not possible to keep away from such people without going out of the world completely:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n mu wama a falafe xɛ wo bɛ a wo nun yɛnɛla birin naxee na duniɲa, a nun milantee, muɲɛtie, nun kuye batuie, wo nun nee naxa dɛ masara. Xa a sa na na ki nɛ, a lima na fan fo wo keli duniɲa ma de!

sentences.english: But the sense of my letter was that if a brother had the name of being one who went after the desires of the flesh, or had the desire for other people's property, or was in the way of using violent language, or being the worse for drink, or took by force what was not his, you might not keep company with such a one, or take food with him.
sentences.susu: N waxi a sɛbɛfe nɛ wo ma, dɛfanɲa naxa lu wo nun mixi tagi, naxan a yɛtɛ findima wo boore danxaniyatɔɛ ra, kɔnɔ a fa findi yɛnɛla ra, xa na mu a ra milante, kuye batui, konbiti, siisila, xa na mu a ra muɲɛti. Wo nun na mixi mɔɔli, wo naxa wo dɛge yati yire keren.

sentences.english: For it is no business of mine to be judging those who are outside; but it is yours to be judging those who are among you;
sentences.susu: N tan mu nɔma mixie makiitide naxee mu na danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama ya ma, kɔnɔ a lanma won xa won boore danxaniyatɔɛe nan makiiti.

sentences.english: As for those who are outside, God is their judge. So put away the evil man from among you.
sentences.susu: Naxee mu na danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama ya ma, Ala nan nee makiitima, kɔnɔ a lanma wo tan xa «mixi ɲaaxi keri wo tagi.»

sentences.english: How is it, that if any one of you has a cause at law against another, he takes it before a Gentile judge and not before the saints?
sentences.susu: Fe nde na mini wo tan danxaniyatɔɛe tagi, wo nɔma sigade di na kalamui sade kaafirie xa kiiti banxi kui? Wo mu sigama sɛniyɛntɔɛe xa yire?

sentences.english: Is it not certain that the saints will be the judges of the world? if then the world will be judged by you, are you unable to give a decision about the smallest things?
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon sɛniyɛntɔɛe nan fama duniɲa birin makiitide? Xa wo tan nan duniɲa makiitima, wo fa taganxi yi kiiti xunxurie sade di?

sentences.english: Is it not certain that we are to be the judges of angels? how much more then of the things of this life?
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon a won fama nɛ malekɛe yati makiitide? Na kui, won fa taganxi yi duniɲa fee makiitide munfe ra?

sentences.english: If then there are questions to be judged in connection with the things of this life, why do you put them in the hands of those who have no position in the church?
sentences.susu: Xa yi duniɲa fe nde bara mini wo tagi gere ra, hali wo mixi xuri nde tongo danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama ya ma, na nɔma nɛ na kiiti sade wo bɛ.

sentences.english: I say this to put you to shame. Is there not among you one wise man who may be able to give a decision between his brothers?
sentences.susu: Wo mu yaagima na ra? Lɔnnila yo mu na wo ya ma naxan nɔma kiiti sade danxaniyatɔɛe tagi?

sentences.english: But a brother who has a cause at law against another takes it before Gentile judges.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ danxaniyatɔɛe e boore kalamuma kaafiri xa kiiti banxi kui.

sentences.english: More than this, it is not to your credit to have causes at law with one another at all. Why not put up with wrong? why not undergo loss?
sentences.susu: Gere to na wo tagi, na bara a masen a wo xun bara rakana. Munfe ra wo mu diɲɛma wo bore haakɛ ma, hali na findixi kasarɛ nan na wo bɛ?

sentences.english: So far from doing this, you yourselves do wrong and take your brothers' property.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo tan harige bama wo boore danxaniyatɔɛe yi ra tinxintareya ra.

sentences.english: Have you not knowledge that evil-doers will have no part in the kingdom of God? Have no false ideas about this: no one who goes after the desires of the flesh, or gives worship to images, or is untrue when married, or is less than a man, or makes a wrong use of men,
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon a mixi ɲaaxi mu ariyanna sɔtɔma kɛ ra? Wo naxa wo yɛtɛ madaxu. Langoe ginɛ yo, kuye batui yo, yɛnɛla yo, langoe xɛmɛ yo, xɛmɛ naxan nun xɛmɛ kafuma,

sentences.english: Or is a thief, or the worse for drink, or makes use of strong language, or takes by force what is not his, will have any part in the kingdom of God.
sentences.susu: muɲɛti, milante, siisila, konbiti, nun mixi madaxui, e sese mu ariyanna sɔtɔma kɛ ra.

sentences.english: And such were some of you; but you have been washed, you have been made holy, you have been given righteousness in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
sentences.susu: Ndee na wo ya ma naxee nu na na fe mɔɔli kui, kɔnɔ wo bara rafiixɛ, wo bara rasɛniyɛn, wo bara matinxin, won Marigi Isa, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xili ra, a nun Ala Xaxili saabui ra.

sentences.english: I am free to do all things; but not all things are wise. I am free to do all things; but I will not let myself come under the power of any.
sentences.susu: Fe birin nadaxaxi n bɛ, kɔnɔ a birin xa mu fan n bɛ. Fe birin nadaxaxi n bɛ, kɔnɔ n mu tinma na fe mɔɔli nde xa nɔ n na.

sentences.english: Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food, and God will put an end to them together. But the body is not for the desires of the flesh, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body:
sentences.susu: Ala nan donse daaxi adama xa baloe ra, a adama daaxi nɛ a xa na donse don, kɔnɔ Ala na birin ɲɔnma nɛ. Ala mu adama fate daaxi a xa yɛnɛ raba. A adama daaxi a Marigi nan bɛ. Marigi man mɛɛnima nɛ adama fate ma.

sentences.english: And God who made the Lord Jesus come back from the dead will do the same for us by his power.
sentences.susu: Ala naxan won Marigi rakelixi faxɛ ma, a fama nɛ won tan fan nakelide faxɛ ma a sɛnbɛ ra.

sentences.english: Do you not see that your bodies are part of the body of Christ? how then may I take what is a part of the body of Christ and make it a part of the body of a loose woman? such a thing may not be.
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon wo fatuxi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi nan ma, alɔ wo fate salonyie fatuxi e bore ra ki naxɛ? Xa mixi fatuxi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi ma, a mu lan na kanyi nun langoe xa kafu.

sentences.english: Or do you not see that he who is joined to a loose woman is one body with her? for God has said, The two of them will become one flesh.
sentences.susu: Astɔfulahi! Wo mu a kolon mixi naxan nun langoe kafuma, a tan nun na langoe findima fate keren nan na? A sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, «Xɛmɛ nun ginɛ findima fate keren nan na.»

sentences.english: But he who is united to the Lord is one spirit.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan bara fatu Marigi ma, e xaxili findima keren nan na.

sentences.english: Keep away from the desires of the flesh. Every sin which a man does is outside of the body; but he who goes after the desires of the flesh does evil to his body.
sentences.susu: Wo wo gi langoeɲa ma. Yunubi gbɛtɛ mu findixi haakɛ ra mixi fate ma, kɔnɔ langoeɲa tan haakɛ sɔtɔma mixi fate nan na.

sentences.english: Or are you not conscious that your body is a house for the Holy Spirit which is in you, and which has been given to you by God? and you are not the owners of yourselves;
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon wo fate findixi Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi nan na? Ala bara a Xaxili raso wo bɔɲɛ i. Wo mu findixi wo yɛtɛ gbe xa ra sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: For a payment has been made for you: let God be honoured in your body.
sentences.susu: Ala nan wo xunsaraxi xunsare xɔrɔxɔɛ ra. Na nan a toxi wo xa Ala matɔxɔ wo fate nun wo xaxili ra, naxee findixi Ala gbe ra.

sentences.english: Now, as to the things in your letter to me: It is good for a man to have nothing to do with a woman.
sentences.susu: N wama wo xa sɛbɛli yaabife. A fan xɛmɛ bɛ a lufe a mu ginɛ dɔxɔ,

sentences.english: But because of the desires of the flesh, let every man have his wife, and every woman her husband.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ yɛnɛ to bara gbo, a lanma xɛmɛ tan, kankan xa a gbe ginɛ sɔtɔ. Ginɛ fan, kankan xa a gbe mɔri sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Let the husband give to the wife what is right; and let the wife do the same to the husband.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ lanma a xa ginɛ waxɔnfe raba futi ki ma. Ginɛ fan lanma a xa a xa mɔri waxɔnfe raba futi ki ma.

sentences.english: The wife has not power over her body, but the husband; and in the same way the husband has not power over his body, but the wife.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ fate luma a xa mɔri xa yaamari nan bun ma, xɛmɛ fan fate luma a xa ginɛ xa yaamari nan bun ma.

sentences.english: Do not keep back from one another what is right, but only for a short time, and by agreement, so that you may give yourselves to prayer, and come together again; so that Satan may not get the better of you through your loss of self-control.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa tondi wo bore bɛ, fo wo firin nalan a ma wo xa Ala maxandi tɛmui naxɛ waxatidi nde bun ma. Na dangi xanbi, wo man xa lu yire keren, xa na mu a ra, xa wo mu fata wo yɛtɛ suxude, Sentanɛ fama nɛ wo ratantande.

sentences.english: But this I say as my opinion, and not as an order of the Lord.
sentences.susu: N xa marasi nde fi wo ma, kɔnɔ yaamari mu a ra.

sentences.english: It is my desire that all men might be even as I am. But every man has the power of his special way of life given him by God, one in this way and one in that.
sentences.susu: A xɔli n ma mixi birin xa lu alɔ n tan, kɔnɔ Ala mu mixi birin kima kɛɲa keren. A a ragirixi nde xa nɔ fe nde rabade, boore fan xa nɔ fe gbɛtɛ rabade.

sentences.english: But I say to the unmarried and to the widows, It is good for them to be even as I am.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala xɛmɛe bɛ, naxee mu nu ginɛ dɔxɔ sinden, xa na mu a ra ginɛ naxee mu na xɛmɛ taa sinden, xa na mu a ra kaaɲɛ ginɛe, xa na mu a ra xɛmɛ naxan xa ginɛ laaxirayaxi, e fan xa bira n ma misaali fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But if they have not self-control let them get married; for married life is better than the burning of desire.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa wo mu nɔma wo yɛtɛ suxude, wo xa futi xiri. Futi xirife fisa fate waxɔnfe bɛ.

sentences.english: But to the married I give orders, though not I but the Lord, that the wife may not go away from her husband
sentences.susu: N bara xɛmɛ nun a xa ginɛ yamari, ginɛ naxa mɛɛ a xa mɔri ra. Na yaamari mu fatanxi n tan na, a fatanxi Marigi nan na.

sentences.english: (Or if she goes away from him, let her keep unmarried, or be united to her husband again); and that the husband may not go away from his wife.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li ginɛ naxa mɛɛ a xa mɔri ra, a xa lu xɛmɛtareɲa kui, xa na mu a ra a xa gbilen a xa mɔri xɔn ma. Xɛmɛ fan naxa mɛɛ a xa ginɛ ra.

sentences.english: But to the rest I say, and not the Lord; If a brother has a wife who is not a Christian, and it is her desire to go on living with him, let him not go away from her.
sentences.susu: Wo tan naxee luxi, n bara wo fan nasi, Marigi xa yaamari mu a ra. Xa a sa li danxaniyatɔɛ bara ginɛ danxaniyatare dɔxɔ, na ginɛ fa tin lude a yi ra, na xɛmɛ naxa mɛɛ a ra.

sentences.english: And if a woman has a husband who is not a Christian, and it is his desire to go on living with her, let her not go away from her husband.
sentences.susu: Xa na mu a ra, xa a sa li ginɛ bara dɔxɔ xɛmɛ danxaniyatare xɔn, na xɛmɛ fa tin na ginɛ ra, na ginɛ naxa mɛɛ a xa mɔri ra.

sentences.english: For the husband who has not faith is made holy through his Christian wife, and the wife who is not a Christian is made holy through the brother: if not, your children would be unholy, but now are they holy.
sentences.susu: N a falama fe naxan ma, na ginɛ xa mɔri danxaniyatare nɔma sɛniyɛnde a xa ginɛ danxaniyatɔɛ saabui ra, xa na mu a ra na ginɛ danxaniyatare nɔma sɛniyɛnde a xa mɔri danxaniyatɔɛ saabui ra. Xa danxaniyatɔɛ mɛɛma a xa denbaya ra, a xa die mu sɛniyɛnma nu, kɔnɔ xa a lu a xa denbaya xun ma, e sɛniyɛnma nɛ.

sentences.english: But if the one who is not a Christian has a desire to go away, let it be so: the brother or the sister in such a position is not forced to do one thing or the other: but it is God's pleasure that we may be at peace with one another.
sentences.susu: Xa danxaniyatare bara mɛɛ a xa ginɛ ra, xa na mu a ra a xa mɔri ra, a xa siga. Xɛmɛ danxaniyatɔɛ, xa na mu a ra ginɛ danxaniyatɔɛ, a mu xirixi mixi danxaniyatare ma. Ala wama nɛ won xa lu bɔɲɛsa kui.

sentences.english: For how may you be certain, O wife, that you will not be the cause of salvation to your husband? or you, O husband, that you may not do the same for your wife?
sentences.susu: Ginɛ, i a kolon xa i nɔma a niyade i xa mɔri xa kisi? Xɛmɛ, i a kolon xa i nɔma a niyade i xa ginɛ xa kisi?

sentences.english: Only, as the Lord has given to a man, and as is the purpose of God for him, so let him go on living. And these are my orders for all the churches.
sentences.susu: Kankan xa ɲɛrɛ kira xɔn ma Marigi a tixi naxan xɔn. Kankan xa wali raba Marigi bɛ a naxan soxi a yi ra. N na yaamari nan masenma danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama birin bɛ.

sentences.english: If any man who is a Christian has had circumcision, let him keep so; and if any man who is a Christian has not had circumcision, let him make no change.
sentences.susu: Xa Ala bara mixi sunnaxi xili danxaniya ma, na kanyi xa tin a xa sunnɛ ra. Xa Ala bara sunnatare xili danxaniya ma, na kanyi xa lu a sunnatareya kui.

sentences.english: Circumcision is nothing, and its opposite is nothing, but only doing the orders of God is of value.
sentences.susu: Sunnafe nun sunnatareya, fefe mu a ra. Ala xa yaamari rabatufe, na nan tide gbo.

sentences.english: Let every man keep the position in which he has been placed by God.
sentences.susu: Kankan xa lu a kɛɲa, alɔ Ala a xilixi tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: If you were a servant when you became a Christian, let it not be a grief to you; but if you have a chance to become free, make use of it.
sentences.susu: Konyi nan nu na i ra, Ala i xilixi tɛmui naxɛ? I naxa kɔntɔfili. Xa i nɔma xɔrɛya sɔtɔde, na fan.

sentences.english: For he who was a servant when he became a Christian is the Lord's free man; and he who was free when he became a Christian is the Lord's servant.
sentences.susu: Hali i Marigi Ala i xilixi konyiya nan kui, lasiri nan i ra i Marigi Ala mabiri. Hali i Marigi Ala i xilixi lasiriya nan kui, konyi nan i ra Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi mabiri.

sentences.english: It is the Lord who has made payment for you: be not servants of men.
sentences.susu: Wo xunsaraxi sare xɔrɔxɔɛ nan na. Wo naxa findi adama xa konyie ra.

sentences.english: My brothers, let every man keep in that condition which is the purpose of God for him.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, kankan xa lu a kɛɲa, alɔ Ala a xilixi tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: Now about virgins I have no orders from the Lord: but I give my opinion as one to whom the Lord has given mercy to be true to him.
sentences.susu: Marigi mu n yamarixi ginɛdimɛdie xa fe ra, kɔnɔ n wama marasi nde fife wo ma, n tan, Ala kinikinixi naxan ma, a naxan matinxinxi.

sentences.english: In my opinion then, because of the present trouble, it is good for a man to keep as he is.
sentences.susu: N tan bɛ, a fisa xa ginɛdimɛdi mu dɔxɔ xɛmɛ taa sinden, barima yi waxati a xɔrɔxɔ.

sentences.english: If you are married to a wife, make no attempt to get free from her: if you are free from a wife, do not take a wife.
sentences.susu: Xa ginɛ kanyi nan i ra, i naxa a bɛɲin. Xa ginɛtare nan i ra, i naxa ginɛ fen.

sentences.english: If you get married it is not a sin; and if an unmarried woman gets married it is not a sin. But those who do so will have trouble in the flesh. But I will not be hard on you.
sentences.susu: Xa i ginɛ fenma, na mu findima yunubi ra. Xa ginɛdimɛdi dɔxɔ xɛmɛ taa, na fan mu findima yunubi ra. Kɔnɔ mixi naxee na mɔɔli rabama, e fama tɔɔrɔde yi duniɲɛigiri kui. N wama e ratangafe na tɔɔrɛ nan ma.

sentences.english: But I say this, my brothers, the time is short; and from now it will be wise for those who have wives to be as if they had them not;
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, n wama naxan masenfe wo bɛ, waxati gbegbe mu luxi sɔnɔn. Keli yakɔsi ma, ginɛ na naxan yi, a xa lu alɔ ginɛtare.

sentences.english: And for those who are in sorrow, to give no signs of it; and for those who are glad, to give no signs of joy; and for those who are getting property, to be as if they had nothing;
sentences.susu: Naxan na wafe, a xa lu alɔ a mu wafe. Naxan sɛɛwaxi, a xa lu alɔ a mu sɛɛwaxi. Naxan na se sarafe, a xa lu alɔ se mu a yi.

sentences.english: And for those who make use of the world, not to be using it fully; for this world's way of life will quickly come to an end.
sentences.susu: Naxan na duniɲa fe rawalife, a xa lu alɔ a tide mu na, barima yi duniɲa na ɲɔnfe nɛ yi ki.

sentences.english: But it is my desire for you to be free from cares. The unmarried man gives his mind to the things of the Lord, how he may give pleasure to the Lord:
sentences.susu: A xɔli n ma wo xa kɔntɔfili birin bɛɲin. Naxan mu futi xirixi, a xa bira Ala xa fee nan fɔxɔ ra, alako Marigi xa ɲɛlɛxin a xa wali ra.

sentences.english: But the married man gives his attention to the things of this world, how he may give pleasure to his wife.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ naxan futi xirixi, a tan nan birama duniɲa fee fɔxɔ ra, alako a xa ginɛ xa ɲɛlɛxin a xa wali ra.

sentences.english: And the wife is not the same as the virgin. The virgin gives her mind to the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy in body and in spirit: but the married woman takes thought for the things of the world, how she may give pleasure to her husband.
sentences.susu: Na tɛmui a na fe firin nan kui na ki. Ginɛ fan, naxan mu na xɛmɛ taa, a findi ginɛdimɛdi ra, a birama Marigi xa fee nan fɔxɔ ra, alako a fate nun a xaxili xa sɛniyɛn. Kɔnɔ naxan dɔxɔxi xɛmɛ taa, a tan nan birama duniɲa fee nan fɔxɔ ra, alako a xa mɔri xa ɲɛlɛxin a xa wali ra.

sentences.english: Now I say this for your profit; not to make things hard for you, but because of what is right, and so that you may be able to give all your attention to the things of the Lord.
sentences.susu: N yi fe falama wo xa munafanyi nan xa fe ra. N mu a falama yanfanteya xa ma. A xɔli n ma wo xa lu fe fanyi nan kui, wo xa gbaku Marigi ma, kɔntɔfili gbɛtɛ yo naxa lu wo ma.

sentences.english: But if, in any man's opinion, he is not doing what is right for his virgin, if she is past her best years, and there is need for it, let him do what seems right to him; it is no sin; let them be married.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan bara ginɛ fen fɔlɔ, a fa a kolon a mu nɔma a yɛtɛ suxude, a a maɲɔxunxi nɛ a a lanma a xa na ginɛ dɔxɔ, a lanma a xa na raba. A mu findixi yunubi ra. Ginɛfenyie xa futi xiri e nun a xa ginɛ tagi.

sentences.english: But the man who is strong in mind and purpose, who is not forced but has control over his desires, does well if he comes to the decision to keep her a virgin.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ ginɛfenyi naxan nɔma a yɛtɛ suxude, naxan bara natɛ tongo a yɛtɛ ra a naxa ginɛ dɔxɔ, na kanyi bara fe fanyi raba.

sentences.english: So then, he who gets married to his virgin does well, and he who keeps her unmarried does better.
sentences.susu: Na kui, naxan ginɛdimɛdi fenxi dɔxɔma, na bara fe fanyi raba, kɔnɔ naxan mu a dɔxɔma, na bara fe fanyi raba dangife boore ra.

sentences.english: It is right for a wife to be with her husband as long as he is living; but when her husband is dead, she is free to be married to another; but only to a Christian.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ nun a xa mɔri luma a ra han a xa simaya danyi nɛ. Kɔnɔ xa a xa mɔri faxa, a nɔma dɔxɔde xɛmɛ gbɛtɛ xɔn ma. A nɔma dɔxɔde xɛmɛ xɔn a nu wa naxan yo xɔn, kɔnɔ a xa findi Ala xa mixi nan na.

sentences.english: But it will be better for her to keep as she is, in my opinion: and it seems to me that I have the Spirit of God.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ n tan bɛ, a xa sɛɛwɛ xun masama nɛ xa a sa lu kaaɲɛ kui. N laxi a ra a Ala Xaxili na n bɔɲɛ i.

sentences.english: Now about things offered to images: we all seem to ourselves to have knowledge. Knowledge gives pride, but love gives true strength.
sentences.susu: Won birin bara fahaamui sɔtɔ sɛrɛxɛ sube xa fe ma naxan baxi kuyee bɛ. Fahaamui nɔma findide yɛtɛ igboɲa ra, kɔnɔ xanunteya nan mixie ralimaniyama.

sentences.english: If anyone seems to himself to have knowledge, so far he has not the right sort of knowledge about anything;
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan ɲɔxɔ a ma a bara gɛ fahaamui sɔtɔde, nde luxi a xa fahaamui ra.

sentences.english: But if anyone has love for God, God has knowledge of him.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan Ala xanuma, Ala bara na kanyi kolon.

sentences.english: So, then, as to the question of taking food offered to images, we are certain that an image is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one.
sentences.susu: N xa fe nde masen wo bɛ sɛrɛxɛ sube donfe ma naxan baxi kuyee bɛ. Won a kolon kuye yo mu na duniɲa naxan findixi Ala ra. Ala keren peti nan na.

sentences.english: For though there are those who have the name of gods, in heaven or on earth, as there are a number of gods and a number of lords,
sentences.susu: Duniɲa mixie fe gbegbe findima alae ra koore nun bɔxi ma. E e xilima «alae,» e e xilima «marigie.»

sentences.english: There is for us only one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we are for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we have our being through him.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ won tan bɛ Ala keren peti nan na, Baba Ala naxan se birin daaxi, won findixi naxan gbe ra. Marigi keren peti nan na, naxan findixi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa ra, se birin daaxi naxan saabui ra, won fan ɲɛngima naxan saabui ra.

sentences.english: Still, all men have not that knowledge: but some, being used till now to the image, are conscious that they are taking food which has been offered to the image; and because they are not strong in the faith, their minds are troubled.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi birin mu gɛxi fahaamui sɔtɔde na fe ma. Mixi naxee nu bara dari kuye fee ra, han yakɔsi e nɛ sɛrɛxɛ sube donma, e tan bɛ a baxi kuye nan bɛ. E xaxili to mu gɛxi fee fahaamude sinden, e yunubi sɔtɔma na sube donfe kui.

sentences.english: But God's approval of us is not based on the food we take: if we do not take it we are no worse for it; and if we take it we are no better.
sentences.susu: Donse mu mixi makɔrɛma Ala ra. Xa won bara a don, xa won bara a lu na, a birin keren.

sentences.english: But take care that this power of yours does not give cause for trouble to the feeble.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a mato a fanyi ra, alako wo xa xɔrɛya naxa a niya fahaamutare xa yunubi sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: For if a man sees you, who have knowledge, taking food as a guest in the house of an image, will it not give him, if he is feeble, the idea that he may take food offered to images?
sentences.susu: Xa fahaamutare nde bara wo tan fahaamui kanyi to, wo dɔxɔxi teebili ra kuyee banxi kui, na nɔma a niyade fahaamutare fan xa kuye sɛrɛxɛ sube don.

sentences.english: And so, through your knowledge, you are the cause of destruction to your brother, for whom Christ underwent death.
sentences.susu: Na kui, fahaamutare, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi faxa naxan bɛ, a fama lɔɛde i tan nan ma fahaamui saabui ra.

sentences.english: And in this way, doing evil to the brothers, and causing trouble to those whose faith is feeble, you are sinning against Christ.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo bara yunubi raba wo ngaxakerenyi fahaamutaree ra, wo man bara yunubi raba Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi ra.

sentences.english: For this reason, if food is a cause of trouble to my brother, I will give up taking meat for ever, so that I may not be a cause of trouble to my brother.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi, xa donse nde a niyama n ngaxakerenyi xa yunubi tongo, n tan bara diɲɛ na donse ma, alako n naxa n ngaxakerenyi rabira.

sentences.english: Am I not free? am I not an Apostle? have I not seen Jesus our Lord? are you not my work in the Lord?
sentences.susu: Lasiri xa mu na n na? Xɛɛra xa mu na n na? N mu won Marigi Isa toxi xɛ? Marigi mu n xɛɛxi wo yire xɛ, alako wo xa danxaniya?

sentences.english: If to others I am not an Apostle, at least I am one to you: for the fact that you are Christians is the sign that I am an Apostle.
sentences.susu: Tɛmunde booree mu n kolon xɛɛra ra, kɔnɔ wo tan n kolon, barima wo xa danxaniya findixi n ma xɛɛraya tɔnxuma nan na Marigi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: My answer to those who are judging me is this.
sentences.susu: N ma xunmafalɛ nan na ki mixie bɛ naxee wama n makiitife.

sentences.english: Have we no right to take food and drink?
sentences.susu: A mu daxa muxu xa muxu dɛge, muxu xa muxu min?

sentences.english: Have we no right to take about with us a Christian wife, like the rest of the Apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
sentences.susu: A mu daxa muxu xa ginɛ danxaniyaxi dɔxɔ, naxan luma muxu sɛɛti ma muxu xa ɲɛrɛ kui, alɔ xɛɛra booree a rabama ki naxɛ, a nun Marigi ngaxakerenyie nun Kefasi?

sentences.english: Or I only and Barnabas, have we no right to take a rest from work?
sentences.susu: Ka n tan nun Baranabasi gbansan nan lan muxu xa wali muxu xa baloe xa fe ra?

sentences.english: Who ever goes to war without looking to someone to be responsible for his payment? who puts in vines and does not take the fruit of them? or who takes care of sheep without drinking of their milk?
sentences.susu: Sɔɔri mundun a yɛtɛ rabaloma? Bɔxi rawali mundun mu a xa sansi bogi donma? Xuruse dɛmadonyi mundun mu a xa xuruse xiɲɛ minma?

sentences.english: Am I talking as a man? does not the law say the same?
sentences.susu: Adama xaxili gbansan nan na ki? Ala xa sɛriyɛ fan mu na mɔɔli masenma xɛ?

sentences.english: For it says in the law of Moses, It is not right to keep the ox from taking the grain when he is crushing it. Is it for the oxen that God is giving orders?
sentences.susu: A sɛbɛxi Tawureta Munsa kui, «Ninge nɛ mɛngi luxutama, wo mu lan wo xa a dɛ xiri.» Na kui, Ala wama mɛɛnife ningee nan gbansan ma,

sentences.english: Or has he us in mind? Yes, it was said for us; because it is right for the ploughman to do his ploughing in hope, and for him who is crushing the grain to do his work hoping for a part in the fruits of it.
sentences.susu: ka a na fala won tan nan fan ma fe ra? Iyo, a na sɛbɛ won tan nan ma fe ra. Walikɛ walima fe nde nan ma. Mixi maale boronma nɛ alako a xa baloe sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: If we have been planting the things of the Spirit for you, does it seem a great thing for you to give us a part in your things of this world?
sentences.susu: Xa muxu bara wakili wo bɛ alako wo xa Ala kolon, a mu lanma xɛ muxu xa se sɔtɔ wo yi ra?

sentences.english: If others have a part in this right over you, have we not even more? But we did not make use of our right, so that we might put nothing in the way of the good news of Christ.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi gbɛtɛe na mɔɔli sɔtɔma wo ra, a mu lanma xɛ muxu singe xa na sɔtɔ? Kɔnɔ muxu mu na findixi teku ra wo mabiri. Muxu bara diɲɛ na birin ma, alako Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa xibaaru fanyi kawandife naxa matɔɔrɔ.

sentences.english: Do you not see that the servants of the holy things get their living from the Temple, and the servants of the altar have their part in the food which is offered on the altar?
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon sɛrɛxɛdubɛe fan baloma sɛrɛxɛe nan na naxee baxi Ala xa hɔrɔmɔbanxi bɛ? Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ naxee sɛrɛxɛ sama sɛrɛxɛbade, e xa baloe minima na sɛrɛxɛe nan kui.

sentences.english: Even so did the Lord give orders that the preachers of the good news might get their living from the good news.
sentences.susu: Na ki Marigi bara yaamari fi a Ala xa xibaaru fanyi kawanditie xa balo e xa kawandi ti kui.

sentences.english: But I have not made use of any of these things: and I am not writing this in the hope that it may be so for me: for it would be better for me to undergo death, than for any man to make this pride of mine of no effect.
sentences.susu: N tan mu na findixi teku ra fefe ma. N man mu yi bataaxɛ sɛbɛxi xɛ alako wo xa n ki. Kawandi tife kɔbiri xanbi a bara findi ɲɛlɛxinyi ra n bɛ. N mu tin mixi yo xa na ɲɛlɛxinyi ba n yi ra, hali na findi faxɛ nan na n bɛ.

sentences.english: For if I am a preacher of the good news, I have no cause for pride in this; because I am forced to do so, for a curse is on me if I do not.
sentences.susu: N mu nɔma n yɛtɛ igbode n ma kawandi wali xa fe ra. Kawandi tife findixi Ala xa yaamari nan na n bɛ. Ɲaxankatɛ na n bɛ, xa n mu Ala xa xibaaru fanyi kawandi.

sentences.english: But if I do it gladly, I have a reward; and if not, I am under orders to do it.
sentences.susu: Xa n keren nan a ɲanigexi nu, a lanma n xa sare sɔtɔ. Kɔnɔ xa a mu fatanxi n yɛtɛ ɲanige xa ra, n na xɛɛraya nan nabafe tun, naxan taxuxi n na.

sentences.english: What then is my reward? This, that when I am giving the good news, I may give it without payment, not making use of my rights as a preacher of the good news.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n sare findima munse ra? N sare findima na ɲɛlɛxinyi nan na, naxan fatanxi Ala xa xibaaru fanyi kawandife ra sare xanbi n nu nɔma naxan maxɔrinde.

sentences.english: For though I was free from all men, I made myself a servant to all, so that more might have salvation.
sentences.susu: Hali lasiri nan n na, n nan n yɛtɛ findima mixi birin xa konyi nan na alako n xa mixi gbegbe sɔtɔ Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: And to the Jews I was as a Jew, so that I might give the good news to them; to those under the law I was the same, not as being myself under the law, but so that I might give the good news to those under the law.
sentences.susu: N nan ɲɛrɛma Yuwifi ki nan ma Yuwifie ya ma alako n xa e sɔtɔ Ala bɛ. N nan ɲɛrɛma Munsa xa sɛriyɛ ki nan ma, hali n mu na na yaamari bun ma, alako n xa mixie sɔtɔ Ala bɛ naxee na na sɛriyɛ bun ma.

sentences.english: To those without the law I was as one without the law, not as being without law to God, but as under law to Christ, so that I might give the good news to those without the law.
sentences.susu: Xa n na mixie ya ma naxee mu na Munsa xa sɛriyɛ bun ma, n fan luma e gbe ki nɛ, alako n xa na mixi mɔɔli sɔtɔ Ala bɛ. N nan ɲɛrɛma na ki nɛ hali n tan to na Ala xa sɛriyɛ bun ma. N na a xa Mixi Sugandixi xa yaamari nan bun ma.

sentences.english: To the feeble, I was as one who is feeble, so that they might have salvation: I have been all things to all men, so that some at least might have salvation.
sentences.susu: N bara ɲɛrɛ fahaamutareɲa ki ma fahaamutaree ya ma, alako n xa e fan sɔtɔ Ala bɛ. N bara fe mɔɔli birin naba, n bara ɲɛrɛ mixi mɔɔli birin gbe ki ma, alako n xa mixi ndee sɔtɔ Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: And I do all things for the cause of the good news, so that I may have a part in it.
sentences.susu: N fe birin nabama alako Ala xa xibaaru fanyi xa kawandi, n fan xa lu na nɛmɛ kui.

sentences.english: Do you not see that in a running competition all take part, but only one gets the reward? So let your minds be fixed on the reward.
sentences.susu: Wo mu a kolon gi mixi naxee gbatama ɲama ya xɔri, mixi keren gbansan nan geenima, a sare sɔtɔ? Wo fan xa ɲɛrɛ a fanyi ra wo xa duniɲɛigiri kui, alako wo xa sare sɔtɔ Ala ra.

sentences.english: And every man who takes part in the sports has self-control in all things. Now they do it to get a crown which is of this world, but we for an eternal crown.
sentences.susu: Gi mixi naxee gbata rabama, e fe xɔrɔxɔɛ mɔɔli birin nabama, alako e xa geeni, hali na sare mu bu. Won tan nan sare nde sɔtɔma naxan buma abadan.

sentences.english: So then I am running, not uncertainly; so I am fighting, not as one who gives blows in the air:
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi n luma n ɲɛrɛ ki mato ra a fanyi ra, n mu bɔnbɔma fe fufafu ra.

sentences.english: But I give blows to my body, and keep it under control, for fear that, after having given the good news to others, I myself might not have God's approval.
sentences.susu: N nan n yɛtɛ suxuma nɛ sɛnbɛ ra, alako n tan kawanditi fan naxa fa Ala xa masenyi matandi, n xa lɔɛ.

sentences.english: For it is my desire, my brothers, that you may keep in mind how all our fathers were under the cloud, and they all went through the sea;
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, n mu wama wo xa nɛɛmu a ma won babae naxan nabaxi. E naxa ɲɛrɛ nuxui bun ma, e naxa baa igiri.

sentences.english: And they all had baptism from Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
sentences.susu: E nun Annabi Munsa, e birin naxa fe keren idangi nuxui kui a nun baa igiri kui.

sentences.english: And they all took the same holy food;
sentences.susu: E birin naxa donse don naxan fatanxi Ala ra.

sentences.english: And the same holy drink: for they all took of the water from the holy rock which came after them: and the rock was Christ.
sentences.susu: E birin naxa minse min, Ala naxan namini fanye ma. Na fanye, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi nan a ra, naxan nu biraxi e fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But with most of them God was not pleased: for they came to their end in the waste land.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi gbegbe nu na e ya ma, naxee mu nu gɛxi rafande Ala ma, na nan a to e naxa faxa gbengberenyi ma.

sentences.english: Now these things were for an example to us, so that our hearts might not go after evil things, as they did.
sentences.susu: E xa ɲɛrɛ birin findixi misaali nan na won bɛ, alako won naxa bira fe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra alɔ e a rabaxi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Then do not go after false gods, as some of them did; as it is said in the holy Writings, After resting and feasting, the people got up to take their pleasure.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa kuyee batu, alɔ ndee a raba ki naxɛ e tagi. A sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui, «Ɲama naxa dɔxɔ e dɛgede, e naxa e min, e fa keli yɛnɛ rabade.»

sentences.english: Again, let us not give way to the desires of the flesh, as some of them did, of whom twenty-three thousand came to their end in one day.
sentences.susu: Won naxa bira yɛnɛ fɔxɔ ra alɔ ndee a raba ki naxɛ e ya ma. Na kui, mixi wulu mɔxɔɲɛn mixi wulu saxan naxa sɔntɔ lɔxɔɛ keren kui.

sentences.english: And let us not put the Lord to the test, as some of them did, and came to their death by snakes.
sentences.susu: Won naxa Marigi mato alɔ ndee a mato ki naxɛ e ya ma, bɔximasee naxee faxa.

sentences.english: And do not say evil things against the Lord, as some of them did, and destruction overtook them.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa wo mawa, alɔ ndee e mawa ki naxɛ e ya ma, sayamalekɛ fa e faxa.

sentences.english: Now these things were done as an example; and were put down in writing for our teaching, on whom the last days have come.
sentences.susu: Na fe mɔɔli e lixi nɛ, a xa findi misaali ra won tan mixie bɛ naxee na waxati dɔnxɔɛ. A birin sɛbɛxi na nan ma.

sentences.english: So let him who seems to himself to be safe go in fear of a fall.
sentences.susu: Na kui, naxan laxi a ra a tixi, a xa mɛɛni a yɛtɛ ma alako a naxa bira.

sentences.english: You have been put to no test but such as is common to man: and God is true, who will not let any test come on you which you are not able to undergo; but he will make with the test a way out of it, so that you may be able to go through it.
sentences.susu: Maratantanyi yo mu wo lixi, adamadi mu nɔma naxan na. Ala na a xui xanbi ra. A mu a luma maratantanyi yo xa wo li, naxan nɔma wo ra. Maratantanyi na wo li, Ala fɛɛrɛ nde fima nɛ wo ma, alako wo xa nɔ minide a kui, wo xa nɔ a ra.

sentences.english: For this cause, my dear brothers, give no worship to false gods.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n xanuntenyie, wo xa gbilen kuye batufe fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: What I am saying is for wise men, do you be the judges of it.
sentences.susu: N na wɔyɛnfe xaxilimae nan bɛ, wo xa wo tuli mati n ma masenyi ra.

sentences.english: The cup of blessing which we take, does it not give us a part in the blood of Christ? and is not the broken bread a taking part in the body of Christ?
sentences.susu: Won Ala tantuma minse naxan ma, na minse mu a masenma xɛ won nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi wuli na a ra? Won taami naxan itaxunma won bore ma, na taami mu a masenma xɛ won nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi fate na a ra?

sentences.english: Because we, being a number of persons, are one bread, we are one body: for we all take part in the one bread.
sentences.susu: Taami keren nan a ra. Won fan, hali won wuya, won bara boni won bore ra, won bara findi mixi keren na, barima won birin taami keren nan donma.

sentences.english: See Israel after the flesh: do not those who take as food the offerings of the altar take a part in the altar?
sentences.susu: Wo Isirayilakae yati mato. Naxee sɛrɛxɛ sube donma, e mu lama xɛ na wali ra naxan nabama sɛrɛxɛbade?

sentences.english: Do I say, then, that what is offered to images is anything, or that the image is anything?
sentences.susu: N wama munse masenfe na kui? Sɛrɛxɛ sube naxan fixi kuye ma a tide gbo? Xa na mu a ra na kuye tide gbo? Astɔfulahi.

sentences.english: What I say is that the things offered by the Gentiles are offered to evil spirits and not to God; and it is not my desire for you to have any part with evil spirits.
sentences.susu: N xa a fala wo bɛ, kuye batuie sɛrɛxɛ bama ɲinnɛe nan bɛ, e mu a bama Ala xa bɛ. N tan mu tinma wo nun ɲinnɛe xa lu fe keren.

sentences.english: It is not possible for you, at the same time, to take the cup of the Lord and the cup of evil spirits; you may not take part in the table of the Lord and the table of evil spirits.
sentences.susu: Wo mu nɔma minse minde Marigi xili ra, wo man xa minse min ɲinnɛe xili fan na. Wo mu nɔma taami donde Marigi xili ra, wo man xa taami don ɲinnɛe xili ra.

sentences.english: Or may we be the cause of envy to the Lord? are we stronger than he?
sentences.susu: Wo wama Marigi raxɔnɔfe nɛ, naxan mu wama a firin nde xɔn? Wo ɲɔxɔ a ma won sɛnbɛ dangi a gbe ra?

sentences.english: We are free to do all things, but there are things which it is not wise to do. We are free to do all things, but not all things are for the common good.
sentences.susu: A birin daxa, kɔnɔ a birin mu fe fanyi raminima. A birin daxa, kɔnɔ a birin mu findima munafanyi ra.

sentences.english: Let a man give attention not only to what is good for himself, but equally to his neighbour's good.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxa a yɛtɛ kan xa munafanyi gbansan xa fen, a xa a boore xa munafanyi fan fen.

sentences.english: Whatever meat may be had at the public market, take as food without question of right or wrong;
sentences.susu: Wo nɔma sube mɔɔli birin donde naxan matima makiiti. Hali wo mu gaaxu, na sese mu findixi yunubi ra,

sentences.english: For the earth is the Lord's and all things in it.
sentences.susu: barima «Alatala nan gbe na bɔxi nun a ise birin na.»

sentences.english: If a Gentile makes a feast for you, and you are pleased to go as a guest, take whatever is put before you, without question of right or wrong.
sentences.susu: Xa danxaniyatare nde wo xili wo xa wo dɛge yire keren, xa wo wama sigafe, wo xa siga, wo xa donse mɔɔli birin don a naxan fima wo ma. Na sese mu findima yunubi ra.

sentences.english: But if anyone says to you, This food has been used as an offering, do not take it, on account of him who said it, and on account of his sense of right and wrong:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa a sa li mixi nde fa a fala wo bɛ, «Yi donse baxi sɛrɛxɛ nan na,» wo naxa na don na kanyi xa fe ra, barima yunubi nan a ra a bɛ a xaxili ki ma.

sentences.english: Right and wrong, I say, not for you, but for the other man; for the fact that I am free is not dependent on another man's sense of right or wrong.
sentences.susu: Yunubi fe mu a ra i tan bɛ i xaxili ki ma, kɔnɔ a mu lanma i naxan nabama i xa yɛtɛralu kui, i boore xa na maɲɔxun i bɛ yunubi ra.

sentences.english: But if I give praise to God for the food which I take, let no man say evil of me for that reason.
sentences.susu: A mu lanma mixi xa fe ɲaaxi maɲɔxun n ma donse xa fe ra, n Ala tantuma naxan ma fe ra.

sentences.english: So then, if it is a question of food or drink, or any other thing, whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
sentences.susu: Na nan na ki, wo naxan yo donma, wo naxan yo minma, wo naxan yo rabama, wo xa na birin naba alako Ala xa matɔxɔɛ sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: Give no cause of trouble to Jews, or to Greeks, or to the church of God.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa mixi yo ratantan, Girɛki yo, Yuwifi yo, Ala xa danxaniyatɔɛ yo.

sentences.english: Even as I give way to all men in all things, not looking for profit for myself, but for the good of others, that they may get salvation.
sentences.susu: N fan ɲɛrɛma na ki nɛ, alako n ma fe birin xa rafan mixi birin ma. N mu na n yɛtɛ xa munafanyi xa fenfe. N na mixi gbegbe xa munafanyi nan fenfe, alako e xa kisi.

sentences.english: So take me for your example, even as I take Christ for mine.
sentences.susu: Wo xa bira n ma misaali fɔxɔ ra, alɔ n fan biraxi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa misaali fɔxɔ ra ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: Now I am pleased to see that you keep me in memory in all things, and that you give attention to the teaching which was handed down from me to you.
sentences.susu: N bara wo matɔxɔ barima wo ratuma n ma fe ma tɛmui birin, wo man n ma yaamarie rabatuma.

sentences.english: But it is important for you to keep this fact in mind, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
sentences.susu: A xɔli n ma wo xa a kolon xɛmɛ birin na Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa yaamari nan bun ma, ginɛ birin na xɛmɛ xa yaamari nan bun ma, a nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi fan na Ala xa yaamari nan bun ma.

sentences.english: Every man who takes part in prayer, or gives teaching as a prophet, with his head covered, puts shame on his head.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ naxan birin salima, xa na mu a ra a wɔyɛnma Ala xili ra, a xunyi makotoxi, a bara a Marigi yelebu.

sentences.english: But every woman who does so with her head unveiled, puts shame on her head: for it is the same as if her hair was cut off.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ naxan birin salima, xa na mu a ra a wɔyɛnma Ala xili ra, a xunyi mu makotoxi, a bara a xa mangɛ yelebu. A luxi nɛ alɔ a xunyi bara bi.

sentences.english: For if a woman is not veiled, let her hair be cut off; but if it is a shame to a woman to have her hair cut off, let her be veiled.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ naxan mu a xunyi makotoma, hali a xunyi bi. Ginɛ xunyi bife to findixi yaagi ra, xa na mu a ra a xunsɛxɛ maxabafe, a lanma nɛ a xa a xunyi makoto.

sentences.english: For it is not right for a man to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ tan mu lanma a xa a xunyi makoto, barima a findixi Ala misaali nun a nɔrɛ nan na, kɔnɔ ginɛ tan findixi xɛmɛ xa nɔrɛ nan na.

sentences.english: For the man did not come from the woman, but the woman from the man.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ xa mu minixi ginɛ i. Ginɛ nan minixi xɛmɛ i.

sentences.english: And the man was not made for the woman, but the woman for the man.
sentences.susu: Xɛmɛ xa mu daaxi ginɛ xa fe ra. Ginɛ nan daaxi xɛmɛ xa fe ra.

sentences.english: For this reason it is right for the woman to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi ginɛ lanma a xa a xunyi makoto malekɛe xa fe ra. A xunyi makotofe findixi tɔnxuma nan na a a na xɛmɛ xa yaamari nan bun ma.

sentences.english: But the woman is not separate from the man, and the man is not separate from the woman in the Lord.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Marigi xa fe kui, ginɛ hayi na xɛmɛ ma, xɛmɛ fan hayi na ginɛ ma.

sentences.english: For as the woman is from the man, so the man is through the woman; but all things are from God.
sentences.susu: Ginɛ minixi xɛmɛ i ki naxɛ, xɛmɛ fan barima ginɛ nan saabui ra. Na birin kelixi Ala nan ma.

sentences.english: Be judges yourselves of the question: does it seem right for a woman to take part in prayer unveiled?
sentences.susu: Wo xa na kiiti sa wo yɛtɛ ra. A daxa ginɛ xa sali a xunyi mu makotoxi?

sentences.english: Does it not seem natural to you that if a man has long hair, it is a cause of shame to him?
sentences.susu: Wo daa ki yɛtɛ yati a masenxi wo bɛ a xɛmɛ xunsɛxɛ na kuya a findixi yaagi nan na a bɛ,

sentences.english: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given to her for a covering.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ ginɛ tan xunsɛxɛ na kuya, na findixi a bɛ nɔrɛ nan na. Xunsɛxɛ kuye fixi ginɛ ma a xunyi makotose nan na.

sentences.english: But if any man will not be ruled in this question, this is not our way of doing things, and it is not done in the churches of God.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde wama na fe matandife, a xa a kolon muxu nun Ala xa danxaniyatɔɛ ɲamae birama na sɛriyɛ nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But in giving you this order, there is one thing about which I am not pleased: it is that when you come together it is not for the better but for the worse.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ fe nde na na wo naxan nabama wo xa malanyie kui, n mu nɔma naxan matɔxɔde. Na nde bama wo xa fe fanyi nan na, a findi fe ɲaaxi ra wo bɛ.

sentences.english: For first of all, it has come to my ears that when you come together in the church, there are divisions among you, and I take the statement to be true in part.
sentences.susu: A fɔlɛ, n bara a mɛ a wo mu lanma wo bore ma wo wo malanma tɛmui naxɛ. N laxi a ra nɔndi nde na na kui.

sentences.english: For divisions are necessary among you, in order that those who have God's approval may be clearly seen among you.
sentences.susu: Lantareya na mini wo tagi, na nɔma nɛ a masende nɔndi na naxee bɛ wo ya ma.

sentences.english: But now, when you come together, it is not possible to take the holy meal of the Lord:
sentences.susu: Wo na wo malan, wo naxan donma a mu findixi Marigi xa sɛrɛxɛ tɔnxuma xa ra,

sentences.english: For when you take your food, everyone takes his meal before the other; and one has not enough food, and another is the worse for drink.
sentences.susu: barima ndee e dɛgema e booree xanbi. Donse nun minse luma ndee yi ra, kɔnɔ e booree tan luma kaamɛ ra.

sentences.english: What? have you not houses to take your meals in? or have you no respect for the church of God, putting the poor to shame? What am I to say to you? am I to give you praise? certainly not.
sentences.susu: Banxie mu na wo yi ra wo wo dɛgema a nun wo wo minma dɛnnaxɛ? Munfe ra wo yoma Ala xa danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama ma, wo fa setaree rayaagi? N xa munse fala wo bɛ? N xa wo matɔxɔ? N mu wo matɔxɔma na xa fe ra.

sentences.english: For it was handed down to me from the Lord, as I gave it to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night when Judas was false to him, took bread,
sentences.susu: Marigi naxan masenxi n bɛ, n bara na dɛntɛgɛ wo bɛ. E Marigi Isa yanfa kɔɛ naxan na, a naxa taami tongo,

sentences.english: And when it had been broken with an act of praise, he said, This is my body which is for you: do this in memory of me.
sentences.susu: a naxa tantui rasiga Ala ma, a fa taami igira, a a so a fɔxirabirɛe yi ra a falafe ra, «Wo n ko, wo a don. Yi findixi n fate nan na, naxan fixi wo bɛ. Wo xa ratu n ma yi saabui ra.»

sentences.english: In the same way, with the cup, after the meal, he said, This cup is the new testament in my blood: do this, whenever you take it, in memory of me.
sentences.susu: E to gɛ e dɛgede, Isa man naxa tɔnbili tongo, a a fala, «N wuli nan ya, saatɛ wuli naxan baxi mixi gbegbe bɛ. Wo na a min tɛmui yo tɛmui, wo xa ratu n ma yi saabui ra.

sentences.english: For whenever you take the bread and the cup you give witness to the Lord's death till he comes.
sentences.susu: Tɛmui yo tɛmui, wo nɛ na taami donma, wo nɛ na minse minma, wo luma Marigi xa faxɛ nan masen na han a gbilen waxati.»

sentences.english: If, then, anyone takes the bread or the cup of the Lord in the wrong spirit, he will be responsible for the body and blood of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, mixi yo naxan na taami don, a na minse min binyɛtareɲa kui, a bara yunubi sɔtɔ Marigi fate nun a wuli ra.

sentences.english: But let no man take of the bread and the cup without testing himself.
sentences.susu: Beenun mixi xa na taami don, beenun mixi xa na minse min, a lanma a xa a yɛtɛ mato,

sentences.english: For a man puts himself in danger, if he takes part in the holy meal without being conscious that it is the Lord's body.
sentences.susu: barima naxan na taami don, a na minse min, a mu a kolon Marigi fate nan a ra, a bara kiiti ɲaaxi sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: For this cause a number of you are feeble and ill, and a number are dead.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi furemae nun sɛnbɛtaree wuyaxi wo ya ma. Ndee ɲan bara bɛlɛ.

sentences.english: But if we were true judges of ourselves, punishment would not come on us.
sentences.susu: Xa won luma won yɛtɛ mato ra, won mu fama kiiti ɲaaxi sɔtɔde.

sentences.english: But if punishment does come, it is sent by the Lord, so that we may be safe when the world is judged.
sentences.susu: Marigi won makiitima nɛ, alako a xa won matinxin, won naxa kiiti ɲaaxi sɔtɔ alɔ duniɲa mixie.

sentences.english: So then, my brothers, when you come together to the holy meal of the Lord, let there be waiting for one another.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, na kui, wo xa wo bore mamɛ, wo wo malanma tɛmui naxɛ Marigi xa sɛrɛxɛ tɔnxuma donde.

sentences.english: If any man is in need of food, let him take his meal in his house; so that you may not come together to your damage. And the rest I will put in order when I come.
sentences.susu: Xa kaamɛ na mixi ma, a xa a dɛge a xɔnyi, alako a naxa findi kiiti ɲaaxi ra wo xa malanyi kui. N na fa, n fama na fe gbɛtɛe yailande naxee kanaxi wo tagi.

sentences.english: But about the things of the spirit, my brothers, it is not right for you to be without teaching.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, a xɔli n ma wo xa fahaamui sɔtɔ fee ra Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi wo kima naxee ra.

sentences.english: You are conscious that when you were Gentiles, in whatever way you were guided, you went after images without voice or power.
sentences.susu: Wo to nu na kaafiriɲa kui, fe nde naxa a niya wo xa bira kuye dunduxie fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: So it is my desire for you to be clear about this; that no one is able to say by the Spirit of God that Jesus is cursed; and no one is able to say that Jesus is Lord, but by the Holy Spirit.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, n xa a fala wo bɛ, mixi naxan wɔyɛnma Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra, a mu nɔma a falade, «Isa dankaxi.» Mixi yo fan mu nɔma a falade, «Isa findixi Marigi nan na,» xa Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui xa mu a ra.

sentences.english: Now there are different qualities given to men, but the same Spirit.
sentences.susu: Ala xa ki dɔxɔɛ wuya, kɔnɔ a birin fatanxi Ala Xaxili keren nan na.

sentences.english: And there are different sorts of servants, but the same Lord.
sentences.susu: Ala xa wali dɔxɔɛ wuya, kɔnɔ a birin fatanxi Marigi keren nan na.

sentences.english: And there are different operations, but the same God, who is working all things in all.
sentences.susu: Ala xa fe rabaxi dɔxɔɛ wuya, kɔnɔ a birin fatanxi Ala keren nan na. Ala keren nan a ragirima wo xa nɔ na fee rabade.

sentences.english: But to every man some form of the Spirit's working is given for the common good.
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili a yɛtɛ masenma kankan bɛ ɲama xa munafanyi xa fe ra.

sentences.english: For to one are given words of wisdom through the Spirit; and to another words of knowledge through the same Spirit:
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili ndee kima xaxilimaya masenyi ra, a ndee kima fe kolonyi masenyi ra,

sentences.english: To another faith in the same Spirit; and to another the power of taking away disease, by the one Spirit;
sentences.susu: a ndee kima sɛnbɛ ra naxan fatanxi danxaniya ra, a ndee kima sɛnbɛ ra naxan a niyama e xa nɔ mixi rayalande,

sentences.english: And to another the power of working wonders; and to another the prophet's word; and to another the power of testing spirits; to another different sorts of tongues; and to another the power of making clear the sense of the tongues:
sentences.susu: a ndee kima sɛnbɛ ra naxan findima kaabanakoe rabafe ra, a ndee kima masenyi ra e xa wɔyɛn Ala xili ra, a ndee kima kolonyi ra alako e xa fata Ala xa fe nun Sentanɛ xa fe tagi rasade, a ndee kima sɛnbɛ ra e xa nɔ xui gbɛtɛe falade, a ndee kima na xuie madangife ra.

sentences.english: But all these are the operations of the one and the same Spirit, giving to every man separately as his pleasure is.
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili keren nan na wali mɔɔli birin nabama. A kankan kima alɔ a a ɲanigexi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: For as the body is one, and has a number of parts, and all the parts make one body, so is Christ.
sentences.susu: Mixi salonsee wuya, kɔnɔ e findixi fate gundi keren nan na. E birin nadɔxɔxi e bore ra, e findi keren na. Won nun Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi na na ki nɛ.

sentences.english: For through the baptism of the one Spirit we were all formed into one body, Jews or Greeks, servants or free men, and were all made full of the same Spirit.
sentences.susu: Won tan danxaniyatɔɛ birin bara Ala Xaxili kerenyi sɔtɔ. Won birin bara findi fate keren na. Yuwifi yo, Girɛki yo, konyi yo, lasiri yo, won birin baloma Xaxili keren nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: For the body is not one part, but a number of parts.
sentences.susu: Fate mu findixi salonse keren gbansan xa ra, e wuya.

sentences.english: If the foot says, Because I am not the hand, I am not a part of the body; it is no less a part of the body.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li i sanyi a fala, «N mu na i fate ma, barima n mu findixi bɛlɛxɛ ra,» na mu a niyama a xa ba i fate ma.

sentences.english: And if the ear says, Because I am not the eye, I am not a part of the body; it is a part of the body all the same.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li i tuli a fala, «N mu na i fate ma, barima n mu findixi ya ra,» na mu a niyama a xa ba i fate ma.

sentences.english: If all the body was an eye, where would be the hearing? if all was hearing, where would be the smelling?
sentences.susu: Xa fate birin sa findixi ya nan na, mixi fe mɛma di? Xa fate birin sa findixi tuli nan na, mixi se xiri mɛma di?

sentences.english: But now God has put every one of the parts in the body as it was pleasing to him.
sentences.susu: Ala bara salonse birin dɔxɔ mixi fate ma, alɔ a wama a xɔn ma ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: And if they were all one part, where would the body be?
sentences.susu: Xa na birin findi salonse keren na, fate fa findima a ra di?

sentences.english: But now they are all different parts, but one body.
sentences.susu: Salonsee wuya, kɔnɔ fate gundi keren na a ra.

sentences.english: And the eye may not say to the hand, I have no need of you: or again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
sentences.susu: I ya mu nɔma a falade i bɛlɛxɛ bɛ, «N hayi mu na i ma.» I xunyi mu nɔma a falade i sanyi bɛ, «N hayi mu na i ma.»

sentences.english: No, those parts which seem to be feeble are the more necessary;
sentences.susu: Na mu nɔma rabade feo! Hali fate salonse naxee sɛnbɛ mu gbo, fate hayi na e ma.

sentences.english: And to those parts of the body which seem to have less honour we give all the more honour; and to those parts of the body which are a cause of shame to us we give the greater respect;
sentences.susu: Won won fate salonse naxee maɲɔxunxi a e tide xurun, won mɛɛnixi nee ma dangi booree ra. Won won fate salonse naxee suturaxi, won mɛɛnixi nee ma dangi booree ra.

sentences.english: But those parts of the body which are beautiful have no need of such care: and so the body has been joined together by God in such a way as to give more honour to those parts which had need of it;
sentences.susu: Salonse naxee mu suturaxi, e hayi mu na a ma mixi xa mɛnni e ma a gbe ra. Ala naxa mixi fate yailan alako salonse naxee maɲɔxunxi a e tide xurun, e tide xa dangi booree ra.

sentences.english: So that there might be no division in the body; but all the parts might have the same care for one another.
sentences.susu: A mu wama won xa fate salonse nde rafisa a boore bɛ. A wama nɛ won xa mɛɛni e birin ma.

sentences.english: And if there is pain in one part of the body, all the parts will be feeling it; or if one part is honoured, all the parts will be glad.
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li salonse keren tɔɔrɔ, salonse booree fan tɔɔrɔma nɛ. Xa a sa li salonse keren bara tide sɔtɔ, salonse birin sɛɛwama nɛ na kui.

sentences.english: Now you are the body of Christ, and every one of you the separate parts of it.
sentences.susu: Wo findixi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi fate nan na. Wo birin bara findi salonsee ra na fate kerenyi ma. Kankan xa wali na na.

sentences.english: And God has put some in the church, first, Apostles; second, prophets; third, teachers; then those with wonder-working powers, then those with the power of taking away disease, helpers, wise guides, users of strange tongues.
sentences.susu: A fɔlɛ, Ala bara ndee ti Isa xa xɛɛrae ra danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama ya ma. Na dangi xanbi, a bara ndee ti namiɲɔnmɛe ra. A saxan nde, a bara ndee ti karamɔxɔe ra. A man bara a niya ndee xa nɔ kaabanako rabade, ndee xa nɔ mixi rayalande, ndee xa nɔ e booree malide ki gbɛtɛ. A bara ndee ti yareratie ra, a bara ndee ki alako e xa nɔ xui gbɛtɛe falade.

sentences.english: Are all Apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? have all the power of working wonders?
sentences.susu: Nee birin findixi xɛɛrae nan na? Nee birin findixi namiɲɔnmɛe nan na? Nee birin findixi karamɔxɔe nan na? Nee birin nɔma kaabanako rabade?

sentences.english: Are all able to take away disease? have all the power of tongues? are all able to give their sense?
sentences.susu: Nee birin fata mixi rayalande? Nee birin nɔma xui gbɛtɛe falade? Nee birin nɔma na xuie madangide e booree bɛ?

sentences.english: But let your desires be turned to the more important things given by the Spirit. And now I am pointing out to you an even better way.
sentences.susu: Wo xa fe birin naba alako Ala xa wo ki fee ra naxee dangi fe birin na. Yakɔsi n xa kira fisamante masen wo bɛ.

sentences.english: If I make use of the tongues of men and of angels, and have not love, I am like sounding brass, or a loud-tongued bell.
sentences.susu: Hali n nɔma adamae nun malekɛe xui falade, xa xanunteya mu na n bɔɲɛ kui, n xui luma nɛ alɔ paani nun tɔlɔnyi bɔnbɔ xui.

sentences.english: And if I have a prophet's power, and have knowledge of all secret things; and if I have all faith, by which mountains may be moved from their place, but have not love, I am nothing.
sentences.susu: Hali n masenyi ti Ala xili ra, n gundo birin kolon, n man fe tilinxi birin fahaamu, xa xanunteya mu na n bɔɲɛ kui, mixi fufafu nan n na. Hali n ma danxaniya gbo han n fa nɔ geya tongode a tide, xa xanunteya mu na n bɔɲɛ kui, n tide yo mu na.

sentences.english: And if I give all my goods to the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it is of no profit to me.
sentences.susu: Hali n nan n harige birin itaxun setaree balofe ra, hali n faxa tɛ xɔɔra Ala xa fe ra, xa xanunteya mu na n bɔɲɛ kui, na mu findima geeni yo ra n bɛ.

sentences.english: Love is never tired of waiting; love is kind; love has no envy; love has no high opinion of itself, love has no pride;
sentences.susu: Xanunteya a niyama nɛ mixi xa findi mixi diɲɛxi ra, a findi mixi malima ra. A mu milama, a mu a yɛtɛ matɔxɔma, a mu a yɛtɛ igboma,

sentences.english: Love's ways are ever fair, it takes no thought for itself; it is not quickly made angry, it takes no account of evil;
sentences.susu: a mu xurutareɲa rabama, a mu a yɛtɛ xa geeni fenma, a mu xɔnɔma. Gbɛsɛnxɔnnɛya mu luma a bɔɲɛ kui,

sentences.english: It takes no pleasure in wrongdoing, but has joy in what is true;
sentences.susu: a mu ɲɛlɛxinma wule ra, a ɲɛlɛxinma nɔndi nan na.

sentences.english: Love has the power of undergoing all things, having faith in all things, hoping all things.
sentences.susu: Xanunteya na naxan bɛ, a diɲɛma fe birin ma, a mu tɛgɛ fefe, a a xaxili tima fe fanyi ra tɛmui birin, a tunnabɛxi fe birin ma.

sentences.english: Though the prophet's word may come to an end, tongues come to nothing, and knowledge have no more value, love has no end.
sentences.susu: Xanunteya mu ɲɔnma abadan. Wɔyɛnfe Ala xili ra a ɲɔnma nɛ, xui gbɛtɛe falafe danma nɛ, kolonyi fan ɲɔnma nɛ.

sentences.english: For our knowledge is only in part, and the prophet's word gives only a part of what is true:
sentences.susu: Won mu fe birin kolon, won mu gɛma namiɲɔnmɛ masenyi birin falade,

sentences.english: But when that which is complete is come, then that which is in part will be no longer necessary.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ fe kamalixi na a li, fe kamalitare ɲɔnma nɛ.

sentences.english: When I was a child, I made use of a child's language, I had a child's feelings and a child's thoughts: now that I am a man, I have put away the things of a child.
sentences.susu: N dimɛdi tɛmui, n ma wɔyɛnyi yo, n ma maɲɔxunyi yo, n xaxili yo, a birin nu findixi dimɛdiɲa nan na. Kɔnɔ n to mɔ, n bara dimɛdi fee lu na.

sentences.english: For now we see things in a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now my knowledge is in part; then it will be complete, even as God's knowledge of me.
sentences.susu: To won mu fee igbɛma a fanyi ra. A luxi alɔ won na won yɛtɛ matofe kike ma naxan mu igbɛma a fanyi ra. Kɔnɔ waxati na fafe, won fee igbɛma nɛ a fanyi ra, a luma nɛ alɔ won nun na fee na ti yire keren. To n mu fe birin kolon, kɔnɔ waxati na fafe, n ma fahaamui fama kamalide, n fa fe kolon alɔ Ala n kolonxi ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: But now we still have faith, hope, love, these three; and the greatest of these is love.
sentences.susu: Fe saxan nan buma: danxaniya, xaxili tide, nun xanunteya. Kɔnɔ xanunteya nan dangi nee birin na.

sentences.english: Go after love; still desiring to have the things which the Spirit gives, but most of all that you may have the prophet's power.
sentences.susu: Xanunteya xa lu wo bɔɲɛ kui. Wo kata wo xa Ala xa kie sɔtɔ a Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi saabui ra. Wɔyɛnfe Ala xili ra, wo xa na nan singe fen.

sentences.english: For he who makes use of tongues is not talking to men but to God; because no one has the sense of what he is saying; but in the Spirit he is talking of secret things.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan xui gbɛtɛe falama, a mu wɔyɛnfe adama xa bɛ, a wɔyɛnma Ala nan bɛ, barima adamadi mu na xui mɔɔli mɛma. Na xui naxan findima gundo ra, Ala Xaxili na nan falama.

sentences.english: But the word of the prophet gives men knowledge and comfort and strength.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxan wɔyɛnma Ala xili ra, a tan fe nan falama adamadie bɛ naxan nɔma e xa danxaniya rasabatide, a e ralimaniya, a sunnunyi ba e ma.

sentences.english: He who makes use of tongues may do good to himself; but he who gives the prophet's word does good to the church.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan wɔyɛnma xui gbɛtɛe ra, a a yɛtɛ gbansan nan malima. Naxan wɔyɛnma Ala xili ra, a danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama nan malima.

sentences.english: Now though it is my desire for you all to have the power of tongues, it would give me more pleasure to be hearing the prophet's word from you; for this is a greater thing than using tongues, if the sense is not given at the same time, for the good of the church.
sentences.susu: A xɔli n ma wo birin xa xui gbɛtɛe fala, kɔnɔ n wama naxan xɔn dangife na ra, wo xa nɔ wɔyɛnde Ala xili ra. Na nan tide gbo dangife xui gbɛtɛe falafe ra, fo na xui gbɛtɛe xa madangi danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama bɛ, alako e xa danxaniya xa sabati.

sentences.english: But, now, my brothers, if I come to you using tongues, what profit will it be to you, if I do not give you a revelation, or knowledge, or the word of the prophet, or teaching?
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi, n ngaxakerenyie, xa a sa li n naxa fa wo yire n xui gbɛtɛe falafe ra wo mu naxee mɛma, na wo malima di? Kɔnɔ xa n fa laamatunyi, kolonyi, Ala xa masenyi, nun xaranyi masende wo bɛ, na nan findima munafanyi ra wo bɛ.

sentences.english: Even things without life, having a voice, such as a music-pipe or other instrument, if they do not give out different sounds, who may be certain what is being played?
sentences.susu: Hali xule nun kɔra, se naxee mu ɲɛngima, xa e sigi sa xui mu fiixɛ, mixi mu nɔma a kolonde.

sentences.english: For if the war-horn gives out an uncertain note, who will get ready for the fight?
sentences.susu: Xa sara xui mu fiixɛ, sɔɔri gali mu nɔma a kolonde gere waxati bara a li.

sentences.english: So if you, in using a strange tongue, say words which have no sense, how will anyone take in what you are saying? for you will be talking to the air.
sentences.susu: Wo tan fan, xa wo xui fala mixie mu naxan kolon, e fa fahaamui sɔtɔma na ma di? Wo wɔyɛnma fufafu.

sentences.english: There are, it may be, a number of different voices in the world, and no voice is without sense.
sentences.susu: Xui wuyaxi nan na duniɲa, kɔnɔ e birin masenyi nde nan tima.

sentences.english: But if the sense of the voice is not clear to me, I am like a man from a strange country to him who is talking, and he will be the same to me.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi wɔyɛn n bɛ xui nde ra n mu naxan kolon, muxu birin bara findi xɔɲɛ ra muxu bore bɛ.

sentences.english: So if you are desiring the things which the Spirit gives, let your minds be turned first to the things which are for the good of the church.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo tan naxee wama Ala xa wo ki, wo xa kata a xa wo ki ki ra naxan danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama rasabatima.

sentences.english: For this reason, let the man who has the power of using tongues make request that he may, at the same time, be able to give the sense.
sentences.susu: Naxan xui gbɛtɛe falama, a xa Ala maxandi alako a man xa fata na xui madangide a booree bɛ.

sentences.english: For if I make use of tongues in my prayers, my spirit makes the prayer, but not my mind.
sentences.susu: Xa n salima xui gbɛtɛe ra, n bɔɲɛ salima, kɔnɔ n salima fahaamutareɲa nan kui.

sentences.english: What then? let my prayer be from the spirit, and equally from the mind; let my song be from the spirit, and equally from mind.
sentences.susu: A lanma n xa munse raba? A lanma n xa sali n bɔɲɛ ra, n man xa sali fahaamui ra. N xa bɛɛti ba n bɔɲɛ ra, n man xa bɛɛti ba fahaamui ra.

sentences.english: For if you give a blessing with the spirit, how will the man who has no knowledge say, So be it, after your prayer, seeing that he has not taken in what you are saying?
sentences.susu: Xa na mu a ra, i na Ala tantu i bɔɲɛ ra, mixi naxan dɔxɔxi i sɛɛti ma, a mu nɔma «Amina» ratinde, barima a mu i xa xui fahaamuma.

sentences.english: For your giving of the blessing is certainly well done, but of no profit to the man without knowledge.
sentences.susu: I tantui fanyi rasigama Ala nan ma, kɔnɔ boore xa danxaniya mu nɔma sabatide na saabui ra.

sentences.english: I give praise to God that I am able to make use of tongues more than you all:
sentences.susu: N bara Ala tantu, barima n xui gbɛtɛe falama dangife wo birin na,

sentences.english: But in the church it would be better for me to make use of five words of which the sense was clear, so that others might have profit, than ten thousand words in a strange tongue.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ mixi wɔyɛn suuli naxan fahaamuma, e tide gbo xaranyi ki ma dangife wɔyɛn wulu ra, naxee falaxi xui gbɛtɛe danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama mu naxee kolon.

sentences.english: My brothers, do not be children in mind: in evil be as little children, but in mind be of full growth.
