sentences.english: But only the high priest went into the second, once a year, not without making an offering of blood for himself and for the errors of the people:
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi nan gbansan nu nɔma sode na yire sɛniyɛnxi firin nde kui. Ɲɛ yo ɲɛ a nu soma naa sanmaya keren, a wuli xanin a xa yunubie nun ɲama xa yunubie xa fe ra e naxan naba a kolontareya ma.

sentences.english: The Holy Spirit witnessing by this that the way into the holy place had not at that time been made open, while the first Tent was still in being;
sentences.susu: Na kui, Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi nu wama a masenfe nɛ a yire naxan nu sɛniyɛn dangife yire birin na, a mɛnni mu nu rabixi mixie bɛ na hɔrɔmɔlingira singe xa waxati.

sentences.english: And this is an image of the present time; when the offerings which are given are not able to make the heart of the worshipper completely clean,
sentences.susu: Na birin findixi misaali nan na yi waxati mixie bɛ. A a masenma a na sɛrɛxɛ birin mu nɔma batulae xaxili rasɛniyɛnde.

sentences.english: Because they are only rules of the flesh, of meats and drinks and washings, which have their place till the time comes when things will be put right.
sentences.susu: Na yaamari singee, donse, minse, nun sali ye xa fe ra, e nu fixi mixie ma e xa yunubie nan xa fe ra, han waxati nɛɛnɛ fama tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: But now Christ has come as the high priest of the good things of the future, through this greater and better Tent, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this world,
sentences.susu: Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi to findi won ma sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi ra, a bara fa hɛɛri ra, a naxan sɔtɔ won bɛ. A bara so Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira fanyi kui, adamadi mu naxan yailanxi yi bɛndɛ fuɲi fari.

sentences.english: And has gone once and for ever into the holy place, having got eternal salvation, not through the blood of goats and young oxen, but through his blood.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ a mu so si kontonyi nun ninge wuli xa ra, a so na yire sɛniyɛnxi fisamante kui a yɛtɛ wuli nan na. A so nɛ kerenyi ra, barima na nu findixi xunsare nan na adamadi bɛ naxan mu ɲɔnma abadan.

sentences.english: For if the blood of goats and oxen, and the dust from the burning of a young cow, being put on the unclean, make the flesh clean:
sentences.susu: Xa si kontonyi nun tura wuli, a nun tɛ xube naxan fatanxi ninge sɛrɛxɛ ra a sa mixi sɛniyɛntaree ma, xa na fe mɔɔli nɔma mixi rasɛniyɛnde nu,

sentences.english: How much more will the blood of Christ, who, being without sin, made an offering of himself to God through the Holy Spirit, make your hearts clean from dead works to be servants of the living God?
sentences.susu: Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi wuli mu dangima xɛ na ra? A naxa a yɛtɛ ba sɛrɛxɛ kamalixi ra Ala bɛ, Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi xa yaamari bun ma, alako a xa won xaxili rasɛniyɛn wali ɲaaxie ma, naxee won faxama. A na raba nɛ won bɛ alako won xa Ala Ɲiɲɛ batu.

sentences.english: And for this cause it is through him that a new agreement has come into being, so that after the errors under the first agreement had been taken away by his death, the word of God might have effect for those who were marked out for an eternal heritage.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a bara findi saabui ra yi saatɛ nɛɛnɛ xa fe ra, mixi xilixie xa kɛ sɔtɔ naxan buma abadan, alɔ a laayidixi e bɛ ki naxɛ. A faxa na nan ma, a findi xunsare ra yunubie xa fe ra naxee rabaxi na saatɛ fori xa waxati bun ma.

sentences.english: Because where there is a testament, there has to be the death of the man who made it.
sentences.susu: Saatɛ naxan findi kɛ fe ra, na mu kamalima sinden, fo saatɛ tongoma faxa.

sentences.english: For a testament has effect after death; for what power has it while the man who made it is living?
sentences.susu: Kɛ mu nɔma sɔtɔde beenun saatɛtongoe xa faxa. A mu sɔtɔma saatɛtongoe baloxi tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: So that even the first agreement was not made without blood.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi na saatɛ singe mu tongoma wuli xanbi.

sentences.english: For when Moses had given all the rules of the law to the people, he took the blood of goats and young oxen, with water and red wool and hyssop, and put it on the book itself and on all the people,
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa to Ala xa sɛriyɛ masen ɲama bɛ, a naxa ningee nun si kontonyie wuli tongo, a nun ye, a fa na kasan Kitaabui nun ɲama ma se nde ra naxan yailanxi hisopi burɛxɛ nun yɛxɛɛ xabe gbeeli ra, a fa a fala, a naxɛ,

sentences.english: Saying, This blood is the sign of the agreement which God has made with you.
sentences.susu: «Wuli nan ya naxan saatɛ xirima wo nun Ala tagi.»

sentences.english: And the blood was put on the Tent and all the holy vessels in the same way.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa man naxa wuli kasan hɔrɔmɔlingira ma, a nun hɔrɔmɔlingira yirabase birin ma.

sentences.english: And by the law almost all things are made clean with blood, and without blood there is no forgiveness.
sentences.susu: A sɛriyɛ ki ma, fayida se birin nasɛniyɛnma wuli nan na. Yunubi mu xafarima wuli ifili xanbi.

sentences.english: For this cause it was necessary to make the copies of the things in heaven clean with these offerings; but the things themselves are made clean with better offerings than these.
sentences.susu: A nu lanma se naxee misaalixi fee ra ariyanna kui, e xa rasɛniyɛn sɛrɛxɛe ra. Ariyanna xa marasɛniyɛnyi rabama sɛrɛxɛe nan na naxee fan booree bɛ.

sentences.english: For Christ did not go into a holy place which had been made by men's hands as the copy of the true one; but he went into heaven itself, and now takes his place before the face of God for us.
sentences.susu: Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi mu soxi hɔrɔmɔlingira xa kui adamadie naxan yailanxi, naxan misaalixi hɔrɔmɔlingira ra naxan na ariyanna. A so ariyanna yati nan kui, alako a xa won ma dɛntɛgɛ sa Ala bɛ.

sentences.english: And he did not have to make an offering of himself again and again, as the high priest goes into the holy place every year with blood which is not his;
sentences.susu: A mu soxi naa sanya wuyaxi, alɔ sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi naxan soma Ala xa hɔrɔmɔlingira kui ɲɛ yo ɲɛ wuli nde ra, naxan mu findixi a gbe ra.

sentences.english: For then he would have undergone a number of deaths from the time of the making of the world: but now he has come to us at the end of the old order, to put away sin by the offering of himself.
sentences.susu: Xa a nu na ki nɛ nu, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi nu lanma nɛ a xa tɔɔrɔ sanmaya wuyaxi kabi duniɲa fɔlɛ ra. Kɔnɔ na mu a ra. Yakɔsi yi waxati dɔnxɔɛ, a naxa mini sanmaya keren, alako a xa yunubi xa fe kana a yɛtɛ sɛrɛxɛ saabui ra.

sentences.english: And because by God's law death comes to men once, and after that they are judged;
sentences.susu: Adamadie faxama nɛ sanya keren, e fa makiiti.

sentences.english: So Christ, having at his first coming taken on himself the sins of men, will be seen a second time, without sin, by those who are waiting for him, for their salvation.
sentences.susu: Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi fan bara faxa sanmaya keren, alako a xa yunubi ba mixi gbegbe ma. A man fama nɛ a firin nde, kɔnɔ na waxati a mu fama yunubie xa fe xa ra, a fama mixie nan bɛ naxee xaxili tixi kisi ra.

sentences.english: For the law, being only a poor copy of the future good things, and not the true image of those things, is never able to make the people who come to the altar every year with the same offerings completely clean.
sentences.susu: Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ misaalixi fe fanyi nan na naxan fama fade. A findixi misaali gbansan nan na. Na nan a toxi a Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ mu nɔma Ala batulae rasɛniyɛnde kerenyi ra, na sɛrɛxɛe saabui ra naxee bama ɲɛ yo ɲɛ.

sentences.english: For if this had been possible, would there not have been an end of those offerings, because the worshippers would have been made completely clean and would have been no longer conscious of sins?
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li a nu nɔma e rasɛniyɛnde nu, mixie mu nu luma sɛrɛxɛe ba ra tɛmui birin, barima sɛrɛxɛ keren gbansan nu nɔma e xa yunubi birin xafaride kerenyi ra, na yunubi xa fe maɲɔxunyi yati mu luma e xunyi.

sentences.english: But year by year there is a memory of sins in those offerings.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ ɲɛ yo ɲɛ na sɛrɛxɛe findima maratuse nan na mixie bɛ a yunubie na e ma.

sentences.english: Because it is not possible for the blood of oxen and goats to take away sins.
sentences.susu: Tura nun si kontonyi wuli mu nɔma yunubie bade.

sentences.english: So that when he comes into the world, he says, You had no desire for offerings, but you made a body ready for me;
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi to so duniɲa, a naxa a masen Ala bɛ, «I mu wama sɛrɛxɛ xɔn. I mu wama hadiya xɔn. I bara fate yailan n bɛ.

sentences.english: You had no joy in burned offerings or in offerings for sin.
sentences.susu: I mu wama sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi xɔn ma, i mu wama sɛrɛxɛ yunubi xafari daaxi fan xɔn ma.

sentences.english: Then I said, See, I have come to do your pleasure, O God (as it is said of me in the roll of the book).
sentences.susu: N naxa a masen, ‹N bara fa. A sɛbɛxi n ma fe ra Kitaabui kui, Ala, n na fafe i sago rabade.›»

sentences.english: After saying, You had no desire for offerings, for burned offerings or offerings for sin (which are made by the law) and you had no pleasure in them,
sentences.susu: Singe a naxa a masen, «I mu wama sɛrɛxɛ yo xɔn ma. E mu rafan i ma. I mu wama hadiya yo xɔn ma. I mu wama sɛrɛxɛ gan daaxi xɔn ma, i mu wama sɛrɛxɛ yunubi xafari daaxi fan xɔn ma.» A nu bara na fala hali na yaamari to nu toma a xa sɛriyɛ kui.

sentences.english: Then he said, See, I have come to do your pleasure. He took away the old order, so that he might put the new order in its place.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, a bara a masen, «Ala, n na be. N bara fa i sago rabade.» Na kui, a naxa fe singe ba na, alako fe firin nde xa ti.

sentences.english: By that pleasure we have been made holy, by the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once and for ever.
sentences.susu: Na ɲanige nan a niyaxi won nasɛniyɛnxi Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa fate saabui ra, naxan baxi sɛrɛxɛ ra kerenyi ra.

sentences.english: And every priest takes his place at the altar day by day, doing what is necessary, and making again and again the same offerings which are never able to take away sins.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ birin e xa wali rabama lɔxɔ yo lɔxɔ. E luma sɛrɛxɛe ba ra naxee mu nɔma yunubie xafaride.

sentences.english: But when Jesus had made one offering for sins for ever, he took his place at the right hand of God;
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ Isa tan, a to gɛ sɛrɛxɛ keren bade yunubie xa fe ra, a naxa a magoro Ala yirefanyi ma, a luma dɛnnaxɛ abadan.

sentences.english: And has been waiting there from that time, till all who are against him are made a foot-rest for his feet.
sentences.susu: A na a mamɛfe a xa ti a yaxuie ma,

sentences.english: Because by one offering he has made complete for ever those who are made holy.
sentences.susu: barima a bara mixie rakamali kerenyi ra, a naxee rasɛniyɛnxi a xa sɛrɛxɛ kerenyi saabui ra.

sentences.english: And the Holy Spirit is a witness for us: for after he had said,
sentences.susu: Ala Xaxili Sɛniyɛnxi na tagi rabama won bɛ yi masenyi ra. A singe, a naxa a masen,

sentences.english: This is the agreement which I will make with them after those days, says the Lord; I will put my laws in their hearts, writing them in their minds; he said,
sentences.susu: «Saatɛ nan ya n naxan tongoma Isirayila bɔnsɔɛ bɛ: Na waxati na dangi, n nan n ma sɛriyɛ luma nɛ e bɔɲɛ ma, n na sɛbɛma nɛ e sondonyi ma.»

sentences.english: And I will keep no more memory of their sins and of their evil-doings.
sentences.susu: A man naxa a masen, «N mu ratuma e xa yunubie nun e xa wali kobie ma sɔnɔn.»

sentences.english: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no more offering for sin.
sentences.susu: Yunubi na gɛ xafaride tɛmui naxɛ, sɛrɛxɛ mu bama na yunubi xa fe ra sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: So then, my brothers, being able to go into the holy place without fear, because of the blood of Jesus,
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, na kui won bara limaniya sɔtɔ sofe ra na yire sɛniyɛnxi fisamante kui Isa wuli saabui ra.

sentences.english: By the new and living way which he made open for us through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
sentences.susu: Isa bara na kisi kira nɛɛnɛ rabi won bɛ, alako won xa dangi na dugi ra naxan gbakuxi hɔrɔmɔlingira kui a fate saabui ra.

sentences.english: And having a great priest over the house of God,
sentences.susu: Won ma sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi to tixi Ala xa banxi xunyi ra,

sentences.english: Let us go in with true hearts, in certain faith, having our hearts made free from the sense of sin and our bodies washed with clean water:
sentences.susu: won xa won makɔrɛ Ala ra bɔɲɛ fiixɛ nun danxaniya ra. Na danxaniya won nalimaniyama nɛ, barima won bɔɲɛ rasɛniyɛnxi won ma yunubie ma, won fate fan maxaxi ye tinse ra.

sentences.english: Let us keep the witness of our hope strong and unshaking, for he is true who has given his word:
sentences.susu: Won xa won xaxili ti Ala ra tunnabɛxi kui, barima naxan laayidi tongoxi won bɛ, a mu nɔma na kanade.

sentences.english: And let us be moving one another at all times to love and good works;
sentences.susu: Won xa mɛɛni won bore ma, alako won xa won bore ralimaniya won xa lu xanunteya nun wali fanyi kui.

sentences.english: Not giving up our meetings, as is the way of some, but keeping one another strong in faith; and all the more because you see the day coming near.
sentences.susu: Won naxa won ma malanyie rabolo de, alɔ ndee na a rabafe ki naxɛ. A lanma won xa won bore ralimaniya. Won to a kolon Ala xa lɔxɔɛ na fafe, won naxa tagan na ma.

sentences.english: For if we do evil on purpose after we have had the knowledge of what is true, there is no more offering for sins,
sentences.susu: Xa a sa li, won Ala xa nɔndi kolon, kɔnɔ won man nu fa lu yunubi raba ra won ɲanige ra, sɛrɛxɛ gbɛtɛ mu na sɔnɔn naxan nɔma won ma yunubie xafaride,

sentences.english: But only a great fear of being judged, and of the fire of wrath which will be the destruction of the haters of God.
sentences.susu: fo gaaxui xungbe Ala xa kiiti ya ra, naxan findima tɛ mankanɛ ra a matandilae bɛ.

sentences.english: A man who has gone against the law of Moses is put to death without pity on the word of two or three witnesses:
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde Annabi Munsa xa sɛriyɛ matandi, e a faxama nɛ kinikinitareɲa kui, seede firin xa na mu a ra saxan xa seedeɲɔxɔya saabui ra.

sentences.english: But will not the man by whom the Son of God has been crushed under foot, and the blood of the agreement with which he was washed clean has been taken as an unholy thing, and who has had no respect for the Spirit of grace, be judged bad enough for a very much worse punishment?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ ɲaxankatɛ dangima na tan na mixie bɛ, naxee Ala xa Di maboronma e sanyi ra, e a xa saatɛ wuli rasɔtɔ naxan e rasɛniyɛnxi, e Ala Xaxili rasɔtɔma naxan hinnɛxi e ra.

sentences.english: For we have had experience of him who says, Punishment is mine, I will give reward. And again, The Lord will be judge of his people.
sentences.susu: Won yi masenyi kanyi kolon, «N tan nan mixi gbeɲɔxɔma, n tan nan e sare fima e ma.» A man sɛbɛxi, «Marigi fama nɛ a xa ɲama makiitide.»

sentences.english: We may well go in fear of falling into the hands of the living God.
sentences.susu: Ala Ɲiɲɛ xa ɲaxankatɛ magaaxu.

sentences.english: But give thought to the days after you had seen the light, when you went through a great war of troubles;
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu na lɔxɔɛ singee ma. Wo to naiyalanyi to, wo naxa wo tunnabɛxi gere xɔrɔxɔɛ kui naxan findixi tɔɔrɛ ra wo bɛ.

sentences.english: In part, in being attacked by angry words and cruel acts, before the eyes of everyone, and in part, in being united with those who were attacked in this way.
sentences.susu: E naxa wo konbi, e naxa wo ɲaxankata ɲama ya xɔri. Wo fan naxa lu mixie sɛɛti ma, naxee bara na tɔɔrɛ mɔɔli sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: For you had pity on those who were in prison, and had joy in the loss of your property, in the knowledge that you still had a better property and one which you would keep for ever.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa kinikini geelimanie ma, wo naxa tin a ra sɛɛwɛ kui e xa wo harige ba wo yi ra, barima wo a kolon harige nde na wo bɛ naxan dangi na boore ra pon, a bu abadan.

sentences.english: So do not give up your hope which will be greatly rewarded.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa fe rabolo, wo xaxili tixi naxan na, barima na sare gbo.

sentences.english: For, having done what was right in God's eyes, you have need of waiting before his word has effect for you.
sentences.susu: Wo hayi na tunnabɛxi ma, alako wo xa Ala sago rakamali, wo fa fe sɔtɔ a naxan laayidixi wo bɛ.

sentences.english: In a very little time he who is coming will come; he will not be slow.
sentences.susu: A sɛbɛxi, «A gbe mu luxi sɔnɔn. Naxan lanma a xa fa, a fama nɛ, a mu dugundima.

sentences.english: But the upright man will be living by his faith; and if he goes back, my soul will have no pleasure in him.
sentences.susu: N ma tinxintɔɛ kisima nɛ danxaniya saabui ra. Kɔnɔ xa a sa li a man naxa gbilen xanbi, n mu ɲɛlɛxinma a xa fe ra.»

sentences.english: But we are not of those who go back to destruction; but of those who have faith even to the salvation of the soul.
sentences.susu: Won mu findixi fe rabɛɲinyie xa ra, naxee xa fe xun nakanama. Won tan findixi danxaniyatɔɛe nan na, naxee kisima.

sentences.english: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, and the sign that the things not seen are true.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya kanyi, a a xaxili tima fe nde ra a laxi naxan na. Hali a mu na fe toma a ya ra, a a kolon nɔndi nan a ra.

sentences.english: For by it our fathers had God's approval.
sentences.susu: Won benbae xili fanyi sɔtɔ na nan ma.

sentences.english: By faith it is clear to us that the order of events was fixed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made from things which only seem to be.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, won a kolon a Ala nan duniɲa daaxi a xa masenyi ra. Se naxan toma naa a fatanxi fe nan na naxan mu toma.

sentences.english: By faith Abel made a better offering to God than Cain, and he had witness through it of his righteousness, God giving his approval of his offering: and his voice still comes to us through it though he is dead.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Habila naxa sɛrɛxɛ ba Ala bɛ naxan nu fan dangife Kabila gbe ra. Ala naxa na sɛrɛxɛ suxu, a Habila findi tinxintɔɛ ra a xa danxaniya saabui ra. Hali Habila to faxaxi, a naxan nabaxi danxaniya ra na findima nɛ masenyi ra won bɛ.

sentences.english: By faith Enoch was taken up to heaven so that he did not see death; he was seen no longer, for God took him away: for before he was taken, witness had been given that he was well-pleasing to God:
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Enoki naxa te koore ma, a mu faxa. Mixi yo mu nɔ a tode, barima Ala nu bara a rate koore ma. Beenun a xa te, Ala nu bara a masen a Enoki rafan a ma.

sentences.english: And without faith it is not possible to be well-pleasing to him, for it is necessary for anyone who comes to God to have the belief that God is, and that he is a rewarder of all those who make a serious search for him.
sentences.susu: Mixi mu nɔma rafande Ala ma danxaniya xanbi. Mixi naxan a makɔrɛma Ala ra, a lanma a xa la a ra a Ala na na, a nun a xa la a ra a Ala mixie nan sare fima naxee a fenma.

sentences.english: By faith Noah, being moved by the fear of God, made ready an ark for the salvation of his family, because God had given him news of things which were not seen at the time; and through it the world was judged by him, and he got for his heritage the righteousness which is by faith.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Nuha naxa kunkui banban alako a xa denbaya xa kisi. Ala nu bara banbaranyi xa fe fala a bɛ beenun a xa duniɲa li. Nuha nu gaaxu Ala ya ra. A xa danxaniya a masenma kiiti bara kana duniɲa bɛ. Nuha naxa tinxinyi sɔtɔ kɛ ra a xa danxaniya saabui ra.

sentences.english: By faith Abraham did as God said when he was ordered to go out into a place which was to be given to him as a heritage, and went out without knowledge of where he was going.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Iburahima naxa Ala xui ratinmɛ sigafe ra bɔxi ma a mu dɛnnaxan kolon, alako a xa mɛnni sɔtɔ kɛ ra.

sentences.english: By faith he was a wanderer in the land of the agreement, as in a strange land, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who had a part with him in the same heritage:
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Iburahima naxa sabati na bɔxi ma, Ala nu bara naxan laayidi a bɛ. A naxa lu mɛnni alɔ xɔɲɛ a xa kiri banxie kui, alɔ Isiyaga nun Yaxuba, naxee findixi na kɛtongoe ra.

sentences.english: For he was looking for the strong town, whose builder and maker is God.
sentences.susu: A nu na a mamɛfe a xa taa sɛnbɛma sɔtɔ, Ala taa naxan kɔɔrinxi, a a ti.

sentences.english: And by faith Sarah herself had power to give birth, when she was very old, because she had faith in him who gave his word;
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Sara dibaritare fan naxa nɔ di baride ɲɛlɛxɛforiɲa kui, barima a nu laxi a ra a Ala mu a xa laayidi kanama.

sentences.english: So that from one man, who was near to death, came children in number as the stars in heaven, or as the sand by the seaside, which may not be numbered.
sentences.susu: Na nan a to, xɛmɛ keren saabui ra, xɛmɔxi naxan mu nu nɔma di sɔtɔde sɔnɔn, na naxa bɔnsɔɛ xungbe sɔtɔ, «naxan xasabi maniyaxi tunbuie xasabi ra naxee na koore ma, a nun mɛyɛnyi xasabi ra naxan na baa dɛ ra. E kɔnti mu nɔma kolonde.»

sentences.english: All these came to their end in faith, not having had the heritage; but having seen it with delight far away, they gave witness that they were wanderers and not of the earth.
sentences.susu: Yi mixie bara faxa e xa danxaniya kui, e mu fee sɔtɔ naxee nu laayidixi e bɛ. E nu laxi a ra a fanyi ra, a na laayidie mu kanama. E nu a kolon a e findixi «xɔɲɛe nan na duniɲa bɛndɛ fuɲi fari.»

sentences.english: For those who say such things make it clear that they are searching for a country for themselves.
sentences.susu: Mixi naxee na fe mɔɔlie falama, e a masenfe nɛ a e na taa gbɛtɛ fenfe e sabatima dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: And truly if they had kept in mind the country from which they went out, they would have had chances of turning back.
sentences.susu: Xa e kelide xɔli nu bara e suxu nu, e nu nɔma gbilende naa.

sentences.english: But now their desire is for a better country, that is to say, for one in heaven; and so it is no shame to God to be named their God; for he has made ready a town for them.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ e nu taa gbɛtɛ fenma naxan fan e kelide bɛ, taa naxan na ariyanna. Na kui, Ala mu yaagixi e ra, e xa a xili e Marigi Ala, barima a nu bara taa yailan e bɛ.

sentences.english: By faith Abraham made an offering of Isaac, when he was tested: and he with whom the agreement had been made gave up as an offering the only son of his body,
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Iburahima mu tondi Isiyaga bade sɛrɛxɛ ra, Ala nu a matoma tɛmui naxɛ. A mu tondi a xa di kerenyi bade sɛrɛxɛ ra, di naxan nu laayidixi a bɛ,

sentences.english: Of whom it had been said, From Isaac will your seed take their name:
sentences.susu: Ala nu bara a fala naxan ma fe ra, «Isiyaga nan findima i bɔnsɔɛ ra, i xili luma naxan xun ma.»

sentences.english: Judging that God was able to give life even to the dead; and because of this he did get him back as if from death.
sentences.susu: Iburahima nu a kolon a Ala sɛnbɛ gbo, hali Isiyaga faxa, a nu nɔma na rakelide faxɛ ma. Fayida na nan naba misaali ra, barima Ala a xa di ragbilen nɛ a ma.

sentences.english: By faith Isaac, blessing Jacob and Esau, gave news of things to come.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Isiyaga naxa duba Yaxuba nun Esayu bɛ e xa simaya xa fe ra.

sentences.english: By faith Jacob gave a blessing to the two sons of Joseph, when he was near to death; and gave God worship, supported by his stick.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Yaxuba naxa duba Yusufu xa die bɛ, a nu luxi dondoronti a xa faxa. A naxa Ala batu, a yi masuxuxi a xa xuli ra.

sentences.english: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, said that the children of Israel would go out of Egypt; and gave orders about his bones.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Yusufu naxa masenyi ti a xa saya makɔrɛ, a lanma e xa naxan naba a fure ra Isirayilakae minima Misira bɔxi ra tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: By faith Moses was kept secretly by his father and mother for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a fair child; and they had no fear of the king's orders.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Munsa to bari, a barimae naxa a nɔxun kike saxan bun ma a xa tofanyi xa fe ra, e mu gaaxu mangɛ xa yaamari ya ra.

sentences.english: By faith Moses, when he became a man, had no desire to be named the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Munsa to mɔ, a naxa tondi findide Firawuna xa di ginɛ xa di ra.

sentences.english: Feeling that it was better to undergo pain with the people of God, than for a short time to have a taste of the pleasures of sin;
sentences.susu: A naxa wa a xɔn ma, a xa tɔɔrɛ sɔtɔ Ala xa ɲama ya ma, dinɛ a xa ɲɛlɛxin yunubi ra waxati dunkedi bun ma.

sentences.english: Judging a part in the shame of Christ to be better than all the wealth of Egypt; for he was looking forward to his reward.
sentences.susu: A bara a kolon Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi xa magore nan fan dangi Misira naafuli ra. A nu sare matoma a fama naxan sɔtɔde yare.

sentences.english: By faith he went out of Egypt, not being turned from his purpose by fear of the wrath of the king; for he kept on his way, as seeing him who is unseen.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Munsa naxa keli Misira bɔxi ma, a mu gaaxu Firawuna xa xɔnɛ ya ra. A naxa a tunnabɛxi, barima a nu gaaxuxi Ala nan ya ra, naxan mu toma.

sentences.english: By faith he kept the Passover, and put the sign of the blood on the houses, so that the angel of destruction might not put their oldest sons to death.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Munsa naxa Sayamalekɛ Dangi Sali raba, a wuli kasan naadɛe ma, alako sayamalekɛ naxa Isirayilakae xa di singee faxa.

sentences.english: By faith they went through the Red Sea as if it had been dry land, though the Egyptians were overcome by the water when they made an attempt to do the same.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Isirayilakae naxa Xulunyumi baa igiri a xaraxi ra. Misirakae to bira e fɔxɔ ra, e naxa madula ye xɔɔra.

sentences.english: By faith the walls of Jericho came down, after they had been circled for seven days.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, Yeriko tɛtɛ naxa bira a yɛtɛ ra, Isirayilakae to gɛ a rabilinde xi solofere bun ma.

sentences.english: By faith Rahab, the loose woman, was not put to death with those who had gone against God's orders, because she had taken into her house in peace those sent to see the land.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, langoe ginɛ Raxabi naxa kisi kaafirie ya ma, barima a nu bara Isirayilaka yire rabɛnyie yigiya a fanyi ra.

sentences.english: What more am I to say? For there would not be time to give the stories of Gideon, Barak, Samson, and Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets:
sentences.susu: N munse sama na fari sɔnɔn? Waxati mu luma n bɛ n xa Gedeyon, Baraki, Samison, Yefite, Dawuda, Samuweli, nun namiɲɔnmɛe xa fee fala.

sentences.english: Who through faith overcame kingdoms, did righteousness, got their reward, kept the mouths of lions shut,
sentences.susu: Danxaniya saabui ra, e naxa nɔ mangataae ra, e naxa ɲɛrɛ tinxinyi kui, e naxa fe laayidixi sɔtɔ, e naxa nɔ yɛtɛ xaaɲɛe ra,

sentences.english: Put out the power of fire, got safely away from the edge of the sword, were made strong when they had been feeble, became full of power in war, and put to flight the armies of the nations.
sentences.susu: e naxa ratanga tɛ xungbe nun santidɛgɛma ma, e xa sɛnbɛtareya naxa findi sɛnbɛ ra, e naxa sɛnbɛ sɔtɔ gere kui, e fa sɔɔri galie keri.

sentences.english: Women had their dead given back to them living; others let themselves be cruelly attacked, having no desire to go free, so that they might have a better life to come;
sentences.susu: Ginɛ ndee naxa e ngaxakerenyi faxaxie to, naxee rakelixi faxɛ ma. Mixi ndee naxa ɲaxankata, e tondi minide na tɔɔrɛ kui, alako e xa marakeli fanyi sɔtɔ.

sentences.english: And others were tested by being laughed at or by blows, and even with chains and prisons:
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee naxa bɔnbɔ, e mayele sɔtɔ, e lu geeli kui, e xirixi yɔlɔnxɔnyi ra.

sentences.english: They were stoned, they were cut up with knives, they were tested, they were put to death with the sword, they went about in sheepskins and in goatskins; being poor and in pain and cruelly attacked,
sentences.susu: Mixi ndee naxa magɔnɔ, e naxa tɔɔrɔ, e naxa a ibolon, e naxa faxa santidɛgɛma ra. Ndee naxa lintan, yɛxɛɛ nun si kiri ragoroxi e ma, se birin baxi e yi ra, e ɲaxankataxi, e halakixi,

sentences.english: Wandering in waste places and in mountains and in holes in the rocks; for whom the world was not good enough.
sentences.susu: e nu fa lintan gbengberenyi ma, geyae longori ra, fɔnmɛe nun yilie kui. A mu nu lanma duniɲa mixie xa na binyɛ sɔtɔ na danxaniyatɔɛe xa lu e ya ma.

sentences.english: And not one of these got the good things of the agreement, though they all had a good record through faith,
sentences.susu: Na mixi naxan birin xili fanyi sɔtɔ e xa danxaniya saabui ra, e mu fee sɔtɔ naxee nu laayidixi e bɛ.

sentences.english: Because God had kept some better thing for us, so that it was not possible for them to become complete without us.
sentences.susu: Ala mu tin e xa fe xa kamali won xanbi. A bara fe fanyi ɲanige won bɛ naxan dangi fe singe ra.

sentences.english: For this reason, as we are circled by so great a cloud of witnesses, putting off every weight, and the sin into which we come so readily, let us keep on running in the way which is marked out for us,
sentences.susu: Na danxaniyatɔɛ gali, naxee bara e xa danxaniya masen duniɲa bɛ, e man xa findi misaali ra won bɛ. Won xa fe birin nun yunubi birin nabolo naxan won tɔɔrɔma won ma ɲɛrɛ kui. Won xa won gi tunnabɛxi ra kira xɔn ma Ala naxan saxi won ya ra.

sentences.english: Having our eyes fixed on Jesus, the guide and end of our faith, who went through the pains of the cross, not caring for the shame, because of the joy which was before him, and who has now taken his place at the right hand of God's seat of power.
sentences.susu: Won xa won ya ti Isa ra, naxan danxaniya kira rabixi won bɛ, naxan fama won ma danxaniya rakamalide. Isa tin nɛ wuri magalanbuxi xa tɔɔrɛ ra, alako a xa sɛɛwa yare. A mu gaaxu na yaagi ra. Na kui, a xa faxɛ dangi xanbi, a naxa a magoro Ala xa kibanyi yirefanyi ma.

sentences.english: Give thought to him who has undergone so much of the hate of sinners against himself, so that you may not be tired and feeble of purpose.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu a xa misaali ma, a tɔɔrɔxi ki naxɛ yunubitɔɛe saabui ra, alako wo naxa tagan, limaniya naxa ba wo yi ra.

sentences.english: Till now you have not given your blood in your fight against sin:
sentences.susu: Wo mu yunubi gerexi sinden, han wo wuli xa mini.

sentences.english: And you have not kept in mind the word which says to you as to sons, My son, do not make little of the Lord's punishment, and do not give up hope when you are judged by him;
sentences.susu: Wo tan, Ala xa die, wo bara nɛɛmu Ala xa masenyi ma wo ralimaniyaxi naxan na, a falafe ra, «N ma di, i naxa yo Marigi xa marakɔrɔsi ma, limaniya naxa ba i yi ra, a i xuruma tɛmui naxɛ.

sentences.english: For the Lord sends punishment on his loved ones; everyone whom he takes as his son has experience of his rod.
sentences.susu: Marigi a xanuntenyi nan xuruma. A naxee birin kolonxi a xa die ra, a e ɲaxankata.»

sentences.english: It is for your training that you undergo these things; God is acting to you as a father does to his sons; for what son does not have punishment from his father?
sentences.susu: Wo xa tin na ra, barima Ala na wo xurufe nɛ alɔ a xa die. Di mundun na, naxan baba mu a xuruma?

sentences.english: But if you have not that punishment of which we all have our part, then you are not true sons, but children of shame.
sentences.susu: Xa Ala mu wo xuruma, alɔ di birin xuruma ki naxɛ, a luxi nɛ alɔ wo mu findixi a xa die ra, a lima a halalɛ mu wo ra.

sentences.english: And again, if the fathers of our flesh gave us punishment and had our respect, how much more will we be under the authority of the Father of spirits, and have life?
sentences.susu: Won babae won xuruma duniɲa, won fan e binya. A mu lanma won xa tin a ra, Baba Ala naxan na ariyanna, a xa won xuru alako won xa kisi?

sentences.english: For they truly gave us punishment for a short time, as it seemed good to them; but he does it for our profit, so that we may become holy as he is.
sentences.susu: Won babae nu won xuruma waxati di nan bun ma e yɛtɛ xaxili ra, kɔnɔ Ala tan won xuruma won ma munafanyi yati nan ma fe ra, alako won xa lu Ala xa sɛniyɛnyi kui.

sentences.english: At the time all punishment seems to be pain and not joy: but after, those who have been trained by it get from it the peace-giving fruit of righteousness.
sentences.susu: Na xurui xɔrɔxɔ, a mu mixi rasɛɛwama a fɔlɛ, kɔnɔ a dɔnxɔɛ ra, a fɔxi tinxinxi raminima nɛ yare bɔɲɛsa kui.

sentences.english: For this cause let the hands which are hanging down be lifted up, and let the feeble knees be made strong,
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, wo xa wo sɛnbɛ so, wo tan naxee bɛlɛxɛe taganxi, naxee xinbi tɔɔrɔxi.

sentences.english: And make straight roads for your feet, so that the feeble may not be turned out of the way, but may be made strong.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo ɲɛrɛ kira tinxinxi xɔn ma, alako mabɛnyie naxa telexun, e xa yalan.

sentences.english: Let your desire be for peace with all men, and to be made holy, without which no man may see the Lord;
sentences.susu: Lanyi xa lu wo nun mixie tagi. Wo xa lu sɛniyɛnyi kui, xa na mu a ra wo mu Marigi toma.

sentences.english: Looking with care to see that no man among you in his behaviour comes short of the grace of God; for fear that some bitter root may come up to be a trouble to you, and that some of you may be made unclean by it;
sentences.susu: Wo xa mɛɛni wo bore ma, alako mixi yo naxa mini Ala xa hinnɛ kui. Wo naxa lu xɔnɔ ra wo bore ma, na fa mixi gbegbe tɔɔrɔ wo ya ma.

sentences.english: And that there may not be any evil liver, or any man without respect for God, like Esau, who let his birthright go for a plate of food.
sentences.susu: Wo mɛɛni de! Wo naxa yɛnɛ raba. Wo naxa sɛriyɛ kana alɔ Esayu, naxan a xa foriɲa tide masaraxi bande lenge keren xa fe ra.

sentences.english: For you have knowledge that even long after, when he was desiring the blessing for his heritage, he was turned away, though he made his request frequently and with weeping; because the past might not be changed.
sentences.susu: Wo a kolon a to nu waxi a baba xa duba a bɛ, a xa foriɲa kɛ sɔtɔ, a baba naxa tondi. Esayu naxa a mayandi yaye ra, kɔnɔ a baba mu tin na ra.

sentences.english: You have not come to a mountain which may be touched, and is burning with fire, and to a black cloud, and a dark smoke, and a violent wind,
sentences.susu: Wo mu wo makɔrɛ na yire ra wo xa wo bɛlɛxɛ din a ra alɔ Isirayilakae fe naxan to gbengberenyi ma. Tɛ nun nuxui fɔɔrɛ nu na geya fari dɛnnaxɛ, foye xungbe nu bɔnbɔ a ra.

sentences.english: And to the sound of a horn, and the voice of words, the hearers of which made request that not a word more might be said to them:
sentences.susu: Wo mu sara xui nun Ala xui magaaxui mɛxi. Isirayilakae to na mɛ, e naxa Munsa mayandi alako e naxa na xui mɛ sɔnɔn.

sentences.english: For the order which said, If the mountain is touched even by a beast, the beast is to be stoned, seemed hard to them;
sentences.susu: E naxa gaaxu Ala xa yaamari ya ra, «Mixi nun sube yo din yi geya ra, na kanyi fama nɛ magɔnɔde, a faxa.»

sentences.english: And the vision was so overpowering that even Moses said, I am shaking and full of fear.
sentences.susu: Na fe nu magaaxu han Annabi Munsa naxa a fala, «N bara gaaxu han n bara sɛrɛn.»

sentences.english: But you have come to the mountain of Zion, to the place of the living God, to the Jerusalem which is in heaven, and to an army of angels which may not be numbered,
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo tan bara wo maso Siyoni geya yire ra, Ala Ɲiɲɛ xa taa naxan na ariyanna, Darisalamu naxan na koore ma, malekɛ wulu wulu malanxi dɛnnaxɛ sɛɛwɛ kui.

sentences.english: To the great meeting and church of the first of those who are named in heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of good men made complete,
sentences.susu: Ala xa ɲama fan na na, naxee xili sɛbɛxi buki kui ariyanna. E findixi Ala xa di singee nan na. Duniɲa Makiitima Ala na mɛnni nɛ, a nun tinxintɔɛ nii naxee xa fe bara kamali.

sentences.english: And to Jesus by whom the new agreement has been made between God and man, and to the sign of the blood which says better things than Abel's blood.
sentences.susu: Isa fan na naa, naxan bara findi saabui ra saatɛ nɛɛnɛ rakamalife ra, naxan wuli bara findi sɛrɛxɛ ra. Na fan dangi Habila gbe sɛrɛxɛ ra.

sentences.english: See that you give ear to his voice which comes to you. For if those whose ears were shut to the voice which came to them on earth did not go free from punishment, what chance have we of going free if we give no attention to him whose voice comes from heaven?
sentences.susu: Wo naxa tondi Ala xa masenyi ra. Mixi naxee tixi duniɲa bɛndɛ fuɲi fari, e to tondi na masenyi ra, e naxa ɲaxankatɛ sɔtɔ. Yakɔsi, won munse sɔtɔma sɔnɔn xa a sa li won tondima masenyi ra, naxan fatanxi Ala yati yati ra naxan na koore ma?

sentences.english: Whose voice was the cause of the shaking of the earth; but now he has made an oath, saying, There will be still one more shaking, not only of the earth, but of heaven.
sentences.susu: Singe Ala xui naxa bɔxi rasɛrɛn, kɔnɔ yakɔsi a bara laayidi tongo, «N man bɔxi rasɛrɛnma nɛ, kɔnɔ yi biyaasi n koore fan nasɛrɛnma nɛ.»

sentences.english: And the words, Still one more, make it clear that there will be a taking away of those things which are shaking, as of things which are made, so that there may be only those things of which no shaking is possible.
sentences.susu: A to a fala, «n man,» na nu wama a masenfe nɛ a se daaxi birin nasɛrɛnma nɛ, a fa kana. Fe naxan mu rasɛrɛnma, na nan luma, a mu kana.

sentences.english: If then, we have a kingdom which will never be moved, let us have grace, so that we may give God such worship as is pleasing to him with fear and respect:
sentences.susu: Won fama lude mangɛya niini naxan bun ma, na tan mu sɛrɛnma, na mu kanama. Na kui, won xa Ala tantu, won xa a batu yaragaaxui nun binyɛ ra a wama naxan xɔn,

sentences.english: For our God is an all-burning fire.
sentences.susu: barima won Marigi Ala luxi nɛ alɔ tɛ naxan se birin ganma.

sentences.english: Go on loving your brothers in the faith.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo tunnabɛxi wo bore maxanufe ra ngaxakerenya kui.

sentences.english: Take care to keep open house: because in this way some have had angels as their guests, without being conscious of it.
sentences.susu: Wo xa xɔɲɛ rasɛnɛ a fanyi ra. Mixi ndee xɔɲɛ yigiyama nɛ, a fa sa li e mu a kolon xa malekɛ na a ra.

sentences.english: Keep in mind those who are in chains, as if you were chained with them, and those who are in trouble, as being yourselves in the body.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu geelimanie ma nun mixie ma naxee ɲaxankataxi. Wo xa fe fanyi raba e bɛ alɔ wo birin na fate bɛndɛ keren nan kui.

sentences.english: Let married life be honoured among all of you and not made unclean; for men untrue in married life will be judged by God.
sentences.susu: Wo birin xa futi binya. Yɛnɛ nun langoeɲa naxa lu wo ya ma, barima Ala fama nɛ na sɛniyɛntareɲa makiitide.

sentences.english: Be free from the love of money and pleased with the things which you have; for he himself has said, I will be with you at all times.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa a lu kɔbiri xa fe milɛ xa wo raɲɛrɛ. Naxan na wo yi, wo xa wo wasa so nɛ. Ala yati naxa a masen, «N mu i rabɛɲinma, n mu i raboloma.»

sentences.english: So that we say with a good heart, The Lord is my helper; I will have no fear: what is man able to do to me?
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi won nɔma a falade limaniya ra, «N Marigi n dɛmɛnma, n mu gaaxuma. Adama tan nɔma munse rabade n na kɔrɛ?»

sentences.english: Keep in mind those who were over you, and who gave you the word of God; seeing the outcome of their way of life, let your faith be like theirs.
sentences.susu: Wo xa ratu wo xa yareratie ma, naxee bara Ala xa masenyi masen wo bɛ. Wo xa e ɲɛrɛ ki mato, e xa danxaniya xa findi misaali ra wo bɛ.

sentences.english: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and for ever.
sentences.susu: Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa mu masarama. A nu na ki naxɛ xoro, a man na na ki nɛ to, a man luma na ki nɛ abadan, na birin kɛɲa keren.

sentences.english: Do not be turned away by different strange teachings, because it is good for your hearts to be made strong by grace, and not by meats, which were of no profit to those who took so much trouble over them.
sentences.susu: Wo naxa bira xaranyi mɔɔli gbɛtɛe fɔxɔ ra. Wo bɔɲɛ xa sɛnbɛ so Ala xa hinnɛ saabui ra. Yaamarie, donse raharamuxie xa fe ra, nee mu nɔma wo malide.

sentences.english: We have an altar from which those priests who are servants in the Tent may not take food.
sentences.susu: Hɔrɔmɔlingira walikɛe mu nɔma sɛrɛxɛ donde naxan baxi won tan bɛ.

sentences.english: For the bodies of the beasts whose blood is taken into the holy place by the high priest as an offering for sin are burned outside the circle of the tents.
sentences.susu: Sɛrɛxɛdubɛ kuntigi xuruse wuli bama nɛ sɛrɛxɛ ra hɔrɔmɔlingira kui yunubie xa fe ra, kɔnɔ na xuruse fate tan ganma nɛ taa fari ma.

sentences.english: For this reason Jesus was put to death outside the walls, so that he might make the people holy by his blood.
sentences.susu: Na nan a toxi, Isa fan to wa ɲama rasɛniyɛnfe a yɛtɛ wuli saabui ra, a naxa ɲaxankata taa fari ma.

sentences.english: Let us then go out to him outside the circle of the tents, taking his shame on ourselves.
sentences.susu: Won fan xa bira a fɔxɔ ra na yaagi kui taa fari ma,

sentences.english: For here we have no fixed resting-place, but our search is for the one which is to come.
sentences.susu: barima won na taa naxan kui, a mu buma. Won taa nan fenfe naxan fama fade.

sentences.english: Let us then make offerings of praise to God at all times through him, that is to say, the fruit of lips giving witness to his name.
sentences.susu: Won xa tantui fi Ala ma sɛrɛxɛ ra tɛmui birin Isa saabui ra. Na sɛrɛxɛ findima won ma masenyi nan na naxan a xili matɔxɔma.

sentences.english: But go on doing good and giving to others, because God is well-pleased with such offerings.
sentences.susu: Wo man naxa nɛɛmu fe fanyie rabade mixie bɛ. Wo xa wo booree ki, barima na fe mɔɔlie findima sɛrɛxɛe nan na naxee rafanxi Ala ma.

sentences.english: Give ear to those who are rulers over you, and do as they say: for they keep watch over your souls, ready to give an account of them; let them be able to do this with joy and not with grief, because that would be of no profit to you.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo xa yareratie xui ratinmɛ, wo xa e xa yaamarie suxu, barima e na mɛɛnife wo ma, alako wo naxa gbilen Ala fɔxɔ ra, xa na mu a ra na dɛntɛgɛ sa fama nɛ e tɔɔrɔde. Wo xa fe birin naba alako e xa nɔ na dɛntɛgɛ sade sɛɛwɛ kui bɔɲɛ mawa xanbi, barima na nan findima wo xa munafanyi ra.

sentences.english: Make prayers for us, for we are certain that our hearts are free from the sense of sin, desiring the right way of life in all things.
sentences.susu: Wo xa Ala maxandi muxu bɛ, barima muxu a kolon muxu xaxili fiixɛ, muxu wama ɲɛrɛfe fe fanyi mɔɔli birin nan kui.

sentences.english: I make this request more strongly, in the hope of coming back to you more quickly.
sentences.susu: Wo man xa Ala maxandi muxu bɛ, alako n xa nɔ gbilende wo yire mafuren mafuren.

sentences.english: Now may the God of peace, who made that great keeper of his flock, even our Lord Jesus, come back from the dead through the blood of the eternal agreement,
sentences.susu: Ala naxan bɔɲɛsa fima mixi ma, Ala naxan won Marigi Isa rakeli faxɛ ma, Isa naxan mɛɛnima a xa mixie ma a xa saatɛ wuli saabui ra, saatɛ naxan mu kanama abadan,

sentences.english: Make you full of every good work and ready to do all his desires, working in us whatever is pleasing in his eyes through Jesus Christ; and may the glory be given to him for ever and ever. So be it.
sentences.susu: Ala xa fɛɛrɛ birin fi wo ma alako wo xa nɔ a sago rabade. Ala xa fe lu won bɔɲɛ ma naxan nafan a ma a xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa saabui ra. Matɔxɔɛ na a bɛ abadan. Amina.

sentences.english: But, brothers, take kindly the words which I have said for your profit; for I have not sent you a long letter.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo xa wo haakɛ to n bɛ yi masenyi xa fe ra, barima n mu wɔyɛnyi xɔnkuyaxi a gbe ra.

sentences.english: Our brother Timothy has been let out of prison; and if he comes here in a short time, he and I will come to you together.
sentences.susu: Wo xa a kolon won ngaxakerenyi Timote bara a yɛtɛ sɔtɔ. Xa a mu bu fade, muxu birin fama nɛ wo yire.

sentences.english: Give words of love from me to those who are rulers over you, and to all the saints. Those who are in Italy send you their love.
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo xa yareratie nun sɛniyɛntɔɛ birin xɛɛbu muxu bɛ. Italikae naxee na be, e fan bara wo xɛɛbu.

sentences.english: May grace be with you all.
sentences.susu: Ala xa hinnɛ wo birin na.

sentences.english: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, sends words of love to the twelve tribes of the Jews living in all parts of the earth.
sentences.susu: N tan Yaki nan yi ki, Ala nun a xa Mixi Sugandixi Marigi Isa xa konyi. N bara wo xɛɛbu, wo tan Isirayila bɔnsɔɛ fu nun firinyi naxee yensenxi ɲamanɛe ma.

sentences.english: Let it be all joy to you, my brothers, when you undergo tests of every sort;
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo xa sɛɛwa tɔɔrɛ mɔɔli birin kui,

sentences.english: Because you have the knowledge that the testing of your faith gives you the power of going on in hope;
sentences.susu: barima wo a kolon a wo tɔɔrɛ naxan sɔtɔma danxaniya kui, a wo duluxɔtɔma nɛ.

sentences.english: But let this power have its full effect, so that you may be made complete, needing nothing.
sentences.susu: Wo xa duluxɔtɔ han a raɲɔnyi alako wo xa danxaniya xa tilin, wo xa findi mixi kamalixie ra, fefe mu luxi naxee xa fe ra.

sentences.english: But if any man among you is without wisdom, let him make his request to God, who gives freely to all without an unkind word, and it will be given to him.
sentences.susu: Xa fahaamui mu na mixi nde yi ra wo ya ma, a kanyi xa Ala maxandi. A a sɔtɔma nɛ, barima Ala mixi birin kima a yiriwaxi ra a xa fonisireya ma.

sentences.english: Let him make his request in faith, doubting nothing; for he who has doubt in his heart is like the waves of the sea, which are troubled by the driving of the wind.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ fo mixi xa Ala maxandi danxaniya ra, a naxa siikɛ, barima mixi siikɛxi luma nɛ alɔ mɔrɔnyi, foye naxan bɔnbɔma, a a matutun.

sentences.english: Let it not seem to such a man that he will get anything from the Lord;
sentences.susu: Na kanyi naxa a maɲɔxun a a se nde sɔtɔma Ala ra,

sentences.english: For there is a division in his mind, and he is uncertain in all his ways.
sentences.susu: barima a xaxili mu tixi Ala gbansan xa ra, a sanyie na kira wuyaxi nan xɔn.

sentences.english: But let the brother of low position be glad that he is lifted up;
sentences.susu: Danxaniyatɔɛ setare xa sɛɛwa barima Ala bara a xa fe ite.

sentences.english: But the man of wealth, that he is made low; because like the flower of the grass he will come to his end.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ banna tan xa sɛɛwa Ala to bara a xa fe magoro, barima a xa fe ɲɔnma nɛ alɔ sansi fuge tofanyi.

sentences.english: For when the sun comes up with its burning heat, the grass gets dry and the grace of its form is gone with the falling flower; so the man of wealth comes to nothing in his ways.
sentences.susu: Soge xɔnɛ na te, sansi lisima nɛ han a fuge bira, a xa tofanyi ɲɔn. A na na ki nɛ banna fan bɛ. A na a xa walie kui tɛmui naxɛ, a birima na lɛɛri nɛ.

sentences.english: There is a blessing on the man who undergoes testing; because, if he has God's approval, he will be given the crown of life, which the Lord has said he will give to those who have love for him.
sentences.susu: Ɲɛlɛxinyi na mixi bɛ naxan a tunnabɛxima tɔɔrɛ kui, barima xa a bara gɛ na tɔɔrɛ raxande, Ala kisi xunnakeli fima nɛ a ma. Ala na nan laayidixi a xanuntenyie bɛ.

sentences.english: Let no man say when he is tested, I am tested by God; for it is not possible for God to be tested by evil, and he himself puts no man to such a test:
sentences.susu: Mixi nɛ wama tantanfe, a naxa a fala a Ala nan a ratantanfe, barima Ala mu birama fe ɲaaxi fɔxɔ ra, a man mu adama yo ratantanma fe ɲaaxi ra.

sentences.english: But every man is tested when he is turned out of the right way by the attraction of his desire.
sentences.susu: Adama yɛtɛ waxɔnfe ɲaaxi nan a ratantanma. Na nan a mabɛndunma han a a rabira.

sentences.english: Then when its time comes, desire gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is of full growth, gives birth to death.
sentences.susu: Adama waxɔnfe ɲaaxi xa di findixi yunubi nan na. Yunubi fan na raba, a xa di findima faxɛ nan na.

sentences.english: Do not be turned from the right way, dear brothers.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyi xanuxie, wo naxa la wule ra.

sentences.english: Every good and true thing is given to us from heaven, coming from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change or any shade made by turning.
sentences.susu: Ki hagigɛ birin fatanxi Daali Mangɛ nan na naxan na koore, naxan soge, kike, nun tunbuie daaxi, naxan mu masarama abadan.

sentences.english: Of his purpose he gave us being, by his true word, so that we might be, in a sense, the first-fruits of all the things which he had made.
sentences.susu: A yɛtɛ sagoe ma, Ala bara won nakisi a xa nɔndi masenyi saabui ra, a won findi a xa die ra, alako won xa binyɛ sɔtɔ dangife a xa daalise birin na.

sentences.english: You have knowledge of this, dear brothers. But let every man be quick in hearing, slow in words, slow to get angry;
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyi xanuxie, wo xa yi wɔyɛnyi mɛ: Wo birin xa wo tuli mati wo bore ra, wo naxa gbata wɔyɛnyi ra, wo bɔɲɛ naxa te mafuren na,

sentences.english: For the righteousness of God does not come about by the wrath of man.
sentences.susu: barima adamadi xa xɔnɛ mu a tutunma Ala xa tinxinyi ma.

sentences.english: For this reason, putting away all dirty behaviour and the overweight of evil, take into your souls without pride the word which, being planted there, is able to give you salvation.
sentences.susu: Na na a ra, wo xa tondi fe ɲaaxi nun fe kobi mɔɔli birin nabade. Wo xa wo yɛtɛ magoro, wo xa nɔndi suxu naxan bara masen wo bɛ, barima na nan nɔma wo rakiside.

sentences.english: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers of it, blinding yourselves with false ideas.
sentences.susu: Wo xa Ala xa masenyi rabatu. Xa wo a ramɛ gbansan kɔnɔ wo mu a raba, wo bara wo yɛtɛ madaxu.

sentences.english: Because if any man is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a glass;
sentences.susu: Xa mixi nde Ala xa masenyi ramɛ, kɔnɔ a mu bira a fɔxɔ ra, a luma nɛ alɔ mixi naxan a yatagi matoma kike ma,

sentences.english: For after looking at himself he goes away, and in a short time he has no memory of what he was like.
sentences.susu: a fa siga, a nɛɛmu a yatagi ma a na ki naxɛ.

sentences.english: But he who goes on looking into the true law which makes him free, being not a hearer without memory but a doer putting it into effect, this man will have a blessing on his acts.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi naxan Ala xa sɛriyɛ kamalixi matoma a fanyi ra, a a tunnabɛxi, a mu nɛɛmu sɛriyɛ ma kɔnɔ a a rabatu, na kanyi barakama nɛ. Ala xa sɛriyɛ xɔrɛya fima nɛ adamadie ma.

sentences.english: If a man seems to have religion and has no control over his tongue but lets himself be tricked by what is false, this man's religion is of no value.
sentences.susu: Mixi yo a yɛtɛ maɲɔxun diinɛla ra, kɔnɔ a mu a dɛ nɔxi, na kanyi na a yɛtɛ madaxufe nɛ. A xa diinɛ tide yo mu na.

sentences.english: The religion which is holy and free from evil in the eyes of our God and Father is this: to take care of children who have no fathers and of widows who are in trouble, and to keep oneself untouched by the world.
sentences.susu: Diinɛ fiixɛ naxan nafan Baba Ala ma, a tan nan ya: won xa mɛɛni kiridie nun kaaɲɛ ginɛe ma e xa tɔɔrɛ kui, duniɲa fe man naxa wo madaxu.

sentences.english: My brothers, if you have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory, do not take a man's position into account.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo naxa mixie rafisa e boore bɛ, barima wo danxaniyaxi won Marigi Isa Nɔrɛ Kanyi nan ma, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi.

sentences.english: For if a man comes into your Synagogue in fair clothing and with a gold ring, and a poor man comes in with dirty clothing,
sentences.susu: Wo xa wo maɲɔxun yi ma: Mixi nde naxa fa wo malanxi dɛnnaxɛ, xurundɛ xɛɛma daaxi na a bɛlɛxɛ ra, dugi tofanyi ragoroxi a ma. Setare fan naxa fa, dugi fori toɲaaxi ragoroxi a ma.

sentences.english: And you do honour to the man in fair clothing and say, Come here and take this good place; and you say to the poor man, Take up your position there, or be seated at my feet;
sentences.susu: Xa wo dugi tofanyi kanyi xɛɛbu a fanyi ra, wo fa a fala a bɛ, «I magorode fanyi nan yi ki,» kɔnɔ wo fa a fala setare tan bɛ, «Ti mɛnni,» xa na mu a ra, «Dɔxɔ bɔxi, n bun ma be,»

sentences.english: Is there not a division in your minds? have you not become judges with evil thoughts?
sentences.susu: wo mu mixi rafisaxi a boore bɛ xɛ na ki? Wo mu ɲɛrɛxi maɲɔxun kobi xa ra na ki?

sentences.english: Give ear, my dear brothers; are not those who are poor in the things of this world marked out by God to have faith as their wealth, and for their heritage the kingdom which he has said he will give to those who have love for him?
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyi xanuxie, wo wo tuli mati n na. Ala bara mixie sugandi naxee findixi setaree ra duniɲa ki ma, alako e xa findi bannamixie ra danxaniya ki ma. Ala bara e sugandi alako e xa findi kɛtongoe ra a xa mangɛya kui. Na nan laayidixi mixie bɛ naxee Ala xanuxi.

sentences.english: But you have put the poor man to shame. Are not the men of wealth rulers over you? do they not take you by force before their judges?
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ wo tan, wo bara setaree mabere. Bannamixie xa mu wo tɔɔrɔma, e wo xanin kiitisa xɔn ma?

sentences.english: Do they not say evil of the holy name which was given to you?
sentences.susu: E tan xa mu wo Marigi xili fanyi rasɔtɔma?

sentences.english: But if you keep the greatest law of all, as it is given in the holy Writings, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself, you do well:
sentences.susu: Wo xa Mangɛ Alatala xa sɛriyɛ nan nabatu, alɔ a sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui ki naxɛ, «I xa i boore xanu alɔ i yɛtɛ kan gundi.» Xa wo na raba, wo bara bira fe fanyi fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But if you take a man's position into account, you do evil, and are judged as evil-doers by the law.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ xa wo mixi ndee rafisa e boore bɛ, wo bara yunubi raba. Sɛriyɛ nan wo makiitima, barima wo bara findi sɛriyɛ matandilae ra.

sentences.english: For anyone who keeps all the law, but makes a slip in one point, is judged to have gone against it all.
sentences.susu: Xa mixi sɛriyɛ birin nabatu kɔnɔ a yire keren matandi, na kanyi bara sɛriyɛ birin matandi,

sentences.english: For he who said, Do not be untrue in married life, is the same who said, Put no man to death. Now if you are not untrue in married life, but you put a man to death, the law is broken.
sentences.susu: barima naxan a falaxi, «I naxa yɛnɛ raba,» a tan nan man a falaxi, «I naxa faxɛ ti.» Hali i mu yɛnɛ raba, kɔnɔ xa i faxɛ ti, i findixi Ala xa sɛriyɛ matandila nan na.

sentences.english: Let your words and your acts be those of men who are to be judged by the law which makes free.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa wɔyɛn, wo man xa wo ɲɛrɛ alɔ naxee fama makiitide sɛriyɛ ra naxan xɔrɛya fima mixi ma.

sentences.english: For the man who has had no mercy will be judged without mercy, but mercy takes pride in overcoming judging.
sentences.susu: Kiiti lɔxɔɛ, Ala mu kinikinima mixi ma naxan mu kinikini a boore adama ma. Kinikini sɛnbɛ gbo kiiti bɛ.

sentences.english: What use is it, my brothers, for a man to say that he has faith, if he does nothing? will such a faith give him salvation?
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, a tide yo mu na xa mixi a fala a a danxaniyaxi, kɔnɔ a mu kɛwali fanyi rabama. Yi danxaniya mɔɔli nɔma mixi rakiside?

sentences.english: If a brother or a sister is without clothing and in need of the day's food,
sentences.susu: Xa wo ngaxakerenyi mageli na a ra, lɔxɔɛ keren baloe mu na a yi ra,

sentences.english: And one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warm and full of food; but you do not give them the things of which their bodies have need, what profit is there in this?
sentences.susu: mixi nde fa lu wo ya ma a a fala a bɛ, «Siga, i naxa kɔntɔfili, i xa dugi nde ragoro i ma, i xa i dɛge,» kɔnɔ a fa lu a mu a xa kɔntɔfili ba, na kanyi xa wɔyɛnyi tide yo mu na.

sentences.english: Even so faith without works is dead.
sentences.susu: Danxaniya na na ki nɛ. Xa a mu mixi tutunma wali fanyie rabafe ma, a tide yo mu na.

sentences.english: But a man may say, You have faith and I have works; let me see your faith without your works, and I will make my faith clear to you by my works.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ mixi nde nɔma a falade, «I tan, danxaniya kanyi nan i ra, kɔnɔ n tan fe fanyi raba nan n na.» Kata i xa i xa danxaniya masen n bɛ wali fanyi xanbi. N tan n ma danxaniya masenma i bɛ n ma kɛwali fanyi nan saabui ra.

sentences.english: You have the belief that God is one, and you do well: the evil spirits have the same belief, shaking with fear.
sentences.susu: I laxi a ra, a Ala keren na a ra. Na fan ki fanyi, kɔnɔ hali ɲinnɛe laxi na ra, e sɛrɛn gaaxui ra.

sentences.english: Do you not see, O foolish man, that faith without works is of no use?
sentences.susu: I tan xaxilitare, i mu a kolon danxaniya naxan mu kɛwali fanyi raminima, a tide yo mu na?

sentences.english: Was not the righteousness of Abraham our father judged by his works, when he made an offering of Isaac his son on the altar?
sentences.susu: Munfe a niya won baba Iburahima naxa findi tinxintɔɛ ra Ala ya i? A mu fatan a xa kɛwalie xa ma, a to a xa di Isiyaga fi Ala ma sɛrɛxɛbade fari?

sentences.english: You see that his faith was helping his works and was made complete by them;
sentences.susu: I bara a to, danxaniya nu walife nɛ a nun a xa kɛwali. Kɛwali nan danxaniya rakamalima.

sentences.english: And the holy Writings were put into effect which said, And Abraham had faith in God and it was put to his account as righteousness; and he was named the friend of God.
sentences.susu: Na kui, a naxa raba alɔ a sɛbɛxi Kitaabui kui ki naxɛ, «Iburahima naxa la Ala ra. Alatala fan naxa na findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ.» Iburahima xili naxa fala «Ala xanuntenyi».

sentences.english: You see that a man's righteousness is judged by his works and not by his faith only.
sentences.susu: Wo bara a to, adamadi xa kɛwali findima tinxinyi nan na a bɛ, a xa danxaniya gbansan xa mu a ra.

sentences.english: And in the same way, was not the righteousness of Rahab, the loose woman, judged by her works, when she took into her house those who were sent and let them go out by another way?
sentences.susu: Langoe ginɛ Raxabi fan xa kɛwali xa mu findi tinxinyi ra a bɛ, a to xɛɛrae rasɛnɛ a xɔnyi, a kira masen e bɛ e e gima naxan na?

sentences.english: For as the body without the spirit is dead even so faith without works is dead.
sentences.susu: Mixi nii na siga, a fate faxama nɛ. Na kui, xa kɛwali fanyi mu na, danxaniya fan ɲɔnma nɛ.

sentences.english: Do not all be teachers, my brothers, because we teachers will be judged more hardly than others.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, a mu lanma mixi wuyaxi xa findi karamɔxɔ ra wo ya ma, barima karamɔxɔe fama makiitide nɛ a xɔrɔxɔɛ ra dangi mixi gbɛtɛe ra.

sentences.english: For we all go wrong in a number of things. If a man never makes a slip in his talk, then he is a complete man and able to keep all his body in control.
sentences.susu: Won birin tantanma fe wuyaxi ma. Xa mixi nde mu tantanma a xa wɔyɛnyi kui, a mu tantanma dɛdɛ. Na kanyi nɔma a yɛtɛ birin suxude tinxinyi kui.

sentences.english: Now if we put bits of iron into horses' mouths so that they may be guided by us, we have complete control of their bodies.
sentences.susu: Mixi na wa soe xa a waxɔnfe raba, a karafoe nan nasoma a dɛ i. Na nan nɔma a fate birin naɲɛrede.

sentences.english: And again ships, though they are so great and are moved by violent winds, are turned by a very small guiding-blade, at the impulse of the man who is using it.
sentences.susu: Kunkui fan na na ki nɛ. Hali kunkui belebele, foye xungbe naxan tutunma, mixi a raɲɛrɛma feya xurudi nan na, a a ragi a na wa sigafe dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: Even so the tongue is a small part of the body, but it takes credit for great things. How much wood may be lighted by a very little fire!
sentences.susu: Nɛnyi fan xurun, kɔnɔ a fe igboma. Wo a mato, tɛ dondoronti di nɔma wondi belebele gande.

sentences.english: And the tongue is a fire; it is the power of evil placed in our bodies, making all the body unclean, putting the wheel of life on fire, and getting its fire from hell.
sentences.susu: Tɛ nan na nɛnyi fan na, naxan findixi duniɲa fe kobi ra. Fate birin nɔxɔma fe ɲaaxi ra a xa wali saabui nan na. Mixi nɛnyi nɔma tɛ sode a xa duniɲɛigiri birin na, barima tɛ nan na nɛnyi ra, tɛ naxan kelima yahannama.

sentences.english: For every sort of beast and bird and every living thing on earth and in the sea has been controlled by man and is under his authority;
sentences.susu: Adamadi nɔma daalise mɔɔli birin xurude. Sube xaaɲɛe, xɔnie, bubusee, nun baa ma yɛxɛe, adamadi bara e birin xuru,

sentences.english: But the tongue may not be controlled by man; it is an unresting evil, it is full of the poison of death.
sentences.susu: kɔnɔ mixi yo mu nɔma adamadi nɛnyi xurude. Xɔnɛ na a ra naxan ma lintanyi mu danma, naxan xa kasarɛ mu ɲɔnma.

sentences.english: With it we give praise to our Lord and Father; and with it we put a curse on men who are made in God's image.
sentences.susu: Won won Baba, won Marigi, batuma nɛnyi kerenyi naxan na, won man adamadi dankama a tan nan na, Ala naxan daaxi a yɛtɛ misaali ra.

sentences.english: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, it is not right for these things to be so.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, dubɛ nun dankɛ minife dɛ keren na, a mu fan.

sentences.english: Does the fountain send from the same outlet sweet and bitter water?
sentences.susu: Ye xɔnɛ nun ye bɛxi nɔma minide dulonyi keren na?

sentences.english: Is a fig-tree able to give us olives, my brothers, or do we get figs from a vine, or sweet water from the salt sea?
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, xɔrɛ bili nɔma tugi bogi raminide? Mangoe bili nɔma xɔrɛ bogi raminide? Fɔxɛ ye minima dulonyi naxan na, ye bɛxi mu minima mɛnni ra.

sentences.english: Who has wisdom and good sense among you? let him make his works clear by a life of gentle wisdom.
sentences.susu: Nde findixi fahaamula nun xaxilima ra wo ya ma? A xa na masen a ɲɛrɛ ki fanyi nun a xa kɛwalie ra, a naxee rabama bɔɲɛ bɛxi kui, naxan fatanxi fahaamui ra.

sentences.english: But if you have bitter envy in your heart and the desire to get the better of others, have no pride in this, talking falsely against what is true.
sentences.susu: Xa tɔɔnɛ ɲaaxi nun milɛ na wo bɔɲɛ kui, wo naxa wo yɛtɛ igbo na fee kui, wo naxa nɔndi masara wule ra.

sentences.english: This wisdom is not from heaven, but is of the earth and the flesh and the Evil One.
sentences.susu: Na xaxili mɔɔli mu kelixi koore xɛ. A kelixi duniɲa nɛ, Ala kolontareya, nun Ibulisa ma.

sentences.english: For where envy is, and the desire to get the better of others, there is no order, but every sort of evil-doing.
sentences.susu: Tɔɔnɛ nun milɛ na dɛnnaxɛ, ya isoe nun fe kobi mɔɔli birin toma na nɛ.

sentences.english: But the wisdom which is from heaven is first holy, then gentle, readily giving way in argument, full of peace and mercy and good works, not doubting, not seeming other than it is.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ fahaamui naxan kelixi koore ma, a sɛniyɛn, a mixi bɔɲɛ sama, a diɲɛma, a kinikinima, a kɛwali fanyi raminima, a mu mixi rafisama a boore bɛ, a mu filankafuiɲa rabama.

sentences.english: And the fruit of righteousness is planted in peace for those who make peace.
sentences.susu: Maale bogi minima a garansanma bɛ ki naxɛ, tinxinyi fan minima mixi bɛ na ki nɛ naxan birama lanyi nun bɔɲɛsa fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: What is the cause of wars and fighting among you? is it not in your desires which are at war in your bodies?
sentences.susu: Wo sɔnxɔma, wo gerema. Na rakelima mun ma? A mu kelima wo waxɔnfe kobie xa ma naxee e boore gerema wo bɔɲɛ kui?

sentences.english: You are burning with desire, and have not your desire, so you put men to death; you are full of envy, and you are not able to get your desire, so you are fighting and making war; you have not your desire, because you do not make request for it.
sentences.susu: Wo wama se nde xɔn, kɔnɔ wo mu a sɔtɔma. Wo faxɛ tima, wo mila wo boore xa se ma, kɔnɔ wo mu nɔma wo waxɔnfe sɔtɔde. Wo sɔnxɔma, wo gerema, kɔnɔ na birin, wo mu sese sɔtɔma barima wo mu Ala maxandima.

sentences.english: You make your request but you do not get it, because your request has been wrongly made, desiring the thing only so that you may make use of it for your pleasure.
sentences.susu: Wo na Ala maxandi fan, wo man mu sese sɔtɔma, barima wo xa maxandi mu fan. Wo maxandi tima alako wo na naxan yo sɔtɔ wo xa a rawali wo waxɔnfe kobie kui.

sentences.english: O you who are false to God, do you not see that the friends of this world are not God's friends? Every man desiring to be a friend of this world makes himself a hater of God.
sentences.susu: Wo tan danxaniyataree, wo mu a kolon naxan duniɲa maxanuma na bara Ala findi a yaxui ra? Duniɲa xanuntenyi findixi mixi nan na naxan Ala xɔnxi.

sentences.english: Or does it seem to you that it is for nothing that the holy Writings say, The spirit which God put into our hearts has a strong desire for us?
sentences.susu: Wo mu Ala xa Kitaabui xa masenyi kolon? Ala wama nɛ won xaxili, a bara naxan fi won ma, a xa bira a tan keren nan fɔxɔ ra.

sentences.english: But he gives more grace. So that the Writings say, God is against the men of pride, but he gives grace to those who make themselves low before him.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ na birin kui, Ala xa hinnɛ gbo dangi fe birin na. Kitaabui a masenma, «Ala mu tinma yɛtɛ igboe ra, kɔnɔ a hinnɛma yɛtɛ magore ra.»

sentences.english: For this cause be ruled by God; but make war on the Evil One and he will be put to flight before you.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa wo yɛtɛ magoro Ala bɛ. Wo tondi Ibulisa bɛ, a fan a gima nɛ wo ya ra.

sentences.english: Come near to God and he will come near to you. Make your hands clean, you evil-doers; put away deceit from your hearts, you false in mind.
sentences.susu: Wo wo maso Ala ra, a fan a masoma nɛ wo ra. Yunubitɔɛe, wo wo yɛtɛ rasɛniyɛn. Filankafuie, wo wo bɔɲɛ rafiixɛ.

sentences.english: Be troubled, with sorrow and weeping; let your laughing be turned to sorrow and your joy to grief.
sentences.susu: Wo wa, wo sunnun, wo nimisa. Wo xa yele xa findi wo bɛ wa ra, wo xa sɛɛwɛ xa findi sunnunyi ra.

sentences.english: Make yourselves low in the eyes of the Lord and you will be lifted up by him.
sentences.susu: Wo wo magoro Marigi bɛ, a fan wo xa fe itema nɛ.

sentences.english: Do not say evil against one another, my brothers. He who says evil against his brother or makes himself his brother's judge, says evil against the law and is judging the law: and in judging the law you become, not a doer of the law but a judge.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo naxa fe kobi fala wo bore xa fe ra. Mixi naxan fe kobi falama a ngaxakerenyi xa fe ra, a a yɛtɛ rafisa a bɛ, na kanyi bara Ala xa sɛriyɛ matandi. A a yɛtɛ rafisaxi Ala xa sɛriyɛ nan bɛ na ki. Xa i bara na raba, i mu na Ala xa sɛriyɛ rabatufe xɛ, i na a matandife nɛ.

sentences.english: There is only one judge and law-giver, even he who has the power of salvation and of destruction; but who are you to be your neighbour's judge?
sentences.susu: Sɛriyɛsa keren peti na a ra, kiitisa fan keren peti na a ra. A tan nan nɔma mixi rakiside, a tan nan nɔma mixi ralɔɛde. Kɔnɔ i tan, nde na i ra, i to i yɛtɛ findixi i boore makiitima ra?

sentences.english: How foolish it is to say, Today or tomorrow we will go into this town, and be there for a year and do business there and get wealth:
sentences.susu: Wo wo tuli mati, wo tan naxee a falama, «To, xa na mu tina, muxu sigama nɛ taa nde, muxu ɲɛ keren ti na yulɛya raba kui, muxu geeni sɔtɔ.»

sentences.english: When you are not certain what will take place tomorrow. What is your life? It is a mist, which is seen for a little time and then is gone.
sentences.susu: Wo na fe mɔɔli falama kɔnɔ wo ɲan mu a kolon naxan fama rabade tina. Wo xa duniɲɛigiri findixi munse ra? Wo luxi nɛ alɔ wuyɛnga naxan toma dondoronti, a fa lɔɛ.

sentences.english: But the right thing to say would be, If it is the Lord's pleasure and if we are still living, we will do this and that.
sentences.susu: A lanma nɛ wo xa yi nan fala, «Xa Ala tin, muxu tina toma nɛ, muxu yi nun yi raba.»

sentences.english: But now you go on glorying in your pride: and all such glorying is evil.
sentences.susu: Kɔnɔ yɛtɛ igboe nan na wo ra. Na mu fan.

sentences.english: The man who has knowledge of how to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin.
sentences.susu: Na kui, xa mixi fe fanyi kolon a lanma a xa naxan naba kɔnɔ a mu a rabama, na bara findi na kanyi bɛ yunubi ra.

sentences.english: Come now, you men of wealth, give yourselves to weeping and crying because of the bitter troubles which are coming to you.
sentences.susu: Yakɔsi wo wo tuli mati, wo tan bannae. Wo xa wo wa xui ite, barima gbaloe nan fafe wo ma.

sentences.english: Your wealth is unclean and insects have made holes in your clothing.
sentences.susu: Wo xa bannaya xun bara rakana, wo xa dugie bara bɔrɔ.

sentences.english: Your gold and your silver are wasted and their waste will be a witness against you, burning into your flesh. You have put by your store in the last days.
sentences.susu: Wo xa xɛɛma nun gbeti bara xɔrixɔri. Na findima seede nan na wo xili ma, a a niya wo fate xa gan tɛ ra. Wo bara naafuli malan yi waxati, kɔnɔ waxati dɔnxɔɛ na a ra.

sentences.english: See, the money which you falsely kept back from the workers cutting the grass in your field, is crying out against you; and the cries of those who took in your grain have come to the ears of the Lord of armies.
sentences.susu: Wo wo tuli mati, wo tan naxee tondixi wo xa xɛ xabae sare fide. Wo xa walikɛe wa xui bara Ala, Daali Mangɛ, tuli li.

sentences.english: You have been living delicately on earth and have taken your pleasure; you have made your hearts fat for a day of destruction.
sentences.susu: Wo xa duniɲɛigiri kui, wo mu tɔnyi dɔxɔxi wo waxɔnfe sese ma. Wo wo yɛtɛ nan tun nalugama. Wo fa luxi nɛ alɔ xuruse turaxi a kɔn naxaba lɔxɔɛ ma.

sentences.english: You have given your decision against the upright man and have put him to death. He puts up no fight against you.
sentences.susu: Wo bara kiiti ɲaaxi sa tinxintɔɛe ma naxee mu nu tixi wo kanke, wo e faxa.

sentences.english: Go on waiting calmly, my brothers, till the coming of the Lord, like the farmer waiting for the good fruit of the earth till the early and late rains have come.
sentences.susu: Na kui, n ngaxakerenyie, wo xa diɲɛ han Marigi fa lɔxɔɛ. Wo xa a raba alɔ xɛsa a rabama ki naxɛ. A diɲɛ han tunɛbirɛ, naxan a niyama sansi xa mɔ, a bogi.

sentences.english: Be as calm in your waiting; let your hearts be strong: because the coming of the Lord is near.
sentences.susu: Wo fan xa diɲɛ. Wo xa limaniya, barima Marigi fa lɔxɔɛ bara makɔrɛ.

sentences.english: Say no hard things against one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged; see, the judge is waiting at the doors.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo naxa fe kobi fala wo bore xa fe ra, xa na mu a ra kiiti na sa, a mu fanma wo bɛ. A gbe mu luxi kiitisa xa fa.

sentences.english: Take as an example of pain nobly undergone and of strength in trouble, the prophets who gave to men the words of the Lord.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, wo xa lu alɔ namiɲɔnmɛ naxee kawandi ti Marigi xili ra, e e tunnabɛxi tɔɔrɛ kui.

sentences.english: We say that those men who have gone through pain are happy: you have the story of Job and the troubles through which he went and have seen that the Lord was full of pity and mercy in the end.
sentences.susu: Won a kolon barakɛ na mixi bɛ naxan a tunnabɛxima tɔɔrɛ kui. Wo bara a mɛ Ayuba a tunnabɛxi ki naxɛ. Wo man bara a to Marigi naxan nabaxi a bɛ a xa tɔɔrɛ dangi xanbi. Marigi xa xanunteya nun a xa kinikini gbo.

sentences.english: But most of all, my brothers, do not take oaths, not by the heaven, or by the earth, or by any other thing: but let your Yes be Yes, and your No be No: so that you may not be judged.
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, naxan dangi fe birin na, wo naxa wo kali koore ra, wo naxa wo kali bɔxi ra, wo naxa wo kali sese ra. Wo na «iyo» fala, a xa findi nɔndi ra. Wo na «ade» fala, a xa findi nɔndi ra. Xa na mu a ra kiiti na sa, a mu fanma wo bɛ.

sentences.english: Is anyone among you in trouble? let him say prayers. Is anyone glad? let him make a song of praise.
sentences.susu: Mixi na wo ya ma naxan tɔɔrɔxi? A kanyi xa Ala maxandi. Mixi na wo ya ma naxan ɲɛlɛxinxi? A kanyi xa Ala tantu bɛɛti ra.

sentences.english: Is anyone among you ill? let him send for the rulers of the church; and let them say prayers over him, putting oil on him in the name of the Lord.
sentences.susu: Mixi na wo ya ma naxan furaxi? A kanyi xa danxaniyatɔɛ ɲama kuntigie xili, e xa Ala maxandi a bɛ, e xa ture nde maso a ma Marigi xili ra.

sentences.english: And by the prayer of faith the man who is ill will be made well, and he will be lifted up by the Lord, and for any sin which he has done he will have forgiveness.
sentences.susu: Ala maxandi naxan fatanxi danxaniya ra, a furema rayalanma nɛ. Marigi furema rakelima nɛ. Xa a bara yunubi raba, Marigi a xafarima nɛ.

sentences.english: So then, make a statement of your sins to one another, and say prayers for one another so that you may be made well. The prayer of a good man is full of power in its working.
sentences.susu: Na kui, wo xa wo xa yunubie fala wo bore bɛ, wo xa Ala maxandi wo bore bɛ, alako wo xa yalan. Tinxintɔɛ Ala maxandi naxan tima, na Ala maxandi xa wali sɛnbɛ gbo.

sentences.english: Elijah was a man of flesh and blood as we are, and he made a strong prayer that there might be no rain; and there was no rain on the earth for three years and six months.
sentences.susu: Eliya nu findixi adamadi nan na alɔ won tan. A to Ala maxandi a bɔɲɛ birin na alako tunɛ naxa fa, Ala naxa a xa dubɛ suxu. Tunɛ mu fa bɔxi ɲɛ saxan kike senni.

sentences.english: And he made another prayer, and the heaven sent down rain and the earth gave her fruit.
sentences.susu: Na dangi xanbi, Eliya man naxa Ala maxandi tunɛ man xa fa. Koore naxa tunɛ bɛɲin, bɔxi sansie naxa bogie ramini.

sentences.english: My brothers, if one of you has gone out of the way of the true faith and another has made him see his error,
sentences.susu: N ngaxakerenyie, xa mixi nde wo ya ma a bara nɔndi kira bɛɲin, kɔnɔ mixi gbɛtɛ fa a ti kira fanyi xɔn ma,

sentences.english: Be certain that he through whom a sinner has been turned from the error of his way, keeps a soul from death and is the cause of forgiveness for sins without number.
sentences.susu: wo xa a kolon, mixi naxan yunubitɔɛ bama a xa yunubi fe ma, a bara a niya yunubitɔɛ xa kisi, a xa yunubi birin bara xafari.

sentences.english: Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, to the saints who are living in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
sentences.susu: N tan Piyɛri, Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa xa xɛɛra, n bara wo xɛɛbu yi sɛbɛli ra, wo tan mixi sugandixi naxee yensenxi ɲamanɛe ma alɔ Pontu, Galati, Kapadose, Asi, nun Bitiniya, e findi xɔɲɛe ra dɛnnaxɛ.

sentences.english: Who, through the purpose of God, have been made holy by the Spirit, disciples of Jesus, made clean by his blood: May you have grace and peace in full measure.
sentences.susu: Baba Ala nu bara wo sugandi kabi a rakuya alɔ a nu wama a xɔn ma ki naxɛ. A Xaxili bara wo rasɛniyɛn, alako wo xa Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa xui ratinmɛ, wo man xa sɛniyɛn a wuli saabui ra. Ala xa hinnɛ nun bɔɲɛsa xa gbo wo yi ra.

sentences.english: Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who through his great mercy has given us a new birth and a living hope by the coming again of Jesus Christ from the dead,
sentences.susu: Tantui na Ala bɛ, won Marigi Isa Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Baba. A bara kinikini won ma, a a niya won xa bari a nɛɛnɛ ra Isa xa marakeli saabui ra. A to Isa rakeli faxɛ ma, a naxa a niya won fan xa a kolon kisi na won bɛ yare.

sentences.english: And a heritage fair, holy and for ever new, waiting in heaven for you,
sentences.susu: Na kisi findixi kɛ sɛniyɛnxi nan na naxan mu ɲɔnma, naxan mu kanama, naxan nagataxi won bɛ ariyanna kui.

sentences.english: Who, by the power of God are kept, through faith, for that salvation, which will be seen at the last day.
sentences.susu: Wo to danxaniyaxi Ala ma, a wo makantama nɛ a sɛnbɛ ra, alako wo xa kisi sɔtɔ, a fama naxan naminide wo ma waxati dɔnxɔɛ.

sentences.english: You have cause for great joy in this, though it may have been necessary for you to be troubled for a little time, being tested in all sorts of ways,
sentences.susu: Na kui, sɛɛwɛ na wo bɛ, hali wo to na tɔɔrɛ mɔɔli birin kui yi saxanyi.

sentences.english: So that the true metal of your faith, being of much greater value than gold (which, though it comes to an end, is tested by fire), may come to light in praise and glory and honour, at the revelation of Jesus Christ:
sentences.susu: Na fe xɔrɔxɔɛe a niyama nɛ fe ɲaaxi birin xa ba wo xa danxaniya kui, a xa findi danxaniya sabatixi ra. A maniyaxi xɛɛma nan na naxan gbi bama tɛ ra. Wo xa danxaniya tide gbo xɛɛma bɛ. Ala xa Mixi Sugandixi Isa na fa, a wo matɔxɔma nɛ, a wo xun nakelima nɛ, a wo binyama nɛ wo xa danxaniya xa fe ra.

sentences.english: To whom your love is given, though you have not seen him; and the faith which you have in him, though you do not see him now, gives you joy greater than words and full of glory:
sentences.susu: Wo bara Isa xanu, hali wo to mu a toxi. Hali wo to mu a toxi fa, wo lama a ra. Sɛɛwɛ xungbe naxan tagi mu nɔma rabade, a bara gbo yɛ wo yi,

sentences.english: For so you have the true end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.
sentences.susu: barima wo bara kisi sɔtɔ, wo xa danxaniya nu wama naxan xɔn.
